In 1479 DR , together with his fellow and the Masters Urlryn Khalazza , Seldszar Elpragh , and Masoj Dhuunyl he helped Q ' Arlynd when he engineered ( with the aid of Eilistraee ) the ritual that transformed all drow not tainted by Wendonai ' s blood into brown - skinned dark elves . Afterward , they all relocated to Rhymanthiin .

title: Balthazar
description: Balthazar Balthazar was a human Bhaalspawn and a monk , and one of the Five . He was perhaps the most powerful of them , and the only one whose goal was not to achieve power for himself . The game .
description_long: Balthazar Balthazar was a human Bhaalspawn and a monk , and one of the Five . He was perhaps the most powerful of them , and the only one whose goal was not to achieve power for himself . The game . In " " Balthazar is found acting as the " de facto " ruler of Amkethran , living in the monastery with his monks while his mercenaries live in and largely control the town outside . Since he ' s so focused on achieving his ultimate goal , he has let the town ' s populace to fall into poverty , and the dishonorable mercenaries run amok amongst them , bullying them at their leisure . Balthazar ' s ultimate goal is to destroy all other Bhaalspawn and , at the end , commit ritual suicide – he believes death is bred in the bones of his kind so deeply that they will always bring destruction regardless of intention , and that destroying them all is the only way to do away with Bhaal ' s essence . As such , he ' s not very different from the other Five in his cooperation with the rest , since they all more or less intend to destroy each other to increase their own power .

title: Balthorr Olaskos
description: Balthorr Olaskos Balthorr " the Bold " Olaskos was a fence and trader in Waterdeep who specialized primarily in currency , coins , and various rare trinkets . Personality . Olaskos was often able to relate a story about any particular item on the spot .
description_long: Balthorr Olaskos Balthorr " the Bold " Olaskos was a fence and trader in Waterdeep who specialized primarily in currency , coins , and various rare trinkets . Personality . Olaskos was often able to relate a story about any particular item on the spot . He operated out of his store , Balthorr ' s Rare and Wondrous Treasures within the city . Relationships . Balthorr was also a spy for the Shadow Thieves .

title: Baltir Merivolst
description: Baltir Merivolst Baltir Merivolst was the most famous commander of the Knights of the Flying Hunt in 1374 DR . Personality . Baltir took personal care of the teaching of some of the Knights ' recruits , knowing that it was vital to have a high level of training , like he had had .
description_long: Baltir Merivolst Baltir Merivolst was the most famous commander of the Knights of the Flying Hunt in 1374 DR . Personality . Baltir took personal care of the teaching of some of the Knights ' recruits , knowing that it was vital to have a high level of training , like he had had . History . Baltir was a very respected leader of the Knights . His most famous action was leading a successful expedition against a Nelanther Isles pirate fleet in 1367 DR . From that episode , his name became known — albeit barely — even outside his country ; in Nimbral , people saw him as a model of a fearless but sensible warrior and a true leader .

title: Baltor
description: Baltor Baltor was a druid who lived in Dambrath . Activities . While in the shape of a dolphin , Baltor studied the enigmatic creatures who clustered off of the shores of southern Dambrath .
description_long: Baltor Baltor was a druid who lived in Dambrath . Activities . While in the shape of a dolphin , Baltor studied the enigmatic creatures who clustered off of the shores of southern Dambrath . His primary goal was to figure out the purpose of the Dance of the Dolphins . Though thirty years had elapsed since his study began , Baltor remained confident that he would solve the mystery within another few short decades . History . Originally from distant Cormyr , he learned the ways of the druid by studying in the Hullack Forest . Once he acquired the ability to shapechange , Baltor set out to see Faerûn . While flying over Dambrath he passed over the Bay of Dancing Dolphins during one of the Dances of the Dolphins . He returned to the Hullack Forest with tales of wonders over this beautiful event and requested that he be sent back to Dambrath to further study the dolphins .

title: Bambryn
description: Bambryn Bambryn was a village in the Vast , lying on the crossroads of the Hlintar Ride , between Hlintar and Dark Hollow , and the Long Reach , between Sendrin and Orlimmin . History . During the early Time of Glorious Fools , after human s first settled the central Vast in the mid – 7th century DR , the vengeful bandit Iljack of the Black Blade plagued the central Vast .
description_long: Bambryn Bambryn was a village in the Vast , lying on the crossroads of the Hlintar Ride , between Hlintar and Dark Hollow , and the Long Reach , between Sendrin and Orlimmin . History . During the early Time of Glorious Fools , after human s first settled the central Vast in the mid – 7th century DR , the vengeful bandit Iljack of the Black Blade plagued the central Vast . He made Bambryn his base of operations . Bambryn was a wealthy village by 1370 DR . Description . Bambryn was a way - village marked by its rural beauty and common hedgerows . There were many horse - ranches and farms . There were manor houses belonging to the wealthy merchants and adventurer s who settled there ; these houses were protected by hired guards and war - dogs . Economy . Thanks to its proximity to local trade - routes , Bambryn was popular with merchants and adventurers , particularly those who ' d been successful but not fully retired . It was a wealthy village , but this was largely invested in agriculture . Bambryn produced quality horses and luxury crops , like flowers , truffles , and other exotic fungi . These plants were kept fresh with cantrip s prior to export . Rumors & Legends .

title: Bamsmack
description: Bamsmack Bamsmacks were diversion tools used by some rogue s . Uses . Imported from exotic Shou Lung , bamsmacks were made from bamboo reed and stuffed with salt .
description_long: Bamsmack Bamsmacks were diversion tools used by some rogue s . Uses . Imported from exotic Shou Lung , bamsmacks were made from bamboo reed and stuffed with salt . Once lit , a bamsmack would explode several moments later with a loud popping sound , offering a diversion for crafty thieves . Tricking a guard with a bamsmack usually only worked one time . Prices . A single bamsmack cost 5 gold .

title: Banak
description: Banak Banak was once the top ranked evil priest in all the Bloodstone lands . He was 24th level until Gareth Dragonsbane and party banished Banak ' s demon patron Orcus , from Faerûn . Since his patron ' s fall , Banak can cast 1st through 3rd level spells and occasionally casts a higher level .
description_long: Banak Banak was once the top ranked evil priest in all the Bloodstone lands . He was 24th level until Gareth Dragonsbane and party banished Banak ' s demon patron Orcus , from Faerûn . Since his patron ' s fall , Banak can cast 1st through 3rd level spells and occasionally casts a higher level . It is unclear how Banak maintains as much power as he has . Its possible he had a stockpile of scrolls , or he might have found a new deity . Still , Banak is experienced and evil enough to remain a threat to goodly folk of Vaasa and Damara . He is one of the top three commanders in the Citadel of Assassins alongside the Grandfather of Assassins and the archmage Knellict . His specialty is the domain of the undead . He casts " animate dead " on whatever corpses he can aquire , and is not averse to using his Staff of the Adder to create a few more corpses .

title: Banak Brawnanvil
description: Banak Brawnanvil Banak Brawnanvil was one of the dwarves of Mithral Hall who defended against the orc s led by Urlgen Threefist . He was the High Commander . In 1370 DR , during the battle with army of orcs commanded by King Obould Many - Arrows , he was hurt by a goblin spear .
description_long: Banak Brawnanvil Banak Brawnanvil was one of the dwarves of Mithral Hall who defended against the orc s led by Urlgen Threefist . He was the High Commander . In 1370 DR , during the battle with army of orcs commanded by King Obould Many - Arrows , he was hurt by a goblin spear . The weapon struck his back and broke his spine , leaving him without the use of his legs . He still had movement thanks to a wheelchair that was made for him by the gnome alchemist Nanfoodle Buswilligan . The dwarf was given control over Mithral Hall when Bruenor was not there . In 1409 DR , Banak was made the eleventh king of Mithral Hall , after Bruenor abdicated by faking his death . Within a few decades , he passed away and his son Connerad took his place as king . Relatives . Banak was King Bruenor Battlehammer ' s cousin , making him Bruenor ' s closest living relative .

title: Bandaerl
description: Bandaerl Bandaerl , son of Rykos , blood of Melair , High Old One of Dumathoin , and protector of Melairbode ' s essence was a dwarven archlich of the Melairkyn clan who protected the tomb of King Melair I in the depths of Undermountain , formerly home to this ancient clan .
description_long: Bandaerl Bandaerl , son of Rykos , blood of Melair , High Old One of Dumathoin , and protector of Melairbode ' s essence was a dwarven archlich of the Melairkyn clan who protected the tomb of King Melair I in the depths of Undermountain , formerly home to this ancient clan .

title: Bandagh
description: Bandagh Bandagh was a orc in the Doomvault dungeon in 1486 DR . History . Bandagh was one of the many Chosen captured by the Red Wizards of Thay and transported to the Doomvault dungeon for experiments .
description_long: Bandagh Bandagh was a orc in the Doomvault dungeon in 1486 DR . History . Bandagh was one of the many Chosen captured by the Red Wizards of Thay and transported to the Doomvault dungeon for experiments . More specifically , he was the chosen of Yurtrus , a minor god of the orc pantheon . Bandagh was freed from his chains by the heroes of Daggerford but he was pockmarked by years of disease .

title: Bandar al - Sa ' adat
description: Bandar al - Sa ' adat Bandar al - Sa ' adat was a town located on the isle of Masud Jazayir in the Nada al - Hazan archipelago within the Crowded Sea south of mainland Zakhara . Organization . The town could field a militia of 100 soldiers who were adept at defending against pirate raids .
description_long: Bandar al - Sa ' adat Bandar al - Sa ' adat was a town located on the isle of Masud Jazayir in the Nada al - Hazan archipelago within the Crowded Sea south of mainland Zakhara . Organization . The town could field a militia of 100 soldiers who were adept at defending against pirate raids . Several wizards offered magical assistance to the militia in times of need . Activities . Sea trade was a major source of income for the town and also caused its population to fluctuate . Inhabitants . This town was ruled by Mahmud Ben Aziz . His brother Karim Ben Aziz was captain of the marketplace guards . Much of Ben Aziz ' s family held other positions of note within the small town . Masudi islanders had a love of words , opting to speak in colorful ways to alleviate boredom . Outsiders to the island often stuck out just because of the way they spoke .

title: Banded agate
description: Banded agate Banded agate was a form of opaque agate with striations of brown , red , blue , and / or white . Description . These ornamental stones were polished smooth and had a waxy feel making it ideal for " worry stones " or " soothe stones " that some merchants would rub or fondle to relieve stress during negotiations .
description_long: Banded agate Banded agate was a form of opaque agate with striations of brown , red , blue , and / or white . Description . These ornamental stones were polished smooth and had a waxy feel making it ideal for " worry stones " or " soothe stones " that some merchants would rub or fondle to relieve stress during negotiations . Banded agate was also used ornamentally , or crushed to a powder and added to sleeping draughts to improve their effectiveness . No such improvement was ever proven however . A typical stone had a base value of 10 gp .

title: Banderhobb
description: Banderhobb Banderhobbs were creatures resembling bipedal toads . They were hybrids of shadow and flesh created by magical means . Creation .
description_long: Banderhobb Banderhobbs were creatures resembling bipedal toads . They were hybrids of shadow and flesh created by magical means . Creation . A banderhobb was birthed by a ritual originally devised by hag , but later any magical creature or mage who knew the ritual could birth a banderhobb . Description . The banderhobb was not capable of speech , but could understand orders . These creatures were as big as an ogre but as silent as the shadows they were created from . Activities . In their short existence , they sought to complete whatever task the one who birthed it ordered it to do . Rumors . There were rumors that in a dark tower in the Shadowfell shadow s sometimes reformed and banderhobbs roamed .

title: Bandit camp ( Mere of Dead Men )
description: Bandit camp ( Mere of Dead Men ) This unnamed bandit camp was a camp located at the southern end of the Mere of Dead Men along the Sword Coast . Location . The bandit camp was located near Fort Locke .
description_long: Bandit camp ( Mere of Dead Men ) This unnamed bandit camp was a camp located at the southern end of the Mere of Dead Men along the Sword Coast . Location . The bandit camp was located near Fort Locke . Structure . The camp was composed of tents and a small building , where the bandit leader lived . The camp was surrounded by wooden walls , while the building was built from straw , wood and stone . Interior . The building was composed of several rooms and halls where experienced bandits lived . There were many weapons and valuables stored inside it . History . The camp was inhabited with bandits , who captured the refugees . The Kalach - Cha could ' ve learned the location from Neeshka and go there to rescue the refugees , then deal with the leader .

title: Bando
description: Bando Bando the Lame was an old halfling priest of Tymora in Daggerford around 1370 DR . History . Bando was once injured in a battle with three lizardfolk , which gave him an injured leg and a deep hatred for the scaly fiends .
description_long: Bando Bando the Lame was an old halfling priest of Tymora in Daggerford around 1370 DR . History . Bando was once injured in a battle with three lizardfolk , which gave him an injured leg and a deep hatred for the scaly fiends . He managed the local shrine to Tymora , the Fairfortune Hall .

title: Bandore
description: Bandore Bandores were bass - range musical instruments similar to cittern s . Description . The sound of the bandore was rich and mellow , and it was capable of reaching lower notes than usual citterns which made them good accompanying instruments for quieter voices .
description_long: Bandore Bandores were bass - range musical instruments similar to cittern s . Description . The sound of the bandore was rich and mellow , and it was capable of reaching lower notes than usual citterns which made them good accompanying instruments for quieter voices . Bandores typically had scalloped sides that were said to enrich their sound . They were available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " .

title: Bane
description: Bane Bane ( pronounced " BAIN " ) was the evil and malicious greater deity of fear , hatred and tyranny and ruler of Banehold . Preferring to plot and scheme , Bane rarely appeared to act in a direct manner ; instead acting through his worshipers and other various agents . His ultimate goal was to eventually control all of Faerûn .
description_long: Bane Bane ( pronounced " BAIN " ) was the evil and malicious greater deity of fear , hatred and tyranny and ruler of Banehold . Preferring to plot and scheme , Bane rarely appeared to act in a direct manner ; instead acting through his worshipers and other various agents . His ultimate goal was to eventually control all of Faerûn . When summoned he had a dark and rather shadowy appearance with a resemblance of dark armor and his tell - tale jeweled dark gauntlet . He emanated an aura of vast power and cruel intelligence . Worshipers . Among the evil gods , Bane ' s church was among the most stable and powerful . While there was a time when the god encouraged sectarianism and violent disputes , that time has long since passed and today the god ' s Faithful were as likely to solve their disputes through reasonable debate as through show of force .

title: Bane ( spell )
description: Bane ( spell ) Bane was an enchantment spell that sapped enemy morale and reduced their combat effectiveness . A conjuration version was known by the name curse and was the reverse of " bless " . Effects .
description_long: Bane ( spell ) Bane was an enchantment spell that sapped enemy morale and reduced their combat effectiveness . A conjuration version was known by the name curse and was the reverse of " bless " . Effects . Those enemies " cursed " were inflicted with trepidation and doubt , lowering their morale and dulling their skill in combat . " Bane " countered and dispelled " bless " and vice versa . After Second Sundering , the " bane " and " bless " spells didn ' t counter and dispel each other but were opposites of each other . Components . This spell required only verbal and somatic components , and the caster ' s ( un ) holy symbol or divine focus . The conjuration version required unholy water . The later enchantment version used a drop of blood .

title: Baneblades of Demron
description: Baneblades of Demron The Baneblades of Demron were six powerful magic sword s forged for the defenders of Myth Drannor before its fall . The archmage Demron was credited with their creation over some three centuries , but they were cooperative efforts among all the races that dwelled in Myth Drannor . Each was designed for a member of a particular race or profession , and their magic ceased to function for anyone else , leaving only a nonmagical weapon of otherwise fine quality .
description_long: Baneblades of Demron The Baneblades of Demron were six powerful magic sword s forged for the defenders of Myth Drannor before its fall . The archmage Demron was credited with their creation over some three centuries , but they were cooperative efforts among all the races that dwelled in Myth Drannor . Each was designed for a member of a particular race or profession , and their magic ceased to function for anyone else , leaving only a nonmagical weapon of otherwise fine quality . They were imbued with holy energy and were particularly effective against outsider s ( those from planes other than the Prime Material Plane ) and undead , and glowed with the light of a torch on command . Each also had their own unique powers . Creation and History . In 346 DR , several senior and junior officers were exiled from Myth Drannor after it was revealed that they had subjected their non - elven troops to horrendous treatment and for willingly sacrificing them in favor of elven troops , especially in the Darkwoods Massacre .

title: Baneguard
description: Baneguard Baneguards were animated skeleton s with magical abilities originally created by cleric s of Bane . The spell " create baneguard " eventually propagated to other evil - and neutral - aligned faiths that found these capable guardians acceptable . Description .
description_long: Baneguard Baneguards were animated skeleton s with magical abilities originally created by cleric s of Bane . The spell " create baneguard " eventually propagated to other evil - and neutral - aligned faiths that found these capable guardians acceptable . Description . Baneguards looked like skeletons and could be created from the bones of most any medium - sized creature . Until they demonstrated magical ability or acted with intelligent forethought , they were indistinguishable from basic , undead skeletons . Personality . Baneguards were of average intelligence and capable of creative , independent thought and actions that did not contradict the orders given to them by their creator . They were not able to speak and were wholly evil . Combat . Baneguards could use any normal weapon or fight with bare claws . They could also use any magic item that did not require a verbal command or a body of flesh , blood , and organs . In combat , a baneguard could activate its " blink " ability , randomly shifting between the Ethereal plane and the Prime Material Plane for a short while , which helped with both offense and defense .

title: Banehold
description: Banehold Banehold , sometimes called the Barrens of Doom and Despair , or Gehenna , particularly in the past , is an evil - aligned plane of existence . It is one of a number of Outer Planes , one of inhospitable locales , including vast deserts of black sand and huge plains of dark granite . There is no water to be found anywhere on the plane , and no sunlight fills the blood - red sky .
description_long: Banehold Banehold , sometimes called the Barrens of Doom and Despair , or Gehenna , particularly in the past , is an evil - aligned plane of existence . It is one of a number of Outer Planes , one of inhospitable locales , including vast deserts of black sand and huge plains of dark granite . There is no water to be found anywhere on the plane , and no sunlight fills the blood - red sky . Deities who make their home on this plane include Bane ( who previously dwelled on Acheron ) Beshaba , Hoar , Loviatar , and Talona . Kuraulyek dwells in this plane ' s Underdark . Structure . The Barrens of Doom and Despair consist of a single infinite plane , there are no constituent layers . It links via the Astral Plane to the planes of the Prime Material ( such as Toril ) and a number of portals directly connect it with Hammergrim and the Blood Rift . Beshaba ' s realm , the Blood Tor , links directly to the Abyss .

title: Banelar naga
description: Banelar naga Banelar nagas ( also simply called banelars ) were evil , spell - wielding naga s with large , humanoid heads . Description . Their eyes had a green tint to them , and their scales were a greenish purple , but they had brown tails tipped with stingers .
description_long: Banelar naga Banelar nagas ( also simply called banelars ) were evil , spell - wielding naga s with large , humanoid heads . Description . Their eyes had a green tint to them , and their scales were a greenish purple , but they had brown tails tipped with stingers . Around their mouths were weak yet agile tentacles . They could breathe in either air or water . Their voices had a hissing aspect to them , and they spoke Common , Orcish , and Draconic languages . Combat . Banelar nagas ' tails had venemous stingers on them , with the poison causing a target ' s skin to turn blue . In addition to this natural weapon , they favored fighting with spells , mainly from the evil , water , and magic domains . They also used a variety of magical items to complement this , sometimes holding them with their tiny tentacles . Society . Banelar nagas followed Bane , with Cyric being a less - favored god whose priests they worked with from 1358 DR until 1372 DR , at which point the majority , but not all , returned to their previous ways .

title: Banelich
description: Banelich A banelich was a lich who was a cleric of Bane during his or her mortal life . Baneliches acted and looked the same as others of their kind , but they continued to worship Bane as an undead . They had the same immunities as regular liches , and gained the rest of the undeads ' powers , such as " paralytic touch " .
description_long: Banelich A banelich was a lich who was a cleric of Bane during his or her mortal life . Baneliches acted and looked the same as others of their kind , but they continued to worship Bane as an undead . They had the same immunities as regular liches , and gained the rest of the undeads ' powers , such as " paralytic touch " .

title: Bangor Battlehammer
description: Bangor Battlehammer Bangor Battlehammer was the father of the more famous Bruenor Battlehammer , king of Mithral Hall . Appendix . Notes .
description_long: Bangor Battlehammer Bangor Battlehammer was the father of the more famous Bruenor Battlehammer , king of Mithral Hall . Appendix . Notes . Considering there is a statue of Bangor in the Hall of Kings in Mithral Hall , he must have been a king at some point . However , he died fighting alongside his father , Garumn , which means either the statue was carved prematurely or Garumn abdicated before he died .

title: Bani Matruj al - Haddar
description: Bani Matruj al - Haddar Bani Matruj al - Haddar , or the Silent Sheikh , was a goblin barber living in Liham in 1367 DR . Personality . Bani was talkative to the point where he would continue to talk until gagged .
description_long: Bani Matruj al - Haddar Bani Matruj al - Haddar , or the Silent Sheikh , was a goblin barber living in Liham in 1367 DR . Personality . Bani was talkative to the point where he would continue to talk until gagged . Description . Bani ' s flat face was accompanied by a broad nose , pointed ears , wide mouth , and sharp fangs . He stood four feet ( 1 . 2 m ) tall . His skin was dull red and he had yellow eyes . Activities . Bani enjoyed drawing out the time he spent with customers . He would often stop grooming them halfway so he could draw up an astrological chart for them . Bani was an excellent source of information on the happenings of Liham .

title: Banish dazzle
description: Banish dazzle Banish dazzle was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects .
description_long: Banish dazzle Banish dazzle was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects . Once this spell was cast the target could see clearly through blinding sunlight and heat shimmer . This spell also helped the target resist other spells directed at their eyes such as " color spray " or " fire charm " . Reflected sunlight from a mirror had no effect on the target , and they were immune from being blinded by light spells . Components . This spell required a shard of glass , mica , gemstone , or clear crystal to cast . The shard was destroyed upon casting .

title: Banishing smite
description: Banishing smite Banishing smite was an abjuration spell for paladin s that made a weapon crackle with power and cause more damage . Effects . The spell caused the chosen weapon to crackle with power and cause serious damage .
description_long: Banishing smite Banishing smite was an abjuration spell for paladin s that made a weapon crackle with power and cause more damage . Effects . The spell caused the chosen weapon to crackle with power and cause serious damage . A struck target with less than certain level of vitality would be banished . A creature from another plane was sent to its native plane , while a creature on its home plane was sent to a harmless demiplane . While there , the target was incapacitated and when the spell ended the creature was sent back to their original location . Components . The spell had only a verbal component .

title: Banishment
description: Banishment Banishment was an abjuration spell that banished outsider s to their home plane . Effects . A " banishment " spell was a more powerful version of the " dismissal " spell .
description_long: Banishment Banishment was an abjuration spell that banished outsider s to their home plane . Effects . A " banishment " spell was a more powerful version of the " dismissal " spell . It enabled the caster to force extraplanar creatures out of his home plane . The number and power of creatures that could be banished increased with the power of the caster . To target a creature , the caster had to present at least one object or substance that the target hated , feared , or otherwise opposed . Each such object or substance made it more likely the caster would overcome the target ' s spell resistance . For example , if this spell were cast on a demon that hated light and was vulnerable to holy water and iron weapons , the caster might use iron , holy water , and a torch in the spell . If the target was banished in its native plain it was sent to a harmless demiplane , and if the spell wasn ' t broken within a minute the creature would remain in its native plain . Components . An item the target found distasteful .

title: Baniya Dolester
description: Baniya Dolester Baniya Dolester was a human female priest ess of Lliira in the city of Procampur in the Vast . History . In the Year of the Shield , 1367 DR , she served as High Priest of the Hall of Success temple in the Temple District of Procampur .
description_long: Baniya Dolester Baniya Dolester was a human female priest ess of Lliira in the city of Procampur in the Vast . History . In the Year of the Shield , 1367 DR , she served as High Priest of the Hall of Success temple in the Temple District of Procampur . It had formerly been dedicated to Waukeen , but was later reconsecrated to Lliira following the apparent death of Waukeen during the Time of Troubles , in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR . One of Dolester ' s duties was to care for the former High Priest , Undil Latheen , who ' d gone mad with the disappearance of Waukeen . In Marpenoth of 1367 DR , when Procampur was struck by the featherlung plague , Dolester worked with High Priest Orn Thavil of Tymora and set up auxiliary shrines in the District of the Poor to treat the sick there . Though their actions halted the spread of the disease , the Thultyrl reprimanded both high priests for breaking Procampur ' s district rules , and were reminded that the city and its laws were older than a number of deities .

title: Bankenfuere
description: Bankenfuere Bankenfuere was Berkthgar the Bold ' s large flamberge sword . Description . The sword had a wavy 4 - ft - long ( 1 .
description_long: Bankenfuere Bankenfuere was Berkthgar the Bold ' s large flamberge sword . Description . The sword had a wavy 4 - ft - long ( 1 . 2 m ) blade with an 8 - in - long ( 0 . 2 m ) before the hilt and cross guard . Berkthgar carried his weapon in a shoulder sheath on his back . History . Around 1358 DR , Berkthgar fought the famed Companion of the Hall Catti - brie with Bankenfuere in Settlestone to settle a disagreement Berkthgar had with Bruenor Battlehammer over Wulfgar ' s warhammer , " Aegis - fang " . After the battle , Berkthgar declared he would make a new legend of his sword , Bankenfuere the Northern Fury . Catti - brie called the sword " Cow - killer " .

title: Banner of renown
description: Banner of renown The Banner of renown was a magical flag that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . This flag displayed the moon and trailing stars symbol of the Land of Fate .
description_long: Banner of renown The Banner of renown was a magical flag that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . This flag displayed the moon and trailing stars symbol of the Land of Fate . Powers . When held during battle , this flag inspired all enlightened persons within 100 ft . ( 30 m ) with supernatural morale , infusing them with bravery and strength of arm . If the bearer of the flag was killed , the flag dissipated and all magical powers vanished instantly .

title: Banshee
description: Banshee A Banshee is a female phantom , embodying the essence of hideousness . Banshees are the spirits of strongwilled , selfish humanoids . They are undead creatures who delight in bringing death to any living creature .
description_long: Banshee A Banshee is a female phantom , embodying the essence of hideousness . Banshees are the spirits of strongwilled , selfish humanoids . They are undead creatures who delight in bringing death to any living creature . It still speaks the language it has known in life . Appearance . A banshee doesn ' t have a defined shape rather a misty form with vague and flowing features . Her aura makes trees and brushes wither in her mere proximity . Her face looks twisted and asymmetric with a hook - nose and pop - eyes . A banshee has long fingers . A banshee appears as a translucent image of its former self in life . With the pass of time the image of the banshee tends to become blurred and indistinct , but still recognizable as a humanoid . A banshee is incorporeal and therefore can only be harmed by magical means with magical weapons or abilities . Because a banshee is an undead it has all the immunities of undead creatures . Combat . The banshee ' s most feared weapon is her piercing moan that can be as hurtful as any weapon . They hate all living things with an unholy fury and they readily attack anyone who trespasses their territory .

title: Bapar Ghalmrin
description: Bapar Ghalmrin Bapar Ghalmrin was a member of Clan Ghalmrin in Starspire Mountains in Tethyr in 1370 DR . Personality . Bapar , as the fourth son , was always considered redundant and expendable , so he dreamed of finding the Wyrmskull Throne and gaining the respect of his distant father and his oldest brothers .
description_long: Bapar Ghalmrin Bapar Ghalmrin was a member of Clan Ghalmrin in Starspire Mountains in Tethyr in 1370 DR . Personality . Bapar , as the fourth son , was always considered redundant and expendable , so he dreamed of finding the Wyrmskull Throne and gaining the respect of his distant father and his oldest brothers . He , like all true members of Clan Ghalmrin , knew that the only true heirs of the ancient kings of Shanatar were duergar . History . In 1370 DR , following some clues , Bapar and his companions Odak Truesteel and Soram Battlebellow discovered that a group possessing one of the lost " Scepters of Shanatar " must be in the village of Toralth . On the night of Uktar 10 , they entered the tavern seeking the " Sondarr Scepter " and interrupting the ballad that a bard was singing for the lost companions of the Shields of the Highland adventuring company . He accused some of the patrons of thieving from the dwarves and asked them to turn over to him the thieves and the stolen goods .

title: Baphomet
description: Baphomet Baphomet was a demon lord who ruled a layer of the Abyss called the Endless Maze . He was the Prince of Beasts and the Demon Lord of Minotaur s . Description .
description_long: Baphomet Baphomet was a demon lord who ruled a layer of the Abyss called the Endless Maze . He was the Prince of Beasts and the Demon Lord of Minotaur s . Description . Baphomet had the appearance of a 12 - foot - tall humanoid with a bull ' s head , a bovine tail , and broad , stubby hands and feet . His body was covered with coarse black hair . His horns curved downward and outward . He wielded a giant bardiche . Baphomet could spit out gouts of unholy water . Realm . Baphomet ' s realm of the " Endless Maze " was the 600th layer of the Abyss , supposedly infinite in size . Here , Baphomet dwelt in his palace , the Lyktion , and spent his time creating various new demonic breeds in his infamous Tower of Science . Some of his more successful creations were the goristroi , the bulezaus , the ghours , and more recently , the feral ankashars . Worshipers . Baphomet had a multitude of minotaur , ogre , and giant followers and minions . He was also served by ghour demons , a race of demons resembling burly , hairless minotaurs which commanded troops of these mortal minions . He sought to use them to further his schemes , notably to gain the upper hand in his battles against Yeenoghu .

title: Bar - lgura
description: Bar - lgura Bar - lguras or barlguras , also known as leaping demons , were ape - like tanar ' ri demon s . Description . Bar - lguras were covered in reddish - brown hair and stood between 5 and 6 feet tall .
description_long: Bar - lgura Bar - lguras or barlguras , also known as leaping demons , were ape - like tanar ' ri demon s . Description . Bar - lguras were covered in reddish - brown hair and stood between 5 and 6 feet tall . They appeared similar to . They usually walked on all four limbs , but were able to stand on two legs . Society . Bar - lguras were used as scouts and footsoldiers by more powerful demons . They preferred to fight and travel in packs , but they didn ' t like the company of lesser demons . Bar - lguras served Demogorgon and when seen outside of the Abyss were associated with the Cult of Demogorgon . Combat . Some , but not all , bar - lguras wielded weapons and wore humanoid armor . They used their powerful arms and legs to attack , as well as their claws . They set ambushes when possible . They were able to use their " teleport " ability to " teleport " both themselves and enemies . A favorite tactic was to " teleport " an enemy into a sealed area where it could not escape . Like other tanar ' ri , bar - lguras could summon other demons when they were in dire straits .

title: Bara Minora
description: Bara Minora Bara Minora was a halfling who worked and cared for Hama Sayif within the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Activities . Bara played her drums while Hama performed his mystical dances .
description_long: Bara Minora Bara Minora was a halfling who worked and cared for Hama Sayif within the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Activities . Bara played her drums while Hama performed his mystical dances . She also took care off all haggling for Hama ' s customers . Relationships . Bara ' s mate was Sika al - Bana . Bara had been with Hama ever since he saved the lives of she and her mate in Al - Akara Mountains . History . Hama once cursed Bara with the evil eye when he caught her lifting the purse from one of his customers .

title: Baraedin
description: Baraedin The Baraedin family was a noble merchant family of the city of Tantras in the Vast . The head of the family sat on the High Council that governed Tantras . In 1358 DR , shortly after the Time of Troubles , the Baraedins were allied with the Mithertul , Onsil , and Naskurl families .
description_long: Baraedin The Baraedin family was a noble merchant family of the city of Tantras in the Vast . The head of the family sat on the High Council that governed Tantras . In 1358 DR , shortly after the Time of Troubles , the Baraedins were allied with the Mithertul , Onsil , and Naskurl families .

title: Baragustas Harbuckler
description: Baragustas Harbuckler Baragustas Harbuckler was a retired carpenter in Red Larch and a member of the Believers during the Elemental Evil crisis . Relationships . Baragustas was an old member of Believers .
description_long: Baragustas Harbuckler Baragustas Harbuckler was a retired carpenter in Red Larch and a member of the Believers during the Elemental Evil crisis . Relationships . Baragustas was an old member of Believers . History . In 1491 DR , he was quite intimidated by Larrakh of the Cult of the Black Earth , who tried to put the Believers in a more active role . He was not part in the murders committed by Ilmeth Waelvur , Marlandro Gaelkur , and Albaeri Mellikho but knew of the matter and covered for them . He was subdued by some adventurers who were investigating in the village .

title: Barakuir
description: Barakuir Barakuir ( the Iron Kingdom ) was a kingdom of the dwarven realm of Shanatar , dominated by the shield dwarf Clan Duergar , whose inhabitants would eventually be transformed into the gray dwarves . The kingdom venerated Laduguer and was ruled by a priest - king who was known as the Iron Shield . History .
description_long: Barakuir Barakuir ( the Iron Kingdom ) was a kingdom of the dwarven realm of Shanatar , dominated by the shield dwarf Clan Duergar , whose inhabitants would eventually be transformed into the gray dwarves . The kingdom venerated Laduguer and was ruled by a priest - king who was known as the Iron Shield . History . Barakuir held fierce rivalries with the neighbouring sub - kingdoms of Drakkalor and Ultoksamrin , which were converted to open conflict during the Spawn Wars from around - 9000 DR . Barakuir swore its allegiance to the Wyrmskull Throne of Shanatar and fought in the Second Spider War from - 8145 to - 8137 DR . As it came to an end , Barakuir believed its king should have been the one selected to rule all of Shanatar , and when this did not happen , Barakuir ' s inhabitants became bitter and turned away from the other kingdoms of Shanatar . Although many clans originally inhabited Barakuir , the ruling Clan Duergar became increasingly tyrannical , leading the other clans to flee . Around - 8100 DR , the Mindstalker Wars between Shanatar and the illithid s of Oryndoll caused Barakuir to become cut off from the rest of Shanatar , preventing reinforcements from arriving .

title: Baralea Braceryn
description: Baralea Braceryn Baralea Braceryn was part - owner , cook , and hostess at the Three Elves inn in Voonlar " circa " the Year of Wild Magic , 1372 DR . Description . She was rotund , but with bird - like quickness .
description_long: Baralea Braceryn Baralea Braceryn was part - owner , cook , and hostess at the Three Elves inn in Voonlar " circa " the Year of Wild Magic , 1372 DR . Description . She was rotund , but with bird - like quickness . Personality . Baralea was flirtatious and bustled about , thoughtfully taking care of her customer ' s needs . Abilities . She was a great cook , able to quickly whip up a meal . She and her sister brewed a sweet beer from berries . Relationships . The Three Elves was a very popular inn throughout the Moonsea region and its owner / operators were highly regarded . Baralea had a sister , Ammatha .

title: Baran al - Amin al - Jinn
description: Baran al - Amin al - Jinn Baran al - Amin al - Jinn was a janni who lived in Al - Yabki Mountains in Zakhara in 1367 DR . Activities . As a priest of Kor , Baran donned the robes of a " qadi " and began acting as a judge at a sacred site in the mountains near Turab and Sikak .
description_long: Baran al - Amin al - Jinn Baran al - Amin al - Jinn was a janni who lived in Al - Yabki Mountains in Zakhara in 1367 DR . Activities . As a priest of Kor , Baran donned the robes of a " qadi " and began acting as a judge at a sacred site in the mountains near Turab and Sikak . He was popular among Al - Badia , many of whom traveled considerable distances to discuss their problems with him .

title: Barandos Hawklin
description: Barandos Hawklin Barandos Hawklin was the popular head of the Hawklin noble family in Suzail in 1368 DR . Description . He had urbane good looks .
description_long: Barandos Hawklin Barandos Hawklin was the popular head of the Hawklin noble family in Suzail in 1368 DR . Description . He had urbane good looks . Personality . Barandos had a particularly sharp wit and was noted as a charmer of ladies both high and low born . His fairness and integrity were as well known as his wealth . History . By 1368 DR Barandos ' leadership of the Hawklin family had led them into much prosperity through various investments in and around the city . Among these , first and foremost , was his support and sponsoring of local adventuring companies .

title: Baraskur
description: Baraskur Baraskur was the main settlement of the Ripped Gut orc tribe . Description . The cavernous fortress of Baraskur was built in memory of a great orc hero .
description_long: Baraskur Baraskur was the main settlement of the Ripped Gut orc tribe . Description . The cavernous fortress of Baraskur was built in memory of a great orc hero . It stood on a slope of the Nether Mountains at the end of a rough path that flanked a precipice . The fortress was located on the southern flank of the Orcsblood Peak between Deadsnows and Sundabar . Orc raiding parties from Baraskur infested Moon Pass , Turnstone Pass , and Fork Road . History . An unusual guardian watched over the Orcs . Centuries ago , an outcast human sorcerer named Aumathra asked for hospitality from the orcs living in Baraskur . Aumathra died ages ago , but her ghost was still nervous . The orcs were able to calm Aumathra ' s ghost by donating a tall , slender female body that had black hair and was skilled at magic , giving the ghost a chance to possess her . Despite that , the ghost became upset . So the orcs started looking for someone with Aumathra ' s likeness . They brought a captured specimen before Aumathra ' s ghost during a dark ceremony where Aumathra possessed the body . She usually spending most of her time rummaging through ruins and surrounding tombs .

title: Barasta Cleeith
description: Barasta Cleeith Barasta Cleeith was a high - ranking member of the Church of Waukeen and a member of the Knights of the Shield in 1370 DR . History . Barasta was the daughter of the Amn ian noble Lord Lurraxol and the wife of fellow noble Lord Cleeith .
description_long: Barasta Cleeith Barasta Cleeith was a high - ranking member of the Church of Waukeen and a member of the Knights of the Shield in 1370 DR . History . Barasta was the daughter of the Amn ian noble Lord Lurraxol and the wife of fellow noble Lord Cleeith . Barasta became a senior priestess of Waukeen at the abbey of Goldspires , just near Athkatla , and in this role Barasta became the oldest and most trusted confidant of Holycoin Tharundar Olhem , the high priest of the entire Faerûn ian church of Waukeen . Her business successes over the years proved her devotion the goddess . Activities . She invested much effort in trading with Maztica , where she possessed an estate in New Amn , after the disastrous war with sahuagin . Her other concern was undermining the nomination of her rival Daerea Ethgil , a fellow priestess at Goldspires , for membership in the Knights .

title: Baravar Cloakshadow
description: Baravar Cloakshadow Baravar Cloakshadow , known as the Sly One , was the neutral good gnome deity of illusion and deception . His dogma primarily concerned the protection of the gnome race through the art of illusion . Worshipers .
description_long: Baravar Cloakshadow Baravar Cloakshadow , known as the Sly One , was the neutral good gnome deity of illusion and deception . His dogma primarily concerned the protection of the gnome race through the art of illusion . Worshipers . Clerics of Baravar were generally sneaky , smart gnomes , who served their communities by instructing them in disguise and camouflage . They prayed for their spells at dusk , and venerated Baravar in a monthly ritual known as " the Cloaking " . The Cloaking was most often held in public places under the new moon , and it was considered a point of honor that outsiders never realized what was happening . Relationships . Baravar was closely allied with the other non - evil members of the gnome pantheon . His other allies were Azuth , Brandobaris , Clangeddin Silverbeard , Erevan Ilesere , Mystra , Sehanine Moonbow , Tymora , and Vergadain . His chief enemies were the deities of the goblin and kobold races . Other foes were Cyric ( for killing his one - time ally , Leira ) , Abbathor , Mask , and Urdlen .

title: Barbarian
description: Barbarian Barbarians were mighty warrior s who rely on their strength and incredible toughness , characterized by a bestial rage empowered either by ancestral totem s and nature spirit s or an inner passion for violence . Barbarians were less versatile than fighter s but were tougher and capable of dealing heavy damage to their foes much more quickly . The most famous barbarian of Toril was likely Wulfgar , friend and companion to Drizzt Do ' Urden .
description_long: Barbarian Barbarians were mighty warrior s who rely on their strength and incredible toughness , characterized by a bestial rage empowered either by ancestral totem s and nature spirit s or an inner passion for violence . Barbarians were less versatile than fighter s but were tougher and capable of dealing heavy damage to their foes much more quickly . The most famous barbarian of Toril was likely Wulfgar , friend and companion to Drizzt Do ' Urden . Culture . Barbarians were common within several organizations within Faerûn such as Uthgardt warrior traditions of the Silver Marches and Icewind Dale , the primal warriors of the Reghed Glacier , wild tribes of the Chondalwood , Chult , and the famous berserkers of Rashemen and its neighboring regions . However , contrary to common belief , not all warriors who lived outside civilization ' s borders were barbarians . Only those who embrace the wild and primal ways of the " rage " could rightly call themselves a barbarian , imbuing them with a wild spirit not found among most warriors .

title: Barbarian lands ( Utter East )
description: Barbarian lands ( Utter East ) East of the kingdom of Ulgarth , in the northern Utter East of the far southeast Faerûn lay barbarian - inhabited lands . Geography . The land was a vast plain , uncharted by the neighboring civilizations .
description_long: Barbarian lands ( Utter East ) East of the kingdom of Ulgarth , in the northern Utter East of the far southeast Faerûn lay barbarian - inhabited lands . Geography . The land was a vast plain , uncharted by the neighboring civilizations . In the west , by the border with Ulgarth , lay Barbarians ' Road . In the southwest corner was the Stony Waste . A river ran across the far eastern side , and the plains abutted the A - Ling Shan , part of the great Yehimal , in the east and the first range crossing the Utter East in the south . Inhabitants . The land was inhabited by a horse - riding barbarian people . Relations . In the 14th century DR . the folk of Ulgarth knew the people of this land as " the Horde " , as barbarians to the east who regularly gathered in great hosts to raid their settlements . The kingdom was vigilant , well - prepared , and even paranoid in defending itself . Convict armies regularly patrolled the eastern borders . Nevertheless , the people of the city of Kaspar preferred to trade with them , though guardedly , and took the pick of their horses after a raid . History .

title: Barbarians ' Road
description: Barbarians ' Road Barbarians ' Road was a road in the kingdom of Ulgarth in southeast Faerûn . It ran north – south , joining the settlements of Dralpur and Kellesar . It formed the well - patrolled border with the barbarian lands to the east .
description_long: Barbarians ' Road Barbarians ' Road was a road in the kingdom of Ulgarth in southeast Faerûn . It ran north – south , joining the settlements of Dralpur and Kellesar . It formed the well - patrolled border with the barbarian lands to the east . Appendix . Notes . Barbarians ' Road is known only from its appearance on the maps on page 53 and 73 of " The Shining South " ( 1993 ) . Its name and easternmost location suggest it is the east border mentioned on page 75 .

title: Barbazu
description: Barbazu Barbazus , also called bearded devils , were the shock troops of the Nine Hells . They led armies of lemure s . Physical description .
description_long: Barbazu Barbazus , also called bearded devils , were the shock troops of the Nine Hells . They led armies of lemure s . Physical description . Barbazus were six feet ( 180 centimeters ) tall and weighed roughly 225 pounds ( 102 kilograms ) . They had snake - like beards , oozing with disease . In battle , they often were outfitted with infernal armor , even though their scaly hides could usually deflect the typical attack . Combat . Bearded devils had aggressive personalities and loved fighting . These fiends used the extended reach of their saw - toothed glaive s to their advantage . Enemies who got too close were grappled and subjected to the foul disease lingering in the devils ' beards . Ecology . These devil s were the elite soldiers of Hell ' s legions . They were savage fighters who would enter a frenzied rage before engaging in battle . Between wars , they found employment as guards and sentinels for more powerful devils . History . In 1480 DR , assassin s and barbazu attacked Lasparhall in Thentia in an attempt to assassinate the rightful ruling family of Hulburg , the Hulmaster s .

title: Barbed dart
description: Barbed dart A barbed dart was a very large dart that is both fletched and barbed . They measured 2 – 3 ft ( 60 – 90 cm ) in length and weighed around 5 lb ( 2 . 5 kg ) .
description_long: Barbed dart A barbed dart was a very large dart that is both fletched and barbed . They measured 2 – 3 ft ( 60 – 90 cm ) in length and weighed around 5 lb ( 2 . 5 kg ) . Barbed darts costed 1 gp each . Around 1372 DR , they were often used by lizardfolk .

title: Barber
description: Barber Barbers were rogue s inhabiting the bazaars of Zakhara . Requirements . All types of rogues could be barbers .
description_long: Barber Barbers were rogue s inhabiting the bazaars of Zakhara . Requirements . All types of rogues could be barbers . However , some Moralist ic areas of Zakhara required female barbers to only service other females . Role . Barbers were masters of the street . Elaborate showmen , these rogues possessed quick wits and sharp tongues . Any gold they couldn ' t talk a customer out of could always be stolen by deft hands . These men and women were always a good source of gossip or for obtaining serious information . Possessions . All kinds of equipment were available to barbers , but they almost always had access to a full barbering kit with a sharp razor . Skills . Barbers were adept and figuring out the functions of magical items . Barbers lacked experience in many skills common to other thieves because they had to spend so much time mastering their barbering crafts , sometimes even attending formal classes .

title: Barber Shop of Gorar al - Aksar
description: Barber Shop of Gorar al - Aksar The Barber Shop of Gorar al - Aksar was a prominent fixture of the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . The walls of the barber shop were festooned with astrological charts and graphs .
description_long: Barber Shop of Gorar al - Aksar The Barber Shop of Gorar al - Aksar was a prominent fixture of the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . The walls of the barber shop were festooned with astrological charts and graphs . Gorar al - Aksar owned a unique smoking efreeti bottle that he kept on display near his work area . In addition to being a delightful collector ' s piece , the bottle proved that at least a few of Gorar ' s lavish tales were true . Activities . Gorar ' s shop was always full of customers . The talkative barber gave them their horoscopes whether they wanted one or not . History . As of 1367 DR , the shop had been in the Grand Bazaar for 40 years . Inhabitants . Gorar owned and operated this establishment .

title: Bard
description: Bard Bards were versatile arcane spellcaster s , capable in combat , art , and magic alike . Bards practiced magic as they would art or song , using their artistic talents to induce magical effects that either bolstered their allies or hindered their enemies , typically through charms and illusions . In addition to their magical skills , bards were artistically talented and extraordinarily well - learned , possessing knowledge in a wide range of fields .
description_long: Bard Bards were versatile arcane spellcaster s , capable in combat , art , and magic alike . Bards practiced magic as they would art or song , using their artistic talents to induce magical effects that either bolstered their allies or hindered their enemies , typically through charms and illusions . In addition to their magical skills , bards were artistically talented and extraordinarily well - learned , possessing knowledge in a wide range of fields . Bards were among the most versatile of adventurer s , capable of learning from practically any trade . The most notable of the world ' s bards during the Era of Upheaval were likely Storm Silverhand of the Seven Sisters or Ningal of Unther . Culture . Both literally and figuratively enchanting , bards drew upon , more than perhaps any other profession , the works of all who ' d come before them . Storytellers , musicians , enchanters , dancers , and lorekeepers , bards were prone to wanderlust , traveling from one place to another in search of new lore or perhaps in the hopes of spreading what they already knew .

title: Bardan ruqad
description: Bardan ruqad Bardan ruqad , which translated in Midani as " cold sleep " , was a rare poison . Properties . " Bardan ruqad " was a strong poison capable of instantly paralyzing the victim .
description_long: Bardan ruqad Bardan ruqad , which translated in Midani as " cold sleep " , was a rare poison . Properties . " Bardan ruqad " was a strong poison capable of instantly paralyzing the victim . Victims under the poison ' s effect remained helplessly inert for up to ten minutes . They were completely aware of what was happening to them during this time , after which they fell into a deep slumber that lasted several hours . This poison did not cause any physical harm in the traditional sense . " Bardan ruqad " even worked against all forms of undead , though they were slightly resistant to its effects when initially taking root . Applications . Though rarely encountered outside of their use of the poison , tasked messenger genie s often applied " bardan ruqad " to their darts and daggers . The messenger genies used this to attack dangerous targets from a distance when delivering messages to them , allowing them to paralyze the target and safely deliver the message and escape before the target could retaliate .

title: Bardran Thulmaer
description: Bardran Thulmaer Shield Duke Bardran Thulmaer was the well - loved leader of the town of Alamontyr . Description . He was an aging but large man with a huge white moustache .
description_long: Bardran Thulmaer Shield Duke Bardran Thulmaer was the well - loved leader of the town of Alamontyr . Description . He was an aging but large man with a huge white moustache . He ruled with a conservative fair style , preferring to consult local religious leaders before making political decisions . Background . The forty Griffon Knights were Bardran Thulmaer ' s personal guard and upholders of the peace in Alamontyr . Although the Shield Duke was popular with his people , he had not named a successor , leading to much speculation about who would succeed him .

title: Bardshyr
description: Bardshyr County Bardshyr was a wide stretch of cattle fields and ranches in the Purple Marches of Tethyr and the site of Castle Tethyr before its destruction . Geography . Bardshyr was the northeastern county of the Purple Marches , located south of the Sulduskoon River .
description_long: Bardshyr County Bardshyr was a wide stretch of cattle fields and ranches in the Purple Marches of Tethyr and the site of Castle Tethyr before its destruction . Geography . Bardshyr was the northeastern county of the Purple Marches , located south of the Sulduskoon River . Moving clockwise from the north , it was bordered by Uluran , Ithmonn , Elemetar , and Vintor . The Ithal Road and the Trade Way passed through the county . Government . In 1370 DR , Bardshyr was officially under the leadership of Count Ellem Sunspear I . However , he left control in the hands of his son , Lhorik Sunspear , because the elder Sunspear ' s wife was dying . The county seat was an old keep known as Saharkhan , where the Ithal Road met the Trade Way .

title: Bareris Anskuld
description: Bareris Anskuld Bareris Anskuld was a human bard . . As a bard he worshipped Oghma and Milil .
description_long: Bareris Anskuld Bareris Anskuld was a human bard . . As a bard he worshipped Oghma and Milil . During the war of Thay he was transformed into an undead being . Appearance . Though Bareris was truly Thay an , he stopped shaving the wheat blonde hair from his head . He could move with a duelist ' s catlike grace . During the war of Thay , Bareris began to neglect himself and his personal hygiene and wore a gaunt face and a cold stare . The Dream Vestige ' s Aftermath . During the encounter with Szass Tam ' s dream vestige Bareris absorbed some of the energies of undeath that bound the entity . He now has most abilities of an undead sentient being . His skin and hair turned chalky white and his eyes turned midnight - black . Possessions . Bareris ' s weapon of choice is the sword which he wears at his hip in a worn leather scabbard . He also possesses a silver - stringed yarting slung across his back . and carries a small dagger . Bareris later gives his yarting to a band of gnoll s as fee for their help in his pursuit of Tammith ' s captors . Bardly Magic .

title: Barge House
description: Barge House The Barge House was a large tavern found in Daleport in 1357 DR . Description . Converted from an old warehouse , the Barge House was massive , easily holding 500 occupants at one time .
description_long: Barge House The Barge House was a large tavern found in Daleport in 1357 DR . Description . Converted from an old warehouse , the Barge House was massive , easily holding 500 occupants at one time . Activities . Most of the inhabitants of the small town of Daleport could be found socializing at the Barge House each night . Given the number of smugglers passing through the region , many rare or illegal goods could be purchased here for the right price .

title: Bargewright Inn
description: Bargewright Inn The Bargewright Inn was an important wayside hub for travelers of all sorts located on Jundar ' s Hill overlooking Ironford on the River Dessarin . Geography . To the south of the Bargewright Inn was Goldenfields .
description_long: Bargewright Inn The Bargewright Inn was an important wayside hub for travelers of all sorts located on Jundar ' s Hill overlooking Ironford on the River Dessarin . Geography . To the south of the Bargewright Inn was Goldenfields . Inhabitants . The Lords of Waterdeep and the Harpers both had agents within the Bargewright as the Zhentarim were vying for control of the surrounding area . Despite these power plays the inn remained a haven for travelers from all throughout the North . History . The inn was fortified by Feston Bargewright after numerous attacks from bandits and brigands ; this feat was accomplished with the help of several Waterdhavian merchants .

title: Barghest
description: Barghest Barghests are evil fiendish shapechanger lupines . Physical description . In its normal form , it resembles a goblin - wolf hybrid with monstrous jaws and razor sharp claws .
description_long: Barghest Barghests are evil fiendish shapechanger lupines . Physical description . In its normal form , it resembles a goblin - wolf hybrid with monstrous jaws and razor sharp claws . As whelps , barghests look like common wolves , except for their size and paws . As they grow larger and more powerful , their skin darkens to bluish - red and eventually turns completely blue . A full - grown barghest is about 6 feet ( 180 cm ) long and weighs 180 pounds ( 82 kg ) . A barghest ’ s eyes glow orange when the creature becomes excited . Abilities . While they have a variety of magical powers , barghests are feared for their ability to consume those they slay and absorb their powers . Young barghests cannot attain standing in their society until they have slain and consumed a number of great mortal heroes . Eventually , these monsters shed their skin and transform into a greater barghest . Society . Barghests originate from the plane of Gehenna but are sent to the Prime Material Plane to mature . Once they have reached maturity , they are allowed to return to their native plane . Their method of doing this is gruesome in nature .

title: Barglun Blackbutter
description: Barglun Blackbutter Barglun Blackbutter was the founder of the Blackbutter Inn in Red Larch . Personality . Barglun was a fat and jovial individual who was fondly remembered as a local legend in the village .
description_long: Barglun Blackbutter Barglun Blackbutter was the founder of the Blackbutter Inn in Red Larch . Personality . Barglun was a fat and jovial individual who was fondly remembered as a local legend in the village . History . Around 1358 DR , Barglum was slain by a pack of wolves .

title: Baric Nylef
description: Baric Nylef Baric Nylef was a knight of Tyr in Bryn Shander sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Baric was a member of the Order of the Gauntlet .
description_long: Baric Nylef Baric Nylef was a knight of Tyr in Bryn Shander sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Baric was a member of the Order of the Gauntlet . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Baric went to Bryn Shander to capture the notorious criminal Worvil Forkbeard , rumored to have hidden in the Ten Towns . He posed as a unemployed caravan guard drinking at the Kelvin ' s Comfrort tavern . Baric was at the tavern when giant s attacked the city . Personality . Baric was a true devotee of Tyr . He waited for the day when he would meet his god . In the meantime , he felt that he must clean the world from evil .

title: Barimus Whitehand
description: Barimus Whitehand Barimus Whitehand was a law enforcement officer in the town of Voonlar sometime during the term of Bron Buorstag Hlammythyl , " i . e . " , from about 1355 DR until at least 1372 DR .
description_long: Barimus Whitehand Barimus Whitehand was a law enforcement officer in the town of Voonlar sometime during the term of Bron Buorstag Hlammythyl , " i . e . " , from about 1355 DR until at least 1372 DR . Personality . He did not pursue violence for violence ' s sake , but liked the peace and orderly calm that resulted from force applied appropriately . Abilities . He was proficient with a greatsword , but had no other significant abilities . Possessions . He wore chain mail but he could don plate mail stored in a few caches around town if needed . He carried a two - handed sword , club , and dagger . History . Barimus joined in a fight on the Bron ' s side one night and was offered the position of deputy on the spot . At some point in his career he received some training from the Zhentilar .

title: Barjin
description: Barjin Barjin was a powerful cleric of Talona . Background . Not much is known of Barjin ' s past .
description_long: Barjin Barjin was a powerful cleric of Talona . Background . Not much is known of Barjin ' s past . Once he was a member of an army in Vaasa under a powerful unknown leader ( presumably Zhengyi , the Witch - King ) . Barjin dabbled in sorcery and necromancy and became quite efficient in each skill . Apparently , his leader became a god - like figure , and that is where Barjin first became a cleric . When his leader and his army fell , only he and a few of his soldiers survived . He claimed to have been visited by Talona ' s avatar , and it was she who led him to Castle Trinity . Barjin quickly rose in rank and became the leader of Castle Trinity ' s triumvirate . By this he also became Aballister Bonaduce ' s nemesis . The Most Fatal Horror . Barjin played a great role in Aballister ' s quest of releasing the " Chaos Curse " upon the Edificant Library . The Curse was a potion that brought people to fulfill their most private desires without caution to the consequences resulting thereof . When finished , Aballister named it " The Most Fatal Horror " , a mock name of Barjin ' s title as a cleric of Talona .

title: Barkskin
description: Barkskin Barkskin was a druid evocation and a transmutation or alteration spell that toughened the skin to a bark - like consistency . Effects . " Barkskin " toughened the skin of the creature touched , giving it natural armor .
description_long: Barkskin Barkskin was a druid evocation and a transmutation or alteration spell that toughened the skin to a bark - like consistency . Effects . " Barkskin " toughened the skin of the creature touched , giving it natural armor . In general , the quality of the armor improved the higher the caster ' s power . The " barkskin " evocation drew upon the caster ' s constitution for the strength of the armor — a tougher caster could bestow tougher armor . The spell would not stack with any other effect that increased natural armor . Components . The post Sundering version and some older versions of this spell required some bark from an oak tree in addition to the verbal and somatic components . All versions of the spell ( but not the evocation ) required the use of the caster ' s holy symbol or divine focus . The post Sundering version had no need to focus or symbols .

title: Barlowe
description: Barlowe Barlowe was a male human of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . Activities . Barlowe was the runner of the smuggler ' s warehouse .
description_long: Barlowe Barlowe was a male human of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . Activities . Barlowe was the runner of the smuggler ' s warehouse . History . Barlowe was a member of the thieves guild , who oversaw the transactions of the smuggler ' s warehouse . Gameplay . If the Kalach - Cha and the companions sided with the thieves and have transported weapons to the warehouse , Barlowe would give them a reward before the Watch came to attack the thieves . If the Kalach - Cha and the companions sided with the Watch , then Barlowe would attack them in the warehouse . Once killed , they could take the papers , which contained codes of the suppliers .

title: Barrelstalk
description: Barrelstalk Barrelstalk was a fungus that grew in the Underdark , named for its barrel - like shape . It had a hard , woody outer surface , but the inside was hollow and could contain about 5 to 8 gallons ( 19 to 30 liters ) of potable water . The inner rings of the barrelstalk were made from an edible pulp .
description_long: Barrelstalk Barrelstalk was a fungus that grew in the Underdark , named for its barrel - like shape . It had a hard , woody outer surface , but the inside was hollow and could contain about 5 to 8 gallons ( 19 to 30 liters ) of potable water . The inner rings of the barrelstalk were made from an edible pulp . A typical specimen yielded about 5 to 10 pounds ( 2 . 3 to 4 . 5 kilograms ) of food . Some reports of this fungus said that it was only edible when young . Once matured , it produced spores that were poisonous , making it useless as a source of food and water .

title: Barrelstone Inn
description: Barrelstone Inn The Barrelstone Inn was a low - quality inn run by around twenty jovial gnome s in Marsember , Cormyr in 1367 DR . Location . The inn was situated on the island immediately south of Starwater Keep in the Cormyrian area .
description_long: Barrelstone Inn The Barrelstone Inn was a low - quality inn run by around twenty jovial gnome s in Marsember , Cormyr in 1367 DR . Location . The inn was situated on the island immediately south of Starwater Keep in the Cormyrian area . Structure . The leaky building was infested with vermin and offered poor quality food . The Barrelstone was always cold with mosses crawling around the damp bedchamber walls and mildew leaving a pungent smell throughout the inn . Luckily , the food did not taste like mildew , but it was wet , freezing , and generally disgusting . Inhabitants . The gnomes who ran the Barrelstone were a bright aspect of the crummy inn ; always telling jokes and playing pranks on each other . In the rundown building , the staff was always dancing around and singing good music . The gnomes were also great story tellers and ballad makers , but even their bardic abilities were no match for the awfulness of the Barrelstone Inn .

title: Barrier of retention
description: Barrier of retention Barrier of retention was an abjuration spell that created a temporary containment trap for all creatures in an area . Effects . The area of effect for this spell was a 10 ft ( 3 .
description_long: Barrier of retention Barrier of retention was an abjuration spell that created a temporary containment trap for all creatures in an area . Effects . The area of effect for this spell was a 10 ft ( 3 . 1 m ) cube per level of the caster . These cubes could be used to form any desired rectangular shape . The " barrier of retention " did no harm to those inside or entering the protected area , but prevented them from leaving unless they could resist the spell . This spell also prevented physical attacks ( melee attacks , ranged weapons , hurled objects ) from exiting the area . The " barrier " did not prevent magical attacks from leaving the area , nor any spellcasting within the area , so " magic missile " could hit targets outside the " barrier " and " teleport " could be used to escape it . " Dispel magic " and similar disenchantments could cancel the " barrier " . The caster was free to enter and leave the protected area at will . Components . This spell required a verbal component . For the somatic component , the priest had to walk the perimeter of the desired area while casting the spell . The material component was a small cage made of silver wire .

title: Barriltar Bhandraddon
description: Barriltar Bhandraddon High Priest Barriltar Bhandraddon served as Torm ' s pontiff and ruled from the magnificent Temple of Torm ' s Coming in Tantras . From this place , the pontiff extended Torm ' s reach and worship by sponsoring continent - wide knightly orders , including the prestigious Order of the Golden Lion .
description_long: Barriltar Bhandraddon High Priest Barriltar Bhandraddon served as Torm ' s pontiff and ruled from the magnificent Temple of Torm ' s Coming in Tantras . From this place , the pontiff extended Torm ' s reach and worship by sponsoring continent - wide knightly orders , including the prestigious Order of the Golden Lion .

title: Barroch
description: Barroch Barroch was said to be the first great bandit lord of the Inner Sea lands . He made his lair at Barroch ' s Hold , a fabled citadel in the Glacier of the White Worm . In the Year of the Worm , 1356 DR , a band of adventurers rediscovered Barroch ' s Hold in the Glacier of the White Worm .
description_long: Barroch Barroch was said to be the first great bandit lord of the Inner Sea lands . He made his lair at Barroch ' s Hold , a fabled citadel in the Glacier of the White Worm . In the Year of the Worm , 1356 DR , a band of adventurers rediscovered Barroch ' s Hold in the Glacier of the White Worm . However , they soon ran into a number of strange creatures , and were separated or killed . Appendix . Notes . It is not known when Barroch lived or where exactly in the Inner Sea he operated . The location of his hold suggests the Moonsea or the Vast .

title: Barroch ' s Hold
description: Barroch ' s Hold Barroch ' s Hold was a citadel located on the Glacier of the White Worm in the Earthspur Mountains , and once the fabled lair of Barroch , the first great bandit lord of the Inner Sea . In the Year of the Worm , 1356 DR , a band of adventurers rediscovered Barroch ' s Hold but soon ran into a number of strange creatures , and were separated or killed . Two of them survived — Yostur Ulhmond and Feenoch the Five - Fingered — and made it to Orm to tell their story , though they would not be drawn on the matter of treasure .
description_long: Barroch ' s Hold Barroch ' s Hold was a citadel located on the Glacier of the White Worm in the Earthspur Mountains , and once the fabled lair of Barroch , the first great bandit lord of the Inner Sea . In the Year of the Worm , 1356 DR , a band of adventurers rediscovered Barroch ' s Hold but soon ran into a number of strange creatures , and were separated or killed . Two of them survived — Yostur Ulhmond and Feenoch the Five - Fingered — and made it to Orm to tell their story , though they would not be drawn on the matter of treasure . By the end of the year , it was said in Hillsfar they were trying to muster a larger group of adventurers , bearing sledges , perhaps intending to return .

title: Barrowin Undurr
description: Barrowin Undurr Barrowin Undurr was a devoted dwarf cleric of Gorm Gulthyn . She had a dour outlook on life but would always stand against evil , especially when it moved against dwarvenkind . History .
description_long: Barrowin Undurr Barrowin Undurr was a devoted dwarf cleric of Gorm Gulthyn . She had a dour outlook on life but would always stand against evil , especially when it moved against dwarvenkind . History . Barrowin was born in the area of the Great Rift , and she managed her family ' s business holdings in Ironmaster near Icewind Dale . She spent fifteen years there on assignment in Ironstar . Her life was not exciting enough for her , so she asked her family for relocation . When that request went unheard , she called on her deity to provide a new path . Gorm answered indirectly . Barrowin found a new life , by falling in love with Storn Skulldark , a wealthy young Ironstar dwarf . Barrowin and Storn set out from Ironstar to build a fortress along the route from Neverwinter to Icewind Dale , within the Spine of the World mountain range . The project had many setbacks , chief of which was the sudden disappearance of Storn Skulldark ' s fortune in Ironmaster . Storn traveled back without Barrowin to find his missing gold . During his journey he was attacked and carried off by a white dragon . His fate was unknown . Barrowin was devastated by this loss .

title: Barthelby
description: Barthelby Barthelby was a high - ranking priest of Jergal in Undermountain in 1479 DR . History . In 1479 DR , an omen reveled that some tombs holy to Jergal inside Undermountain had been forgotten and needed to be tended .
description_long: Barthelby Barthelby was a high - ranking priest of Jergal in Undermountain in 1479 DR . History . In 1479 DR , an omen reveled that some tombs holy to Jergal inside Undermountain had been forgotten and needed to be tended . Barthelby led an expedition to Waterdeep in order to rededicate them to Jergal . After a search in Waterdeep ' s libraries , he and his fellows identified the locations of the tombs and entered Undermountain to do their work and also build a shrine to their god . Barthelby was waiting for another priest to relieve him but instead the undead minions of the vampire Dayan attacked . Barthelby barricaded himself inside the shrine . Personality . Like all his fellow priests of Jergal , Barthelby was morose . He believed that one day he would die in a horrible way but tried to not think about it . However , he was very scrupulous in his work .

title: Bartholomew Blackdagger
description: Bartholomew Blackdagger Bartholomew Blackdagger was an undead pirate in service to Garrundar in the Pirate Skyhold north of Neverwinter . History . Bartholomew led a very powerful band of sky pirates .
description_long: Bartholomew Blackdagger Bartholomew Blackdagger was an undead pirate in service to Garrundar in the Pirate Skyhold north of Neverwinter . History . Bartholomew led a very powerful band of sky pirates . Bartholomew Blackdagger and his sky pirates once tried to capture Garrundar but they failed spectacularly and the black dragon pursued them back to their hideout . Garrundar took control of the lizardfolk that lived there and he weaved a powerful spell that cursed the pirates into undeath and bound them . In 1484 DR , Company Yargo , needing a base and more sky ships , sent an adventurer to clear out the area . The adventurer killed Bartholomew before coming to the dragon .

title: Barthus
