description_long: Clan Bukbukken Clan Bukbukken was the name of the clan of Duergar that worshiped Shimmergloom the shadow dragon . Physical description . Like most Duergar , the clan had grey skin and stocky features . Whilst living in Mithral Hall , each clan member could afford to have their own set of mithral armor and weapons . History . When Shimmergloom took control of Mithral Hall , the clan worked under his command mining mithral for almost 200 years . When the Hall was liberated by Bruenor Battlehammer and the Companions of the Hall in 1356 DR , the clan was mostly slain . Those that survived fled back to the Underdark . Known members . There are few names mentioned in the lore , regarding the clan :

title: Clan Delzimmer
description: Clan Delzimmer Clan Delzimmer was a dwarven clan from Delzimmer . The Delzimmer clan ' s Waterdeep townhouse , as of 1374 DR , was an opulent four - storey building on Swords Street , adjacent to Sapphire House . Adjoining to the north was Sablehearth , the Irlingstar mansion .
description_long: Clan Delzimmer Clan Delzimmer was a dwarven clan from Delzimmer . The Delzimmer clan ' s Waterdeep townhouse , as of 1374 DR , was an opulent four - storey building on Swords Street , adjacent to Sapphire House . Adjoining to the north was Sablehearth , the Irlingstar mansion .

title: Clan Duergar
description: Clan Duergar Clan Duergar was a shield dwarf clan of Shanatar whose members were eventually enslaved by the illithid s and became the duergar , a race of gray dwarves . History . The Clan was one of many who splintered off to form a new kingdom in the early days of Shanatar , venerating Laduguer in a strict theocracy , naming it Barakuir .
description_long: Clan Duergar Clan Duergar was a shield dwarf clan of Shanatar whose members were eventually enslaved by the illithid s and became the duergar , a race of gray dwarves . History . The Clan was one of many who splintered off to form a new kingdom in the early days of Shanatar , venerating Laduguer in a strict theocracy , naming it Barakuir . The sub - kingdom held fierce rivalries with neighbouring Drakkalor and Ultoksamrin , which became conflict from about - 9000 DR in the Spawn Wars . Barakuir swore allegiance to Shanatar and the Wyrmskull Throne but Clan Duergar , the ruling clan of the sub - kingdom , became more and more tyrannical , leading more and more dwarves of other clans to flee . During the Mindstalker Wars around - 8100 DR , Barakuir became cut off from the rest of Shanatar , and fell to its illithid conquerers , who enslaved its populace for thousands of years . Eventually , as slaves , the inhabitants transformed into a new dwarven race known as the duergar ( or gray dwarves ) . It rose up and liberated itself around - 4000 DR , spreading out into the Underdark .

title: Clan Forgebar
description: Clan Forgebar Clan Forgebar was a savage dwarven family of around seventy hill dwarves who lived in caves in Mount Galardrym in the Sword Mountains . History . Around 1372 DR , the clan launched three attacks on the nearby gnome settlement of Ieirithymbul , but each time they came close to total elimination due to the gold dragon Palarandusk , the " Unseen Protector " .
description_long: Clan Forgebar Clan Forgebar was a savage dwarven family of around seventy hill dwarves who lived in caves in Mount Galardrym in the Sword Mountains . History . Around 1372 DR , the clan launched three attacks on the nearby gnome settlement of Ieirithymbul , but each time they came close to total elimination due to the gold dragon Palarandusk , the " Unseen Protector " .

title: Clan Hammerhand
description: Clan Hammerhand Clan Hammerhand was a shield dwarf clan of both Ravens Bluff in the Vast , and of Earthfast in the Earthfast Mountains in north Faerûn and the Earthroot region of the Underdark . History . The Hammerhands wee a clan with a long history , being well established in Earthfast of old and in Sarbreen before it fell in the Year of the Bloody Crown , 649 DR .
description_long: Clan Hammerhand Clan Hammerhand was a shield dwarf clan of both Ravens Bluff in the Vast , and of Earthfast in the Earthfast Mountains in north Faerûn and the Earthroot region of the Underdark . History . The Hammerhands wee a clan with a long history , being well established in Earthfast of old and in Sarbreen before it fell in the Year of the Bloody Crown , 649 DR . Though they eventually moved out of Earthfast , they remained in Ravens Bluff , the human city built over the ruins of Sarbreen . Several members of Clan Hammerhand fought in the Horde Wars of the Year of the Turret , 1360 DR , in which the dwarves of war - torn Earthfast also took part . After the war , the Hammerhands decided to resettle in their entirety in Earthfast . This necessitated warring against the local goblinoid s besieging the city . Therefore , two hundred Hammerhands became mercenaries to gain experience and earn money to support their clan . Arriving in the late 1360s DR , the Hammerhands were much - needed reinforcements for Earthfast . Their assistance gave the dwarves there time to fortify the defenses of Alagh Rorncaurak before 1369 DR . Organization .

title: Clan Herlinga
description: Clan Herlinga Clan Herlinga was a dwarven clan who occupied Hagga Shan in the Hordelands . Activities . These red - bearded dwarves lived in caves on the west side of Hagga Shan , which they referred to as the " Glittering Spires .
description_long: Clan Herlinga Clan Herlinga was a dwarven clan who occupied Hagga Shan in the Hordelands . Activities . These red - bearded dwarves lived in caves on the west side of Hagga Shan , which they referred to as the " Glittering Spires . " Since contact between the dwarves and the nomads of the steppe was very rare , the nomads developed superstitions about the " little men . " This was all very amusing to the dwarves , who used it as a bargaining chip or for some harmless practical jokes , further strengthening the superstitions . The Herlinga Clan raised goats which they used to carry goods to trade - meets . History . The Herlinga Clan originally hailed from Sossal , but sailed across Yal Tengri sometime during the 1000s DR to find new lands to settle .

title: Clan Ironeater
description: Clan Ironeater Clan Ironeater was a dwarven clan who spent centuries guarding some of the otherwise empty holds of Illefarn from intruders . History . With the demise of Phalorm in 615 DR the demihuman defenders of that realm were no more .
description_long: Clan Ironeater Clan Ironeater was a dwarven clan who spent centuries guarding some of the otherwise empty holds of Illefarn from intruders . History . With the demise of Phalorm in 615 DR the demihuman defenders of that realm were no more . Casualties had been too high to possibly sustain the realm but the clan of dwarves known as the Ironeaters held on stubbornly to the area underneath Mount Illefarn for many centuries . Circa 1257 DR , Derval Ironeater , the king of the clan at the time , decided that their numbers were no longer sufficient to survive in those tunnels and ordered his clan to the surface where they integrated themselves into the populations of Daggerford , Secomber and Waterdeep In 1354 DR , the elder of Derval ' s younger brothers , Korin Ironaxe , who always disagreed with Derval ' s decision to leave their home , took a force of 32 dwarves and gnome s to resume their anscestral duty after their youngest brother Derwin discovered an anvil , believed to be an altar to Moradin ( though it was actually dedicated to Imix ) - taking it as a sign that Moradin wanted them to reclaim their home .

title: Clan Ironstar
description: Clan Ironstar Clan Ironstar was a dwarven clan whose realm was founded in - 2919 DR beneath Firstpeak , Secondpeak and Thirdpeak , also known as " Ironstar Mountain " , " Northlook " and " Wyrmtongue " . Organization . The clan sign was a white four - pointed star on top of a black anvil .
description_long: Clan Ironstar Clan Ironstar was a dwarven clan whose realm was founded in - 2919 DR beneath Firstpeak , Secondpeak and Thirdpeak , also known as " Ironstar Mountain " , " Northlook " and " Wyrmtongue " . Organization . The clan sign was a white four - pointed star on top of a black anvil . Activities . After abandonment of their realm , Ironstar dwarves could still be found in Evereska , Mintarn , or below Mount Helimbrar . They were alleged to have changed their identities to conceal their status as members of the clan . Possessions . The dwarves constructed mace s from their secret darksteel alloy called Ironstar mace s . Relationships . Ironstar regularly traded with gnome s and halfling s via barges on the River Surbrin which ferried their goods to the Sword Coast for sale . History . In 207 DR , the Ironstar realm was overwhelmed by orc invaders , and the clan fled south led by King Daurvos Frostbeard . Pursued by troll s and orcs , Frostbeard was slain at the Stone Bridge where Moradin appeared and drove the orcs back . After abandonment , the realm could still be reached via Blingdenstone as of around 1370 DR .

title: Clan Karuck
description: Clan Karuck Clan Karuck was a small group of ogrillon s that resided in the Underdark beneath the Spine of the World . History . In 1372 DR , Toogwik Tuk communicated with the clan leader , Grguch , and brought the tribe to the surface .
description_long: Clan Karuck Clan Karuck was a small group of ogrillon s that resided in the Underdark beneath the Spine of the World . History . In 1372 DR , Toogwik Tuk communicated with the clan leader , Grguch , and brought the tribe to the surface . During the campaign , they caused great damage to the Moonwood and also forced the elves themselves to retreat on a number of occasions . They used the elves ' own tactics against them , as the elves believed the orcs were mindless creatures . Although Clan Karuck had forced two retreats , these were not definitive victories , as two pegasus riders watching movements on the forest floor and Tos ' un Armgo aided their escape . Leadership . The clan , as with most orcs , used shamans , with Hakuun being the chief advisor to Grguch . Abilities . The clan were extremely resilient to assault and great tacticians , though whether this was thanks to Grguch or outside influences was unclear .

title: Clan Melairkyn
description: Clan Melairkyn Clan Melairkyn was an ancient dwarven clan of artisans , explorers , and traders . When King Melair I discovered deposits of mithral in the rock beneath Mount Waterdeep in - 1288 DR , the area was rapidly expanded into Melairbode , later known as Undermountain . Their home was under increasing threat from the drow over the course of the centuries , until a huge attack in 34 DR killed King Melair IV , who was their ruler at the time , and forced them deeper into the mountain .
description_long: Clan Melairkyn Clan Melairkyn was an ancient dwarven clan of artisans , explorers , and traders . When King Melair I discovered deposits of mithral in the rock beneath Mount Waterdeep in - 1288 DR , the area was rapidly expanded into Melairbode , later known as Undermountain . Their home was under increasing threat from the drow over the course of the centuries , until a huge attack in 34 DR killed King Melair IV , who was their ruler at the time , and forced them deeper into the mountain . They were driven out of Undermountain in 211 DR . Rumors . Some scholars said that around one hundred dwarves from the Melairkyn clan escaped the final slaughter , fled Undermountain , and ventured west or south . Some claimed that they were involved in the creation of Phalorm , the Fallen Kingdom , yet some maintained that the Melairkyn still populated the depths of Undermountain . Survivors . In actual fact , a tiny number of members of the Melairkyn clan still existed by 1370 DR :

title: Clan Nornglast
description: Clan Nornglast Clan Nornglast was an extinct noble house of Eskorn . History . Clan Nornglast was one of the most prominent clans of Eskorn , and its members were the founders of the " Royal Keep " of the same name .
description_long: Clan Nornglast Clan Nornglast was an extinct noble house of Eskorn . History . Clan Nornglast was one of the most prominent clans of Eskorn , and its members were the founders of the " Royal Keep " of the same name . They had an incredibly fabulous wealth but expended most of it in a secret project nobody knew about it . Eskornar commoners called it the " Nornglast Secret " , as a way to say that the Nornglast were different to other nobles but nobody knew how . Clan Nornglast disappeared many years before the Spellplague .

title: Clan Roaryl
description: Clan Roaryl Clan Roaryl was a noble house of Eskorn , and the ruling dynasty of the kingdom as of 1479 DR . History . Clan Roaryl was founded by the legendary hero Aunglass Roaryl after he defeated the dragon Eskornamundyr .
description_long: Clan Roaryl Clan Roaryl was a noble house of Eskorn , and the ruling dynasty of the kingdom as of 1479 DR . History . Clan Roaryl was founded by the legendary hero Aunglass Roaryl after he defeated the dragon Eskornamundyr . The clan later became the fifth ruling dynasty of Eskorn .

title: Clan Wilddragon
description: Clan Wilddragon Clan Wilddragon was an extinct noble house of Eskorn . History . Clan Wilddragon was one of the dynasties that ruled Eskorn centuries before the Spellplague .
description_long: Clan Wilddragon Clan Wilddragon was an extinct noble house of Eskorn . History . Clan Wilddragon was one of the dynasties that ruled Eskorn centuries before the Spellplague . This clan was very popular in legends and songs , and Eskorn was called the " Wild Dragon Realm " after it . It was believed that Clan Wilddragon was totally exterminated by a rival clan , although some sages and legends claimed that a few descendants of the clan still survived in the 15th century DR , ignorant of their own lineages . Those surviving Wilddragons were accomplished adventurers and outlaws . According to legends , when the Wilddragons returned to the throne , Eskorn would become a prosperous land .

title: Clan Xornbane
description: Clan Xornbane Clan Xornbane was a duergar mercenary band in the Underdark that was led by Khorrl Xornbane . Description . Clan Xornbane consisted of several thousand duergar .
description_long: Clan Xornbane Clan Xornbane was a duergar mercenary band in the Underdark that was led by Khorrl Xornbane . Description . Clan Xornbane consisted of several thousand duergar . When their leader Khorrl entered Ched Nasad in 1372 DR , he counted more than 20 wagons , plus more were coming . At that time , they were equipped with crossbows and stonefire firepots . History . In 1372 DR , Clan Xornbane was hired by the Ched Nasad an drow House Zauvirr through a liaison named Zammzt ( secretly an agent of the Jaezred Chaulssin ) . The band was to fight and destroy House Melarn . However , Zammzt instructed them to attack too early . They successfully killed Matron Mother Drisinil Melarn but House Zauvirr ' s captives escaped and the duergar contributed to the chaos in Ched Nasad that led to its ultimate destruction . Matron Mother Ssipriina Zauvirr attacked Khorrl , killing him ; the band fled the city .

title: Clangeddin Silverbeard
description: Clangeddin Silverbeard Clangeddin Silverbeard , pronounced ( " clan " - gedh - din " sihl " - vur - beard ) , was the dwarven deity of battle and honour in warfare . He was known as the the Father of Battle and the Lord of the Twin Axes . His holy symbol was two crossed battleaxes .
description_long: Clangeddin Silverbeard Clangeddin Silverbeard , pronounced ( " clan " - gedh - din " sihl " - vur - beard ) , was the dwarven deity of battle and honour in warfare . He was known as the the Father of Battle and the Lord of the Twin Axes . His holy symbol was two crossed battleaxes . He delighted in battle , although he did not tolerate treachery or deceit , and he expected his followers to do the same . He and his followers hated giants and trained their fellow dwarves in special ways to fight them . The domains associated with him were : Dwarf , Good , Law , Strength , and War , and his favored weapon was the battleaxe . He was also a lawful good exarch of Moradin . Worshipers . Clangeddin ' s clerics , known as " alaghor " ( " Those who demonstrate valor in battle " ) taught and learnt the art of forging armour and weapons , and practiced military training each day . Though they sought to make their dwarven brethren stronger on the battlefield through their teachings , followers of Clangeddin were often viewed as little more than bloodthirsty barbarians among other races . Clangeddin ' s priests wore silver war helms and chain mail .

title: Clangor
description: Clangor Clangor , also known as Acheron , is a plane of eternal battle . Armies of goblin and kobold petitioners , often led by barghests , clash in struggle , only to be resurrected the following dawn and start the battle again , over and over . It is the home plane of Hruggek , Kurtulmak and Maglubiyet .
description_long: Clangor Clangor , also known as Acheron , is a plane of eternal battle . Armies of goblin and kobold petitioners , often led by barghests , clash in struggle , only to be resurrected the following dawn and start the battle again , over and over . It is the home plane of Hruggek , Kurtulmak and Maglubiyet . Hruggek resides in Hruggekolohk , a warren of caves , inhabited by small villages of hobgoblin petitioners , waging war with the tactics of ambush . Kurtulmak lives in another warren of caves , Draukari . The caves are narrow , short , muddy , and so twisted that it is very easy to get lost and get ambushed by an angry tribe of kobolds . Maglubiyet resides in a fort called Grashmog , the Hearth of Battle . Grashmog serves as a temple and training camp for clerics and warriors . The most feared ones are the Steelbiters , respected for their bond with the fiendish winter wolf mounts . Avalas , also called the Battleplains , is the location of the orc realm of Nishrek and the goblin realm of Clangor . Bane ' s realm , " the Black Bastion " , is also on Avalas . Gilgeam ' s realm Zigguraxus existed here until that god ' s death . Laduguer ' s realm " Hammergrim " is here .

title: Clargannuth ( family )
description: Clargannuth ( family ) The Clargannuth family was a noble house of Gontal , and part of the Twelvefold . They held great political influence in Gontal , specially in Gontal City , where common folk believed the Twelvefold families held uncountable treasures in their manors and vaults , and were the true power behind the throne . They controlled most of the commerce in Gontal , as well as many illegal activities .
description_long: Clargannuth ( family ) The Clargannuth family was a noble house of Gontal , and part of the Twelvefold . They held great political influence in Gontal , specially in Gontal City , where common folk believed the Twelvefold families held uncountable treasures in their manors and vaults , and were the true power behind the throne . They controlled most of the commerce in Gontal , as well as many illegal activities .

title: Clariburnus Tanthul
description: Clariburnus Tanthul Clariburnus Tanthul was one of the Twelve Princes of Shade who led Netheril . In charge of Shadovar operations in New Neverwinter , Clariburnus led the Netherese in an attempt to restore Xinlenal , and the first Mythallar , to Toril . Personality .
description_long: Clariburnus Tanthul Clariburnus Tanthul was one of the Twelve Princes of Shade who led Netheril . In charge of Shadovar operations in New Neverwinter , Clariburnus led the Netherese in an attempt to restore Xinlenal , and the first Mythallar , to Toril . Personality . Despite never showing emotion in his flat , whispering voice or unlined skin , Clairburnus had attained more humanity than any of the other twelve princes . Despite this , Clairburnus is merciless without honour , viewing cheating as a resourceful tactic . When necessary , though , Tanthul can don a facade of charm to mask the dead soul that he is . Abilities . Despite the hyperbole that came with being one of the Princes of Shade , Clariburnus was recognised by those closest to him as a skilled warrior and tactical commander . Possessions . Clariburnus often sported a magic al " + 3 glaive of wounding " . History . Early life . One of the Twelve Princes of Shade , Clairburnus held power in Netheril since before the fall of the First Empire . He soon gained notoriety as the youngest captain in the military of Thultanthar . Return of Netheril .

title: Clarion
description: Clarion Clarion was a male adult silver dragon . History . He helped Queen Dagnabbet of Mithral Hall transport an elite strike team of six dwarven warriors , who were charged with carrying out a mission on behalf of the Lords ' Alliance , to disable the strongholds of cloud giant s that floated throughout the North .
description_long: Clarion Clarion was a male adult silver dragon . History . He helped Queen Dagnabbet of Mithral Hall transport an elite strike team of six dwarven warriors , who were charged with carrying out a mission on behalf of the Lords ' Alliance , to disable the strongholds of cloud giant s that floated throughout the North . Clarion supposedly owed the queen a favor , so he agreed to help the dwarves .

title: Clarity of mind
description: Clarity of mind Clarity of mind was an abjuration spell that warded against spells affecting perception . Effect . The caster granted the subject the insight to defend against spells from the charm ( " charm monster " ) , compulsion ( " dominate animal " ) , or glamer ( " change self " ) subschools of magic .
description_long: Clarity of mind Clarity of mind was an abjuration spell that warded against spells affecting perception . Effect . The caster granted the subject the insight to defend against spells from the charm ( " charm monster " ) , compulsion ( " dominate animal " ) , or glamer ( " change self " ) subschools of magic . " Clarity of mind " also improved the likelyhood of the target striking an opponent that had concealment from a glamer spell ( such as " blur " and " displacement " ) .

title: Clarry
description: Clarry Clarry was a blended wine crafted in Faerûn . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description .
description_long: Clarry Clarry was a blended wine crafted in Faerûn . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description . Clarry was made by blending common table wines with honey and spices . Pink Clarry was used for special occasions . Prices . Clarry could be purchased in the following containers :

title: Claugiyliamatar
description: Claugiyliamatar Claugiyliamatar was a green dragon who tried to influence the politics of Waterdeep and Neverwinter through her own criminal gang . Personality . Claugiyliamatar was always fascinated by powerful elven and human females and the spells that transformed dragon s into humans .
description_long: Claugiyliamatar Claugiyliamatar was a green dragon who tried to influence the politics of Waterdeep and Neverwinter through her own criminal gang . Personality . Claugiyliamatar was always fascinated by powerful elven and human females and the spells that transformed dragon s into humans . Her main aspiration was to be one of those powerful women , living in the hustle and bustle of city life . However , finding a way in which to do so without risking her safety proved problematic . History . Sages believe that Claugiyliamatar arrived in Kryptgarden Forest in 1303 DR and made her lair there in Deeping Cave . She earned the enmity of House Brokengulf when she posed as a silver dragon and offered to rid their grazing lands of herself . Having learned where her payment was waiting , she ate the men guarding it and stole it . She then used more illusions to make it appear that she was fighting with herself , though actually , all she was doing was destroying the fences that secured the Brokengulf ' s animals so that she could eat them later . Finally , she disappeared behind the mountains , altered her appearance to look injured and returned claiming victory .

title: Claw ( kuo - toa )
description: Claw ( kuo - toa ) The Claw was a male half - fiend kuo - toa and the leader of a small sect of kuo - toa in the Shrine of the Claw on the Lake of Shadows . Description . Unlike others of his kind , the Claw ' s teeth protruded from his mouth and his eyes glowed with an unearthly radiance .
description_long: Claw ( kuo - toa ) The Claw was a male half - fiend kuo - toa and the leader of a small sect of kuo - toa in the Shrine of the Claw on the Lake of Shadows . Description . Unlike others of his kind , the Claw ' s teeth protruded from his mouth and his eyes glowed with an unearthly radiance . A row of sharp spines ran down the length of his back , giving the Claw an altogether fearsome appearance . Personality . The Claw was a hateful and boastful creature that could not abide air - breathers or surface - dwellers . The few times he would deign to converse would be to preach death to his opponents or brag of his might . A discerning and patient combatant , however , the Claw would try to lead foes into open water where he could outmaneuver them or call upon his fiend ish kraken ally . Abilities . Trained in the arts of an assassin , the Claw could administer lethal and precise strikes against unprepared enemies . Adept with either the pincer staff of the kuo - toa or a stealthy dagger , the Claw was agile and canny enough to mix and match his fighting style to prey on an opponent ' s weaknesses .

title: Claw ( organization )
description: Claw ( organization ) The Claw were a mercenary company based in Evermoors . Tactics . Usually , the Claw had no true organization , with basic tactics but their regenerative abilities proved to be very effective .
description_long: Claw ( organization ) The Claw were a mercenary company based in Evermoors . Tactics . Usually , the Claw had no true organization , with basic tactics but their regenerative abilities proved to be very effective . Contracts . They charged 1000 gold piece s per month for their services . Leadership . The Claw was a company of troll s directed by four human wizard s directed by four mind flayer s under the leadership of the alhoon Killithor , who ruled as a dictator .

title: Claw Hollow
description: Claw Hollow Claw Hollow was one of the People of the Black Blood hideouts in the Silver Marches . Geography . Claw Hollow was located in the northern reach of the Moonwood .
description_long: Claw Hollow Claw Hollow was one of the People of the Black Blood hideouts in the Silver Marches . Geography . Claw Hollow was located in the northern reach of the Moonwood . This tribe marked its territory with splashes of " blood - wine " , which consisted of both boiled wine and blood of their kills . Around the forest , there were a dozen or shelters belonging to the tribe . Description . The refuge also acted as a rally point . Here , the lycanthropes treated their wounded and sick kin . They also used this place as a safe - zone when the Knights in Silver were out hunting them in the forest . Often , nearly half of the tribe was away from the settlement , busy hunting in the nearby woods . The stronghold of the tribe was built within two rings of stockades , erected around a rocky promontory and a network of underground caverns . The People defended Claw Hollow with crossbows equipped with poisoned darts , javelins and stones . In the bottom of a well , there was a great natural cave , full of junk and feces , where a trapped otyugh dwelt . The otyugh was captured and imprisoned several years before .

title: Claw bracer
description: Claw bracer An orc ish claw bracer is the signature weapon of Luthic . She fights bare - handed with her claws because only the males of the community are allowed to wield a weapon . In passive respect to the Cave Mother , males ignore the use of a claw bracer .
description_long: Claw bracer An orc ish claw bracer is the signature weapon of Luthic . She fights bare - handed with her claws because only the males of the community are allowed to wield a weapon . In passive respect to the Cave Mother , males ignore the use of a claw bracer . Weapon Details . The claw ' s sharp claws are a dangerous slashing weapon . The end of the claws " nails " hook savagely inward into a piercing weapon . The hooked end is generally used for grappling as orc women are not trained in how to fight and typical fights among orc women involve scratching , slapping , hair - pulling , wrestling with minimal punching or weapon play . However if an orc woman is forced to fight , expect it to be an " extremely feral fight . " This is especially true if she is fighting in the defense of her " home " . Special Maneuvers . The claw bracer may be designed to work as a locked gauntlet and have small chains and braces that allow the wearer to attach it to the arm so it cannot be dropped easily . The bracers make it more difficult for the user to be disarmed in combat . Spellcasting , or other delicate skills , were impossible if a claw bracer was locked on the wrist .

title: Claw of Malar
description: Claw of Malar The Claw of Malar was a potent artifact associated with the god Malar the Beastlord . Description . The Claw of Malar was an actual humanoid right hand , with gray skin and long , pointed fingernails .
description_long: Claw of Malar The Claw of Malar was a potent artifact associated with the god Malar the Beastlord . Description . The Claw of Malar was an actual humanoid right hand , with gray skin and long , pointed fingernails . It clutched tightly a clear bauble . The wrist was set into an ornate golden cuff , which was suspended from a cord , enabling it to be worn around the neck . History . The Claw of Malar came into the possession of Pasha Abon Duum of Manshaka , who had made a deal with Malar himself . With its power , he thought he could challenge the power of Tyr , the Just God . Duum wore it on a cord around his neck . However , in the Year of the Prince , 1357 DR , when Duum finally came to Gladsheim to confront Tyr , he was surprised to find the thief Conner instead . The Catlord snatched away the Claw of Malar and passed it to Conner . Ultimately , the real Tyr showed up and took the Claw ; Conner had made a secret deal to bring him the Claw . Duum was left to cower before the god .

title: Claw of the revenancer
description: Claw of the revenancer The claw of the revenancer was an enchanted silver gauntlet that had the distinction of being an artifact of the drow goddess Kiaransalee . It was famously wielded by the high priestess , Irae T ' sarran during the the Silence of Lolth . Description .
description_long: Claw of the revenancer The claw of the revenancer was an enchanted silver gauntlet that had the distinction of being an artifact of the drow goddess Kiaransalee . It was famously wielded by the high priestess , Irae T ' sarran during the the Silence of Lolth . Description . The " claw of the revenancer " was a finely wrought silver gauntlet that wrapped around the hand and forearm of the wearer . It had an delicate bracelet that , by way of an intricate lattice , connected to a set of five silver rings that , in turn , attached over the wearer ' s fingers . Although it appeared as a purely decorative magical item , the " claw " was shaped to also be used as melee weapon and , true to its name , could inflict wounds consistent with a viciously clawed hand . Powers . Uniquely , the " claw of the revenancer " had the combined powers of a magic ring , glove , and bracelet all in one item . The " claw " granted the wearer a great degree of protection ; it had the powers of both a set of " bracers of armor + 5 " and an " amulet of natural armor + 5 " . Additionally , it functioned as a " + 1 gauntlet " in power when used during combat as a " claw " .

title: Clawrift
description: Clawrift The Clawrift was a deep , dark chasm in the center of the drow city of Menzoberranzan . . Description .
description_long: Clawrift The Clawrift was a deep , dark chasm in the center of the drow city of Menzoberranzan . . Description . The Clawrift was a deep , claw - shaped rift in the center of the city . Its various deep valleys were described as " fingers . " The widest and deepest part of the Clawrift was called the " thumb " of the Clawrift . House Oblodra ' s kobold slaves were housed in pens and extensive tunnels and walkways that extended deep into the Clawrift . The Clawrift was surrounded by the district of Duthcloim . Locations . Until 1358 DR , House Oblodra ' s compound clung to a cliff face between the two " fingers " of the Clawrift . Its compound was small but protected on three sides by the Clawrift and guarded by soldiers on the other side . After the house ' s fall in 1358 DR , only ruins of the compound remained . The chasm was home to the mercenary band Bregan D ' aerthe ' s secret headquarters in Menzoberranzan . The Cathlyre was an exotic bird aviary situated against the stalactites of the Clawrift ' s eastern perimeter . Activity . The depths of the Clawrift and its central location meant that it was a ready location for many dangerous pastimes in the city .

title: Claws of Malar
description: Claws of Malar Claws of Malar were unique claw bracer s that belonged to followers of Malar and were used in ritualistic hunts , ceremonies , and as personal weapons . Description . Typically created by the carrier , they were fashioned to mimic clawed beast paws , such as lion , tiger , or bear .
description_long: Claws of Malar Claws of Malar were unique claw bracer s that belonged to followers of Malar and were used in ritualistic hunts , ceremonies , and as personal weapons . Description . Typically created by the carrier , they were fashioned to mimic clawed beast paws , such as lion , tiger , or bear . Powers . They were " + 1 wounding claw bracers .

title: Claws of the savage
description: Claws of the savage Claws of the savage is a transmutation spell that replaces the touched creature ' s hands with sickle - like claws . Effect . The caster grants one creature two long claws that replace its hands , tentacle tips , or whatever else is appropriate .
description_long: Claws of the savage Claws of the savage is a transmutation spell that replaces the touched creature ' s hands with sickle - like claws . Effect . The caster grants one creature two long claws that replace its hands , tentacle tips , or whatever else is appropriate . The claws deal damage based on the creature ’ s size . The creature can make attacks with both claws as if it were proficient with them . Just as with a creature that has natural weapons , the subject takes no penalty for making two claw attacks . The subject is treated as armed . Furthermore , these claws ' damage and ability to strike targets are boosted . If the creature already has claws , those claws gain a similar enhancement on damage and hit potential bonus on attack and damage rolls , and the claws ’ damage increases as if the creature were two size categories larger .

title: Clay golem
description: Clay golem Clay golems were human - shaped construct s modeled out of clay that were usually divinely infused with a spirit from the Elemental Plane of Earth by priests . Since clay was a weak vessel for life , damaged clay golems tended to release the spirit bound to them and would go berserk until completely destroyed or repaired .
description_long: Clay golem Clay golems were human - shaped construct s modeled out of clay that were usually divinely infused with a spirit from the Elemental Plane of Earth by priests . Since clay was a weak vessel for life , damaged clay golems tended to release the spirit bound to them and would go berserk until completely destroyed or repaired .

title: Clayton Emery
description: Clayton Emery Clayton Emery has been a blacksmith , a dishwasher , a schoolteacher in Australia , a carpenter , a zookeeper , a farmhand , a land surveyor , and a volunteer firefighter , among other things . He was an award - winning technical writer for ten years . His novels include " Tales of Robin Hood " ; " Shadow World # 1 : The Burning Goddess " and " Shadow World # 3 : City of Assassins " ; the Whispering Woods trilogy for " Magic : The Gathering " ; the Robin & Marian stories in Ellery Queen ' s " Mystery Magazine " , and other works .
description_long: Clayton Emery Clayton Emery has been a blacksmith , a dishwasher , a schoolteacher in Australia , a carpenter , a zookeeper , a farmhand , a land surveyor , and a volunteer firefighter , among other things . He was an award - winning technical writer for ten years . His novels include " Tales of Robin Hood " ; " Shadow World # 1 : The Burning Goddess " and " Shadow World # 3 : City of Assassins " ; the Whispering Woods trilogy for " Magic : The Gathering " ; the Robin & Marian stories in Ellery Queen ' s " Mystery Magazine " , and other works . He lives in New Hampshire with his wife and son , and has played the Dungeons & Dragons game since forever .

title: Cleanse water
description: Cleanse water Cleanse water was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell purified a body of water , removing all poisons , toxins , salt , or any other unpleasant or armful effects .
description_long: Cleanse water Cleanse water was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell purified a body of water , removing all poisons , toxins , salt , or any other unpleasant or armful effects . This spell could even turn a magical potion into regular water . Wizards with more power were able to affect larger bodies of water . Once cast , the effects of the spell were permanent for the target body of water . However , this did not prevent the water from being contaminated again in the future . The reverse of this spell , " pollute water " , had the exact opposite effect , contaminating the water with a strong poison . Components . This spell required a handful of sand tainted with a drop of the caster ' blood to cast .

title: Clear Whirl River
description: Clear Whirl River The Clear Whirl River was the major river of the kingdom of Hartsvale . Description . The river was cold and often full of ice .
description_long: Clear Whirl River The Clear Whirl River was the major river of the kingdom of Hartsvale . Description . The river was cold and often full of ice . On an island in the middle of the river was located Castle Hartwick , from which the monarch of Hartsvale ruled . Geography . The river began in two separate forks in the hills between the Ice Mountains and the Ice Spires . The eastern fork started at Lake Woe . Once the forks came together , the river flowed north through Hartsvale . It continued flowing north until it emptied into the Endless Ice Sea after passing through Storming Gorge . Wyrm River was one of its tributaries .

title: Clear path
description: Clear path Clear path was an alteration spell that cleared a corridor in front of the caster as he or she traveled through rough terrain . The reverse of this spell , called clutter path , obfuscated the terrain behind the caster , covering any tracks . Effects .
description_long: Clear path Clear path was an alteration spell that cleared a corridor in front of the caster as he or she traveled through rough terrain . The reverse of this spell , called clutter path , obfuscated the terrain behind the caster , covering any tracks . Effects . This spell operated in natural environments that were considered rough terrain , such as jungles , forests , rocky terrain , or snow . It was not able to clear natural hazards such as lava or quicksand and had no effect on bodies of water . Structures and handmade barriers or magically created terrain were also immune to this spell . As the caster moved forward , a path 10 ft ( 3 m ) wide was cleared of weeds , vines , stones , underbrush , snow and ice , or other such impediments to travel for 10 ft ( 3 m ) in front of the caster . This created a continuous path as long as the caster continued moving forward . " Clear path " lasted for a number of hours and more experienced casters could extend it for more hours . Note that tracking the passage of the caster was child ' s play as the created path was quite obvious .

title: Clearflow River
description: Clearflow River The Clearflow River was located in the Hordelands near the Lake of Mists . Geography . The Clearflow River flowed south from the Lake of Mists across the Great Amber Steppes until it connected with the River Murghol .
description_long: Clearflow River The Clearflow River was located in the Hordelands near the Lake of Mists . Geography . The Clearflow River flowed south from the Lake of Mists across the Great Amber Steppes until it connected with the River Murghol . History . The western bank of the Clearflow River was considered by many to be the edge of civilized lands before the vast expanse of the barbarian Hordelands . The threat of the nomadic barbarians , as well as possible reprisals from neighboring nations in reaction to the defenses that would be needed to defend the river , kept farming and development along the Clearflow River to a minimum .

title: Clearlight
description: Clearlight The Clearlight temple was a run - down temple of Tymora in Luskan . The temple took its name from the large stained glass window in the roof which , as of 1480 DR , was the only know glass window remaining in Luskan . The temple was used as the headquarters of the Coin Spinners gang and was heavily reinforced so that it resembled a fortress and the complex was heavily guarded .
description_long: Clearlight The Clearlight temple was a run - down temple of Tymora in Luskan . The temple took its name from the large stained glass window in the roof which , as of 1480 DR , was the only know glass window remaining in Luskan . The temple was used as the headquarters of the Coin Spinners gang and was heavily reinforced so that it resembled a fortress and the complex was heavily guarded . Most of the statuary had been removed but the idol of Tymora near the altar was more or less intact and the coin - shaped altar remained . The room leading to the inner sanctum occupied by Eden of the Clearlight was heavily trapped .

title: Cleiophane
description: Cleiophane Cleiophane ( sometimes misspelled as " clelophane " ) was a variety of ( also known as or ) that often yielded large specimens of gemstone quality . Description . Sphalerite was a mineral that occurred in crystals of yellow , orange , red , and brown .
description_long: Cleiophane Cleiophane ( sometimes misspelled as " clelophane " ) was a variety of ( also known as or ) that often yielded large specimens of gemstone quality . Description . Sphalerite was a mineral that occurred in crystals of yellow , orange , red , and brown . Cleiophane was sphalerite with pale green " flash " that made beautiful , semi - precious stones , often in unusually large sizes up to 3 inches ( 8 centimeters ) across . Unfortunately , cleiophane was not hard enough to be used in jewelry that was subject to shock or wear . A typical stone had a base value of 50 gp . Powers . This gemstone had the remarkable ability to capture a three - dimensional mental image of the bearer and his or her surroundings out to a spherical radius of ten feet ( three meters ) . The cleiophane gem had to be touched , worn , or carried by the subject when a spell of any type was cast by or on the subject . When these conditions were met , it was likely that a new image of that moment either was added to other images stored in the gem , or ( more probably ) replaced all previously stored images . This power was known as the " echo effect " .

title: Cleric
description: Cleric A cleric was a divine servant of one or more gods , serving them with martial might and divine magic fueled by their own strength of faith . As agents of a divine authority , clerics were empowered both by ritual training and their god ' s particular favor . Relatively rare , clerics inspired both reverence and terror , depending on their aims and who they serve .
description_long: Cleric A cleric was a divine servant of one or more gods , serving them with martial might and divine magic fueled by their own strength of faith . As agents of a divine authority , clerics were empowered both by ritual training and their god ' s particular favor . Relatively rare , clerics inspired both reverence and terror , depending on their aims and who they serve . Perhaps the best known — and most infamous — cleric on Toril was Fzoul Chembryl before his ascension to god hood . Other well - known clerics were Cadderly Bonaduce , a Chosen of Deneir , and Qilue Veladorn , one of the Seven Sisters and a cleric of Eilistraee . Culture . Religion was deeply important to the majority of people on Toril , who felt that the gods were a very real and active presence in their lives , something that was not very far from the truth . For this reason , serving the gods was something that most people did as just a regular part of their lives . Clerics were elite agents of gods , empowered beyond the capabilities of regular priest s and sworn to follow and obey the tenets of their religion in ways that the average mortal couldn ' t .

title: Cli lyre
description: Cli lyre A Cli lyre was a masterwork magic lyre and one of the Instruments of the Bards . Description . " Cli lyres " were superior in every way to ordinary lyres .
description_long: Cli lyre A Cli lyre was a masterwork magic lyre and one of the Instruments of the Bards . Description . " Cli lyres " were superior in every way to ordinary lyres . Like other Instruments of the Bards , they could only be used properly by bard s , and could be dangerous if anyone else attempted to play or even carry them . Powers . Bards wielding a " Cli lyre " had their charming abilities greatly amplified by their magic . Like all Instruments of the Bards , these lyres had the capability of storing spells . A bard playing a " Cli lyre " could invoke the spells " Fly " , " Invisibility " , " Levitate " , " Protection from evil and good " , " Stone shape " , " Wall of fire " and " Wind wall " each once a day , until the instrument recharged its magic at the next dawn . History . The first " Cli lyres " were created by a legendary bard in the Moonshae Isles named Falataer . He used them to test and reward the students of the Cli level of his bardic college , which came to be regarded individually as a legendary bard college in its own right . Over time , other bards have copied the original design , while retaining the original name in Falataer ' s honor .

title: Clicking Heels
description: Clicking Heels Clicking Heels was a hamlet on the southern slopes of the Spine of the World , northeast of Mithral Hall . Description . It consisted of a cluster of houses surrounded by a piled stone wall .
description_long: Clicking Heels Clicking Heels was a hamlet on the southern slopes of the Spine of the World , northeast of Mithral Hall . Description . It consisted of a cluster of houses surrounded by a piled stone wall . Inhabitants . Its population was two hundred humans in 1370 DR . The settlement was home to one unnamed cleric who possessed little in the way of healing magic . History . Tred McKnuckles and Nikwillig stumbled upon Clicking Heels when Tred was injured , and its inhabitants allowed them to rest there for more than a tenday . Clicking Heels was later attacked and razed by a force of frost giant s and worg - riding orc s in 1370 DR , about a tenday after the departure of Tred and Nikwillig .

title: Cliffs of Leaping Horses
description: Cliffs of Leaping Horses The Cliffs of Leaping Horses were a series of plains and hills located in northern Mulhorand . The region was known for its large equine population . Geography .
description_long: Cliffs of Leaping Horses The Cliffs of Leaping Horses were a series of plains and hills located in northern Mulhorand . The region was known for its large equine population . Geography . Rising several hundred feet above sea level lay the lands known as the Cliffs of Leaping Horses . This arid region extended to the Alamber Sea , where caves were commonly found along the coastline . Inhabitants . No true humanoid settlements were found in this region , though outposts existed where individuals captured and trained the horses that gave the area its name . Also , the caves along the coast were known to shelter pirates that sailed the Alamber Sea . The Cliffs of Leaping Horses were also known to be home to significant hippogriff and griffon populations .

title: Cliffs of Tanghai
description: Cliffs of Tanghai The Cliffs of Tanghai were a series of cliffs or bluffs beside the Hungtse River in Shou Lung . Inscribed with the teachings of the Path of Enlightenment by the Celestial Emperor himself , they were a holy site of the faith and the surest evidence of the existence of the Celestial Heaven . Geography .
description_long: Cliffs of Tanghai The Cliffs of Tanghai were a series of cliffs or bluffs beside the Hungtse River in Shou Lung . Inscribed with the teachings of the Path of Enlightenment by the Celestial Emperor himself , they were a holy site of the faith and the surest evidence of the existence of the Celestial Heaven . Geography . The Cliffs of Tanghai overlooked the mouth of the Hungste River near Taitun , where the Upper Hungste River and another river flowed into the main Hungste River . They comprised a huge cliff of black basalt and sheer bluffs of granite . Description . The letters of the inscriptions each stood a full meter high ( 3 . 3 feet ) and were carved into the solid stone . They were carved along the cliff ' s outer face , and were so high above the ground they could only be reached via flight . History . It was believed that the Celestial Emperor caused red - hued lighting to rain from the heavens and blast the letters into the face of the Cliffs of Tanghai in Shou Year 440 ( −810 DR ) , in order that mortals be reminded of his will for all time .

title: Cliffside Cranny
description: Cliffside Cranny The Cliffside Cranny was a hole in Luskan ' s wall created by an earthquake that occurred around 1460 DR . The cranny was assessable by foot or boat and served as an unofficial city gate . In 1480 DR the cranny was guarded by Waterdavian guardsmen assigned to keep plague victims from leaving Luskan .
description_long: Cliffside Cranny The Cliffside Cranny was a hole in Luskan ' s wall created by an earthquake that occurred around 1460 DR . The cranny was assessable by foot or boat and served as an unofficial city gate . In 1480 DR the cranny was guarded by Waterdavian guardsmen assigned to keep plague victims from leaving Luskan .

title: Climbing irons
description: Climbing irons Climbing irons were leg attachments used to make climbing wooden surfaces easier . Uses . Climbing irons were metal rods that attached to the lower leg .
description_long: Climbing irons Climbing irons were leg attachments used to make climbing wooden surfaces easier . Uses . Climbing irons were metal rods that attached to the lower leg . A barbed ankle spike could be forced into a tree or wooden structure while climbing to ensure a steady platform for the feet . Many rogue s used these to scale wooden building in cities . The drawback of using climbing irons is that the wearers movement speed while on flat land was reduced by roughly 1 / 4 .

title: Cloak Wood
description: Cloak Wood Cloak Wood , also stylized as Cloakwood , was an ancient , thickly grown forest in the Western Heartlands region on the south end of the Sword Coast . Description . Cloak Wood was a thickly overgrown ancient forest .
description_long: Cloak Wood Cloak Wood , also stylized as Cloakwood , was an ancient , thickly grown forest in the Western Heartlands region on the south end of the Sword Coast . Description . Cloak Wood was a thickly overgrown ancient forest . The forest was full of elm , breech , felsul , and hiexel trees . The forest had a rugged landscape with many stream - cut ravines shaded by tall specimens of beech , elm , and white pine . Unlike the cliffs to the north , Cloak Wood ' s shoreline theoretically allowed a ship to moor and send a small boat to shore for water and supplies . In practice , only desperate mariners dared the wood ' s population of giant spider s , quickling s , satyr s , stirge s , korred s , hangman tree s , and other uncommon creatures . The sages of nearby Candlekeep asserted that Cloak Wood contained portal s to several other parts of the cosmos . As of 1479 DR , however , these portals were believed to be defunct . History . In 1376 DR , Cloak Wood was the base of operations of the Red Fang Marauders . It also housed their main base , Felldane Manor .

title: Cloak from undead
description: Cloak from undead Cloak from undead was an alteration spell that made one individual invisible to the undead . Effects . Similar to the priest spell " invisibility to undead " , the affected person or creature could move and operate with impunity near undead , as long as they took no hostile action , including attempts to turn them .
description_long: Cloak from undead Cloak from undead was an alteration spell that made one individual invisible to the undead . Effects . Similar to the priest spell " invisibility to undead " , the affected person or creature could move and operate with impunity near undead , as long as they took no hostile action , including attempts to turn them . If an attack was made by a cloaked creature , only the target undead noticed — the spell was not broken for other undead nearby . This spell worked flawlessly every time on lower - level undead , but less often against the more powerful . No vampire was ever known to be fooled by this spell . Components . The spell required verbal , somatic , and material components , including a pinch of powedered silver and a piece of bone . History . This spell was in general use around Faerûn , once it was published in Volo ' s Guide to All Things Magical .

title: Cloak of Gathering Shadows
description: Cloak of Gathering Shadows The Cloak of Gathering Shadows was a ritual used by sha ' ir s to grant their gen the ability to hide within shadows with ease . Preparation . This ritual required a spider web found beneath the shadow of a rock .
description_long: Cloak of Gathering Shadows The Cloak of Gathering Shadows was a ritual used by sha ' ir s to grant their gen the ability to hide within shadows with ease . Preparation . This ritual required a spider web found beneath the shadow of a rock . The web needed to at least be large enough to cover the upper body of the gen . Additionally , the ritual needed the hair of a stealthy individual , typically a holy slayer or skilled thief . The spider web was fixed to the gen ' s back during the 18 hour ritual , granting the gen the ability to hide in the shadows like a skilled thief . The chance of hiding was increased if a more skilled sha ' ir completed the ritual .

title: Cloak of bravery
description: Cloak of bravery Cloak of bravery was a divine conjuration spell that protected up to four creatures from all forms of fear . The reverse of this spell , known as cloak of fear , gave one creature an aura of fear . Effects .
description_long: Cloak of bravery Cloak of bravery was a divine conjuration spell that protected up to four creatures from all forms of fear . The reverse of this spell , known as cloak of fear , gave one creature an aura of fear . Effects . " Cloak of bravery " could be cast on one to four creatures , although the fewer the targets , the better the protection . This was a one - use spell , that lasted up to eight hours or until the subject was exposed to a " fear " effect , which ever occurred first . This spell gave an increased chance to resist " scare " , " fear " , " emotion " , the fear aura of dragons , " etc . " " Cloak of fear " could only be applied to one creature and it surrounded the target with an aura of fear out to a radius of 3 ft ( 0 . 9 m ) . The recipient could choose to turn off and on this aura at will , but the effect could only be used once . If not used before eight hours had passed , then the spell expired . All creatures that entered the circle of fear and did not resist the magic of this spell fled in panic ( possibly dropping whatever they were holding ) for up to 16 minutes . Undead creatures were not affected by this spell . Components .

title: Cloak of chaos
description: Cloak of chaos Cloak of chaos was an abjuration spell that granted magical armor and magical resistance . Effect . A random pattern of color surrounded the subjects , protecting them from attacks , granting them resistance to spells cast by lawful creatures , and confusing lawful creatures when they struck the subjects .
description_long: Cloak of chaos Cloak of chaos was an abjuration spell that granted magical armor and magical resistance . Effect . A random pattern of color surrounded the subjects , protecting them from attacks , granting them resistance to spells cast by lawful creatures , and confusing lawful creatures when they struck the subjects . This abjuration had four effects : First , the warded creatures gained magical armor and resistance . Unlike " protection from law " , this benefit applied against all attacks , not just against attacks by lawful creatures . Second , the warded creatures gained spell resistance against lawful spells and spells cast by lawful creatures . Third , the abjuration blocked possession and mental influence , just as " protection from law " did . Finally , if a lawful creature succeeded with a melee attack against a warded creature , the offending attacker was momentarily confused unless he or she had the willpower to prevent it . Focus . A tiny reliquary containing some sacred relic , such as a scrap of parchment from a chaotic text . The reliquary cost at least 500 gp .

title: Cloak of dark power
description: Cloak of dark power Cloak of dark power was an abjuration spell unique to cleric s with the Drow domain . It created a haze around the subject to counteract the effects of sunlight on the drow . Effect .
description_long: Cloak of dark power Cloak of dark power was an abjuration spell unique to cleric s with the Drow domain . It created a haze around the subject to counteract the effects of sunlight on the drow . Effect . " Cloak of dark power " created a dusky haze around the subject . The haze did not interfere with vision , but the subject and anything he or she wore or carried was protected from the effects of full sunlight , even under the open , daytime sky of the surface world . A drow subject suffered no blindness or bright - light combat penalties while under the effects of a " cloak of dark power " .

title: Cloak of elvenkind
description: Cloak of elvenkind A cloak of elvenkind was a magical item that granted increased powers of stealth . The " jellaba of concealment " functioned in the same manner as a " cloak of elvenkind " . This magical robe originated in Zakhara .
description_long: Cloak of elvenkind A cloak of elvenkind was a magical item that granted increased powers of stealth . The " jellaba of concealment " functioned in the same manner as a " cloak of elvenkind " . This magical robe originated in Zakhara . Description . A " cloak of elvenkind " was an ordinary - looking cloak , and gray in color . Powers . When the hood was drawn over the wearer ' s head , it increased the wearer ' s ability to hide . Creation . The creator of a " cloak of elvenkind " had to be an elf and had to know the spell " invisibility " .

title: Cloak of the crow
description: Cloak of the crow The cloak of the crow was an enchanted cloak worn by Dahlia Sin ' felle . Physcial description . The " cloak of the crow " was a high - collared black cape that could transform its wear into a giant crow .
description_long: Cloak of the crow The cloak of the crow was an enchanted cloak worn by Dahlia Sin ' felle . Physcial description . The " cloak of the crow " was a high - collared black cape that could transform its wear into a giant crow . Powers . The " cloak of the crow " was also reputed to affect changes to its bearer . When worn by Kensidan the " cloak of the crow " made the man appear more bird like , giving him a awkward gait , stiff legged walk , and long , hooked nose . History . The " cloak of the crow " was worn by Kensidan the Crow , of Ship Rethnor . In the year 1451 DR , the " cloak of the crow " was wore by Borlann , the grandson of Kensidan . Following the death of Borlann , Sylora Salm became the wearer of the " cloak of the crow " . In the year 1463 DR , Dahlia Sin ' felle took possession of the " cloak of the crow " after her and her companions Drizzt Do ' Urden and Barrabus the Gray defeated Sylora Salm .

title: Cloak undead
description: Cloak undead Cloak undead was a necromancy or divination spell that made all undead within a certain radius invisible . The earliest version of this spell could be cast in reverse as " detect undead " . Effects .
description_long: Cloak undead Cloak undead was a necromancy or divination spell that made all undead within a certain radius invisible . The earliest version of this spell could be cast in reverse as " detect undead " . Effects . The earliest version of this spell had a radius of 10 ft ( 3 m ) per experience level of the caster and was centered on ( and moved with ) the caster . The later version of " cloak undead " had a fixed radius of 15 ft ( 4 . 6 m ) but could be set on an object or willing creature and moved with the focus for the duration of the spell . This spell prevented " detect undead " but not " detect invisible " or any form of " true seeing " . Undead that were cloaked from a cleric could not be turned unless the cleric could detect them somehow . Undead straying beyond the effective radius or attacking in any fashion immediately became visible . This spell did not allow undead to enter areas that were warded against undead . Components . The spell required only verbal and somatic components . History . This spell was generally known around Faerûn , once it had been published in Volo ' s Guide to All Things Magical .

title: Cloaked sniper
description: Cloaked sniper Cloaked snipers are a variety of rogue s who specialize in making highly accurate , long - ranged strikes . Prized by kings and kingpins alike , cloaked snipers are adept at slaying their enemies with little risk of retaliation . Through stealth and deadly accuracy , cloaked snipers , wielding their favored crossbow s , are sometimes as valuable as a company of lesser archers .
description_long: Cloaked sniper Cloaked snipers are a variety of rogue s who specialize in making highly accurate , long - ranged strikes . Prized by kings and kingpins alike , cloaked snipers are adept at slaying their enemies with little risk of retaliation . Through stealth and deadly accuracy , cloaked snipers , wielding their favored crossbow s , are sometimes as valuable as a company of lesser archers . Though they have a long tradition of excellence amongst dwarves , cloaked snipers belong to no one culture or organization , instead coming from all backgrounds . A cloaked sniper is as likely to serve a general as he is a pirate . What unites cloaked snipers is not a shared allegiance or philosophy , but a skill set they all share . Experts at dealing damage from afar , cloaked snipers prefer to fire from a hidden location , safe from reprisal . Cloaked snipers are not completely adverse to close ranged combat , however , and are experts at laying ambushes as well as at putting good reconnaissance to use . Abilities . Cloaked snipers , much like sharpshooter s , prefer the expert use of little ammo to peppering their enemies .

title: Cloaker
description: Cloaker Cloakers were intelligent creatures that dwelt underground and resembled large flying manta rays when active . At rest , they looked like a black cloak , hence their name . Although they were usually found in a flock of twelve or fewer individuals , they were thought to have built the Underdark city Ikemmu Cloakers often waited in ambush for their prey and generally attempted to engulf an opponent with their wings .
description_long: Cloaker Cloakers were intelligent creatures that dwelt underground and resembled large flying manta rays when active . At rest , they looked like a black cloak , hence their name . Although they were usually found in a flock of twelve or fewer individuals , they were thought to have built the Underdark city Ikemmu Cloakers often waited in ambush for their prey and generally attempted to engulf an opponent with their wings . They also had the ability to emit a subsonic moan which caused fear or nausea in opponents and could shift shadows to conceal themselves or create a mirror image . Notes . Cloakers were strange and mysterious aberrations that lived in the dark and shadowed places of the world . They often made their home in the realm below the surface of the world , where they could use their abilities to manipulate shadows and produce terrifying moans to their greatest effect . Much like their namesake , cloakers appeared to be cloak - shaped creatures . When unfurled their bodies resembled a manta ray , but when relaxed , they appeared to be a black cloak . The ivory talons at the ends of their wings even appeared to be clasps .

title: Cloaker Wars
description: Cloaker Wars The Cloaker Wars occurred around - 10800 DR when Taark Shanat ' s dwarves ( migrating west from Bhaerynden ) engaged the inhabitants of Rringlor Noroth . This included four blue dragons occupying the Rift of Dhalnadar who were all slain by Taark , bringing a victory for the dwarves . Alatorin and its famous Brightaxe Hall was established on this site .
description_long: Cloaker Wars The Cloaker Wars occurred around - 10800 DR when Taark Shanat ' s dwarves ( migrating west from Bhaerynden ) engaged the inhabitants of Rringlor Noroth . This included four blue dragons occupying the Rift of Dhalnadar who were all slain by Taark , bringing a victory for the dwarves . Alatorin and its famous Brightaxe Hall was established on this site . The founding of Alatorin is regarded by shield dwarves as the start of the First Great Age of Shanatar . The skulls of the four dragons were brought together with a throne that emerged from the floor of the cavern ( which was by then Brightaxe Hall ) , by a deity who was probably Dumathoin , and this created the Wyrmskull Throne .

title: Clockwork mage
description: Clockwork mage Clockwork mages , or mechanicians were unique wizard s in Zakhara who focused on building magical constructs instead of practicing traditional spellcraft . Requirements . Clockwork mages not only had to possess high intelligence , but they also needed to be gifted with dextrous fingers to manipulate the fine workings of their machines .
description_long: Clockwork mage Clockwork mages , or mechanicians were unique wizard s in Zakhara who focused on building magical constructs instead of practicing traditional spellcraft . Requirements . Clockwork mages not only had to possess high intelligence , but they also needed to be gifted with dextrous fingers to manipulate the fine workings of their machines . Role . Mechanicians were viewed with mixed feelings of mockery and awe by most other mages for their ability to create wondrous things . Many commoners thought of them as little more than toy - makers . Some mechanicians even encouraged this view in order to hide their true work . Possessions . These mages could use normal weapons like other wizards , but they were also adept with using hammers . They never wore armor . Benefits . Clockwork mages were able to construct machines called clockwork device s that were imbued with spell - like powers . The limit of the kind of machines they built , and their function , was up to the clockwork mage ' s imagination , available time , and monetary funding . Hindrances . Mechanicians could not cast spells like other wizards .

title: Cloister of St . Uzurr
description: Cloister of St . Uzurr The Cloister of St . Uzurr was a temple of Ilmater that lay at the heart of city of Uzurr in Lapaliiya and was home to the Order of St .
description_long: Cloister of St . Uzurr The Cloister of St . Uzurr was a temple of Ilmater that lay at the heart of city of Uzurr in Lapaliiya and was home to the Order of St . Uzurr . History . It was founded during the time of the Shoon Imperium ( 27 – 450 DR ) , when Ilmatari missionaries of the Order of St . Uzurr traveled from Calimshan to Lapaliiya . On a hilltop west of the Lapal Way , they constructed a walled monastery with a cloister , named the Cloister of St . Uzurr after their patron saint . In the following centuries , a city grew up around the monastery , which became known simply as " Uzurr " . A member of the Order was a spy working for the yuan - ti House Eselemas and reported on Kadar ' s research into curing tainted one s and broodguard s . In response , yuan - ti pureblood s began infiltrating Uzurr on Eleasias 1 , the Year of Rogue Dragons , 1373 DR , with the aim of assassinating Kadar . Organization . Both the monastery and the city were governed by the Abbot of St . Uzurr . " Circa " 1372 DR , this was Abbot Kadar al Ilmater . Activities . The Order , Cloister , and city cultivated , produced and exported olive s , wine s , and assorted spice s to support themselves .

title: Clone
description: Clone Clone was a necromancy spell that created a clone of a creature . Effect . The " clone " spell effectively made a dormant clone from a 1 cubic inch of flesh in 120 days within an appropriately sized container .
description_long: Clone Clone was a necromancy spell that created a clone of a creature . Effect . The " clone " spell effectively made a dormant clone from a 1 cubic inch of flesh in 120 days within an appropriately sized container . The creature could be made younger then the original and would remain dormant until the soul of the original was free and willing to return . It was only after the 120 days that the clone matured and then could be able to take the soul . The clone had all the memories and abilities of the original but none of the possessions . Components . The spell required verbal and somatic components , a diamond worth at least 1000 gold piece s , 1 cubic inch of flesh from the creature to be cloned , and an appropriately sized container worth at least 2000 gold pieces .

title: Clothes for the Enlightened
description: Clothes for the Enlightened Clothes for the Enlightened was a shop located in the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . This shop was actually a pair of large red - striped pavilion tents .
description_long: Clothes for the Enlightened Clothes for the Enlightened was a shop located in the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . This shop was actually a pair of large red - striped pavilion tents . Activities . Hakim carried all of the items needed to complete an entire wardrobe . With silk purchased directly from the House of Al - Kamari , Hakim earned a reputation for offering fabulous clothing items . Inhabitants . Hakim Sayad owned and operated this establishment . Several members of the Royal Court of Huzuz purchase their garments from Hakim .

title: Clothiers ' District
description: Clothiers ' District The Clothiers ' District was the center for all industry revolving around cloth in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . Located within the Clothiers ' Quarter , this district was by far the most aromatic part of Huzuz .
description_long: Clothiers ' District The Clothiers ' District was the center for all industry revolving around cloth in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . Located within the Clothiers ' Quarter , this district was by far the most aromatic part of Huzuz . Harsh smells from tanneries and boiling dyes infused the air of the Clothiers ' District with their pungent aroma . The Farmers ' Road and Clothiers ' Way ran north to south along the east side of the Clothiers ' District , separating it from the Peasants ' District . A small section of the Enlightened Way touched the southern section of the Clothiers ' District . To the north sat the Northwest District . Activities . Cloth , silk , and linen was produced in this district then sold to tailors or embroiderers who made finished products . Notable Features . Many prominent merchant houses owned property within the Clothiers ' District , including :

title: Clothiers ' Quarter
description: Clothiers ' Quarter The Clothiers ' Quarter was one of the four quarters of Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . The Clothiers ' Quarter encompassed the Clothiers ' District , Merchants ' District , and the seedy Northwest District , forming the west and northwest portion of the city .
description_long: Clothiers ' Quarter The Clothiers ' Quarter was one of the four quarters of Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . The Clothiers ' Quarter encompassed the Clothiers ' District , Merchants ' District , and the seedy Northwest District , forming the west and northwest portion of the city . Thanks to the sprawling Grand Bazaar , and other smaller areas of trade , the Clothiers ' Quarter was the center of trade and business within Golden Huzuz where anything from coffee to slaves could be purchased .

title: Clothiers ' Way
description: Clothiers ' Way Clothiers ' Way was located in Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . Clothiers ' Way branched off of the South Road at the Gulf Gate , entering Huzuz from the south and passing northeast between the Peasants ' District , Northwest District and Clothiers ' District before terminating at the Grand Bazaar in the Merchants ' District .
description_long: Clothiers ' Way Clothiers ' Way was located in Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . Clothiers ' Way branched off of the South Road at the Gulf Gate , entering Huzuz from the south and passing northeast between the Peasants ' District , Northwest District and Clothiers ' District before terminating at the Grand Bazaar in the Merchants ' District .

title: Cloud Crown Palace
description: Cloud Crown Palace Cloud Crown Palace was the finest example of Evereska ' s natural architecture . The palace resembled a stand of bluetop s packed so closely together that the huge boles grew into each other . The scaling on the bark was so expertly done that even a practiced sculptor ' s eye would not have known it was stone , it was a place of mighty defensive magics and ancient towers .
description_long: Cloud Crown Palace Cloud Crown Palace was the finest example of Evereska ' s natural architecture . The palace resembled a stand of bluetop s packed so closely together that the huge boles grew into each other . The scaling on the bark was so expertly done that even a practiced sculptor ' s eye would not have known it was stone , it was a place of mighty defensive magics and ancient towers . It was also the home of the Vale Lord and where the Hill Elders met . The majority of the Vale Guard was stationed here along with members of the Spell Guard , and elements of the Swords of Evereska where Noble Blades and Lordly Wands performed their stints in the Noble Militia .

title: Cloud Peaks
description: Cloud Peaks The Cloud Peaks were a range of mountains in West Faerûn , and they marked the northern border of Amn . Sportsmen and - women who could afford the cost would use the cliffs of the range for rock climbing . Geography .
description_long: Cloud Peaks The Cloud Peaks were a range of mountains in West Faerûn , and they marked the northern border of Amn . Sportsmen and - women who could afford the cost would use the cliffs of the range for rock climbing . Geography . While a small mountain range , the Cloud Peaks were very tall . The tallest mountain in the range , Mount Speartop , had an elevation of 14 , 500 feet above sea level . Many steep ravines and sudden drops lay along the paths , and the winds were dangerous . The mountains were snow - covered most of the year and quite cool . Fauna . Many sheep and goats roamed the foothills of the Cloud Peaks , grazing . Production . The mountains were thoroughly mined for iron , gems , and precious metals . The town of Crimmor processed a good portion of the ore and gems coming from the Peaks before shipping them to Athkatla . Inhabitants . Tribes of ogre s and hill giant s lived here . A family of cloud giant s lived here also until they were eliminated in 1342 DR . Both remorhaz es and white dragon s inhabited these mountains as well . One such white dragon was named Icehaupt . He lived on Mount Speartop but preferred to never leave his lair .

title: Cloud Wizard
description: Cloud Wizard Cloud Wizard was a powerful wizard among the vile yak - folk of the World Pillar Mountains in 1367 DR . Activities . In addition to being one of the most powerful wizards among the yikarians , Cloud Wizard was also a member of the Seven Sages and the appointed governor of the Fiend ' s Wing province within the Land of the Yak - Men .
description_long: Cloud Wizard Cloud Wizard was a powerful wizard among the vile yak - folk of the World Pillar Mountains in 1367 DR . Activities . In addition to being one of the most powerful wizards among the yikarians , Cloud Wizard was also a member of the Seven Sages and the appointed governor of the Fiend ' s Wing province within the Land of the Yak - Men . He ruled from a cloud - island mountain peak . Cloud Wizard helped educate young yikarians in the use of magic . He also created an impressive collection of magical trinkets that he presented to the Lotus Emperor during the yak - folk ' s mid - winter festival . Rumors & Legends . Cloud Wizard was believed to have created the sinister marrash . Even if that was not true , he still had a close relationships with the dangerous archers .

title: Cloud giant
description: Cloud giant Cloud giants were a race of giant s who preferred living among the clouds . Description . Cloud giants ' skin ranged in color from milky white to light sky blue .
description_long: Cloud giant Cloud giants were a race of giant s who preferred living among the clouds . Description . Cloud giants ' skin ranged in color from milky white to light sky blue . Their hair was silvery white or brass , and their eyes were iridescent blue . Adult males were about 18 feet tall and weighed about 5 , 000 pounds . Cloud giants preferred to wear fine clothing and jewelry . Cloud giants had vision that extended into the infrared , ( although this was not infravision , ) which allowed them to see particularly well through fog and cloud . They also had an excellent sense of smell . They spoke Jotunskye and Jotun . Abilities . Cloud giants all possessed some control over their namesake , being able to summon forth a cloud of fog and mist at will . Society . These giants preferred to live in the tallest mountains or even higher if possible . Those with magical talents often create floating castles or cities in which to dwell , held aloft in the sky atop a mass of clouds . Cloud giants often kept dire lion s as pets or guardians .

title: Cloud of daggers
description: Cloud of daggers Cloud of daggers was a simple spell learned by some wizard s .
