Upon casting the wizards " cloud of daggers " conjured a cloud of small , flying daggers of force within an area of roughly five feet in diameter , within fifty feet of the caster . These daggers cut to shreds anything in their path , though they were weak enough that more powerful foes may be lightly harmed .
description_long: Cloud of daggers Cloud of daggers was a simple spell learned by some wizard s . Upon casting the wizards " cloud of daggers " conjured a cloud of small , flying daggers of force within an area of roughly five feet in diameter , within fifty feet of the caster . These daggers cut to shreds anything in their path , though they were weak enough that more powerful foes may be lightly harmed . The cloud remained in place for only a short while , a brief moment at best , but since the wizard could cast it at - will it could be reformed at any time . If a wizard grew to exceptional power , the dangerous of wading into a " cloud of daggers " become twice fold . The post sundering version of the spell was much the same except if used as a higher spell level it would have been even more powerful . This version also was not restricted too the wizard and could be cast at a range of 90 feet . Components . Verbal and somatic components and a silver of glass .

title: Cloud palace
description: Cloud palace A cloud palace or cloud castle was an abode of cloud giant s kept floating on a single large cloud by magic . Description . A cloud palace was like any other cloud giant castle , only it was constructed upon a magical , solid cloud .
description_long: Cloud palace A cloud palace or cloud castle was an abode of cloud giant s kept floating on a single large cloud by magic . Description . A cloud palace was like any other cloud giant castle , only it was constructed upon a magical , solid cloud . In addition to the castle structure itself , the island of cloud upon which it was built was said to contain giant - sized gardens with luscious fruit trees . Cloud giants could not steer or control where a cloud palace went ; they relied on the blowing of the wind and would dock their palace at various mountain peaks whenever they drifted to such points . Construction . The construction of a cloud palace was an especially complicated endeavor , which was exhausting to all those involved . To begin , it required at least twelve cloud giants working together and using their inherent control over clouds and fog to gather a massive cloud centered over a single runecaster . This waiting runecaster performed a ten - hour ritual involving a rune - inscribed pebble contained in a small leather pouch . If he or she was successful , the mass of cloud solidified , and the other runecasters forced the cloud into the sky again .

title: Cloudkill
description: Cloudkill Cloudkill was a conjuration or evocation spell that filled an area with a extremely lethal cloud . Effect . " Cloudkill " would release a yellowish green cloud that was heavier than air so it would always sink to the ground or into holes .
description_long: Cloudkill Cloudkill was a conjuration or evocation spell that filled an area with a extremely lethal cloud . Effect . " Cloudkill " would release a yellowish green cloud that was heavier than air so it would always sink to the ground or into holes . When cast , the cloud would travel away from the caster and could be broken apart by strong winds or dense vegetation . The cloud would instantly kill " weak " creatures and greatly injure stronger creatures with its poison . It did not matter if the creature held its breath as the poison would still affect it . After the Spellplague , the cloud would only harm targets and could be moved by the wizard who also needed to sustain it . The post - Second Sundering version had some of the same features as the older versions , like being heavy and affecting creatures whether they held their breath or didn ' t need to breath . This version also lasted for 10 minutes and moved 10 feet ( 3 meters ) every 6 seconds away from the caster . If used with a higher spell level , it would cause more damage . Components . Only vocal and somatic components were needed . History .

title: Cloudtop Tower
description: Cloudtop Tower Cloudtop Tower is the second highest spire within the city of Evereska . It is built from white marble and made to resemble a stand of blueleaf trees . It is home to the High Magi of the Cloudtop Circle , advisers to the Council of Hill Elders and commanders of the Spell Guard .
description_long: Cloudtop Tower Cloudtop Tower is the second highest spire within the city of Evereska . It is built from white marble and made to resemble a stand of blueleaf trees . It is home to the High Magi of the Cloudtop Circle , advisers to the Council of Hill Elders and commanders of the Spell Guard .

title: Cloven Mountains
description: Cloven Mountains The Cloven Mountains were a wide and barren mountain range rising from the waters of the Deepwash . Geography . The range ran from east to west and was split in two by the Wintercloak River , which was how the mountains received their name .
description_long: Cloven Mountains The Cloven Mountains were a wide and barren mountain range rising from the waters of the Deepwash . Geography . The range ran from east to west and was split in two by the Wintercloak River , which was how the mountains received their name . The mountains of the western spur were called the High Peaks and filled most of the barony of Ahlarkhem in Erlkazar . The eastern portion of the mountains were located in the Vilhon Reach . The tallest peak in the High Peaks was 10 , 000 feet above sea level . The Arglander River flowed down from the High Peaks and into the Deepwash . Inhabitants . The Cloven Mountains were inhabited by a handful of warring goblinoid and orc ish tribes . Rumors . A rumor of a monstrous cat - like beast living in the mountains was told . It was said that the mysterious creature preyed on the goblinoids and anyone foolhardy enough to hunt it .

title: Cloven Shield
description: Cloven Shield The Cloven Shield was a loud inn and tavern in Marsember , Cormyr . Geography . The tavern was situated on the island immediately south of Morningmist Hall in the Cormyrian area .
description_long: Cloven Shield The Cloven Shield was a loud inn and tavern in Marsember , Cormyr . Geography . The tavern was situated on the island immediately south of Morningmist Hall in the Cormyrian area . Structure . Upon entering the inn , customers passed under a sign painted with a shield broken in two , and found a place designed for drinking and partying into the late hours . Atmosphere . Even though the building was falling apart and the guests were noisy , the establishment offered fair quality food at a cheap price . Used by adventurers as well as Zhentarim , the Cult of the Dragon , and those from Thay , fights and brawls broke out almost every night . Many of these unsavory customers were looking to hire mercenaries and others of ill repute . Prices . Large rooms could be rented per night for 10 gp ( including stabling and meals for nine people ) .

title: Club
description: Club The club is one of the oldest weapons known . Any blunt object that can be swung with force enough to cause damage can be considered a club . They are considered simple , one - handed melee weapons .
description_long: Club The club is one of the oldest weapons known . Any blunt object that can be swung with force enough to cause damage can be considered a club . They are considered simple , one - handed melee weapons . The mace is the military version of a club . Description . Many blunt wooden sticks can be considered clubs , such as table legs , large branches , or tree trunks in the case of some giants and other large creatures . Normally a club costs nothing because it can be easily made from materials found in the environment . Weaponology . Most clubs can be made of any material and cause bludgeoning wounds against enemies . While most wooden clubs weigh around 3lbs ( 1 . 4kg ) , a hill giant or mountain giant ' s tree trunk club is going to weigh much more . Other materials can be used to reinforce the wood of the weapon , such as bands of metal or resinous materials . Enchantments . Clubs can carry any enchantment typical to other weapons . Again , the only limitation would be the enchanter ' s power , and the material of the club itself . Spells , such as " Shillelagh , " can mimic club effects , or create powerful magical weapons .

title: Clusterfang
description: Clusterfang Clusterfang was a poor translation into Common of a particular deepspawn ' s given name . It operated in the southern Sword Coast and Vilhon Reach regions in concert with the Twisted Rune . No one who knew of its existence could guess at why Clusterfang had allied itself with this organization of evil magic - users , but it obviously saw some benefit of doing so .
description_long: Clusterfang Clusterfang was a poor translation into Common of a particular deepspawn ' s given name . It operated in the southern Sword Coast and Vilhon Reach regions in concert with the Twisted Rune . No one who knew of its existence could guess at why Clusterfang had allied itself with this organization of evil magic - users , but it obviously saw some benefit of doing so . Clusterfang laired under the city of Zazesspur , being the second deepspawn to do so .

title: Clyde Caldwell
description: Clyde Caldwell Clyde Caldwell is an American artist and self - described fantasy illustrator . Originally a commercial illustrator for ad agencies , he gained fame working for TSR , Inc . from 1982 to 1992 , illustrating many products at a time the game was at the peak of its popularity .
description_long: Clyde Caldwell Clyde Caldwell is an American artist and self - described fantasy illustrator . Originally a commercial illustrator for ad agencies , he gained fame working for TSR , Inc . from 1982 to 1992 , illustrating many products at a time the game was at the peak of its popularity . Since 1992 he has worked as a freelance artist .

title: Clytemorrenestrix
description: Clytemorrenestrix Clytemorrenestrix , or Nestrix to her human companions , was a mature blue dragon who was changed by the Spellplague into a human woman . History . Pre - Spellplague .
description_long: Clytemorrenestrix Clytemorrenestrix , or Nestrix to her human companions , was a mature blue dragon who was changed by the Spellplague into a human woman . History . Pre - Spellplague . Nestrix lived in the Raurin desert during her early years where she met her mate Tantlevgithus . At some point they moved to the Calim desert where she made a name for herself and acquired a sizable hoard by terrorizing caravans . The day the Spellplague struck on 29th Tarsakh , 1385 DR , a thief named Lyra sneaked into Nestrix ' s lair and attempted to steal a jeweled choker . Nestrix chased the thief into the desert and both were overcome by the blue flame of the spell storm . Lyra ' s body was transformed into that of a bronze dragon but the stolen choker choked her to death . Nestrix was turned into a human woman but many of Lyra ' s memories and possibly some of her consciousness were transferred to Nestrix . Post - Spellplague . Nestrix ' lair and her eggs were destroyed by the Spellplague and her mate was killed . Since she had nothing tying her to the Calim any longer she wandered throughout Faerûn for many years . In 1478 DR she killed a wizard in Cormyr , possibly in self defense .

title: Coast Road
description: Coast Road The Coast Road ran along the west coast of the Vast , connecting the cities of Ravens Bluff and Tantras . From south to north , it started at Ravens Bluff , passed over the Fire River via the great multi - span bridge at Mossbridges , and ended at Tantras . On the way , it linked with the High Trail , Feldar ' s Trail , the Tantras Trail , and the Cross Road .
description_long: Coast Road The Coast Road ran along the west coast of the Vast , connecting the cities of Ravens Bluff and Tantras . From south to north , it started at Ravens Bluff , passed over the Fire River via the great multi - span bridge at Mossbridges , and ended at Tantras . On the way , it linked with the High Trail , Feldar ' s Trail , the Tantras Trail , and the Cross Road .

title: Coast Trail
description: Coast Trail The Coast Trail was a alternative to the Trade Way as a means to travel from Calimport to Memnon , avoiding the Calim Desert . As the name suggests , the trail followed the windy coast along the southern and western edges of Calimshan . The path was only wide enough for a single cart and covered rocky terrain , but it was far enough from the effects of Memnon ' s Crackle .
description_long: Coast Trail The Coast Trail was a alternative to the Trade Way as a means to travel from Calimport to Memnon , avoiding the Calim Desert . As the name suggests , the trail followed the windy coast along the southern and western edges of Calimshan . The path was only wide enough for a single cart and covered rocky terrain , but it was far enough from the effects of Memnon ' s Crackle . The trail was primarily used by adventurers or other vagabonds . Many hermits , smugglers , or other folk who wished to live undetected built structures a mile or so off the path . Besides Calimport and Memnon , the town of Teshburl lies along the trail , as does the House of St . Liwan ' s Blessing , a monastery to Ilmater .

title: Coast Way
description: Coast Way The Coast Way was a long , well - traveled trade road along the west coast of Faerûn . The Coast Way was just a part of the much larger Trade Way that started at Calimport in the south and went along the coastline all the way north to Waterdeep . The section of road between Baldur ' s Gate and Tethyr was generally known as the Coast Way .
description_long: Coast Way The Coast Way was a long , well - traveled trade road along the west coast of Faerûn . The Coast Way was just a part of the much larger Trade Way that started at Calimport in the south and went along the coastline all the way north to Waterdeep . The section of road between Baldur ' s Gate and Tethyr was generally known as the Coast Way .

title: Coast circle
description: Coast circle The coast circle was a druid circle associated with the transitional region between sea and land , teeming with life of infinite variety , beating with the pulse of waves crashing ashore . Druids who took up the cause of nature in such a region had an affinity for this circle and the suite of spells that came to them without cost ( they could cast them at any time without having to prepare them in advance ) .
description_long: Coast circle The coast circle was a druid circle associated with the transitional region between sea and land , teeming with life of infinite variety , beating with the pulse of waves crashing ashore . Druids who took up the cause of nature in such a region had an affinity for this circle and the suite of spells that came to them without cost ( they could cast them at any time without having to prepare them in advance ) .

title: Coaster
description: Coaster A coaster , also known as a round ship , was a medium - sized sailing ship used on the Inner Sea . They were favored by Aglarond , Chessenta , Chondath , and Turmish . Description .
description_long: Coaster A coaster , also known as a round ship , was a medium - sized sailing ship used on the Inner Sea . They were favored by Aglarond , Chessenta , Chondath , and Turmish . Description . As the name implies , coasters were designed to sail in the shallower waters near a coast . They were relatively slow and not particularly safe for deep sea voyages , but could carry a respectable amount of cargo with fewer crew than most cargo ships . Typically 60 ft ( 18 m ) long at the keel and 20 ft ( 6 m ) wide , coasters had two masts with triangular sails and no oars . The rudder was mounted off one side , and above deck there was often only a small sterncastle . Crew size ranged from a minimum of 12 to a maximum of 40 , including passengers . A coaster could be armed with a large weapon ( such as catapult or ballista ) but was not built to wield a ram .

title: Cobble
description: Cobble Cobble was a dwarven cleric in Mithral Hall . Description . He was a squat and round dwarf with a short yellow beard .
description_long: Cobble Cobble was a dwarven cleric in Mithral Hall . Description . He was a squat and round dwarf with a short yellow beard . Personality . The dwarven cleric was said to be strong in magic and have deep insight into the world . History . In 1357 DR , Bruenor Battlehammer gave him the title Holy Cleric of the Hall . Death . In 1357 DR , the Companions of the Hall delved deep into Mithral Hall searching for Drizzt Do ' Urden after Bruenor discovered Artemis Entreri was masquerading as Regis . While hunting for Drizzt , Cobble saw metal shavings on the floor and realized a spell trap . He shouted for the others to fall back but was crushed to death beneath a wall of solid iron cast by Vierna Do ' Urden .

title: Cockatrice
description: Cockatrice The cockatrice was a small avian magical beast . It was notorious for its petrification ability . It was closely related to the pyrolisk .
description_long: Cockatrice The cockatrice was a small avian magical beast . It was notorious for its petrification ability . It was closely related to the pyrolisk . Description . Although about the size of a large turkey or goose and weighing 25 pounds ( 11 . 3 kilograms ) , a cockatrice more closely resembled a chicken , but it was a hideous hybrid with the wings of a bat and a lizard - like tail . A male cockatrice had a rooster ' s wattles and comb , which the females lacked . It had red glowing eyes . Combat . Any creature that a cockatrice bit could be permanently turned into stone . Cockatrices were immune to their own petrifying bite and that of other cockatrices , though not of other petrifying creatures and spells . Cockatrices ferociously attacked any creature that appeared to threaten them or their lairs . Typically , flocks of them would attempt to overwhelm or confuse their opponents , and flew at their faces . Ecology . Female cockatrices were very rare , much more so than the males .

title: Cocoa
description: Cocoa Cocoa was a powdered product from Maztica that was used to prepare a bitter beverage . It was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description .
description_long: Cocoa Cocoa was a powdered product from Maztica that was used to prepare a bitter beverage . It was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description . When mixed with water , cocoa powder produced a bitter beverage that was said to possess restorative and stimulating properties . It was also reputed to be an aphrodisiac . Cocoa beverage was also very popular in Calimshan , where it was mostly enjoyed by the wealthy in little shops .

title: Code Helm
description: Code Helm The Code Helm was an organization based on the planet of Glyth around 1359 DR . Activities . Code Helm was focused on destroying the mind flayer s .
description_long: Code Helm The Code Helm was an organization based on the planet of Glyth around 1359 DR . Activities . Code Helm was focused on destroying the mind flayer s . They funded their operation from loot gathered from mind flayer spelljamming ships . While not technically a mercenary company , if offered money and a chance to slay illithid , Code Helm would likely take the offer . Base of Operations . The company resided on an outpost within the third ring of Glyth , unless they were actively transporting rescued persons to their homes . Membership . Members of Code Helm were brave men and women devotees of Helm who lived outside Toril . Many were cleric s of Helm , but most were actually paladin s of other gods dedicated to Code Helm ' s ideals . Helm granted both his own clerics and these paladins a special spell of " mental prowess " for joining Code Helm . In 1359 DR , the leader of the group was Easel Gifford of Amn , a paladin of Torm . The group was ruled under a strict , military - like hierarchy , originally by the priests of Helm , but since so many other religions ( 80 % ) were involved , this was changed .

title: Codex of Araunt
description: Codex of Araunt The Codex of Araunt was a tract originally recorded on stone tablets by Lod , a bone naga and founder of the Eminence of Araunt . History . More than five - hundred years before the Year of the Ageless One , the codex prophesied the slow expansion of the Eminence in the centuries that followed .
description_long: Codex of Araunt The Codex of Araunt was a tract originally recorded on stone tablets by Lod , a bone naga and founder of the Eminence of Araunt . History . More than five - hundred years before the Year of the Ageless One , the codex prophesied the slow expansion of the Eminence in the centuries that followed . Abilities . The " Codex " contained several rituals and spells :

title: Coelenite
description: Coelenite Coelenites were colony creatures that began life as single - celled organisms that grew a hardened shell similar to coral . Rudimentary intelligence was achieved when groups of coelenites lived together as a colony , eventually becoming sentient when enough coelenites gathered . Description .
description_long: Coelenite Coelenites were colony creatures that began life as single - celled organisms that grew a hardened shell similar to coral . Rudimentary intelligence was achieved when groups of coelenites lived together as a colony , eventually becoming sentient when enough coelenites gathered . Description . Coelenites living in a colony “ grew ” a humanoid form by secreting hardened shells that were modified to suite their desire . They often looked like a man encrusted with coral but lacked any sensory organs . Their dexterity was quite poor . Combat . Coelenites were slow but dangerous . They usually attacked in the water but were known to climb aboard ships or land as well . Arrows , blunt , and edged weapons barely scratched a coelenite ’ s hard exoskeleton . Spell s affecting a single target , such as " finger of death " , were utterly useless against them . Area effect spells targeting only a small portion of a coelenite would barely harm the creature , but an area effect spell engulfing the entire creature would instantly kill it . Coelenites were immune to all enchantment or charm spells .

title: Coffee House of Buri
description: Coffee House of Buri The Coffee House of Buri was a small shop in Bandar al - Sa ' adat in 1367 DR . Location . The establishment was located near Usamah the Carpet Dealer in the Bandar al - Sa ' adat marketplace .
description_long: Coffee House of Buri The Coffee House of Buri was a small shop in Bandar al - Sa ' adat in 1367 DR . Location . The establishment was located near Usamah the Carpet Dealer in the Bandar al - Sa ' adat marketplace . Structure . Near the carpet dealer ' s stand , the structure was buried behind a large line of stacked fruit . Interior . The interior of the Coffee House of Buri was furnished with carpets and ragged cushions . Customers enjoyed a pleasant variety of sweet and overly spiced coffee . Inhabitants . Both Alix and Karbuqa were known to frequent the coffee house .

title: Coffee ceremony
description: Coffee ceremony The coffee ceremony was a crucial social interaction among Zakharans . All Zakharans , from a wealthy Al - Hadhar all the way to a free - roaming Al - Badia , were appraised by their peers for their coffee - making . Unless a woman was the master of the house or tent , this was typically a man ' s responsibility .
description_long: Coffee ceremony The coffee ceremony was a crucial social interaction among Zakharans . All Zakharans , from a wealthy Al - Hadhar all the way to a free - roaming Al - Badia , were appraised by their peers for their coffee - making . Unless a woman was the master of the house or tent , this was typically a man ' s responsibility . Al - Badia treated this tradition with the utmost importance . Where nobles from the city would often delegate the coffee - making tasks to servants , Al - Badia cherished the hands - on responsibility themselves . The actual ceremony began when a host sat before a small hollow of sand and lit a fire , usually fueled by camel dung . The host would then spread all of their coffee - making equipment out before them , including two coffee pots — one battered and one polished . During this time the host would engage in light conversation with their guests , though being careful to avoid questions about their health or business since that would be considered rude behavior . The host then proceeded to make the coffee in the battered pot , only transferring it to the newer pot when it was as black as night . Pouring the coffee required several basic steps .

title: Cog
description: Cog A cog was a small , one masted sailing ship used on the Sea of Fallen Stars . Another ship , also called a cog , had two masts and was a larger version of the coaster . Description .
description_long: Cog A cog was a small , one masted sailing ship used on the Sea of Fallen Stars . Another ship , also called a cog , had two masts and was a larger version of the coaster . Description . The smaller version of cog had only one mast and , because of its small size and limited space for provisions , it was not seaworthy enough for long ocean voyages . A cog had a rounded hull made from sturdy wood . It had only a partial deck ; that is , a deck only covered its ends . It had raised bow and stern platforms , but these were open , not enclosed . A cog was about 40 feet long and 20 feet wide and the deck came about ten feet out of the water . It could carry 40 tons of cargo . A cog required at least four crew members to man the vessel at all times and could carry a compliment of 20 crew and passengers . Its sailing speed was two miles per hour in light winds . The larger version had two masts with square sails and cargo capacity similar to a caravel . The minimum crew size was 10 with a maximum of 25 . It was 85 ft ( 26 m ) long at the keel and 20 ft ( 6 m ) across the beam . It usually had only one deck and could be outfitted with fore - and sterncastles .

title: Coggin ' s Rise
description: Coggin ' s Rise Coggin ' s Rise was a trail that ran through the hills from Stagwick to Castle Hartwick . The hills in the region were covered with white - barked aspen trees . It took between a half hour and an hour to travel the full distance by horse .
description_long: Coggin ' s Rise Coggin ' s Rise was a trail that ran through the hills from Stagwick to Castle Hartwick . The hills in the region were covered with white - barked aspen trees . It took between a half hour and an hour to travel the full distance by horse . History . It was off Coggin ' s Rise where Princess Brianna and her firbolg bodyguard Morten were ambushed by Ice Spire ogre s led by Goboka in 1366 DR . The princess was kidnapped , because her father , King Camden had promised her to the tribe of ogres in exchange for their assistance in his war against his brother Dunstan years prior .

title: Cognition thief
description: Cognition thief A cognition thief was a psionicist who specialized in espionage via psionics and was a member of the Hall of Mental Splendor . Culture . Cognition thieves were psychic spies who specialized in raiding the minds of their targets to rob them of their secret thoughts and even their wits .
description_long: Cognition thief A cognition thief was a psionicist who specialized in espionage via psionics and was a member of the Hall of Mental Splendor . Culture . Cognition thieves were psychic spies who specialized in raiding the minds of their targets to rob them of their secret thoughts and even their wits . Their powers were subtle and they appeared inconspicuous , making them highly effective spies . All known cognition thieves around 1373 DR were trained at the Hall of Mental Splendor in Skullport . The majority continued to work as mercenary spies for that organization , but a few had retired or departed on less friendly terms . Cognition thieves were commonly found in Waterdeep , the city on the land above Skullport . Entry . A would - be cognition thief needed skills in deception , disguise , the gathering of information , and / or picking locks . They also had to be inquisitors who could use their psionic focus to sense deceit in others . Finally , they needed to be able to manifest the power " psionic blast " . Most cognition thieves began as psion s dedicated to the telepathy discipline , but wilder s and other kinds of psion were also possible .

title: Coiled Cabal
description: Coiled Cabal The Coiled Cabal is a secret society of arcane spellcasters dominated by the Hss ' tafin , but draws members from all the great houses of the yuan - ti . Though the " vrael olo " do not consider it an independent tribe in its own right , it is often treated like one in intertribal politics , especially since membership requires that loyalty to the society take precedence over tribal allegiances . Symbol .
description_long: Coiled Cabal The Coiled Cabal is a secret society of arcane spellcasters dominated by the Hss ' tafin , but draws members from all the great houses of the yuan - ti . Though the " vrael olo " do not consider it an independent tribe in its own right , it is often treated like one in intertribal politics , especially since membership requires that loyalty to the society take precedence over tribal allegiances . Symbol . The mark of the Coiled Cabal is an S - shaped serpent with open - jawed heads at both ends . In the Forgotten Realms . The Coiled Cabal has power bases in the Great Petrified Serpent at the Serpent Hills , Ss ' kowlyn ' raa in the Forest of Wyrms , Semorav ' s Tower in Hlondeth , the ruins of Lhesper in The Shaar , and at various ruins and settlements currently under construction in the Black Jungles . Politics . The society is allied with the Eselemas , Extaminos , and Hss ' tafi tribes , but it often marches to its own drum . Members of the Coiled Cabal clash most frequently with the Se ' Sehen tribe because both groups see themselves as the rightful leaders in the push for open dominance of Faerûn . Organization & Hierarchy .

title: Coiled dragon
description: Coiled dragon The coiled dragon was a magical chalice . It was one of the Wo - ha Ui - jung , a collection of magical vessels created by the Han people of Koryo in ancient times . Description .
description_long: Coiled dragon The coiled dragon was a magical chalice . It was one of the Wo - ha Ui - jung , a collection of magical vessels created by the Han people of Koryo in ancient times . Description . Carved in the shape of a dragon , the vessel was huge at 1 foot ( 30 . 48 cm ) wide , but it was very shallow . Powers . When filled with liquid silver and a single drop of blood from the one who would use it , the pool of silver became a mirror revealing any sight in Kara - Tur from the perspective of the Celestial Heavens above . Through concentration , the viewer could direct the mirror to anywhere in the land , whether to seek something out to or to spy . History . As perhaps the greatest of the Wo - ha Ui - jung , the " coiled dragon " < nowiki > ' s < / nowiki > powers had most likely at one stage influenced the history of Koryo . History recorded the Chinhan people as the last to hold the " coiled dragon " in around the 7th century before Dalereckoning , but it had been lost for two millennia by the 14th century DR .

title: Coin Spinners
description: Coin Spinners The Coin Spinners were a Luskan street gang that was based in the old Clearlight temple of Tymora . The Coin Spinners were active at least as early as 1475 DR . The gang took its name from the coin that symbolized the goddess and its symbol was a coin that incorporated both Tymora ' s and Beshaba ' s symbols .
description_long: Coin Spinners The Coin Spinners were a Luskan street gang that was based in the old Clearlight temple of Tymora . The Coin Spinners were active at least as early as 1475 DR . The gang took its name from the coin that symbolized the goddess and its symbol was a coin that incorporated both Tymora ' s and Beshaba ' s symbols . The gang used charitable activities such as as feeding the poor as a front for criminal acts , which included protection rackets .

title: Cold Field
description: Cold Field The Cold Field was a flat , treeless moor located south of Cormanthor and Velarswood between Harrowdale and Scardale . Description . The Cold Field was a battlefield haunted by ghosts of soldiers .
description_long: Cold Field The Cold Field was a flat , treeless moor located south of Cormanthor and Velarswood between Harrowdale and Scardale . Description . The Cold Field was a battlefield haunted by ghosts of soldiers . The land was scarred by dragon ' s breath . It was most dangerous in winter . In summertime , shepherds from the local dales used the field as pasture for their sheep , since the animals didn ' t mind the restless spirits . History . The Cold Field was the site of a great battle and was therefore haunted by ghosts . Mathira Melarn , an Eilistraee an priestesses and bearer of the Crescent Blade , was slain here and the blade wound up in the gullet of a purple worm . The blade was retrieved in 1372 DR by Halisstra Melarn and Ryld Argith ; Halisstra then carried the blade to the Demonweb Pits , intending ( but failing ) to slay Lolth .

title: Cold Heart
description: Cold Heart Cold Heart was the favored weapon of Kiaransalee , the drow goddess of undeath . Description . It was a curved dagger that constantly dripped acid .
description_long: Cold Heart Cold Heart was the favored weapon of Kiaransalee , the drow goddess of undeath . Description . It was a curved dagger that constantly dripped acid . Abilities . A " + 4 dagger " , those struck by it were also harmed by ongoing acid burns .

title: Cold Vale
description: Cold Vale The Cold Vale was a wild and desolate region between the southern edge of the Cold Wood and the northern spur of the Rauvin Mountains . Geography . The Cold Vale was located between the Cold Wood ( later the Glimmerwood ) to the north and the Rauvin Mountains to the south .
description_long: Cold Vale The Cold Vale was a wild and desolate region between the southern edge of the Cold Wood and the northern spur of the Rauvin Mountains . Geography . The Cold Vale was located between the Cold Wood ( later the Glimmerwood ) to the north and the Rauvin Mountains to the south . The northern mouth of Dead Orc Pass opened up into the vale . To the east , the vale opened up into Adbar Run . To the west , the vale ended against the Night Trees forest ( later part of the Glimmerwood ] ] and the foothills around Citadel Felbarr . The River Rauvin passed through the vale from the Cold Wood before going underground north of the Dead Orc Pass into the Rauvinheart caverns . Description . The Cold Vale was a land of broken hills , steep ravines , swift cold streams , and mossy gorges . History . In the past , dwarf - paths crisscrossed the vale , leading from Citadel Felbarr to Citadel Adbar . By 1372 DR , these paths had fallen into disuse and were largely forgotten , even by the dwarves . In 1484 DR , Bromm , one of the twin kings of Citadel Adbar , was beheaded in the Cold Vale by the orc warlord Hartusk in what became known as the Battle of the Cold Vale .

title: Cold Wood
description: Cold Wood The Cold Wood was a forest on the edge of the Silver Marches . By about 1460 DR , the Moonwood had grown together with the Cold Wood and the larger forest was known as the Glimmerwood . Geography .
description_long: Cold Wood The Cold Wood was a forest on the edge of the Silver Marches . By about 1460 DR , the Moonwood had grown together with the Cold Wood and the larger forest was known as the Glimmerwood . Geography . It was located between the Spine of the World , Rauvin Mountains , and Ice Mountains . A wild place , the Cold Wood was largely untouched by civilization ; most woodcutters and homesteaders avoided it . Flora . The forest was full of , , and trees . Inhabitants . Snow tiger s , orc s , ettin s , and a bebilith have been known to roam the Cold Wood . The Uthgardt barbarians hunted in the area , but would not cut any living tree or kept fires to a minimum to protect the forest . The Red Tiger Tribe considered the northern part of the wood their territory . Several bands of outcasts from Uthgardt society were known to live around the area as well .

title: Cold domain
description: Cold domain The Cold domain was a deity domain that granted divine spellcasters cold - themed spell s and powers . The spellcaster gained the abilities to rebuke and command cold creatures and to turn and destroy fire creatures . Deities with the Cold domain .
description_long: Cold domain The Cold domain was a deity domain that granted divine spellcasters cold - themed spell s and powers . The spellcaster gained the abilities to rebuke and command cold creatures and to turn and destroy fire creatures . Deities with the Cold domain . Auril , Bahamut , and Ulutiu offered the cold domain to their clerics .

title: Cold fire
description: Cold fire Cold fire was a divine magic spell available to priests of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It could temporarily change hot flames into cold , or damage a cold - sensitive creature . Effects .
description_long: Cold fire Cold fire was a divine magic spell available to priests of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It could temporarily change hot flames into cold , or damage a cold - sensitive creature . Effects . This spell could be used on normal or magical fires of size up to a 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) cube . The target had to be within 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) of the caster and the spell lasted for two minutes . Higher level casters could extend this range and duration . The hot fire was immediately transformed into blue and white flames that radiated cold and inflicted cold damage on creatures that came into contact with them . The targeted flames had to be relatively permanent — " cold fire " would work on a small " wall of fire " but not on the instantaneous burst of a " fireball " , for example . If a creature that was vulnerable to cold was the target of " cold fire " , this spell did cold damage to that creature ( instantaneously , like a " fireball " , but only targeting one creature ) . Higher level casters could cause more damage . If the creature managed to resist the magic of this spell , it took half the normal damage .

title: Cold iron
description: Cold iron Cold iron is forged at a lower temperature than normal iron or steel , in order to preserve its properties . It is mined deep underground , and famed for its efficacy against fey creatures . Cold iron weapons cost twice as much as their standard counterparts .
description_long: Cold iron Cold iron is forged at a lower temperature than normal iron or steel , in order to preserve its properties . It is mined deep underground , and famed for its efficacy against fey creatures . Cold iron weapons cost twice as much as their standard counterparts .

title: Cold snap
description: Cold snap Cold snap was a divine magic spell available to priests of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It caused a dramatic drop in temperature over a wide area that lasted for hours . Effects .
description_long: Cold snap Cold snap was a divine magic spell available to priests of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It caused a dramatic drop in temperature over a wide area that lasted for hours . Effects . For a cleric casting this spell , the area of effect was a circle , centered on the caster , with a radius of one mile ( 1 . 6 kilometers ) and the duration varied from two to eight hours . For a druid casting this spell , the radius was two miles ( 3 . 2 kilometers ) and the duration varied from four to sixteen hours . The casting time was only one minute . When cast , this spell lowered the temperature in the affected area by 5° F ( about 2 . 8° C ) per level of the caster , up to a maximum change of 50° F ( about 28° C ) , but not below −20° F ( −29° C ) . If this brought the ambient temperature below 40° F ( 4 . 4° C ) , the fortitude of unprotected individuals was increasingly challenged , but if properly attired in winter clothing they would suffer no lasting ill effects . If the temperature dropped below 30° F ( −1° C ) , fragile plants and fruit crops could be damaged with prolonged exposure ( three or more hours ) .

title: Colderan Morn
description: Colderan Morn Colderan Morn was a male human wizard and once a tyrannical Mage - lord of Daggerdale . He was also the great - grandfather of the famous Randal Morn . Description .
description_long: Colderan Morn Colderan Morn was a male human wizard and once a tyrannical Mage - lord of Daggerdale . He was also the great - grandfather of the famous Randal Morn . Description . Colderan was a rather corpulent man who dressed in rich clothing and his short , chubby fingers would often hold a staff . Personality . Although infamous for his tyrannical rule , Colderan had a strong romantic streak , often showering bards with gold in exchange for tales of tragic love or hard - won romance . He was also a sucker for pretty women . Possessions . The wealth of Colderan from plundering dwarves and taxing his populace was uncounted but he was noted for a few unique items of his own making . His " ring of thorns " granted him numerous powers over plants and could be recharged , though only Colderan knew how . He also penned a number of lorebooks on arcane plant lore which contained notes on how to create nightshade s and a treatise on sleep magic which oultines the construction of his ambitious " net of dreams " . History . In 1267 DR , many years before Randal Morn reclaimed Daggerdale from the Zhentarim , Colderan ruled the dale with an iron fist .

title: Colin McComb
description: Colin McComb Colin McComb is an author and game designer who has worked for TSR , Inc . and . Education .
description_long: Colin McComb Colin McComb is an author and game designer who has worked for TSR , Inc . and . Education . McComb received a degree in Philosophy from . Works . While at TSR , McComb worked with Monte Cook to expand the setting as well as on core Dungeons & Dragons material . He also co - authored " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " for the Forgotten Realms setting . With Interplay , McComb contributed to the game .

title: Coliseum ( Maerimydra )
description: Coliseum ( Maerimydra ) The Coliseum was an enormous structure built by the drow of Maerimydra to entertain the masses with battles between slaves , prisoners , and exotic beasts . Location . Located in the southern end of Maerimydra , the coliseum was more than half a mile from northern entrance to the city .
description_long: Coliseum ( Maerimydra ) The Coliseum was an enormous structure built by the drow of Maerimydra to entertain the masses with battles between slaves , prisoners , and exotic beasts . Location . Located in the southern end of Maerimydra , the coliseum was more than half a mile from northern entrance to the city . Structure . Exterior . The Coliseum of Maerimydra was an enormous oval building with its outer walls reaching a height of 60 ft ( 18 . 2 m ) . The top of the outer walls were lined with crenelations and windows peppered the sides . Along the north - eastern side of the coliseum , six great double doors opened for the public to enter . On the opposite side of the arena lay a smaller public entrance . Two more sets of double doors lay either end of the coliseum to provide access to the arena directly . Interior . Beyond the six large doors that formed the public entrance , a public gallery , nearly 200 ft ( 60 . 9 m ) long and 40 ft ( 12 . 1 m ) wide , was situated beneath the coliseum ' s stands . Impressive staircases led up to the seating area above at three points . Torches of flickering " continual flame " hung from the ceiling to illuminate the chamber .

title: Collector
description: Collector Collectors are a special type of scavenger found in the city of Sigil . They and their group focus on the recovery of bodies on the streets and understreets of Sigil . Their leader was Pharod until his slaying by the shades that chased the Nameless One .
description_long: Collector Collectors are a special type of scavenger found in the city of Sigil . They and their group focus on the recovery of bodies on the streets and understreets of Sigil . Their leader was Pharod until his slaying by the shades that chased the Nameless One . After collection , a body , or " deader " in the cant of the Collectors , is taken to the Mortuary for disposal . Money is paid to the Collectors by the Dustmen , the caretakers of the Mortuary . Appearance and Skills . Collectors are typically seen in nondescript gray or tan robes . They are lightly armed with daggers , and typically wear no armor . Their fighting skills are not even of the proficient level , though there are exceptions . Outlook . Collectors can be of any alignment , as corpses couldn ' t care less who collects them . Sometimes , evil aligned Collectors attempt to hasten the death of a person , to collect a body that much sooner . Typically , these corpses are stripped of anything remotely valuable before their sale to the Dustmen .

title: College of the Eclipse
description: College of the Eclipse The College of the Eclipse was a society of psionicist s dedicated to the teaching of psionics , based in the city of Riatavin in Tethyr and active in the mid - 1370s DR . Base of Operations . The College ' s headquarters in Riatavin were described as like a fortress .
description_long: College of the Eclipse The College of the Eclipse was a society of psionicist s dedicated to the teaching of psionics , based in the city of Riatavin in Tethyr and active in the mid - 1370s DR . Base of Operations . The College ' s headquarters in Riatavin were described as like a fortress . Reputation . Although the College of the Eclipse was entirely open about what it did , most folk in Tethyr thought them to be simply another cabal of mages . Even conventional wizard organizations might wonder at their " strange magic " . The College encouraged such misconceptions . Activities . Devoted to the teaching and advancement of psionics , the College provided cheap and rudimentary training in the Invisible Art . Anyone who desired to enrol could undertake an entrance exam to determine psionic aptitude , and then pay tuition fees . Basic training took a few tenday s . Successful graduates could receive psionic item s as awards and graduation gifts . Higher - level students were permitted access to the college ' s libraries and laboratories for research , and could rent living space in their headquarters .

title: Color spray
description: Color spray Color spray was a spell used by wizard s that , when cast , created a vivid cone or fan shape of clashing colors which sprang forth from the caster ' s hand or implement . Enemies hit were not only injured lightly by the sheer power of the magical light , but are also dazed into a momentary stupor . Prior to the Spellplague , the spell was more versatile and could cause creatures to become stunned , blinded , or possibly knock them unconscious .
description_long: Color spray Color spray was a spell used by wizard s that , when cast , created a vivid cone or fan shape of clashing colors which sprang forth from the caster ' s hand or implement . Enemies hit were not only injured lightly by the sheer power of the magical light , but are also dazed into a momentary stupor . Prior to the Spellplague , the spell was more versatile and could cause creatures to become stunned , blinded , or possibly knock them unconscious . The spell was also used by sorcerer s and contrary to its use afterwards , could only be cast a number of times per day that the caster had either prepared for it or had the energy left for spellcasting . After the Spellplague , the spell , while difficult enough in use to require a short rest from its caster before being used again , became usable many more times per day . The post sundering version of the spell was much like the older versions except it only blinded creatures and the large amount of damage it caused was all laid on the targets one after the other until all the damage was dealt out . This version also became more powerful if used with a higher spell level . Components .

title: Colson
description: Colson Colson was the adopted daughter of Wulfgar and Delly Curtie who Wulfgar saved from the small town of Auckney . She was originally the daughter of Meralda Ganderlay , Lady of Auckney , and Jaka Sculi . History .
description_long: Colson Colson was the adopted daughter of Wulfgar and Delly Curtie who Wulfgar saved from the small town of Auckney . She was originally the daughter of Meralda Ganderlay , Lady of Auckney , and Jaka Sculi . History . Meralda claimed that she was raped by Wulfgar and that Colson was his child , though in truth , it belonged to the charismatic Jaka Sculi who had sired her shortly before Meralda was to be married . Feeling guilty she helped Wulfgar escape the dungeons of Castle Auck . Wulfgar , having discovered the reality of the child ' s heritage , came back to Auckney several months later to see what had become of the brave woman and her child . Seeing that the child ' s life was in danger from a weak willed Lord , and his bitter sister , Wulfgar rescued her , promising Meralda that he would treat her as his own . Eventually he raised the child with Delly . Colson and Delly stayed at Captain Deudermont ' s house in Waterdeep while Wulfgar sailed with Deudermont in search of Aegis - fang . When Colson was a toddler , Delly was killed after being controlled by Khazid ' hea to fight with Orcs .

title: Colstan Rhuul
description: Colstan Rhuul Colstan Rhuul was an Illuskan human cleric of Bane and one of the most trusted agents of the Xanathar , the leader of the Xanathar Thieves ' Guild of Skullport . History . Colstan was a cleric of Bane , but he briefly turned to Cyric , before coming back to Bane when his god returned in 1372 DR .
description_long: Colstan Rhuul Colstan Rhuul was an Illuskan human cleric of Bane and one of the most trusted agents of the Xanathar , the leader of the Xanathar Thieves ' Guild of Skullport . History . Colstan was a cleric of Bane , but he briefly turned to Cyric , before coming back to Bane when his god returned in 1372 DR . Activities . Colstan was second - in - command of the Hand , the snatch - and - grab kidnapping agents of the Eye . He prided himself knowing by sight all the major players in Waterdhavian politics , though not necessarily the most famous . His main hobby was the uncovering identities of the Lords of Waterdeep . He managed to identify Brianne Byndraeth , a revelation that was very useful for his fellow Xanathar agent , Randulaith . He usually sent hireswords to start a brawl or similar incident with all new adventurers in the city , in order to steal their belongings and get them captured by the Hand . Personality . Colstan was a patient , calculating schemer who avoided personal danger whenever he can , preferring to work at a distance through hired knives and behind - the - scenes manipulation .

title: Combat readiness
description: Combat readiness Combat readiness enables the subject to act more rapidly in combat . Effect . When the spell is cast , the subject ' s eyes widen and briefly shine white .
description_long: Combat readiness Combat readiness enables the subject to act more rapidly in combat . Effect . When the spell is cast , the subject ' s eyes widen and briefly shine white . Thereafter until the spell ' s duration ends , the subject gains increased reaction time at the beginning of a combat encounter . The subject is also better able to defend against adversaries in flanking positions .

title: Combat sphere
description: Combat sphere The Combat sphere was a group of spells granted to cleric s , crusader s , and monk s that could be used to smite their foes . Appendix . Notes .
description_long: Combat sphere The Combat sphere was a group of spells granted to cleric s , crusader s , and monk s that could be used to smite their foes . Appendix . Notes . Spells in normal text were listed in the Tome of Magic 2nd edition . Spells in italics were added to the Combat Sphere in the sourcebook .

title: Combat veteran
description: Combat veteran Combat veterans are experienced and battle - hardened warlord s who have been through perils that should have killed them and lived to tell the tale . As a result , combat veterans have a measure of training earned not through study or practice , but actual experience on the battlefield , giving them an unusually improvised methodology that has proven very effective at keeping them alive . While combat veterans might not be as inspirational in a purely charismatic way as some warlords , they exude confidence in their men just by the very fact that , no matter what the world has thrown at them , the combat veteran still stands ready for battle .
description_long: Combat veteran Combat veterans are experienced and battle - hardened warlord s who have been through perils that should have killed them and lived to tell the tale . As a result , combat veterans have a measure of training earned not through study or practice , but actual experience on the battlefield , giving them an unusually improvised methodology that has proven very effective at keeping them alive . While combat veterans might not be as inspirational in a purely charismatic way as some warlords , they exude confidence in their men just by the very fact that , no matter what the world has thrown at them , the combat veteran still stands ready for battle . Abilities . Combat veterans have learned the hard way how to survive in battle and the techniques they ’ ve developed from direct combat experience reflect this . Combat veterans early on learn to keep their soldiers moving and out of danger , barking out a movement order on the spur of the moment . Combat veterans are also more durable , their bodies acclimatized to the perils of combat . As such , combat veterans more frequently recover from their wounds than most other warrior s as well as healing more quickly .

title: Combine
description: Combine Combine was an evocation spell that allowed the caster to temporarily increase his or her effective level with respect to turning undead and casting spells . This required the help of two to four additional priests . Effects .
description_long: Combine Combine was an evocation spell that allowed the caster to temporarily increase his or her effective level with respect to turning undead and casting spells . This required the help of two to four additional priests . Effects . The caster of this spell was usually the most experienced priest , who stood in the center as the assisting priests joined hands to form a ring around the caster . Upon casting the " combine " spell , his or her effective level was raised by one for each assisting priest . This allowed the caster to turn more powerful undead and cast spells with more range , duration , area of effect , or whatever parameters were related to the caster ' s experience level . The spells that could be enhanced this way were limited to the spells currently memorized by the caster of " combine " . The assisting priests had to concentrate on maintaining the " combine " effect while holding hands in a circle . Therefore they could not dodge attacks easily nor use weapons or shields . If any of the assisting priests lost concentration , the " combine " spell was canceled .

title: Comet K ' Thoutek
description: Comet K ' Thoutek K ' Thoutek is a large comet in Realmspace that circumnavigates the sun in an extremely elliptical orbit . Its only remaining inhabitant of a once large group of oortling s is their greatest wizard , now an undead haunt bent on revenge against the illithid s who destroyed the colony . The appearance of comet K ' Thoutek is seen as a sign for the birth of a powerful person by astronomers on Toril .
description_long: Comet K ' Thoutek K ' Thoutek is a large comet in Realmspace that circumnavigates the sun in an extremely elliptical orbit . Its only remaining inhabitant of a once large group of oortling s is their greatest wizard , now an undead haunt bent on revenge against the illithid s who destroyed the colony . The appearance of comet K ' Thoutek is seen as a sign for the birth of a powerful person by astronomers on Toril .

title: Command
description: Command Command was an enchantment spell that forced one subject to briefly obey a one - word command . Effects . The command word had to be given in a language the subject could understand and the effect lasted for only one minute .
description_long: Command Command was an enchantment spell that forced one subject to briefly obey a one - word command . Effects . The command word had to be given in a language the subject could understand and the effect lasted for only one minute . Commands that were known to work included : " approach " , " back " , " drop " , " fall " , " flee " , " fly " , " go " , " halt " , " leave " , " rest " , " run " , " sleep " , " stop " , and " surrender " . Newer versions of this spell were limited to " approach " , " drop " , " fall " , " flee " and " halt " . The command had to be unequivocal to the subject or it would be ignored or misinterpreted . A command to " suicide " would fail because the word was generally used as a noun rather than a verb . Unless the subject resisted , they would carry out the order to the best of their ability . If commanded to " die " , the target would fall in a faint and be unresponsive for one minute and then recover fully . The post sundering version effected a single target unless used with a higher level and the only commands that where known to be usable where " approach " , " drop " , " flee " , " grovel " and " halt " .

title: Command element
description: Command element Command element was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . There were four versions of this spell , one for each of the elements .
description_long: Command element Command element was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . There were four versions of this spell , one for each of the elements . The caster needed to memorize each version separately . Effects . This spell allowed the caster control over the four elements so long as they were not directly attacking or affecting living creatures with them . The caster could sculpt , part , move , and shape each element . The implications of these actions were only limited by the imagination and creativity of the caster . Examples of potential outcomes of using this spell included : Components . This spell only required verbal and somatic components to cast .

title: Command monster
description: Command monster Command monster was a divine enchantment spell , similar to " command " , that forced one creature to obey a one - word order . Effects . This spell was similar to the beginning level " command " spell but it did not require the caster to know a language understood by the target , was harder to resist , and it had greater range ( 60 yd / 55 m ) and duration .
description_long: Command monster Command monster was a divine enchantment spell , similar to " command " , that forced one creature to obey a one - word order . Effects . This spell was similar to the beginning level " command " spell but it did not require the caster to know a language understood by the target , was harder to resist , and it had greater range ( 60 yd / 55 m ) and duration . " Command monster " translated the command into whatever language or method of communication the target creature understood , as long as the creature had a modicum of intelligence ( enough to understand the command ) . Only creatures with greater life experience than the caster or exceptionally high intelligence had a chance to resist this spell . The command had to be clear , concise , and unequivocal for the creature to understand and not misinterpret . The target obeyed the command to the best of its ability for a minimum of five minutes and even longer for more experienced casters . If the command put the life of the target creature in jeopardy , then it got a chance to resist the spell even if it normally would not be able to do so .

title: Command water spirits
description: Command water spirits Command water spirits was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell did not actually allow the caster to command water spirits , instead it allowed them to manipulate the currents of large bodies of water to move objects on or under the surface .
description_long: Command water spirits Command water spirits was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell did not actually allow the caster to command water spirits , instead it allowed them to manipulate the currents of large bodies of water to move objects on or under the surface . This spell was particularly useful for controlling ships in becalmed water or during a severe storm . The caster could also use this spell to create a powerful undertow to drown his enemies . Components . This spell required a clear glass to cast .

title: Command word
description: Command word A command word , or a trigger word is a word that needs to be spoken aloud to activate a magical effect . A command word or words can be any word . Though common words are often avoided as to avoid activating a magical effect accidentally .
description_long: Command word A command word , or a trigger word is a word that needs to be spoken aloud to activate a magical effect . A command word or words can be any word . Though common words are often avoided as to avoid activating a magical effect accidentally . Often a command word is a seemingly nonsensical word or a word from an ancient language . In the time after the fall of Myth Drannor it was common for several centuries to hide a command word inside a more easily memorized phrase . However this fell out of use after too many magics were unintentionally activated . Often nowadays command words are best described as elegant nonsense . Overwords are command words that can activate many magical effects , spells or items . Several wizards attempt to learn these words and capbook s are sold of them at every Mage Fair . Careful folks keep command words secret , as many seek command words . The spells Identify and analyze dweomer can both reveal command words . Magic Items . Many magical items use command words to activate them . Often command words can be found written right on a magical item . Some time the word maybe hidden in a pattern or design .

title: Commander ' s ring
description: Commander ' s ring A commander ' s ring was a magic + 2 ring that was made by the War Wizards of Cormyr for their military commanders . Three times a day each , the ring could produce the effects of " daylight " , " feather fall " , " knock " , and " wall of force " , but only when the correct command word was uttered . If a purple dragon ring was worn on the same hand as this ring , they were treated as one ring .
description_long: Commander ' s ring A commander ' s ring was a magic + 2 ring that was made by the War Wizards of Cormyr for their military commanders . Three times a day each , the ring could produce the effects of " daylight " , " feather fall " , " knock " , and " wall of force " , but only when the correct command word was uttered . If a purple dragon ring was worn on the same hand as this ring , they were treated as one ring . The wearer was able to detect any purple dragon rings within 100 feet ( 30m ) , but this power of detection was blocked by stone , metal , wood , or other solid boundaries . These rings were worth around 120 , 000 gold pieces each . In the Year of the Ageless One ( 1479 DR ) , Royal Magician Ganrahast Aeiulvana , Lord Warder Vainrence , former Royal Magician Vangerdahast Aeiulvana , and Storm Silverhand found a way to enchant the rings to safely allow telepathic communication through the " team " and " commander ' s ring s " , a feat previously impossible due to the aftereffects of the Spellplague .

title: Commani
description: Commani The Commani were a tribe of nomadic human s living in the Hordelands . Territory . The Commani lived in the southwestern region of the Endless Waste .
description_long: Commani The Commani were a tribe of nomadic human s living in the Hordelands . Territory . The Commani lived in the southwestern region of the Endless Waste . Their lands bordered those of the Khassidi and Naican tribes . Society . They spoke the Commani language , a language influenced by the Raumatharan Empire , and understandable to speakers of Khassidi and Naican . The Commani were known to sometimes raid goats from the dwarves of the Herlinga clan . They were friends with the neighboring Khassidi and Naican tribes and hostile to the Fankiang and Kashghun . The Commani and Khassidi sometimes raided together in the west , and the Commani and Naican sometimes raided together to the south in Semphar . History . The Commani shared a common history with the Khassidi at many points . Long ago , during a " couralitai " , a grand council of the " khans " ( princes of the villages ) , all the tribes were in attendance . During a heated argument at the council , the " khan " of the Commani and his sons were assassinated . The murderers were never discovered , but the Commani suspected the Kashghun . Moreover , they believed that the Fankiang had defended the attackers .

title: Commani language
description: Commani language Commani was a language in the Imaskari languages group , spoken in the western Hordelands . Description . Like other languages in the same region , Commani had round and broad vowel sounds with rolled R sounds .
description_long: Commani language Commani was a language in the Imaskari languages group , spoken in the western Hordelands . Description . Like other languages in the same region , Commani had round and broad vowel sounds with rolled R sounds . Speakers . This tongue was spoken by the nomadic Commani tribe . Script . Commani did not have a written form . History . It was considered to be one of the Northern Imaskari languages and was strongly influenced by the empire of Raumathar .

title: Commarth
description: Commarth Commarth was the commander of the border armies of Sembia but he was also one of the Wearers of the Purple of the Cult of the Dragon . History . As leader of the Cult he was involved in the hunt for Shandril Shessair in 1357 DR , and was in his position in 1369 DR .
description_long: Commarth Commarth was the commander of the border armies of Sembia but he was also one of the Wearers of the Purple of the Cult of the Dragon . History . As leader of the Cult he was involved in the hunt for Shandril Shessair in 1357 DR , and was in his position in 1369 DR .

title: Common
description: Common Common was the trade language of Faerûn . Almost every sentient , civilized being spoke a smattering of it , and most were fluent . While most could not read or write the language , generally , the people of Faerûn were able to converse with each other in this language .
description_long: Common Common was the trade language of Faerûn . Almost every sentient , civilized being spoke a smattering of it , and most were fluent . While most could not read or write the language , generally , the people of Faerûn were able to converse with each other in this language . Description . Common was little more than a trade language ; that is , it was not useful for complicated topics . It was simple and not very expressive as a language . Speakers . Nearly everyone on the surface of Faerûn spoke Common as a second language , including non - human s . Those in remote areas spoke it badly , but most could get by . Dialects . Dialects varied from region to region , but generally , communication was possible . Calant was a melodious dialect spoken on the Sword Coast , while Kouroo was a Chult an variant , and Skaevrym was spoken in Sossal , but there were literally thousands of other local dialects . The Common spoken throughout Faerûn was properly called Thorasta by linguists and peoples from other continents , such as Zakhara .

title: Common bloodrose
description: Common bloodrose The common bloodrose was a flowering plant that could be found growing in the Rose Garden of the Battle of Bones . Description . This plant produced medium sized flowers that were the color of blood .
description_long: Common bloodrose The common bloodrose was a flowering plant that could be found growing in the Rose Garden of the Battle of Bones . Description . This plant produced medium sized flowers that were the color of blood . The bush was well - thorned and had dark green stems with dark leaves . History . Despite its name , the common bloodrose was anything but common due to its sensitivity to extreme temperatures . Some kind of magical force probably sustained it within the Rose Garden and the fickle temperature swings of the Battle of Bones . These plants were rumored to be originally cultivated by a group of cleric s living near Teziir . The plants were presented to the Lord of Suzail and never appeared in the wild until 1100 DR , the Year of the Bloodrose . None of these plants survived to the next year . Even those taken indoors perished . Adorning your clothing with a bloodrose was a sign of elite or wealthy status .

title: Common dictionary
description: Common dictionary Most players in our world simply use Common as a direct translation from whatever language they speak . However , certain words are different , as demonstrated by the following list . A .
description_long: Common dictionary Most players in our world simply use Common as a direct translation from whatever language they speak . However , certain words are different , as demonstrated by the following list . A . Alae : - Fortunate Meeting ( Contraction of an elven phrase ) . a greeting ( and reassurance of peaceful intentions ) between travelers in the southern and eastern coastlands around The Sea of Fallen Stars . B . Badaulder : - Balderdash , hogwash , nonsense , etc . Bluefin : - Tuna Blusterwing : - Grouse Boar : - Pig ( animal ) Broadleaf : - Kale Browncap : - Wild mushroom Burslake ( or simply slake ) : - Trout Bustard : - Turkey C . Codloose winker : - Lecher D . Darburl : - Angry Darkblade : - Mercenary with dubious morals and / or loyalty Doorguard : - A guard that guards a doorway of a building . Durgos : - Peace ( Corrupted from the orc " Durgreos " ) . Used by mongrelmen and human slavers . F . Fieldings : - Vegetables Fireseared : - Grilled Flamed : - Seared G . Galad ! : - Heartlands word meaning something akin to " Gadzooks ! " or " Zounds ! " Glim : - Eyecatchingly beautiful or flashy . Goldenpanned : - Sautéed Gulletfire : - Bad beer or wine . H .

title: Commune
description: Commune Commune was a divination spell that allowed a priest to ask yes or no questions of his or her deity . Effects . By means of this spell , the caster was put in contact with his or her deity , either directly or through a proxy , agent , or servant .
description_long: Commune Commune was a divination spell that allowed a priest to ask yes or no questions of his or her deity . Effects . By means of this spell , the caster was put in contact with his or her deity , either directly or through a proxy , agent , or servant . The priest was allowed to ask one question per experience level and could expect a truthful yes or no answer based on the entity ' s knowledge at the time . Note that even greater deities were not necessarily omniscient , so answers such as " I don ' t know " or " unclear " were possible . If a yes or no answer would be ambiguous , the entity could choose to elaborate with a few more words if it served their purpose . If the caster ' s attention wavered between questions , the spell was ended . The post sundering version allowed three questions regardless of level and if a one word answer would be misleading the answer could be a short phrase . if cast several times before a long rest it becomes about 25 % more unlikely to get a answer . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required the use of the caster ' s holy symbol or divine focus , some ( un ) holy water , and burning incense .

title: Commune with nature
description: Commune with nature Commune with nature was a divination spell that allowed the caster to learn about the surrounding terrain for a few miles / kilometers . The more advanced the caster , the further the effect . Effects .
description_long: Commune with nature Commune with nature was a divination spell that allowed the caster to learn about the surrounding terrain for a few miles / kilometers . The more advanced the caster , the further the effect . Effects . This spell attuned the caster with the natural surroundings , extending outward for a few miles / kilometers in all directions . From this , knowledge could be gleaned about the terrain , plant life , mineral deposits , bodies of water , buildings , animal population , presence of woodland creatures , presence of unnatural creatures , presence of people , and the general health of the region . Up to three facts could be learned about the area in the time it took to cast the spell . Older versions of this spell allowed more facts to be learned , but they were more narrowly limited . The range of this spell depended on the power of the caster , but was quite limited underground , compared to casting the spell outdoors . Buildings appeared as blank areas in the caster ' s vision because the spell did not function where nature had been replaced by construction or settlement ( such as in dungeons and towns ) .

title: Community domain
description: Community domain The Community domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters community spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Exalted Deeds " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Community Domain Powers .
description_long: Community domain The Community domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters community spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Exalted Deeds " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Community Domain Powers . The cleric gains the ability to cast " calm emotions " once per day as a spell - like ability .

title: Community of the high brows
description: Community of the high brows The " community of the high brows " was a mountain giant tribe dwelling in the Orbrekh in the Orsraun Mountains of Turmish . Organization . The community of the high brows was led by Oogle , its shaman , in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR .
description_long: Community of the high brows The " community of the high brows " was a mountain giant tribe dwelling in the Orbrekh in the Orsraun Mountains of Turmish . Organization . The community of the high brows was led by Oogle , its shaman , in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . There were about 30 to 35 mountain giants in the tribe . Behavior . The giants wished only to be left alone in peace . Their relative peacefulness made the Orbrekh the safest part of the Orsrauns for travellers . Relationships . The mountain giants wiped out the Onusclan orc s , who dwelled in the rest of the Orsrauns , when they crossed into the Orbrekh . The community had an unknown relationship with the Emerald Enclave , which saw Enclave druids regularly visiting the tribe .

title: Companions Codex
description: Companions Codex The Companions Codex is a series of novels by R . A . Salvatore featuring Drizzt Do ' Urden and the reborn Companions of the Hall .
description_long: Companions Codex The Companions Codex is a series of novels by R . A . Salvatore featuring Drizzt Do ' Urden and the reborn Companions of the Hall . The series follows the Neverwinter Saga and " The Companions " . " The Companions " sets up the rebirth of the Companions of the Hall and leads directly into the first book of the Companions Codex series and thus could be considered " book zero " of the series . Comics . There is also a series of comics that leads up to the beginning of " Night of the Hunter " . The collection is not officially part of the Companions Codex , but it is closely connected and gives more information about how Tos ' un Armgo and Doum ' wielle Armgo came to arrive in the Underdark .

title: Companions of the Hall
description: Companions of the Hall The Companions of the Hall was the unofficial name for the adventurers who retook and subsequently defended Mithral Hall . The members consisted of King Bruenor Battlehammer , Drizzt Do ' Urden and his companion Guenhwyvar , and Catti - brie , Wulfgar and Regis . Ivan and Pikel Bouldershoulder were also usually included as members due to their extensive help in defending Mithral Hall from Obould Many - Arrows , as was Thibbledorf Pwent , Bruenor ' s bodygard .
description_long: Companions of the Hall The Companions of the Hall was the unofficial name for the adventurers who retook and subsequently defended Mithral Hall . The members consisted of King Bruenor Battlehammer , Drizzt Do ' Urden and his companion Guenhwyvar , and Catti - brie , Wulfgar and Regis . Ivan and Pikel Bouldershoulder were also usually included as members due to their extensive help in defending Mithral Hall from Obould Many - Arrows , as was Thibbledorf Pwent , Bruenor ' s bodygard . History . As of 1372 DR , Bruenor , having discovered that what he thought was Gauntlgrym was actually the ruins of Baffenburg , lead the political overtures with the fledgling kingdom of Many - Arrows . Wulfgar then left the group , returning to Icewind Dale to rejoin the Elk Tribe . Cattie - brie gave up the life of the warrior and embraced tutelage from Alustriel in the Art . In 1385 DR at the beginning of the Spellplague ( the time the book The Ghost King took place ) , Catti - brie was struck by Blue Fire during her meditations and got caught between two planes of existence : the Shadowfell and the Prime Material Plane .

title: Companions of the Noble Heart
description: Companions of the Noble Heart The Companions of the Noble Heart were a knightly order of paladin s devoted to the faith of Ilmater , the One Who Endures . Activities . The Companions of the Noble Heart had the duty of seeking out destroying the cruel , those people who tortured and enjoyed the suffering of others .
description_long: Companions of the Noble Heart The Companions of the Noble Heart were a knightly order of paladin s devoted to the faith of Ilmater , the One Who Endures . Activities . The Companions of the Noble Heart had the duty of seeking out destroying the cruel , those people who tortured and enjoyed the suffering of others . The Companions were very aggressive in seeking out their chosen adversaries . They especially disliked the church of Loviatar , their greatest foes , and once they had slain all evil - doers within a temple of Loviatar , the Companions would happily destroy the building , right down to the ground .
