The five council positions are held by : House Selemchant who sponsors the Cowled Wizards of Athkatla , House Dannihyr which belongs to the Shadow Thieves , House Alibakkar , House Ophal and House Nashivaar which is closely allied with the Church of Cyric . 1372 DR . The Council of Six is the mysterious , anonymous group that rules over the nation of Amn , their goal being to keep money flowing through the country at all costs . It is based in the Council House , a fortress - like structure in Athkatla . Each member is ranked in hierarchy with the highest having the most seniority . They are , from highest to lowest , Meisarch , Tessarch , Namarch , Iltarch , Pommarch and Dahaunarch . When a member of the council dies , every member below them will move up a rank and a new Dahaunarch is elected from among the wealthiest and thus most powerful merchant families of Amn . There have only been eleven rulers since the creation of the council in 1333 DR . Anonymity . The council ' s members choose to remain anonymous .

title: Council of Four
description: Council of Four The Council of Four was the governing body of the city of Baldur ' s Gate consisting of four powerful individuals elected for life . The council was part of the Lords ' Alliance , which includes Waterdeep , Neverwinter and Silverymoon , among others . < ref name = FRCS / CotRp27 > < / ref > The council is now replaced by a parliament .
description_long: Council of Four The Council of Four was the governing body of the city of Baldur ' s Gate consisting of four powerful individuals elected for life . The council was part of the Lords ' Alliance , which includes Waterdeep , Neverwinter and Silverymoon , among others . < ref name = FRCS / CotRp27 > < / ref > The council is now replaced by a parliament . History . The history of the council dates back to the earliest days of Baldur ' s Gate and the conflict between the rich farmers of the walled city and the sea - captains of the harbor who refused to pay for entering the gate that had been financed by their colleague Balduran . The captains overthrew the farmers and the four eldest among them was installed as rulers , jokingly calling themselves " dukes " . Sometime before 1479 DR Grand Duke Valarken tried to seize power using lycanthropic mercenaries but failed . After that , surviving Grand Duke Portyr dissolved the council and now rules the city together with a parliament . Grand Dukes . In 1357 DR the dukes were :

title: Council of Guilds
description: Council of Guilds The Council of Guilds ran the daily affairs of Daggerford . Activities . Imitating the masked Lords of Waterdeep , the council members wore masks and shrouded themselves in robes to hide their identities at council meetings , but everyone in Daggerford knew who the council members were .
description_long: Council of Guilds The Council of Guilds ran the daily affairs of Daggerford . Activities . Imitating the masked Lords of Waterdeep , the council members wore masks and shrouded themselves in robes to hide their identities at council meetings , but everyone in Daggerford knew who the council members were . The council consisted of the heads of the town ' s loose , informal trade guilds : the Smiths ' Guild , the Merchants ' Guild , the Tanners ' Guild , the Farmers ' Guild , the Watermen ' s Guild , the Rivermen ' s Guild , the Taverners ' Guild , and a handful of others . The council also included the head of the militia , the duke ' s master - at - arms , and the chief priests of the town ' s four primary religions : Chauntea , Lathander , Tempus , and Tymora .

title: Council of Loggers
description: Council of Loggers The Council of Loggers was a trade guild located in Estanil in the Hordelands . Activities . Comprised of mill owners and representatives from companies who harvested lumber from the Shalhoond , the Council of Loggers used their considerable economical leverage to control Abul Fiydah , the Amir of Estanil .
description_long: Council of Loggers The Council of Loggers was a trade guild located in Estanil in the Hordelands . Activities . Comprised of mill owners and representatives from companies who harvested lumber from the Shalhoond , the Council of Loggers used their considerable economical leverage to control Abul Fiydah , the Amir of Estanil . Threats of strike , embargoes , and even secession were used to undermine Abul ' s authority . History . The Council of Loggers , and Estanil along with it , was utterly destroyed several times in the past when the Caliph of Semphar tired of their threats . Base of Operations . Estanil was the base of operations for the Council of Loggers .

title: Council of Mages
description: Council of Mages The Council of Mages was a primarily advisory group of arcane spellcasters who served the Forest Kingdom and its king directly . Activities . While the War Wizards would focus purely on military matters , it was the Council ' s job to advise the king on all matters magical ( thereby helping to craft the laws governing magic ) , create magic items for the royal family , and battle the most dire of magical threats to Cormyr .
description_long: Council of Mages The Council of Mages was a primarily advisory group of arcane spellcasters who served the Forest Kingdom and its king directly . Activities . While the War Wizards would focus purely on military matters , it was the Council ' s job to advise the king on all matters magical ( thereby helping to craft the laws governing magic ) , create magic items for the royal family , and battle the most dire of magical threats to Cormyr . All available members of the Council met once every month to hear the concerns of arcane spellcasters in Cormyr and consider all applicants who wished to join the War Wizards . History . In 1284 DR , when Rhigaerd II was prevented from ascending the throne by Salember , the War Wizards were divided in their loyalties . Two years later , the Royal Magician Jorunhast made the executive decision to kill Salember but , in doing so , was exiled for murdering a member of the royal family . The position of Royal Magician was disbanded and without a single polarizing individual to lead them , the War Wizards were gravely weakened and lost a lot of power and prestige .

title: Council of Merchants
description: Council of Merchants The Council of Merchants were the rulers of the Shining Lands . Organization . The eleven wealthiest merchants within the Shining Lands comprised the Council of Merchants .
description_long: Council of Merchants The Council of Merchants were the rulers of the Shining Lands . Organization . The eleven wealthiest merchants within the Shining Lands comprised the Council of Merchants . This was determined by simple arithmetic . Those with the most income were awarded seats . Because of this , at least a few council seats changed hands on a yearly basis . As of 1367 DR , Kara Jeratma was the head of the council ; a position her family held since her great - grandfather Jeradeem . Aside from the main Council , each city within the Shining Lands had their own version of the Council of Merchants consisting of the eleven richest merchants within that particular city .

title: Council of Savants
description: Council of Savants The Council of Savants were an advisory body to the duergar Deepking of Gracklstugh , and was made up of derro savants . Organization . Only the thirty - six best derro savants were admitted into the council , and succession almost always included an incumbent member ' s demise .
description_long: Council of Savants The Council of Savants were an advisory body to the duergar Deepking of Gracklstugh , and was made up of derro savants . Organization . Only the thirty - six best derro savants were admitted into the council , and succession almost always included an incumbent member ' s demise . The savants controlled members of some duergar clans through magic and guile , and were always looking for ways to expand their influence . History . The start of the Council coincided with the beginning of the derro presence in the Deepkingdom . In the Year of the Cairngorm Crown , 972 DR , the scattered derro tribes in the Northdark launched yet another Uniting War , this time against Gracklstugh . The duergar under the new Deepking Tarngardt Steelshadow VII ( his predecessor Barthorn V having died in the derro ' s assault ) launched a crusade to exterminate the scattered derro clans throughout the Northdark , and several hundred derro were brought back to Gracklstugh in chains . For centuries , the derro were only labor slaves but slowly their numbers increased .

title: Council of Sparkling Stones
description: Council of Sparkling Stones The Council of Sparkling Stones is an elected council in Mirabar . Members must swear an oath of loyalty to Mirabar and its marchion . It meets each fall to plan the year ahead and organise trade agreements .
description_long: Council of Sparkling Stones The Council of Sparkling Stones is an elected council in Mirabar . Members must swear an oath of loyalty to Mirabar and its marchion . It meets each fall to plan the year ahead and organise trade agreements . Composition . As of 1368 DR , the Council comprises 42 members . Of these , 10 are shield dwarves and 32 are human s . 16 councilors are female , and 26 are male . The marchion ( currently Elastul Raurym ) is the chief justice . Elections are held annually in the spring to determine the new members who will take their positions at the next meeting in the fall . Meeting . The Council meets once a year in the fall , usually over four days . There is an informal discussion , then a chance for short , formal speeches , then a secret ballot to decide upon what has been discussed . The marchion then travels to the cities in the south to personally bring the news , and to negotiate trade , acquiring deals for luxuries not available in Mirabar .

title: Council of Spiders
description: Council of Spiders The Council of Spiders was an organization of drow wizard s who sought representation on the Ruling Council of Menzoberranzan . History . In the late 15th century DR , minor wizards of various noble houses of Menzoberranzan ( most prominently House Xorlarrin and House Barrison Del ' Armgo ) formed the Council of Spiders to gain seats on the Ruling Council alongside the priestesses of Lolth .
description_long: Council of Spiders The Council of Spiders was an organization of drow wizard s who sought representation on the Ruling Council of Menzoberranzan . History . In the late 15th century DR , minor wizards of various noble houses of Menzoberranzan ( most prominently House Xorlarrin and House Barrison Del ' Armgo ) formed the Council of Spiders to gain seats on the Ruling Council alongside the priestesses of Lolth . A major method was to get the support of a higher - ranking wizard . Raelaryn Xorlarrin , one of the Council ' s elders , invited his cousin Hoshtar to a meeting in the ruins of House Srune ' Lett ' s compound in Narbondellyn . During the meeting , Raelaryn and an elder from House Barrison Del ' Armgo were killed by Merinid Dalael , an assassin from the Jaezred Chaulssin , and Hoshtar was taken captive . Adventurers in the employ of House Xorlarrin , House Melarn , and Bregan D ' aerthe arrived looking for the prisoner , resulting in a fight with the Council of Spiders . However , the adventurers defeated the Merinid and rescued Hoshtarr , discovering the assassins ' plot . The Council also set up a meeting with the Archmage of Menzoberranzan , Gromph Baenre .

title: Council of the Marches
description: Council of the Marches The Council of the Marches was the ruling body of the League of the Silver Marches consisting of the High Lady , representatives of the six signatory states ( known as Peers ) , the commander of the Ardent Legion , the Lady Protector and a rotating Member - at - Large appointed by the Lady .
description_long: Council of the Marches The Council of the Marches was the ruling body of the League of the Silver Marches consisting of the High Lady , representatives of the six signatory states ( known as Peers ) , the commander of the Ardent Legion , the Lady Protector and a rotating Member - at - Large appointed by the Lady .

title: Counterspell
description: Counterspell Counterspell was an abjuration spell that attempted to stop another spell from being cast . Effect . If a creature within 60 feet ( 18 .
description_long: Counterspell Counterspell was an abjuration spell that attempted to stop another spell from being cast . Effect . If a creature within 60 feet ( 18 . 3 meters ) of the caster attempted to cast a spell , then the caster could make a instant reaction to attempt to counter it . If the spell was of the same spell level as " counterspell " , then it would end but if it was more powerful it had a chance of failing . If the caster wanted to interrupt a spell of higher level she could cast " counterspell " as a higher level spell , if the targeted spell had the same level or lower then it would be stopped . Components . Only a somatic component was needed .

title: Courage
description: Courage Courage was an enchantment spell that crusader s and battle clerics could use to boost the morale of up to 200 individuals organized in a fighting unit . Effects . This spell lasted until sundown or until the unit was faced with a situation that challenged their morale , whichever came first .
description_long: Courage Courage was an enchantment spell that crusader s and battle clerics could use to boost the morale of up to 200 individuals organized in a fighting unit . Effects . This spell lasted until sundown or until the unit was faced with a situation that challenged their morale , whichever came first . Multiple castings of this spell did not stack , i . e . , no more than one " courage " spell could be active on a unit at a time . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a small cube of cast iron .

title: Courageous
description: Courageous The Courageous , or Abd al - Jari , was a group of farisan who fought for the Preachers in 1367 DR . Base of Operations . The Courageous were based in the fortress of Sarahin located deep within the Haunted Lands .
description_long: Courageous The Courageous , or Abd al - Jari , was a group of farisan who fought for the Preachers in 1367 DR . Base of Operations . The Courageous were based in the fortress of Sarahin located deep within the Haunted Lands . Activities . This group served the holy slayer s of the Preachers as a source of muscle when needed . Members . All of the members of the Courageous were dwarves . Their commander was Mamoud ibn Asra .

title: Couralitai
description: Couralitai A couralitai was a scheduled meeting of the khans or princes of the people inhabiting the Hordelands . History . These meetings occurred every fall at the vale of Ejen Horo , located between the Khopet Dag Mountains and the Mountains of Copper .
description_long: Couralitai A couralitai was a scheduled meeting of the khans or princes of the people inhabiting the Hordelands . History . These meetings occurred every fall at the vale of Ejen Horo , located between the Khopet Dag Mountains and the Mountains of Copper . The couralitai was traditionally used to arrange marriages , settle feuds , determine blood prices for murders , and even to acknowledge a new khan . A khahan could also be elected during these meetings .

title: Courdh Mizzrym
description: Courdh Mizzrym Courdh Mizzrym was the Archmage Emeritus of Menzoberranzan and house wizard of the House Mizzrym in 1370 DR . Courdh was the aged Past Master who oversaw all teaching at the Academy . He was in charge of experimenting with and guarding the most powerful magical items held by Sorcere .
description_long: Courdh Mizzrym Courdh Mizzrym was the Archmage Emeritus of Menzoberranzan and house wizard of the House Mizzrym in 1370 DR . Courdh was the aged Past Master who oversaw all teaching at the Academy . He was in charge of experimenting with and guarding the most powerful magical items held by Sorcere . He was also secretly Sorcere ' s overseer of security , and hence the spymaster in charge of watching the noble houses .

title: Court District
description: Court District The Court District was one of the wards of Huzuz , the City of Delights . Description . The Court District was the wealthiest section of Huzuz .
description_long: Court District The Court District was one of the wards of Huzuz , the City of Delights . Description . The Court District was the wealthiest section of Huzuz . It encompassed the royal palace and had a splendid view of the Golden Mosque . Since anyone of note , and wealth , desired to live in the Court District , the influx of inhabitants caused builders to elevate their construction in the form of beautiful towering minarets that could be found throughout this section of the city . The Court District was virtually surrounded by many other districts ; including the Craft District to the north , the East District to the east , the Affluent District to the south , and the Pilgrims ' District to the west . Major roads within the Court District included : Activities . This district housed a myriad of personalities including wealthy merchants , mysterious sorcerers , and nobles of the court .

title: Court herald
description: Court herald Court herald was a prestige class in Faerûn that was closely related to that of the Loremaster . Heralds focused primarily on gaining knowledge . Becoming a herald .
description_long: Court herald Court herald was a prestige class in Faerûn that was closely related to that of the Loremaster . Heralds focused primarily on gaining knowledge . Becoming a herald . Anyone who decided to enter into this prestige class was visited by two experienced heralds who presented the novice with several books containing general lore . After answering questions from the prospective herald , they provided him or her with contacts , usually in the form of knowledgeable sages or Harpers , then took their leave . They later checked up on the student , sometimes in secret , reporting his or her progress to even more learned heralds .

title: Court of Enlightenment
description: Court of Enlightenment The Court of Enlightenment , or the first court , was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . This large court faced the Golden Mosque .
description_long: Court of Enlightenment The Court of Enlightenment , or the first court , was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . This large court faced the Golden Mosque . Elaborate decorative tiles of red and blue covered many of the surfaces . When viewed from the upper levels these tiles formed an outline of the Golden Mosque . The massive area in front of the Court could easily hold 50 , 000 people at one time . Activities . The Grand Caliph would address his people on his Ascension Day from the Pavilion of the Enlightened Throne found within the Court . History . The red and blue tiles used to depict past Grand Caliph s , but Khalil al - Assad al - Zahir had the tiles rearranged to show the Golden Mosque and demonstrate his devotion to the Enlightened Gods .

title: Court of Grandeur
description: Court of Grandeur The Court of Grandeur , or the third court , was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . This large court was decorated with a bounty of flowers and climbing vines .
description_long: Court of Grandeur The Court of Grandeur , or the third court , was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . This large court was decorated with a bounty of flowers and climbing vines . Statues of historical Grand Caliph s were scattered throughout the area . All of the priceless works of art were carved by master artisans . Activities . Because of the beautiful decorations and intimate atmosphere , the third court was a favored spot for romantic meetings . Many of the bowers here were enchanted to block unwanted eavesdropping , making them ideal for these meetings . However , some were enchanted to relay messages to the Grand Vizier ' s attention . Inhabitants . Priests of Selan grew the rarest flowers in all of Zakhara within the Court of Grandeur . A pair of singing tree s could also be found here .

title: Court of Proclamations
description: Court of Proclamations The Court of Proclamations , or the second court , was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Activities . This large court was capable of holding 2 , 000 visitors at one time .
description_long: Court of Proclamations The Court of Proclamations , or the second court , was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Activities . This large court was capable of holding 2 , 000 visitors at one time . Important proclamations were announced here on a weekly basis . The nature of these announcements included awarding new titles , commendations , as well as announcing individuals who had earned disgrace and censure from the court .

title: Court of Rhythm
description: Court of Rhythm The Court of Rhythm was a religious organization in Zakhara whose members followed the teachings of Hajama , the Zakharan god of courage . The Court of Rhythm favored the short sword . Activities .
description_long: Court of Rhythm The Court of Rhythm was a religious organization in Zakhara whose members followed the teachings of Hajama , the Zakharan god of courage . The Court of Rhythm favored the short sword . Activities . Mystics of the Court of Rhythm gained their spiritual power through pounding drums in rhythm , usually with many others of their organization . They were popular among dancing groups , but singing and chanting mystics did not care for them . Base of Operations . Members of the Court of Rhythm were found within the Ruined Kingdoms , in Afyal , and scattered throughout the Crowded Sea .

title: Court of Rorn
description: Court of Rorn The Court of Rorn was a religious cult dedicated to the primordial Rorn , that operated in Fimbrul , Returned Abeir . Activities . The Court of Rorn goal was to prepare the world for the awakening of Rorn .
description_long: Court of Rorn The Court of Rorn was a religious cult dedicated to the primordial Rorn , that operated in Fimbrul , Returned Abeir . Activities . The Court of Rorn goal was to prepare the world for the awakening of Rorn . In order to do that , its members sought to cripple the dragon hegemony of Returned Abeir , and also tried to control at least the lesser dragon nobles . They also tried to destroy the gods , and studied them and their followers . Membership . The Court of Rorn was composed of earth giant s , who were the most high ranking members of the organization . Below them was a legion of servant creatures of any race , spies , informants , cultists , and sellswords across Returned Abeir , many who were not aware that they were working for a primordial . Members of the Court of Rorn also employed prehistoric beasts such as felljaws , haraevors , and tentacled torments , who were preserved since ancient times by Rorn itself . Rorn was the nominal leader of the Court , and although he was capable of commune with its members , due to its sleeping state members the Court of Rorn acted on their own . History .

title: Courtyard of Lolth
description: Courtyard of Lolth The Courtyard of Lolth was a temple dedicated to Lolth in Maerimydra and was destroyed during the Silence of Lolth . Location . Located on the noble plateau above the rest of Maerimydra , the Courtyard of Lolth was reached from the city proper by ascending a great sweeping staircase at the end of the Grand Boulevard .
description_long: Courtyard of Lolth The Courtyard of Lolth was a temple dedicated to Lolth in Maerimydra and was destroyed during the Silence of Lolth . Location . Located on the noble plateau above the rest of Maerimydra , the Courtyard of Lolth was reached from the city proper by ascending a great sweeping staircase at the end of the Grand Boulevard . Structure . Exterior . The Courtyard of Lolth was constructed in the semblance of an enormous spider with an elegantly sculpted archway forming the stony fangs of the building . Each wall was adorned with designs of alien and distorted spiders . Interior . Inside the Courtyard of Lolth , the temple was formed of numerous rooms and its entrance was flanked by orbs of glowing , pale , blue - green magic al light . After the temple ' s destruction in 1372 DR , the interior of the Courtyard of Lolth was nothing more than a blasted ruin , with a blackened crater at its center . Defenses . Merely passing through the archway of the Courtyard of Lolth rendered all invisible creatures visible . This was an " invisbility purge " effect that emanated from the glowing orbs in the archway . History .

title: Cowled Wizards
description: Cowled Wizards The Cowled Wizards are a secret organization of wizard s in Amn . They were originally created by Alisar of Esmeltaran in the 13th century . Alisar and the mages wanted to preserve magical lore and they saw themselves as saviors of the Art and as agents of Azuth and Deneir .
description_long: Cowled Wizards The Cowled Wizards are a secret organization of wizard s in Amn . They were originally created by Alisar of Esmeltaran in the 13th century . Alisar and the mages wanted to preserve magical lore and they saw themselves as saviors of the Art and as agents of Azuth and Deneir . Moving underground , they became librarians of lore and teachers to those with potential . The Cowled Wizards also kept an eye on foreign wizards passing through Amn , keeping rogue wizards in line to protect Amnians and the Cowled Wizards ' secrecy . Organization . Each cell of Cowled Wizards is isolated in a town or city and ruled by the highest - level mage in that area . As long as politics do not pit one cell leader against the first and still largest Athkatlan cell and its leader , local Cowled Wizards can meet others in Athkatla in secret rooms beneath Jann Lane . There they can organize things and get into contact with distant Cowled Wizard cells , and join or communicate with them . By day , the members work as merchants , booksellers , herbalists , apothecaries , or the like . During their meetings they wear their cowled hoods and robes .

title: Coyo
description: Coyo Coyo was a Nexal an general of history . History . Under the rule of Zomoc , Coyo was the chief general of the Revered Councilor .
description_long: Coyo Coyo was a Nexal an general of history . History . Under the rule of Zomoc , Coyo was the chief general of the Revered Councilor . He was tasked with the mission of subjugating the fierce Kolan tribes . Coyo accomplished the task but Zomoc grew jealous and so plotted against him with the patriarch of Zaltec . At the peak of the celebration , the patriarch announced a very special honor for Coyo : he would offer his heart to the god . Meanwhile , the patriarch cast a spell to confuse Coyo ' s mind so the great general went voluntarily to the altar , where he was sacrificed . Zomoc was pleased , despite the fact Coyo had always been loyal to him . However , in time , Zomoc descended into paranoia , always suspecting someone of plotting against him . After five years , Zomoc died in his sleep with his face distorted by horror . His successor was Itzo , the nephew of Coyo .

title: Cracker and Whacker
description: Cracker and Whacker Cracker and Whacker were twin morning star s that were the chief weapons of the dwarf Athrogate . Description . " Cracker " and " Whacker " were both gray glassteel morning star s , with spiked metal heads attached to the ends of adamantine chains .
description_long: Cracker and Whacker Cracker and Whacker were twin morning star s that were the chief weapons of the dwarf Athrogate . Description . " Cracker " and " Whacker " were both gray glassteel morning star s , with spiked metal heads attached to the ends of adamantine chains . Athrogate generally wielded " Cracker " in the left hand and " Whacker " in the right hand . Powers . On command , " Cracker " emitted from the small nubs on the striking ball a dark reddish and chalky fluid , the ichor of a rust monster , which corroded other metals on contact . " Whacker " coated itself with a clear , blue - gray , oily liquid known as oil of impact , which oozed from the spikes . Used together , with first a strike by " Cracker " then strikes by " Whacker " , Athrogate could smash anything from a thick iron wall to an iron golem into rust flakes . History . In 1484 DR , Athrogate used his morning stars to smash through the iron wall sealing off Mithral Hall from the Underdark .

title: Crackers
description: Crackers Crackers were crispy tidbits of bread . A selection with herbs from the Dalelands was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description .
description_long: Crackers Crackers were crispy tidbits of bread . A selection with herbs from the Dalelands was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description . Crackers were produced in several different flavors : onion , garlic , pepper , or savory . Packages contained three dozen crackers , and could be ordered either with a single flavor or in " Gourmet Packs " that contained all four flavors .

title: Crackletongue
description: Crackletongue Crackletongue was the magical saber of Zaranda Star . It was a saber of sharpness + 5 , with a basket hilt . When drawn , blue flames ran along the blade .
description_long: Crackletongue Crackletongue was the magical saber of Zaranda Star . It was a saber of sharpness + 5 , with a basket hilt . When drawn , blue flames ran along the blade . The flames crackled when it was around evil . When the saber struck something evil , it emitted a snarl and showers of blue flame .

title: Craft District
description: Craft District The Craft District was a district of Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . The Craft District was found in the North Quarter and covered a large portion of the northeast corner of Huzuz .
description_long: Craft District The Craft District was a district of Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . The Craft District was found in the North Quarter and covered a large portion of the northeast corner of Huzuz . This district was nestled between the Warehouse District along the Street of the Ajami to the west and the East District along the Ghost ' s Route to the south . The Street of the Learned exited Huzuz through the Craft District , leading many students to the ferries that transported them to Al - Bidir Sallah on the opposite bank of Al - Sarif River . Inhabitants . As the name implied , the Craft District was the home of many artisans and craftsmen , including some major families and guilds . Those with the coin to spend to satisfy their eclectic tastes often came to the Craft District to sate their curiosity and desires .

title: Craggnor
description: Craggnor Craggnor was a member of the reformed Cult of the Dragon under Severin Silrajin . History . Craggnor was a cultist and a great friend of White Wyrmspeaker Varramzord .
description_long: Craggnor Craggnor was a member of the reformed Cult of the Dragon under Severin Silrajin . History . Craggnor was a cultist and a great friend of White Wyrmspeaker Varramzord . For this , he was kidnapped by Talis Kasterel , who hoped to learn from Craggnor the weaknesses of Varramzord . He transported Craggnor to the Cult ' s hunting lodge in the Greypeak Mountains . Despite bribes and torture , Craggnor did not betray Varramzord .

title: Cragmaw tribe
description: Cragmaw tribe The Cragmaw were a tribe of goblin s , bugbear s , and hobgoblin s operating in Neverwinter Wood and the Triboar Trail . The members of the tribe sharpened their teeth , which led to the name of the tribe . King Grol ruled the tribe as a whole from Cragmaw Castle , while Klarg lead a smaller group from the Cragmaw Hideout .
description_long: Cragmaw tribe The Cragmaw were a tribe of goblin s , bugbear s , and hobgoblin s operating in Neverwinter Wood and the Triboar Trail . The members of the tribe sharpened their teeth , which led to the name of the tribe . King Grol ruled the tribe as a whole from Cragmaw Castle , while Klarg lead a smaller group from the Cragmaw Hideout . The Cragmaws were hired by Nezznar to capture Gundren Rockseeker .

title: Crags
description: Crags The Crags were a series of hills and broken mounds south of Mirabar . History . In the past many mines were located in this area .
description_long: Crags The Crags were a series of hills and broken mounds south of Mirabar . History . In the past many mines were located in this area . The mines are dead and worked out and now home to various creatures . The kingdom of Grimmantle was also located here . Geography . The terrain was quite harsh .

title: Cranium rat
description: Cranium rat Cranium rats were psionically enhanced rat s , transformed by mind flayer s through bombardment with psionic energy . Behavior . When isolated , cranium rats behaved like ordinary rats , using their telepathy to communicate basic feelings .
description_long: Cranium rat Cranium rats were psionically enhanced rat s , transformed by mind flayer s through bombardment with psionic energy . Behavior . When isolated , cranium rats behaved like ordinary rats , using their telepathy to communicate basic feelings . When forming a swarm , however , the collective intelligence of the rats was combined into a single collective entity , which could also access enhanced psionic abilities from the mind flayer that created them . In such cases , a swarm of cranium rats could use psionic powers similar to spell s . Ecology . Cranium rats were used as spies for mind flayer colonies . They infiltrated surface communities and read the inhabitants ' thoughts , later transmitting them to the elder brain .

title: Crannak Smoulderburn
description: Crannak Smoulderburn Crannak Smoulderburn ( pronounced KRAN - uck SMOL - der - burn ) was a derro smith and a high - ranking member of the Cult of the Eternal Flame in the Moonsea region . Description . Crannak was bald - his hair frequently burned off in fires of his own creation .
description_long: Crannak Smoulderburn Crannak Smoulderburn ( pronounced KRAN - uck SMOL - der - burn ) was a derro smith and a high - ranking member of the Cult of the Eternal Flame in the Moonsea region . Description . Crannak was bald - his hair frequently burned off in fires of his own creation . His left arm ended in a stump , to which he had attached an iron prosthetic of a clenched fist . Personality . Crannak was a pyromaniac whose only desire was to see everything on fire . In his rare lucid moments he demonstrated a manipulative cunning , placing his devoted apprentices in between himself and sources of danger , fleeing if he felt overmatched . He was seen cackling maniacally in the presence of fire . Possessions . Crannak was noted to have possessed a " healing ember " , and sometimes carried unstable magical smoke bombs . He set fires and used his magic in battle but also carried a dagger . History . At one point , Crannak was caught in a fire that severely burned the left half of his body - leaving him blind in one eye and severely mutilating his hand .

title: Crawler
description: Crawler Crawlers were small elemental vermin native to the Elemental Plane of Earth that could also be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . Crawlers had a crested dog - like head with feelers located near the snout .
description_long: Crawler Crawlers were small elemental vermin native to the Elemental Plane of Earth that could also be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . Crawlers had a crested dog - like head with feelers located near the snout . Their sharp claws were used to dig through soil . Most crawlers were brown in color . Ecology . A crawler used its feelers to navigate in total darkness and to locate food . Crawlers survived by consuming vegetable and mineral matter . They were small but aggressive , leaping at attacking anything that disturbed them .

title: Crawling claw
description: Crawling claw A swarm of crawling claws was made from the hands of some 300 small - and medium - sized humanoids . This construct acted like a swarm of insects , but perhaps with even less intelligence . Nevertheless , it was quite disturbing when viewed first hand .
description_long: Crawling claw A swarm of crawling claws was made from the hands of some 300 small - and medium - sized humanoids . This construct acted like a swarm of insects , but perhaps with even less intelligence . Nevertheless , it was quite disturbing when viewed first hand . Description . Using their fingers as legs , the hands crawled toward whatever they sensed as a target and swarmed over it . They could also leap six feet ( 1 . 8 m ) vertically . The swarm had no discernible front , back , or central body . Behavior . A swarm of crawling claws had only enough intelligence to perform simple guard duty or similar tasks . Combat . As sightless and nearly mindless constructs , crawling claws had some distinct advantages in combat . They were unaffected by illusions , gaze attacks , and other sight - related attacks . They were immune to disease , poison , stun , sleep , paralysis , death effects , necromancy effects , energy drain , ability drain , fatigue , exhaustion , and mind - based effects such as phantasms , patterns , charm , compulsion , and morale effects . They could not be effectively harmed by spells that targeted one creature or a limited number of creatures .

title: Create baneguard
description: Create baneguard Create baneguard was a divine magic spell available to cleric s of Bane , the Black Hand . It animated a baneguard out of an intact skeleton . Other ways of creating a baneguard were discovered , but this spell was specific to Bane and did not spread to other faiths until after his " death " in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR .
description_long: Create baneguard Create baneguard was a divine magic spell available to cleric s of Bane , the Black Hand . It animated a baneguard out of an intact skeleton . Other ways of creating a baneguard were discovered , but this spell was specific to Bane and did not spread to other faiths until after his " death " in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR . Effects . This spell took less than a minute to cast and the cleric had to touch the skeleton that was to be animated . Upon completion , the skeletal form rose , ready to attack . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required an intact skeleton of approximately human size or smaller , and 20 drops of blood from a true dragon . History . This spell was originally developed by priests of Bane , the Lord of Darkness . Eventually other evil - and neutral - aligned faiths learned this spell or a variant of it , and it was often called just " create undead " .

title: Create campsite
description: Create campsite Create campsite was a conjuration spell that summoned many invisible servants to set up a comfortable campsite . The reverse of this spell , break camp , could pack and clean up a campsite , leaving no trace . Effects .
description_long: Create campsite Create campsite was a conjuration spell that summoned many invisible servants to set up a comfortable campsite . The reverse of this spell , break camp , could pack and clean up a campsite , leaving no trace . Effects . The caster designated an area for the campsite and how many people were to be accommodated . The area could be no larger than a circle of 50 ft ( 15 . 2 m ) radius and accommodate no more than three people per level of the caster . If there was camping gear available , the invisible sprites used it to erect tents , lay out bedrolls , fetch water and firewood , start a campfire and prepare a plain meal . If there was inadequate gear , the servants used whatever materials were available in the general vicinity ( 50 yd / 46 m from the campsite ) , making beds from grasses or igloos for shelter for example . Within the limitations of the available gear and the environment , the servants made the guests as comfortable as possible . The campsite was created in about 15 minutes or less and was expertly crafted to blend in with the surroundings , making it somewhat difficult to detect visually .

title: Create crypt servant
description: Create crypt servant Create crypt servant was a necromancy spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was usable by wizard s and priest s ( cleric s ) . Effects .
description_long: Create crypt servant Create crypt servant was a necromancy spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was usable by wizard s and priest s ( cleric s ) . Effects . " Create crypt servant " was used , similarly to the simpler " animate dead " spell , to reanimate the body of a deceased person as a special undead called a crypt servant , that was especially suited to protect and maintain a designated tomb . The spell had to be performed at the burial place intended as the servant ' s domain in order to function . Apart from conventional means , a crypt servant could be destroyed by the reversed form of this spell , destroy crypt servant , or " dispel magic " . The spell intended for the even more powerful undead , " destroy crypt thing " , was also effective against a crypt servant . Components . Apart from an intact corpse , this spell only needed verbal and somatic components . History . This spell was originally employed in the ruined kingdoms of Kadar and Nog .

title: Create direguard
description: Create direguard Create direguard was a divine magic spell available to cleric s of Cyric , Prince of Madness . It animated a direguard out of an intact skeleton . Other ways of creating a direguard were discovered , but this spell was specific to Cyric and a jealously guarded secret .
description_long: Create direguard Create direguard was a divine magic spell available to cleric s of Cyric , Prince of Madness . It animated a direguard out of an intact skeleton . Other ways of creating a direguard were discovered , but this spell was specific to Cyric and a jealously guarded secret . Effects . This spell took one minute to cast and the cleric had to touch the skeleton that was to be animated . Upon completion , flames of red ignited in the skeleton ' s eye sockets and the direguard rose ready to attack , wearing armor that was shadowy black but with the bones visible through it . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required an intact skeleton of approximately human size or smaller , and 20 drops of blood from a true dragon . History . This spell was an improved version of the " create baneguard " spell used by priests of Bane , the Black Hand . Eventually other evil faiths learned this spell or a variant of it , and it was often called just " create undead " , although the caster who wanted to create a direguard had to be more experienced than a caster that could just learn " create baneguard " .

title: Create food and water
description: Create food and water Create food and water was a conjuration or alteration spell that caused food and water to appear . Effects . The food was simple and bland , but very nourishing .
description_long: Create food and water Create food and water was a conjuration or alteration spell that caused food and water to appear . Effects . The food was simple and bland , but very nourishing . For each level of the caster , enough food and water could be created to feed three human - sized creatures or one horse - sized creature for one day . The water was like clean rain water but the food did not keep and had to be discarded after 24 hours unless " purify food and drink " was used to prevent spoilage . The post sundering vertion of the spell created 45 pounds of food and 30 gallons of water , this should feed 15 people or 5 steeds . The food is nourishing but bland and also goes bad after 24 hours , the water is good and doesn ' t spoil . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell .

title: Create frenzy dog
description: Create frenzy dog Create frenzy dog was an evil druid spell used by certain druids in the forest of Chondalwood to transform almost any animal into a frenzy dog , a magically enhanced creature . Although the spell caused a corruption in nature to create the frenzy dog , druids justified this by their use of these creatures in the protection of their forest environment . The spell was barely known outside the Chondalwood and the druids used it sparingly because they were aware of the potential damage large numbers of frenzy dogs would cause .
description_long: Create frenzy dog Create frenzy dog was an evil druid spell used by certain druids in the forest of Chondalwood to transform almost any animal into a frenzy dog , a magically enhanced creature . Although the spell caused a corruption in nature to create the frenzy dog , druids justified this by their use of these creatures in the protection of their forest environment . The spell was barely known outside the Chondalwood and the druids used it sparingly because they were aware of the potential damage large numbers of frenzy dogs would cause .

title: Create greater undead
description: Create greater undead ' Create greater undead " was a necromancy spell that created more powerful undead than the lesser " create undead " spell . Effect . This spell functioned in the same manner as " create undead " , except that it allowed the caster to create more powerful and intelligent sorts of undead .
description_long: Create greater undead ' Create greater undead " was a necromancy spell that created more powerful undead than the lesser " create undead " spell . Effect . This spell functioned in the same manner as " create undead " , except that it allowed the caster to create more powerful and intelligent sorts of undead . The type of undead created was based on how powerful the caster is . In order of magnitude , these types were : mummies , spectre s , vampire s , and ghost s .

title: Create jungle minions
description: Create jungle minions Create jungle minions was a divine magic spell available to priest s of the Zakhara n savage goddess Ragarra , and some specialized kahin s . It transformed certain creatures into lesser segarran s . Effects .
description_long: Create jungle minions Create jungle minions was a divine magic spell available to priest s of the Zakhara n savage goddess Ragarra , and some specialized kahin s . It transformed certain creatures into lesser segarran s . Effects . Depending on the power of the priest , this spell created three or more of the humanoid , crocodile - headed divine minion s of the godess Ragarra called lesser segarrans either from crocodile s or alligator s , or from demihuman s , human s or humanoid s . Even unwilling targets ran the risk of being affected by this spell . Unlike with the related " conjure jungle minions " , this transformation was permanent , but like with the less - powerful spell , the caster could direct the actions of newly made segarrans , usually to attack their enemies , until they made a kill . The segarrans then consumed any slain victims and only afterwards followed the commands of the priest again . If no opponent was overwhelmed and devoured , the caster often was afflicted with a " curse " , showing Ragarra ' s disfavor . Components .

title: Create or destroy water
description: Create or destroy water Create or destroy water , also known simply as create water or destroy water , was a transmutation / alteration or conjuration spell that could create a quantity of drinkable water or remove a like quantity of standing water . Effects . This spell had two functions with opposite effects .
description_long: Create or destroy water Create or destroy water , also known simply as create water or destroy water , was a transmutation / alteration or conjuration spell that could create a quantity of drinkable water or remove a like quantity of standing water . Effects . This spell had two functions with opposite effects . " Create water " conjured into being a quantity of potable water equivalent to rainwater . The earliest versions of this spell created up to 4 gal ( 15 L ) of pure water per level of the caster within a distance of 10 ft ( 3 m ) to 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) and took one minute to cast . The next version reduced this to 2 gal ( 7 . 6 L ) per level but increased the range and could be cast as a cantrip or orison by cleric s and druid s . The rare version used by wizard s brought forth 1 gal per level only . After the Second Sundering , the basic spell could summon 10 gal ( 38 L ) of water and an addition 10 gal for each higher level allotted to the spell . The range of this version was 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) . " Create water " required an appropriately - sized empty volume in which to place the water .

title: Create shade
description: Create shade Create shade was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a patch of shaded ground .
description_long: Create shade Create shade was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a patch of shaded ground . It was extremely useful when traversing the blistering deserts of Zakhara . The shaded area functioned just like normal shade , allowing creatures to cool themselves and consume less water . This spell could only work when cast upon solid ground . Components . This spell did not require any physical components to cast .

title: Create soundstaff
description: Create soundstaff Create soundstaff was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell diminished noise by gathering it into a special staff .
description_long: Create soundstaff Create soundstaff was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell diminished noise by gathering it into a special staff . The staff was planted into the ground or affixed to a structure when cast , creating a sphere of peace and quiet that lasted for 60 days . The staff muffled any form of sonic attack , causing greatly decreased negative effects . If the staff was removed from its location before the 60th or after the 61st day , then all magic stored within was lost . The staff needed to be reset on precisely the 60th day in order to function again when the spell was cast . Staves removed on the 60th day could function as a weapon that emitted a sonic cone - shaped blast similar to " power word , stun " . Components . This spell required a staff of dark wood with a white or blue stone worth at least 300 gp to cast .

title: Create undead
description: Create undead Create undead was a necromancy spell that created one or several undead under the casters service . Effect . A older version of the spell allowed the caster to bring into being a ghoul , ghast , mummy or mohrg depending on the caster ' s ability .
description_long: Create undead Create undead was a necromancy spell that created one or several undead under the casters service . Effect . A older version of the spell allowed the caster to bring into being a ghoul , ghast , mummy or mohrg depending on the caster ' s ability . The undead that the spell creates was not necessarily obedient to its master so it was often necessary to possess the power to command the undead before casting this spell . In order for the spell to be cast , it must be cast on one a corpse , and a black onyx gem must have been placed in one of the corpse ' s eye sockets or the mouth . The more powerful undead being created , the more valuable the gem have been . The gem was consumed by the spell . The post Second Sundering version could target three corpses , these targets became ghouls under the casters control and where controlled within a range of 120 feet ( 36 , 5 meters ) . These ghouls could be ordered to perform simple commands like guarding and would perform the task until it is done , if no task is given creature will only defend it self .

title: Creation
description: Creation Creation was a illusion spell that took threads of the Shadowfell to form a inanimate object of plant stuffs . Effect . The object could be no larger then a 5 foot ( 1 , 5 meters ) cube and be of a material and form of something the caster have seen before .
description_long: Creation Creation was a illusion spell that took threads of the Shadowfell to form a inanimate object of plant stuffs . Effect . The object could be no larger then a 5 foot ( 1 , 5 meters ) cube and be of a material and form of something the caster have seen before . The objects could be soft goods , wood or even made from minerals , but the time these things remained depended on what materials they where turned in to . The time the object remained ranged from a day for other plant stuffs to a minute for adamantine or Mithral and if the object was made from different components the lowest time was the chosen one . If a object created by this spell was used as casting components for another spell , that spell would then fail . If this spell was cast as a higher level then the cube size would increase by 5 per level . Components . To cast this spell the caster needed vocal , somatic components and a tiny piece of the item that the spell was supposed to create .

title: Creative Creed
description: Creative Creed The Creative Creed was one of the major illithid Creeds in the Realms . They advocated that the best way to expand their knowledge base was to create , invent , or discover new psionic disciplines , technology , and psionic items . They successfully built flying craft , living troop transports and weaponry , and other unique psionic items .
description_long: Creative Creed The Creative Creed was one of the major illithid Creeds in the Realms . They advocated that the best way to expand their knowledge base was to create , invent , or discover new psionic disciplines , technology , and psionic items . They successfully built flying craft , living troop transports and weaponry , and other unique psionic items . Oryndoll . In Oryndoll , illithid s in the Creative Creed worked in The Workshops , which were their laboratories . Many workshops were actually located in individual domiciles but were still able to accommodate one to twelve illithid scientists .

title: Creator race
description: Creator race The five creator race s ( or " Iquar ' Tel ' Quessir " in the language of the elves ) dominated Faerûn during the Days of Thunder . All are considered native to Abeir - Toril , as are their descendants and creations . Most historians agree that the creator races were the sarrukh ( creators of the yuan - ti , naga , lizardfolk , and scalykind ) , the batrachi ( known as amphibioids , and the creators of the bullywug s , doppelganger s , kopru , kuo - toa , locathah , siv s , tako and other shapeshifting , amphibious , or piscine races ) , the aearee ( known as avians , and creators of the aarakocra , kenku , and other birdlike humanoids ) , the fey ( known as sylvans , and creators of korreds , sprite s , and pixie s ) and humans .
description_long: Creator race The five creator race s ( or " Iquar ' Tel ' Quessir " in the language of the elves ) dominated Faerûn during the Days of Thunder . All are considered native to Abeir - Toril , as are their descendants and creations . Most historians agree that the creator races were the sarrukh ( creators of the yuan - ti , naga , lizardfolk , and scalykind ) , the batrachi ( known as amphibioids , and the creators of the bullywug s , doppelganger s , kopru , kuo - toa , locathah , siv s , tako and other shapeshifting , amphibious , or piscine races ) , the aearee ( known as avians , and creators of the aarakocra , kenku , and other birdlike humanoids ) , the fey ( known as sylvans , and creators of korreds , sprite s , and pixie s ) and humans . Other sages incorrectly leave out the aearee but include dragons in the list . Elves and dwarves are not counted as creator races because they , as well as some human ethnic groups , were immigrants to Abeir - Toril from other worlds .

title: Cree
description: Cree Cree was a shadar - kai warrior living in the city of Ikemmu on the Shadowfell side . Relationships . He was a brother of Skagi and a close friend of Ashok .
description_long: Cree Cree was a shadar - kai warrior living in the city of Ikemmu on the Shadowfell side . Relationships . He was a brother of Skagi and a close friend of Ashok . History . In 1479 DR , Cree journeyed with Skagi , Ashok , and Vedoran to a shadar - kai enclave in the Shadowfell on a mission to rescue the witch Ilvani . In 1480 DR , he traveled with a caravan to Rashemen to discover the source of the visions that were haunting Ilvani . Appearance . Cree was small and wiry and had close - cropped brown hair and a pair of scimitar tattoos on his temples . One of his eyes had been destroyed by a shadow snake , and he placed a tattoo of a snake over his missing eye . Equipment . Cree dual - wielded katar daggers .

title: Creel
description: Creel The Creel were one of the smallest tribes of Nar found in Narfell . There were 750 Creel in 1357 DR . Activities .
description_long: Creel The Creel were one of the smallest tribes of Nar found in Narfell . There were 750 Creel in 1357 DR . Activities . Because of their humiliating defeat at the hands of the undead forces under the command of Zhengyi , the Creel were notoriously violent toward anyone found on their land , including other tribes of Nar . Base of Operations . The Creel inhabited the lands in northwestern Narfell along the shores of Icelace Lake .

title: Creeper rose
description: Creeper rose Creeper roses were common in the Rose Garden of the Battle of Bones . Description . Creeper roses were vigorous plants with pink flowers .
description_long: Creeper rose Creeper roses were common in the Rose Garden of the Battle of Bones . Description . Creeper roses were vigorous plants with pink flowers . They climbed at will and attached to anything in their path . At the Rose Garden , the vines would wrap around bones and scattered weapons , creating a sturdy horizontal framework for the rest of the garden and giving it a macabre appearance . When picked , these flowers did not last long unless kept in warm water with a bit of sugar added . Flowers blooming under these conditions gave off a powerful scent .

title: Creeping doom
description: Creeping doom Creeping doom was a conjuration spell that called into being a carpet of insects that attacked selected targets . Effects . Early versions of this spell summoned 500 to 1 , 000 poisonous spider s , scorpions , beetle s , and centipede s that swarmed over a 20 ft ( 6 .
description_long: Creeping doom Creeping doom was a conjuration spell that called into being a carpet of insects that attacked selected targets . Effects . Early versions of this spell summoned 500 to 1 , 000 poisonous spider s , scorpions , beetle s , and centipede s that swarmed over a 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) square area . The later version of this spell summoned up to ten swarms of centipedes , each of which could be commanded independently . A swarm could attack any creature that could be damaged by normal weapons and quickly kill them by sheer numbers even though each bug did minimum damage . Swarms could be directed to move , killing anything in their path . If a swarm got too far away from the caster , the early version started to lose bugs , whereas the later version just stopped moving and attacked any creatures in its area . Components . This spell required only verbal and somatic components to cast .

title: Crenshinibon
description: Crenshinibon Crenshinibon , also called " The Crystal Shard " , was a unique , magical artifact . Powers and personality . Crenshinibon was a vile relic of immense power , a crystal shard that drew its magical energy from the light of the sun .
description_long: Crenshinibon Crenshinibon , also called " The Crystal Shard " , was a unique , magical artifact . Powers and personality . Crenshinibon was a vile relic of immense power , a crystal shard that drew its magical energy from the light of the sun . Crenshinibon was a sentient artifact , and it possessed a never - ending hunger for power and glory at whatever cost ; therefore , Crenshinibon was not a reasonable being . It always desired a powerful wielder , usually a corruptible magic - user of some sort , and greatly enhanced that wielder ' s powers . The Crystal Shard also insidiously manipulated its wielder and would readily abandon him or her for someone more capable of furthering its goals of ultimate conquest . The relic could lure in thousands of evil - intentioned beings with its magical call , creating a grand army for its wielder and so - called master . Perhaps Crenshinibon ' s most magnificent ability was its power to create an enormous crystalline tower , known as Cryshal - Tirith ( meaning " crystal tower " in Elven ) .

title: Crescent Blade
description: Crescent Blade The Crescent Blade was a magical sword created by the goddess Eilistraee . Description . The blade was curved , resembling a crescent moon attached to a leather hilt .
description_long: Crescent Blade The Crescent Blade was a magical sword created by the goddess Eilistraee . Description . The blade was curved , resembling a crescent moon attached to a leather hilt . The blade ' s enchantments included moonlight - - it could cut through armor and stone - - - protection against evil , and being able to strike quickly . If the wielder was a true priestess , she could use it to sever the neck of any creature , including gods . It was also said to be able to destroy the souls of those who were killed by it . There was silver inlaid in the blade . On it were Drow words that translated to " Be your heart filled with light and your cause be true ; I shall not fail you . " When wielded , the Crescent Blade spouted crimson fire . History . It was said that Eilistraee plucked a pebble from the heavens and tossed it to earth . It grew as large as a boulder and very hot . It was made of moonmetal ; if you look at the moon , you can see a hole in the shape of a crescent . The boulder was forged into a crescent - shaped blade with enchantments .

title: Crescentcoat
description: Crescentcoat In the Heralds of Faerûn organization , the office of Crescentcoat was one of the High Heralds . This office was primarily responsible for training the local Heralds and was also given the difficult task of presenting all sides of issues brought up for debate among the High Heralds . Crescentcoat traditionally played the role of " devil ' s advocate " to ensure the council came to their conclusions honestly after considering the ramifications of each aspect .
description_long: Crescentcoat In the Heralds of Faerûn organization , the office of Crescentcoat was one of the High Heralds . This office was primarily responsible for training the local Heralds and was also given the difficult task of presenting all sides of issues brought up for debate among the High Heralds . Crescentcoat traditionally played the role of " devil ' s advocate " to ensure the council came to their conclusions honestly after considering the ramifications of each aspect . Although not a solid tradition , this office was filled by a female more often than not . The residence of this office was a fortification known as Moonrise Towers on the banks of the River Chionthar west of Elturel . Possessions . This office derived its name from a beautiful cloth - of - silver woven with a pattern of interlocking crescent moons . In addition to a regal appearance , the garment gave the wearer the power of a " ring of shooting stars " . The rod of office was made of ivory enchanted to be harder than adamantine and with the same function as a " rod of smiting " .

title: Cressaro
description: Cressaro Cressaro was the cloud giant castellan of Lyn Armaal sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Cressaro was a young giant in the late 1480s or early 1490s DR .
description_long: Cressaro Cressaro was the cloud giant castellan of Lyn Armaal sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Cressaro was a young giant in the late 1480s or early 1490s DR . He was the castellan , consort and personal bodyguard of Countess Sansuri . His normal duty was overseeing the correct flying of Lyn Armaal . Personality . Cressaro followed the orders of Sansuri without doubts , deeply loyal to her .

title: Cressyl Blackbones
description: Cressyl Blackbones Cressyl Blackbones was a male orc and a red half - dragon from the Thunder Peaks . He led a small army of orcs near the eastern edge of the Hullack Forest . Description .
description_long: Cressyl Blackbones Cressyl Blackbones was a male orc and a red half - dragon from the Thunder Peaks . He led a small army of orcs near the eastern edge of the Hullack Forest . Description . Standing 6 ' 10 " ( 2 . 08 meters ) , Cressyl towered over most and with his red skin and ashen scent it made him stand out from the other orcs in his tribe . This accompanied by his yellow fangs and empty left eye socket compounded his baleful visage . Possessions . Cressyl made use of a magic dire flail whenever he went into battle and was outfitted in enchanted half - plate mail armor . In addition , Cressyl was at all times with his pet howler , Spike . History . In the summer of 1372 DR , members of the Cult of the Dragon inadvertently opened a portal near where Cressyl Blackbone ' s orcs were resting . The ensuing combat was quickly finished by the orcs and they learned the secret of opening the portal from one of the cultists . Over the next few days , the orcs slowly explored the portal nexus that the cultists had come from , expanding their raiding until they met more resistance and counterattacks by the cultists .

title: Cricket
description: Cricket A cricket is a type of insect . Species . Horse .
description_long: Cricket A cricket is a type of insect . Species . Horse . Horse crickets were known for seeking shade by hopping into the mouths of bluetail snake s and then being swallowed . Lyra Sunrose listed them as examples of how Cormanthor had the world ' s dumbest insects . Locations . The cricket was known to inhabit the following areas :

title: Crimdrac
description: Crimdrac Crimdrac was a dracolich ally of Dracandros in Battledale in 1357 DR . History . Crimdrac was a red dragon dracolich created by the Cult of the Dragon .
description_long: Crimdrac Crimdrac was a dracolich ally of Dracandros in Battledale in 1357 DR . History . Crimdrac was a red dragon dracolich created by the Cult of the Dragon . However , he allied with the Red Wizard of Thay Dracandros for the chance to learn spell s . Thanks to him , Dracandros ruled the village of Hap . Crimdrac was killed by the adventuring party possessing the Azure Bonds . Personality . Crimdrac was basically a compulsive liar : he tried to claim as his own all kinds of exploit made by a dragon in the Dragon Reach . He planned to betray Dracandros after the Red Wizard had taught him magic .

title: Crimel
description: Crimel Crimel was a small city in Luiren in the Shining South . Geography . Crimel was found along the edge of the Long Forest .
description_long: Crimel Crimel was a small city in Luiren in the Shining South . Geography . Crimel was found along the edge of the Long Forest . Inhabitants . Only a thousand people lived in the city . Most of them were directly involved in the logging business given the close proximity to the Long Forest . Priests of Yondalla ensured that any timber harvest from the forest was done in an appropriate manner . Silvo Carver served as mayor of Crimel . Armed Forces . A small force of 50 halfling warders protected Crimel . These Warder ' s were particularly skilled in the ways of the forest .

title: Crimmor
description: Crimmor Crimmor was the Caravan Capital of Amn . Many caravan s were sponsored and arranged in Athkatla , but the goods were loaded onto barges there and towed up the Alandor River by horses and mules on River Road until they reached their mustering point at Crimmor . Some folk said nearly every caravan in Faerûn passed through Crimmor in time .
description_long: Crimmor Crimmor was the Caravan Capital of Amn . Many caravan s were sponsored and arranged in Athkatla , but the goods were loaded onto barges there and towed up the Alandor River by horses and mules on River Road until they reached their mustering point at Crimmor . Some folk said nearly every caravan in Faerûn passed through Crimmor in time .

title: Crinti
description: Crinti The Crinti ( drowic for " noble ones " ) , also referred to as Shadow - Amazons by the Halruaa ns , were the half - drow and half - elf aristocracy and ruling class of Dambrath . History . In 831 DR the Arkaiun people were defeated at the Battle of Crimtar by the combined efforts of the drow of T ' lindhet and one hundred and twelve priestesses of Loviatar who became later known as The First .
description_long: Crinti The Crinti ( drowic for " noble ones " ) , also referred to as Shadow - Amazons by the Halruaa ns , were the half - drow and half - elf aristocracy and ruling class of Dambrath . History . In 831 DR the Arkaiun people were defeated at the Battle of Crimtar by the combined efforts of the drow of T ' lindhet and one hundred and twelve priestesses of Loviatar who became later known as The First . In exchange for their assistance in defeating the Arkaiuns , the drow of T ' lindhet allowed the half - elf priestesses to rule Dambrath in their stead . In time , some of these half - elf priestesses bore half - drow children , who became known as the Crinti . ) and by 1373 DR were about fifteen percent of Dambrath ' s population . By 1479 DR , the Crinti had been wiped out in Dambrath . Appearance . The Crinti were a people from a convoluted mixture of bloodlines : the drow of T ' lindhet , the one hundred and twelve half - elf priestesses of Loviatar known as The First , and human barbarians taken as slaves or lovers by the drow and half - elves . Most Crinti had darker gray or black skin , silver or white hair , and widely varied eye colors known among humans or elves .

title: Cripakolus
description: Cripakolus Cripakolus was an azer lord on the Elemental Plane of Fire in 1373 DR . History . Cripakolus was the leader of the azer Everash Tribe in the Elemental Plane of Fire .
description_long: Cripakolus Cripakolus was an azer lord on the Elemental Plane of Fire in 1373 DR . History . Cripakolus was the leader of the azer Everash Tribe in the Elemental Plane of Fire . However , most of his fellows were enslaved by the efreet of Hafiz al - Milhab to work in his mine . Thus , in 1373 DR , when his men captured Kaanyr Vhok and his allies , Cripakolus bargained with Kaanyr , offering them their freedom and to show them a passage to the City of Brass , in exchange for destroying the efreet mine for azers . Appendix . Appearances . Novels . The Empyrean Odyssey :

title: Crippled Mountain
description: Crippled Mountain The Crippled Mountain , originally known as the Celestial Mountain , was a volcano located in Skelkor , Returned Abeir . History . The Celestial Mountain was the lair of the red dragon Rhodrolytharnestrix , the most powerful of the dragon tyrants of Abeir .
description_long: Crippled Mountain The Crippled Mountain , originally known as the Celestial Mountain , was a volcano located in Skelkor , Returned Abeir . History . The Celestial Mountain was the lair of the red dragon Rhodrolytharnestrix , the most powerful of the dragon tyrants of Abeir . To kill Rhodrolytharnestrix , the dragonborn rebels Iskara , Shurideh , Reshvemi , and Thuchir went to the interior of the volcano during the Battle of the Crippled Mountain , and using a powerful artifact known as the Eye of Blazing Rorn , triggered a powerful eruption that destroyed the mountain . Since then , the mountain became known as the Crippled Mountain . Legacy . The ash from the eruption fell for forty days , and the dragonborn began to call themselves the " " vayemniri " " ( Ash - Marked Ones , in draconic ) , so that they would always remember the way they gained their freedom . Likewise , Clan Verthisathurgiesh , one of the most powerful clans of Tymanther , was named after the Crippled Mountain .

title: Crommower Pwent
description: Crommower Pwent Crommower Pwent was a dwarven battlerager and a dear friend and traveling companion of Gandalug Battlehammer , the First King of Mithril Hall . Description . Crommower was a dirty dwarf with a black beard and a clean - shaven head to secure the spiked helmet on his head .
description_long: Crommower Pwent Crommower Pwent was a dwarven battlerager and a dear friend and traveling companion of Gandalug Battlehammer , the First King of Mithril Hall . Description . Crommower was a dirty dwarf with a black beard and a clean - shaven head to secure the spiked helmet on his head . He wore bladed armor and boasted the furious battlerager mentality . History . Around - 643 DR , Gandalug Battlehammer left Mithril Hall with Crommower and the two adventurers descended into the depths under the dwarven stronghold . While exploring , they ran into drow soldiers , including Yvonnel Baenre , and Crommower died slaying many enemies .

title: Cron Bolver
description: Cron Bolver Cron Bolver was a member of the Knights of Black Fist in Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Bolver had a lot of power in the city and made sure that all knew this .
description_long: Cron Bolver Cron Bolver was a member of the Knights of Black Fist in Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Bolver had a lot of power in the city and made sure that all knew this . He took pleasure from his job and often accepted bribes . Bolver had a sharp wit and a sharper tongue . History . Bolver was one of the Black Fist lieutenants in charge of the Stojanow Gate . After the Vorgansharax ' s coup Bolver became one of the Tears of Virulence , maintaining all his power . He was displaced with a patrol to capture Madame Freona but was defeated and killed by an adventuring party hired by the resistance to permit the escape of Freona . Activities . Bolver usually stayed at a desk in the Black Fist barracks to answer to citizens ' petitions .

title: Crookspar Parlor
description: Crookspar Parlor Crookspar Parlor was a gambling den located in the Crown , the highest section of Skullport . The lower floor was open to anyone with coin while the upper floor was divided into private rooms in which high stake games of chance were played . The establishment was considered neutral turf by Skullport ' s gangs and leaders of the town ' s gangs often gambled in the private rooms .
