description: Daria Daria the Hammer was a mercenary recruiter in Waterdeep . Activities . Daria was a talented merchant but was also the best - known mercenary recruiter in the City of Splendors .
description_long: Daria Daria the Hammer was a mercenary recruiter in Waterdeep . Activities . Daria was a talented merchant but was also the best - known mercenary recruiter in the City of Splendors . She often worked with Blazidon One - Eye and Filiare if she needed to recruit special units . Usually she recruited and led her company in battle . She was a master tactician .

title: Darien
description: Darien Darien was a Szarkai before Lolth turned her into a albino - drider during the Night of Wailing . Once she had been sent by the drow of Maztica to Faerûn where she should find a tool for their plans of getting full control over the cult of Zaltec in her home . She found the young soldier Cordell and helped him to survive a lost battle .
description_long: Darien Darien was a Szarkai before Lolth turned her into a albino - drider during the Night of Wailing . Once she had been sent by the drow of Maztica to Faerûn where she should find a tool for their plans of getting full control over the cult of Zaltec in her home . She found the young soldier Cordell and helped him to survive a lost battle . After that they founded the Golden Legion and she became one of the most trustet leaders at Cordell ' s side . Ten years later the legion won a fierce battle in Amn against the pirate Akbet - Khrul and Cordell was summoned before the Council of Six . He made them finance his expedition to the west over the Trackless Sea where he hoped to find a new route to Kara - Tur . But instead of the famous realm they found the continent of Maztica and here Darien was once again of great use for the legion . It was her magic which helped them to defeat the army of Payit in the battle of Ulatos and later to kill Takamal , the Revered Counselor of Kultaka , amidst his own men in a another battle .

title: Daring acrobat
description: Daring acrobat A daring acrobat is a rogue who has learned to master acrobat ic techniques . Wondrous to behold these daring acrobats might be professional performers , religious devotees of Tempus or Tymora , or expert thieves . Some obtain their skills from a school and others from a family tradition , while most of the remainder are self - taught , learning their skills as a matter of self - preservation .
description_long: Daring acrobat A daring acrobat is a rogue who has learned to master acrobat ic techniques . Wondrous to behold these daring acrobats might be professional performers , religious devotees of Tempus or Tymora , or expert thieves . Some obtain their skills from a school and others from a family tradition , while most of the remainder are self - taught , learning their skills as a matter of self - preservation . Whatever their trade or origin , daring acrobats find the spectacular tricks and maneuvers they ' ve learned to be a vital part of that path , allowing them to move more quickly and tumble out of danger ' s way . Though flashy , the stunts daring acrobats perform are far more than light amusements and when applied in combat , can be the difference between life and death . Daring acrobats move with greater agility and balance than either their allies or enemies , dancing in and out of harm ' s way . Because of their training daring acrobats might survive perils that would surely fell more clumsy warriors . Abilities . Daring acrobats rely on agility and balance over deadliness or endurance , though all who take the path have a dose of the latter two as well .

title: Darius Bormul VI
description: Darius Bormul VI Darius Bormul VI was a Council of Six ' s envoy in Maztica in 1370 DR . Activities . Lord Darius was concerned about the apparent disinterest of Governor Cordell to maintain the Council ' s hold over Maztica after the settling of New Waterdeep .
description_long: Darius Bormul VI Darius Bormul VI was a Council of Six ' s envoy in Maztica in 1370 DR . Activities . Lord Darius was concerned about the apparent disinterest of Governor Cordell to maintain the Council ' s hold over Maztica after the settling of New Waterdeep . He also funded the new colony of Lord Drakosa .

title: Dark - Eyed One
description: Dark - Eyed One The Dark - Eyed One was an adventurer and mage in the ruin of Spellgard . History . The Dark - Eyed One was an evil adventurer member of the Free Company of the Crescent .
description_long: Dark - Eyed One The Dark - Eyed One was an adventurer and mage in the ruin of Spellgard . History . The Dark - Eyed One was an evil adventurer member of the Free Company of the Crescent . In 1479 DR , he went with his fellows to Spellgard hoping to find Lady Saharel ' s treasures . Personality . Nobody apart from Devlin knew the motives of the Dark - Eyed One or even his name . He followed Devlin ' s orders without question . He did not speak much with others but often he murmured to himself .

title: Dark Army of the Night
description: Dark Army of the Night The Dark Army of Night was formed by Lord Vanrak Moonstar , a minor Waterdeep noble , after his father was killed by a mysterious , uncurable wasting disease that was possibly brought back with him after Vanrak returned from an expedition to the Black Jungles of Tashalar . Vanrak , his body and mind weakened by his arduous travels , was overcome with grief and blamed the priests of Selûne from the High House of Stars for his father ' s death . So engrossed in his grief , Vanrak was an easy convert to Shar ' s worship .
description_long: Dark Army of the Night The Dark Army of Night was formed by Lord Vanrak Moonstar , a minor Waterdeep noble , after his father was killed by a mysterious , uncurable wasting disease that was possibly brought back with him after Vanrak returned from an expedition to the Black Jungles of Tashalar . Vanrak , his body and mind weakened by his arduous travels , was overcome with grief and blamed the priests of Selûne from the High House of Stars for his father ' s death . So engrossed in his grief , Vanrak was an easy convert to Shar ' s worship . Vanrak assumed leadership of the family and quietly started converting family members and servants to his new faith . 26 years later he openly declared his faith and organized a small mercenary army , led by Sharran preists which he used to terrorize Waterdeep ' s harbour . Vanrak ' s sister , Lady Alathene Moonstar , in 1130 DR took refuge , with the rest of her Selûne - worshiping family in the High House of Stars and petitioned the courts to strip her brother of his title and banish him , providing evidence of numerous heinous crimes .

title: Dark Arrow Keep
description: Dark Arrow Keep King Obould XVII ruled the Kingdom of Many - Arrows from the central chamber in this trapped fortress . Known for its slit - covered , confounding corridors and blind alleys , Dark Arrow Keep also housed the Pit ; an arena used by the King to judge his chieftains and mete out brutal punishments . Description .
description_long: Dark Arrow Keep King Obould XVII ruled the Kingdom of Many - Arrows from the central chamber in this trapped fortress . Known for its slit - covered , confounding corridors and blind alleys , Dark Arrow Keep also housed the Pit ; an arena used by the King to judge his chieftains and mete out brutal punishments . Description . Dark Arrow Keep was the centre of the Many - arrows kingdom - a sprawling chaotic city enclosed by a palisade resting on earthworks and rubble . Situated 3 miles from the Surbin river bank and around 40 miles north of Mithral Hall , the city may have been be chaotically laid out , but due to the irregular - shaped buildings and walls inside it was hard to get lost . A vast majority of the residents lived in simple tents along twisting , nameless roads . Known for its metal workers , Dark Arrow Keep was the industrial centre of the kingdom . The Citadel . The Citadel was the largest structure in the city . Made of stone , wood and iron it was constructed to be a fortress within a fortress with a large host of royal guards to defend the King ' s family . The citadel was built around the throne room , which is the largest open area in the keep .

title: Dark Dagger
description: Dark Dagger The Dark Dagger was a widespread group of Vhaeraun - worshiping drow . Their goal was to increase the influence of the drow on the surface and to gain power to fight against the church of Lolth . Headquarters .
description_long: Dark Dagger The Dark Dagger was a widespread group of Vhaeraun - worshiping drow . Their goal was to increase the influence of the drow on the surface and to gain power to fight against the church of Lolth . Headquarters . In the 14th century DR , the Dark Dagger was active in Skullport , Turmish , the Vilhon Reach , Amn , and Calimshan and were expanding to other cities around the Sea of Fallen Stars . Members . The Dark Dagger was led by drow males but recruited human s and half - elves as well . Members of the Dark Dagger used poisons to which they were immune , resulting from prolonged and controlled exposure . It seemed that common members or cells were called Points and the leaders held the title Envenomed Edge . History . In 1359 DR , in the course of the Darkstalker Wars , the Dark Dagger in Skullport suffered an attack by assassins hired by Ralan el Pesarkhal . This attack caused casualties that numbered half of the Skullport cell ' s members and made it impossible to send money and material supplies to their southern fellows . This interruption caused their bid to gain control over Calimshan ' s underworld to fail .

title: Dark Disaster
description: Dark Disaster The Dark Disaster , or the Killing Storms , was a tragedy in - 10 , 500 DR that totally turned the territory of the elven kingdom of Miyeritar into a barren wasteland . History . In - 11800 DR , the elven nation of Miyeritar was annexed by another elven nation called Aryvandaar and pacified by - 11300 DR .
description_long: Dark Disaster The Dark Disaster , or the Killing Storms , was a tragedy in - 10 , 500 DR that totally turned the territory of the elven kingdom of Miyeritar into a barren wasteland . History . In - 11800 DR , the elven nation of Miyeritar was annexed by another elven nation called Aryvandaar and pacified by - 11300 DR . The Dark Disaster struck - 10500 DR and killed many innocents , though a large number of Miyeritar ’ s original inhabitants already left for other places . Culprits . The Killing Storms weren ’ t a natural disaster but an artificial one . There seemed to be two potential culprits . The first theory said that the high mages from Aryvandaar were the culprits . According to it , they assassinated Miyeritar ’ s high mages to drop the nation ’ s defences against the Killing Storms , which they caused for an unspecified reason to destroy their own territory which they have pacified by that time . This theory was popular but , due to lack of evidence , completely unfounded . The second theory said that elven high mages on Miyeritar ' s side accidentally caused the disaster when they broke a taboo and tried to harness corrupt magic for resistance reasons . Effects .

title: Dark Diviners
description: Dark Diviners A cadre of wizard ' s based in Myth Drannor ' s Windsong Tower , the Dark Diviners discovered the tome the Book of the Black . Written ( in part ) by the Netherese seer Augathra the Mad , the book revealed many of the goddess Shar ' s dark secrets . The Dark Diviners wrote of their findings and insights in the Leaves of One Night .
description_long: Dark Diviners A cadre of wizard ' s based in Myth Drannor ' s Windsong Tower , the Dark Diviners discovered the tome the Book of the Black . Written ( in part ) by the Netherese seer Augathra the Mad , the book revealed many of the goddess Shar ' s dark secrets . The Dark Diviners wrote of their findings and insights in the Leaves of One Night . Shar , displeased with their work , and acrimonious of their text , cursed both books and arranged for them to be stolen from Windsong Tower after which they were not to be seen again for centuries . After the theft , the Dark Diviners left Windsong Tower to try to recreate their stolen work ( the Leaves of One Night was unique ) and deduce what went wrong .

title: Dark Dominion
description: Dark Dominion All of the tunnels within a 5 mile radius of Menzoberranzan are known as the Dark Dominion . Drow patrols are a constant presence of the region . They search for banned creatures , monsters and surface elves and challenge them once spotted .
description_long: Dark Dominion All of the tunnels within a 5 mile radius of Menzoberranzan are known as the Dark Dominion . Drow patrols are a constant presence of the region . They search for banned creatures , monsters and surface elves and challenge them once spotted . A few guard outposts can also be found in these tunnels . At least ten of the tunnels that start here lead to the surface . One that leads straight past Blingdenstone and into Mithral Hall and one that leads to the High Forest are the two most commonly used .

title: Dark Eight
description: Dark Eight The Dark Eight were a coven of pit fiend generals who resided on the Ninth Layer of Hell , Nessus . They plotted and strategized the movements of Hell ' s armies . Bel , Lord of the First Layer , was once a mighty leader on the battlefields of the War , and used his influence with the Dark Eight to retain control of Avernus .
description_long: Dark Eight The Dark Eight were a coven of pit fiend generals who resided on the Ninth Layer of Hell , Nessus . They plotted and strategized the movements of Hell ' s armies . Bel , Lord of the First Layer , was once a mighty leader on the battlefields of the War , and used his influence with the Dark Eight to retain control of Avernus .

title: Dark Exodus
description: Dark Exodus The mystery of the Gray migrations remains a puzzle to all folk in the Delimbiyr Vale save the High Forest orc s themselves , and none of them are willing to talk about it . The party ventures into the tusker ' s former home to find out why , only to be attacked by drow ! A treant then tasks them with saving a large number of fey who are being held hostage by the drow .
description_long: Dark Exodus The mystery of the Gray migrations remains a puzzle to all folk in the Delimbiyr Vale save the High Forest orc s themselves , and none of them are willing to talk about it . The party ventures into the tusker ' s former home to find out why , only to be attacked by drow ! A treant then tasks them with saving a large number of fey who are being held hostage by the drow .

title: Dark God Reformed
description: Dark God Reformed The Dark God Reformed was a temple and walled compound dedicated to Cyric in Voonlar . In the days before the supposed death of Bane , the Black Hand , it was a Banite temple named The Dark Lord ' s Hand , and it had other names under previous leaders . Location .
description_long: Dark God Reformed The Dark God Reformed was a temple and walled compound dedicated to Cyric in Voonlar . In the days before the supposed death of Bane , the Black Hand , it was a Banite temple named The Dark Lord ' s Hand , and it had other names under previous leaders . Location . Voonlar was a trading town and farming community located in the southwest corner of the Moonsea region of north Faerûn . The temple was located just off of the North Ride across from the Bounty of the Goddess and was accessed by two short lanes , one from the North Ride and one from Runstal ' s Ride . A short distance down the North Ride to the southwest was the Locktower , headquarters of the local Bron ( sheriff ) . Structure . The spire atop the temple ' s three - story entry tower rose up sharply for another 80 feet ( 24 meters ) to make it the tallest structure in Voonlar and the surrounding countryside . As such , its needle tip was often struck by lightning , and the rest of the structure was in similar shape . The walls of the Dark God Reformed were made of black stone , and many were sagging , leaning , or bulging .

title: Dark Hollow
description: Dark Hollow Dark Hollow was a village in the Vast , lying on the crossroads of the Hlintar Ride and Feldar ' s Trail , between Bambryn , Fallentree , Dragon Falls and Highbank Forest , in the Fire River uplands . Description . Dark Hollow was a small village and named for the valley it sat in , which was shaded by many trees .
description_long: Dark Hollow Dark Hollow was a village in the Vast , lying on the crossroads of the Hlintar Ride and Feldar ' s Trail , between Bambryn , Fallentree , Dragon Falls and Highbank Forest , in the Fire River uplands . Description . Dark Hollow was a small village and named for the valley it sat in , which was shaded by many trees . It had a reputation as a strange and hazardous place , where faerie dragon s played , intruders were the victims of practical jokes by brownie s and other forest fey , and common animal s were the familiar s of crazed wizard s . These wizards were said by other folk to make their homes in rundown cabins in the forest , and to be conducting dangerous experiments with new spells that would let them one day take over the world . There were many hedge - wizards in Dark Hollow , of all kinds and practices . With magic being an expensive practice , most of their wealth was tied up in magic items and supplies . They kept these valuables cleverly hidden , well - guarded and trapped . A few built wand s into their desk to fire at those in front of them . Some had their small familiars carry these items piece by piece to otherwise - inaccessible locations .

title: Dark House
description: Dark House The Dark House was the name taken by a group of exiled Waterdavian lordlings who took to banditry along the Southern Sword Coast beginning around 1440 DR and was still active as of 1479 DR . The gang was led by the notorious Blakrho " Blackthroat " Phull .
description_long: Dark House The Dark House was the name taken by a group of exiled Waterdavian lordlings who took to banditry along the Southern Sword Coast beginning around 1440 DR and was still active as of 1479 DR . The gang was led by the notorious Blakrho " Blackthroat " Phull .

title: Dark Linsa
description: Dark Linsa Dark Linsa was a Welcomers thief during the late 1480s DR . History . Linsa was a thief in Phlan working for the Welcomers thieves guild .
description_long: Dark Linsa Dark Linsa was a Welcomers thief during the late 1480s DR . History . Linsa was a thief in Phlan working for the Welcomers thieves guild . After Vorgansharax ' s coup , they allied with the Zhentarim . During the Rage of Demons , she was sent by the Zhent s to kept under control a celebration for Mielikki in the village of Elventree in Cormanthor with a message from Chaab to fellow Zhents .

title: Dark Moon heresy
description: Dark Moon heresy The Dark Moon heresy was the belief that Selûne and Shar were two aspects of the same deity . Believers of this doctrine could be found teaching it to others . Origin .
description_long: Dark Moon heresy The Dark Moon heresy was the belief that Selûne and Shar were two aspects of the same deity . Believers of this doctrine could be found teaching it to others . Origin . The Dark Moon heresy was originally a scam made up by Alorgoth to lure less than unwavering worshippers of both Selûne and Shar , his goddes , to one place , the Twofold Temple , and kill them all there . Followers ' treatment by the deities . As mentioned above , those who believed in the Dark Moon Heresy held that Selûne and Shar were two faces of the same goddess . While all followers of this heresy weren ' t allowed into either goddesses ' realm on death and were judged " False " , Alorgoth was apprently onto something with his lie for clerics who supported this heresy were supported by the two - or according to them one - goddess with full access to both churchs ' spells and permission - so to speak - to grossly violate the two churchs ' tenets .

title: Dark Seldarine
description: Dark Seldarine The Dark Seldarine was the drow pantheon of gods . Overview . The Dark Seldarine , the pantheon of the drow , was led by Lolth , the Spider Queen .
description_long: Dark Seldarine The Dark Seldarine was the drow pantheon of gods . Overview . The Dark Seldarine , the pantheon of the drow , was led by Lolth , the Spider Queen . She dominated the drow race ’ s lives and urged them into heavy infighting . She was opposed to varying degrees by the rest of the pantheon . Vhaeraun , her son , was among the opposers . He had the largest following on the surface and the second largest overall among the Dark Seldarine . Lolth considered him her real rival and enemy . The others were minor players . This might give off the impression , that the Dark Seldarine was characterized by this two - top battle , it wasn ’ t . In truth , Lolth ’ s domination over the pantheon and the drow was to such an extent , that even information on the other gods wasn ’ t readily accessible to the drow . Vhaeraun ’ s existence and agenda was common knowledge among surface drow and in the Underdark where the Spider Queen wasn ’ t absolute , in other words , it was scarce where she was absolute . Eilistraee , Lolth ’ s daughter , was both on the surface and in the Underdark the stuff of wildly inaccurate and wrong legends .

title: Dark Shrine
description: Dark Shrine The Dark Shrine was a temple which was the seat of orthodox worship of Bane in Zhentil Keep . History . In 1268 DR , Fzoul Chembryl took control of the Dark Shrine of Bane and the Black Altar .
description_long: Dark Shrine The Dark Shrine was a temple which was the seat of orthodox worship of Bane in Zhentil Keep . History . In 1268 DR , Fzoul Chembryl took control of the Dark Shrine of Bane and the Black Altar . Around 1357 DR , the establishment broke from the Black Altar and Ginali took control . In 1367 DR , the Dark Shrine was destroyed by Xeno Mirrormane and his Cyric followers . Inhabitants . When the temple was run by the human cleric Ginali , his congregation consisted of thirty - four clerics and ninety - six followers .

title: Dark Speech
description: Dark Speech Dark Speech is the secret language of evil god s , a language of such evil that demon s and devil s avoid speaking it , for fear it might consume them . It is extremely difficult for mortals to learn even a single word of it , but each word is full of dread power that can be used to provoke emotions , empower magic , or corrupt physical objects . Fiend s find the language easier to learn than mortals do .
description_long: Dark Speech Dark Speech is the secret language of evil god s , a language of such evil that demon s and devil s avoid speaking it , for fear it might consume them . It is extremely difficult for mortals to learn even a single word of it , but each word is full of dread power that can be used to provoke emotions , empower magic , or corrupt physical objects . Fiend s find the language easier to learn than mortals do .

title: Dark Watch
description: Dark Watch The Dark Watch was a mercenary company based in the Orsraun Mountains and active in the Sea of Fallen Stars . Organization . The company was a group of archers mounted on hippogriff s .
description_long: Dark Watch The Dark Watch was a mercenary company based in the Orsraun Mountains and active in the Sea of Fallen Stars . Organization . The company was a group of archers mounted on hippogriff s . Activities . Usually the Dark Watch worked for pirate gangs who wanted to destroy another pirate group . Possessions . These mercenaries fought with longsword s and longbow s . History . Around 1357 DR , they fought on the losing side during the war against the arcanaloth Yrkhetep . During the Battle of Five Crowns , the original leader of the Dark Watch , Thurindar Pelamar , was killed by a member of the Sunshafts . Members . Their leader Lothar Pelamar was the brother of Thurindar .

title: Dark Wave
description: Dark Wave The Dark Wave was a small group of holy slayer s that were operating out of Hawa in 1367 DR . Activities . The Dark Wave served the Cult of Istishia , against their will .
description_long: Dark Wave The Dark Wave was a small group of holy slayer s that were operating out of Hawa in 1367 DR . Activities . The Dark Wave served the Cult of Istishia , against their will . They carried out assassinations when ordered . Base of Operations . Hawa , on the island of the Genie ' s Turban within the Corsair Domains , served as the base for the Dark Wave . Relationships . All members of the Dark Wave were under the influence of a ghul - kin named Faizah and her Waters of devotion . Members . The Dark Wave only had three members : Setara bint Aasim , Shadha , and Sahlah .

title: Dark Weavings Bazaar
description: Dark Weavings Bazaar The Dark Weavings Bazaar is the marketplace of the city of Sshamath , at the bottom of the cave . In hundreds of tents and small shops in stalagmites the visitor can buy almost everything . If he does not find what he is looking for , he can hire someone to find it for him , even humans to go search for the item in the world above .
description_long: Dark Weavings Bazaar The Dark Weavings Bazaar is the marketplace of the city of Sshamath , at the bottom of the cave . In hundreds of tents and small shops in stalagmites the visitor can buy almost everything . If he does not find what he is looking for , he can hire someone to find it for him , even humans to go search for the item in the world above . In the center of the bazaar lies the slave market . In most places such a market would consist of many tents and cages but in a city full of wizards it is housed in one building . Magical glyphs on each side try to encourage passants to buy one or more slaves . The slaves are held in magical clearstones , where they are magically shrunk to get into the fist - sized cubes and can be easily stored on the shelves .

title: Dark Wind Stables
description: Dark Wind Stables The Dark Wind Stables were located within the great fortress of Sarahin in the Haunted Lands . Description . Basalt floors and white - washed stone walls adorned the stables .
description_long: Dark Wind Stables The Dark Wind Stables were located within the great fortress of Sarahin in the Haunted Lands . Description . Basalt floors and white - washed stone walls adorned the stables . The stalls and lintels were made from cedar wood . Inhabitants . These stables housed racing camels called mehari and horses used for racing and sending messages . Hisan bin Hanif cared for the horses . Beyond the mundane animals , the stables also held a two - headed roc named Sar , and a pegasus named Sulbain .

title: Dark aura
description: Dark aura Dark aura was a divine magic spell available to priests of Cyric , the Mad God . It surrounded the caster with a gloomy atmosphere that greatly improved the caster ' s combat ability and , to a lesser extent , that of all evil - aligned creatures within the vicinity . At the same time , it hindered the combat ability of good - aligned creatures .
description_long: Dark aura Dark aura was a divine magic spell available to priests of Cyric , the Mad God . It surrounded the caster with a gloomy atmosphere that greatly improved the caster ' s combat ability and , to a lesser extent , that of all evil - aligned creatures within the vicinity . At the same time , it hindered the combat ability of good - aligned creatures . Effects . This spell lasted for seven minutes and had a spherical radius of 70 ft ( 21 m ) centered on the caster . More experienced casters could extend the duration and the radius of effect . The " dark aura " was a noticeable dimness , similar to a partial eclipse ( vision was not impaired , there was just less light ) that enveloped the caster and all within the area of effect . Those that were evil in alignment felt a slight improvement in their combat abilities . Those that were of good alignment felt the weight of menace on them and had their combat prowess degraded by a similar amount . Beings that were neutral on the good / evil spectrum were completely unaffected by this spell . The caster received three times the boost that other evil creatures gained to combat actions .

title: Dark creature
description: Dark creature A dark creature was a type of creature that had a strong connection to the Plane of Shadow , possessing a supernatural ability to hide in shadows and other powers . Description . Dark creatures resembled their counterparts on the Material Plane , though they were strange and distorted reflections .
description_long: Dark creature A dark creature was a type of creature that had a strong connection to the Plane of Shadow , possessing a supernatural ability to hide in shadows and other powers . Description . Dark creatures resembled their counterparts on the Material Plane , though they were strange and distorted reflections . They tended to be much duller in coloration , with skin tones and hair highlights having more gray and black hues , while brighter colors , like yellow or white , almost never appeared upon them . Overall , they seemed more shadowy and eerie . They also weighed somewhat less than an equivalent creature , suggesting a portion of their very substance had been replaced by the shadowstuff of the Plane of Shadow . Abilities . A dark creature possessed a supernatural ability for melding with shadow . Even while being observed and standing in plain sight , a dark creature could hide itself within a nearby shadow , provided there was no daylight or magical light to illuminate them . They were also incredibly stealthy , whether in hiding or creeping about unheard . Dark creatures also possessed darkvision to a distance of 60 feet ( 18 .

title: Dark creeper
description: Dark creeper The dark creepers were a race of humanoid s dwelling in the Underdark . They were natural rogue s with powers of stealth and shadow . They were one of the two subraces of the dark one s .
description_long: Dark creeper The dark creepers were a race of humanoid s dwelling in the Underdark . They were natural rogue s with powers of stealth and shadow . They were one of the two subraces of the dark one s . Description . Although humanoid in form , dark creepers were stunted in built , being small and slight . Unusually , they had unguligrade legs ( similar to a goat ' s ) , ending in small black hooves in place of feet . These hooves were soft , making no sound on stone . A dark creeper ' s skin was pallid , and it had a large nose , feral - or sinister - looking beady eyes , and bushy eyebrows . They only ever wore black , shrouding themselves all over in cloaks , wraps and turbans or hoods . They typically fought in leather armor and wielded a dagger or short sword and longbow suiting their size . Powers . Thrice a day , a dark creeper could envelop itself in cloak of shadows , concealing it from view even in bright light , aiding its defense . This darkness was magical , so a foe needed the ability to see in magical darkness to penetrate it . A dark creeper could utilize all its acute senses — hearing and smell as well as sight — to discern its surroundings and locate beings .

title: Dark elf
description: Dark elf Dark elves , were elves , known as Ssri - tel - quessir in the elven tongue , and were the ancestors of the drow . The two terms were oftentimes used interchangeably , even by elves ( Tel - quessir ) themselves . Dark elves had dark brown skin , as opposed to the ebony skin that drow presently have .
description_long: Dark elf Dark elves , were elves , known as Ssri - tel - quessir in the elven tongue , and were the ancestors of the drow . The two terms were oftentimes used interchangeably , even by elves ( Tel - quessir ) themselves . Dark elves had dark brown skin , as opposed to the ebony skin that drow presently have . They also " may " have had black hair instead of white and no darkvision . Dark elves were also not tainted with Wendonai ' s blood . History . Roughly , twenty - seven millennia before the raising of the Standing Stone , the Fey creator race opened gates to the Feywild in an effort to undermine the ruling dragon empires . Through these portals , the first elves immigrated to Toril . These primitive green elves worship the Faerie gods ( not the Seldarine , which were unknown at this time ) . Although most green elves were content to remain in small scattered tribes , one group known as the Ilythiiri , negotiated a truce with dragonkind and began carving out a small kingdom in the south . The great Ilythiir capital at Atorrnash would remain a shining beacon of elf culture for millennia .

title: Dark embrace
description: Dark embrace Dark embrace was a spell used by priests of Vhaeraun to store a spell for rapid use at a later time . Effects . On casting , a dark mask was created around the face , in which a second spell could be stored .
description_long: Dark embrace Dark embrace was a spell used by priests of Vhaeraun to store a spell for rapid use at a later time . Effects . On casting , a dark mask was created around the face , in which a second spell could be stored . This stored spell could be rapidly unleashed , either on the caster or on another person . In the latter case , the mask placed itself on the target , who was then subject to the spell . The mask created by " dark embrace " could be used as a substitute for a holy symbol . Components . This spell required only verbal components to cast . Special . A darkmask who had reached a sufficient level of skill could also use " dark embrace " , though their version was used for rapid casting and transfer of spells .

title: Dark mirror
description: Dark mirror Dark mirror was a combination abjuration and alteration spell that could counter , reflect , or penetrate " darkness " spells . Effects . This spell had three variants , one of which had to be chosen at the time of casting .
description_long: Dark mirror Dark mirror was a combination abjuration and alteration spell that could counter , reflect , or penetrate " darkness " spells . Effects . This spell had three variants , one of which had to be chosen at the time of casting . The first variant prevented magical darkness from enveloping the caster — all manner of " darkness " spells targeting the caster of " dark mirror " , or in the vicinity , were countered . The second variant reflected all " darkness " spells back upon their caster . If the target of the reflection resisted his or her own spell , then it fizzled . The caster of " dark mirror " could choose to reflect magical darkness spells back to the location of the attacker , rather that at the attacker ' s person , in which case no resistance was possible , but the attacker could choose to leave the darkened area . The third variant allowed the caster to be unimpaired by magical darkness , seeing as they normally would , out to a distance of 10 ft ( 3 m ) per level of the caster .

title: Dark naga
description: Dark naga A dark naga was a naga subspecies that looked like a large purple snake or eel with a barbed stinger at the end of its tail and a human face . Dark nagas could speak Common and Infernal . They liked to plot with other creatures of evil alignment so that they could gather wealth more easily .
description_long: Dark naga A dark naga was a naga subspecies that looked like a large purple snake or eel with a barbed stinger at the end of its tail and a human face . Dark nagas could speak Common and Infernal . They liked to plot with other creatures of evil alignment so that they could gather wealth more easily . Description . Dark nagas measured approximately 12 feet long and weighed about 300 pounds . Their scales were dark blue or purple , often with black frills or scale patterns . The body of a dark naga was more similar to that of an eel rather than a snake . Its tail ended in a poisonous stinger . Their veins contained an oily black gore . Society . Dark nagas craved power and wealth . They loved using their magical powers and the treasures they found in ancient ruins to rule those who were weaker than themselves . Combat . Dark nagas would attempt to use high terrain to their advantage to stay out of the reach of their enemies . Abilities . They could cast sorcerer spells and their stings carried a poison that could induce a nightmarish sleep . They were resistant to all charm effects and had the permanent ability to " detect thoughts " .

title: Dark one
description: Dark one The dark ones were a race of humanoid s dwelling in the Underdark . They were natural rogue s with powers of stealth and shadow . They were divided into two subraces : the short , gnome - like dark creeper s and the human - like dark stalker s .
description_long: Dark one The dark ones were a race of humanoid s dwelling in the Underdark . They were natural rogue s with powers of stealth and shadow . They were divided into two subraces : the short , gnome - like dark creeper s and the human - like dark stalker s . However , it was hard to say if they were actually the same race . Description . Although dark creepers and dark stalkers looked very different , all dark ones wore only black clothing . Powers . Thrice a day , a dark one could envelop itself in cloak of shadows , concealing it from view even in bright light , aiding its defense . This darkness was magical , so a foe needed the ability to see in magical darkness to penetrate it . A dark one could utilize all its acute senses — hearing and smell as well as sight — to discern its surroundings and locate beings . Even in absolute darkness , it had perfect sight out to 60 feet ( 18 . 3 meters ) . However , when caught in daylight ( natural or magical ) , a dark one was dazzled or badly demoralized in all ways . Personality . The dark ones hated light of any kind , and would assault any being who carried a source of illumination , whether a lantern , a torch , or magic .

title: Dark promise
description: Dark promise Dark promise was a divine magic spell available to priests of Bane , the Black Lord . It put the victim under a type of " geas " that adversely affected his or her health each time the " promise " was broken . After Bane ' s supposed death in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR , Cyric granted spells to Banite priests for a decade , so it was possible this spell could be found within the church of Cyric .
description_long: Dark promise Dark promise was a divine magic spell available to priests of Bane , the Black Lord . It put the victim under a type of " geas " that adversely affected his or her health each time the " promise " was broken . After Bane ' s supposed death in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR , Cyric granted spells to Banite priests for a decade , so it was possible this spell could be found within the church of Cyric . Effects . The caster had to touch the target of this spell as it was being cast . If the recipient was unwilling , they got one chance to resist the spell or be permanently bound to a " dark promise " . The " promise " had to be spoken by the caster , had to be an order that was in Bane ' s interest , and could not cause the victim to do something suicidal . Therefore , promises such as " Never eat " , " Fight without weapons or armor " , or " Don ' t think about purple orcs " would not work and the spell would fizzle . Appropriate commands included " Never tell anyone about this place " , " Never attack a servant of Bane " , and " For every ten silver pieces you receive in a tenday , give the church of Bane one silver piece " .

title: Dark stalker
description: Dark stalker The dark stalkers were a race of humanoid s dwelling in the Underdark . They were natural rogue s with powers of stealth and shadow . They were one of the two subraces of the dark one s .
description_long: Dark stalker The dark stalkers were a race of humanoid s dwelling in the Underdark . They were natural rogue s with powers of stealth and shadow . They were one of the two subraces of the dark one s . Description . Unlike their dark creeper kin , dark stalkers appeared almost fully human , but with dusky skin and pale , even white eyes . They only ever wore black clothing of somber style with masks to cover their faces . They fought in leather armor . and wielded a short sword and javelin or rapier , longbow , and dagger . Powers . Thrice a day , a dark stalker could envelop itself in cloak of shadows , concealing it from view even in bright light , aiding its defense . This darkness was magical , so a foe needed the ability to see in magical darkness to penetrate it . A dark stalker could utilize all its acute senses — hearing and smell as well as sight — to discern its surroundings and locate beings . Even in absolute darkness , it had perfect sight out to 60 feet ( 18 . 3 meters ) . However , when caught in daylight ( natural or magical ) , a dark stalker was dazzled or badly demoralized in all ways . A dark stalker could conjure a " fog cloud " spell twice a day .

title: Dark tree
description: Dark tree A dark tree was an evil intelligent tree that looked like a cypress tree , but slightly darker and devoid of moss . It was known to grapple and bite . It lived on drinking blood from human s and other intelligent creatures that wandered into its native jungle .
description_long: Dark tree A dark tree was an evil intelligent tree that looked like a cypress tree , but slightly darker and devoid of moss . It was known to grapple and bite . It lived on drinking blood from human s and other intelligent creatures that wandered into its native jungle . History . It was said that a Halruaa n wizard called Benauril wanted to create the dark trees as servants not unlike treant s around the mid - to - late 1100s DR . The experiment went horribly wrong and the servants slew their master . They spread into the surrounding forests . By 1372 DR , travelers had reported encountering these dangerous and huge plants in the Aerilpar Forest , the Forest of Amtar , Rethild , the Toadsquat Mountains , and the southern and eastern reaches of the Lluirwood . Description . Resembling a darker version of the harmless cypress tree , the dark trees grew to 18 – 20 feet ( 5 . 5 – 6 . 1m ) in height , with a span of branches 40 feet ( 12 m ) across . There were reports of dark trees growing to twice that size , possibly due to their long lifespan . Discerning a dark tree from a normal tree was not an easy task .

title: Darkas
description: Darkas Darkas the Storyteller was a half - elven woman who dwelled in Memnon in Calimshan through the 13th and 14th centuries DR . At over a century old by 1370 DR , she was gray - haired and had only one eye , but it remained keenly observant . She had a very good memory of her long life in Memnon , and clearly knew all the rumors and happenings about the city .
description_long: Darkas Darkas the Storyteller was a half - elven woman who dwelled in Memnon in Calimshan through the 13th and 14th centuries DR . At over a century old by 1370 DR , she was gray - haired and had only one eye , but it remained keenly observant . She had a very good memory of her long life in Memnon , and clearly knew all the rumors and happenings about the city . The secrets she knew were suggested in her songs . She was popular with almost everyone in Memnon , and was very influential politically .

title: Darkberry
description: Darkberry Darkberry was a type of berry bush found in forests around the Sea of Fallen Stars . They grew in clumps hidden deep in the forests . Darkberry bushes produced small purple berries , only a few of which ripened each fall , and they were growing rarer every year by 1372 DR .
description_long: Darkberry Darkberry was a type of berry bush found in forests around the Sea of Fallen Stars . They grew in clumps hidden deep in the forests . Darkberry bushes produced small purple berries , only a few of which ripened each fall , and they were growing rarer every year by 1372 DR . Ripe darkberries contained shadowstuff ; when split or crushed , they released a circle of blackness 5 feet ( 1 . 5 meters ) wide , large enough to hide a humanoid , for a dozen seconds . A single darkberry cost 5 gp .

title: Darkbolt
description: Darkbolt Darkbolt was an evocation spell unique to cleric s with the Darkness domain . It released bolts of darkness that damaged and dazed the target . Effect .
description_long: Darkbolt Darkbolt was an evocation spell unique to cleric s with the Darkness domain . It released bolts of darkness that damaged and dazed the target . Effect . The caster unleashed beams of darkness from his open palm . The caster had to succeed at a ranged touch attack in order to strike the target . The number of bolts the cleric could hurl increased with his power although only a maximum seven bolts could be thrown . A Darkbolt dealt a moderate amount of damage to a living creature , and the creature was dazed for a short time . Undead took no damage from the spell , but could be dazed .

title: Darkdance Manor
description: Darkdance Manor Darkdance Manor was a large decrepit manor located in the west end of Westgate near Tidetown . Structure . The manor had been maintained for years by the family ' s loyal dwarf servant Elevar .
description_long: Darkdance Manor Darkdance Manor was a large decrepit manor located in the west end of Westgate near Tidetown . Structure . The manor had been maintained for years by the family ' s loyal dwarf servant Elevar . The manor had a magic gate that opened only for family members . History . The manor was the ancestral home of House Darkdance although the last family members abandoned the property decades prior to 1480 DR , when Myrin Darkdance moved into the mansion .

title: Darkening
description: Darkening The Darkening was the name given to a spell that cast shadows over the Silver Marches in preparation for the drow and orc invasion of that land starting in 1484 DR . The spell was given to the drow wizard Tsabrak Xorlarrin by the illithid Methil El - Viddenvelp by the order of Matron Mother Quenthel Baenre . While casting the spell , Tsabrak was said to have served as a conduit of Lolth , the first such occurrence since Yvonnel Baenre channeled Lolth in when destroying House Oblodra in 1358 / 1359 DR .
description_long: Darkening The Darkening was the name given to a spell that cast shadows over the Silver Marches in preparation for the drow and orc invasion of that land starting in 1484 DR . The spell was given to the drow wizard Tsabrak Xorlarrin by the illithid Methil El - Viddenvelp by the order of Matron Mother Quenthel Baenre . While casting the spell , Tsabrak was said to have served as a conduit of Lolth , the first such occurrence since Yvonnel Baenre channeled Lolth in when destroying House Oblodra in 1358 / 1359 DR . The effects of the Darkening were described as " roiling clouds of smoke or some other foul substance that turned daylight into something less than moonlight and hid the stars entirely . "

title: Darkflow River
description: Darkflow River The Darkflow River , or simply the Darkflow , was a short river in the Vast Swamp that formed part of the border between Cormyr and Sembia in the east . Geography . The source of the Darkflow lay in the heart of the Vast Swamp , being fed by the marsh - water itself , and it flowed south into the Lake of Dragons .
description_long: Darkflow River The Darkflow River , or simply the Darkflow , was a short river in the Vast Swamp that formed part of the border between Cormyr and Sembia in the east . Geography . The source of the Darkflow lay in the heart of the Vast Swamp , being fed by the marsh - water itself , and it flowed south into the Lake of Dragons . The regular rains over the Vast Swamp caused the Darkflow to swell and flood the lands beside it . Description . The river was wide and flowed only sluggishly . As the name suggested , the water was so dark that it was described as " inky " . This was a result of sediment , filth , and pollution in the Vast Swamp — the water was not filtered or cleaned as would happen in a natural marsh . As a result , the river - water was foul and stinking . Fauna . The river was home to countless dangerous creatures . Activities . Lizardmen dwelling in the Vast Swamp sometimes ventured down the Darkflow to raid villages . History . The village of Battlerise , which stood on the west bank of the Darkflow River , was once beset by lizardmen from the river and monsters emerging from the Vast Swamp . Long before the 1360s DR , its population had plummeted .

title: Darkhold
description: Darkhold Darkhold , originally called The Keep of the Fallen Hills , was the western stronghold of the Zhentarim , located near the Sunset Mountains in the Western Heartlands . Government . In 1372 DR , Darkhold was led by the Pereghost , who commanded its 800 warriors , and Dhamir Ercals , who led the resident clerics of Cyric .
description_long: Darkhold Darkhold , originally called The Keep of the Fallen Hills , was the western stronghold of the Zhentarim , located near the Sunset Mountains in the Western Heartlands . Government . In 1372 DR , Darkhold was led by the Pereghost , who commanded its 800 warriors , and Dhamir Ercals , who led the resident clerics of Cyric . Though both leaders were servants of Cyric and were preparing for the inevitable holy war against the Banites , the hatred between them was such that more time was spent on assassination plots than their Zhentarim duties . By 1489 DR , the Pereghost ( or a new ruler wearing his armor ) was publically acknowledged as the sole master of Darkhold , though the Beholder Manxam also appeared to be a member of the stronghold ' s senior leadership . In addition to the fluctuating ranks of Zhentarim agents using the castle as a base of operations , Darkhold maintained two war units ( one of heavy infantry and one of archers ) and an aerie of trained wyverns . History . Darkhold was built to suit giant - sized humanoids . Some said that the looming castle was built a millennium prior to 1370 DR by giant s as a summer capital for the Giant Empires .

title: Darklake
description: Darklake The Darklake was a series of connected bodies of water in the Underdark . They were formerly linked by waterfalls but later governed by locks created by dwarven engineers . Geography .
description_long: Darklake The Darklake was a series of connected bodies of water in the Underdark . They were formerly linked by waterfalls but later governed by locks created by dwarven engineers . Geography . On the shores of the Darklake were the settlements of Gracklstugh and Mantol - Derith ( northwest ) . The Darklake was located some 100 miles north and east of the Labyrinth . Dwarven tunnels carved over the Darklake connected Ammarindar to Menzoberranzan , a distance of some 250 miles . Description . The Darklake was located in a huge cavern more than 100 miles across . The cavern was up to 1 , 000 feet tall in some places , but very low in others . It could take more than two days to transverse the lake ( from Mantol - Derith to Gracklstugh by boat . The surface of the Darklake was broken with stalagmites , stalactites , and columns . The duergar of Gracklstugh patrolled the Darklake . Inhabitants . The caverns were used as a relatively safe passage by duergar , although the place had its share of monsters ( mainly freshwater troll s and a type of evil intelligent freshwater manta ray ) .

title: Darklands
description: Darklands The Darklands were located underneath the heart of Faerûn and formed an important domain of the Underdark . Geography . Located above the Darklands was the Dragon Coast , portions of the Orsraun Mountains , Turmish , and Chessenta .
description_long: Darklands The Darklands were located underneath the heart of Faerûn and formed an important domain of the Underdark . Geography . Located above the Darklands was the Dragon Coast , portions of the Orsraun Mountains , Turmish , and Chessenta . This vast subterranean realm stretched all the way from Cairnheim in the west to Traaskl Thorog in the east . Notable locations . Cities . The great duergar city of Dunspeirrin was the most powerful stronghold in the region . However , the duergar controlled only a relatively small part of the Darklands , owing to the sheer size of the region .

title: Darkling
description: Darkling Darklings were a lineage of fey that suffered a curse from the Summer Queen , forever doomed to absorb light and to suffer rapid aging from exposure to it . The absorbed light over the lifetime of a darkling was explosively released at the time of its death , destroying its body and much of its surroundings . Society .
description_long: Darkling Darklings were a lineage of fey that suffered a curse from the Summer Queen , forever doomed to absorb light and to suffer rapid aging from exposure to it . The absorbed light over the lifetime of a darkling was explosively released at the time of its death , destroying its body and much of its surroundings . Society . Due to their curse , most darklings dwelt in caves or underground . Under cities , they typically worked as thieves or assassins . Despite this curse , however , darklings retained their love for beauty , and sometimes risked watching a sunset or occasionally using light to appreciate the colors in a piece of art . It was possible for the most experienced darklings to undertake a ritual in order to become elders . The ritual consisted of applying glowing tattoos over its body , therefore releasing some of the accumulated light . If unsuccessful , the ritual was fatal . Otherwise , it resulted in a darkling elder : a taller and fairer form , similar to a grey - skinned elf . History . It was told in legends that a seelie fey , whose real name has been erased from history , betrayed the Summer Queen . In her wrath , she cursed him and his entire house .

title: Darkmaiden ' s Leap
description: Darkmaiden ' s Leap Darkmaiden ' s Leap was a shrine sacred to the goddess Eilistraee and her followers , found in the northern High Forest , southeast of Everlund . Description . Darkmaiden ' s Leap was a small clearing with a large flat - top gray rock about six feet tall and five feet in diamater .
description_long: Darkmaiden ' s Leap Darkmaiden ' s Leap was a shrine sacred to the goddess Eilistraee and her followers , found in the northern High Forest , southeast of Everlund . Description . Darkmaiden ' s Leap was a small clearing with a large flat - top gray rock about six feet tall and five feet in diamater . Pre - Time of Troubles the stone was known as Hastrin ' s Grayrock , but after 1358 DR , the time when the place became sacred to Dark Maiden , the top of the stone bore a single left footprint the size of a drow female ' s foot and the place was named Darkmaiden ' s Leap by the followers of the goddess . Properties . Darmmaiden ' s Leap was a planar touchstone , a hub of energies linking strongly connected planes together ( in this case , Toril and Eilistraee ' s realm in Arvandor ) . Darkmaiden ' s Leap was infused with the magic of Eilistraee .

title: Darkmask
description: Darkmask The Darkmask was a special divine caster of Vhaeraun . They were considered the elite among the clerics . Becoming a Darkmask .
description_long: Darkmask The Darkmask was a special divine caster of Vhaeraun . They were considered the elite among the clerics . Becoming a Darkmask . Formerly open only to male drow , the gender barrier was dropped and entry opened to half - drow at latest in 1372 DR , the darkmask was a special kind of divine caster of Vhaeraun with skills in stealth , generally a ranger or a cleric with the skills of a rogue or a ranger . A would be darkmask had to fulfill a number of requirements . Rudimentary skills in , namely in stealing , basic survival skills in the wilderness , hiding and sneaking , out of which hiding and sneaking needed special training . One also needed to be trained to be inured by the effects of sunlight , naturally a requirement a half - drow fulfilled by virtue of being a half - drow . They also needed experience at fighting a clerical follower of Lolth , though they only needed to survive the encounter and not necessarily win . General Information . All members of Vhaeraun ’ s clergy had some degree of skill in trickery and often learned the additional skills of a rogue .

title: Darkness
description: Darkness Darkness was an evocation or alteration spell that created an area impenetrable to normal light . Effects . The area shrouded by this spell was 20 ft ( 6 .
description_long: Darkness Darkness was an evocation or alteration spell that created an area impenetrable to normal light . Effects . The area shrouded by this spell was 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) in radius . The range and duration of this spell varied with the spellcasting tradition . The evocation school version required the caster to touch an object which then " radiated " darkness . The darkness could be blocked just like light by covering the dweomered object . The divine magic version of this spell could be cast from up to 120 yards ( 110 m ) away and onto any object or just into the air . The effect remained in place unless cast upon a movable object , and was not blockable if cast on an area . The ranged version of this spell allowed the caster a chance to blind a creature by successfully casting the spell centered on its visual organs . The reverse of this spell , " light " , caused the area to be illuminated with a duration double that of " darkness " . " Darkness " spells could be used to counter or dispel " light " of equal or lesser power , and vice versa . Sinhala stones were known to prevent magical darkness .

title: Darkness , 15 ' radius
description: Darkness , 15 ' radius Darkness , 15 ' radius ( originally , Fahren ' s darkness ) was an alteration spell that made an area impervious to normal light . Effects . This spell was similar to " darkness " except for the smaller radius of effect ( 15 ft / 4 .
description_long: Darkness , 15 ' radius Darkness , 15 ' radius ( originally , Fahren ' s darkness ) was an alteration spell that made an area impervious to normal light . Effects . This spell was similar to " darkness " except for the smaller radius of effect ( 15 ft / 4 . 6 m as opposed to 20 ft / 6 . 1 m ) and the ability to cast it at a range . The range of this spell increased with the experience of the caster . The darkness was total , preventing sight for even those creatures that could normally see in the dark , and immobile , because it affected an area rather than an object . The illusionist version of this spell had a shorter , more unpredictable duration than the wizard version . " Darkness , 15 ' radius " countered and was countered by " light " and " continual light " . Sinhala stones were known to prevent magical darkness . History . The spell was invented by the Netherese arcanist Fahren in −1479 DR .

title: Darkness domain
description: Darkness domain The Darkness domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters darkness spell powers . There are two versions of this domain : one from the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting " ( 3rd Edition ) , and the other from the " Book of Vile Darkness " . Cleric s can select their spells from either list at the DM ' s discretion .
description_long: Darkness domain The Darkness domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters darkness spell powers . There are two versions of this domain : one from the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting " ( 3rd Edition ) , and the other from the " Book of Vile Darkness " . Cleric s can select their spells from either list at the DM ' s discretion . Darkness Domain Powers . Clerics with the darkness domain can fight while blind , and concealed targets gain no benefit from their concealment .

title: Darksong Knight
description: Darksong Knight Darksong Knights were the elite warriors of Eilistraee , famed for their tireless hunting of the demonic agents of Lolth . They were mostly active in the lands of ancient Ilythiir . As of the 1490s DR , post Second Sundering , the Darksong Knights were very much active , but existed only in small numbers .
description_long: Darksong Knight Darksong Knights were the elite warriors of Eilistraee , famed for their tireless hunting of the demonic agents of Lolth . They were mostly active in the lands of ancient Ilythiir . As of the 1490s DR , post Second Sundering , the Darksong Knights were very much active , but existed only in small numbers . Abilities . As the prey of the Darksong Knights were the demonic servants of Lolth , they honed their skills to fight these creatures , especially yochlol : they knew how to predict the demons ' movements and strike with precision and force . Utilizing a dance - like and complex style of swordplay , the trained Darksong Knight in battle was far more mobile and deceptive than other fighters . Notable Darksong Knights . Cavatina Xarann

title: Darkstalker Wars
description: Darkstalker Wars The Darkstalker Wars were a series of battles between the various guild thieves and assassin s of Calimshan in the wake of the death of Bhaal . They were the first major event of the Tenth Age of Calimshan . All Bhaal - worshiping assassins were killed by Bane just before the end of the Time of Troubles .
description_long: Darkstalker Wars The Darkstalker Wars were a series of battles between the various guild thieves and assassin s of Calimshan in the wake of the death of Bhaal . They were the first major event of the Tenth Age of Calimshan . All Bhaal - worshiping assassins were killed by Bane just before the end of the Time of Troubles . The criminal underworld in Calimshan was thrown into utter turmoil as the Shadow Thieves , whose assassins , including the entire ruling council of the guild , almost universally worshipped Bhaal , tried to consolidate their sudden loss in power by drastically reorganizing their remaining operatives . Rashid el Djenispool , the syl - pasha of Calimshan at the time , had long tolerated the Shadow Thieves , as battling a single criminal element in his nation was , in many ways , easier than combatting several different factions at once . The Shadow Thieves had direct control of almost all crime in Calimshan until Bhaal ' s death whereupon the other guilds and freelancers felt the need to take their place in the power vacuum that had been created .

title: Darkturret
description: Darkturret Darkturret was a ruined castle located on the banks of the River Orlaphar in Gontal . Because it was exposed to the Spellplague , the ruins of Darkturret existed outside time and space . Background .
description_long: Darkturret Darkturret was a ruined castle located on the banks of the River Orlaphar in Gontal . Because it was exposed to the Spellplague , the ruins of Darkturret existed outside time and space . Background . As a place that existed outside time and space , the castle could shift through time , trapping within its ruins creatures and adventurers from any time period of either Abeir and Toril . The ghosts of the members of the Garrandar family were also trapped forever in Darkturret . Among the rooms of Darkturret , there was one connected to a time period when the goddess Mystryl was still alive , another room connected to the year 569 DR , and another to the year 2421 DR . Another room had magic al crystal spheres that allowed a person to see specific historical events . Among the events showed by the spheres were : History . Darkturret was originally built long ago by a unnamed wizard to serve as its home . After being affected by the Spellplague , the original site was removed from normal time and space .

title: Darkvision
description: Darkvision Darkvision referred to the ability to see in the dark by allowing a creature to discern forms , as in normal daylight vision , only in shades of greys . It was similar to low - light vision , a trait more commonly found among surface races . Underground creatures often had darkvision , including drow , illithid s , and minotaur s .
description_long: Darkvision Darkvision referred to the ability to see in the dark by allowing a creature to discern forms , as in normal daylight vision , only in shades of greys . It was similar to low - light vision , a trait more commonly found among surface races . Underground creatures often had darkvision , including drow , illithid s , and minotaur s .

title: Darkvision ( spell )
description: Darkvision ( spell ) Darkvision was an transmutation spell that gave vision in total darkness . Effect . The older version of the spell made the caster see within 60 feet ( 18 meters ) of total darkness , everything in total darkness would appear black and white .
description_long: Darkvision ( spell ) Darkvision was an transmutation spell that gave vision in total darkness . Effect . The older version of the spell made the caster see within 60 feet ( 18 meters ) of total darkness , everything in total darkness would appear black and white . This version could be made permanent with Permanency spell . The post Second Sundering version gave the same ability but better : 60 feet normal vision in total darkness . Components . Vocal and somatic components where needed as well as a agate or a pinch of dried carrot .

title: Darkwalker
description: Darkwalker Darkwalkers were a group of warlock s bound by the dark pact to an exceptional degree . Attitudes . Opening themselves up to the full power of the darkness , darkwalkers cared little for the fate of their own soul s , which others might try and protect from the corrupting powers that darkwalkers dealt with on a regular basis .
description_long: Darkwalker Darkwalkers were a group of warlock s bound by the dark pact to an exceptional degree . Attitudes . Opening themselves up to the full power of the darkness , darkwalkers cared little for the fate of their own soul s , which others might try and protect from the corrupting powers that darkwalkers dealt with on a regular basis . Darkwalkers knew , however , that this ultimately limited their power and so did not give in to such fears , accepting what came as a matter of consequence . Culture . Most warlocks who dealt with the demon s of the Abyss were more than a little concerned with losing their souls in the process , a danger far from insubstantial or imaginary . However , darkwalkers felt that protecting oneself from this was merely delaying the inevitable so instead of squalling in fear or trying to hold back their power , darkwalkers embraced it fully , using it to confront and counter the powers they dealt with rather than falling back from them . As a result , darkwalkers obtained an almost otherworldly presence , removing themselves from the affairs of the mortal world while not wholly embracing the ways of their dark patrons .

title: Darkwalker on Moonshae
description: Darkwalker on Moonshae Darkwalker on Moonshae , by Douglas Niles , is the first book in the Moonshae trilogy . It was the first novel set in the " Forgotten Realms " , followed in published order by " The Crystal Shard " by R . A .
description_long: Darkwalker on Moonshae Darkwalker on Moonshae , by Douglas Niles , is the first book in the Moonshae trilogy . It was the first novel set in the " Forgotten Realms " , followed in published order by " The Crystal Shard " by R . A . Salvatore . Summary . Kazgoroth , the Beast , has come into the world to destroy the power of the Earthmother . Changing its shape as needs be , the Beast goes across the island of Gwynneth , corrupting everything in its way . Its destination is a large gathering of Northmen raiders at Oman ' s Isle , in the middle of the Moonshaes , where they are preparing an assault on the kingdom of Corwell . The Northmen don ' t realize yet that this is going to be more than just a plundering raid . They don ' t know that their leader isn ' t King Thelgaar Ironhand , but the Beast , who has killed the king and assumed his shape . Meanwhile , the Earthmother , aware of the danger and hurting from the corruption brought to the land , her body , by the vile presence of the Beast , awakes her children - the Leviathan , the Pack , and Kamerynn , the unicorn . They will try to stop Kazgoroth in different ways , but that won ' t be enough .

title: Darkwoods Massacre
description: Darkwoods Massacre The Darkwoods Massacre was a battle fought in the Darkwoods of Cormanthor between an orc horde from Vastar and combined elven and human forces of the Akh ' Velahr of Cormanthyr in the Year of Seven Stones , 335 DR . Events . Lead up .
description_long: Darkwoods Massacre The Darkwoods Massacre was a battle fought in the Darkwoods of Cormanthor between an orc horde from Vastar and combined elven and human forces of the Akh ' Velahr of Cormanthyr in the Year of Seven Stones , 335 DR . Events . Lead up . Late in the Year of Cold Clashes , 331 DR , the orcs of Vastar launched a surprise attack on Cormanthyr , and occupied a portion of the lands east of the Old Elven Court . They solidified their forces in the area over the next few years . The akh ' velahrn forces of Myth Drannor attempted to recover these lands three times . The battle . The fourth major effort by the akh ' velahrn occurred in the height of the summer of the Year of Seven Stones , 335 DR as they ventured into the Darkwoods against them . However , the akh ' velahrn forces suffered from ineptness and bigotry among its elven officers . Troop placements were biased , communications were not maintained and orders were not shared while in camp . Worse , they treated the non - elven soldiers cruelly , willingly sacrificing them for the safety of their elven comrades .

title: Darla
description: Darla Darla was a young thief in Neverwinter . Activities . Darla was one the leaders of the Little Rats , a gang of children affiliated with Dead Rats gang , acting as spies and messengers .
description_long: Darla Darla was a young thief in Neverwinter . Activities . Darla was one the leaders of the Little Rats , a gang of children affiliated with Dead Rats gang , acting as spies and messengers . History . In 1479 DR , she approached an adventuring party that was investigating the kidnapping cases . She offered vital information that connected an Ashmadai cell to Elden Vargas .

title: Darlan Mortem
description: Darlan Mortem Darlan Morten was a male half - elf shadow adept who was one of the members of the Shadow Council of the Shadow Thieves . Darlan was an obscure manipulator of the Shadow Weave who used his position to increase his collection of magic items . His duty was to control the guild ' s operations between Baldur ' s Gate and Amn .
description_long: Darlan Mortem Darlan Morten was a male half - elf shadow adept who was one of the members of the Shadow Council of the Shadow Thieves . Darlan was an obscure manipulator of the Shadow Weave who used his position to increase his collection of magic items . His duty was to control the guild ' s operations between Baldur ' s Gate and Amn .

title: Darlisan
description: Darlisan Darlisan the Rover was one of the best hunters in Vaasa in 1479 DR . Activities . Darlisan was a superb hunter and an infallible tracker .
description_long: Darlisan Darlisan the Rover was one of the best hunters in Vaasa in 1479 DR . Activities . Darlisan was a superb hunter and an infallible tracker . He worked guiding caravans or collecting bounties but Darlisan usually hunted in the Bleak Steppes of Haatar - Baen . Personality . Darlisan was a man of few words .

title: Darlutheene Ambershields
description: Darlutheene Ambershields Darlutheene Ambershields is the daughter of a family of servants in Suzail , Cormyr . Appearance . Darlutheene has blonde hair and violet eyes .
description_long: Darlutheene Ambershields Darlutheene Ambershields is the daughter of a family of servants in Suzail , Cormyr . Appearance . Darlutheene has blonde hair and violet eyes . She is overweight and likes to dress in fancy clothes , such as a royal blue gown , peacock plumes and a silk top . She also wears false gems and other jewellery like rings . She has six maids - of - adornment who do her make - up .

title: Darmon
description: Darmon Sir Darmon was a male human and member of the Nine of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . If the Kalach - Cha and the companions sided with the Watch and raided the Smuggler ' s warehouse , Darmon would appear before them giving orders to his men , since this problem worried Lord Nasher himself .
description_long: Darmon Sir Darmon was a male human and member of the Nine of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . If the Kalach - Cha and the companions sided with the Watch and raided the Smuggler ' s warehouse , Darmon would appear before them giving orders to his men , since this problem worried Lord Nasher himself . The Kalach - Cha would ' ve told him that the thieves at the warehouse have been dealt with . Darmon and his men would be sad as they had to be at the court with gentleman and ladies . However , Kalach - Cha could recommend the Sunken Flagon as the place to drink , making Darmon and his men cheerful and Kalach - Cha a bit chaotic .

title: Darmshall
description: Darmshall Darmshall was a small city in the hostile lands of Vaasa in the Bloodstone Lands . Structure . It was as much a fortress as it was a city surrounded by capable walls lined with siege weaponry and grizzled soldiers .
description_long: Darmshall Darmshall was a small city in the hostile lands of Vaasa in the Bloodstone Lands . Structure . It was as much a fortress as it was a city surrounded by capable walls lined with siege weaponry and grizzled soldiers . Beneath the city was a huge store of food and supplies to enable the city to withstand long periods of isolation . History . The city was founded by the Tenblades adventuring band during the early explorations of the region . The group ' s leader , Romas Thunderclap , built the fortress to act as a bastion of order in Vaasa after two of his companions were murdered . His efforts were successful , as even during the conquests of Zhengyi the Witch - King , Darmshall never fell , despite being besieged by many goblins .

title: Darni House
description: Darni House The Darni House was a located in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . A small mosque dedicated to Jisan decorated the center of the Darni House .
description_long: Darni House The Darni House was a located in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . A small mosque dedicated to Jisan decorated the center of the Darni House . An impressively stocked library could also be found here . Activities . Prices at the Darni House were steep , but a combination of good food , quick services , skilled craftsmen , and fine lodgings kept most patrons coming back on a regular basis . Inhabitants . Janik Darni was the proprietor of the Darni House . He employed two full platoons of the Diligent to maintain security . Due to its upper - class caterings , the Darni House attracted gem and silk merchants , as well as others who carried valuable cargo . Darni employed a rawun to entertain guests at night , and a barber to keep them well - groomed .

title: Daroush
description: Daroush Daroush was a small mining village located in the Aphrunn Mountains . Geography . Daroush lay at the eastern end of Lilit Pass in the Aphrunn Mountains .
description_long: Daroush Daroush was a small mining village located in the Aphrunn Mountains . Geography . Daroush lay at the eastern end of Lilit Pass in the Aphrunn Mountains . Trade . Daroush traded ores from its mines . Gold was one of the main metals mined in Daroush . Nearby towns like Aelor relied heavily on Daroush ' s gold trade . Once the mine dried up , the inhabitants of Aelor migrated to Amah . Defenses . Unsurprisingly , considering its size , Daroush had few defenses . History . Daroush was established in 50 DR as a dwarven mining colony . At some point , after the mines ran dry , the dwarves abandoned Daroush and returned to Alaoreum . In 145 DR , a small segment of Dempster Turmish ' s army accidentally marched into Lilit Pass and ended up in Daroush . The troops captured the village without raising a sword . By 1370 DR the mining village was almost completely empty . Some humans still mined for gold , but the best ore had been extracted by the dwarven founders of the mine . Rumors and Legends . As of 1370 DR , there were reports of dark dwarves ( likely duergar ) roaming the mine shafts . This lead to the miners seeking adventurers to protect them and investigate the sightings .

title: Darrawn
description: Darrawn Darrawn was the capital and only proper city of the nation of Fimbrul , on Returned Abeir . It was inhabited only by earth giant s and their galeb duhr servants . Background .
description_long: Darrawn Darrawn was the capital and only proper city of the nation of Fimbrul , on Returned Abeir . It was inhabited only by earth giant s and their galeb duhr servants . Background . The giant s of Darrawn spent their time hunting in the caverns and valleys of the Howling Mountains , while waging war against dragon s , the oni and their orc s servants , and rebel groups of galeb duhrs . Architecture . Darrawn ' s structures were coaxed from natural rock instead of just built in , and the homes of Fimbran giants were wonderful caves full of rock draperies , silica falls , glowing crystalline stalactites , and other wonders made of stone . Trivia . A typical abeir an giant drink , the gulluk , originated in Darrawn .

title: Darreth
description: Darreth Darreth was a prisoner at the Temple of Elemental Evil under Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . History . Darreth lived in Womford in the Dessarin Valley .
description_long: Darreth Darreth was a prisoner at the Temple of Elemental Evil under Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . History . Darreth lived in Womford in the Dessarin Valley . In 1491 DR , he was captured by elemental cultists who took him to the altar of the Temple of Elemental Evil in order to use him as a sacrifice . However , some adventurers infiltrated the temple and freed him .

title: Darrin Drader
description: Darrin Drader Darrin Drader is a novelist and game designer who co - authored several Forgotten Realms and core D & D sourcebooks . He was employed as a writer at 38 Studios , a computer gaming company owned by Curt Shilling and R . A .
description_long: Darrin Drader Darrin Drader is a novelist and game designer who co - authored several Forgotten Realms and core D & D sourcebooks . He was employed as a writer at 38 Studios , a computer gaming company owned by Curt Shilling and R . A . Salvatore until its financial collapse .

title: Darromar
description: Darromar Darromar , formerly known as Ithmong , was a metropolis and the capital of Tethyr . Geography . It lay on the River Ith .
description_long: Darromar Darromar , formerly known as Ithmong , was a metropolis and the capital of Tethyr . Geography . It lay on the River Ith . Its central location ensured that the queen ' s armies in 1479 DR were never more than five days ' hard ride from any trouble in her domain . Government . The city was formerly ruled by a council , but Queen Zaranda felt that it was necessary to have one person in charge at the top . This position was held by the Lord - Mayor Ternan Grannox in 1370 DR . It was a position that was appointed or elected once every three years .
