When cast , the target had to be within 240 yd ( 220 m ) of the caster , but for the duration of the spell , the distance between caster and target did not matter as long as they were both on the same plane of existence .
description_long: Death link Death link , also known as body sympathy , was an arcane necromantic spell that connected the caster with a target creature in such a way that damage or healing to one also affected the other . Effects . When cast , the target had to be within 240 yd ( 220 m ) of the caster , but for the duration of the spell , the distance between caster and target did not matter as long as they were both on the same plane of existence . If one of the participants traveled to a different plane , then the link was severed with no ill consequence . For the oldest version of this spell , it was only required that the caster visualize his or her victim . While linked , any damage suffered or healing bequeathed to one was also transferred to the other . The spell lasted a minimum of two hours and forty minutes ; longer for more experienced casters . The target had a chance to resist the magic of this spell or else both participants were locked into the spell — even the caster could not dispel it prematurely . If the caster was killed , then so was the linked creature , but not vice versa .

title: Death slaad
description: Death slaad Death slaadi were very powerful evil slaad shapechangers and spellcasters . Description . Death slaadi emerged as the result of a gray slaad having devoured the corpse of a dead death slaad .
description_long: Death slaad Death slaadi were very powerful evil slaad shapechangers and spellcasters . Description . Death slaadi emerged as the result of a gray slaad having devoured the corpse of a dead death slaad . As their previous form , they could wield greatsword s and imbue them with their own magic . The death slaadi were infused with energy from the Negative Energy plane , which made them sadistic and cruel creatures . They commanded armies of lesser red and blue slaadi to invade other planes and used the survivors as hosts to spawn new slaadi .

title: Death smoke
description: Death smoke Death smoke was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a cloud of dark noxious gas that could not be blown or burned away .
description_long: Death smoke Death smoke was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a cloud of dark noxious gas that could not be blown or burned away . Creatures that needed to breathe suffered physical damage while they remained within the cloud . " Death smoke " was heavier than air so flowed down stairs and crevasses with ease . Components . This spell required a crushed insect or arachnid and a pinch of sand to cast .

title: Death spear
description: Death spear A death spear or death lance was a longspear infused with negative energy and used by elite drow warriors . Description . These longspears were 10 feet ( 3 meters ) long and made of a dull - gray metal with mottled and sparkling patterns along its length .
description_long: Death spear A death spear or death lance was a longspear infused with negative energy and used by elite drow warriors . Description . These longspears were 10 feet ( 3 meters ) long and made of a dull - gray metal with mottled and sparkling patterns along its length . Additionally , they emanated an aura of negative energy . Powers . A " death spear " was a " + 1 longspear " . Suffused in an aura of negative energy , each blow struck by one of these weapons inflicted additional negative energy that chilled its victim . Additionally , the spear had limited charges to drain the life force of those it impaled , as dark tendrils of black light writhed down the lance . Two versions of these weapons existed ; their charges affected the victim to greater or lesser degrees . History . The " death lance " ( or " death spear " ) was invented by powerful drow wizard s and used in the protection of the city gates and temples in drow cities . In 1372 DR , at the Undying Temple , above the Deep Wastes city of Maerimydra , Irae T ' sarran used elite defenders equipped with " death spears " to protect her sanctum .

title: Death talisman
description: Death talisman Death talisman was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was usable by wizard s and priest s ( cleric s ) . Effects .
description_long: Death talisman Death talisman was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was usable by wizard s and priest s ( cleric s ) . Effects . " Death talisman " allowed the caster to enchant a small item and link it to their health . The enchanted item would remain in the exact same condition that it was when the spell was cast so long as the caster remained healthy . When the caster died , the item would corrode and fall apart . The caster needed to remain within 1 , 000 miles ( 1609 kilometers ) of the item for the enchantment to remain . Given the large range of the spell , this was especially useful for a wizard ' s companion ' s equipment . Archers with their bows enchanted with this spell never had to worry about water damage , breaking their bow , etc . This duration of this spell was based on the caster ' s power . Components . The only component needed to cast this spell was the item that was to be enchanted .

title: Death tyrant
description: Death tyrant Death tyrants were an undead form of beholder , similar to zombie s , that retained some innate magical abilities . They were often used by powerful wizard s as guardians . They were almost never encountered near other beholders , who found them abhorrent .
description_long: Death tyrant Death tyrants were an undead form of beholder , similar to zombie s , that retained some innate magical abilities . They were often used by powerful wizard s as guardians . They were almost never encountered near other beholders , who found them abhorrent . Description . A death tyrant was the result of a beholder ' s mad dreams of existing beyond death . On the rare occasion in which such dreams took hold of a live beholder , its flesh rotted away , and a naked skull with spectral points of red light for eyes would emerge . A death tyrant held much of the powers of the original beholder , now fueled by the power of Undeath . Although somewhat similar to a zombie , a death tyrant was a much more powerful creature , that continued to lord over others the same way beholders did . On the other hand , a true beholder zombie was the result of the necromantic reanimation of a dead beholder , and although a formidable foe , was a considerably weaker creature and a mindless servant .

title: Death ward ( spell )
description: Death ward ( spell ) Death ward was a necromancy spell that granted immunity to and effects or simply prevented death . Effects . The older version made the subject immune to all death spells and magical death effects .
description_long: Death ward ( spell ) Death ward was a necromancy spell that granted immunity to and effects or simply prevented death . Effects . The older version made the subject immune to all death spells and magical death effects . The spell did not protect against other harmful effects , such as injury , poison , or petrification , even if they might be lethal . The post Second Sundering version made the target able to avoid death , but only once . The spell lasted 8 hours . During this time , if ever the target was to suffer an effect that would kill it instantly , the effect would be negated . If the target was wounded so that it was close to death , it would instantly be stabilized . If either of these happened , death ward would end . Users . It was unique in that it was one of the only necromancy spells available to paladin s . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were needed and a divine focus for the older version .

title: Deathcalm
description: Deathcalm Deathcalm the Loved helped to run Galvendo ' s Lodge with her companion and business partner Galvendo , of whom the lodge was named . She assisted in such ways as raising clients who had met their end on hunting trips with Galvendo . < ref name = " N : GSF / Cities & Civilization - p27 " > < / ref >
description_long: Deathcalm Deathcalm the Loved helped to run Galvendo ' s Lodge with her companion and business partner Galvendo , of whom the lodge was named . She assisted in such ways as raising clients who had met their end on hunting trips with Galvendo . < ref name = " N : GSF / Cities & Civilization - p27 " > < / ref >

title: Deathwatch
description: Deathwatch Deathwatch was a necromancy spell that , within an area of thirty feet , informed the caster how badly wounded subjects were . Effects . Using the foul sight granted by the powers of unlife , the caster could determine the condition of creatures near death within the spell ' s range .
description_long: Deathwatch Deathwatch was a necromancy spell that , within an area of thirty feet , informed the caster how badly wounded subjects were . Effects . Using the foul sight granted by the powers of unlife , the caster could determine the condition of creatures near death within the spell ' s range . He or she instantly knew whether each creature within the area was dead , dying , gravely wounded , undead , or neither alive nor dead ( such as a construct ) . This spell foiled any spell or ability that allowed creatures to feign death . Components . This spell required only verbal and somatic components to cast .

title: Deathway
description: Deathway The deathways were a network of portal s linking crypts , catacombs , graveyards and other places related to the Eminence of Araunt . Description . The deathways were located in tombs , crypts , catacombs , graveyards and such other places , that were marked with the sign of the Eminence , three vertical slashes above .
description_long: Deathway The deathways were a network of portal s linking crypts , catacombs , graveyards and other places related to the Eminence of Araunt . Description . The deathways were located in tombs , crypts , catacombs , graveyards and such other places , that were marked with the sign of the Eminence , three vertical slashes above . Although those places were normal tombs or crypts for the unwary people , for those intelligent undead who knew the significance of the sign , or for the few living agents who worked for the Eminence , those places became portals that linked to everyone of the " principalities " of the Eminence across Abeir , and later Toril . History . The deathways were created by Lod , the founder of the Eminence , about five hundred years before 1479 DR , while he was in the world of Abeir . Lod recorded the way of creating the deathways in his " Codex of Araunt " . Initially the deathways linked only places within the world of Abeir and the continent of Laerakond , but in the decade of the 1470s DR , the deathways began to spread across Faerûn , as far as Thay . Since then , the deathways began to spread across the world at an astounding rate .

title: Debbi
description: Debbi The debbi was a mammal native to the warm deserts of Zakhara . Description . This 2 ft ( 0 .
description_long: Debbi The debbi was a mammal native to the warm deserts of Zakhara . Description . This 2 ft ( 0 . 6 m ) creature resembled a hybrid of a and a . Debbie were agile like monkeys , strong like hyenas , and their small hands allowed them to use simple items . Combat . The beast was highly effective with its fists , bite , and bolts of golden lightning , but it could intimidate its foes into fleeing by stamping its thunderous feet , and using magic to make its fur crackle and spark . If the magic did not work , and the debbi saw that its opponent was stronger , then it escaped and tried to hide . Debbi also had an immunity to all kinds of magical fear . Debbi often climbed trees and threw missiles at their enemies . They could swing a crude club when at close range . Although debbi were rather weak when found alone , their ability to intimidate made them formidable opponents . These horrible and selfish creatures did not show mercy . Habitat / Society . All other desert creatures despised debbi for their cowardice and selfishness . Debbi lived in packs , and the pack members even despised each other , but still they often united their efforts to confront a common enemy .

title: Decastave
description: Decastave Decastave was an evocation spell that converted a small piece of wood into a 10 - ft - long ( just over 3 m ) force - staff that could be used as a magic weapon . Effects . The magical pole was of fixed length , 2 in ( 5 cm ) in diameter , and rigidly inflexible .
description_long: Decastave Decastave was an evocation spell that converted a small piece of wood into a 10 - ft - long ( just over 3 m ) force - staff that could be used as a magic weapon . Effects . The magical pole was of fixed length , 2 in ( 5 cm ) in diameter , and rigidly inflexible . It could be wielded like a staff and could damage creatures immune to non - magical weapons . The " decastave " could be dissipated in a few ways : Once per casting of this spell , the wizard could elect to drain a small amount of health upon a successful hit . The health was transferred to the wizard similar to a " vampiric touch " but could not increase health beyond normal capacity . Components . This spell required verbal and somatic components , and a small piece of wood that was consumed by the casting . History . This spell was generally known around Faerûn , once it had been published in " Volo ' s Guide to All Things Magical " .

title: Deceive prying
description: Deceive prying Deceive prying was a spell used by priests of Vhaeraun to pass mental examination . Effects . Upon casting , the caster determined some criteria , such as religious and moral standards ; these standards didn ' t need to match up with the caster ' s actual mental state .
description_long: Deceive prying Deceive prying was a spell used by priests of Vhaeraun to pass mental examination . Effects . Upon casting , the caster determined some criteria , such as religious and moral standards ; these standards didn ' t need to match up with the caster ' s actual mental state . The caster or creature touched by the caster gave away this false information when mentally examined by magical or psionic means . The spell provided surface thoughts depending on the set criteria to be read by the examiner . The spell also provided minor protection against spells that were directed at mentally controlling the recipient , while not hindering the mental activity of the same , including mental magical activity . . Components . This spell required only material , verbal and somatic components to cast .

title: Deceiver genie
description: Deceiver genie Deceiver genies were tasked djinn whose lives revolved around deception and illusion . Oddly enough , deceiver genies were more susceptible to believing illusions than most creatures . Description .
description_long: Deceiver genie Deceiver genies were tasked djinn whose lives revolved around deception and illusion . Oddly enough , deceiver genies were more susceptible to believing illusions than most creatures . Description . The true form of a deceiver genie was difficult to ascertain because of the constant web of illusions surrounding them . Powerful sha ' ir s were needed to penetrate their true appearance . In their natural form , deceiver genies were tall and gaunt . They had one blue eye and one brown . Their skin was a mottled grey color . Combat . These genies were cowards who were constantly surrounded by an illusionary effect similar to that of a displacer beast . All deceiver genies could use the following spell - like abilities at will : " change self " , " delude " , " false vision " , " tongues " , " misdirection " , " undetectable lie " , " whispering wind " . They could use the following abilities twice per day : " distance distortion " , " massmorph " , " spectral force " , " shadow magic " .

title: Deekin Scalesinger
description: Deekin Scalesinger Deekin Scalesinger was a male kobold bard adventurer in the North in the 1370s DR . Description . He was a gray - scaled kobold who was often seen with pen and paper in hand as well as his lute .
description_long: Deekin Scalesinger Deekin Scalesinger was a male kobold bard adventurer in the North in the 1370s DR . Description . He was a gray - scaled kobold who was often seen with pen and paper in hand as well as his lute . Personality . Unlike many other kobolds in his tribe , Deekin showed very peaceful tendencies and dreamed of pursuits other than stealing and mining . He wished to be known throughout Faerûn for his heroic stories . Deekin was constantly talking in third person . He showed deep loyalty to those he worked for but also saw everyone as a character in his book . Whilst being part - dragon himself , his past experiences with his white dragon master , Tymofarrar , resulted in a deep fear of dragons . Abilities . Deekin was a proficient bard and was particularly skilled in his lute . His artistic abilities were also shown in his writing . History . Deekin was a member of the Dripping Fang clan and worked under the command of Tymofarrar . His master was often entertained by Deekin ' s storytelling and songs . Tymofarrar also taught Deekin the skills to become chief of the clan as well to become a sorcerer .

title: Deep Duerra
description: Deep Duerra Deep Duerra ( " dwair " - uh ) , also known as Queen of the Invisible Art or the Axe Princess of Conquest , was the duergar demigod of psionics , conquest and expansion . Worshipers . Deep Duerra and her cleric s were known below the surface as " Norothor " ( " those who seized enemy lands " ) .
description_long: Deep Duerra Deep Duerra ( " dwair " - uh ) , also known as Queen of the Invisible Art or the Axe Princess of Conquest , was the duergar demigod of psionics , conquest and expansion . Worshipers . Deep Duerra and her cleric s were known below the surface as " Norothor " ( " those who seized enemy lands " ) . While very few surfacers knew of the goddess and her faith , the Norothor were the talk of underground waystations and trading communities because of their recent efforts in the Underdark . Even the older duergar who served Laduguer considered the Norothor to be a nuisance , because of the strong degree in which they preached expansionism . Regardless , the Norothor served an important role in duergar society , since they trained the natural psionic abilities of young gray dwarves , they attended to and controlled the underclass of slaves , and they scouted and cleared out nearby tunnels so the community could continue to grow . Because of their focus on the mental disciplines they were often used as ambassadors to psionic races such as the illithid s and aboleth s . The brashness inherent of the faith however , ensured that many of these missions ended disastrously .

title: Deep Imaskar
description: Deep Imaskar Deep Imaskar , also known as The City of the Great Seal , was created during the fall of the Imaskar Empire in −2481 by the wizard lord Ilphemon as a safe haven for his followers and family . The fled carrying an artifact of immense power , the Third Imaskarcana . The city was located in the lower Underdark , somewhere below the Endless Waste .
description_long: Deep Imaskar Deep Imaskar , also known as The City of the Great Seal , was created during the fall of the Imaskar Empire in −2481 by the wizard lord Ilphemon as a safe haven for his followers and family . The fled carrying an artifact of immense power , the Third Imaskarcana . The city was located in the lower Underdark , somewhere below the Endless Waste . As of the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR , it housed the largest group of surviving descendants of the Imaskar empire , but this changed with the founding and growth of High Imaskar sometime after the Spellplague .

title: Deep Imaskari
description: Deep Imaskari Deep Imaskari are heirs to the lost empire of Imaskar . Few have survived when their slaves , having been abducted from other worlds and magical monsters ( phaerimm ) created by the war wizards of the Imaskari , were turned against them . Their empire crumbled leaving only ancient cities becoming ruins .
description_long: Deep Imaskari Deep Imaskari are heirs to the lost empire of Imaskar . Few have survived when their slaves , having been abducted from other worlds and magical monsters ( phaerimm ) created by the war wizards of the Imaskari , were turned against them . Their empire crumbled leaving only ancient cities becoming ruins . Those few that survived fled deep down beneath the surface of Faerûn , purposely shutting themselves off from the events of the surfaceworld . Living thousands of years in voluntarily chosen exile and under influence of strong magics practiced by their own wizards , the Imaskari turned into a human subrace adapted to life underground . Whilst barriers once held the Imaskari hidden from the outside world , and vice versa the outside world from the Imaskari , these barriers have now been breached . Imaskari are now starting to wander into a wider realm , exploring the surroundings of their underground home . Personality . Deep Imaskari are guarded and detached , keeping an unconscious watchful eye in all their interactions . Even before their fleeing into the deep bowels of the earth , they were fascinated by magics .

title: Deep King
description: Deep King Deep King was a title used by a dwarven ruler , equivalent to a king . History . The dwarven kingdom of Roldilar , founded in 610 DR , was ruled by Deep King Tuir Stonebeard .
description_long: Deep King Deep King was a title used by a dwarven ruler , equivalent to a king . History . The dwarven kingdom of Roldilar , founded in 610 DR , was ruled by Deep King Tuir Stonebeard . It dominated the lands of the Vast , below and aboveground . As Roldilar fell in 649 DR , Tuir was the last deep king whose dominion spread over the surface , and the last to be well known there .

title: Deep Kingdom
description: Deep Kingdom The Deep Kingdom , also known as the Deep Realm , was the name of a kingdom of gold dwarves that was found in the caverns of the Great Rift and the surface lands surrounding it . Geography . When first established , the Deep Kingdom occupied lesser caverns and tunnels under the Eastern Shaar .
description_long: Deep Kingdom The Deep Kingdom , also known as the Deep Realm , was the name of a kingdom of gold dwarves that was found in the caverns of the Great Rift and the surface lands surrounding it . Geography . When first established , the Deep Kingdom occupied lesser caverns and tunnels under the Eastern Shaar . History . The Deep Kingdom was established after the fall of Telantiwar and stood unconquered for generations . The Thunder Blessing filled the caverns of the Deep Kingdom beyond their capacity , so a large number of gold dwarves set out to expand in new lands .

title: Deep Sashelas
description: Deep Sashelas Deep Sashelas was an elven deity who made his home on Arvandor , although he was rumored to maintain a demesne off the coast of the Moonshae Isles known as " Tír faoi Thoinn " . He was heavily involved with the lives of the sea peoples and spent most of his time with deities from that realm . He gave one group of Corellon ' s creations the ability to breathe and live underwater , wishing to see the wisdom and goodness of the elves prevail in the deeper and wilder realms of the sea .
description_long: Deep Sashelas Deep Sashelas was an elven deity who made his home on Arvandor , although he was rumored to maintain a demesne off the coast of the Moonshae Isles known as " Tír faoi Thoinn " . He was heavily involved with the lives of the sea peoples and spent most of his time with deities from that realm . He gave one group of Corellon ' s creations the ability to breathe and live underwater , wishing to see the wisdom and goodness of the elves prevail in the deeper and wilder realms of the sea . He was heavily involved in the constant reshaping of the ocean depths , creating reefs and islands , tinkering with undersea volcanoes and the like . Deep Sashelas was a political deity ; he made considerable efforts to maintain the unity of the Asathalfinare and was on good terms with non - evil human sea and water deities . He had a special enmity for Sekolah , the sahuagin god and for Panzuriel whom he helped banish and weaken . Worshipers . Deep Sashelas ' priests had many responsibilities . They acted as mediators and befrienders of non evil aquatic races and protectors of dolphins . All priests had to take a dolphin companion to progress through the ranks of priesthood .

title: Deep Speech
description: Deep Speech Deep Speech was the language of aberration s , an alien form of communication originating in the Far Realm . When written by mortals it used the Espruar script , as it was first transcribed by the drow due to frequent contact between the two groups stemming from living in relatively close proximity within the Underdark .
description_long: Deep Speech Deep Speech was the language of aberration s , an alien form of communication originating in the Far Realm . When written by mortals it used the Espruar script , as it was first transcribed by the drow due to frequent contact between the two groups stemming from living in relatively close proximity within the Underdark .

title: Deep Wastes
description: Deep Wastes The Deep Wastes formed a small domain part of the vast Underdark hidden away underneath the surface of the Dalelands and the Moonsea . Geography . Stretching from the Earthspur Mountains with few entrances from the surface , a large portion of the Deep Wastes remained unexplored by travelers of the more adventurous type .
description_long: Deep Wastes The Deep Wastes formed a small domain part of the vast Underdark hidden away underneath the surface of the Dalelands and the Moonsea . Geography . Stretching from the Earthspur Mountains with few entrances from the surface , a large portion of the Deep Wastes remained unexplored by travelers of the more adventurous type . Inhabitants . The region was sparsely populated due to the collapse of the drow city of Maerimydra which once held Shadowdale as a conquered surface land . Around 1372 DR , the abandoned drow city was in ruins .

title: Deep Wilds
description: Deep Wilds The Deep Wilds was a plane in the Astral Sea that was home to nature deities including Silvanus , Mielikki , Auril , Malar and Umberlee . Silvanus ruled the plane and the other deities who dwelled in the Deep Wilds served him . Every type of environment found on Toril was also found in the Deep Wilds although the version found in the Deep Wilds was much more extreme than that on Toril .
description_long: Deep Wilds The Deep Wilds was a plane in the Astral Sea that was home to nature deities including Silvanus , Mielikki , Auril , Malar and Umberlee . Silvanus ruled the plane and the other deities who dwelled in the Deep Wilds served him . Every type of environment found on Toril was also found in the Deep Wilds although the version found in the Deep Wilds was much more extreme than that on Toril . Silvanus himself dwelt in Summeroak , in the heart of a vast woodland of mighty trees . Umberlee lived under the Blood Sea which is wracked constantly by gale force winds and Malar lived in the Land of the Hunt . Auril dwelt in the Land Under Eternal Ice which was reputed to be the coldest place in any plane of existence .

title: Deep diviner
description: Deep diviner The Deep Diviner is a prestige class of the Underdark that uses the mystical energies of the deep places of the world to accomplish feats of magic . They are particularly impressive because of their use of Node Magic , which involves manipulating deposits of magic within the Underdark , called Earth Node s . Deep Diviners use Earth Nodes to enhance and refuel their own magic , which focuses primarily on communicating with the stone that surrounds them and the Elemental Plane of Earth .
description_long: Deep diviner The Deep Diviner is a prestige class of the Underdark that uses the mystical energies of the deep places of the world to accomplish feats of magic . They are particularly impressive because of their use of Node Magic , which involves manipulating deposits of magic within the Underdark , called Earth Node s . Deep Diviners use Earth Nodes to enhance and refuel their own magic , which focuses primarily on communicating with the stone that surrounds them and the Elemental Plane of Earth . They become quite formidable , eventually becoming capable of calling upon Earth Elementals and becoming one themselves .

title: Deep dragon
description: Deep dragon Deep dragons , also called purple dragons , were a type of chromatic dragon that lived in the Underdark . Description . Despite their large size , deep dragons were slender and agile , allowing them to crawl through the tunnels of the Underdark .
description_long: Deep dragon Deep dragons , also called purple dragons , were a type of chromatic dragon that lived in the Underdark . Description . Despite their large size , deep dragons were slender and agile , allowing them to crawl through the tunnels of the Underdark . In the light , the dragons ' scales were the color of amethyst , but in the dark , they appeared nearly black . Ecology . Purple dragons inhabited the Underdark and were rarely known on the surface . Combat . A deep dragon ' s breath weapon was psychic and caused the target to be dazed or dominated , depending on the strength of the wyrm . Deep dragons were harmed by direct sunlight .

title: Deep gnome
description: Deep gnome Deep gnomes , called svirfneblin in their own language , are a gnome subrace that live in the Underdark . While their surface cousins are known for their boundless optimism and cheerful mischief , the " svirfneblin " are serious and suspicious creatures . They survive in the Underdark by maintaining wariness of others and working hard to keep their underground society secret .
description_long: Deep gnome Deep gnomes , called svirfneblin in their own language , are a gnome subrace that live in the Underdark . While their surface cousins are known for their boundless optimism and cheerful mischief , the " svirfneblin " are serious and suspicious creatures . They survive in the Underdark by maintaining wariness of others and working hard to keep their underground society secret . History . Although gnomes in general lack any kind of cohesive history , deep gnomes bring this cultural idiosyncrasy to its greatest extremes . Deep gnomes lack not only a tradition of keeping records or writing biographies , but they also have never developed a calendar or a method by which to track the passing of time as the drow have . To a deep gnome the very concept of day or night is foreign , having never seen the light of the sun or the stars of a night sky . In fact , so deep - rooted is this cultural lack of time - keeping , either of the past , present , or future , that among outsiders the history of the deep gnomes amounts to little more than the story of Blingdenstone , the only deep gnome settlement known of prevalently among non - svirneblin .

title: Deep rothé
description: Deep rothé Deep rothé were a variety of rothé that lived in the Underdark . Description . Deep rothé were smaller than surface rothé , standing only 4 feet tall at the shoulder .
description_long: Deep rothé Deep rothé were a variety of rothé that lived in the Underdark . Description . Deep rothé were smaller than surface rothé , standing only 4 feet tall at the shoulder . They had shaggy brown coats that darkened to black near the legs and belly . Their hooves and horns were dark green or black and their eyes were yellow or pinkish . Behavior . Like other rothé , deep rothé were usually found in herds of 11 - 20 individuals . They had the ability to magically create " dancing lights " to communicate with other members of their herd . They were known to be very stubborn . Ecology . Deep rothé ' s favorite food was cave moss , which was only found in " faerzress " - rich regions . Otherwise , they ate nearly anything that grew in the Underdark , especially fungi , moss , and lichen . Due to their habitat and diet , they were immune to any harmful effects of mold and fungus . They were also resistant to enchantments . The meat of deep rothé was considered more tender and less gamey than surface beef . Combat . Deep rothé could fight with both their teeth and horns . They were skittish and prone to stampeding , which could be quite dangerous for anyone in their path .

title: Deep scion
description: Deep scion Deep scions were people who surrendered their bodies and souls to an evil aquatic power ( usually a kraken ) in exchange for their lives . Upon surrendering , they were transformed by a ritual into amphibious shapechanger s , in service to their masters . Description .
description_long: Deep scion Deep scions were people who surrendered their bodies and souls to an evil aquatic power ( usually a kraken ) in exchange for their lives . Upon surrendering , they were transformed by a ritual into amphibious shapechanger s , in service to their masters . Description . Deep scions believed that their true form was the one they assumed when they returned to the sea . However , when killed , a deep scion ' s corpse would revert to the form it was before its transformation . Society . A newly transformed deep scion would usually return to its former home while appearing to be the person it used to be , but might also take a new identity . However the manner of its return to the surface , the deep scion ' s only purpose was to infiltrate into humanoid society in order to carry out its master ' s wishes .

title: Deep slumber
description: Deep slumber Deep slumber was an improved version of " sleep " that affected more creatures and / or tougher creatures . Effects . This spell could only be cast a close range ( unlike " sleep " which had a medium range ) but it could affect more creatures caught in the 10 ft ( 3 m ) radius burst and potentially tougher creatures as well .
description_long: Deep slumber Deep slumber was an improved version of " sleep " that affected more creatures and / or tougher creatures . Effects . This spell could only be cast a close range ( unlike " sleep " which had a medium range ) but it could affect more creatures caught in the 10 ft ( 3 m ) radius burst and potentially tougher creatures as well . Like " sleep " , the smallest and weakest creatures succumbed first and then the larger / tougher creatures if there was enough magical energy left in the spell . For creatures of equivalent size / toughness , the ones closest to the center of the effect were enchanted first . If any creature resisted this spell , they were unaffected . Those that did not resist fell asleep for a number of minutes equal to the experience level of the caster . This spell had no effect on undead , construct s , or creatures already unconscious . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a few rose petals , a live cricket , or a pinch of fine - grained sand .

title: Deepearth
description: Deepearth Deepearth was a city and the surroundings areas in the Underdark under the Galena Mountains in the Bloodstone Lands . History . Deepearth was settled by deep gnome s .
description_long: Deepearth Deepearth was a city and the surroundings areas in the Underdark under the Galena Mountains in the Bloodstone Lands . History . Deepearth was settled by deep gnome s . In the surrounding caverns lived some clans of duergar s . Sometimes the duergars engaged the gnomes in skirmish in order to gain food , cattle and sometimes slaves but with few successes . At last a great deep gnome army devastated the duergars territories stopping the raids . However one night a solitary duergar infiltrated Deepearth and discovered inside an abandoned gnome mine a pool of mercury ( in truth a gate to Abyss ) . He touched the liquid and was quickly possessed by the demon lord Orcus . With Orcus as their leader the duergar managed to seize Deepearth . In 1357 DR however the Gareth Dragonsbane ' s party arrived in Deepearth and fought the duergars and te minions of Orcus . In 1359 DR the gnomes had regained the control of the city and worked with the dwarves of Orothiar Clan in oder to exploit The Mines of Bloodstone .

title: Deeping
description: Deeping The Deeping was a stream in the Cormanthor forest . Wildlife . The waters of the Deeping ran clear and was home to a large number of and .
description_long: Deeping The Deeping was a stream in the Cormanthor forest . Wildlife . The waters of the Deeping ran clear and was home to a large number of and . In the western section of the Deeping , Deeping shrimp spawned and were fished by halfling s who used special trawling nets of tightly woven mesh combined with wooden boards that floated on the surface .

title: Deepspawn
description: Deepspawn Deepspawn were monstrous aberration s that could spawn many other varieties of monsters . Description . Deepspawn looked like large , rubbery spheres of mottled grey and brown .
description_long: Deepspawn Deepspawn were monstrous aberration s that could spawn many other varieties of monsters . Description . Deepspawn looked like large , rubbery spheres of mottled grey and brown . Six arms projected from their bodies ; three were tentacle - arms , and three were jaw - arms , ending in mouths of many teeth . A deepspawn also had over 40 long , retractable , flexible eye stalks , but it extended only three or four at a time , well away from harm . Ecology . For a deepspawn to give birth to other monsters , it first needed to devour one . It made an exact " record " of the creature , and replicated the creature using ingredients from the surroundings . If the deepspawn could claim resources from the dead and dying on a battlefield , it could produce a new spawn every three days . Typically , it gathered materials from the wild and could only produce offspring at a much slower rate . Only exact duplicates could be created by a deepspawn . They had an intense , inborn loyalty to the parent . They were sent away to live on their own unless there was sufficient food in the area to support them . There were typically one to four spawn kept around as general servants . History .

title: Deepwash
description: Deepwash The Deepwash was a freshwater lake and , as of 1370 – 1372 DR , the largest lake in the Vilhon Reach . The northwestern stretch was known as Shalane Lake in Erlkazar . Geography .
description_long: Deepwash The Deepwash was a freshwater lake and , as of 1370 – 1372 DR , the largest lake in the Vilhon Reach . The northwestern stretch was known as Shalane Lake in Erlkazar . Geography . The lake was almost as deep as Lake Esmel in Amn . It was filled by tributaries from the Cloven Mountains ( such as Arglander River ) and the Deepwing Mountains , and by Shalane River flowing from Impresk Lake . Its main outlet was the Wintercloak River . It was known to be filled with fish . Fishing was safest in the Shalane Lake region , because the dragon turtle did not enter those waters as often . The Shalane Lake stretch formed part of the eastern border of the barony of Shalanar in Erlkazar , and the whole of the lake served as the northern border of Ahlarkhem . Inhabitants . The lake was very deep and was home to a very large dragon turtle , with a shell 30 feet ( 10 meters ) in diameter , who resided near to Surkh . In Surkh , it was highly respected , and some even worshiped it , believing it to be an honor to be killed and eaten by it . The turtle was large enough to be able to capsize ships , with a very high level of intelligence .

title: Deepwing Mountains
description: Deepwing Mountains The Deepwing Mountains were a small , east – west mountain range southeast of the Shining Plains in the Vilhon Reach . They were located between the Orsraun Mountains and the Cloven Mountains and north of the Deepwash . The mountains were populated with a number of large , flying monsters , including manticore s , griffon s and hippogriff s , red dragon s , and wyvern s .
description_long: Deepwing Mountains The Deepwing Mountains were a small , east – west mountain range southeast of the Shining Plains in the Vilhon Reach . They were located between the Orsraun Mountains and the Cloven Mountains and north of the Deepwash . The mountains were populated with a number of large , flying monsters , including manticore s , griffon s and hippogriff s , red dragon s , and wyvern s .

title: Defender of Sealtiel
description: Defender of Sealtiel Defenders of Sealtiel are the earthly servants of the celestial paragon Sealtiel , the patron of defenders - those who protect the weak , fight off the forces of evil , and defend the ideals of truth and goodness from evil deception . The Defenders of Sealtiel are a knightly order sworn to uphold said ideals , and where the fists of Raziel take an offensive role in the eternal struggle against evil , the defenders remain at home and fight back against counterassault . Background .
description_long: Defender of Sealtiel Defenders of Sealtiel are the earthly servants of the celestial paragon Sealtiel , the patron of defenders - those who protect the weak , fight off the forces of evil , and defend the ideals of truth and goodness from evil deception . The Defenders of Sealtiel are a knightly order sworn to uphold said ideals , and where the fists of Raziel take an offensive role in the eternal struggle against evil , the defenders remain at home and fight back against counterassault . Background . The vast majority of the defenders of Sealtiel were are former paladin s , fighter s , and rangers . Also among them are the occasional cleric or monk ( often multiclass ) . Even rarer , but highly valued , are fighter / rogue s , who are more often found among the fists of Raziel . Arcane spellcasters find little appeal in the order and are almost nonexistent . The adventuring life has little appeal to most defenders of Sealtiel , who prefer to stay in civilization and protect . When they do venture into the wilds , it ' s typically as a bodyguard ; the defender will travel with the defended wherever they are needed .

title: Defenders Mamluk Society
description: Defenders Mamluk Society The Defenders Mamluk Society , also known as the Defenders , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Defenders were charged with the protection and defense of mighty Qudra .
description_long: Defenders Mamluk Society The Defenders Mamluk Society , also known as the Defenders , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Defenders were charged with the protection and defense of mighty Qudra . Organization . The Defenders were led by Akir Abd al - Himaya . Base of Operations . Since the defense of the city was the sole task , the Defenders were rarely encountered outside of her walls .

title: Defiance in Phlan
description: Defiance in Phlan Defiance in Phlan , designed by Shawn Merwin , is an adventure module set in the " Forgotten Realms " using the " Dungeons & Dragons " 5th edition ruleset . It focuses on Phlan , the Cult of the Dragon , and the Madame Freona ' s Tea Kettle . Summary .
description_long: Defiance in Phlan Defiance in Phlan , designed by Shawn Merwin , is an adventure module set in the " Forgotten Realms " using the " Dungeons & Dragons " 5th edition ruleset . It focuses on Phlan , the Cult of the Dragon , and the Madame Freona ' s Tea Kettle . Summary . The adventure starts off at Madame Freona ' s Tea Kettle , where adventurers are approached by a series of agents from the Harpers , the Order of the Gauntlet , the Emerald Enclave , the Lord ' s Alliance , and in turn the Zhentarim . Each subsequent mission leads the party to cross paths with the plots of the Cult of the Dragon and a number of draconic leads . These include a deal for a blue dragon tooth , the former lair of a black dragon , a polymorph ed green dragon , a stolen dragon egg , and a map to the lair of a white dragon . Index . Organizations .

title: Degasus Tarensun
description: Degasus Tarensun Degasus Tarensun was a minor assassin of the Night Masks in 1370 DR . History . Degasus was born in the Caravan Cities but grew up in Westgate after being abandoned at the city ' s docks at the age of six .
description_long: Degasus Tarensun Degasus Tarensun was a minor assassin of the Night Masks in 1370 DR . History . Degasus was born in the Caravan Cities but grew up in Westgate after being abandoned at the city ' s docks at the age of six . He was adopted by a Night Masks cell that used him as a runner and lookout while teaching him all they knew about living on the streets . Later , Degasus ' s natural charisma impressed the wizard Tersonm , who taught him to read , write , and to recognize spells . Degasus made a series of very difficult assassinations and became a rising star assassin among Westgate ' s nobles .

title: Degrodel
description: Degrodel Degrodel was an abjurer wizard living in Baldur ' s Gate . He had a collection of construct s , doomguard s , and helmed horror s . Degrodel employed Gorion ' s Ward to recover the helm of Balduran , recently resurfaced .
description_long: Degrodel Degrodel was an abjurer wizard living in Baldur ' s Gate . He had a collection of construct s , doomguard s , and helmed horror s . Degrodel employed Gorion ' s Ward to recover the helm of Balduran , recently resurfaced . After Gorion ' s Ward took the helm to him , he summoned all his constructs to throw them out of his home without paying .

title: Dehydration
description: Dehydration Dehydration was a powerful wizard spell that combined the schools of alteration and necromancy to devastating effect . It was used commonly by the members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects .
description_long: Dehydration Dehydration was a powerful wizard spell that combined the schools of alteration and necromancy to devastating effect . It was used commonly by the members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . If the caster of this spell was able to successfully touch the target , and if the target was not able to resist the spell ' s effects , the magic instantly dehydrated the target , causing a substantial permanent loss of their bodily fortitude and health . The spell was capable of killing weaker individuals . Victims suffering from this magical - induced " dehydration " were able to counteract the effects by consuming water so long as they remained inactive and did not lose additional fluids to perspiration . An inactive victim who consumed one quarter gallon ( 1 liter ) of water within one day would naturally replenish the health they lost from the spell . Active or encumbered victims needed to consume a half gallon or more to achieve the same results . Re - hydrating their body did not restore health lost from the physical damage the spell caused . Instead , it merely returned their core fortitude to its original state . Components .

title: Deinyn Fembrys
description: Deinyn Fembrys Deinyn Fembrys was a male Chondathan human cleric of Shar . He was one of a group of clerics Shar posing as clerics of Mystra at a false Temple of Mystra in Wheloon in Cormyr in 1374 DR . History .
description_long: Deinyn Fembrys Deinyn Fembrys was a male Chondathan human cleric of Shar . He was one of a group of clerics Shar posing as clerics of Mystra at a false Temple of Mystra in Wheloon in Cormyr in 1374 DR . History . Serving Lady of Mystery Naedaenya Arthas , Deinyn posed as " Starweaver " Fembrys at the false Temple of Mystra in the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR . His role was to take petitioners through the so - called " Mystra ' s Sacred Trust " , a three - day - long rite designed to sap their willpower , before he exposed them to the " dominating " influence of the " Starry Gnosis " . Victims were abducted and sent to their counterparts in the Vast Swamp . Those who were unsuitable or resisted Fembrys tortured to death and mutilated ; he murdered at least people this way , including Amnic Basult , Duncan , and Kenniwick . In early Eleint , Tunaster Dranik , a genuine cleric of Mystra , stopped by the temple , though the false priests gave him a frosty reception . In the end , Starweaver Fembrys met with him , but Dranik was so off - put by him that he turned and fled from the temple . Priests and guards have chase but Tunaster escaped .

title: Deirdre Kendrick
description: Deirdre Kendrick Deidre Kendrick was the firstborn daughter of Robyn Kendrick and Tristan Kendrick . Relationships . As a gifted magic - user , she was trained first by wizard Keane and later by Sinioth an aspect of Talos .
description_long: Deirdre Kendrick Deidre Kendrick was the firstborn daughter of Robyn Kendrick and Tristan Kendrick . Relationships . As a gifted magic - user , she was trained first by wizard Keane and later by Sinioth an aspect of Talos . History . Deirdre Kendrick was the first daughter of King Tristan and Queen Robyn Kendrick . Deirdre was joined one year later by her sister Alicia . As they grew up , Deirdre was often openly hostile to her sister , apparently already suffering from doubt and inadequacy that she channeled into rage . She was taught by Kaene , but he stopped when he understood the void in her heart . In 1365 DR , Sinioth seduced her . At first , Talos used Deidre in a positive mode , sending her to stop the Ityak - Ortheel and to save her father from sahuagin . However , afterward , Deidre became a complete pawn of Talos and the storm god used her to start a war to conquer the isles . In the end , Deidre was killed by her sister Alicia Kendrick .

title: Deirk Erlich
description: Deirk Erlich Deirk Erlich was a man living in Hillsfar . History . Deirk lived with his family in the slums of Hillsfar until , during the Rage of Demons , his brother Haakon Erlich , a officer of the Red Plumes , told him that the Tinfellow Farm was now vacant and he could take him there .
description_long: Deirk Erlich Deirk Erlich was a man living in Hillsfar . History . Deirk lived with his family in the slums of Hillsfar until , during the Rage of Demons , his brother Haakon Erlich , a officer of the Red Plumes , told him that the Tinfellow Farm was now vacant and he could take him there . Deirk , with his sons and a carpenter , started repairing the farm , when an adventuring party arrived asking about the Tinfellow family . Deirk lied to them , saying that he had lived here for years and had recently been attacked by elves .

title: Deity
description: Deity A deity is a being of great power that controls some aspect of mortal affairs , referred to as the god ' s portfolio . True gods are called Estelar and differ from the Dawn Titans ( primordial s ) . All deities were either elevated to their positions by Ao ( the overseer ) or were approved by Ao to be worshiped in the Realms , in the case of interloper deities .
description_long: Deity A deity is a being of great power that controls some aspect of mortal affairs , referred to as the god ' s portfolio . True gods are called Estelar and differ from the Dawn Titans ( primordial s ) . All deities were either elevated to their positions by Ao ( the overseer ) or were approved by Ao to be worshiped in the Realms , in the case of interloper deities . No divine power may found a permanent faith and power base without his approval , though there are cases of short - term semi - divine beings who gather faith from worshipers without being deities . The most noted example of this is the various fiendish cults that have arisen . In at least two cases , the worship of these cults have provided enough power or filled a niche that was not otherwise filled , and the fiends in question have become deities in their own right . Both Gargauth and the minotaur deity Baphomet became deities building on the power foundation of a fiendish cult . Worshipers are necessary for the continued existence and powers of a deity . The numbers and fervor of a god ' s worshipers determine in large part the power of the deity .

title: Dejor Rasthavin
description: Dejor Rasthavin Dejor Rasthavin was a sage and historian of Selgaunt and a regional agent of the Moonstars in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . Personality . Dejor was a quiet and soft - spoken man , with a great interest in history and politic of the Sea of Fallen Stars History .
description_long: Dejor Rasthavin Dejor Rasthavin was a sage and historian of Selgaunt and a regional agent of the Moonstars in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . Personality . Dejor was a quiet and soft - spoken man , with a great interest in history and politic of the Sea of Fallen Stars History . Dejor was a wizard and a sage from a wealthy family of Selgaunt in Sembia . His field of research was the history and the politic of the humanity in the Inner Sea region . For his position Dejor was invited to all parties of the city and there he gathered information for the Moonstars .

title: Del Geery
description: Del Geery Del Geery was a human farmer in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the mid – 14th century DR . He was notably prosperous and enterprising , particularly in the hydra trade . History .
description_long: Del Geery Del Geery was a human farmer in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the mid – 14th century DR . He was notably prosperous and enterprising , particularly in the hydra trade . History . In the late 1340s DR , Geery increased the yields of his crops of carrots and clover , but his fertile fields attracted hordes of rabbit s . These were followed by a variety of predators , like badger s and wolves . Normal means of controlling such pests , like traps and poison , failed to curb their numbers — for every animal trapped or killed , it seemed two more arrived . At a loss , Geery consulted his neighbor , the explorer Hadley Erridge , who proposed that Geery get a hydra . A hydra , Erridge claimed , would devour or scare off the pests then depart when there were no more prey . The damage to the farm would be more than outweighed by the benefits of getting rid of the burgeoning pest population , Erridge thought . Despite his skepticism , Geery agreed to finance Erridge with 20 , 000 gold piece s for an expedition into the Vast Swamp to capture a live hydra . Erridge and his thirty - man expedition ventured into the feared swamp .

title: Dela Alder
description: Dela Alder Dela Alder was the proprietor of the Traveler ' s Cloak Inn within the city of Mulmaster . History . In 1374 DR , Alder ran the inn with her husband Vesvur Alder .
description_long: Dela Alder Dela Alder was the proprietor of the Traveler ' s Cloak Inn within the city of Mulmaster . History . In 1374 DR , Alder ran the inn with her husband Vesvur Alder . After being a widow for many years , she remarried after allowing Vesvur , a bard , to pay for his extended stay at the inn by entertaining the patrons .

title: Delaan Winterhound
description: Delaan Winterhound Delaan Winterhound was a ranger of the Emerald Enclave and their main delegate at the Council of Waterdeep . Personality . Delaan preferred the wild spaces of the North and felt uncomfortable in Waterdeep .
description_long: Delaan Winterhound Delaan Winterhound was a ranger of the Emerald Enclave and their main delegate at the Council of Waterdeep . Personality . Delaan preferred the wild spaces of the North and felt uncomfortable in Waterdeep . He believed that the Cult of the Dragon needed to be stopped , as they caused too much destruction that would unbalanced nature ' s equilibrium . However , his primary concern was the natural order . History . Delaan lived in the northern wilderness . Once a year , he visited his friend in Nesmé . When the menace of Severin Silrajin ' s Cult of the Dragon became global , Delaan was chosen as the leading delegate at the Council of Waterdeep . Eventually , he was able to call on the help of treants against the Cult if he was impressed by the adventurers recruited to stop the Cult Relationship . Delaan had a winter wolf companion called Loska . He was also good friend of the famed treant Turlang of the High Forest .

title: Delacrae Gentleblossom
description: Delacrae Gentleblossom Delacrae Gentleblossom was a sage and shopkeeper in Phlan in 1489 DR . History . Delacrae ran a shop in Phlan called All Questions Answered , where she used her sage knowledge to answer customers ' questions .
description_long: Delacrae Gentleblossom Delacrae Gentleblossom was a sage and shopkeeper in Phlan in 1489 DR . History . Delacrae ran a shop in Phlan called All Questions Answered , where she used her sage knowledge to answer customers ' questions . She was consulted about a suspect dracolich or ghost ship ' s attack but she had no answers in this case .

title: Delayed blast fireball
description: Delayed blast fireball Delayed blast fireball , or delayed blast fire ball was an evocation spell that was like " fireball " but could be given a timed detonation . Effect . Other than being similar to " fireball " , the damage of the spell was increased and the spell would detonate with a timed trigger .
description_long: Delayed blast fireball Delayed blast fireball , or delayed blast fire ball was an evocation spell that was like " fireball " but could be given a timed detonation . Effect . Other than being similar to " fireball " , the damage of the spell was increased and the spell would detonate with a timed trigger . Later versions of the spell created a fiery " bead " that could be thrown and explode , sometimes in the thrower ' s hand . The post - Second Sundering version of the spell could be made even more powerful if cast by a user with more skill . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were needed for the casting . History . This spell was invented by the arcanist and Fire Warden of Netheril Noanar and called Noanar ' s delayed fireball in −2305 DR ( two years earlier than the simpler " fireball " ) .

title: Delban
description: Delban Delban was an Elder Evil from the Far Realm who had taken possession of one of the stars of Realmspace . Unlike normal stars , Delban didn ' t have a fixed place in the sky but instead danced and wavered across the Realmspace . Description .
description_long: Delban Delban was an Elder Evil from the Far Realm who had taken possession of one of the stars of Realmspace . Unlike normal stars , Delban didn ' t have a fixed place in the sky but instead danced and wavered across the Realmspace . Description . Delban was an ice white star . History . Delban , and the other Far Realm - infested stars of Realmspace , were somehow related to the Eldest . Delban was usually visible only in winters , but sometimes it shone without reason in any other seasons , surprising scholars who studied stars . Of all the Far Realm - infested stars , Delban was the most cruel and bitter . Delban was one of the stars the warlock Japheth Donard sought out in 1396 DR , after having lose his pact with the archfey Neifion .

title: Delbyl
description: Delbyl Delbyl was a town located in southern Murghôm . Description . Delbyl sat at the point where the Road of the Dawn split into its northern and southern branches .
description_long: Delbyl Delbyl was a town located in southern Murghôm . Description . Delbyl sat at the point where the Road of the Dawn split into its northern and southern branches . The town was made up of mud - brick houses , with a few gardens , orchards , and courtyards surrounded by walls . Wild animals such as goats , hens , geese , and sheep wandered the streets . Delbyl had a market , but it was mostly used by shepherds and farmers who brought their wares in from the surrounding countryside , selling to the merchants passing through the town on their way to Murghôm or Semphar . Inhabitants . Emir Yaghi - Siyan ruled Delbyl . No armed garrison was kept at the town , but a small group of twelve maliks and their men kept order in the city . They were considered strict , and used wooden rods for punishing people .

title: Deleira Truesilver
description: Deleira Truesilver Deleira Truesilver was a noble from Suzail and a lady of the Truesilver noble house . History . Around 1479 DR , the beholder - kin Talane was suddenly awoken by Manshoon in the private room of Lady Deleira .
description_long: Deleira Truesilver Deleira Truesilver was a noble from Suzail and a lady of the Truesilver noble house . History . Around 1479 DR , the beholder - kin Talane was suddenly awoken by Manshoon in the private room of Lady Deleira . Soon Talane ordered Deleira to find Elminster Aumar .

title: Delethyrsos
description: Delethyrsos Delethyrsos was a shadow dragon and the personal mount of Hadrhune in 1375 DR . History . Delethyrsos was at his master ' s side during Hadrhune ' s secret plot to obtain the " Quess ' Ar ' Teranthvar " , and was slain together with Hadrhune by an adventuring party recruited to stop him .
description_long: Delethyrsos Delethyrsos was a shadow dragon and the personal mount of Hadrhune in 1375 DR . History . Delethyrsos was at his master ' s side during Hadrhune ' s secret plot to obtain the " Quess ' Ar ' Teranthvar " , and was slain together with Hadrhune by an adventuring party recruited to stop him .

title: Delf
description: Delf Brother Delf was a priest of the god Deneir the Scribe , who lived at a monastery near Verdusk . Brother Delf once wrote a document recounting the origins of various magical creatures . In it , he gave one of the few known accounts of the creation of the peryton s , though he may simply have been retelling an ancient legend .
description_long: Delf Brother Delf was a priest of the god Deneir the Scribe , who lived at a monastery near Verdusk . Brother Delf once wrote a document recounting the origins of various magical creatures . In it , he gave one of the few known accounts of the creation of the peryton s , though he may simply have been retelling an ancient legend . He told how the Khala of Imaskar had been cursed by five gods of law for their wickedness and worship of Bane , and transformed into the peryton . This tale was unsupported by fact , but it did explain all their unusual human traits . The ranger Talyssa Strongbow visited the monastery and discovered Delf ' s writings , and repeated it in a book she wrote about the land of Thar .

title: Delfen Ondabarl
description: Delfen Ondabarl Delfen Ondabarl was the greatest wizard of Daggerford around 1370 DR . History . Delfen was an adventuring wizard from Iriaebor who retired to Daggerford around 1355 DR .
description_long: Delfen Ondabarl Delfen Ondabarl was the greatest wizard of Daggerford around 1370 DR . History . Delfen was an adventuring wizard from Iriaebor who retired to Daggerford around 1355 DR . After retirement , he spent his time tutoring the next generation of mages . He lived in an abandoned tower in exchange for a donation to the duchy ' s treasure . He became famous from Icewind Dale to Calimshan as a very patient teacher of the arcane arts . Delfen also helped the local militia in all magical matters . Delfen was presumed dead around 1385 DR . However , in 1485 DR , he returned to the town , not a day older , and reclaimed possession of his tower . He was Delfen for certain , but never spoke about what had happened to him in his century ' s absence .

title: Delg Ironstar
description: Delg Ironstar Delg Ironstar , also called Delg Hammerhand , was a dwarven fighter and part of the Company of the Bright Spear . He was also a member of the Harpers and was one of the last members of the legendary noble clan of dwarves , Clan Ironstar . Equipment .
description_long: Delg Ironstar Delg Ironstar , also called Delg Hammerhand , was a dwarven fighter and part of the Company of the Bright Spear . He was also a member of the Harpers and was one of the last members of the legendary noble clan of dwarves , Clan Ironstar . Equipment . He used a battle axe . He called upon Clangeddin Silverbeard ( by singing a heroic , dwarven chant ) , which granted him additional , but unknown powers and skills in combat . When he did so , his axe and the warhammer he wielded off - hand began to glow . Allies . He was one of the closest friends of Shandril Shessair . History . He was one of the few survivors of the Company of the Bright Spear after the company left the Rising Moon inn in Deepingdale in 1357 DR . He was killed by a gargoyle in the Stonelands . The creature lifted him up in the air , but was killed by Delg shortly after . Delg crashed to the ground , impaling himself on a rock , and died .

title: Delgar Munsch
description: Delgar Munsch Delgar Munsch was a hunter at Bridgefort in Boareskyr Bridge around 1368 DR . He owned a cabin in the area , where Delgar and his company of hunters took their prey , including goblin s and orc s , which they later sold at Baldur ' s Gate . Around 1367 DR , he retired after a very good season but when the crusade of the Shining Lady arrived nearby he joined the crusaders , even becoming an officer .
description_long: Delgar Munsch Delgar Munsch was a hunter at Bridgefort in Boareskyr Bridge around 1368 DR . He owned a cabin in the area , where Delgar and his company of hunters took their prey , including goblin s and orc s , which they later sold at Baldur ' s Gate . Around 1367 DR , he retired after a very good season but when the crusade of the Shining Lady arrived nearby he joined the crusaders , even becoming an officer . He was a man with an inflated sense of his own importance but he was a superb hunter .

title: Delhumide
description: Delhumide Delhumide is the name of the central tharch or region of Thay and its local capital . History . 2300 years ago , when Thay had been a Mulhorand i colony , Delhumide was one of its greatest cities and bastions of power .
description_long: Delhumide Delhumide is the name of the central tharch or region of Thay and its local capital . History . 2300 years ago , when Thay had been a Mulhorand i colony , Delhumide was one of its greatest cities and bastions of power . When the Red Wizards rebelled , they destroyed the town , using the darkest sort of sorcery to accomplish their task . In 1375 DR , the ground where the city ' s ruins still stood was still unclean . Demons walked there and a man could suffer from madness or leprosy just by venturing there . Shattered battlemets and toppled towers could be seen though many of the buildings remained essentially intact .

title: Delia
description: Delia The city of Delia was elevated in - 1401 DR ( 2458 NY ) by Lady Polaris . Geography . Originally Delia was an island crafted carefully by the druids and was altered once it became an enclave under the care of Lady Polaris .
description_long: Delia The city of Delia was elevated in - 1401 DR ( 2458 NY ) by Lady Polaris . Geography . Originally Delia was an island crafted carefully by the druids and was altered once it became an enclave under the care of Lady Polaris . Its treetop city architecture was soon expanded by more conventional means to support the wide array of magical research and city services that Lady Polaris demanded . Inhabitants . Lady Polaris later became tired of managing the city and turned it over to two of her students , Candlemas and Sysquemalyn during the Age of Discovery . History . Delia was the only known Netherese enclave known for druid ic and elven ways , though it soon became like the other enclaves . This caused the druids and elves who founded the city to leave for the more ground - based surroundings .

title: Delimbiyr
description: Delimbiyr The Delimbiyr , also know as the River Shining , was a river that ran through the Savage Frontier and the Western Heartlands . Geography . Starting deep in the Nether Mountains , flowing south through Delimbiyr Vale , it was joined near Loudwater by the combined flow of the River Loagrann and the River Greyflow .
description_long: Delimbiyr The Delimbiyr , also know as the River Shining , was a river that ran through the Savage Frontier and the Western Heartlands . Geography . Starting deep in the Nether Mountains , flowing south through Delimbiyr Vale , it was joined near Loudwater by the combined flow of the River Loagrann and the River Greyflow . It continued west between the southern edge of the High Forest and the northern edge of the High Moor to empty into the Sea of Swords near Daggerford . Headwaters . The headwaters of the Delimbiyr River consisted of three streams . These were , named west to east , the River Aulantrar ( or Deepingstream ) , the River Starsilver ( or Silver Stream ) , and the Norlnryn . Fauna . The Delimbiyr River was full of szorp fish .

title: Delimbiyr Vale
description: Delimbiyr Vale Delimbiyr Vale was an area in the North , encompassing the upper reaches of the Delimbiyr River . Geography . The Vale was bound on the north by the Nether Mountains and to the south by the South Wood .
description_long: Delimbiyr Vale Delimbiyr Vale was an area in the North , encompassing the upper reaches of the Delimbiyr River . Geography . The Vale was bound on the north by the Nether Mountains and to the south by the South Wood . The western edge was the High Forest but no part of the High Forest was considered a part of the Vale . The eastern edge was ill - defined but did include the Fallen Lands , once a part of Netheril . Two areas of the Delimbiyr Vale are often referred to as " Upvale " and " Gray Vale " by the locals . Upvale was an area of open grasslands in northern Delimbiyr Vale between Tall Trees and the Far Forest . Gray Vale was in the southwest and consisted of the area of grasslands through which the rivers Greyflow and Loagrann flowed . Travel through Gray Vale was often dangerous due to bugbear raids . Description . Nobody seemed to be interested in founding a settlement in this place since the valley was a desolate region , so it was forsaken along with its falling ruins , monsters , and its ancient secrets . For centuries , the demonic forces of Hellgate Keep controlled this area , but the fall of that ancient citadel put an end to its authority in the region .

title: Delimbiyran
description: Delimbiyran The city of Delimbiyran was one of the ' three crowns ' of Phalorm , representing the human s of that kingdom . Near the end of Phalorm ' s existence , Delimbiyran had grown beyond the need for allies and , indeed their elven peers from Ardeep had left the kingdom to travel to Evermeet and their severely depopulated dwarven allies had retreated from the area , effectively putting an end to the realm . The humans allowed any of the gnomes and halflings of Phalorm who wanted to stay in the alliance to do so as long as they swore fealty to king Javilarhh II , who founded the Kingdom of Man , officially called Delimbiyran after his capital city .
description_long: Delimbiyran The city of Delimbiyran was one of the ' three crowns ' of Phalorm , representing the human s of that kingdom . Near the end of Phalorm ' s existence , Delimbiyran had grown beyond the need for allies and , indeed their elven peers from Ardeep had left the kingdom to travel to Evermeet and their severely depopulated dwarven allies had retreated from the area , effectively putting an end to the realm . The humans allowed any of the gnomes and halflings of Phalorm who wanted to stay in the alliance to do so as long as they swore fealty to king Javilarhh II , who founded the Kingdom of Man , officially called Delimbiyran after his capital city . This new realm was to encompass all the land that belonged to Phalorm . Phalorm had been constantly beset by the orc s of the surrounding areas and so Delimbiyran spent the next fifty five years building defensive castles and sending out constant raids into the Sword Mountains and southern High Moor where the orcs lived . This period became known as the ' Endless Battle ' .

title: Delina
description: Delina Delina was a moon elf wild mage sorcerer who decided to travel to Baldur ' s Gate in order to find her twin brother , Deniak , whom she sensed was in trouble via their mystic bond . Personality . Inquisitive and fearless , she may have looked vulnerable but she carried a great strength within .
description_long: Delina Delina was a moon elf wild mage sorcerer who decided to travel to Baldur ' s Gate in order to find her twin brother , Deniak , whom she sensed was in trouble via their mystic bond . Personality . Inquisitive and fearless , she may have looked vulnerable but she carried a great strength within . History . As a child , Delina and her brother went to magical studies together , but she frequently skipped her lessons . One day , when playing and wrestling with her brother , he scolded her for her lack of ability and he refused to let her go . Enraged , her wild magic appeared for the first time . After this point , her skills seemed to surpass Deniak ' s , angering him greatly and making him jealous . His emotional state transferred to his sister , causing another wild magical surge . At some point , Deniak left for Baldur ' s Gate and later Delina felt her mystic bond with her brother become chilled , as if a strange darkness washed over him . At this point , she decided to travel to Baldur ' s Gate to save him . Upon entering the city , she was beset by gargoyle s and in order to defend herself she attempted to cast a spell .

title: Delisle
description: Delisle Delisle was a gnome in Daggerford around 1370 DR . Activities . Hailing from Ice Peak , Delisle always lamented about the heat and the humidity of Daggerford .
description_long: Delisle Delisle was a gnome in Daggerford around 1370 DR . Activities . Hailing from Ice Peak , Delisle always lamented about the heat and the humidity of Daggerford . Many counseled her to go back to Ice Peak but Delisle didn ' t want anything to do with the Luskan pirate ships that harbored in her hometown .

title: Delitar
description: Delitar Delitar the Slow was considered by many to be the greatest human historian in the Realms in 1358 DR . Activities . Delitar was one of the most respected historians of the Realms , and was quoted by many sages .
description_long: Delitar Delitar the Slow was considered by many to be the greatest human historian in the Realms in 1358 DR . Activities . Delitar was one of the most respected historians of the Realms , and was quoted by many sages . He had three subservient sages specializing in regional history and many scribes that worked under him . His nickname derived from his very slow speech .

title: Dell McCourt
description: Dell McCourt Dell McCourt was a dwarf soldier of the Dagult Neverember army in Neverwinter . History . Dell recruited an adventurer just arrived in the city to collect arrows from the dead in a skirmish with the undead of Valindra Shadowmantle and delivered them to the archers commanded by private Hawthidon .
description_long: Dell McCourt Dell McCourt was a dwarf soldier of the Dagult Neverember army in Neverwinter . History . Dell recruited an adventurer just arrived in the city to collect arrows from the dead in a skirmish with the undead of Valindra Shadowmantle and delivered them to the archers commanded by private Hawthidon .

title: Dellanil Quil ' quien
description: Dellanil Quil ' quien Dellanil Quil ' quien was once an elven king of Shilmista and one of the forests legendary heroes . It is also the title of an ancient tome containing writings of King Dellanil Quil ' quien . The Book .
description_long: Dellanil Quil ' quien Dellanil Quil ' quien was once an elven king of Shilmista and one of the forests legendary heroes . It is also the title of an ancient tome containing writings of King Dellanil Quil ' quien . The Book . Cadderly Bonaduce found the tome in a deserted cave in the Daoine Dune . It is bound in black leather and inscribed with the high elven runes for " D , Q , q " . The tome is locked by a snap . A dream , or more a vision finally helped Cadderly to understand and translate the ancient writings . Contents . The Dellanil Quil ' quien contains arcane writings , using old elven symbols . There is an account of how King Dellanil Quil ' quien awakened the trees of Shilmista and how the elves crushed an invading force of goblins with the help of the trees . Summons of the Trees . This is not a simple spell , but a calling to awaken the powers of the forest . Cadderly and Elbereth , the elven prince of Shilmista , recited the words of the summons at Sildritch Trea and awakened a couple ancient oaks to help conquer the orcish , goblinoid and titan forces of the ogrillon Ragnor and free Shilmista once again

title: Delly Curtie
description: Delly Curtie Delly Curtie , born Delenia Curtie , was the wife of Wulfgar and before that , a wench at Arumn ' s tavern in Luskan . She sold herself to men almost every night , including people such as Morik the Rogue . Description .
description_long: Delly Curtie Delly Curtie , born Delenia Curtie , was the wife of Wulfgar and before that , a wench at Arumn ' s tavern in Luskan . She sold herself to men almost every night , including people such as Morik the Rogue . Description . Delly Curtie is a girl with blonde - brown hair that does not look very clean . Her eyes are a rare shade of light brown and her grin is slightly crooked . Personality . Delly has a typically sarcastic attitude . She also tries to act as a lady whilst caring for baby Colson . She has not had an easy life from what ' s told of her story , she works for Arumn Gardpeck in his tavern The Cutlass in Luskan . She is somewhat promiscuous seeking the safety and security of the menfolk she spends her time with , seeking protection from harm and seeing relations with these men as a fair trade for her security . Finally though , she settles with Wulfgar and leaves Luskan . She has had relationships with a variety of men , including Morik , at one point , Wulfgars ' best friend . But she seems to sort herself out and actually inspires Wulfgar as much as she can on his travels .

title: Delmarin Island
description: Delmarin Island Delmarin Island was a small , remote , and desolate island located in the Sea of Swords west of Orlumbor , somewhat north of Mintarn , and east of the Korinn Archipelago . It was surrounded by perilous reefs . It was inhabited by fog giant s .
description_long: Delmarin Island Delmarin Island was a small , remote , and desolate island located in the Sea of Swords west of Orlumbor , somewhat north of Mintarn , and east of the Korinn Archipelago . It was surrounded by perilous reefs . It was inhabited by fog giant s .

title: Delmuth Echorn
description: Delmuth Echorn Delmuth Echorn was the young elven heir of House Echorn in Cormanthyr at the time that Elminster Aumar was nominated Armathor . History . Delmuth was the heir of the Echorn , one of the most noble of elven houses .
description_long: Delmuth Echorn Delmuth Echorn was the young elven heir of House Echorn in Cormanthyr at the time that Elminster Aumar was nominated Armathor . History . Delmuth was the heir of the Echorn , one of the most noble of elven houses . When he found that a human had been nominated as armathor in 241 DR , he decided to quickly slay him . However , Elminster proved a very formidable opponent and in the end it was Elminster that killed Delmuth .

title: Delphe
