description_long: Dessarin Valley The Dessarin Valley was situated between the Sword Mountains and the High Forest . It was home to a diverse range of folk , although most inhabitants were either human s or halfling s . The main industry of the Dessarin Valley was agriculture , and Goldenfields played a large part in the agricultural economy of the North . History . In - 4420 DR , the shield dwarf kingdom of Besilmer was founded . Besilmer was a very atypical dwarf kingdom , built above ground with fields and pastures to support it . For years , Besilmer flourished but then fell under attack by giants and trolls . This led to the construction of Tyar - Besil , an underground city . Besilmer fell a century after its construction . Ruins from the kingdom still stood in 1491 DR , most notably the Stone Bridge that spanned the Dessarin River ; and , although in poor condition , the ruins known as the Halls of the Hunting Axe . In 893 DR , the Knights of the Silver Horn discovered the ruins of Tyar - Besil . The knights set up strongholds in the ruins but came under attack by Uruth Ukrypt . This led to Dessarin Valley being dragged into the Orcfastings War , and the First and Second Trollwars .

title: Desther Indelayne
description: Desther Indelayne Desther Indelayne is an antagonist in the original campaign of " Neverwinter Nights . " After the plague breaks out in Neverwinter , Desther and followers of his arrive , claiming to be priests of Helm sent to help cure the plague with their blessings . Upon the successful creation of a cure for the plague , Desther takes this potion and retreats through a portal to Helm ' s Hold .
description_long: Desther Indelayne Desther Indelayne is an antagonist in the original campaign of " Neverwinter Nights . " After the plague breaks out in Neverwinter , Desther and followers of his arrive , claiming to be priests of Helm sent to help cure the plague with their blessings . Upon the successful creation of a cure for the plague , Desther takes this potion and retreats through a portal to Helm ' s Hold . It is learned that Desther was actually an agent of Maugrim sent to Neverwinter to help spread the plague through his followers ' " blessings " and that he and his false Helmites had killed the true Helmites and taken Helm ' s Hold as their base of operations . The hero follows Desther through his escape portal to Helm ' s Hold , confronting him there and defeating him in combat . Desther is then taken back to Neverwinter to face judgment and is executed for his crimes along with Fenthick , who is wrongly denounced as having been in conspiracy with him .

title: Destroyer
description: Destroyer The Destroyer , or He Who Learns to Destroy , was a yak - man who lived beneath Huzuz in the Lair of the Unspeakable in 1367 DR . Activities . The Destroyer learned to speak Midani from a slave in the World Pillar Mountains .
description_long: Destroyer The Destroyer , or He Who Learns to Destroy , was a yak - man who lived beneath Huzuz in the Lair of the Unspeakable in 1367 DR . Activities . The Destroyer learned to speak Midani from a slave in the World Pillar Mountains . Since he could read and write the language , he spent much of his time studying stolen texts written in Midani . Over the years he raided all of the great mosques , save the Golden Mosque , for books , amassing quit a collection . He also stole books from wizards and other libraries . Any useful information he learned was given to the Unspeakable so he could use it against the Grand Caliph . He ventured forth to the mosques with an earthservant when he needed new reading material . The Destroyer was able to create one of the finest libraries in all of Huzuz from his illicit ventures . Possessions . The Destroyer used a " staff of withering " .

title: Destroyers
description: Destroyers The Destroyers were a mercenary company based in Halabar in Halruaa . They specialized in providing artillery support , both mundane and magical , to regular armies . They were commanded by Daltim Flamefist , a noted mage , psionicist , scholar , and noble of Halruaa .
description_long: Destroyers The Destroyers were a mercenary company based in Halabar in Halruaa . They specialized in providing artillery support , both mundane and magical , to regular armies . They were commanded by Daltim Flamefist , a noted mage , psionicist , scholar , and noble of Halruaa . History . Daltim Flamefist was the noble - born son of an Elder of the wizard - ruled realm of Halruaa , and he had ambitions to become an Elder himself . However , he first had to gain experience , and to this end , he became the commander of the Destroyers , often leading them into battle . The Destroyers became involved in the civil war in Tethyr in the 1360s DR . While there , Daltim ' s " Tome of Fire " went missing , presumed stolen , as he was unlikely to forgotten or lost it . Organization . Membership . The Destroyers kept a standing army . It comprised some 50 members : 15 mages ( wizard s and sorcerer s ) , 15 psionicist s , and 20 fighter s . The mages and psionicists were all of low - to - middling rank and specialized in destructive magical schools and psionic disciplines . The psionicists were some of the best known mind mages in Halruaa .

title: Destruction
description: Destruction Destruction was a necromancy spell that could kill a creature and obliterate its body . Earlier versions of this spell were the " resurrection " spell cast in reverse , which turned a creature to dust . Effects .
description_long: Destruction Destruction was a necromancy spell that could kill a creature and obliterate its body . Earlier versions of this spell were the " resurrection " spell cast in reverse , which turned a creature to dust . Effects . The older versions of this spell required the caster to successfully touch the victim in order to turn them to dust . The newer version had a range of about 50 to 100 ft ( 15 to 30 m ) or more , depending on the level of the caster . Unless they were able to overcome the magic of this spell , the target of this spell was killed instantly and their body was consumed , leaving nothing behind but their clothes , equipment , and possessions . Even if they were fortitudinous enough to resist , they were subjected to a large amount of damage which could also prove fatal . Creatures obliterated by this spell could only be recovered by a " true resurrection " , a " miracle " , or a thoughtfully worded " wish " followed by a " resurrection " . When cast in reverse , " resurrection " could return a creature to life and full vigorous health as long as there was at least a piece of the deceased that was part of the body at the time of death . Components .

title: Destruction wave
description: Destruction wave Destruction wave was an evocation spell that had the caster strike the ground to throw divine energies at surrounding targets . Effects . When the caster uttered this spell and struck the ground for emphasis , a wave of energy emanated explosively from the caster and hit any number of chosen targets within 30 ft ( 9 .
description_long: Destruction wave Destruction wave was an evocation spell that had the caster strike the ground to throw divine energies at surrounding targets . Effects . When the caster uttered this spell and struck the ground for emphasis , a wave of energy emanated explosively from the caster and hit any number of chosen targets within 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) . The force took the form of a thunderclap and could knock creatures to the ground . In addition to this blast of godly might , the caster could choose the divine energy to be radiant or necrotic in nature , further damaging the targets . Sturdy creatures affected by the blast had a chance to resist the spell . If so , they took only half the damage and remained standing . Components . Only a vocal component was needed for the casting of this spell . Striking the ground was apparently an optional dramatic gesture . Errata . In the first publication of Player ' s Handbook 5th edition , " destructive wave " is referred to as " destructive smite " in the paladin spell listing .

title: Detect chaos
description: Detect chaos Detect chaos was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with a chaotic aura . Effects . This spell functioned exactly like " detect evil " except it detected chaotic auras from demon s , chaotic clerics , spells , magic items , etc .
description_long: Detect chaos Detect chaos was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with a chaotic aura . Effects . This spell functioned exactly like " detect evil " except it detected chaotic auras from demon s , chaotic clerics , spells , magic items , etc .

title: Detect evil
description: Detect evil Detect evil was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with an evil aura . Some versions of this spell were reversible , becoming " detect good " , and operated in the same manner but for good auras instead . Effects .
description_long: Detect evil Detect evil was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with an evil aura . Some versions of this spell were reversible , becoming " detect good " , and operated in the same manner but for good auras instead . Effects . There have been a few different versions of this spell over the years , but they all worked in about the same way : the caster concentrated in a particular direction and learned about any creatures or objects that radiated evil in the direction viewed . The newer , cleric - only version of this spell had a cone - shaped area of effect and a range of 60 ft ( 18 . 3 m ) . Auras could be detected even with some interposing structures or surfaces , within limits . Anything less than 3 ft ( 91 cm ) of dirt or wood , 1 ft ( 30 cm ) of stone , or 1 in ( 2 . 5 cm ) of common metal could be penetrated , but a thin sheet of lead was proof against this divination . Upon first casting this spell and concentrating for a few seconds , the presence or absence of evil could be known . After a few seconds more , the most powerful aura was easily detected and a count of all detectable auras was possible .

title: Detect evil and good
description: Detect evil and good Detect evil and good was a divination spell that detected outsider s of different types and other types of creatures within 30 feet ( 9 meters ) . Effect . The caster could sense desecrated or consecrated ground as well as aberration s , celestial s , elemental s , fey , fiend s , or undead .
description_long: Detect evil and good Detect evil and good was a divination spell that detected outsider s of different types and other types of creatures within 30 feet ( 9 meters ) . Effect . The caster could sense desecrated or consecrated ground as well as aberration s , celestial s , elemental s , fey , fiend s , or undead . The spell could not penetrate three feet of wood or dirt , one foot of stone , or one inch of steel or a thin sheet of lead . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were needed for the casting of this spell .

title: Detect good
description: Detect good Detect good was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with a good aura . Some versions of this spell were reversible , becoming " detect evil " , and operated in the same manner but for evil auras instead . Effects .
description_long: Detect good Detect good was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with a good aura . Some versions of this spell were reversible , becoming " detect evil " , and operated in the same manner but for evil auras instead . Effects . This spell functioned exactly like " detect evil " except it detected good auras from paladin s , good clerics , spells , magic items , etc . Just as poison did not show up as evil , beneficial potions did not register as good .

title: Detect law
description: Detect law Detect law was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with a lawful aura . Effects . This spell functioned exactly like " detect evil " except it detected lawful auras from paladin s , lawful clerics , spells , magic items , etc .
description_long: Detect law Detect law was a divination spell that provided information about objects or creatures with a lawful aura . Effects . This spell functioned exactly like " detect evil " except it detected lawful auras from paladin s , lawful clerics , spells , magic items , etc .

title: Detect lycanthrope
description: Detect lycanthrope Detect lycanthrope allowed the caster to sense the presence of all lycanthropes within its area , which could be a few miles in radius . Infected lycanthropes were more likely to evade the effects of this spell than natural lycanthropes . The caster was unable to tell which kind of lycanthropes were out there , or any information about them other than their location .
description_long: Detect lycanthrope Detect lycanthrope allowed the caster to sense the presence of all lycanthropes within its area , which could be a few miles in radius . Infected lycanthropes were more likely to evade the effects of this spell than natural lycanthropes . The caster was unable to tell which kind of lycanthropes were out there , or any information about them other than their location . Lycanthropes would be detected regardless of their current aspect . This spell was created by Avan Vatsisen and he was likely the only one to be able to use it .

title: Detect magic
description: Detect magic Detect magic was a divination spell that was sometimes categorized as a universal spell . It allowed the caster to become aware of magical emanations in the direction the caster was facing , within range of the spell . After the Spellplague , it became a trained skill for those with affinity for magic .
description_long: Detect magic Detect magic was a divination spell that was sometimes categorized as a universal spell . It allowed the caster to become aware of magical emanations in the direction the caster was facing , within range of the spell . After the Spellplague , it became a trained skill for those with affinity for magic . Effects . Over the years , this spell has evolved , growing in capability while becoming easier to learn . Early illusionists didn ' t learn this spell until they reached second level while divine and other arcane casters could learn it at first level . Eventually this spell became a cantrip for wizards and an orison for priests . After the Art recovered from the Spellplague , a spellcaster could be trained to identify rituals , magical effects , and even sense the presence of magic through most any barrier . At first , each practitioner of magic had their own version of " detect magic " . Magic - user s including illusionists could sense magic in a 10 ft ( 3 m ) wide corridor 60 ft ( 18 . 3 m ) long and for a duration based on their experience level . Cleric s and druid s could only " see " magical auras out to 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) and 40 ft ( 12 .

title: Detect metals and minerals
description: Detect metals and minerals Detect metals and minerals was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . However , by 1372 DR , it was known to cleric s and mages in Faerûn .
description_long: Detect metals and minerals Detect metals and minerals was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . However , by 1372 DR , it was known to cleric s and mages in Faerûn . Effects . The caster used this spell to determine the location of a single type of ore or mineral per casting , revealing the direction and distance of the material to the caster . Additionally , the relative amount of material present at the location was also revealed . It could locate anything from a heap of coins to a vein of ore , and penetrated stone and other barriers and obstacles . It was common for larger quantities of the material to hide smaller quantities in the same area , forcing the caster to focus their concentration as he or she approached the location . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a small magnet , a vial of weak acid , and a small portion of the material that the caster wished to detect . By 1372 DR , one only needed the sample material , but it had to be at least 10 pounds ( 4 . 5 kilograms ) .

title: Detect poison
description: Detect poison Detect poison was a divination spell that allowed the caster to sense if a creature or an object was poisonous or had been poisoned . Effect . Upon casting this spell , the caster could examine one creature , object , or a 5 ft ( 3 .
description_long: Detect poison Detect poison was a divination spell that allowed the caster to sense if a creature or an object was poisonous or had been poisoned . Effect . Upon casting this spell , the caster could examine one creature , object , or a 5 ft ( 3 . 5 m ) volume and know instantly if it had been poisoned or if it was poisonous to the caster . The earlier version of this spell was not instantaneous but lasted for at least 10 minutes and the caster could examine multiple targets at a rate of one per minute . Both versions had a chance to determine the exact type of poison . The probability of success for the newer version depended on the caster ' s wisdom while the earlier spell depended on the caster ' s level . Skilled alchemist s could also use their alchemical knowledge to detect poison . This spell could successfully detect poison through barriers , but could not penetrate 3 ft ( 91 cm ) of wood or dirt , 1 ft ( 30 cm ) of stone , 1 in ( 2 . 5 cm ) of regular metals , or a thin layer of lead . Components . Both versions of this spell required verbal and somatic components , but only the older version needed a strip of vellum , blessed specifically for this purpose .

title: Detect poison and disease
description: Detect poison and disease Detect poison and disease was a divination spell that detected diseases , poisons , or poisonous creatures . Effect . Upon casting this spell , the caster could sense disease , poisons , and poisonous creatures within a 30 ft ( 9 .
description_long: Detect poison and disease Detect poison and disease was a divination spell that detected diseases , poisons , or poisonous creatures . Effect . Upon casting this spell , the caster could sense disease , poisons , and poisonous creatures within a 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) radius and know their location and type ( " e . g . " , rabies , yellow mold , or snake ) . This ability lasted while the caster concentrated on the detection , or for 10 minutes , whichever was less . This spell could successfully detect poison or disease through barriers , but could not penetrate 3 ft ( 91 cm ) of wood or dirt , 1 ft ( 30 cm ) of stone , 1 in ( 2 . 5 cm ) of regular metals , or a thin layer of lead . " Detect poison and disease " could also be cast as a ritual . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a yew leaf to cast .

title: Detect psionics ( spell )
description: Detect psionics ( spell ) Detect psionics was an arcane divination spell that served as a magical counterpart to " psionic sense " , allowing a mage to detect psionic creatures and activity . Effects . The " detect psionics " spell functioned as a magical version of the psionic devotion " psionic sense " , enabling its user to sense all psionic activity within a distance from themselves .
description_long: Detect psionics ( spell ) Detect psionics was an arcane divination spell that served as a magical counterpart to " psionic sense " , allowing a mage to detect psionic creatures and activity . Effects . The " detect psionics " spell functioned as a magical version of the psionic devotion " psionic sense " , enabling its user to sense all psionic activity within a distance from themselves . The power of the caster determined this distance and the type of information acquired , whether there were psionic creatures present , how powerful was the psionic activity , and the direction and distance to the activity . Components . The spell required verbal , somatic , and material components . History . The Halruaa n mage Daltim Flamefist , a noted scholar on psionics , gave details of the " detect psionics " spell to his fellow mages at a symposium of wizards in Halruaa in the 1360s DR .

title: Detect scrying
description: Detect scrying Detect scrying was a divination spell that alerted one to magical eavesdropping . Effect . The caster immediately became aware of any attempt at observation by means of " clairaudience / clairvoyance " or " scrying " .
description_long: Detect scrying Detect scrying was a divination spell that alerted one to magical eavesdropping . Effect . The caster immediately became aware of any attempt at observation by means of " clairaudience / clairvoyance " or " scrying " . The spell ' s effect radiated from and moved with the caster . The spell also revealed the use of " crystal balls " or other magic scrying devices . The caster knew the location of every magical sensor within the spell ' s area , if the " scrying " attempt originated within the area . If the attempt originated outside this range , the caster might receive a visual image of the scrier and a sense of the scrier ' s direction and distance . Realmslore . When " detect scrying " uncovered a spell , a brilliant blue - white flash would burn in the area . Material components . A small piece of mirror and a miniature brass hearing trumpet .

title: Detect secret doors
description: Detect secret doors Detect secret doors is a divination spell that reveals hidden doors within 60 feet of the caster . Effect . When cast , this spell allows the caster to detect secret doors , compartments , caches , and so forth .
description_long: Detect secret doors Detect secret doors is a divination spell that reveals hidden doors within 60 feet of the caster . Effect . When cast , this spell allows the caster to detect secret doors , compartments , caches , and so forth . Only passages , doors , or openings that have been specifically constructed to escape detection are detected by this spell - an ordinary trapdoor underneath a pile of creates will not be detected . The amount of information revealed by this spell depends on how long the caster studies a particular area or object . Upon casting the spell , the caster becomes aware of the presence or absence of secret doors . Slowly , the spell reveals the number of secret doors and the location of each . If an aura is outside the caster ' s line of sight , then they can discern its direction but not its exact location . If the caster continues to take in the area , the spell begins to reveal mechanisms or triggers for one particular secret portal when closely examined by the caster . The spell can penetrate barriers , but a foot of stone , an inch of common metal , a thin sheet of lead , or three feet of wood or dirt blocks it .

title: Detect snares and pits
description: Detect snares and pits Detect snares and pits was a divination spell that made the caster aware of pits , deadfalls , and snares in a chosen direction . Effects . This spell could detect terrain hazards , creature hazards , and even magical hazards as long as they were not mechanically complex and resembled pits , deadfalls , or snares .
description_long: Detect snares and pits Detect snares and pits was a divination spell that made the caster aware of pits , deadfalls , and snares in a chosen direction . Effects . This spell could detect terrain hazards , creature hazards , and even magical hazards as long as they were not mechanically complex and resembled pits , deadfalls , or snares . Sinkholes , trapdoor spider s , ant lion s , hunting snares , quicksand , unstable rock walls , " trip " and " snare " spells , and spike / spear / crossbow traps and the like were all detectable by this spell . The caster experienced a premonition of danger when facing a hazard , which increased as he or she closed the distance . The older version of " detect snares and pits " divined in a corridor 10 ft ( 3 m ) by 40 ft ( 12 . 2 m ) . The newer version had a cone - shaped area of effect that extended 60 ft ( 18 . 3 m ) from the caster . The newer version also revealed more information the longer the caster concentrated in a particular direction . Not only the presence of hazards , but their number and location ( if within line of sight ) , and finally the type of one hazard and its triggering mechanism or conditions could be determined .

title: Detect thoughts
description: Detect thoughts Detect thoughts , also known as ESP , is a divination spell that allows one to " listen " to surface thoughts . Effect . The amount of information revealed depends on how long the caster studies a particular area or subject .
description_long: Detect thoughts Detect thoughts , also known as ESP , is a divination spell that allows one to " listen " to surface thoughts . Effect . The amount of information revealed depends on how long the caster studies a particular area or subject . The spell can penetrate barriers , but 30cm ( 1ft ) of stone , 2 . 5cm ( 1in ) of common metal , a thin sheet of lead , or 1m ( 3ft ) of wood or dirt blocks it . The post Second Sundering version of the spell also allowed the caster to detect the surface thoughts of a creature and " detect " where they are . This spell could be used for interrogation and also to probe deeper into the targets mind . The spell could not detect or read the mind of very unintelligent creatures or creatures that doesn ' t speak any language . The spell reached 30 feet , and lasted 1 minute but could not penetrate 3 ft ( 91 cm ) of wood or dirt , 2 ft ( 60 cm ) of stone , 2 in ( 5 cm ) of regular metals , or a thin layer of lead . Arcane focus . A copper piece .

title: Detect undead
description: Detect undead Detect undead was a divination or necromancy spell that revealed undead creatures within a certain distance from the caster . The earliest version of this spell could be cast in reverse as " cloak undead " . Effects .
description_long: Detect undead Detect undead was a divination or necromancy spell that revealed undead creatures within a certain distance from the caster . The earliest version of this spell could be cast in reverse as " cloak undead " . Effects . This spell evolved over time . The earliest version operated in a sphere centered on the caster of radius equal to 10 ft ( 3 m ) times the experience level of the caster and it revealed the location of even invisible or concealed undead . A prickling sensation warned the caster if any undead entered the area during the few minutes of the spell ' s duration . The next version of " detect undead " had a much greater range ( 60 ft / 18 . 3 m plus 10 ft / 3 m per level of the caster ) and duration ( 30 minutes ) but only worked in a corridor 10 ft ( 3 m ) wide , forcing the caster to turn about in order to sweep out the entire surrounding area . This version only gave direction to the undead , not location or distance , and it could be blocked by 1 ft ( 30 cm ) of solid stone , 3 ft ( 0 . 9 m ) of wood or dirt , or a thin sheet of metal . The next version of this spell was limited to a range of 60 ft ( 18 .

title: Dethek
description: Dethek Dethek was the name of a runic script used by the Dwarvish language , as well as some , and by the giant , ogre , orc , gnome , goblin , and terran languages . It consisted of letters , numerals and symbols for common words or phrases . " Dethek " was also sometimes used to refer to the Dwarvish language as a whole .
description_long: Dethek Dethek was the name of a runic script used by the Dwarvish language , as well as some , and by the giant , ogre , orc , gnome , goblin , and terran languages . It consisted of letters , numerals and symbols for common words or phrases . " Dethek " was also sometimes used to refer to the Dwarvish language as a whole . Writing . Alphabet . The Dethek runic alphabet consisted of 24 characters . The sounds " w " , " x " , and " z " were represented by the same character . This might have been confusing for humans trying to translate into Common . It was not an issue for native Dethek users , as few words in those languages had these letters . Numerals . The Dethek method of counting used a collection of straight lines , joined together to create a number . This means that each number appeared as a single character . The characters for 1 and 5 were combined in various logical ways to create the numbers 1 to 9 : The characters for 1 , 5 , and 10 were combined to created numbers up to 20 : Numbers from 20 to 99 could be created using logical combinations of the 1 , 5 , and 10 symbols : To make 100 , simply invert a 10 on top of itself ( 10×10 = 100 ) .

title: Dethud Tanthul
description: Dethud Tanthul Prince Dethud Tanthul was perhaps the most reserved of the twelve princes of Netheril . His reputation for silence was famous throughout the City of Shade ; he rarely spoke directly to anyone , and when he did , it was usually with the voice of wisdom . Among the royal family , Dethud was the closest thing to a peacemaker .
description_long: Dethud Tanthul Prince Dethud Tanthul was perhaps the most reserved of the twelve princes of Netheril . His reputation for silence was famous throughout the City of Shade ; he rarely spoke directly to anyone , and when he did , it was usually with the voice of wisdom . Among the royal family , Dethud was the closest thing to a peacemaker . The other eleven princes continued to seek Dethud ' s advice on many of their most vexing problems and private quarrels . Dethud rarely took sides in such matters , but analyzed the situation and offered incisive , logical solutions . The High Prince often included Dethud in military or political councils , making the quiet prince more influential than most of his brethren . When pressed for his opinion regarding the best means of achieving his father ' s goal of conquest , Dethud favored Melegaunt ' s policy of manipulation . Lore . Prince Dethud ' s personal sigil was a stylized black sunburst on a pale yellow field . Relationships . Dethud had two daughters , Manarlume Tanthul and Lelavdra Tanthul .

title: Detrinius Wands
description: Detrinius Wands Detrinius Wands was a Faerun ian lich in T ' u Lung in 1358 DR . History . Detrinius Wands was a lich from Faerun who decided to go to Kara - Tur , believing it was a land without cleric s .
description_long: Detrinius Wands Detrinius Wands was a Faerun ian lich in T ' u Lung in 1358 DR . History . Detrinius Wands was a lich from Faerun who decided to go to Kara - Tur , believing it was a land without cleric s . However , he was trapped by a " curse " in a maze in T ' u Lung ' s Underdark . Personality . Detrinius went mad from solitude . He was desperate for company . If he met someone , Detrinius tried by all means not to remain alone anymore . He also wanted news about the outside world .

title: Deudermont
description: Deudermont Captain Deudermont was a friend of Drizzt and the Companions of the Hall . He was the captain of the famous " Sea Sprite " , a large pirate - hunting vessel commissioned to him by the Lords of Waterdeep . Deudermont was recognized as perhaps the most successful pirate hunters of all time , and not even the elves knew of one better .
description_long: Deudermont Captain Deudermont was a friend of Drizzt and the Companions of the Hall . He was the captain of the famous " Sea Sprite " , a large pirate - hunting vessel commissioned to him by the Lords of Waterdeep . Deudermont was recognized as perhaps the most successful pirate hunters of all time , and not even the elves knew of one better . Description . Deudermont was a tall refined man . By his look , one would expect to find him amongst the lords and ladies during his shore time , but he cared about his crew . He typically spent his time keeping an eye on them , and making sure they stayed out of trouble . Personality . Deudermont was almost unshakeably loyal to his crew , and expected that loyalty in return . When Drizzt arrived to sail with the " Sea Sprite " , Deudermont was initially skeptical of the drow ' s motives , but Drizzt quickly proved himself and found a place among the ship ' s complement . Relationships . His trusted right - hand man was the wizard Robillard , who was second - in - command on the " Sea Sprite " and a capable magic user . History .

title: Deularla Ithruen
description: Deularla Ithruen Deularla " Hightower " Ithruen was a gold elf wizard and adventurer from Evermeet who resided in Cormyr in 1367 DR . Activities . Deularla used her spellcasting abilities as an adventurer in the Six Splendid Swords band .
description_long: Deularla Ithruen Deularla " Hightower " Ithruen was a gold elf wizard and adventurer from Evermeet who resided in Cormyr in 1367 DR . Activities . Deularla used her spellcasting abilities as an adventurer in the Six Splendid Swords band . Relationships . Though not initially attracted to him , Deularla eventually became smitten with a fellow adventurer and member of the Six Splendid Swords , Dunman Kiriag . They were married shortly thereafter . History . Deularla was killed by a dragon ' s fiery breath . She used her last ounce of strength to cast a spell enabling her essence into her husband . Her spirit lived within Dunman , warning him of danger and helping him to recall obscure memories . On occasion she would use Dunman ' s body to speak to others as herself .

title: Deva
description: Deva Devas are a specific type of aasimar that , unlike typical examples of the race , are all in fact angel ic souls contained within mortal bodies . These souls are reborn again and again , meaning that devas have access to the experiences of several lifetimes in their subconscious and sometimes waking mind as well . These souls are obliged to fight in the cosmic war against evil , though some stray from this path and are reincarnated in their next life as rakshasa s .
description_long: Deva Devas are a specific type of aasimar that , unlike typical examples of the race , are all in fact angel ic souls contained within mortal bodies . These souls are reborn again and again , meaning that devas have access to the experiences of several lifetimes in their subconscious and sometimes waking mind as well . These souls are obliged to fight in the cosmic war against evil , though some stray from this path and are reincarnated in their next life as rakshasa s . Physically , devas appear similar to aasimar , though in a fashion more distinct than many aasimar , who could be mistaken for human . Devas also possess a number of abilities unique to them . Despite this , devas can be and historically have been considered aasimar . Ecology . Physical characteristics . Devas bear the mark of their celestial touch through many different physical features that often vary from individual to individual . Nearly all devas are uncommonly beautiful and still , and they are often significantly taller than humans as well . When a deva ’ s features are unshapely it is often the result of extreme circumstances , such as grave injury or severe illness .

title: Deva ( angel )
description: Deva ( angel ) A deva is a category of angel , part of those known as " celestial stewards " . Celestial stewards are those angels who directly serve the gods of the Celestial Planes , and include devas , light s , planetar s , and solar s . There are three types of devas : astral devas , monadic devas , and movanic devas .
description_long: Deva ( angel ) A deva is a category of angel , part of those known as " celestial stewards " . Celestial stewards are those angels who directly serve the gods of the Celestial Planes , and include devas , light s , planetar s , and solar s . There are three types of devas : astral devas , monadic devas , and movanic devas . Astral deva . The golden - hued astral devas chiefly exist to battle fiends in the Fiendish Planes . They also travel the Astral Plane to rescue lost or stranded mortals of good alignment . Monadic deva . The dark - skinned , green - eyed monadic devas exist to watch over the Elemental Chaos for the gods of Good . They can survive any elemental environment without ill effect . Movanic deva . The milky - white movanic devas travel the Prime Material Plane to aid prominent followers of the gods of good in times of great need . While they more often appear disguised as humanoid s or animals , they can manifest in their winged angelic form , with shining silver hair and piercing silver eyes , if this suits their needs .

title: Devamari
description: Devamari Devamari was a doppelganger criminal in Mulmaster in 1491 DR . Activities . The doppelganger acted as the right hand of crime lord Gethmedra Darmov at the Black Blade and Bloody Boar tavern / gladiator arena .
description_long: Devamari Devamari was a doppelganger criminal in Mulmaster in 1491 DR . Activities . The doppelganger acted as the right hand of crime lord Gethmedra Darmov at the Black Blade and Bloody Boar tavern / gladiator arena . Its role was to prevent gladiators from using magic in the fights .

title: Devane
description: Devane Devane was the Helm ite Bishop of Maztica in 1362 DR . History . He was a protégée of the late Bishop Domincus of Amn and communicated with the bishop through magical means until Domincus was sacrificed to Zaltec by the Viperhands .
description_long: Devane Devane was the Helm ite Bishop of Maztica in 1362 DR . History . He was a protégée of the late Bishop Domincus of Amn and communicated with the bishop through magical means until Domincus was sacrificed to Zaltec by the Viperhands . Because of his relationship with Domincus , the Council of Six selected Devane as the chief priest on the second Maztican expedition . Devane was given a flying carpet to ride and he used this magic al device to impress the natives . Devane was initially loyal to Don Vaez , the expedition ' s leader , but switched allegiance to Cordell shortly before the second battle of Ulatos . Devane fought bravely during the battle and was later promoted to bishop . In 1362 DR , the Helmite missionary Mirandos went missing with a small group of Payit warriors and Bishop Devane commissioned a group of adventurers to track her down and bring her back if possible . In 1370 DR Devane grew dissatisfied for the few new Helmite coverts and petitioned governor Cordell to sent expeditions to new unexplored lands inland in order to " reveal Helm s truth to the savages " .

title: Devastate undead
description: Devastate undead Devastate undead , also known as disrupt undead , was an arcane necromancy spell that sapped undead of their negative energy and destroyed them . Effects . The spellcaster fired a beam at a number of undead targets and destroyed them in a manner similar to the power of a " disruption " weapon .
description_long: Devastate undead Devastate undead , also known as disrupt undead , was an arcane necromancy spell that sapped undead of their negative energy and destroyed them . Effects . The spellcaster fired a beam at a number of undead targets and destroyed them in a manner similar to the power of a " disruption " weapon . A particularly resilient undead could resist or even be unaffected by the spell . A living being was immune to its effect . The spell had a secondary effect of channeling negative energy from a damaged or destroyed undead back to the caster . This could either hurt the caster ( if they were alive ) or heal the caster ( if they were undead themselves ) . Components . The spell required a " disruption " weapon of any kind as a focus . History . The " devastate undead " spell was developed by the arch - lich Larloch . He used it to heal himself by sacrificing his undead servant creatures . He could even potentially use it to permanently boost his unlife force .

title: Devic
description: Devic Devic was a language spoken by the inhabitants of the city of Solon and the kingdom of Ulgarth in southeast Faerûn . It was found in the region between Solon and the Dustwall in the north , Xontuil Bay and the Great Sea in the west , and the Yehimal Mountains in the east . It was categorized as part of the Imaskari languages group , in the Durpari language s subgroup .
description_long: Devic Devic was a language spoken by the inhabitants of the city of Solon and the kingdom of Ulgarth in southeast Faerûn . It was found in the region between Solon and the Dustwall in the north , Xontuil Bay and the Great Sea in the west , and the Yehimal Mountains in the east . It was categorized as part of the Imaskari languages group , in the Durpari language s subgroup . Devic was primarily the language of Ulgarth , where the Ulgarthic dialect was spoken . However , the Solonese dialect was used in Solon . It was associated with the Devic culture of Solon .

title: Devil
description: Devil Devils were a lawful evil race of fiend s who hailed from the Nine Hells of Baator , a dominion of the Astral Sea ruled over by the god Asmodeus . True to their alignment , devils were locked into a strict hierarchy which culminated with the Lords of the Nine , the powerful rulers of the Hells . Types of devils .
description_long: Devil Devils were a lawful evil race of fiend s who hailed from the Nine Hells of Baator , a dominion of the Astral Sea ruled over by the god Asmodeus . True to their alignment , devils were locked into a strict hierarchy which culminated with the Lords of the Nine , the powerful rulers of the Hells . Types of devils . Baatezu . This ruling class of devils ruled tyrannically over their domains in Baator . Abishai . Abishai were a subgroup of baatezu created by Tiamat . Imps . Imps were relatively weak devils typically used as wizard s ' familiars . Other Types . Alu - fiend • Archdevil • Cambion • Chain devil • Desert devil • Duergar • Gorechain devil • Hellcat • Hellfire engine • Infernal armor animus • Kalabon • Misfortune devil • Shocktroop devil • Succubus • Withering devil

title: Devlin
description: Devlin Devlin was an adventurer in the ruins of Spellgard in 1479 DR . History . Devlin was an evil adventurer leading the Free Company of the Crescent .
description_long: Devlin Devlin was an adventurer in the ruins of Spellgard in 1479 DR . History . Devlin was an evil adventurer leading the Free Company of the Crescent . In 1479 DR , he went with his fellows to Spellgard hoping to find Lady Saharel ' s treasures . Personality . Devlin was a charismatic but uncaring individual . He loved double - crossing others , even for momentary advantages .

title: Devoted Mamluk Society
description: Devoted Mamluk Society The Devoted Mamluk Society , also known as the Devoted , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Devoted and Exalted were bitter rivals , leading to frequent conflicts in the region of the Cities of the Pantheon .
description_long: Devoted Mamluk Society The Devoted Mamluk Society , also known as the Devoted , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Devoted and Exalted were bitter rivals , leading to frequent conflicts in the region of the Cities of the Pantheon . Organization . The Devoted were led by Amahl Abd al - Muhlis , the Most Respected Warrior . Base of Operations . The Devoted were scattered through the Cities of the Pantheon , but their strongest presence was within I ' tiraf and Fahhas .

title: Devourer
description: Devourer Devourers were fiends who acted in the service of Orcus . They were used to create armies of undead by consuming the bodies and souls of humanoid s . Lesser demon s could be promoted to devourers by proving themselves to Orcus .
description_long: Devourer Devourers were fiends who acted in the service of Orcus . They were used to create armies of undead by consuming the bodies and souls of humanoid s . Lesser demon s could be promoted to devourers by proving themselves to Orcus . A devourer created new undead by bringing a humanoid creature to the brink of death , and then trapping its victim inside its ribcage . While there , the devourer tortured its victim ' s soul with telepathic noise until death , after which an undead would come out in its service .

title: Devout Mamluk Society
description: Devout Mamluk Society The Devout Mamluk Society , also known as the Devout , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . This mamluk organization was tasked with protecting the prince of Kadarasto , Nari ibn Aman .
description_long: Devout Mamluk Society The Devout Mamluk Society , also known as the Devout , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . This mamluk organization was tasked with protecting the prince of Kadarasto , Nari ibn Aman . History . This group was initially part of the Devoted . They were originally sent with the goal of expanding religious activity in the region , but most of their time and concern was spent protecting the young prince , so the Grand Caliph recognized them as a separate mamluk organization . Organization . The Devout were led by Mustah Abd al - Nasik . Base of Operations . The Devout were based within the Cities of the Ancients in Kadarastro .

title: Dhaerhaera Nanatar
description: Dhaerhaera Nanatar Dhaerhaera Nanatar was a female human wizard and adventurer who made her home in Tantras in the Vast around 1358 DR . She was one of the more notable mages of the city at the time . In the late 1350s DR , Dhaerhaera captured a griffon and successfully tamed it and taught it to carry her as a rider .
description_long: Dhaerhaera Nanatar Dhaerhaera Nanatar was a female human wizard and adventurer who made her home in Tantras in the Vast around 1358 DR . She was one of the more notable mages of the city at the time . In the late 1350s DR , Dhaerhaera captured a griffon and successfully tamed it and taught it to carry her as a rider . Riding her griffin , she regularly flew around the Vast looking for adventure . After the Time of Troubles in 1358 DR , her project was exploring the old mountain tombs and strongholds of elves and humans , dating back to the time when dwarves ruled the Vast . She sought lost magic , and had some success in this .

title: Dhaerivus
description: Dhaerivus Dhaerivus was a human wizard with dark eyes and a thin white face . Description . The mage wore a dark with glowing mystic signs , and carried a staff adorned with gem s and a crystal sphere at one end .
description_long: Dhaerivus Dhaerivus was a human wizard with dark eyes and a thin white face . Description . The mage wore a dark with glowing mystic signs , and carried a staff adorned with gem s and a crystal sphere at one end . He had many rings on his fingers . History . Dhaerivus was once turned into a toad at a magefair .

title: Dhafiyand
description: Dhafiyand Dhafiyand was a Red Wizard of Thay in Neverwinter in 1478 DR . History . Dhafiyand was a Red Wizard that concealed his true allegiance and managed to become the spymaster of the Protector of Neverwinter , Dagult Neverember .
description_long: Dhafiyand Dhafiyand was a Red Wizard of Thay in Neverwinter in 1478 DR . History . Dhafiyand was a Red Wizard that concealed his true allegiance and managed to become the spymaster of the Protector of Neverwinter , Dagult Neverember . Working with Valindra Shadowmantle and fellow Red Wizard Tolivast , he hatched a complex plot to use the Sons of Alagondar as cover for killing Dagult . In order to achieve this objective , Dhafiyand hired Rucas Sarfael and ordered him to infiltrate the Nashers through Elyne Tschavarz . In the end , however , Rucas discovered the deception in time and managed to save Dagult from Dhafiyand and his undead minions . In the fighting Dhafiyand was killed and so the Thay ans lost an irreplaceable agent and were unveiled as enemies of Neverwinter .

title: Dhairn
description: Dhairn Dhairn was a judicator of Selvetarm . History . Dhairn was part of a group of drow exiled from Eryndlyn for focusing too much to Selvetarm instead of Lolth In 1375 DR , Dhairn went to recruit a large group of drider s living in the Underdark under the Misty Forest for membership in the Selvetargtlin .
description_long: Dhairn Dhairn was a judicator of Selvetarm . History . Dhairn was part of a group of drow exiled from Eryndlyn for focusing too much to Selvetarm instead of Lolth In 1375 DR , Dhairn went to recruit a large group of drider s living in the Underdark under the Misty Forest for membership in the Selvetargtlin . Later meantime various group of Underdark monsters , chitine , neogi , drider s and spellgaunt s attacked all the Eilistraee ' s shrines in surface , Dhairn led the main force of the Selvertargltlin to attack the Promenade of the Dark Maiden He fought well against Qilué Veladorn . However at last in Abyss Cavatina Xarann killed Selvetarn himself and Dhairn felling confused and powerless . He was trying to escape when Qilue ' s blade skewered his back .

title: Dhalgrave
description: Dhalgrave Dhalgrave was the leader of the malaugrym in 1358 DR . Activities . As Shadowmaster , Dhalgrave had mastery over the Shadowcrown and the Doomstars , two powerful artifact s given by Malaug himself to the leader of his kin .
description_long: Dhalgrave Dhalgrave was the leader of the malaugrym in 1358 DR . Activities . As Shadowmaster , Dhalgrave had mastery over the Shadowcrown and the Doomstars , two powerful artifact s given by Malaug himself to the leader of his kin . He had always with him his bodyguard Malator . History . In 1357 DR , Dhalgrave noticed the hunt for Shandril Shessair . In 1358 DR , Dhalgrave knew he was dying so he needed to choose a replacement as Shadowmaster Supreme . When Lady Saharel , one of the only two beings besides Dhalgrave who knew how to wield , empower , or destroy the Crown and Stars of Malaug , died defending Elminster Aumar , Dhalgrave ordered a hunt upon Elminster , the other remaining being . He declared the killer of the Old Mage would be the next Shadowmaster Supreme . After it was discovered that the Simbul was hidden among a large malaugrym ' s party that was attacking El , causing the death of most of them , Dhalgrave ordered to close the gate to Toril until decided what do with this new foe . Some time later Dhalgrave disappeared .

title: Dhamir Ercals
description: Dhamir Ercals Dhamir Ercals was the high priest of Cyric in Darkhold and one of the Zhentarim leaders of the fortress in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . History . Dhamir led the Second Banedeath in Darkhold , purging all non - Cyric followers .
description_long: Dhamir Ercals Dhamir Ercals was the high priest of Cyric in Darkhold and one of the Zhentarim leaders of the fortress in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . History . Dhamir led the Second Banedeath in Darkhold , purging all non - Cyric followers . Impressed , Sememmon offered Dhamir command of the keep , which he quickly accepted , becoming the leader of the Cyricist Zhents there . But Dhamir ' s aims were greater : he wanted to assume control of the Twin Towers of the Eternal Eclipse and use them to advance in the Zhent hierarchy . He also started plotting an evil crusade against eastern powers like Mulhorand and Iyachtu Xvim .

title: Dhampyr
description: Dhampyr Dhampyrs , also known as " daywalkers , " are living creatures who have inherited some of the tainted blood of vampire s . Some are the descendants of male vampires and mortal females , but many others have dhampyrs for parents and some result from a vampire of either sex biting a pregnant female . A dhampyr ' s powers may lie dormant for years before being quickened ; dhampyrs may also have children who are normal in every respect .
description_long: Dhampyr Dhampyrs , also known as " daywalkers , " are living creatures who have inherited some of the tainted blood of vampire s . Some are the descendants of male vampires and mortal females , but many others have dhampyrs for parents and some result from a vampire of either sex biting a pregnant female . A dhampyr ' s powers may lie dormant for years before being quickened ; dhampyrs may also have children who are normal in every respect . Possessing some of the strengths of vampires and none of their traditional weaknesses , dhampyrs are simultaneously valued and discriminated against by both sides of their heritage . Ecology . Physical characteristics . Dhampyrs are thin and willowy , with pale skin and slightly pointed ears . They have slightly pronounced canines and blood - red eyes . Dhampyrs are unharmed by sunlight or positive energy the way true vampires are . Many dhampyrs feel the characteristic bloodlust of a vampire as well as the ability to feed off of blood for sustenance or healing , though their thirst is much milder than that of true vampires and not all or even most dhampyrs carry out the practice . Abilities .

title: Dharbang River
description: Dharbang River The Dharbang River was located in Ra - Khati . Geography . The Dharbang River was the smaller of Ra - Khati ' s two major rivers ; the larger being the Gogrus River .
description_long: Dharbang River The Dharbang River was located in Ra - Khati . Geography . The Dharbang River was the smaller of Ra - Khati ' s two major rivers ; the larger being the Gogrus River . This river originated from a glacier located in Katakoro Shan on Ra - Khati ' s southeastern border , flowing until it formed Norasil near the center of the kingdom before joining the Gogrus to the west . Locations . This river was considered one of the Thousand Sacred Sources of the Gaya , drawing pilgrims from all over the region . Three holy sites were located along the river . The first was the junction of the Dharbang and the Gogrus . Locals called this spot the " Bed of Two Lovers . " The water here was calm compared to the raging currents downstream . It was rumored to have healing properties . Any who bathed here were restored to full health and all ailments were vanquished . Water taken from this spot did not retain its unique healing properties , however . Legend stated that the source of the healing power came when the Great Teacher , and founder of the Path , meditated at this spot for five weeks without eating or sleeping . During that time , he achieved the fifth stage of enlightenment .

title: Dharjamyn Thauntle
description: Dharjamyn Thauntle Dharjamyn Thauntle was a cobbler who operated Thauntle ' s Good Heels and Soles in the South Ward of Waterdeep . Personality . The cobbler had a personal collection of gemstones , but claimed that due to his age , he was unable to search for rare stones in the areas surrounding the city .
description_long: Dharjamyn Thauntle Dharjamyn Thauntle was a cobbler who operated Thauntle ' s Good Heels and Soles in the South Ward of Waterdeep . Personality . The cobbler had a personal collection of gemstones , but claimed that due to his age , he was unable to search for rare stones in the areas surrounding the city . Instead , Dharjamyn searched for gem s on the slopes of Mount Waterdeep , which was frowned upon by the City Guard . History . Around 1374 DR , Dharjamyn found a number of rubies on Mount Waterdeep , but was warned by city guardsman Horthan Hethdance to stay away from the mountain .

title: Dharva Scatterheart
description: Dharva Scatterheart Dharva Scatterheart was the would - be - queen of Greenfields in 1372 DR . She enjoyed the open space , freedom from taxation , and the caravans that regularly pass through . Allied with the Shadow Thieves , Dharva had established a small town called Greenest on the trail that led to Berdusk .
description_long: Dharva Scatterheart Dharva Scatterheart was the would - be - queen of Greenfields in 1372 DR . She enjoyed the open space , freedom from taxation , and the caravans that regularly pass through . Allied with the Shadow Thieves , Dharva had established a small town called Greenest on the trail that led to Berdusk . She was not particularly happy to be in business with the likes of them , but tolerated it nonetheless .

title: Dhast
description: Dhast Dhast was a coastal hamlet on the east coast of The Fang in east Faerûn . As of 1368 DR , the population was split between a clifftop community and a smaller number of fishermen living on the beach . The two portions of the hamlet were linked via a trail , and a rivalry existed between them , each side considering the other to be stupid and wicked .
description_long: Dhast Dhast was a coastal hamlet on the east coast of The Fang in east Faerûn . As of 1368 DR , the population was split between a clifftop community and a smaller number of fishermen living on the beach . The two portions of the hamlet were linked via a trail , and a rivalry existed between them , each side considering the other to be stupid and wicked . People in Dhast did not trust outsiders , because most were descendants of those who were refugees to The Fang during the conflict with the half - elves .

title: Dhaztanar
description: Dhaztanar Dhaztanar , or the Crystal - towered , was the capital of Semphar and the kingdom ' s largest city . Location . Dhaztanar marked one end of the Silk Road , making it a bustling epicenter of trade and commerce .
description_long: Dhaztanar Dhaztanar , or the Crystal - towered , was the capital of Semphar and the kingdom ' s largest city . Location . Dhaztanar marked one end of the Silk Road , making it a bustling epicenter of trade and commerce . The city was nestled along the eastern banks of the Semphar Water , which was a portion of the larger lake of Gbor Nor . Description . Most of the buildings in Dhaztanar were constructed of stone or brick ; wood was scarcely used since it had to be imported from the Shalhoond . A typical house in Dhaztanar was two stories tall , making the state buildings appear more grand as they towered over them . History . Dhaztanar was a fierce rival of Zindalankh , which was located on the opposite bank of the Semphar Water in Murghôm . Inhabitants . The Caliph and master of Semphar , Abu Bakr , lived in Dhaztanar within the splendid palace of Dar al - Kalif . Elves , dwarves , gnomes , halflings , and some goblin - kind , were present in the city . The Harpers were rumored to have a presence or outpost in the city .

title: Dhedluk ( town )
description: Dhedluk ( town ) Dhedluk ( pronounced " dead - LUKE " ) was a small town surrounded by a stockade in the King ' s Forest in Cormyr . It had a population of 936 as of 1372 DR . It was a farming and woodcarving community led by Lord Thiombar .
description_long: Dhedluk ( town ) Dhedluk ( pronounced " dead - LUKE " ) was a small town surrounded by a stockade in the King ' s Forest in Cormyr . It had a population of 936 as of 1372 DR . It was a farming and woodcarving community led by Lord Thiombar . A short forest trail called the Ranger ' s Way linked it to Waymoot in the southwest and Starwater Road led north , out of the forest to Eveningstar . It was a beautiful place , with dappled sunlight reaching down through the eaves of gigantic trees covered in moss . It was a popular place for nobles and Purple Dragons to retire to , which was why a small stone and timber hut could be sold for upwards of 16 , 000 golden lion s . Despite being primarily a logging village , expanding the forest clearing was forbidden in the 1360s DR . There were still bogs surrounding the town , which meant it remained popular with skilled woodcarvers and herbalists . There were three small quail ranches and a boobrie farm . Most travelers recognize Dhedluk for one thing : the Blushing Maiden Inn , which was run by Thiombar . There was also a two - way " portal " just outside the town , which led to an area near the court buildings at Castle Obarskyr in Suzail .

title: Dhelt
description: Dhelt Dhelt was a human man of Elturel in the Chionthar Valley . He was a paladin of Helm , the High Rider of the Hellriders and Lord of Elturel . Under his reign , Elturel became one of the safest and best - defended communities within the region , despite his competitive nature .
description_long: Dhelt Dhelt was a human man of Elturel in the Chionthar Valley . He was a paladin of Helm , the High Rider of the Hellriders and Lord of Elturel . Under his reign , Elturel became one of the safest and best - defended communities within the region , despite his competitive nature . The vigilant watch of the Lord ' s soldiers made Elturel a safe haven for merchants and other travelers passing through .

title: Dhenna Shavres
description: Dhenna Shavres Dhenna Shavres was a Red Wizard and leader of the Rose Keep enclave in Aglarond . Relationships . She managed to keep running the enclave even after the War of the Zulkirs , when all Red Wizards outside Thay were recalled home by Szass Tam or faced exile .
description_long: Dhenna Shavres Dhenna Shavres was a Red Wizard and leader of the Rose Keep enclave in Aglarond . Relationships . She managed to keep running the enclave even after the War of the Zulkirs , when all Red Wizards outside Thay were recalled home by Szass Tam or faced exile . She also gained the trust of the neighboring Aglarondans . History . In 1396 DR , she briefly met Raidon Kane and the ex – Red Wizard Seren Juramot .

title: Dheolur
description: Dheolur Dheolur was a former noble house of Cormyr . One of its houses was situated beyond the Royal Gardens in Suzail , Cormyr , and another in the King ' s Forest , protected by a 20 foot high ( 6 . 1m ) wall , built on top of the ruins of a temple of Moander .
description_long: Dheolur Dheolur was a former noble house of Cormyr . One of its houses was situated beyond the Royal Gardens in Suzail , Cormyr , and another in the King ' s Forest , protected by a 20 foot high ( 6 . 1m ) wall , built on top of the ruins of a temple of Moander . The house was elevated to nobility by the grandfather of King Duar Obarskyr . When Magrath the Minotaur seized control of Suzail around 429 DR , the house swore fealty to him almost immediately .

title: Dheubpurcwenpyl
description: Dheubpurcwenpyl Dheubpurcwenpyl was one of the most powerful deep dragon s in the Underdark in 1370 DR . Reputation . She was so powerful that nobody challenged her authority and even the neighboring drow of Guallidurth had to go around her domain and even revered her as " Malla Harl Valsharess " , or " Honored Queen of the Depths " .
description_long: Dheubpurcwenpyl Dheubpurcwenpyl was one of the most powerful deep dragon s in the Underdark in 1370 DR . Reputation . She was so powerful that nobody challenged her authority and even the neighboring drow of Guallidurth had to go around her domain and even revered her as " Malla Harl Valsharess " , or " Honored Queen of the Depths " . Many mistook Dheubpurcwenpyl for a shadow dragon , leading some scholars to believe that she knew a spell called " shadow dragon " that transformed herself into a shadow being . Lair . Dheubpurcwenpyl had in her hoard most of the lost treasures of Old Shanatar . Her lair was in the Rift of Dhalnadar , a great chasm south of the Marching Mountains , famous for waterfalls and jungles .

title: Dhinnilith
description: Dhinnilith Dhinnilith was a phantom city rumored to appear on moonless nights every few years , hovering over the waters of the Vilhon Reach , just north of the Chondalwood . History . Dhinnilith was the first of the twelve Cities of the Sword of Jhaamdath , founded in - 5750 DR by that empire ' s psionic rulers .
description_long: Dhinnilith Dhinnilith was a phantom city rumored to appear on moonless nights every few years , hovering over the waters of the Vilhon Reach , just north of the Chondalwood . History . Dhinnilith was the first of the twelve Cities of the Sword of Jhaamdath , founded in - 5750 DR by that empire ' s psionic rulers . It was supposed destroyed with the rest of Jhaamdath in - 255 DR , when the elves used high magic to send a tidal wave in retaliation for the slaughter of the elves of the Chondalwood . As of 1374 DR , no explorer had located the ruins of Dhinnilith on the bottom of the Vilhon Reach . Rumors and Legends . Persistent rumors were spread that Dhinnilith had somehow survived the great destruction of the Year of Furious Waves . It was claimed that a city of phantom stone would rise out of the waters of the Vilhon Reach on moonless nights and vanish before sunrise . The last such sighting occurred in 1371 DR . While as of 1374 DR , no adventurer had explored the transient city , the truth was that the city ' s only remaining inhabitant was a caller in darkness , a ghostly cloud with thousands of human faces , silently screaming in terror and anguish .

title: Dhoelath
description: Dhoelath Dhoelath was a high mage who lived in his tower , Dhoelath ' s Tower , in Leuthilspar on Evermeet . Personality . The wizard was reclusive , but had been known to take on an apprentice .
description_long: Dhoelath Dhoelath was a high mage who lived in his tower , Dhoelath ' s Tower , in Leuthilspar on Evermeet . Personality . The wizard was reclusive , but had been known to take on an apprentice . History . Around 1367 DR , Dhoelath was an important defender of the Leuthilspar .

title: Dhoelath ' s Tower
description: Dhoelath ' s Tower Dhoelath ' s Tower was a green marble tower in Leuthilspar , Evermeet . Description . The black and white striped tower had balconies and a reflective black marble roof .
description_long: Dhoelath ' s Tower Dhoelath ' s Tower was a green marble tower in Leuthilspar , Evermeet . Description . The black and white striped tower had balconies and a reflective black marble roof . History . Around 1367 DR , the tower was inhabited by the wizard Dhoelath . Rumors and legends . Hidden within the halls of the tower , Dhoelath was said to hold the secret to powerful high magic .

title: Dhow
description: Dhow A dhow was a small sailing ship with a single , triangular sail . Dhows are generally too small to be used as military vessels . In Calimshan .
description_long: Dhow A dhow was a small sailing ship with a single , triangular sail . Dhows are generally too small to be used as military vessels . In Calimshan . They were commonly used in Calimshan by fishermen . In Zakhara . All ships of Zakhara n build were dhows — indeed " dhow " was the Midani term for " ship " . Various sizes of dhows , from 40 to 200 feet ( 12 to 61 meters ) in length were employed in the Land of Fate . Five distinct types were recognized : the baghla , the barijah , the boom , the sambuk , and the zaruq ( or zarug ) .

title: Dhusarra el Abhuk
description: Dhusarra el Abhuk Huntmistress Dhusarra yr Fadila el Abhuk was a Calishite human vampire ( formerly an adventurer ) who lived in Undermountain and worshiped Malar . She famously conducted a High Hunt in the city of Waterdeep . Dhusarra ' s former master was Noreyth Harpell .
description_long: Dhusarra el Abhuk Huntmistress Dhusarra yr Fadila el Abhuk was a Calishite human vampire ( formerly an adventurer ) who lived in Undermountain and worshiped Malar . She famously conducted a High Hunt in the city of Waterdeep . Dhusarra ' s former master was Noreyth Harpell . Description . Dhusarra appeared to be a beautiful woman in her mid twenties . She had long black hair and eyes the colour of chestnuts . She tended to dress in black silk tunics and breeches with black slippers . She also followed the common tradition of malar ite priests by wearing trophies from slain foes , her apparent favourite being the complete pelt of a displacer beast made into a cloak / headdress . Personality . Dhusarra was noted for being cunning , haughty , ruthless and vengeful . She slew fellow malarites to increase her standing in the church and was determined to find whoever was responsible for sending the Company of the Red Dawn against her master despite the attack leading to her freedom . Relationships . Before she was made undead , Dhusarra led the Malarites of Wyllowwood , though she seemed not to have reestablished her relationship with them after she regained her independence .

title: Diabolic domain
description: Diabolic domain The Diabolic domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters diabolic spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Vile Darkness " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Diabolic Domain Powers .
description_long: Diabolic domain The Diabolic domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters diabolic spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Vile Darkness " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Diabolic Domain Powers . Once a day , the cleric can improve his / her skill at bluffing , diplomacy , intimidation , or sensing motives .

title: Diabolic grasp
description: Diabolic grasp Diabolic grasp was a moderately complex spell known to warlock s , particularly those of the infernal pact . When cast , " diabolic grasp " allowed a warlock to lift a creature of an ogre ' s size or smaller within fifty feet of him or her with a summoned talon from the Hells and move them telekinetically a distance of at least five feet . The creature could be tossed as far as ten feet , or possibly further , if the caster was an infernal warlock of considerable intelligence .
description_long: Diabolic grasp Diabolic grasp was a moderately complex spell known to warlock s , particularly those of the infernal pact . When cast , " diabolic grasp " allowed a warlock to lift a creature of an ogre ' s size or smaller within fifty feet of him or her with a summoned talon from the Hells and move them telekinetically a distance of at least five feet . The creature could be tossed as far as ten feet , or possibly further , if the caster was an infernal warlock of considerable intelligence . The spell was both physically and mentally straining on its caster , its power dependent in part upon the durability of the warlock , and once cast it couldn ' t be recast without a rest of at least a few minutes on the warlock ' s part .

title: Diamond
description: Diamond Diamond was an extremely hard gemstone found primarily in the cold , mountainous region of Faerûn and anywhere on Toril that had seen volcanic activity , either active or dormant . Nearly all probable diamond locations were deep underground , making them accessible only to dwarves and the other subterranean races . Description .
description_long: Diamond Diamond was an extremely hard gemstone found primarily in the cold , mountainous region of Faerûn and anywhere on Toril that had seen volcanic activity , either active or dormant . Nearly all probable diamond locations were deep underground , making them accessible only to dwarves and the other subterranean races . Description . Gem quality diamonds were translucent to transparent and came in a variety of colors . The most valuable hues were clear ( also described as blue - white ) , canary yellow , pink , brown , and deep blue . They were almost exclusively facet cut because , if done correctly , diamonds refracted ordinary light into beautiful flashes of color ( known as " fire " in lapidary parlance ) . Diamonds were frequently worn for adornment . Very few substances were harder than diamond and all were just as rare and scarce , or more so . Diamonds could be used to engrave almost anything and were prized for making fine cutting and piercing tools for artisans . A typical properly cut specimen had a base value of 5 , 000 gp . Powers . Diamonds had an affinity for divination magic , and in the crafting of spells or items that improved vision or located objects .

title: Diancastra
description: Diancastra Diancastra was a deity in the giant pantheon , the Ordning . She was a minor trickster goddess , unlike her older sisters Hiatea and Iallanis . History .
description_long: Diancastra Diancastra was a deity in the giant pantheon , the Ordning . She was a minor trickster goddess , unlike her older sisters Hiatea and Iallanis . History . She was fathered by Annam All - Father himself , but her mother is unknown , speculated to be a cloud or storm giant . Unlike her sister Hiatea , she did not earn her divinity through feats of strength , but rather by acts of wit and wile . She accomplished this by stealing a magical necklace from Blibdoolpoolp the Sea Mother , disguising herself as a kuo - toa and sneaking into the Sea Mother ' s palace . After her theft from the Sea Mother , she soon announced herself to Annam right before his departure from Toril . Citing her sister as Hiatea as a reason why she should be given divine status as well , Annam issued her one task to prove it : to circle the earth in an hour or less , knowing she could not accomplish this task ( lacking great powers and items ) . She went into Stronmaus ' s library , took one of his atlases , and tore out a page illustrating the world ( much to Stronmaus ' displeasure ) . She drew a circle around the world , and presented it towards the All - Father .

title: Diatryma
description: Diatryma The diatryma was a large , flightless bird native to the Underdark . Description . The gigantic bird was about 8 ft ( 2 .
description_long: Diatryma The diatryma was a large , flightless bird native to the Underdark . Description . The gigantic bird was about 8 ft ( 2 . 4 m ) - 12 ft tall . ( 3 . 7 m ) Its short wings rendered it flightless . It had a thick neck and a deadly powerful hooked beak . Uses . The drow used their hugely plumed feathers for decoration . The mercenary , Jarlaxle , sported one of these on his wide brimmed hat , as ornamental and as a functional magical item . By blowing into the feather , Jarlaxle was able to summon a diatryma bird .

title: Dice
description: Dice Dice was " one of the four universal games " of Faerûn along with chess , draughts , and Talis . It was played on multiple plane s of existence . Description .
description_long: Dice Dice was " one of the four universal games " of Faerûn along with chess , draughts , and Talis . It was played on multiple plane s of existence . Description . Multiple games could be played with dice , such as various gambling games and other bar - entertainment . They came in a variety of geometric shapes . Dice were often carved from ivory . Typical dice sets came in leather cups , which were used for rolling them . Turmish was a known producer of dice , and Aurora ' s Emporium sold dice imported from that country .

title: Dictum
description: Dictum Dictum is an evocation spell that kills , paralyzes , weakens , or dazes nonlawful subjects . It is the lawful counterpart to the chaotic spell " word of chaos " . Effect .
description_long: Dictum Dictum is an evocation spell that kills , paralyzes , weakens , or dazes nonlawful subjects . It is the lawful counterpart to the chaotic spell " word of chaos " . Effect . Uttering " dictum " creates two effects . If you are on your home plane , nonlawful extraplanar creatures within the area are instantly banished back to their home planes . Creatures so banished cannot return for at least 1 day . This effect takes place regardless of whether the creatures hear the " dictum " . Creatures native to your plane who hear the " dictum " and are not lawful suffer the following ill effects : The effects are cumulative .

title: Dier Ashlin
description: Dier Ashlin Dier Ashlin was a male human Zhentilar soldier during the Time of Troubles in 1358 DR He was guarding the Temple of Bane in Zhentil Keep when the god Bane himself , in the corpse of Fzoul Chembryl , arrived in the city after the disastrous Battle of Shadowdale . Ashlin , believing he was speaking to Fzoul , explained the change in the city ' s government after the defeat .
description_long: Dier Ashlin Dier Ashlin was a male human Zhentilar soldier during the Time of Troubles in 1358 DR He was guarding the Temple of Bane in Zhentil Keep when the god Bane himself , in the corpse of Fzoul Chembryl , arrived in the city after the disastrous Battle of Shadowdale . Ashlin , believing he was speaking to Fzoul , explained the change in the city ' s government after the defeat .

title: Diesel
description: Diesel Diesel , whose real name was David S . LaForce , is an artist who designed the maps for many TSR , Inc . products .
description_long: Diesel Diesel , whose real name was David S . LaForce , is an artist who designed the maps for many TSR , Inc . products . Background . LaForce was born on August 10 , 1959 . He was given the nickname " Diesel " because several people at TSR were named David , and his initials could be pronounced like " diesel " . Career . LaForce began working for TSR in 1979 , beginning in their shipping department before it was discovered that he loved to draw . He was then hired to work for the art department and remained with TSR until 1998 .

title: Dietr
description: Dietr Dietr was a halfling soul residing in the halfling sphere of heaven , the Green Fields in 1372 . During his second confrontation with the lichdrow Lord Dyrr , the Archmage of Menzoberranzan , Gromph Baenre , was physically sent by his enemy to the Green Fields . Here , Gromph met Dietr , who was enjoying his afterlife .
description_long: Dietr Dietr was a halfling soul residing in the halfling sphere of heaven , the Green Fields in 1372 . During his second confrontation with the lichdrow Lord Dyrr , the Archmage of Menzoberranzan , Gromph Baenre , was physically sent by his enemy to the Green Fields . Here , Gromph met Dietr , who was enjoying his afterlife . However , after meeting with a living being , Dietr was reminded of his mortal life and his loved ones who remained in the Realms , especially his mother in Luiren . So , when Gromph went back to Toril , Dietr followed him . However , arriving in the Menzoberranzan Bazaar , Dietr , having abandoned the heaven , become a huecuva . Gromph felt no sympathy for Dietr and forced him to go up against the Lichdrow ; Dietr was easily destroyed .

title: Digitalogist
description: Digitalogist Digitalogists were wizard s in Zakhara who used the unique connection between mathematics and magic to create powerful formulas when they cast spells . Requirements . Due to the immense amount of time spent studying complex mathematical equations , digitalogists were always logical and reasonable individuals .
description_long: Digitalogist Digitalogists were wizard s in Zakhara who used the unique connection between mathematics and magic to create powerful formulas when they cast spells . Requirements . Due to the immense amount of time spent studying complex mathematical equations , digitalogists were always logical and reasonable individuals . Role . Digitalogists were considered by many to be the most studious of all wizards . Other wizards viewed them with admiration since only a digitalogist was able to expertly break - down a spell into its functional components in order to make it perform at a higher level of efficiency . Possessions . A digitalogist could use the same weapons that regular wizards used . They never wore armor . Benefits . These wizards possessed a greater analytical understanding of magic compared to normal wizards . Because of this they were able to cast powerful spells that they would otherwise not have access to until much later . Hindrances . Digitalogists were precise in their magical administrations . Because of this it took them longer to cast spells and longer to learn new spells . They could only use a magical scroll that was created by another digitalogist .

title: Dihl al - Suq
