description: Dihl al - Suq Dihl al - Suq , or the Northern Sea Route , was a trade route located in Zakhara in 1367 DR . The Northern Sea Route was preferred by merchants shipping goods to Hiyal , Wasat , and beyond through the Sea of Caravans . Description .
description_long: Dihl al - Suq Dihl al - Suq , or the Northern Sea Route , was a trade route located in Zakhara in 1367 DR . The Northern Sea Route was preferred by merchants shipping goods to Hiyal , Wasat , and beyond through the Sea of Caravans . Description . Cargo transported using this route departed Huzuz following the natural currents flowing to the north , avoiding the deepest sections of Suq Bay where the currents slowed . History . Suq Bay had few truly dangerous storms , but pirate activity was often a problem for vessels traveling by this route . To thwart the pirates , Golden Huzuz kept 20 heavily armed warships patrolling the bay at all times . They were tasked with hunting pirates and destroying any sea monsters they encountered .

title: Dihl al - Taif
description: Dihl al - Taif Dihl al - Taif , or the Ghost ' s Route , was a trade route located in Zakhara in 1367 DR . The portion of Dihl al - Taif found within mighty Huzuz was called the Caravan Boulevard . Description .
description_long: Dihl al - Taif Dihl al - Taif , or the Ghost ' s Route , was a trade route located in Zakhara in 1367 DR . The portion of Dihl al - Taif found within mighty Huzuz was called the Caravan Boulevard . Description . Caravans travelling by Dihl al - Taif followed Al - Sarif River east from Huzuz for 90 miles ( 145 km ) before heading north into the Haunted Lands . Another 100 miles ( 160 km ) of travel through harsh desert brought them to the small village of Zarif . Zarif was the last chance to re - supply for hundreds of miles . After departing Zarif , several days of travel brought the caravan to the Oasis of Solitude . This oasis marked the last source of fresh water before reaching Al - Malih River . A 200 mile ( 320 km ) stretch of barren wasteland greeted the caravan before the land finally began to turn green again where it met Al - Malih River , which flowed northeast directly toward Halwa for another 150 miles ( 240 km ) . History . Though rife with danger , this heavily trafficked trade route was the quickest way to transport goods between Halwa and Huzuz .

title: Dihliz
description: Dihliz Dihliz was located on the edges of Zakhara n civilization about 50 miles north from the mouth of the Nogaro River . It served as a starting point for expeditions to the ruins and jungles of the lost kingdoms of Nog and Kadar , gaining it the title of the " Gateway City " . Between the distant influences of the Grand Caliph in Huzuz and the Padishah of Afyal , corruption grew rampant , compromising the existing regulations about the export of treasures and antiquities .
description_long: Dihliz Dihliz was located on the edges of Zakhara n civilization about 50 miles north from the mouth of the Nogaro River . It served as a starting point for expeditions to the ruins and jungles of the lost kingdoms of Nog and Kadar , gaining it the title of the " Gateway City " . Between the distant influences of the Grand Caliph in Huzuz and the Padishah of Afyal , corruption grew rampant , compromising the existing regulations about the export of treasures and antiquities . Aside from plunder ( and corruption ) , the main products of Dihliz were rice and serving as a trading point to and around the Pantheon cities .

title: Diinakvil Rylafyrn
description: Diinakvil Rylafyrn Diinakvil Rylafyrn was the leader of the derro Council of Savants of Gracklstugh in 1370 DR and 1372 DR . Personality . Diinakvil was a firm supporter of the status quo and spent most of his efforts in ruining the more outrageous plots of his fellow derro savants .
description_long: Diinakvil Rylafyrn Diinakvil Rylafyrn was the leader of the derro Council of Savants of Gracklstugh in 1370 DR and 1372 DR . Personality . Diinakvil was a firm supporter of the status quo and spent most of his efforts in ruining the more outrageous plots of his fellow derro savants . His areas of expertise were dwarven history of northwest Faerûn ( duergar and shield dwarf ) , politics , and slave trading in the Underdark . History . Diinakvil was the longest - surviving member of the Council of Savants , and among the most political influential people of Gracklstugh . Some rival savants suspected that Diinakvil had some secret hold over King Tarngardt because the Deep King rarely did not follow the derro ' s suggestions . He also served under the rule of Horgar Steelshadow .

title: Diirinka
description: Diirinka Diirinka was the god of the derro , monstrous hybrids of dwarves and humans that inhabited the Underdark . His symbol was a spiral of gray , black , and white . He was a deity of magic and knowledge , as well as cruelty .
description_long: Diirinka Diirinka was the god of the derro , monstrous hybrids of dwarves and humans that inhabited the Underdark . His symbol was a spiral of gray , black , and white . He was a deity of magic and knowledge , as well as cruelty . He resided in the realm called the Hidden Betrayal on Pandemonium ' s layer of Phlegethon . Origins . Diirinka was thought to be the son between Moradin and Berronar Truesilver as well as the brother to Abbathor , Clangeddin Silverbeard , Sharindlar , Vergadain , Thard Harr , Gorm Gulthyn , Marthammor Duin , Dugmaren Brightmantle , Laduguer and Diinkarazan , in the case of the latter twin . He was banished by his father alongside his brother , though it wasn ' t clear for what . It should be noted that Diirinka might not exist , as the truth behind the Derro ' s origins was that they were a form of dwarves tortured into insanity by the illithid s . Though interestingly , worship of entities called Diirinka and Diinkarazan existed in Old Shanatar .

title: Dikanie
description: Dikanie A dikanie was a type of gigantic crab found in the Straits of Koryo between the island of Saishu and the mainland Koryo Peninsula in Kara - Tur . These orange - hued crustaceans grew to 30 – 40 feet ( 9 . 1 – 12 .
description_long: Dikanie A dikanie was a type of gigantic crab found in the Straits of Koryo between the island of Saishu and the mainland Koryo Peninsula in Kara - Tur . These orange - hued crustaceans grew to 30 – 40 feet ( 9 . 1 – 12 . 2 meters ) in length . The Straits of Koryo were famed for their huge tidal ranges and speeds . When the tide went out , an unwary sailor could find their boat beached for hours in the mud and easy prey for the dikanie .

title: Dileen Shurlef
description: Dileen Shurlef Dileen Shurlef was an assassin during the Time of Troubles . History . Shurlef was an assassin and a devoted worshiper of Bhaal who helped his god when he was cast out into the Realms in 1358 DR .
description_long: Dileen Shurlef Dileen Shurlef was an assassin during the Time of Troubles . History . Shurlef was an assassin and a devoted worshiper of Bhaal who helped his god when he was cast out into the Realms in 1358 DR . Dileen died when the god Bane called to him all the souls of the assassins .

title: Diligent Mamluk Society
description: Diligent Mamluk Society The Diligent Mamluk Society , also known as the Diligent , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . Within the Warehouse District of Huzuz , the Diligent Mamluk Society acted as a security force .
description_long: Diligent Mamluk Society The Diligent Mamluk Society , also known as the Diligent , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . Within the Warehouse District of Huzuz , the Diligent Mamluk Society acted as a security force . Though only possessing roughly 200 members , the mamluk s vigilantly guarded their masters ' property against theft and even fire on occasion . Organization . Platoons comprised of 10 guards and a single leader patroledl the streets of the Warehouse district , with 3 full platoons on duty each night . Patrol leaders would discuss and vary their routes every evening to dissuade thieves from recognizing patterns in their movements . Ethical priests of Hajama and specialized sea mage s also supported the Diligent though this assignment was often seen as " beneath them . " The sea mages came in handy when fighting fires within the Warehouse District . Possessions . The Diligent favored weapon was the khopesh sword but many also carried a katar ( punching dagger ) for close fighting . Because of the brutal heat from the sun , daytime patrols equipped themselves with standard padded armor while their nighttime counterparts favored chain mail .

title: Dillard Portyr
description: Dillard Portyr Dillard Portyr was the leading Grand Duke of Baldur ' s Gate in 1479 DR . Personality . Dillard disliked conflict , mostly for not being able to manage the stress .
description_long: Dillard Portyr Dillard Portyr was the leading Grand Duke of Baldur ' s Gate in 1479 DR . Personality . Dillard disliked conflict , mostly for not being able to manage the stress . As a leader he was a weathercock , turning wherever the wind blew him . History . Dillard was the most senior of the Grand Dukes and for this reason their unofficial leader . He survived Valarken ' s coup in 1386 DR . In 1479 DR , Dillard also survived the crisis the culminated in the resurrection of Bhaal .

title: Dimension
description: Dimension The dimension school of magic was a " school of effect " rather than one of the traditional schools of magic , which were based on philosophy . Studying dimensionalism was a " specialist " track that exploited space , time , and other dimensions to achieve success .
description_long: Dimension The dimension school of magic was a " school of effect " rather than one of the traditional schools of magic , which were based on philosophy . Studying dimensionalism was a " specialist " track that exploited space , time , and other dimensions to achieve success .

title: Dimension door
description: Dimension door Dimension door was a conjuration or alteration spell that unerringly teleported the caster and possibly other objects or creatures to a nearby location . Effects . When using " dimension door " , the caster chose a destination that the caster could see , visualize , or describe precisely in distance and / or direction , and was instantly teleported there without error .
description_long: Dimension door Dimension door was a conjuration or alteration spell that unerringly teleported the caster and possibly other objects or creatures to a nearby location . Effects . When using " dimension door " , the caster chose a destination that the caster could see , visualize , or describe precisely in distance and / or direction , and was instantly teleported there without error . For example , " onto the bough of that tree " , " back to the entrance of this mansion " , or " downward 300 ft at a 45 - degree angle to the south " were sufficient . The earliest versions of this spell had a minimum range of 630 ft ( 192 m ) that could be extended by casters of higher levels . There was also a weight limit to how much living or non - living matter the caster could take along . Before the Spellplague , the minimum range was slightly longer ( 680 ft or 207 m ) and other willing creatures ( or their weight equivalent ) could be teleported as long as they were in contact with the caster , either directly or in joined - hands fashion . The caster ' s level determined how many and what size creatures ( and their possessions ) could be teleported .

title: Dimensional anchor
description: Dimensional anchor Dimensional anchor was an abjuration or alteration spell that barred extradimensional movement . Effects . When cast , an emerald - green beam of light emitted from the caster ' s hand .
description_long: Dimensional anchor Dimensional anchor was an abjuration or alteration spell that barred extradimensional movement . Effects . When cast , an emerald - green beam of light emitted from the caster ' s hand . The newer version of this spell required the caster to make a successful ranged attack on the target , while the older version only needed line of sight to the target and contact was automatic . The creature or object targeted was completely surrounded by green radiance that prevented any transition to other planes . Affects and abilities blocked included " astral projection " , " blink " , " dimension door " , " ethereal jaunt " , " etherealness " , " gate " , " maze " , " phase door " , phasing ( like the spider ) , " plane shift " , " shadow walk " , " teleport " , and similar spell - like or psionic abilities . If a physical " gate " or " teleportation circle " was targeted , it prevented operation for the duration of the spell .

title: Dimensional thunder
description: Dimensional thunder Dimensional thunder was a teleportation spell used by swordmage s , most often those of the raging storm path , who preferred to use the forces of thunder and lightning together . With " dimensional thunder " a swordmage could cut a hole in the fabric of the Prime , slipping through into to another location , how far away depending on the swordmage ' s constitution . In the process , the swordmage brought with him or her a wake of thunderous sound , which could be deadly to nearby enemies and which boomed outward from the swordmage ' s weapon .
description_long: Dimensional thunder Dimensional thunder was a teleportation spell used by swordmage s , most often those of the raging storm path , who preferred to use the forces of thunder and lightning together . With " dimensional thunder " a swordmage could cut a hole in the fabric of the Prime , slipping through into to another location , how far away depending on the swordmage ' s constitution . In the process , the swordmage brought with him or her a wake of thunderous sound , which could be deadly to nearby enemies and which boomed outward from the swordmage ' s weapon . The sound echoed for some time afterward , causing continuous pain to a swordmage ' s adversaries . It was not an easy spell to cast , however , and could only be used once per day .

title: Dimensional warp
description: Dimensional warp Dimensional warp is a teleportation spell used by some swordmage s early on in their training . When cast , " dimensional warp " teleports up to two friendly creatures , including the caster if he or she so wishes . When the teleportation is complete the two creatures will have swapped locations , with the each standing where the other was a moment before .
description_long: Dimensional warp Dimensional warp is a teleportation spell used by some swordmage s early on in their training . When cast , " dimensional warp " teleports up to two friendly creatures , including the caster if he or she so wishes . When the teleportation is complete the two creatures will have swapped locations , with the each standing where the other was a moment before . The two creatures must be roughly the same in size . For example , the spell would not work on a human and a giant . It would , however , work on a halfling and an ogre . " Dimensional warp " requires some degree of concentration , but not as much as more powerful spells and it can be recast easily after a short rest of a few minutes or more .

title: Dimian Ree
description: Dimian Ree Dimian Ree was the baron of Morov in Damara in 1359 DR . History . In 1357 DR Dimian refused to support the army of the Barony of Bloodstone against Zhengyi , believing a suicide effort .
description_long: Dimian Ree Dimian Ree was the baron of Morov in Damara in 1359 DR . History . In 1357 DR Dimian refused to support the army of the Barony of Bloodstone against Zhengyi , believing a suicide effort . However Gareth Dragonsbane managed to truly defeat the Witch - King , gaining immense support . Dimian worked very hard to regain support after that move . In 1359 he had regained his position and was the principal claimant to the throne alongside Gareth Dragonsbane . In oder to gain more support Dimian deeply secretly approached the Grandfather of Assassins . Personality . Dimian was a cruel and ruthless individual , always in search of power and would stop at nothing to achieve it . He claimed to worship Ilmater but was only a facade to win the allegiance of the Damara n people . Relationships . Dimian was distantly related to the royal family . He was cousin of Tarkos Ree , head of the Tightpurse thieves guild . Dimian ' s best ally was the baroness Sylvia of Ostel .

title: Dimon
description: Dimon Dimon was the tharchion of Tyraturos in the realm of Thay and also a priest of Bane . Appearance . Dimon had fairer skin than most Mulan .
description_long: Dimon Dimon was the tharchion of Tyraturos in the realm of Thay and also a priest of Bane . Appearance . Dimon had fairer skin than most Mulan . Blue veins showed across his shaven head . He wore the black gauntlet emblematic of his order . Importance . Dimon housed the council of zulkir s during the war of Thay in 1385 DR . During one of their meetings , Dimon was attacked by the bored Nevron , who conjured an advespa to kill the priest . Suddenly , Bane took possession of his worshiper and endured the attack of the devil , in the end killing it with Dimon ' s hands . Bane encouraged the zulkirs to fight Szass Tam again at the Keep of Sorrows under cover of the magic - crippling effect of the Spellplague . However , after the god disappeared , Dimon died from the wounds inflicted by the advespa .

title: Dimswart
description: Dimswart Lord Dimswart was one of the leading sages in service to the royalty of Cormyr in Suzail . Appearance . Dimswart was short and stout , with gray hair and sparkling blue eyes .
description_long: Dimswart Lord Dimswart was one of the leading sages in service to the royalty of Cormyr in Suzail . Appearance . Dimswart was short and stout , with gray hair and sparkling blue eyes . History . In 1369 DR , Dimswart was called to aid in the abraxus affair . He determined that the affliction was a venom that spread a blood disease resistant to conventional magic , causing internal organ damage . Possessions . Dimswart carries a large black satchel with silver latches .

title: Dimwold
description: Dimwold Dimwold was a fire mephit in the service of Orcus in the Abyss in 1357 DR . Activities . Dimwold acted as a messenger between the balor commander Ter - soth and the palace of Orcus but often he was very lazy .
description_long: Dimwold Dimwold was a fire mephit in the service of Orcus in the Abyss in 1357 DR . Activities . Dimwold acted as a messenger between the balor commander Ter - soth and the palace of Orcus but often he was very lazy . History . At one point , Ter - soth reported that Dimwold was bad in his work and the mephit was punished being confined to the mountains . In 1357 DR , he was waiting for the occasion to avenge this and maybe advance himself . Personality . Dimwold was bored of his work . He considered himself a genius , destined to rule like a demon lord . He waiting for the right occasion to advance himself . He hated Ter - soth . He always acted for his self - interest , betraying anyone .

title: Dinam
description: Dinam Dinam was a member of the Dukars of Myth Nantar in Serôs in 1370 DR . Personality . Dinam , on the surface , was a polite , well - mannered , individual but with people he trusted he showed his ribald sense of humor and total trust in his companions .
description_long: Dinam Dinam was a member of the Dukars of Myth Nantar in Serôs in 1370 DR . Personality . Dinam , on the surface , was a polite , well - mannered , individual but with people he trusted he showed his ribald sense of humor and total trust in his companions . He believed he had been reborn into the Dukars and his goal was to help preserve the Nantarn Alliance great . History . Dinam was a noble hailing from Sembia who went on adventures . In 1361 DR , during a voyage over the Sea of Fallen Stars , his ship was attacked by pirates and he fell overboard just north of the Whamite Isles . Dinam woke up in Myth Nantar without memory of his life on the surface . Soon , Qos entrusted Dinam with becoming one of the first Dukars of the Order of Maalirn . In 1370 DR , Dinam , with his companions Paxas and Ka ' ioa ' Tara , were guiding ships attacked by Myth Nantar ' s " mythal " away from the city and toward the Shipwreck Plains . In one of the ships they discovered surface dwellers .

title: Dinin Do ' Urden
description: Dinin Do ' Urden Dinin Do ' Urden was a drow fighter of House Do ' Urden of Menzoberranzan . He later became a drider . History .
description_long: Dinin Do ' Urden Dinin Do ' Urden was a drow fighter of House Do ' Urden of Menzoberranzan . He later became a drider . History . House Do ' Urden . In 1297 DR , secondboy Dinin accompanied the soldiers of House Do ' Urden in a successful attack on House DeVir . During the battle , Dinin took advantage of an opportune moment to distract his older brother , Nalfein Do ' Urden , and put a sword in his back . Dinin then ascended to become elderboy of House Do ' Urden . That action fortuitously saved the life of newborn Drizzt Do ' Urden , who was to be sacrificed to Lolth as the third living son ; Nalfein ' s death was deemed an acceptable sacrifice instead . Twenty years later , Dinin became a master at Melee - Magthere , the drow academy for fighters . He watched over his younger brother , Drizzt Do ' Urden , and was a member of the same training patrol , along with Masoj Hun ' ett and Berg ' inyon Baenre . In one of their excursions into the Underdark , Dinin cut off both hands of the svirfneblin Belwar Dissengulp , sparing his life only after Drizzt convinced him that the gnome could return home as an example to those that cross the path of the drow .

title: Dinnom Baraizal
description: Dinnom Baraizal Dinnom Baraizal was one of the ten Cloakmasters of Athkatla for the Shadow Thieves around 1370 DR . History . Dinnom was only a passable assassin , but in 1368 DR he was promoted by Rheax Bormul to the position of Cloakmaster of the Bridge district of Athkatla and proved a good choice .
description_long: Dinnom Baraizal Dinnom Baraizal was one of the ten Cloakmasters of Athkatla for the Shadow Thieves around 1370 DR . History . Dinnom was only a passable assassin , but in 1368 DR he was promoted by Rheax Bormul to the position of Cloakmaster of the Bridge district of Athkatla and proved a good choice . Personality . Dinnom was only a mediocre assassin but proved to be an excellent planner and administrator . He made a blood oath with Rheax , which ensured his loyalty to Rheax . Dinnom actually had no intentions of betraying Rheax , who was his patron and whom he respected .

title: Dioptase
description: Dioptase Dioptase , also known as diopside , was a small semi - precious stone that had unusual healing properties . Description . These deep emerald - green stones were typically found in small crystals that were riddled with flaws and only yielded tiny faceted gems .
description_long: Dioptase Dioptase , also known as diopside , was a small semi - precious stone that had unusual healing properties . Description . These deep emerald - green stones were typically found in small crystals that were riddled with flaws and only yielded tiny faceted gems . Because dioptase was soft and brittle , it found uses in items that were not expected to be subject to rough handling , such as decorating figurines or fancy lace . Larger specimens were extremely rare and commanded higher prices . A typical stone had a base value of 50 gp . Powers . Dioptase gems could be used to make a potion that acted similar to a " potion of healing " . They dissolved in any liquid that was actively enchanted with any spell . The process took about twenty minutes to complete , and the liquid had to stay enchanted for at least that amount of time . For every dioptase gem dissolved , the potion would restore a minimum amount of health to the creature that drank it .

title: Dirana
description: Dirana Dirana was a member of the Cult of the Crushing Wave at the Fane of the Eye under Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . History . In 1491 DR , Dirana lived at the Temple of the Crushing Wave in Tyar - Besil .
description_long: Dirana Dirana was a member of the Cult of the Crushing Wave at the Fane of the Eye under Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . History . In 1491 DR , Dirana lived at the Temple of the Crushing Wave in Tyar - Besil . However , she was captured in a skirmish by the Cult of the Eternal Flame and put in a jail in the Fane ' s Eternal Flame section until some adventurers infiltrated the fane and defeated the earth cultists and found her .

title: Dire Whiner
description: Dire Whiner The Dire Whiner was a female demon in Abyss in 1357 DR . Activities . The Dire Whiner lived in a swamp in the Layers of the Abyss ruled by Orcus .
description_long: Dire Whiner The Dire Whiner was a female demon in Abyss in 1357 DR . Activities . The Dire Whiner lived in a swamp in the Layers of the Abyss ruled by Orcus . She obtained food , treasure , and other necessities by using her special abilities to whine , complain , and put down , which were magically powered insults , upon demon s , mephit s , and other inhabitants of the layer .

title: Dire Wood
description: Dire Wood The Dire Wood was a part of the High Forest . Geography . It was defined by a ring of completely albino oak trees surrounding the hills in the eastern High Forest .
description_long: Dire Wood The Dire Wood was a part of the High Forest . Geography . It was defined by a ring of completely albino oak trees surrounding the hills in the eastern High Forest . Inside the outer ring of pale oaks stood a thicker ring of blackened and petrified trees . Within the rings , normal trees and heavy undergrowth were mixed with petrified trees , all sprouting from reddish soil . History . A single red stone butte at the base of a high cliff was all that remained of the fallen body of Karsus , made gigantic by the divine energy he stole . Notable locations . Contained within the Dire Wood was the ruins of Karse , a Netheril settlement .

title: Dire bat
description: Dire bat Dire bats were giant bats the size of horses . Description . Dire bats averaged 200 pounds ( 90 kilograms ) and had leathery wings that stretched fifteen feet ( 4 .
description_long: Dire bat Dire bats were giant bats the size of horses . Description . Dire bats averaged 200 pounds ( 90 kilograms ) and had leathery wings that stretched fifteen feet ( 4 . 6 meters ) from end to end . Their bodies were covered in shaggy fur . Behavior . Dire bats hunted at night and rested during the day . They were stealthy and used echolocation to locate prey . These bats were easy to startle and tended to kill or drive away any other encountered creatures with their bite . Ecology . Dire bats flourished in the deepest regions of the Underdark . Reputation . Dire bats were favored by the orc god Shargaas . They were used as mounts by members of the Shadovar military and Zhentarim skymage s . Shield dwarves of Oghrann in the Upperdark kept large populations of dire bats to use as mounts as well .

title: Dire bear
description: Dire bear A dire bear was a huge version of the typical bear . Description . Most dire bears were 12 ft ( 3 .
description_long: Dire bear A dire bear was a huge version of the typical bear . Description . Most dire bears were 12 ft ( 3 . 7 m ) long and weighed as much as 8 , 000 lb ( 3 . 6 tons ) . Combat . Dire bears ripped at opponents with their claws and could also bite . When the prey was grabbed , the massive bear would maul the creature with its ursine strength . Personality . Being omnivorous , dire bears usually did not bother to attack creatures unless they were defending a food source or a personal domain . Dire bears were wild beast s , though , and would feast on human flesh as readily as any other game animal . Ecology . These bears lived in small groups or preferred to be alone . Many humanoid s would train bears to act as guards or pets , such as hill giant s and ettin s .

title: Dire boar
description: Dire boar Dire boars were omnivores and spent much of their time searching for food . Unlike ordinary pigs , dire boars were vicious and would attack any creature that approached . Combat .
description_long: Dire boar Dire boars were omnivores and spent much of their time searching for food . Unlike ordinary pigs , dire boars were vicious and would attack any creature that approached . Combat . In combat , dire boars attempted to charge their opponent and gore it with their tusks .

title: Dire charm
description: Dire charm Dire charm was an enchantment spell that caused one person to go on a murderous rampage . Effects . Similar to " charm person " , this spell worked on humanoid creatures of medium size or smaller .
description_long: Dire charm Dire charm was an enchantment spell that caused one person to go on a murderous rampage . Effects . Similar to " charm person " , this spell worked on humanoid creatures of medium size or smaller . The spell operated by making the subject believe they really enjoyed killing , whereupon they would immediately attack with berserker fury the nearest person other than the caster , friend or foe . The subject used the quickest and deadliest means available and continued until all potential targets were eliminated . If no targets were available , the subject reverted to normal behavior as if nothing was wrong . If a new target was spotted before the spell expired , the subject again launched an attack with intent to kill . The subject of this spell would not attack the caster unless the caster attacked the subject , in which case the subject would single - mindedly attempt to kill the caster and no one else . Components . Verbal , somatic , and material components were required to cast this spell . History . This spell was revealed in the publication Volo ' s Guide to All Things Magical .

title: Dire corby
description: Dire corby Dire corbies were a mutated semi - humanoid horrors that were once flightless birds . They were common to the southern reaches of the Underdark . Description .
description_long: Dire corby Dire corbies were a mutated semi - humanoid horrors that were once flightless birds . They were common to the southern reaches of the Underdark . Description . Dire corbies were bipedal and black skinned . They possessed a beaked bird ' s head , the torso of a man , and were both featherless and wingless . Both of their powerful - looking arms ended in hooked , wicked claws , and their legs ended in a three - toed foot . Belwar Dissengulp remarked that dire corbies look like a drow - bird crossbreed . History . Dire corbies were known to inhabit one of the vaults in Gauntlgrym around 1479 DR .

title: Dire flail
description: Dire flail The dire flail was a two - handed , exotic melee weapon that could be used as a double weapon . Description . A dire flail was essentially two flail s mounted on either end of a stout haft shorter than a quarterstaff .
description_long: Dire flail The dire flail was a two - handed , exotic melee weapon that could be used as a double weapon . Description . A dire flail was essentially two flail s mounted on either end of a stout haft shorter than a quarterstaff . The chains that attached the spiked metal balls or metal rods were longer than those of a normal flail but shorter than on a heavy flail . An average dire flail cost 90 gp and weighed 10 lbs ( 4 . 5 kg ) . Combat . The dire flail was a double weapon that could be used as if fighting with two separate weapons when wielded two - handed . The chains of this and other members of the flail family were particularly good for entangling enemy weapons and disarming them . The dire flail could also be used to make trip attacks . Notable wielders . Notable wielders of dire flails were : Notable dire flails . One form of " Kozah ' s Needle " was a three - section bar connected by chains , otherwise known as a dire threshing flail . See Polearm # Special Cases .

title: Dire lion
description: Dire lion A dire lion was a larger cousins of the lion . Description . Dire lions could grow as large as fifteen feet long and weigh as much as 3 , 500 pounds .
description_long: Dire lion A dire lion was a larger cousins of the lion . Description . Dire lions could grow as large as fifteen feet long and weigh as much as 3 , 500 pounds . They resembled normal lions in that they had tawny fur with spots and that the males had short manes . They differed from normal lions in having bony spine and brow ridges . Behavior . Dire lions showed similar behavior to normal lions in how they patiently stalked their prey , yet they would take on much larger creatures . They liked to hide in tall grass or heavy undergrowth . Combat . Like normal lions , dire lions would rush at and pounce upon their prey , clinging to it with their powerful jaws and clawing with all four paws . Ecology . Dire lions were found as sole individuals , in pairs , or as small prides of between six and ten animals . Reputation . Cloud giant s often kept dire lions as pets or guardians . Powerful druid s or ranger s were known to have such animals as companions .

title: Dire radiance
description: Dire radiance Dire radiance is among the most basic spell s known to warlock s of the star pact . " Dire radiance " , when cast , allows the warlock to call forth a shaft of brilliant , chilling light from the heavens , using it to cause excruciating pain to a creature within fifty feet . If the creature attempts to approach the warlock , the beam intensifies , causing even greater pain .
description_long: Dire radiance Dire radiance is among the most basic spell s known to warlock s of the star pact . " Dire radiance " , when cast , allows the warlock to call forth a shaft of brilliant , chilling light from the heavens , using it to cause excruciating pain to a creature within fifty feet . If the creature attempts to approach the warlock , the beam intensifies , causing even greater pain . The potency of " dire radiance " is largely determined by the constitution of the warlock casting it and warlocks of great experience and power cast a significantly more powerful version of the spell .

title: Dire rat
description: Dire rat Dire rats were dangerous creatures . They were much larger than the common rat and were found in dungeons and city sewers . The bite of these creatures carried a potentially lethal disease known as filth fever .
description_long: Dire rat Dire rats were dangerous creatures . They were much larger than the common rat and were found in dungeons and city sewers . The bite of these creatures carried a potentially lethal disease known as filth fever . Locations . Dire rats could be found in the wild in the Silver Marches , particularly in the Rauvin Vale and Sundabar Vale , as well as in the High Forest . Appendix . Trivia . A dire rat could be summoned as an animal companion in " Neverwinter Nights " .

title: Dire tiger
description: Dire tiger Dire tigers , also called smilodons , were giant cats with a pair of huge fangs jutting from their powerful jaws . Due to these teeth , they were often referred to as saber - toothed tigers . Dire tigers preyed on just about anything that moved .
description_long: Dire tiger Dire tigers , also called smilodons , were giant cats with a pair of huge fangs jutting from their powerful jaws . Due to these teeth , they were often referred to as saber - toothed tigers . Dire tigers preyed on just about anything that moved . They would patiently stalk a potential meal , striking whenever the creature let down its guard . Physical description . Dire tigers grew to be over 12 feet long and could weigh up to 6 , 000 pounds . Combat . A dire tiger attacked by running at prey , leaping , and clawing and biting as it raked with its rear claws .

title: Dire weasel
description: Dire weasel Dire weasels were larger , more - aggressive versions of normal weasels . Physical description . Dire weasels had sleek , long bodies up to ten feet long and could reach a weight of 700 pounds .
description_long: Dire weasel Dire weasels were larger , more - aggressive versions of normal weasels . Physical description . Dire weasels had sleek , long bodies up to ten feet long and could reach a weight of 700 pounds . Combat . Dire weasels were nocturnal and stalked their prey , leaping upon it and latching on with their blood - draining bite .

title: Dire wolf
description: Dire wolf A dire wolf was a dire version of a grey wolf , being a larger and more primitive or feral breed of wolf . Description . Dire wolves grew to about 9 feet ( 2 .
description_long: Dire wolf A dire wolf was a dire version of a grey wolf , being a larger and more primitive or feral breed of wolf . Description . Dire wolves grew to about 9 feet ( 2 . 7 meters ) long and weighed up to 800 pounds ( 363 kilograms ) , about the size of a horse . Their fur was thick and a mottled grey or black in color , and they had fiery eyes . Behavior . Dire wolves were far more aggressive than normal wolves , attacking and killing anything they could catch . They could be found singly as lone wolves or in packs numbering five to eight dire wolves . Ecology . They could generally be found in temperate forest environments . Abilities . They had keen senses , including a sharp sense of smell , allowing them to track their prey by scent . They could also move stealthily on the hunt . Combat . Dire wolves fought in packs , fighting efficiently and surrounding their prey and flanking it to gain an advantage . Their bite was their only weapon , but they could drag a creature to the ground once they had gotten a hold of them . History . In the Year of the Prince , 1357 DR , Conner and a young boy were traveling on a moor when fog swept in and they were beset by starving dire wolves .

title: Director
description: Director Directors were beholder abominations that served as hive shock troops . Activities . A director ' s primary function was as a cavalry fighter .
description_long: Director Directors were beholder abominations that served as hive shock troops . Activities . A director ' s primary function was as a cavalry fighter . They possessed a mind - link with specialized riding animals . The director was extremely large , being around 9 ft . ( 2 . 7 m ) in diameter . Its central eye was proportionately smaller than that of a true beholder . Directors possessed only six eyestalks atop their bodies and three clawed tentacles located on their undersides . They used these tentacles to ride their mounts .

title: Direguard
description: Direguard A direguard was a more powerful version of a baneguard created by cleric s of Cyric ( and later , Iyachtu Xvim , Velsharoon , and others ) , lich es , and death knight s . After the Spellplague , there were two known varieties : the direguard deathbringer and the direguard assassin . Description .
description_long: Direguard A direguard was a more powerful version of a baneguard created by cleric s of Cyric ( and later , Iyachtu Xvim , Velsharoon , and others ) , lich es , and death knight s . After the Spellplague , there were two known varieties : the direguard deathbringer and the direguard assassin . Description . While baneguards looked like normal undead skeletons , direguards had flames of red burning in their eye sockets and shadowy black armor through which their bones could be seen . Direguard deathbringers had glowing claws that crackled with force . Direguard assassins were shrouded in shadow and manifested a glowing red blade in their hand . Personality . Direguards were of average intelligence and capable of creative , independent thought and actions that did not contradict the orders given to them by their creator . They were not able to speak and were wholly evil . Combat . Direguards had all the abilities of a baneguard ( able to shoot " magic missile s " and " blink " ) plus they could " see invisible and ethereal " creatures . The shadowy aura that surrounded them gave them extra armor in combat . Direguards could use any normal weapon or attack barehanded .

title: Dirs
description: Dirs Dirs , or the Jaw - Tooth , was a rocky island located in the Nada al - Hazan achipelago within the Crowded Sea . Geography . This island was covered with rocky outcroppings and dried grasses , making in rather inhospitable to humans .
description_long: Dirs Dirs , or the Jaw - Tooth , was a rocky island located in the Nada al - Hazan achipelago within the Crowded Sea . Geography . This island was covered with rocky outcroppings and dried grasses , making in rather inhospitable to humans . Inhabitants . This island was home to a group of skilled hunting falcons . These falcons were so prized that they were given as gifts to sultans , caliphs , and even kings beyond the borders of Zakhara . No settlements were found on the island of Dirs because of the presence of the hunting birds ' fierce protectors : the maskhi . The maskhi only trusted the Ben Nabil family from Bandar al - Sa ' adat . Once per year they were allowed to collect a few of the falcons and train them .

title: Disc of secrets
description: Disc of secrets A disc of secrets was an un holy symbol of Shar that bore an illusion to conceal its appearance , allowing a Sharran cleric to hide their true allegiance . Description . The " disc of secrets " normally appeared to be a blank silver disc on an ordinary silver chain .
description_long: Disc of secrets A disc of secrets was an un holy symbol of Shar that bore an illusion to conceal its appearance , allowing a Sharran cleric to hide their true allegiance . Description . The " disc of secrets " normally appeared to be a blank silver disc on an ordinary silver chain . Beneath this illusion was an unholy symbol of Shar , a black disc of jet within a ring of purple amethyst s . Powers . A shadow illusion was laid on the " disc of secrets " ; this was partially real and could not be disbelieved . The command phrase , " Reveal your secret to no one " , ironically revealed its true appearance . In all respects , a " disc of secrets " served as an unholy symbol of Shar in the hands of one of her clerics . The magic ' s only purpose was to conceal this fact . Uniquely , a " disc of secrets " belonging to Shan Thar , a cleric of Cyric , bore a second illusion . Speaking the command word " lies " after the first command phrase caused the jawless white skull to appear within the black disc . Creation . Fashioning a " disc of secrets " required knowledge of the " shadow conjuration " spell and a mastery of Shadow Weave magic . History .

title: Discern lies
description: Discern lies Discern lies , also known as detect lie , was a divination spell that reveals deliberate falsehoods . Effect . Each round , you concentrate on one subject , who must be in range .
description_long: Discern lies Discern lies , also known as detect lie , was a divination spell that reveals deliberate falsehoods . Effect . Each round , you concentrate on one subject , who must be in range . You know if the subject deliberately and knowingly speaks a lie by discerning disturbances in her aura caused by lying . The spell does not reveal the truth , uncover unintentional inaccuracies , or necessarily reveal evasions . Each round , you may concentrate on a different subject . The reversed form , undetectable lie , protected against magical detection of lies spoken by the target for 24 hours .

title: Discern location
description: Discern location Discern location is a divination spell that determines the exact location of a creature or object . Effects . A " discern location " spell is among the most powerful means of locating creatures or objects .
description_long: Discern location Discern location is a divination spell that determines the exact location of a creature or object . Effects . A " discern location " spell is among the most powerful means of locating creatures or objects . Nothing short of the direct intervention of a deity keeps you from learning the exact location of a single individual or object . Discern location circumvents normal means of protection from scrying or location . The spell reveals the name of the location ( place , name , business name , building name , or the like ) , community , county ( or similar political division ) , country , continent , and plane where the subject lies . To find a creature with the spell , you must have seen the creature or have some item that once belonged to it . To find an object , you must have touched the object at least once .

title: Disciples of St . Sollars the Twice - Martyred
description: Disciples of St . Sollars the Twice - Martyred The Disciples of St . Sollars the Twice - Martyred , also known as the Order of the Yellow Rose or the Monks of the Yellow Rose , was a monastic order devoted to St .
description_long: Disciples of St . Sollars the Twice - Martyred The Disciples of St . Sollars the Twice - Martyred , also known as the Order of the Yellow Rose or the Monks of the Yellow Rose , was a monastic order devoted to St . Sollars and Ilmater , The One Who Endures . They were noted for the Monastery of the Yellow Rose , located high in the Earthspur Mountains near to the Glacier of the White Worm . Dogma . As followers of Ilmater , the Disciples of St . Sollars were ascetics and favored the simpler things , but were devoted to creating beauty in hardship . The monks did not attempt to force their ways or beliefs on others . Instead , they went about their business confident in their faith . The Disciples of St . Sollars were known as loyal allies and as dangerous enemies . They were highly respected on issues of truth and diplomacy and for their inner strength . Dwelling on the Glacier of the White Worm , the monks shared their home with a terrible beast : the remorhaz or white worm . This was a massive , insectoid creature , some 20 feet ( 6 . 1 meters ) long , aggressive and predatory , that could tunnel through ice and earth and generated extreme heat from its body .

title: Disciples of the White Rod
description: Disciples of the White Rod The Disciples of the White Rod were a monastic order of the faith of Loviatar . All monk s of the faith were members of the order . They were based out of an abbey near Calimport .
description_long: Disciples of the White Rod The Disciples of the White Rod were a monastic order of the faith of Loviatar . All monk s of the faith were members of the order . They were based out of an abbey near Calimport . They were named after a token bestowed on the order ' s founder by the goddess herself . It was kept as a holy relic at their abbey .

title: Disguise self
description: Disguise self Disguise self , also known as change self , was an illusion spell that changed one ' s appearance . This spell was originally called Quantoul ' s changer in the days of the first Netherese empire . Effects .
description_long: Disguise self Disguise self , also known as change self , was an illusion spell that changed one ' s appearance . This spell was originally called Quantoul ' s changer in the days of the first Netherese empire . Effects . The caster ' s appearance changed , including facial features , skin , clothing , armor , weapons , and accoutrements . The caster could appear up to 1 ft ( 30 cm ) shorter or taller , thin , fat , or in between . The caster could not change body type , i . e . , a human caster had to stay generally humanoid - shaped and bipedal . Otherwise , the extent of the apparent change was at the discretion of the caster , ranging from an obscure feature to an entirely new look . Skin blemishes , scars , facial hair , hair color , complexion , and gender changes were all possible . " Disguise self " did not disguise the caster ' s voice nor change the audible properties of armor or equipment . Chain mail could be made to look like a leather , but it would still sound like chain mail when the caster moved . Likewise , the tactile properties of materials were not altered . If someone slapped you on the back , they would feel chain mail and not leather .

title: Disguise undead
description: Disguise undead Disguise undead was an arcane spell that crossed multiple schools of magic including alteration , illusion , and necromancy . It altered the appearance of one or more undead creatures so they could pass for live , healthy creatures . A less effective but easier to learn illusion - only spell by the same name was later developed .
description_long: Disguise undead Disguise undead was an arcane spell that crossed multiple schools of magic including alteration , illusion , and necromancy . It altered the appearance of one or more undead creatures so they could pass for live , healthy creatures . A less effective but easier to learn illusion - only spell by the same name was later developed . Effects . The number of undead creatures that could be affected by the earlier versions of this spell was equal to the level of the spellcaster . Each target grew flesh , organs , hair , and skin to resemble what they looked like when alive and healthy , although if deformed in life then the disguise included those deformities . The flesh looked and felt as expected for the type of creature , although it did not bleed , sweat , or smell . No abilities were granted to a target . If it could not speak while undead , then this spell did not grant the ability of speech , " etc . " Abilities that relied on smell or appearance , such as the nausea - inducing odor of a ghast or a fear - inducing visage , were negated by this spell . The spell took a full ten minutes to cast and lasted ten minutes per level of the caster .

title: Dishdashah
description: Dishdashah A dishdashah was a type of clothing worn in Zakhara . Description . Dishdashahs were simple tunics that were often worn by farmers or poor merchants .
description_long: Dishdashah A dishdashah was a type of clothing worn in Zakhara . Description . Dishdashahs were simple tunics that were often worn by farmers or poor merchants . Length varied down to the knees or ankles . They were held tight by a sash or rope . Prices . Dishdashahs could be purchased for 6 – 12 silver piece s .

title: Disintegrate
description: Disintegrate Disintegrate , originally called Aksa ' s disintegrate , was an alteration or transmutation spell that created a thin green ray that made a creature or a object of a certain size vanish , or be reduced to ash or dust . Effect . Older versions of " disintegrate " made the target disappear no matter if it was a creature , or magical matter , or a 1 " cubic volume of other material .
description_long: Disintegrate Disintegrate , originally called Aksa ' s disintegrate , was an alteration or transmutation spell that created a thin green ray that made a creature or a object of a certain size vanish , or be reduced to ash or dust . Effect . Older versions of " disintegrate " made the target disappear no matter if it was a creature , or magical matter , or a 1 " cubic volume of other material . The newer versions spell struck and injured a target , and if killed , the ray caused the creature to disintegrate into a pile of fine dust , although any equipment was not affected . The ray could also disintegrate as much as one 10 - foot - cube of nonliving matter , even objects constructed entirely of force , but it could not affect magical effects , such as a " globe of invulnerability " . Only one creature or object could be affected per casting . The spell has a range of over 100 ' ( 30 m ) . Material components . In order to cast the spell , the caster had to use a lodestone and a pinch of dust . History . The spell was invented by the Netherese arcanist Aksa the Destroyer in −2095 DR .

title: Dismal Caverns
description: Dismal Caverns Dismal Caverns was an Astral dominion in the World Axis cosmology model . Prior to the Spellplague it was known as Deep Caverns in the World Tree cosmology model . It was the home plane of the Great Mother , Ilsensine , Laogzed , and Ghaunadaur .
description_long: Dismal Caverns Dismal Caverns was an Astral dominion in the World Axis cosmology model . Prior to the Spellplague it was known as Deep Caverns in the World Tree cosmology model . It was the home plane of the Great Mother , Ilsensine , Laogzed , and Ghaunadaur . Description . This plane was a great solid mass of rock perforated by caverns , chasms , and tunnels of all sizes . There was no sky and no light except for that given off by luminous fungi and molten lava flows . Portions of the Caverns were subject to swift winds that howled through the maze of tunnels . Mapping the labyrinth of tunnels was completely impossible because within the demesnes of the deities the passageways and walls obeyed their will and could open , close , change direction , or collapse on an infernal whim . Inhabitants . Dismal Caverns was the afterlife destination of most beholder , illithid , and troglodyte petitioners , and they appeared here much the same as they had in life . Their behavior was also similar as in their former lives and the disparate groups viewed each other with disdain , hatred , or animosity .

title: Dismind
description: Dismind Dismind was an arcane enchantment spell that disassociated an individual ' s mind from their body , leaving the body in an invulnerable state of suspended animation , usually as a final escape from a deadly situation . The reverse of this spell , known as restore mind , reunited the body with the absent mind and had other beneficial uses . Effects .
description_long: Dismind Dismind was an arcane enchantment spell that disassociated an individual ' s mind from their body , leaving the body in an invulnerable state of suspended animation , usually as a final escape from a deadly situation . The reverse of this spell , known as restore mind , reunited the body with the absent mind and had other beneficial uses . Effects . Upon uttering the incantation of this spell , the mind of the caster , or the creature he or she touched , became free from the body to wander aimlessly about the Prime Material Plane ( or whatever plane the body was on , presumably ) . It drifted randomly , undetectable and unassailable by any known means including psionics . While in this state , the mind was not fully conscious . It could not direct its movement or focus on anything in particular and its memory of everything it experienced was unreliable . Meanwhile , the body was instantly encased in an invulnerable field of magical force that perfectly preserved it in its current state and position .

title: Dismissal
description: Dismissal Dismissal , also known as abjure , was an abjuration spell that could send an extraplanar creature back to its plane of origin . Effects . If the caster overcame the target ' s magic resistance ( if any ) , then a momentary battle of wills ensued where the outcome was influenced by the relative difference in experience levels between the caster and the target .
description_long: Dismissal Dismissal , also known as abjure , was an abjuration spell that could send an extraplanar creature back to its plane of origin . Effects . If the caster overcame the target ' s magic resistance ( if any ) , then a momentary battle of wills ensued where the outcome was influenced by the relative difference in experience levels between the caster and the target . If the caster failed , then nothing happened , but if the caster succeeded then the creature was instantly banished from the plane of existence the creature and caster were on , back to its home plane . The caster had no control over where on the destination plane the creature would land , and indeed the newer version of this spell sometimes sent the creature to a plane that was not its home plane . The older version of this spell was rather harsh in that the banished creature could suffer system shock from being wrenched out of one existence and into another . Components . The newer version of this spell required the caster ' s holy symbol or divine focus and also verbal and somatic components .

title: Dispater
description: Dispater Dispater was an archdevil of the Nine Hells , and the Lord of the Iron City of Dis . Paranoid and reclusive , he never leaves his inner sanctum . He was always stoic , emotionless , and expressionless .
description_long: Dispater Dispater was an archdevil of the Nine Hells , and the Lord of the Iron City of Dis . Paranoid and reclusive , he never leaves his inner sanctum . He was always stoic , emotionless , and expressionless . He remained this way constantly even in the heat of battle . History . Dispater , along with Mephistopheles , were once allies of Mammon , but Mammon betrayed them both .

title: Dispel chaos
description: Dispel chaos Dispel chaos was an abjuration spell that worked exactly like " dispel evil " except it affected chaotic spells and creatures instead of evil ones . Effects . The effects of this spell were the same as " dispel evil " except the aura surrounding the spellcaster was a solid , unwavering blue and made of lawful energy .
description_long: Dispel chaos Dispel chaos was an abjuration spell that worked exactly like " dispel evil " except it affected chaotic spells and creatures instead of evil ones . Effects . The effects of this spell were the same as " dispel evil " except the aura surrounding the spellcaster was a solid , unwavering blue and made of lawful energy . Components . Verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell plus the caster ' s ( un ) holy symbol or divine focus .

title: Dispel evil
description: Dispel evil Dispel evil was an abjuration spell that protected the caster from evil attacks , could banish summoned evil creatures , or dispel enchantments cast by evil spellcasters . The reverse of this spell , dispel good , had the same effects on good attacks , creatures , and enchantments . Effects .
description_long: Dispel evil Dispel evil was an abjuration spell that protected the caster from evil attacks , could banish summoned evil creatures , or dispel enchantments cast by evil spellcasters . The reverse of this spell , dispel good , had the same effects on good attacks , creatures , and enchantments . Effects . The newer versions of this spell had three possible effects , the oldest version had only two . All versions made it very difficult for a creature of evil alignment to successfully attack the caster . This lasted for the duration of the spell , or until another effect was used , whichever came first . While the spell was in effect , a bright white field of holy energy shimmered around the caster . All versions also allowed the caster a chance to banish an evil creature , but varied on what manner of creatures could be affected . The two older versions worked on evil summoned creatures , or any monster that was forced to do evil deeds . These included aerial servant s , demon s , devil s , djinn , elementals , invisible stalker s , and creatures or monsters summoned by " animal summoning I " or " monster summoning I " and the like .

title: Dispel evil and good
description: Dispel evil and good Dispel evil and good was an abjuration spell that granted protection from fey , undead , and monsters from beyond the Prime Material Plane . Effects . For a minute , the caster was covered in shimmering light that created a disadvantage for attacking celestial , elemental , fey , and fiend creatures targeting the caster .
description_long: Dispel evil and good Dispel evil and good was an abjuration spell that granted protection from fey , undead , and monsters from beyond the Prime Material Plane . Effects . For a minute , the caster was covered in shimmering light that created a disadvantage for attacking celestial , elemental , fey , and fiend creatures targeting the caster . The caster could use the spell to " break enchantment " and lose the spell but touching a creature that was charmed , frightened or possessed by a creature that the spell defended against made the target lose those conditions . The caster could also use the spell to use " dismissal " on a creature that the spell defended against . This would attempt to send the creature back to its plane of origin ( unless it was already there ) . Undead and fey who were not on their home planes were sent to the Shadowfell and the Feywild , respectively . The spell would then be lost . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required holy water or powdered silver and iron .

title: Dispel fatigue
description: Dispel fatigue Dispel fatigue was a necromancy spell that alleviated weariness and exhaustion in the recipient . Effects . One creature within a range of 90 ft ( 27 .
description_long: Dispel fatigue Dispel fatigue was a necromancy spell that alleviated weariness and exhaustion in the recipient . Effects . One creature within a range of 90 ft ( 27 . 4 m ) could be reinvigorated by this spell . All effects of physical and mental exertion were removed , leaving the subject fully rested and refreshed . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a sprinkling of springwater that had been " bless ed " .

title: Dispel fog
description: Dispel fog Dispel fog was an arcane abjuration spell that removed mist and fog from an area around the caster . Effects . This spell took one minute to cast and cleared a circular area with a radius of at least 50 ft ( 15 m ) .
description_long: Dispel fog Dispel fog was an arcane abjuration spell that removed mist and fog from an area around the caster . Effects . This spell took one minute to cast and cleared a circular area with a radius of at least 50 ft ( 15 m ) . More experienced casters could increase that radius . Any natural or magical fog or mist in the area was permanently destroyed and the area remained clear for at least 50 minutes ( again , longer for more experienced casters ) , after which it could be replaced by generating more or merely blowing in from elsewhere . Creatures in mist form , such as vampire s , caught in the area of effect were either forced to transform out of mist form , or take a significant amount of damage . Components . This spell required only verbal and somatic components to cast . History . This spell was associated with the pirates roaming the Sea of Fallen Stars .

title: Dispel good
description: Dispel good Dispel good was an abjuration spell that worked exactly like " dispel evil " except it affected good spells and creatures instead of evil ones . Effects . The effects of this spell were the same as " dispel evil " except the aura surrounding the spellcaster was dark and made of quivering unholy energy .
description_long: Dispel good Dispel good was an abjuration spell that worked exactly like " dispel evil " except it affected good spells and creatures instead of evil ones . Effects . The effects of this spell were the same as " dispel evil " except the aura surrounding the spellcaster was dark and made of quivering unholy energy . Components . Verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell . The newest version also used the caster ' s ( un ) holy symbol or divine focus , while the older versions required ( un ) holy water .

title: Dispel law
description: Dispel law Dispel law was an abjuration spell that worked exactly like " dispel evil " except it affected lawful spells and creatures instead of evil ones . Effects . The effects of this spell were the same as " dispel evil " except the aura surrounding the spellcaster was yellow , flickered like a candle , and made of chaotic energy .
description_long: Dispel law Dispel law was an abjuration spell that worked exactly like " dispel evil " except it affected lawful spells and creatures instead of evil ones . Effects . The effects of this spell were the same as " dispel evil " except the aura surrounding the spellcaster was yellow , flickered like a candle , and made of chaotic energy . Components . Verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell plus the caster ' s ( un ) holy symbol or divine focus .

title: Dispel magic
description: Dispel magic Dispel magic was a abjuration spell that could negate magic on a creature or object ( including potions ) , or interfere with casting spells and the use of spell - like abilities . Effects . When a magic effect is dispelled it ceases to function as if the spell duration had expired .
description_long: Dispel magic Dispel magic was a abjuration spell that could negate magic on a creature or object ( including potions ) , or interfere with casting spells and the use of spell - like abilities . Effects . When a magic effect is dispelled it ceases to function as if the spell duration had expired . Some spells were crafted specifically not to be susceptible to dispelling , but these were the exception rather than the rule . Casters could always dispel their own spells . Magical items that had magic built into them as part of their construction could not be permanently dispelled by this spell , but they could be made temporarily nonmagical for a short time . The chance to dispel an effect was based on the difference in level between the caster of " dispel " and the caster / creator / inherent power of the target . This spell could be cast in one of three ways , as chosen by the caster : The older versions of this spell did a combination of all three of the above uses : acting like targeted dispel over the entire area of effect on each creature or object ( including those worn or carried ) and possibly counterspelling any casting being done in the area of effect at that instant .

title: Dispel mirage
description: Dispel mirage Dispel mirage was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a magical field capable of destroying false images including mirages , illusions , etc .
description_long: Dispel mirage Dispel mirage was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a magical field capable of destroying false images including mirages , illusions , etc . Natural invisibility and higher powered illusion spells were not affected by this spell . Components . This spell required a handful of sand to cast .

title: Dispel silence
description: Dispel silence Dispel silence was an abjuration and alteration spell that counteracted the effects of magical silence . Effects . For the duration of the spell , the area of effect was protected against " silence " spells .
description_long: Dispel silence Dispel silence was an abjuration and alteration spell that counteracted the effects of magical silence . Effects . For the duration of the spell , the area of effect was protected against " silence " spells . The area of effect was a sphere whose radius was 10 ft ( 3 m ) per level of the caster , and was immobile . Any " silence " effects inside or overlapped by this volume did not operate , allowing speaking , spell - casting , etc . Components . No verbal component was required , allowing this spell to be cast even in a " silenced " area . The material component was a pinch of diamond powder worth at least 50 gp that was tossed into the air as the spell was cast .

title: Dispelling
description: Dispelling Dispelling is a quality that can be applied to weapons . Once per day , the wielder can use the weapon to " dispel " magic on whatever the weapon next touches . Creation .
description_long: Dispelling Dispelling is a quality that can be applied to weapons . Once per day , the wielder can use the weapon to " dispel " magic on whatever the weapon next touches . Creation . In order to forge a " dispelling " weapon , the caster must have " dispel magic " available .

title: Displacer beast
description: Displacer beast A displacer beast , also known as a dirlagraun , was a monstrous magical creature . History . The beast appears to have originated in the Feywild .
description_long: Displacer beast A displacer beast , also known as a dirlagraun , was a monstrous magical creature . History . The beast appears to have originated in the Feywild . Physical description . Displacer beasts were large cat - like creatures with six legs and a pair of long tentacles sprouting from their shoulders . They were covered in a pelt of blue - black fur . They were usually about 9 feet long and weighed as much as 500 pounds , but the occasional mutant could be twice this size . Abilities . Displacer beasts used their innate magic to bend light , making them appear to be a foot or two from their actual positions . Ecology . These monsters lived in small groups or preferred to be alone . Many humanoid s trained them to act as guards or pets , such as evil fey and oni s . Society . Like many big cats , displacer beasts were often pack hunters , although they were sometimes encountered alone . Appendix . Discrepancy . On page 66 of " Monster Manual 3 . 5 " , the alignment of the displacer beast is lawful evil , but in the " Monster Manual 4th edition " , the creatures ' alignment has changed to unaligned . In the " Monster Manual 5th edition " , it has again become lawful evil .

title: Displacer serpent
description: Displacer serpent A displacer serpent was a magical beast , a snake - like with a " displacement " - like ability . Description . A displacer serpent resembled a snake some 8 feet ( 2 .
description_long: Displacer serpent A displacer serpent was a magical beast , a snake - like with a " displacement " - like ability . Description . A displacer serpent resembled a snake some 8 feet ( 2 . 4 meters ) in length and 200 pounds ( 90 kilograms ) in weight . It had a soft scaly hide a deep blue - black in color . Down its flanks ran two bright , glowing violet stripes , which appeared almost to hover away some distance from the beast ' s body . Its eyes were glowing green color . Behavior . The displacer serpent was sentient , though not very intelligent , and had a furtive manner , attacking if hungry or bored and fleeing if threatened . They were ravenous carnivores , however , able to eat any living creature . They preferred small prey but were not shy of hunting large creatures . They normally dwelt in warm forests and made nests of hair and detritus . They spoke Draconic , but not well , and with a hissing tone . Some might be taught to say other words . Abilities . The displacer serpent ' s key ability was its " displacement " - like power : it was permanently shrouded in a glamer than bent light and made it appear always to be in a slightly different location .

title: Disruption
description: Disruption Disruption is a weapon property . Weapons with this property are often wielded by paladin s and Kelemvor ites , and are specifically designed to fight undead . Creation .
description_long: Disruption Disruption is a weapon property . Weapons with this property are often wielded by paladin s and Kelemvor ites , and are specifically designed to fight undead . Creation . He who would enchant a " disruption " weapon must have the " heal " spell available . The property can only be used on a bludgeoning weapon , such as a club or mace . Activation . The " disruption " property is permanently active . Whenever an undead foe is struck with a disruption weapon , it must successfully resist the enchantment with an effort of will or be destroyed instantly .

title: Dissolution
description: Dissolution Dissolution by Richard Lee Byers is the first book in the War of the Spider Queen series . Summary . The city of Menzoberranzan is being subject to the Silence of Lolth : priestesses no longer have access to their clerical magic .
description_long: Dissolution Dissolution by Richard Lee Byers is the first book in the War of the Spider Queen series . Summary . The city of Menzoberranzan is being subject to the Silence of Lolth : priestesses no longer have access to their clerical magic . Many drow males have apparently discovered this fact and run off . After an accident that kills several of his students , Pharaun Mizzrym , a master of Sorcere , is assigned by the Archmage of Menzoberranzan to track down those renegades to " redeem " himself . He convinces his friend Ryld Argith , a master of Melee - Magthere who is bored of his position , to help him in this endeavour . Meanwhile , Gromph Baenre has decided to assassinate his sister , the matron mistress of Arach - Tinilith , Quenthel Baenre . He sends several demon servants to complete the job , thwarted each time by Quenthel ' s skill in avoiding death . Quenthel discovers and frustrates a coup instigated by lower priestesses , slaying all of the rebels .

title: Dissonant whispers
description: Dissonant whispers Dissonant whispers was an enchantment spell that created a cacophonous whisper that damaged a target and could make it run away . Effect . The caster would whisper a cacophonous sound that only the target could hear .
description_long: Dissonant whispers Dissonant whispers was an enchantment spell that created a cacophonous whisper that damaged a target and could make it run away . Effect . The caster would whisper a cacophonous sound that only the target could hear . It caused damage to the target and if they couldn ' t resist the spell they had to move away from the caster . If the target did resist the spell , then they only took half the damage and didn ' t have to retreat . If the spell was cast with a higher spell level , then the spell caused more damage to the target . A target that couldn ' t hear would not be effected by the spell . Components . Only a vocal component was needed for the casting of this spell .

title: Disthene
description: Disthene Disthene , also known as , was a plentiful ornamental stone found across the " Realms " . Description . Disthene cleaved easily but was difficult to facet - cut because it was prone to splitting in unwanted directions .
description_long: Disthene Disthene , also known as , was a plentiful ornamental stone found across the " Realms " . Description . Disthene cleaved easily but was difficult to facet - cut because it was prone to splitting in unwanted directions . This stone could easily be cleaved making it difficult to cut in facets without splitting . Flawless disthene was difficult to find but came in crystals ranging in color from pale green to dark blue . A typical stone had a base value of 10 gp . Good quality blue facet - grade crystals were the most prized at double the base value for 20 gp . Powers . Disthene was crushed to powder and used as a material component in , or to make inks for inscribing scrolls of , spells that controlled and shaped fire .

title: Distort
description: Distort Distort was a simple alteration spell used to alter sound . This spell was created by the famed wizard Darsson Spellmaker . Effects .
description_long: Distort Distort was a simple alteration spell used to alter sound . This spell was created by the famed wizard Darsson Spellmaker . Effects . This spell allowed the caster to change the nature of any sound within several paces of the source of the sound . The volume of the sound stayed the same , but the pitch , timbre , resonance and tone could all be changed . All of these changes were accomplished by mental commands from the caster . Components . This spell only required verbal and somatic components .

title: Ditriv Starkdale
description: Ditriv Starkdale Ditriv Starkdale was a sage at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose in the late 15th century DR . Personality . Ditriv was focused only on his research .
description_long: Ditriv Starkdale Ditriv Starkdale was a sage at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose in the late 15th century DR . Personality . Ditriv was focused only on his research . History . Ditriv was one of the guests at the monastery in 1491 DR . He needed to use the monastery ' s libraries for his research into the development of Damaran settlements over the last few centuries and their interaction with the Nar , goblin s , and orc s .

title: Divination
description: Divination The divination school of magic contains spells that enable the caster to learn secrets long forgotten , interpret dreams , predict the future , to find hidden things or foil deceptive spells . Among them are included detect magic and scry . A wizard who specializes in divination is known as a diviner .
description_long: Divination The divination school of magic contains spells that enable the caster to learn secrets long forgotten , interpret dreams , predict the future , to find hidden things or foil deceptive spells . Among them are included detect magic and scry . A wizard who specializes in divination is known as a diviner . Divination is often considered the " weakest " of the schools ; specialist diviners need only forsake one other school , other than the normal two , and no other specialist can use Divination as one of their forsaken schools . In 2nd edition D & D the divination school was divided into major / minor schools called greater / lesser divination . Lesser divination spells were available to all wizards regardless of specialization .

title: Divination ( spell )
description: Divination ( spell ) Divination was a divination spell that was similar to " augury " but it foretold the outcome should the caster choose to enter a certain area . Effect . The oldest version of the spell told of the strength of monsters and the value of treasure in a known area and if the caster would invoke forces of supernatural evil or good if they attempted to enter .
description_long: Divination ( spell ) Divination was a divination spell that was similar to " augury " but it foretold the outcome should the caster choose to enter a certain area . Effect . The oldest version of the spell told of the strength of monsters and the value of treasure in a known area and if the caster would invoke forces of supernatural evil or good if they attempted to enter . It had a fairly good success rate that got better with the caster ' s ability . For a later version , the caster inquired about a certain activity or event within the next seven days and received indications about success or failure of the venture . It would also tell if a goal would be advantageous for the caster . It had the same success rate as the previous version . The next version of the spell performed similarly , but with a higher success rate . The post Second Sundering version of this spell functioned much the same as the previous ones . It could detect future events seven days into the future and give a short answer . However , each casting of the spell before a lengthy rest would induce a greater risk of getting a random answer . Components .

title: Divination sphere
description: Divination sphere The Divination sphere was a group of spells granted to cleric s and monk s that could be used to find lost objects or information , or assist in making choices by giving glimpses of possible futures . Spells in normal text were listed in the Tome of Magic 2nd edition . Spells in italics were added to the Divination Sphere in the sourcebook .
description_long: Divination sphere The Divination sphere was a group of spells granted to cleric s and monk s that could be used to find lost objects or information , or assist in making choices by giving glimpses of possible futures . Spells in normal text were listed in the Tome of Magic 2nd edition . Spells in italics were added to the Divination Sphere in the sourcebook .

title: Divine champion
description: Divine champion Divine champions are powerful individuals in the service of a specific deity .
