description_long: Durpari - Shaartan Patois Durpari - Shaartan Patois was a creole of Durpari and Shaaran spoken by the inhabitants of the eastern Shaar , from the Council Hills in the north to the Toadsquat Mountains in the south , and from Landrise in the west to Giant ' s Belt in the east .

title: Durpari language
description: Durpari language Durpari was a regional tongue of Southeast Faerûn and the official language of the Durpar i Kingdoms . Speakers . Durpari was spoken in Durpar , Estagund , Var the Golden , and Veldorn , and was the primary language in those kingdoms .
description_long: Durpari language Durpari was a regional tongue of Southeast Faerûn and the official language of the Durpar i Kingdoms . Speakers . Durpari was spoken in Durpar , Estagund , Var the Golden , and Veldorn , and was the primary language in those kingdoms . Other places it was commonly spoken included the Golden Water , Luiren , Mulhorand , Nimbral , the Shaar , and among Shou expatriates in Faerûn . Script . Like many human languages , Durpari used the Thorass alphabet , which the Durpari people adapted from the west . Related Languages . While an Imaskari language , Durpari was strongly influenced by Draconic and by Mulhorandi and other Rauric languages . Some scholars divided Durpari into three sub - languages — Alarric , ( the primary version of the language spoken in Durpar , Estagund , and Var , ) Raurindi , and Devic . Alarric was further subdivided into the Shining and Desert dialects . A creole of Durpari , Durpari - Shaartan Patois , was spoken in the eastern Shaar . Examples . Common Durpari surnames included Beszrizma , Datharathi , Melpurvatta , Nalambar , Saqarastar , and Tiliputakas .

title: Durth
description: Durth Durth was a deep gnome . History . In 1377 DR , Durth was one of the deep gnomes hired by Cavatina Xarann to act as a guide for the the combined force of Sshamath wizards and priests of Eilistraee to the main temple of Kiaransalee , which they planned to attack .
description_long: Durth Durth was a deep gnome . History . In 1377 DR , Durth was one of the deep gnomes hired by Cavatina Xarann to act as a guide for the the combined force of Sshamath wizards and priests of Eilistraee to the main temple of Kiaransalee , which they planned to attack . However Durth and his companion had long had business with the Crones of Kiaransalee , providing them with voidstone . So they double - crossed the drow . They tried to kill Q ' arlynd Melarn but instead Q ' arlynd knocked Durth down and killed his companion .

title: Durthan
description: Durthan The Durthans were a secretive group of women who operated in Rashemen . They called upon the darker spirits of the country . They were the antithesis of the Witches of Rashemen and worked against them for the rulership of the realm .
description_long: Durthan The Durthans were a secretive group of women who operated in Rashemen . They called upon the darker spirits of the country . They were the antithesis of the Witches of Rashemen and worked against them for the rulership of the realm . They wore masks like the hathran s to disguise their identities and pretended that they were of the same order . They used dark magic and were very seductive .

title: Durzagon
description: Durzagon A durzagon was the offspring of a devil and duergar . History . Sometimes , a devil would secretly breed with a duergar .
description_long: Durzagon A durzagon was the offspring of a devil and duergar . History . Sometimes , a devil would secretly breed with a duergar . The result was a half - fiend whose birth was celebrated in both the Hells and Duergar society . Description . Durzagon were taller than both dwarves and duergar , averaging about 5 ft . ( 1 . 5 m ) They were usually rust - colored and bald with a red - streaked grey beard . Personality . Durzagon tended to be revered by their peers as powerful leaders . The durgazon themselves concealed their true heritage either from ignorance or deliberate secrecy to keep knowledge of their powers from their enemies . Abilities . A durzagon ' s beard quills contained a sulfuric poison that physically weakened foes . Their resistances were a cross between both devils and demon s with a resistance to fire , cold , electricity , and acid . They were also immune to poison .

title: Dus Abd al - Dawwar
description: Dus Abd al - Dawwar Dus Abd al - Dawwar was the admiral and commander of the Wanderers Mamluk Society in Qudra in 1367 DR . Activities . Dus spent most of his time trying to bring at least half of Qudra ' s fleet of ships up to working order through constant repairs .
description_long: Dus Abd al - Dawwar Dus Abd al - Dawwar was the admiral and commander of the Wanderers Mamluk Society in Qudra in 1367 DR . Activities . Dus spent most of his time trying to bring at least half of Qudra ' s fleet of ships up to working order through constant repairs .

title: Dusk Ports
description: Dusk Ports The Dusk Ports were a collection of seemingly free trade cities on the western shores of the Dragon Sea . In reality , they were vassal states to the green dragon Orlarrakh . Geography .
description_long: Dusk Ports The Dusk Ports were a collection of seemingly free trade cities on the western shores of the Dragon Sea . In reality , they were vassal states to the green dragon Orlarrakh . Geography . The Dusk Ports were located on the western shore of the Dragon Sea . Government . Although in appearance each port was an independent and self - ruling state , rival to each other and never cooperating in anything , in reality all ports were under the thumb of Orlarrakh , the Green Duchess , who in turn was a vassal of the ruler of Melabrauth . Background . All cities of the Dusk Ports were rivals of those of the Windrise Ports , not only because those cities were also trade ports , and therefore commercial rivals , but also because the Dusk Ports employed pirate s , a practice frowned upon in the Windrise Ports .

title: Dusk Road
description: Dusk Road The Dusk Road was a short , moderately traveled trade road in the Western Heartlands of Faerûn . The Dusk Road started at Iriaebor in the south and went northwest , crossing the River Reaching at Hill ' s Edge and continuing along the coastline all the way north to Waterdeep .
description_long: Dusk Road The Dusk Road was a short , moderately traveled trade road in the Western Heartlands of Faerûn . The Dusk Road started at Iriaebor in the south and went northwest , crossing the River Reaching at Hill ' s Edge and continuing along the coastline all the way north to Waterdeep .

title: Dusklan
description: Dusklan Dusklan was a port city and a member of the confederation of the Dusk Ports on Returned Abeir . Background . Dusklan was the most racially diverse of the Dusk Ports , having citizens of a variety of races , even orc s .
description_long: Dusklan Dusklan was a port city and a member of the confederation of the Dusk Ports on Returned Abeir . Background . Dusklan was the most racially diverse of the Dusk Ports , having citizens of a variety of races , even orc s . Dusklan also boasted kinship to escaped slaves , who composed most on the inhabitants of the city . However , most of the time the escaped slaves were used to appease the wrath of the green dragon Orlarrakh . Dusklan was reputed to be the merriest of the Dusk Ports . Locals enjoyed feasting , dancing , singing , theater , and public pranks . Thefts and tavern brawls were common , but murder , kidnapping , and arson were almost unheard of . Government . Dusklan was ruled by a Duspranar , a magistrate who issued decrees , and passed sentences in trade disputes and matters of justice . Usually , a new Duspranar was chosen after Orlarrakh visited the city . Suchs visits were infrequent and the green dragon rarely stay long enough to eat more than a few unlucky citizens . Economy . Dusklan was the center for counterfeiting in Returned Abeir .

title: Duskwood
description: Duskwood The Duskwood was a forest in the Border Kingdoms . It covered the eastern side of the Border Kingdoms area , between the Realm of the Smoking Star and the Realm of the Ready Sword . Description .
description_long: Duskwood The Duskwood was a forest in the Border Kingdoms . It covered the eastern side of the Border Kingdoms area , between the Realm of the Smoking Star and the Realm of the Ready Sword . Description . Of all forests in the Border Kingdoms , the Duskwood was the deepest and most untamed . It had dense undergrowth . Inhabitants . Giant spider s , huge snake s , owlbear s , and badger mice were all found in the Duskwood . Beholder s were also said to lurk there . History . By 1479 DR , the Duskwood no longer existed , having been swallowed by the desert wasteland of the Shaar Desolation created through climate change brought about by the Spellplague .

title: Duskwood ( tree )
description: Duskwood ( tree ) Duskwood was a type of tree found growing all over Faerûn . Description . Duskwoods grew in densely packed groves , blocked the light and appeared rather eerie , giving them their name .
description_long: Duskwood ( tree ) Duskwood was a type of tree found growing all over Faerûn . Description . Duskwoods grew in densely packed groves , blocked the light and appeared rather eerie , giving them their name . They had smooth black bark and the trunks grew to an average height of 60 feet ( 18 . 2 meters ) , with small lacy branches high on the tree . Atop these trunks were small branches . The wood was smoky gray and as tough as iron . Duskwoods were very resistant to fire . Usage . Some craftspeople fashioned weapons out of duskwood in place of metal . Such items weighed half as much as their metal counterparts . Duskwood didn ' t make good armor ( even with a " wood shape " spell ) , though a passable breastplate could be made out of it . Mast spars and roof beams were usually made of duskwood . The " Blackstaff " and the " Scepter of Savras " were made of duskwood . Locations . Duskwood trees were known to be found in the following places :

title: Dust curtain
description: Dust curtain Dust curtain was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a controlled gale that lifted dust from the surrounding area .
description_long: Dust curtain Dust curtain was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a controlled gale that lifted dust from the surrounding area . The caster could create either a wall of dust or a swirling cloud . This spell was useful to blind enemies or conceal allies . If the caster ' s concentration was broken then the spell would end . The caster was able to move the wall or cloud around wherever they chose . Dust clouds could even be shaped into virtually any form . Components . This spell required a handful of sand to cast .

title: Dust genasi
description: Dust genasi A dust genasi , or dust para - genasi , was a sub - race of the genasi . It was a para - genasi , meaning that it was descended from two different elemental outsider s , namely an outsider of elemental air and an outsider of elemental earth , forming para - elemental dust . Personality .
description_long: Dust genasi A dust genasi , or dust para - genasi , was a sub - race of the genasi . It was a para - genasi , meaning that it was descended from two different elemental outsider s , namely an outsider of elemental air and an outsider of elemental earth , forming para - elemental dust . Personality . These smart but often - sarcastic folk had a tendency toward the bleak and macabre , with a morbid interest in death and decay made them less them popular with others . They invariably wore dark or black attire , often even wearing funeral vestments or the like , no matter how inappropriate this might be . Though usually neutral in outlook , they had a slight inclination towards chaos . Most lived as rogue s . Description . Dust para - genasi were bony and gaunt of build , with pale skin and dark circles under their eyes . Most of them had traits like dehydrated skin or a cloud of dust about them that came from their mixed ancestry . Though a nimble breed , they were often in poor health . They did not breathe . Abilities . They possessed a natural defense against dust - oriented spell s .

title: Dust mephit
description: Dust mephit A dust mephit was a mephit from the Elemental Plane of Air or Quasi - Elemental Plane of Dust . Description . A dust mephit was about four feet ( 120 centimeters ) tall and weighed a couple pounds ( about one kilogram ) .
description_long: Dust mephit A dust mephit was a mephit from the Elemental Plane of Air or Quasi - Elemental Plane of Dust . Description . A dust mephit was about four feet ( 120 centimeters ) tall and weighed a couple pounds ( about one kilogram ) . They had rough gray skin , which seemed to produce dust and grit constantly as they moved . Like all mephits , dust mephits were imp ish in appearance and had wispy wings . Personality . Dust mephits typically seemed sorrowful and irritable . Abilities . Dust mephits could heal themselves as long as they were in a dusty , dry environment . They had the ability to breathe a conical cloud of irritating particulates , which could cause burning eyes and itching skin in victims . They also had the innate power to surround themselves with a blurring cloud of dust about once every hour or to call forth a powerful wall of roiling dust once per day . They were immune to the effects of fire or poisons . Combat . When forced to fight , these mephits were exceptionally persistent and would rarely ever retreat , biting and clawing and injuring opponents with their breath . Society .

title: Dustclaws
description: Dustclaws The Dustclaws were a Luskan gang lead by a half - orc named Duulgrin . The gang ' s symbol was a dripping claw inside a circle . In 1480 DR , the gang had sixty members and operated out of a tavern .
description_long: Dustclaws The Dustclaws were a Luskan gang lead by a half - orc named Duulgrin . The gang ' s symbol was a dripping claw inside a circle . In 1480 DR , the gang had sixty members and operated out of a tavern . The gang ' s leader was killed by Sithe during Kalen Dren ' s attempt to clean up the city . After Duulgrin ' s death , the gang chose Sithe as their leader and she lead the gang for a brief time .

title: Dustdigger
description: Dustdigger A dustdigger was a huge monster that lurked underground and projected illusions to lure prey into its maw . Description . A dustdigger resembled a huge five - pointed upside - down starfish with flexible arms and a many - fanged mouth in the center , which faced upwards .
description_long: Dustdigger A dustdigger was a huge monster that lurked underground and projected illusions to lure prey into its maw . Description . A dustdigger resembled a huge five - pointed upside - down starfish with flexible arms and a many - fanged mouth in the center , which faced upwards . It had a tough , armored hide , but the underbelly ( facing up ) was comparatively softer . The outer hide was dark blue and purple , and the inner hide was orange . Behavior . Dustdiggers usually formed groups of up to twenty individuals . They often traveled as a group but did not exhibit pack behavior . They traveled short distances , only at night and only for a few minutes before digging a hole and settling in again . Tactics . A dustdigger would dig a hole in loose , sandy soil or a dune , and cover itself with a layer of sand , then inflate itself to form a slight mound . Lying in wait just under the surface , a dustdigger trapped creatures walking over it by deflating rapidly , causing a sinkhole effect as the shifting sand hopefully prevented the victim from avoiding its mouth .

title: Duster
description: Duster Dusters were small elemental vermin native to the Elemental Plane of Air that could also be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . They were weaker relatives of dust devil s . Description .
description_long: Duster Dusters were small elemental vermin native to the Elemental Plane of Air that could also be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . They were weaker relatives of dust devil s . Description . These creatures resembled a small armadillo that walked upright and had human - shaped hands . They sported a long proboscis that they used during feeding . Ecology . Dusters fed on flowers , or other scented items like perfume . If confronted , they used their power of invisibility and flew away . They were capable of creating a tiny whirlwind with their beak that temporarily blinded opponents .

title: Dusts of death
description: Dusts of death Dusts of death was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spelled turned dust or sand into a deadly poison .
description_long: Dusts of death Dusts of death was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spelled turned dust or sand into a deadly poison . The poison was undetectable , but casting " detect magic " revealed a magical nature about the dust . If consumed , this dust instantly killed the consumer . The only trace of foul play would be a bit of dust around the victim ' s lips and nostrils . Many sorcerous societies in Zakhara used this spell as their prime method of assassination . Components . This spell required a pinch of sand or dust to cast .

title: Dustwall Mountains
description: Dustwall Mountains The Dustwall Mountains ( also called simply the Dustwalls or just the Dustwall ) separated southern Raurin from northern Durpar in the Shining South . They were so named because they protected Durpar from the turbulent sandstorms that ravaged the Raurin desert . It had many names , being also known as the Mountains of War and the Mountains of Adama .
description_long: Dustwall Mountains The Dustwall Mountains ( also called simply the Dustwalls or just the Dustwall ) separated southern Raurin from northern Durpar in the Shining South . They were so named because they protected Durpar from the turbulent sandstorms that ravaged the Raurin desert . It had many names , being also known as the Mountains of War and the Mountains of Adama . Geography . The Dustwall appeared to be an arm of the great Yehimal . In the east , where the Dustwall joined the wider mountains of the A - Ling Shan ( one of the many mountain ranges that comprised the Yehimal ) , were the Ice Peaks . A short branch of the Dustwall ran south into Durpar ; this was called the Gryphon Mountains . This name was also sometimes applied to the Dustwall Mountains as a whole . The Dustwall continued west in the Giant ' s Belt , a similar range that curved north and continued to separate the Shining Lands from the Raurin . The Dustwall Mountains marked the northern borders of the lands of Durpar , Var , and Estagund , and of Ulgarth , separating them from the forbidding lands of the Dust Desert . They shielded the southern lands against the raging sandstorms .

title: Dusty Hoof
description: Dusty Hoof The Dusty Hoof was an inn and tavern located on the east side of Northstorm Street at the six - way intersection of the Walk in Scornubel . Structure . The building was long and narrow with high ceilings .
description_long: Dusty Hoof The Dusty Hoof was an inn and tavern located on the east side of Northstorm Street at the six - way intersection of the Walk in Scornubel . Structure . The building was long and narrow with high ceilings . The basement contained the kitchen and gaming rooms , the street level was the tap room , and the dining room , which was closed at night , was on the upper level . Rooms for rent occupied the three floors above this . None but the rooms at the front of the building had windows . The cellars beneath the building were supposed to link up with dry sewers and were apparently used for smuggling . Inhabitants . Its patrons were mainly drovers and caravan wagonfolk . Most of the clientele used the place merely to eat and sleep , so there was little violence . Food and drink . A selection of roasts , stews and vegetables were on offer , including the specialty " hoof soup " , which was supposedly made by boiling up the hooves of the local livestock . Portion sizes were large . Ale , wine , sherry , and mead were offered as drinks .

title: Duth Gulkanun
description: Duth Gulkanun Duth Gulkanun was a War Wizard of Cormyr . History . In 1480 DR , Gulkanun went to Castle Irlingstar with Nostyn Vandur .
description_long: Duth Gulkanun Duth Gulkanun was a War Wizard of Cormyr . History . In 1480 DR , Gulkanun went to Castle Irlingstar with Nostyn Vandur . He tried to stop Lord Steward Gelnur Farland , Arclath Delcastle , and Amarune Whitewave from opening the cells . Later he agreed to form a partnership with them in order to uncover the killer that plagued the castle .

title: Duthcloim
description: Duthcloim Duthcloim , also known as Manyfolk , was a district in the drow city of Menzoberranzan . Description . The district of Duthcloim surrounded the Bazaar and the Clawrift , a huge chasm in the center of the city .
description_long: Duthcloim Duthcloim , also known as Manyfolk , was a district in the drow city of Menzoberranzan . Description . The district of Duthcloim surrounded the Bazaar and the Clawrift , a huge chasm in the center of the city . Its narrow streets were filled with shops and three - story tallhouses carved from stalagmites . Patrols deterred most open crime . Duthcloim was known for being the most colorful , diverse , and tolerant district of the city . It was home to many merchants and family houses ( both noble and commoner ) . Nearly all drow commoners in Menzoberranzan lived in or had originated in Duthcloim . Many noble houses maintained secondary ( often secret ) houses in the district . Many non - drow lived in this district and were generally treated peaceably by all but noble - born drow , but they were not allowed to openly worship any deity but Lolth . Drow living in the neighboring district of West Wall , which had few ( if any ) shops , preferred to shop in Duthcloim .

title: Dutiful Mamluk Society
description: Dutiful Mamluk Society The Dutiful Mamluk Society , also known as the Dutiful , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Dutiful represented the largest and most powerful mamluk organization in the entire Land of Fate .
description_long: Dutiful Mamluk Society The Dutiful Mamluk Society , also known as the Dutiful , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Dutiful represented the largest and most powerful mamluk organization in the entire Land of Fate . Despite this , they were bitter rivals with the Respected , who dominated the Free Cities of Zakhara north of Qudra . Organization . The Dutiful were led by the dwarven Emir Hatit Abd al - Wajib . Base of Operations . This large organizations had a presence in most cities in Zakhara , but most of their power was centered in Qudra , Huzuz , and Utaqa .

title: Duupox
description: Duupox Duupox was a morkoth member of the Arcanum of Olleth in Serôs in 1370 DR . History . Thanks to his skills , Duupox rose through the Arcanum ' s ranks until he became one of the apprentices of Arcount Axar Xyrl .
description_long: Duupox Duupox was a morkoth member of the Arcanum of Olleth in Serôs in 1370 DR . History . Thanks to his skills , Duupox rose through the Arcanum ' s ranks until he became one of the apprentices of Arcount Axar Xyrl . During the Twelfth Serôs War , Duupox participated in the Olleth raids on the Tower of Numos at Abydos . However , there he was defeated and scarred by the triton hero Keros the Wanderer . In 1370 DR , Axar Xyrl allied with the aquatic elf tyrant Gantar Kraok and the arcount sent Duupox with Major Qyzal to organize am ambush against some surface dwellers who were enemies of Kraok . Later , Axar Xyrl , together with Gantar Kraok , also entered the battle to help his subordinates . However , Gantar recklessly hurled spells that struck the morkoth and when Axar Xyrl and Duupox confronted the elf about it , Gantar insulted everyone in the place and teleport ed away . Therefore , in revenge , Axar offered an alliance to the surface dwellers . Personality . Duupox was a greedy and opportunistic individual . After his skirmish with Keros , he became more ruthless . Duupox dreamed of one day having his revenge against Keros .

title: Duvan
description: Duvan Duvan is a human rogue and adventurer - for - hire of about twenty years of age who works for the copper dragon Tyrangal in Ormpetarr . History . Early Life .
description_long: Duvan Duvan is a human rogue and adventurer - for - hire of about twenty years of age who works for the copper dragon Tyrangal in Ormpetarr . History . Early Life . Duvan grew up in a small farming village with his father and twin sister Tilfani . His mother died in childbirth . When Duvan was ten , remnants of the spellplague swept through his village instantly killing most all of the villagers with the exception of Duvan and his sister . His sister became ill and wasted away leaving Duvan by himself . Wildhome . Duvan was later found by a band of wild elves who took him to Wildhome in the Chondalwood and adopted him as a member of the tribe . There , the elves taught Duvan the basics of woodcraft and stealth . When it was time for Duvan ' s coming of age ceremony , the elves took him to the edge of the Plaguewrought Land and etched a design on his body . Duvan approached the border of the plagueland in the hope that the blue fire would permanently tattoo the etching but no matter how far he went into the plagueland , he was unaffected by the spellplague . After this incident , he was treated as a pariah by the wild elves .

title: Duvessa Shane
description: Duvessa Shane Duvessa Shane was the speaker of Bryn Shander in 1485 DR and sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Duvessa was the daughter of a Waterdhavian trader and a woman of Icewind Dale .
description_long: Duvessa Shane Duvessa Shane was the speaker of Bryn Shander in 1485 DR and sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Duvessa was the daughter of a Waterdhavian trader and a woman of Icewind Dale . In time , she became the speaker of Bryn Shander and leader of the Ten Towns ' s council . In 1485 DR , with many threats to the dale arising , Duvessa met and befriended a trader from Waterdeep , Vaelish Gant , who soon became her unofficial political aide . On Eleint 23 of that year , an election was called for the position of speaker and Duvessa ran for reelection . What she did not know was that Vaelish was secretly a wizard from Arcane Brotherhood who plotted to replace her and had engineered some of the troubles in the dale . Vaelish ' s plan was to kidnap Duvessa on election day and afterward propose himself as a stronger leader . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR she was at the council chamber when giant s attacked the city . Personality . Duvessa inherited her mother ' s talent for negotiation and her father ' s charm . Some people thought her temerity but she always obtained what she wanted She believed that people of Ten Towns can survive all kind of storm .

title: Dwahvel Tiggerwillies
description: Dwahvel Tiggerwillies Dwahvel Tiggerwillies was a halfling woman and a cousin of Dondon Tiggerwillies . She was the guildmistress of a halfling guild based in Calimport , and the proprietor of the Copper Ante . She did not entertain many who were not halflings .
description_long: Dwahvel Tiggerwillies Dwahvel Tiggerwillies was a halfling woman and a cousin of Dondon Tiggerwillies . She was the guildmistress of a halfling guild based in Calimport , and the proprietor of the Copper Ante . She did not entertain many who were not halflings . She was very good at procuring information , and was used frequently for this purpose by Artemis Entreri . She informed Artemis about his situation when he was " kelp - enwalled " , and when Merle Pariso , a battle mage from the Basadoni Guild , sought to kill him . Artemis Entreri considered her as a friend ( his first real friend ) and spoke openly with her , sharing opinions and thoughts that he shared with nobody else . She helped Artemis with his plan to escape from Calimport by obtaining information about Cadderly Bonaduce , feeding misinformation to Sharlotta Vespers , and by procuring a copy of the Crenshinibon .

title: Dwalimar Omen
description: Dwalimar Omen Dwalimar Omen was the captain of the Halruaan caravel " Realms Master " in 1370 DR . History . Dwalimar hailed from Halruaa .
description_long: Dwalimar Omen Dwalimar Omen was the captain of the Halruaan caravel " Realms Master " in 1370 DR . History . Dwalimar hailed from Halruaa . In one of the adventures he undertook for the Netyarch , he acquired the Astrolabe of Nimbral for his nation . Years later , the Netyarch Zalathorm Kirkson gave Omen the mission of finding and destroying dangerously powerful artifact s using the Astrolabe . However , the astrolabe was destroyed during the Time of Troubles . At one point , Omen contracted a curse that was slowly killing him . Personality . Omen had a hot temper and a huge ego but was a fatherly figure for his crew . Omen used to be pompous and stern to impress people and charming when he wanted something . His disease could leave him very moody . However , a difficult task would galvanize Omen and he would forget his condition for a time . Omen first and foremost thought about protecting people from those that abused their power .

title: Dwarf
description: Dwarf Dwarves , sometimes called the Stout Folk , were a natural humanoid race common throughout parts of Toril as well as Abeir . Dwarves were a tough , tradition - abiding folk known for their strong martial traditions and beautiful craftsmanship . Description .
description_long: Dwarf Dwarves , sometimes called the Stout Folk , were a natural humanoid race common throughout parts of Toril as well as Abeir . Dwarves were a tough , tradition - abiding folk known for their strong martial traditions and beautiful craftsmanship . Description . Physical characteristics . Dwarves were a short race , as their name implied , standing from 4 ' 3 " – 4 ' 9 " ( 1 . 3 – 1 . 45 meters ) on average , with gold dwarves a bit shorter . What Dwarves lacked in height they made up for in bulk ; they were , on average , about as heavy as humans . A dwarf could weigh anywhere from about 160 – 220 lbs ( 73 – 100 kg ) . Dwarven males were a bit taller and heavier than their female counterparts . Like humans , dwarves had a wide variety of skin , eye , and hair colors , typically pale among shield dwarves and deeply tanned or brown amongst gold dwarves . Hazel eyes were common throughout the race , with blue eyes more common amongst shield dwarves and brown or green eyes found amongst the gold dwarves . Male dwarves were often bald and grew thick facial hair sometimes used to display social status .

title: Dwarfbane
description: Dwarfbane Dwarfbane was a poison that was especially effective against dwarves . Description . Dwarfbane was gummy in its consistency .
description_long: Dwarfbane Dwarfbane was a poison that was especially effective against dwarves . Description . Dwarfbane was gummy in its consistency . Uses . The duergar of the Underdark often coated darts and other weapons with this poison for the use in traps . History . Though the duergar were completely immune to the poison , dwarfbane was lethal to all other dwarves .

title: Dwarfhome
description: Dwarfhome Dwarfhome is a lawful good - aligned astral dominion , home to the god Moradin and his wife , the goddess Berronar . Formerly located on Mount Celestia , on its forth layer Solania , it was the home of the dwarven pantheon . Since the Spellplague it has floated freely in the Astral Sea like all dominions .
description_long: Dwarfhome Dwarfhome is a lawful good - aligned astral dominion , home to the god Moradin and his wife , the goddess Berronar . Formerly located on Mount Celestia , on its forth layer Solania , it was the home of the dwarven pantheon . Since the Spellplague it has floated freely in the Astral Sea like all dominions . Moradin makes his domain , with his wife Berronar Truesilver and the other dwarven deities in A vast dwarven mansion called " Erackinor " located on the slopes of Solania . Here exists the giant " Soul Forges " , that Moradin is said to use to temper the spirits of his people . Solania , the fourth layer , is also called " The Crystal Heaven " . Many valleys comprise Solania , covered with luminescent fogs and strange scents . The peaks are homes to numerous holy shrines , including monasteries and magnificent cathedrals . Many of the slopes are rich in precious ores and minerals and are mined by populations of dwarves that reside there .

title: Dwarnid Inkpeddler
description: Dwarnid Inkpeddler Dwarnid Inkpeddler was a dwarf tattooer in Skullport . History . In his youth , Dwarnid was the personal slave of Zulkir Druxus Rhym .
description_long: Dwarnid Inkpeddler Dwarnid Inkpeddler was a dwarf tattooer in Skullport . History . In his youth , Dwarnid was the personal slave of Zulkir Druxus Rhym . Noticing his latent talent in painting , Druxus encouraged the young dwarf and soon Dwarnid flourished . At this point , Druxus taught him the arts of the tattoo . Dwarnid in time became the most talented tattooer in Thay , creating wonderful artworks . Finally , he decided to escape and go to Skullport , which Dwarnid knew was too far for Druxus ' s agents . Here , he opened a tattoo shop and became famous in the city .

title: Dwarven defender
description: Dwarven defender The path of the dwarven defender or dwarven hero is a highly trained and specialized fighter tradition that is available to the dwarven race . These individuals take pride from the noble history of their race and its constant vigilance against exterior threats such as giant s or goblinoid s , which they hope to match in spirit as well as form . Culture .
description_long: Dwarven defender The path of the dwarven defender or dwarven hero is a highly trained and specialized fighter tradition that is available to the dwarven race . These individuals take pride from the noble history of their race and its constant vigilance against exterior threats such as giant s or goblinoid s , which they hope to match in spirit as well as form . Culture . Common dwarven soldiers are known for their martial vigilance and brotherhood , with many a war story telling of how any one dwarf is worth two fighter s of any other race . Dwarven defenders take this reputed strength and loyalty to new heights . They are masters of the dwarven fighting traditions as well as devoted to the protection and continued prosperity of their brethren . Trained particularly in defensive techniques these hardy warriors hold the line even as they break through the enemy ' s . Many dwarves who are devoted to Berronar Truesilver or Gorm Gulthyn or who are otherwise charged with protecting their clanholds usually take the path of the dwarven defender . Any one of these individuals can help to make a dwarven defensive line almost impenetrable . Abilities .

title: Dwarven waraxe
description: Dwarven waraxe A dwarven waraxe is an exotic one - handed ( or martial two - handed ) melee weapon . Description . The dwarven waraxe is a single - bladed axe larger and heavier than a battleaxe but less so than the double - bladed greataxe .
description_long: Dwarven waraxe A dwarven waraxe is an exotic one - handed ( or martial two - handed ) melee weapon . Description . The dwarven waraxe is a single - bladed axe larger and heavier than a battleaxe but less so than the double - bladed greataxe . An average dwarven waraxe costs 30gp and weighs 8lbs ( 3 . 6kg ) . Weaponology . It requires special training to use a dwarven waraxe one - handed and is therefore considered exotic . It may be used with two hands by a medium - sized creature as a martial weapon . A dwarf treats this axe as a martial weapon even when using it one - handed .

title: Dwarves ' Deep ( settlement )
description: Dwarves ' Deep ( settlement ) Dwarves ' Deep , or simply " the Deep " , was a subterranean dwarven settlement somewhere in Faerûn . History . It was once home to Forgemaster Inkstain and his kin , before he left for the city of Procampur in the Vast .
description_long: Dwarves ' Deep ( settlement ) Dwarves ' Deep , or simply " the Deep " , was a subterranean dwarven settlement somewhere in Faerûn . History . It was once home to Forgemaster Inkstain and his kin , before he left for the city of Procampur in the Vast . He organized for a printing press to be shipped up from the Deep , which he used for a printing business he ran by 1362 DR .

title: Dwarvish
description: Dwarvish Dwarvish or Dwarven was the name for a family of languages used by dwarves . The dwarves called their own language Dethek , but most other races used that term to refer to the runic alphabet in which the language was written . Although a verbally dying language by 1400 DR , Dwarvish was still found all over Faerûn inscribed into weapons , buildings and mystical items .
description_long: Dwarvish Dwarvish or Dwarven was the name for a family of languages used by dwarves . The dwarves called their own language Dethek , but most other races used that term to refer to the runic alphabet in which the language was written . Although a verbally dying language by 1400 DR , Dwarvish was still found all over Faerûn inscribed into weapons , buildings and mystical items . The language followed dwarves all over Faerûn and beyond , making it an extremely widespread language . Communities and races that had been separated for some time evolved their own dialects . History . Originating from the ancient Elder language , Dwarvish saw many incarnations and variations . Although once a strong and exclusive language , actual Dwarvish words only make up a fraction of the words used by dwarves today . Many dwarves tend to speak common littered with Dwarvish words . Dwarven record - keepers and historians are among the few left that could speak whole verses in pure Dwarvish . Dialects . Being such an old language , Dwarvish has been subject to various changes over the generations and has spawned numerous dialects . All of these dialects employ Dethek as their written alphabet . Kurit .

title: Dweomerheart
description: Dweomerheart Dweomerheart was a Celestial plane in the World Tree cosmology model and was also the name of the scintillating city that was the realm of Mystra here in the World Tree model and on the plane of Elysium in the Great Wheel model . The other deities of magic , Azuth , Savras , and Velsharoon , also made their homes on this plane not far from Mystra ' s domain . Dweomerheart was destroyed in a cataclysmic explosion in the Year of Blue Fire , 1385 DR , after Cyric assassinated Mystra causing the Spellplague .
description_long: Dweomerheart Dweomerheart was a Celestial plane in the World Tree cosmology model and was also the name of the scintillating city that was the realm of Mystra here in the World Tree model and on the plane of Elysium in the Great Wheel model . The other deities of magic , Azuth , Savras , and Velsharoon , also made their homes on this plane not far from Mystra ' s domain . Dweomerheart was destroyed in a cataclysmic explosion in the Year of Blue Fire , 1385 DR , after Cyric assassinated Mystra causing the Spellplague . Though the deities of Dweomerheart largely perished , most of the faithful of Mystra , Azuth , and the other gods dwelling there were transported safely to the Fugue Plane where they were restored and re - assigned , many of them ending up either in Towers of Night , Gates of the Moon , or Kelemvor ' s own City of Judgment . Description . This plane was mostly uninhabited mountain ranges , teeming with wildlife , with no known " portals " to the other planes of existence . The only way to access this plane other than traveling through the Astral was via branches of the World Tree itself , which connected to other Celestial planes .

title: Dweomerkeeper
description: Dweomerkeeper The Dweomerkeeper is a special prestige class for worshipers of Mystra . They serve the Lady of Mysteries by tending to the Weave and help aid Mystra and her clergy in increasing the use of magic across the Realms . Dweomerkeepers form a powerful connection with the Weave , losing their ability to ever call upon the power of the Shadow Weave .
description_long: Dweomerkeeper The Dweomerkeeper is a special prestige class for worshipers of Mystra . They serve the Lady of Mysteries by tending to the Weave and help aid Mystra and her clergy in increasing the use of magic across the Realms . Dweomerkeepers form a powerful connection with the Weave , losing their ability to ever call upon the power of the Shadow Weave .

title: Dwiergus
description: Dwiergus Dwiergus was a truly ancient demon lord , at least as old as Pale Night . He held dominion over the shaping of demonic races , and was once a tutor of Baphomet . Dwiergus ' realm was known as Fleshforges , and was the 558th layer of the Abyss .
description_long: Dwiergus Dwiergus was a truly ancient demon lord , at least as old as Pale Night . He held dominion over the shaping of demonic races , and was once a tutor of Baphomet . Dwiergus ' realm was known as Fleshforges , and was the 558th layer of the Abyss .

title: Dying gray dwarf
description: Dying gray dwarf This dying gray dwarf was a male duergar who attacked the village of West Harbor on the Sword Coast North in 1374 DR . History . This dwarf was one of the attackers of West Harbor .
description_long: Dying gray dwarf This dying gray dwarf was a male duergar who attacked the village of West Harbor on the Sword Coast North in 1374 DR . History . This dwarf was one of the attackers of West Harbor . Despite being wounded , he managed to kill several villagers , calling them weak . The Kalach - Cha had the option of healing him or slaying the duergar personally . In any case , the duergar died .

title: Dylohra
description: Dylohra Dylohra was a half - elf waitress in Mulmaster in 1491 DR . Personality . Dylohra was the oldest of her sisters and felt responsible for them .
description_long: Dylohra Dylohra was a half - elf waitress in Mulmaster in 1491 DR . Personality . Dylohra was the oldest of her sisters and felt responsible for them . History . Dylohra and her family lived near Zhentil Keep , where her father worked for the Zhentarim . After that city ' s destruction , they transferred to Mulmaster , where she began working as a maid and her father as a mason . In 1491 DR , she became worried about her youngest sister , Lyrene , who desperately wanted to join the Zhentarim like their ancestors , and disappeared . Dylohra asked for the help of an adventuring party she met at one of the parties held in her employer ' s house . Activities . In 1491 DR , Dylohra worked at the Astrid Saj estate .

title: Dyltharra
description: Dyltharra Dyltharra was a half - elf high priestess of the temple of Selûne in Velprintalar , Aglarond , around 1368 DR . She led six other priestesses at the temple and helped to maintain contact between the Simbul , the Royal Council of Aglarond , and the Harpers .
description_long: Dyltharra Dyltharra was a half - elf high priestess of the temple of Selûne in Velprintalar , Aglarond , around 1368 DR . She led six other priestesses at the temple and helped to maintain contact between the Simbul , the Royal Council of Aglarond , and the Harpers .

title: Dynaheir
description: Dynaheir Dynaheir was a young wizard specialized in invocation magic , and a wychlaran of Rashemen . Her speech was somewhat archaic and she was very demanding of her companions . She had come to the Sword Coast along with her bodyguard Minsc as part of a rite of passage .
description_long: Dynaheir Dynaheir was a young wizard specialized in invocation magic , and a wychlaran of Rashemen . Her speech was somewhat archaic and she was very demanding of her companions . She had come to the Sword Coast along with her bodyguard Minsc as part of a rite of passage . The two became separated when they were attacked by gnolls and she was taken captive . She was rescued by the protagonist and traveled with them during their conflict with Sarevok , only to meet her untimely demise soon after in the hands of Irenicus ' s lackeys .

title: Dynarth Bloodcowl
description: Dynarth Bloodcowl Dynarth Bloodcowl was the most lethal assassin of the Night Masks in 1370 DR . History . Although nearly totally lacking in stealth and discretion , Dynarth remained one of the top assassins of Westgate .
description_long: Dynarth Bloodcowl Dynarth Bloodcowl was the most lethal assassin of the Night Masks in 1370 DR . History . Although nearly totally lacking in stealth and discretion , Dynarth remained one of the top assassins of Westgate . He was not necessarily hired to kill a dangerous enemy , but rather to send a brutal message to the victim ' s associates .

title: Dyon G ' ennivalz
description: Dyon G ' ennivalz Dyon G ' ennivalz was the name of a drow city known by the illithid Yharaskrik when it was young . In 1366 DR , Yharaskrik mentioned it when questioning Kimmuriel Oblodra as to where he hailed from , though he actually came from Menzoberranzan .
description_long: Dyon G ' ennivalz Dyon G ' ennivalz was the name of a drow city known by the illithid Yharaskrik when it was young . In 1366 DR , Yharaskrik mentioned it when questioning Kimmuriel Oblodra as to where he hailed from , though he actually came from Menzoberranzan .

title: Dyrr
description: Dyrr Lord Dyrr , commonly known as Lichdrow Dyrr or simply the Lichdrow and also called " Old Dyrr " or " Master Dyrr , " was the de facto ruler of House Agrach Dyrr in Menzoberranzan and the power behind Yasraena Dyrr ' s throne . In addition to his large magical and political power , the Lichdrow had lived for at least two millennia , and he was once shown to contemplate his possible ascension to divinity in the future . Thus , before his death , he was probably one of the most powerful magic users in the Underdark .
description_long: Dyrr Lord Dyrr , commonly known as Lichdrow Dyrr or simply the Lichdrow and also called " Old Dyrr " or " Master Dyrr , " was the de facto ruler of House Agrach Dyrr in Menzoberranzan and the power behind Yasraena Dyrr ' s throne . In addition to his large magical and political power , the Lichdrow had lived for at least two millennia , and he was once shown to contemplate his possible ascension to divinity in the future . Thus , before his death , he was probably one of the most powerful magic users in the Underdark . His only rivals in power , in fact , were possibly the Archmage of Menzoberranzan himself — Gromph Baenre — and Jalynfein the Spider Mage . Description . The Lichdrow used his magic to appear as a normal male drow . However , his true appearance , which could be seen by those with arcane abilities , was that of a typical skeletal , decaying lich . History . In 1372 DR , Lord Dyrr was older than 2 , 000 years .

title: Dzunn
description: Dzunn Dzunn was a merchant from the city of Sheirtalar in Lapaliiya in the 14th century DR . Dzunn partnered with six other merchants — Alvund of Ormpetarr , Chond of Calaunt , Jhasso of Baldur ' s Gate , Nammna of Milvarune , Pomphur of Almraiven , and Shield of Everlund — to form the Seven Suns Trading Coster . The " Seven Suns " referred to the seven merchants themselves .
description_long: Dzunn Dzunn was a merchant from the city of Sheirtalar in Lapaliiya in the 14th century DR . Dzunn partnered with six other merchants — Alvund of Ormpetarr , Chond of Calaunt , Jhasso of Baldur ' s Gate , Nammna of Milvarune , Pomphur of Almraiven , and Shield of Everlund — to form the Seven Suns Trading Coster . The " Seven Suns " referred to the seven merchants themselves . Dzunn ' s own small merchant company was converted into a regional base for the coster . Dzunn and the Seven Suns were in business by 1358 DR , and still going by 1374 DR .

title: E ' Tyon Bay
description: E ' Tyon Bay E ' Tyon Bay was a bay to the north of the city of Singye in the kingdom of Koryo in Kara - Tur , lying beside the Quang Muku Forest . By 1357 DR , E ' Tyon Bay had become infested by tigerworm s , which sunk four fishing boats and a merchant ship . Singye authorities offered a reward to any who could eliminate the menace .
description_long: E ' Tyon Bay E ' Tyon Bay was a bay to the north of the city of Singye in the kingdom of Koryo in Kara - Tur , lying beside the Quang Muku Forest . By 1357 DR , E ' Tyon Bay had become infested by tigerworm s , which sunk four fishing boats and a merchant ship . Singye authorities offered a reward to any who could eliminate the menace .

title: Eadro
description: Eadro Eadro ( " ee - AD - ro " ) was the creator of the locathah and merfolk and was worshiped exclusively by those two races , though each worshiped him differently . Worshipers . Merfolk .
description_long: Eadro Eadro ( " ee - AD - ro " ) was the creator of the locathah and merfolk and was worshiped exclusively by those two races , though each worshiped him differently . Worshipers . Merfolk . The merfolk worshiped Eadro with passion , making their supplications open to non - merfolk so that they might hear songs devoted to him . The songs and swimming dances they used in prayer changed with every season as well as during their numerous holidays . They were accepting of the differences in the locathahs ' beliefs , but these beliefs were confusing to the merfolk . Locathah . The locathah worshiped him as the Deliverer . Only males were allowed in the clergy and their religious practices were kept secret from all others . They used prayer as a form of redemption from the punishment they believed was bestowed upon their race for improper worship , pointing to the frequent enslavement of the locathah by others and their scaly bodies as opposed to the merfolk ' s smoother ones . They aimed to use their prayer to be redeemed and transformed into merfolk .

title: Eadyan Falconmoon
description: Eadyan Falconmoon Eadyan Falconmoon was the priest of Chauntea of the small town of Greenest , located in the Western Heartlands in west Faerûn . Personality . Eadyan remained calm even during the chaos of the attack .
description_long: Eadyan Falconmoon Eadyan Falconmoon was the priest of Chauntea of the small town of Greenest , located in the Western Heartlands in west Faerûn . Personality . Eadyan remained calm even during the chaos of the attack . History . During the battle with the Cult of the Dragon , Eadyan gathered as many people as possible inside the temple , one of the most durable buildings , in order to keep them safe from cultist raiders .

title: Eaerlann
description: Eaerlann Eaerlann was a powerful elven kingdom of wood and moon elves in the valley of the Delimbiyr River and a portion of the eastern High Forest that was founded by Sharrven nobles in - 4700 DR and lasted for around six thousand years . Together with Sharrven it suppressed the spread of evil in Siluvanede and maintained the peace . Their land was bound by the eastern part of the High Forest from Turnstone Pass in the north to the Shining Falls in the south .
description_long: Eaerlann Eaerlann was a powerful elven kingdom of wood and moon elves in the valley of the Delimbiyr River and a portion of the eastern High Forest that was founded by Sharrven nobles in - 4700 DR and lasted for around six thousand years . Together with Sharrven it suppressed the spread of evil in Siluvanede and maintained the peace . Their land was bound by the eastern part of the High Forest from Turnstone Pass in the north to the Shining Falls in the south . In 882 DR the combination of the demon ic invasion that spilled forth from Ascalhorn , the continued assault of the orc hordes , and the weakening of the kingdom by elves Retreating to Evermeet resulted in the kingdom ' s collapse . After the collapse some of the elves of Eaerlann joined with dwarves and humans to form the Fallen Kingdom . Ecology . The Eaerlanni elves made their homes by hollowing out select trees and connecting them with lavish yet conventional rope bridges and platforms , striving to live with their surroundings instead of atop them - because of this , many of their settlements have not withstood the passage of time and are no longer present though some traces still remain .

title: Eaerlraun Shadowlyn
description: Eaerlraun Shadowlyn Eaerlraun Shadowlyn was the Harper master of Moongleam Tower in Everlund . History . In 1372 DR , Eaerlraun held the title of Moonlord and was simpathetic to the Moonstar cause .
description_long: Eaerlraun Shadowlyn Eaerlraun Shadowlyn was the Harper master of Moongleam Tower in Everlund . History . In 1372 DR , Eaerlraun held the title of Moonlord and was simpathetic to the Moonstar cause . He was the one that kept alive the Harpers ' traditions after the Spellplague , focusing in fighting the shadovar .

title: Eagle
description: Eagle Eagles were large , majestic birds of prey that were often seen as symbols of nobility or as divine messengers . Description . They were generally larger than other birds , with a powerful build and heavier head and beak .
description_long: Eagle Eagles were large , majestic birds of prey that were often seen as symbols of nobility or as divine messengers . Description . They were generally larger than other birds , with a powerful build and heavier head and beak . They possess broad wings allowing for faster flight . Eagles weighed between 8 and 15 pounds with an average wingspan of 7 feet . Ecology . Eagles build their nests on tall trees or high cliffs . These nests were called eyries . Combat . Eagles hunted their prey from the sky using their enhanced vision , which enabled them to see small animals from great distances away . They captured food with their long talons and powerful beaks . In culture . Eagles were often used in the names of places , families , and organizations . It was also used in spell and item names , such as " eagle ' s splendor " .

title: Eagle ' s splendor
description: Eagle ' s splendor Eagle ' s splendor is a transmutation spell that makes the subject more charismatic . Effect . The transmuted creature becomes more poised , articulate , and personally forceful .
description_long: Eagle ' s splendor Eagle ' s splendor is a transmutation spell that makes the subject more charismatic . Effect . The transmuted creature becomes more poised , articulate , and personally forceful . Sorcerer s and bard s who receive " eagle ' s splendor " do not gain extra spells , but their existing spells are harder to resist . Arcane material component . A few feathers or a pinch of dung from an eagle are required to cast this spell .

title: Eagle ( spirit )
description: Eagle ( spirit ) Eagle was a deity and animal spirit worshiped by the green elves of Evermeet . Description . His role was to bestow good fortune but also to bring omens of impending catastrophes .
description_long: Eagle ( spirit ) Eagle was a deity and animal spirit worshiped by the green elves of Evermeet . Description . His role was to bestow good fortune but also to bring omens of impending catastrophes . The spirit appeared as a giant black eagle , and sometimes as a giant warrior visible in the clouds . His gaze could be lightning and his voice thunder . Relationships . Like the other nature spirits venerated by the Sy - tel - quessir , Eagle served the pantheon of the Seldarine . Priesthood . Eagle ' s priests worked for the common good and tried to achieve good fortune for their community . Worshipers . Next to the green elves of Toril , this powerful spirit was also worshiped under the name of Thunder by the peoples of Earth . Some of the djinn of Zakhara also payed homage to him , and he had a mosque at their Citadel of Ice and Steel .

title: Eagle Knights ( Maztica )
description: Eagle Knights ( Maztica ) The Eagle Knights were elite warrior s in Maztica . Organization . The lower echelon soldiers were known as Eagle Warriors and the leaders were called Eagle Knights .
description_long: Eagle Knights ( Maztica ) The Eagle Knights were elite warrior s in Maztica . Organization . The lower echelon soldiers were known as Eagle Warriors and the leaders were called Eagle Knights . They practiced hishna magic and some were able to shapechange into eagle s . Possessions . All warriors of the Eagle Knights fought with a maca and a bow . High - level knights wore eagle cloak s , which were mantles made of eagle feathers . Relationships . They were usually the scouts of the Maztica n armies .

title: Eagles
description: Eagles The Eagles were a group of hobgoblin soldiers , who served the Preachers in the fortress of Sarahin in 1367 DR . Base of Operations . The Eagles were based in the fortress of Sarahin , located deep within the Haunted Lands .
description_long: Eagles The Eagles were a group of hobgoblin soldiers , who served the Preachers in the fortress of Sarahin in 1367 DR . Base of Operations . The Eagles were based in the fortress of Sarahin , located deep within the Haunted Lands . Activities . The Eagles were well - trained but lacked experience , since the fortress of Sarahin had not been attacked in living memory . Members . All of the members of the Eagles were hobgoblins , save their commander , Mamoud ibn Asra , who was a dwarf .

title: Eagles ' Eyrie
description: Eagles ' Eyrie Eagles ' Eyrie was a rocky knoll just outside the town of Dagger Falls ; it was noted as a site sacred to the Brightblade clan of dwarves . Geography . A bare rocky hill , this natural lookout point gave a view high over the nearby town of Dagger Falls .
description_long: Eagles ' Eyrie Eagles ' Eyrie was a rocky knoll just outside the town of Dagger Falls ; it was noted as a site sacred to the Brightblade clan of dwarves . Geography . A bare rocky hill , this natural lookout point gave a view high over the nearby town of Dagger Falls . A winding trail allowed a rough ascent through sharp , steep cliffs to the top of Eagles ' Eyrie . Trade . Eagles ' Eyrie was once used as a watchpost over dwarven trading routes from the Mines of Tethyamar to towns such Hillsfar , Voonlar , and Zhentil Keep . History . At one time , Eagles ' Eyrie was a dwarven stronghold , keeping watch over valuable dwarven trade routes leading to the Mines of Tethyamar , until the fall of the kingdom of Tethyamar in 1104 DR . Shortly thereafter , in the mid - 1200s , Colderan Morn drove the remaining dwarves from the outpost after a perceived slight against his wife , Belesaria .

title: Eagus
description: Eagus Eagus was a mercenary who was killed by Abdel Adrian in 1368 DR . Appearance . Eagus had a messy greying brown beard and yellow teeth .
description_long: Eagus Eagus was a mercenary who was killed by Abdel Adrian in 1368 DR . Appearance . Eagus had a messy greying brown beard and yellow teeth . Equipment . Eagus wielded a halberd and wore rusty armour . Background . Eagus lost a bet to Abdel in Julkoun , eight months prior to Eagus ' s death , and as a result , he bore a scar on his face . Eagus was in combat alongside Kamon and others , against Abdel and Gorion , when he was stabbed by Abdel ' s broadsword . Eagus disarmed the sword from Abdel , but lost a lot of blood from his stab wound , and succumbed to death when Abdel cut his throat with a silver dagger .

title: Ear seeker
description: Ear seeker Ear seekers were small parasitic insects found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . Ear seekers were small insects measuring about 6 inches ( 15 cm ) in length .
description_long: Ear seeker Ear seekers were small parasitic insects found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . Ear seekers were small insects measuring about 6 inches ( 15 cm ) in length . Ecology . Adults were found near wood where they could eat dead cellulose . A warm place was needed to lay their eggs , and they preferred human or humanoid hosts . Ear seekers lay in wait within wood , typically a door , and darted out when a potential host pressed their ear up against the door to listen . The ear seeker laid its eggs within the host then crawled out to die . The eggs hatched within hours , burrowing deeper into the host where they could feed on blood or flesh . The host remained unaware of the presence of the eggs until they hatched and an itching sensation was experienced . The burrowing larvae caused a small degree of pain when they moved deeper into the host ' s flesh . They would remain within the host , causing cumulative physical harm , until the host died , at which point they would discard the host . The " cure disease " spell killed the larvae but did not heal the damage caused by their burrowing .

title: Earblade
description: Earblade Earblades were a rogue ' s last chance to beat the noose . Uses . By far , hanging was the most popular method for the execution of criminals .
description_long: Earblade Earblades were a rogue ' s last chance to beat the noose . Uses . By far , hanging was the most popular method for the execution of criminals . With an earblade attached , a guilty thief had a small chance to cut or weaken the rope tied around his neck , allowing for a slim chance of escape . One earblade was typically worn on each ear since the rope would be placed on either side of the thieves ' neck . Aurora ' s Emporium offered a money - back guarantee to any thief not completely satisfied with the performance of this product . Prices . A single earblade cost 1 silver piece , but most smart thieves purchased one for each ear .

title: Eardon
description: Eardon Brother Eardon was a wandering priest of Lathander during the Elemental Evil crisis . Activities . Eardon wandered northwest Faerûn , using his powers to help villagers as a messenger or priest .
description_long: Eardon Brother Eardon was a wandering priest of Lathander during the Elemental Evil crisis . Activities . Eardon wandered northwest Faerûn , using his powers to help villagers as a messenger or priest . History . In 1491 DR , Eardon was at the Swinging Sword tavern when some adventurers were hired to find a diplomatic caravan that had disappeared near the city . He confirmed that he had seen the caravan a few days before in Beliard .

title: Earring of Prince Mamoon
description: Earring of Prince Mamoon The Earring of Prince Mamoon was an item that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These pieces of jewelry were hoops of jet coral covered with intricate calligraphy .
description_long: Earring of Prince Mamoon The Earring of Prince Mamoon was an item that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These pieces of jewelry were hoops of jet coral covered with intricate calligraphy . Powers . These earrings were fashioned by Prince Mamoon of the marid s . He created them for his students of " marqab " , a school for sha ' ir s in Gana . Anyone who presented one of these earrings gained acceptance into the school .

title: Earth
description: Earth Earth was a world on an alternate Material Plane . People . A number of human peoples of Faerûn originally came from another world , which is widely believed to have been Earth .
description_long: Earth Earth was a world on an alternate Material Plane . People . A number of human peoples of Faerûn originally came from another world , which is widely believed to have been Earth . To replenish their population after a devastating plague , the mages of the Imaskar Empire in Faerûn opened two great " gate s " to this other world , and kidnapped numerous human s to serve as their slaves . Those of Mulhorand hailed from given life by the seasonal flooding of and those of Unther from of empire and glory . After transporting them back to Abeir - Toril , the Imaskari closed the gates forever . Intermarrying both with each other and the Imaskari , they became the Mulan . With them , they brought their own societies , mature culture , and later , the gods of the Mulhorandi and Untheric pantheon s . Later came a people from known for their daring philosophies . These were followed by folk from with a culture tied to nature , the sea , and the warrior history of its . These brought their own societies and faiths , and settled around the time of the rise of Netheril .

title: Earth ' s End
description: Earth ' s End Earth ' s End was an isolated Underdark town located 20 miles ( 32 km ) beneath northeastern Halruaa . The town contained a number of portals and a passageway that led to the Underchasm . Some of the portals did nothing other than let in light from aboveground and some let in water and fresh air from the Elemental Chaos .
description_long: Earth ' s End Earth ' s End was an isolated Underdark town located 20 miles ( 32 km ) beneath northeastern Halruaa . The town contained a number of portals and a passageway that led to the Underchasm . Some of the portals did nothing other than let in light from aboveground and some let in water and fresh air from the Elemental Chaos . There were also portals to Root Hold and the Monastery of the Yellow Rose . Inhabitants . Earthsoul genasi were common in the town and made up most of the town guard . The mayor was always a genasi . The humans of the town were less common but most were powerful wizard s . There were also a small number of dwarves and earth elemental s in the town . History . The establishment date of the town was unknown but during the Spellplague a group of seven human wizards sought refuge in the city . The wizards set about to make the town more habitable to humans by creating passageways through the rock and to the surface via the Underchasm .

title: Earth ( element )
description: Earth ( element ) The element of earth was one of the four fundamental building blocks of matter : solid , stable , and unyielding in character . It encompassed all kinds of stone and rock , but also soil , metal ores and sand . Cosmology .
description_long: Earth ( element ) The element of earth was one of the four fundamental building blocks of matter : solid , stable , and unyielding in character . It encompassed all kinds of stone and rock , but also soil , metal ores and sand . Cosmology . Earth manifested its position in the cosmos as the Elemental Plane of Earth , one of the Inner Planes . The element was also represented there in living form as earth elemental s . The ruler over the portfolio of earth in Faerûn and Zakhara was the elemental lord Grumbar , while it was held by Geb in the Mulhorandi pantheon and Plutoq in the Maztica n pantheon . Among demihuman deities , Segojan Earthcaller of the gnome s , Urogalan of the halfling s , and Dumathoin of the dwarves held dominion over earth , but Garl Glittergold , Callarduran Smoothhands , Laduguer , and all other dwarven deities were concerned with the element , too . The evil archomental Ogrémoch also sought to rule the element of earth , but was secretly thwarted by the much more powerful Grumbar . Magic . School of elemental earth . Many magic al spells utilized the element of earth .

title: Earth Node
description: Earth Node An Earth Node was a geological anomaly beneath the surface of Faerûn . They usually existed only at points were the invisible streams of arcane magic that permeated Faerûn intersected . Those creatures in tune with arcane magic could sometimes sense the presence of a node .
description_long: Earth Node An Earth Node was a geological anomaly beneath the surface of Faerûn . They usually existed only at points were the invisible streams of arcane magic that permeated Faerûn intersected . Those creatures in tune with arcane magic could sometimes sense the presence of a node . The power field of nodes varied from approximately 30 feet ( 9 meters ) to 1 / 2 mile ( 0 . 8 km . ) Description . The physical form of Earth Nodes varied but could take the form of a giant geode or a strangely regularly shaped cavern . Uses . Some arcane casters were able to tap into the power of a node and occasionally nodes could be used as teleportation devices .

title: Earth Spider
description: Earth Spider The Earth Spider was a terrible monster in Kozakura in 1358 DR . History . Once the Earth Spider ruled over Shou Lung but he and his legion were banished by the Celestial Emperor in the Realms of Mirrors .
description_long: Earth Spider The Earth Spider was a terrible monster in Kozakura in 1358 DR . History . Once the Earth Spider ruled over Shou Lung but he and his legion were banished by the Celestial Emperor in the Realms of Mirrors . He could not escape unless he wed a girl of Wood Spirit people . However , the Earth Spider could possess a human and used them his vessel . One of his vessels was the evil monk Jinchin , who led a revolt against the Shimamura Clan in Kanazaki Province . In truth , the Earth Spider wanted to capture the spirit woman Onoye , one of the companions of Doin Sanehiro , in order to fulfill the conditions for his release . However , in the end , Doin killed Jinchin , ending the Earth Spider ' s powers over Toril . In 1357 the Earth Spider had managed to dominate also the bakemono and goblin spider of the Keluh Valley in Chu ' Yuan province of Shou Lung .

title: Earth giant
description: Earth giant Earth giants were the most brutish of giant s , that lived in mountains , rocky barrens , canyons , and other such regions . Physical description . Earth giants were creatures whose bodies were made of rock and stone .
description_long: Earth giant Earth giants were the most brutish of giant s , that lived in mountains , rocky barrens , canyons , and other such regions . Physical description . Earth giants were creatures whose bodies were made of rock and stone . The eldest had halos of swirling stones and boulders constantly orbiting around them . Personality . Earth giants were cruel and territorial , and often enslaved weaker creatures . The mordrins were very calm as well , and unshakably loyal to the primordial Rorn the Fury . History . Most earth giants of Abeir were servants of Rorn the Fury . The first earth giants made by Rorn called themselves mordrins . A few of them founded the nation of Fimbrul in the continent of Laerakond . It was believed by some scholars that earth giants were the ones who created the galeb duhr as a slave race , and Fimbran earth giants indeed had galeb duhr servants .

title: Eartheart
description: Eartheart Eartheart is the principal settlement for the Gold Dwarves in East Rift and it is still the cultural and spiritual center for its people . Dwarves take on pilgrimages to behold the great holy city and take their trips from other countries and the deeps to reach their goal , it use to house great temples and shrines to all the Dwarven pantheon and dwarf heroes but after the great collapse much was lost . Leadership .
description_long: Eartheart Eartheart is the principal settlement for the Gold Dwarves in East Rift and it is still the cultural and spiritual center for its people . Dwarves take on pilgrimages to behold the great holy city and take their trips from other countries and the deeps to reach their goal , it use to house great temples and shrines to all the Dwarven pantheon and dwarf heroes but after the great collapse much was lost . Leadership . The lords of their old homes relocated here as well the Deep Lord s . The old ways of the Deep Lords are still the same as they use intermediaries and masking themselves to undermine the attempts of assassin s or drow infiltrators . The Gold Dwarves outnumber every other race in the city and therefor have full control of the city and it ' s communities . City expansion . After the fall of Underhome due to the weight of sea and stone the Gold Dwarves fled their broken home to take refuge in this more secure settlement . Other peoples and other dwarf races fled to Eartheart from their old homes and the surface . With the massive influx of people they had to expand the city ; a challenge the innovative dwarfs meet .

title: Eartheart defender
description: Eartheart defender Eartheart defenders , not to be confused with dwarven defender s , are an elite organization of dwarven divine spellcasters whose role it is to defend and serve the interests of East Rift , for whose capital the Eartheart defenders are named . With an unmovable spirit like the stones that make up dwarven cities , Eartheart defenders stand against the enemies of their race . Culture .
description_long: Eartheart defender Eartheart defenders , not to be confused with dwarven defender s , are an elite organization of dwarven divine spellcasters whose role it is to defend and serve the interests of East Rift , for whose capital the Eartheart defenders are named . With an unmovable spirit like the stones that make up dwarven cities , Eartheart defenders stand against the enemies of their race . Culture . Eartheart defenders are , like dwarven defenders , tied to the dwarven martial traditions and idea of brotherhood . However , while dwarven defenders see themselves as the defenders of their race , Eartheart defenders , in spite of their more localized origin , have a broader view and see themselves as defenders of the earth itself . To an Eartheart defender , the stones they walk upon are sacred and worthy of respect and dignity . Those who feel otherwise are the Eartheart defenders ' natural enemies . Eartheart defenders feel a bond amongst one another and see each other as simply a part of a greater whole .

title: Earthfast
description: Earthfast Earthfast was a shield dwarven city located in the Earthfast Mountains near Impiltur , from a high mountain valley to deep beneath in the Earthroot region of the Underdark . Though it was a war - torn city under constant siege from orcs and goblins , Earthfast was a capable ally of Cormyr and an able defender of Faerûn against the Tuigan Horde . History .
description_long: Earthfast Earthfast was a shield dwarven city located in the Earthfast Mountains near Impiltur , from a high mountain valley to deep beneath in the Earthroot region of the Underdark . Though it was a war - torn city under constant siege from orcs and goblins , Earthfast was a capable ally of Cormyr and an able defender of Faerûn against the Tuigan Horde . History . Dwarves from Earthfast founded the underground town of Proeskampalar in the Year of the Starry Shroud , −153 DR . That same year , it was joined by human refugees from fallen Jhaamdath ( what was later Chondath ) who also settled there . Proeskampalar thrived and became the city later known as Procampur . Earthfast weapon - smiths were commissioned to forge the " Greatsword of Impiltur " to mark the coronation of King Sarshel the True of neighboring Impiltur in the Year of the Proud Father , 732 DR . However , it could not be completed until the Year of the Splendid Stag , 734 DR , in time for the coronation of his son Halanter I . Halanter was known as " Arausamman " , or " Great Friend " , to the dwarves of Earthfast for centuries to come . At that time , Earthfast was ruled by Ironlord Barundar mac Idrin .

title: Earthfast Mountains
description: Earthfast Mountains The Earthfast Mountains , or simply the Earthfasts , were a small mountain range in north Faerûn , running from the Dragon Reach in the west , through the Vast and into Impiltur in the east . It was an arm of the greater Earthspur Mountains to the north . Geographical features .
description_long: Earthfast Mountains The Earthfast Mountains , or simply the Earthfasts , were a small mountain range in north Faerûn , running from the Dragon Reach in the west , through the Vast and into Impiltur in the east . It was an arm of the greater Earthspur Mountains to the north . Geographical features . Despite being somewhat smaller than the Earthspur Mountains , the Earthfast Mountains were jagged and only slightly less harsh , and just as hard to cross or climb . The mountains had rocky peaks and steep slopes , and were separated by abrupt gorges . Fortunately , a few passes permitted traffic through the range , connecting the north and south parts of the Vast . In the west , the High Trail ran through Elvenblood Pass , and in the east , the North Road ran through Glorming Pass . One famous but hidden peak in the Earthfasts was Iron Dragon Mountain . The Hill of Tombs was the southernmost point of the mountain range , lying in Impiltur near the coast of the Sea of Fallen Stars . The Fire River originated in these mountains and flowed west through the Vast into the Dragon Reach .

title: Earthfast plate
description: Earthfast plate Earthfast plate was a type of full plate armor forged by the shield dwarves of Earthfast in the Earthfast Mountains of north Faerûn . It was famous for its non - magical strength . Construction .
description_long: Earthfast plate Earthfast plate was a type of full plate armor forged by the shield dwarves of Earthfast in the Earthfast Mountains of north Faerûn . It was famous for its non - magical strength . Construction . Earthfast plate armor was a full plate armor of great strength , equivalent to " full plate + 2 " but without being magical . It was said to be as good as the work of the legendary lost Clan Ironstar . For this , it was extraordinarily expensive . History . Most suits of Earthfast armor were , naturally , designed for dwarves . Although the Earthfast dwarves could once be commissioned to make their armor for outsiders , they stopped when their city fell under constant siege from orc s and goblin s . They had barely enough time to make and maintain their own , let own forge new sets for others . Thus , the few suits sized for non - dwarves were usually well - guarded treasures of wealthy families , in Amn , Sembia , Waterdeep and other places . After Princess Alusair Obarskyr of Cormyr fought alongside the Earthfast dwarves in the Year of the Serpent , 1359 DR , they made her a suit of Earthfast plate armor made of finest mithril steel .

title: Earthmother
description: Earthmother The Earthmother was believed to be an aspect of the deity Chauntea , but in truth she was a primal spirit representing the power of nature on Toril . The Earthmother was venerated as a goddess by the Ffolk , the native human inhabitants of the Moonshae islands . The Earthmother had three " mortal " servants : The Leviathan , the Unicorn , and the Pack ( an enormous pack of well - coordinated wolves ) , each with powers beyond the usual for their kind due to the Earthmother ' s favor .
description_long: Earthmother The Earthmother was believed to be an aspect of the deity Chauntea , but in truth she was a primal spirit representing the power of nature on Toril . The Earthmother was venerated as a goddess by the Ffolk , the native human inhabitants of the Moonshae islands . The Earthmother had three " mortal " servants : The Leviathan , the Unicorn , and the Pack ( an enormous pack of well - coordinated wolves ) , each with powers beyond the usual for their kind due to the Earthmother ' s favor .

title: Earthquake
description: Earthquake Earthquake was an evocation or alteration spell that unleashed a powerful but localized tremor . Effect . The effect of the tremor depended on the type of terrain it was cast in , so a cavern would collapse and damage those caught in the collapse where heavily damaged .
description_long: Earthquake Earthquake was an evocation or alteration spell that unleashed a powerful but localized tremor . Effect .
