This gentle hymn clouds the minds of evil creatures , causing targets of the spell to forgo attacks of opportunity for the spell ' s duration .
description_long: Faerinaal ' s hymn Named for the consort to the eladrin queen Morwel , Faerinaal ' s hymn is an enchantment spell that prevents attacks of opportunity by evil creatures . Effect . This gentle hymn clouds the minds of evil creatures , causing targets of the spell to forgo attacks of opportunity for the spell ' s duration . A target must be able to hear the hymn to be affected by the spell .

title: Faerlthann Obarskyr
description: Faerlthann Obarskyr King Faerlthann Obarskyr was the first king of Cormyr . Appearance . Faerlthann was tall with tanned skin .
description_long: Faerlthann Obarskyr King Faerlthann Obarskyr was the first king of Cormyr . Appearance . Faerlthann was tall with tanned skin . Relatives . Faerlthann ' s father was Ondeth Obarskyr and his mother was Suzara Obarskyr . He had a brother called Rhiiman Obarskyr . He had four sons , Imlon , Embrus , Eskruis and Rhiiman . Background . Faerlthann came to the land that would become known as Suzail with his father , mother and younger brother in 6 DR , although his mother and brother left in 12 DR to return to Impiltur . Faerlthann was very disapproving of his father ' s secret relationship with Minda Bleth after it had been revealed , believing it to be a betrayal of his mother . After the death of his father Ondeth in 26 DR , Faerlthann was crowned after discussing the matter with Iliphar Nelnueve and his elven court . Baerauble Etharr was appointed as Faerlthann ' s advisor . The historical seat of power in Suzail , Faerlthann ' s Keep , takes its name from Faerlthann . Possessions . Faerlthann possessed the sword Ansrivarr , which was once Mondar Bleth ' s sword .

title: Faerntarn
description: Faerntarn The Royal Palace of Faertarn ( formerly Gallowglass Hall ) was the royal palace of Tethyr after the Reclamation Wars . Location . The palace was built upon the Ithal Crag within the Royal Quarter of the capital city of Darromar .
description_long: Faerntarn The Royal Palace of Faertarn ( formerly Gallowglass Hall ) was the royal palace of Tethyr after the Reclamation Wars . Location . The palace was built upon the Ithal Crag within the Royal Quarter of the capital city of Darromar . Sitting atop the hill , Faerntarn afforded a view of the whole city . Structure . The palace complex was composed of a main keep , a garrison building , and assorted other buildings all within a granite curtain wall . Defenses . The castle was entered through a gate with three . The towered walls provided defense , and each building contained additional protections as well . The knightly order known as the Warriors of the Star , many of whom were formerly members of Star Protective Services , defended the palace . Their barracks were in the South Tower of the castle . Interior . The garrison building provided housing for the royal guards and court staff . The original castle structure included 70 rooms , and these were used by the royal family , their direct advisers , and closest friends . History . Construction on the original castle was begun in the Year of the Hunted Elk ( 841 DR ) and completed two years later in the Year of Amber .

title: Faersynd Floshin
description: Faersynd Floshin Faersynd Floshin was one of the leaders of the daemonfey in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . Relationships . Faersynd ' s consort was Talya Floshin .
description_long: Faersynd Floshin Faersynd Floshin was one of the leaders of the daemonfey in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . Relationships . Faersynd ' s consort was Talya Floshin . History . Faersynd was the lord and patriarch of House Floshin . In 1270 DR , he joined the clergy of Ghaunadaur after he saw the god ' s power against Eaerlann . In 1370 DR , he tried to recruit a cult of followers of Ghaunadaur among fellow fey ' ri . He provided to Sarya Dlardrageth the services of some tanar ' ri servants of his god . Personality . Faersynd was truly devoted to Ghaunadaur . He tried to covert all people he met . Faersynd cared nothing for leading his House , a duty he left to his consort Talya . He believed that Xiiltharra Dlardlagleth had been a pawn of Ghaunadaur .

title: Faervian
description: Faervian Faervian is a Baneblade of Demron , the fourth in that series , and is in the shape of a longsword . It was originally created for the Spell - Major of Cormanthyr as a replacement for the lost " Ary ' Faern ' Kerym " elfblade ( the Artblade ) . It is known to humans as " Battlebane " , and more colloquially as the " Sword of Art " or the " Mage ' s Blade " .
description_long: Faervian Faervian is a Baneblade of Demron , the fourth in that series , and is in the shape of a longsword . It was originally created for the Spell - Major of Cormanthyr as a replacement for the lost " Ary ' Faern ' Kerym " elfblade ( the Artblade ) . It is known to humans as " Battlebane " , and more colloquially as the " Sword of Art " or the " Mage ' s Blade " . Appearance . Faervian looks as though it were forged from one solid piece of burnished steel , and it glows a deep purple when drawn . The craftsmanship of this blade , unlike the others , is distinctly elven . The hilt of the sword is longer than normal and gently twists , creating a good gripping surface . It has no quillons ( meaning there is no cross guard ) . Its distinctive feature is a large spherical " eye " that is placed at the top of the hilt ( between the blade and the hilt ) . The carved eye ' s pupil always faces outward , as if looking at its target , creating an eerie effect to its foes . The blade weighs half as much as a blade of its size should weigh , yet is quite strong . Like the other baneblades it has a corona of flames dancing along its edge , of purple color in the case of Faervian .

title: Faeryl Zauvirr
description: Faeryl Zauvirr Faeryl Zauvirr was the Ched Nasad an ambassador to Menzoberranzan from ca . 1358 DR to 1372 DR . Description .
description_long: Faeryl Zauvirr Faeryl Zauvirr was the Ched Nasad an ambassador to Menzoberranzan from ca . 1358 DR to 1372 DR . Description . Faeryl was tall and thickly built . She wielded a magical adamantine rod that morphed into the " Mother ' s Kiss " warhammer and also carried a crossbow . History . Faeryl served as ambassador to Menzoberranzan for fourteen years until 1372 DR . Umrae was one of Faeryl ' s retainers and worked as her scribe . She betrayed Faeryl to House Baenre in 1372 DR was was killed in ghoul form . In 1372 DR , caravans from Ched Nasad stopped arriving from outside the city . Faeryl approached Matron Mother Triel Baenre for permission to leave the city and investigate , but Triel , fearing that Faeryl would bring news of Menzoberranzan ' s weakness due to the Silence of Lolth , would not let her leave . Faeryl tried to escape with her retainers , and , indeed , they made it past the city ' s gates before a Bregan D ' aerthe team led by Valas Hune captured them and returned them to Triel . Triel locked Faeryl up and gave her to her son Jeggred to play with .

title: Faerzress
description: Faerzress Faerzress was a magic al radiation only found in the Underdark . It was said to be a remnant of the forces that shaped the Underdark terrain and it interfered with the casting of some spells . Faerzress and drow culture .
description_long: Faerzress Faerzress was a magic al radiation only found in the Underdark . It was said to be a remnant of the forces that shaped the Underdark terrain and it interfered with the casting of some spells . Faerzress and drow culture . " Faerzress " was a Drow word , and it played a major role in drow city planning . Drow sought out areas with strong " faerzress " to build their cities and outposts in to keep others from scrying their doings or teleporting inside the city . Drow also used faerzress to create magical artifacts . The dark elf mage Q ' arlynd Melarn discovered that " faerzress " was in fact created by Elven High Magic when the drow retreated to the Underdark so they could not escape by magical means . Effects on magic . " Faerzress " could affect magic and spellcasting in unpredictable ways , in some ways like wild magic . Although the knowledge of " faerzress " among surface - dwellers was sparse , it was known to mainly affect divination and conjuration spells , making teleport ing by magic in the Underdark a risky effort . Some areas in the Underdark had stronger " faerzress " emanations than others .

title: Faerûn
description: Faerûn Faerûn was a major continent on the planet of Toril . Geography . The continent included terrain that was as varied as any other .
description_long: Faerûn Faerûn was a major continent on the planet of Toril . Geography . The continent included terrain that was as varied as any other . Besides the exterior coastline to the west and south , the most dominant feature on the continent was the Sea of Fallen Stars . This was an irregular inland sea that kept the interior lands fertile and served as a major trade route for many of the bordering nations . Next in significance was the Shaar , a broad region of grasslands in the south that , together with the Lake of Steam , separated the area around the inland sea from the coastal nations at the southern edge of the continent . To the east , Faerûn was bordered by a vast region of steppes from Kara - Tur , and in the north were massive glaciers ( Pelvuria and Reghed ) and tundra . South of the continent , separated by the Great Sea , was the sub - tropical land of Zakhara . The continent included the following geographic and political regions . Northwest . A region of wilderness , difficult winter weather , orc hordes , and barbarian tribes , this region was generally referred to as " The North " .

title: Faerûnian languages
description: Faerûnian languages The Faerûnian languages were a family of languages spoken by the majority of human s on the continent of Faerûn . The Faerûnian language family encompassed roughly 50 distinct human languages , including Common . Language Groups .
description_long: Faerûnian languages The Faerûnian languages were a family of languages spoken by the majority of human s on the continent of Faerûn . The Faerûnian language family encompassed roughly 50 distinct human languages , including Common . Language Groups . The following language groups were considered by scholars to belong to the Faerûnian language family : Script . The vast majority of languages in this family used the Thorass alphabet .

title: Fagara
description: Fagara Fagara was a spice from T ' u Lung . It was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description .
description_long: Fagara Fagara was a spice from T ' u Lung . It was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description . Fagara was similar to peppercorns in taste and size , but also with an added numbness and a mild tingling sensation . It was very potent , so a small portion was sufficient even for large dishes .

title: Fahhas
description: Fahhas Fahhas was a city that lay between I ' tiraf and Hilm , where Al - Naqus River flowed into the Golden Gulf , in Zakhara . It was one of Cities of the Pantheon . Though blessed with fertile grazing areas and fruit orchards around it , and rich clays for pottery in its river valley , the city was characterized by the brooding mood of its ruler and citizens .
description_long: Fahhas Fahhas was a city that lay between I ' tiraf and Hilm , where Al - Naqus River flowed into the Golden Gulf , in Zakhara . It was one of Cities of the Pantheon . Though blessed with fertile grazing areas and fruit orchards around it , and rich clays for pottery in its river valley , the city was characterized by the brooding mood of its ruler and citizens . Their main motivation was said to be the search for spiritual betterment , so Fahhas was called " City of Searching " .

title: Failed Shadow Gate
description: Failed Shadow Gate A failed Shadow Gate was the result when an attempt to create a gate leading to the Plane of Shadow failed in some way . Rather than take a being to that plane , it risked subsuming their flesh with shadow , either killing them or transforming them into a dark creature . Effect .
description_long: Failed Shadow Gate A failed Shadow Gate was the result when an attempt to create a gate leading to the Plane of Shadow failed in some way . Rather than take a being to that plane , it risked subsuming their flesh with shadow , either killing them or transforming them into a dark creature . Effect . A being that dared walk through a failed Shadow Gate was taken — for one brief , stuttering instant — to the Plane of Shadow , and in that moment a kind of seed of shadow was implanted in their flesh . After traversing the failed gate , a heartbeat later , a change came over them . They felt a film of cold flow over their body , and their skin , clothes , and items all appeared blurred . At this point , the victim could either accept the change or resist it with a great force of will , but success was not guaranteed . Those who accepted or succumbed to the change saw their flesh and matter subsumed by shadow . This itself had only a 50 % chance of success , and of survival . Complete subsumption saw the being survive intact and gain a " shadow mantle " , which they could call up once a day to become a dark creature for some ten minutes at a time .

title: Fairin Icemantle
description: Fairin Icemantle Fairin Icemantle was a male sage of the 6th and 7th centuries DR . Fairin was the author of the " Treatise Against Blood - Metal " , in which he expressed his reservations about orcslayer blades whose steel was poisonous to orc s . He feared that they would lead to the development of other alloys toxic to many races , and spread death and destruction .
description_long: Fairin Icemantle Fairin Icemantle was a male sage of the 6th and 7th centuries DR . Fairin was the author of the " Treatise Against Blood - Metal " , in which he expressed his reservations about orcslayer blades whose steel was poisonous to orc s . He feared that they would lead to the development of other alloys toxic to many races , and spread death and destruction . His treatise also discussed the dwarven attack on the orc kingdom of Vastar in the Year of the Spellfire , 610 DR , in which the dwarves wielded the new orcslayer blades . This provided the only first - hand account of the conflict to later generations . Fairin described the dwarven slaughter of the orcs , saying that they " run in waist - high riot across the land " .

title: Faith of the Nine Travelers
description: Faith of the Nine Travelers The Faith of the Nine Travelers , or simply " the Nine Travelers " , was a faith common in Shou Lung and Wa in Kara - Tur . Dogma . The Faith of the Nine Travelers was less a faith or religion and more a set of customs and a philosophy .
description_long: Faith of the Nine Travelers The Faith of the Nine Travelers , or simply " the Nine Travelers " , was a faith common in Shou Lung and Wa in Kara - Tur . Dogma . The Faith of the Nine Travelers was less a faith or religion and more a set of customs and a philosophy . It held that Heaven was a vast mirror of the empire of Shou Lung , with its own empire , government , bureaucracy , and emperor . All of this in fact correctly described the Celestial Empire , which held spiritual authority over Kara - Tur , more closely than other religion . Nevertheless , outsiders tended to disbelieve it out of hand , for the simple fact that it seemed so banal and mundane . In particular , adherents followed the Nine Immortals , also known as the Nine Travelers , and held that they were enormously powerful beings of the Celestial Bureaucracy . Each was followed by a different sect . However , believers argued about which of the Nine was the leader , in which they were mistaken . A fundamental tenet of the faith was that even the lowest commoner could rise to become a ruler . This view was openly commended by the nobility but of course not exactly encouraged .

title: Faithful Mamluk Society
description: Faithful Mamluk Society The Faithful Mamluk Society , also known as the Faithful , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Faithful represented one of the more powerful mamluk societies in Qudra .
description_long: Faithful Mamluk Society The Faithful Mamluk Society , also known as the Faithful , was a military organization in Zakhara . Activities . The Faithful represented one of the more powerful mamluk societies in Qudra . In addition to their duties in Qudra , they loyally served the Grand Caliph in golden Huzuz . Organization . The Faithful were led by General Adun Abd al - Amin . Base of Operations . Most of the mamluk s of the Faithful lived and worked in Qudra , but a strong presence was maintained in Huzuz as well .

title: Faithless
description: Faithless The Faithless are mortals who do not have a divine patron . This could be because the mortal never worshiped a deity ( or rejected outright the worship of any deity ) , the mortal ' s divine patron has died , or that their divine patron rejected them for whatever reason . A soul who does worship a deity but did not sufficiently uphold their patron ' s dogma is instead judged False .
description_long: Faithless The Faithless are mortals who do not have a divine patron . This could be because the mortal never worshiped a deity ( or rejected outright the worship of any deity ) , the mortal ' s divine patron has died , or that their divine patron rejected them for whatever reason . A soul who does worship a deity but did not sufficiently uphold their patron ' s dogma is instead judged False . A Faithless soul receives only one sentence when it reaches The City of Judgment on the Fugue Plane : the Wall of the Faithless . The soul is bound onto the wall by a green mold that binds The Faithless ( and only The Faithless ) to the wall . Over time the soul dissolves into the very substance of the wall . Demon s propagate by stealing Faithless souls from the wall and retreating with them back to the Abyss . Other References . The video game presents the player with the option of forever destroying The Wall of The Faithless , so that The Faithless no longer endure any punishment in the afterlife .

title: Falchion
description: Falchion A Falchion is a large , single - edged , two - handed sword . Description . The falchion looks much like a big scimitar with a wide blade curved toward the tip .
description_long: Falchion A Falchion is a large , single - edged , two - handed sword . Description . The falchion looks much like a big scimitar with a wide blade curved toward the tip . The blade is one - sided and heavy , weighing as much as some greatsword s . The pommel , cross guard , and grip are similar to a bastard sword . An average falchion costs 75gp and weighs 8lbs ( 3 . 6kg ) . Use . The heavy blade of the falchion gives it an almost axe - like ability to chop through armor and yet retain the advantages of a sword . Its weight requires two hands and special training to wield effectively and is therefore considered a martial weapon . Realmslore . Several heroes of the realm , including Aoth Fezim and Gaedynn Ulraes , have wielded falchion swords .

title: Falcon
description: Falcon Falcons were small birds of prey , often used in hunting . Reputation . Falcons were a favored animal of the Mulhorandi god Anhur and the [ [ halfling ] god [ [ Arvoreen ] ] .
description_long: Falcon Falcons were small birds of prey , often used in hunting . Reputation . Falcons were a favored animal of the Mulhorandi god Anhur and the [ [ halfling ] god [ [ Arvoreen ] ] . They were sacred to the goddesses [ [ Milil ] ] and [ [ Red Knight ] ] as well . [ [ Moon elf | Moon elves ] ] had a special fondness for falcons and often kept them as pets . [ [ Centaur ] ] s within the forest of [ [ Cormanthor ] ] used falcons as scouts . In some [ [ human ] ] lands , such as [ [ Cormyr ] ] , formal education among the aristocracy included falconry . Some [ [ ranger ] ] s kept falcons as animal companions . Appendix . References . [ [ Category : Animals ] ] [ [ Category : Birds ] ]

title: Falcon ' s Wings
description: Falcon ' s Wings The Falcon ' s Wings was a ritual used by sha ' ir s to grant the permanent ability of flight to their gen s . Preparation . The sha ' ir needed to collect the feathers of a falcon taken directly from the falcon ' s aerie .
description_long: Falcon ' s Wings The Falcon ' s Wings was a ritual used by sha ' ir s to grant the permanent ability of flight to their gen s . Preparation . The sha ' ir needed to collect the feathers of a falcon taken directly from the falcon ' s aerie . It was vital to the success of the ritual that the sha ' ir collect the feathers themselves . Once collected , the feathers were glued to the gen using a special unguent . The associated materials needed to create the unguent cost 1 , 000 dinar s . The actual ritual lasted for 36 hours . If the ritual succeeded , the gen would be granted the permanent ability of flight with exceptional control and maneuverability . A gen could fly for up to one hour before exhaustion set in .

title: Falconsrise
description: Falconsrise Falconsrise was an island that lay west of the Singing Rocks in the Trackless Sea , off the coast of Calimshan in west Faerûn . Geography & Description . Falconsrise emerged alone from the sea , and it was too small to appear on many charts of the area .
description_long: Falconsrise Falconsrise was an island that lay west of the Singing Rocks in the Trackless Sea , off the coast of Calimshan in west Faerûn . Geography & Description . Falconsrise emerged alone from the sea , and it was too small to appear on many charts of the area . It was a windswept place , but managed a tiny , freshwater lake , enabling life to cling to it . It had no natural predators since the last rock cat was slain . History . Falconsrise was once the abode of Onthaer of Athkatla , a saintly hermit of Ilmater . Onthaer wrestled and killed the last rock cat on the island . The island was next the hermitage of the disgraced Archsufferer Bloirt Waelarn , sentenced to the island for triggering a holy war within the Church of Ilmater in 1267 DR . But as the ship took him to Falconsrise , Waelarn used his magic to murder most of the crew . An Ilmatari priest escaped the slaughter and locked himself in a cabin , using the brief opportunity to contact an archmage he knew , before Waelarn broke in and murdered him too . The archmage soon arrived , grabbed Waelarn off the ship , and delivered him to Falconsrise .

title: Falconstar Wayshipping
description: Falconstar Wayshipping Falconstar Wayshipping was a business located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . It rented out storage space for cargo . It was owned by Mhaernos Falconstar .
description_long: Falconstar Wayshipping Falconstar Wayshipping was a business located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . It rented out storage space for cargo . It was owned by Mhaernos Falconstar . Description & Defenses . Falconstar Wayshipping made up the southernmost reach of the city on the east bank of the Wyvernflow , " circa " 1369 DR , lying south of the Cormyrean Coins Coster compound . The business included a warehouse and a wharf , which were lit by " driftglobe " s . Two zombie ettin s guarded the wharf , guards watched the warehouse . Assisting these guards was some worse creature that twice killed and devoured whole raiding pirate bands . Services . The business rented storage space to caravan masters and ship captains transshipping or wayshipping their cargoes between land and river routes . History . Falconstar Wayshipping was in business by 1358 DR and still in business in 1369 DR . Famed traveler Volothamp Geddarm wrote about the business in " Volo ' s Guide to Cormyr " .

title: Faldorn
description: Faldorn Faldorn is a member of the Shadow Druids , a militant sect of druid s that believes in the violent struggle of nature against man . She disagrees vehemently with Jaheira and her mainstream druidic views of man co - existing peacefully alongside nature . However , despite her militant beliefs ( and extremely aggressive character portrait ) , Faldorn ' s speech and behavior in " Baldur ' s Gate " is surprisingly mellow and laid - back .
description_long: Faldorn Faldorn is a member of the Shadow Druids , a militant sect of druid s that believes in the violent struggle of nature against man . She disagrees vehemently with Jaheira and her mainstream druidic views of man co - existing peacefully alongside nature . However , despite her militant beliefs ( and extremely aggressive character portrait ) , Faldorn ' s speech and behavior in " Baldur ' s Gate " is surprisingly mellow and laid - back . She can be found in the Cloakwood forest fighting against the Iron Throne . Once the Iron Throne is dealt with , she travels south to a druid grove in Amn near Trademeet and with some of her Shadow Druid allies takes it over , sending animals to attack the town until defeated in a druidic combat ritual . She is voiced by Heidi Shannon .

title: Falgor
description: Falgor Falgor was a male human living in Port Llast on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . Falgor was the innkeeper of Alliance Arms Inn in Port Llast .
description_long: Falgor Falgor was a male human living in Port Llast on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . Falgor was the innkeeper of Alliance Arms Inn in Port Llast . Gameplay . The Kalach - Cha could talk with Falgor to learn about the people who visited his tavern .

title: Fall of Frostsilver
description: Fall of Frostsilver Fall of Frostsilver was an RPGA module set in Icewind Dale that was released at the 2007 Worldwide Dungeons & Dragons Game Day . It was written by Forgotten Realms Continuity Editor Matthew Sernett in honor of the 20th anniversary of the creation of Drizzt Do ' Urden . Summary .
description_long: Fall of Frostsilver Fall of Frostsilver was an RPGA module set in Icewind Dale that was released at the 2007 Worldwide Dungeons & Dragons Game Day . It was written by Forgotten Realms Continuity Editor Matthew Sernett in honor of the 20th anniversary of the creation of Drizzt Do ' Urden . Summary . A party of adventurers in Icewind Dale have discovered an ancient trail map that marks the location of a dwarven hold called Frostsilver . They are urged on to explore the site by a pair of dwarf brothers , who recognize it as their ancestral clanhold . Upon entering the place though , they find it occupied by goblinoid s led by a pair of Underdark slavers . Appendix . Notes . The cover art was a recycled image used on the cover of the module " Scourge of the Howling Horde " , which had been released the previous year .

title: Fall of Zhentil Keep
description: Fall of Zhentil Keep The Fall of Zhentil Keep started on Nightal 27 1368 DR and lasted until Kythorn 13 1369 DR . Background . The attack was but one part of Cyric ' s plan to consolidate and increase his divine powers since the rules of divinity had been changed by Ao in the wake of the Time of Troubles .
description_long: Fall of Zhentil Keep The Fall of Zhentil Keep started on Nightal 27 1368 DR and lasted until Kythorn 13 1369 DR . Background . The attack was but one part of Cyric ' s plan to consolidate and increase his divine powers since the rules of divinity had been changed by Ao in the wake of the Time of Troubles . He summoned a monstrous army of humanoids and mighty frost creatures from the north and instructed them to lay siege to Zhentil Keep . He hoped that the sight of such an army approaching would galvanize his worshipers faith in him as they prayed for salvation and then he would appear in person , banish the army and recieve the adulations of the keep ' s inhabitants . This , in turn , would give him the divine power to quell a rebellion that was brewing in the City of Strife on the Fugue Plane . To start it all off , he planned that his high priest Xeno Mirrormane would publically read from the " Cyrinishad " , a book enspelled to turn any who read or heard the words into a devout worshiper of Cyric . Nothing went to plan . Another book had been written and the Cyrinishad was replaced with it , read by Fzoul Chembryl who only reluctantly worshiped Cyric .

title: Fallen Giant Rift
description: Fallen Giant Rift Fallen Giant Rift was a crack in the earth within the Plain of Standing Stones in Anauroch . Description . Fallen Giant Rift was located east of the Tagorlar mountain range within the Plain of Standing Stones .
description_long: Fallen Giant Rift Fallen Giant Rift was a crack in the earth within the Plain of Standing Stones in Anauroch . Description . Fallen Giant Rift was located east of the Tagorlar mountain range within the Plain of Standing Stones . The rift was a crooked and branched canyon or ravine that stretched for nearly 24 miles ( 39 kilometers ) and was more than three miles ( five kilometers ) wide in places . At a depth of several hundred feet ( about a hundred meters ) , the floor of the rift was packed - down earth covered in thick grasses — a rare haven of life within the otherwise arid Plain of Standing Stones . Here lived long - horned antelope , sheep , and goats . A spring at one end of the rift provided water for the hidden valley , and this source of water fed several pools throughout the ravine . Gold veins were found in some of the caves within the rift . Inhabitants . Living within caves in the rift walls overlooking the pools were hill giant s . They would hurl large rocks down upon anyone coming to drink the water in their pools , and they kept the wild herd populations from growing out of control .

title: Fallen Lands
description: Fallen Lands The Fallen Lands are an rocky , barren area just west of Anauroch . This is the present - day ( circa 1479 DR ) name for the strip of habitable land west of Anauroch , stretching between the Far Forest ( now overrun by evil things out of Hellgate Keep ) and Weathercote Wood . The Fallen Lands are now home only to monsters , it seems , although rumors persist of powerful mages inhabiting the southern end , and hurling back the evil creatures of Hellgate Keep with their art .
description_long: Fallen Lands The Fallen Lands are an rocky , barren area just west of Anauroch . This is the present - day ( circa 1479 DR ) name for the strip of habitable land west of Anauroch , stretching between the Far Forest ( now overrun by evil things out of Hellgate Keep ) and Weathercote Wood . The Fallen Lands are now home only to monsters , it seems , although rumors persist of powerful mages inhabiting the southern end , and hurling back the evil creatures of Hellgate Keep with their art . This was once part of the realm of Netheril , a kingdom of mages who could not stem the expansion of the Great Desert ; some sages say that many of them set out south across the Realms to find a new home , and founded the present - day realm of Halruaa . Reports from the adventurers Vanthorm and Haladan indicate that when they visited The Fallen Lands some five winters ago , they observed a beholder of awesome size directing hobgoblin servants to capture monstrous beasts and conduct a strange bestial breeding program .

title: Fallentree
description: Fallentree Fallentree was a village in the Vast , lying where Feldar ' s Trail from Dark Hollow met Blaern ' s Trail between Sendrin and Dead Tree Hollow . History . The area was once plagued by bandits , who lurked in the pine woods and ambushed travelers on the road .
description_long: Fallentree Fallentree was a village in the Vast , lying where Feldar ' s Trail from Dark Hollow met Blaern ' s Trail between Sendrin and Dead Tree Hollow . History . The area was once plagued by bandits , who lurked in the pine woods and ambushed travelers on the road . Some charged upon their victims , while others dropped tall pine trees across the road to force caravans to stop . In time , the merchants stopped passing through , and so the bandits had to increase their range . Eventually , merchants going through the Fallentree area gathered into great caravans with armies of guards . Bandit raids became sizable battles , and the most powerful gangs were destroyed . Smaller gangs remained in the area by 1370 DR , but swiftly came and went due to death or infighting . Description . Fallentree was a village lying by the side of the road , named — obviously — for its fallen trees . The lands around were rolling hills with about a dozen small woods of dark pine s . The village was known for its horse farms . Local legends .

title: Falrinn Greathorm
description: Falrinn Greathorm Fulrinn Greathorm was a strange gnome smuggler incidentally involved in the Second Sundering in 1486 DR . History . In 1486 DR , Falrinn transported the reaver Anton Marivaldi out of the city of Westgate in order to meet with the boy Chosen of Lathander , Stedd Whitehorn .
description_long: Falrinn Greathorm Fulrinn Greathorm was a strange gnome smuggler incidentally involved in the Second Sundering in 1486 DR . History . In 1486 DR , Falrinn transported the reaver Anton Marivaldi out of the city of Westgate in order to meet with the boy Chosen of Lathander , Stedd Whitehorn . Afterward , he transported Anton ' s group for a time . Later , Falrinn transported Arietta Seasilver ; Kleef Kenric , paladin follower of the dead god Helm ; and two Chosen , Malik el Sami , follower of Cyric , and Joelle Emmeline , follower of Sune , out of Marsember along with his ship , the " Lonely Roamer " .

title: False life
description: False life False life was a necromancy spell that granted the caster a temporary boost of health above his or her normal healthy state . Effects . This spell only affected the caster and lasted a number of hours per the power of the caster , or until the extra health was lost ( due to injury or disease , for example ) , whichever came first .
description_long: False life False life was a necromancy spell that granted the caster a temporary boost of health above his or her normal healthy state . Effects . This spell only affected the caster and lasted a number of hours per the power of the caster , or until the extra health was lost ( due to injury or disease , for example ) , whichever came first . After the Second Sundering , the spell would grant a higher temporary health boost depending what level the spell was cast as . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , the caster had to draw mystical sigils on his or her body with a small quantity of alcohol or distilled spirits . The sigils faded from view when the alcohol evaporated .

title: False vision
description: False vision False vision is an illusion spell that fools scrying with an illusion . Effect . You and all you desire within the area of the spell become undetectable to scrying ( whether by spell or magic device ) .
description_long: False vision False vision is an illusion spell that fools scrying with an illusion . Effect . You and all you desire within the area of the spell become undetectable to scrying ( whether by spell or magic device ) . Furthermore , if you are aware of an attempt to scry , you can create whatever image you desire , including sight and sound , according to the medium of the scrying method . To do this , you must concentrate on the figment you are creating . Once concentration is broken , no further images can be created , although the area remains undetectable for the duration of the spell . Material component . The ground dust of a jade worth at least 250 gp , which is sprinkled into the air when the spell is cast .

title: Falstaff
description: Falstaff Falstaff was one of the many Doomguide s who were part of the contingent in Neverdeath Graveyard in Neverwinter in 1484 DR . He and some of his fellows were lost in the graveyard after an assault by undead . Falstaff was killed when pierced by arrows .
description_long: Falstaff Falstaff was one of the many Doomguide s who were part of the contingent in Neverdeath Graveyard in Neverwinter in 1484 DR . He and some of his fellows were lost in the graveyard after an assault by undead . Falstaff was killed when pierced by arrows . To prevent him from being resurrected by necromancers , an adventurer recruited to rescue the lost Doomguides burned his body .

title: Faltyn Gos
description: Faltyn Gos Zor Faltyn Gos was a noble in Mulmaster . Personality . Faltyn indulged in self - appreciation , always reminding everyone of his contributions to the city .
description_long: Faltyn Gos Zor Faltyn Gos was a noble in Mulmaster . Personality . Faltyn indulged in self - appreciation , always reminding everyone of his contributions to the city . He became very upset if not called by his correct title of " Zor Gos " . History . Faltyn was a member of the Blade s . In 1491 DR , he competed with other Blades over arts . Thus , for the birthday of his wife Tiega Gos , Faltyn commissioned his nephew Andrik Gos to make a painting of her and hired Marim Tem as a musician . However , during the party , his wife was the target of a mysterious attack , so he decided to hire an adventuring party to uncover the truth .

title: Falwan Underbough
description: Falwan Underbough Falwan Underbough was a community leader in Cormanthor . History . Falwan was a famous baker in Hillsfar , known among nobility for his " half cakes " until the reintroduction of the First Great Law of Humanity by Torin Nomerthal forced Falwan and his family to escape the city .
description_long: Falwan Underbough Falwan Underbough was a community leader in Cormanthor . History . Falwan was a famous baker in Hillsfar , known among nobility for his " half cakes " until the reintroduction of the First Great Law of Humanity by Torin Nomerthal forced Falwan and his family to escape the city . He took refuge in Cormanthor with many other non - human refugees . In time , they formed a small community and Falwan somehow became their leader and spokesman . During the Rage of Demons , he was afraid of numerous drow arriving on the surface in the area . Personality . Falwan was very proud of his work as a baker and suffered for the loss of his business . He was a friendly individual but experience made him cautious toward armed human s . Relationship . Falwan had good dealings with Elanil Elassidil and the leaders of Elventree .

title: Falzo Hawklin
description: Falzo Hawklin Lord Falzo Hawklin was a noble of the Hawklin family and a commander among Alusair Obarskyr ' s Blades . Lord Falzo Hawklin resided in a modestly sized manor on the northern side of Suzail ' s great Promenade with extensive gardens . Description .
description_long: Falzo Hawklin Lord Falzo Hawklin was a noble of the Hawklin family and a commander among Alusair Obarskyr ' s Blades . Lord Falzo Hawklin resided in a modestly sized manor on the northern side of Suzail ' s great Promenade with extensive gardens . Description . Smooth - voiced , tall , dark - featured , and dressed in flawless black garb , Falzo appeared to be every bit the image of what a noble should be . As a young man he was known to be incredibly handsome . Personality . Quick of wit and intellect , Falzo Hawklin bore himself with the mature comportment and relaxed manners of one of the most sophisticated nobles , even in his younger years . Possessions . Falzo carried several magical devices , such as a " ring of mind shielding " , a " ring of protection " , and " bracers of armor " , and he could often be seen wearing a magical and ceremonial - looking , ornate dagger at his side . History . In mid - 1372 DR , Lord Falzo Hawklin was instructed by Alusair , the Steel Regent , to wipe out a group of bandits spotted in some ruins near the Black Crater of Tilverton .

title: Familiar
description: Familiar A familiar is a normal creature that has been summoned to service by a sorcerer or wizard , after which it becomes a magical beast and gains new powers . They are magically linked to their masters , in some sense , practically existing as one being . All familiars have special abilities along with granting special abilities to its master .
description_long: Familiar A familiar is a normal creature that has been summoned to service by a sorcerer or wizard , after which it becomes a magical beast and gains new powers . They are magically linked to their masters , in some sense , practically existing as one being . All familiars have special abilities along with granting special abilities to its master . Acquiring a Familiar . In order to aquire a familiar , the prospective master must first locate the kind of creature desired . This can be as convenient a task as visiting a city and purchasing a suitable animal within an appropriate shop . Some more exotic familiars usually take more effort to locate . After locating the familiar , the master must arrange to keep the familiar nearby for the day - long ritual that binds the two together . Wise masters choose familiars that are friendly enough not to wander away , but sometimes the creature must be caged or otherwise restrained . There are various rituals that bind familiars to spellcasters , ranging from a few gestures or chants to some drawings sketched on the floor around the pair – all repeated necessarily at intervals throughout the day .

title: Fandour
description: Fandour Fandour is an entity of unkown nature imprisoned in a pocket plane . The reasons for his imprionment are unclear , although the Githyanki may have been responsible . A Gith on a merchant vessel that was sunk by Moonsea pirates in 1460 DR possessed a bracelet known as the Rythanko that was tied to Fandour .
description_long: Fandour Fandour is an entity of unkown nature imprisoned in a pocket plane . The reasons for his imprionment are unclear , although the Githyanki may have been responsible . A Gith on a merchant vessel that was sunk by Moonsea pirates in 1460 DR possessed a bracelet known as the Rythanko that was tied to Fandour . The bracelet was taken by a young pirate named Gareth Jadaren and was later used to steal some of Fandour ' s power to create the wards of Jadaren ' s Hold . Over the millenia , Fandour ' s consciousness reached out to the Prime Material Plane and made contact with several humans . Fandour was able to subconsciously contact the monks of Shadrun of the Snows , which he refers to as the Nexus , and influence them to create ritual drawings which may help free him from his prison . Fandour refers to both the drawings and those he influences as Vectors . Fandour was nearly released in 1600 DR , but his plans were largely derailed ( albeit unintentionally ) by the deva Lakini .

title: Fane of Lolth
description: Fane of Lolth The Fane of Lolth was a temple dedicated to Lolth in Szith Morcane that was open for the denizens of the settlement to come and worship . Location . Located above the seat of House Morcane in Szith Morcane , the Fane of Lolth was reached only by ascending one of its eight spiderweb ladders .
description_long: Fane of Lolth The Fane of Lolth was a temple dedicated to Lolth in Szith Morcane that was open for the denizens of the settlement to come and worship . Location . Located above the seat of House Morcane in Szith Morcane , the Fane of Lolth was reached only by ascending one of its eight spiderweb ladders . Structure . The Fane of Lolth was constructed in the semblance of an enormous spider . Eight spiderweb ladders comprised its legs and descended to House Morcane beneath it . Interior . Inside the Fane of Lolth , the temple was separated into the outer fane ( which formed the forepart of the spider - structure ) and the inner fane ( which formed the abdomen section of the spider - structure ) . These two sections were divided by a heavy iron gate that could only be passed safely by female drow worshipers of Lolth . The outer fane was shaped to appear like the front section of a gigantic spider . An altar on a raised platform resided in the area that was constructed in the likeness of the spider ' s fangs . The inner fane comprised a pair of short , curved walls within which was a long sacrificial altar .

title: Fane of Quarvelsharess
description: Fane of Quarvelsharess The Fane of Quarvelsharess , also called the Fane of the Goddess , was a public cathedral dedicated to Lolth in the district of West Wall in Menzoberranzan . History . The Fane of the Quarvelsharess was a " gift " of House Baenre , providing , for the first time , a place for the general public to worship .
description_long: Fane of Quarvelsharess The Fane of Quarvelsharess , also called the Fane of the Goddess , was a public cathedral dedicated to Lolth in the district of West Wall in Menzoberranzan . History . The Fane of the Quarvelsharess was a " gift " of House Baenre , providing , for the first time , a place for the general public to worship . Its construction out of stone was an " epic union of artistry and engineering " that was completed in 1475 DR . Staff . Sos ' Umptu Baenre was a high priestess at the Fane .

title: Fane of Shadows
description: Fane of Shadows The Fane of Shadows was a that journeyed the worlds on the currents of the secret Weave . The place had many names in many tongues , and was also known as the Temple of Night or the Umbral Shrine . Location .
description_long: Fane of Shadows The Fane of Shadows was a that journeyed the worlds on the currents of the secret Weave . The place had many names in many tongues , and was also known as the Temple of Night or the Umbral Shrine . Location . Created by Shar , it served as many dark gods of many worlds , and as a gift of the god of shadows to their faithful ; a sanctuary that journeyed through time and worlds . It also served as a bastion and armory for the servants of the twilight . It was located within the Lightless Lake ( the Moonmere ) in the Gulthmere Forest , but it only materialized during a certain date at midnight , and stayed only temporarily in each world for a short time . Upon its arrival onto Toril , the Fane appeared within the depths of the Lightless Lake in a diffuse , ochre light . The entirety of the temple was situated on an invisible platform encapsulated within a dome of air . The architecture included black - veined columns , graceful arches , and thick pillars all crafted from marble , basalt , obsidian , or ebony . The Fane of Shadows was guarded by a host of shadow s inside the courtyard area . They were only hostile to those not subservient to shadow . Interior .

title: Fane of the Eye
description: Fane of the Eye The Fane of the Eye was a large cavern complex deep under the Dessarin Valley . It was centered around a black ziggurat temple built by renegade drow and dedicated to the Elder Elemental Eye . The cult that built it eventually died out or were hunted by drow loyal to Lolth .
description_long: Fane of the Eye The Fane of the Eye was a large cavern complex deep under the Dessarin Valley . It was centered around a black ziggurat temple built by renegade drow and dedicated to the Elder Elemental Eye . The cult that built it eventually died out or were hunted by drow loyal to Lolth . The complex remained abandoned until Vizeran DeVir found it and used it to forge the weapons " Ironfang " , " Drown " , " Tinderstike " , and " Windvane " . He left the weapons there until the Fane of the Eye was found in 1491 DR by the latest incarnation of the Cult of Elemental Evil .

title: Fanedown
description: Fanedown Fanedown was one of the river ports along the coast of the Sword River in the Sword Lands , Returned Abeir . Background . Fanedown was known for its many minstrels , jesters , and because , as of 1479 DR , was one of the few places in Returned Abeir where books were published .
description_long: Fanedown Fanedown was one of the river ports along the coast of the Sword River in the Sword Lands , Returned Abeir . Background . Fanedown was known for its many minstrels , jesters , and because , as of 1479 DR , was one of the few places in Returned Abeir where books were published .

title: Faneuil Hardisty
description: Faneuil Hardisty Baron Faneuil Hardisty was a warrior of Tethyr who attempted to bring an end to the anarchy within the region by any means available to him . Background . Along with Zaranda Star , Faneuil was a captain in King Azoun ' s crusade against the Tuigan Horde .
description_long: Faneuil Hardisty Baron Faneuil Hardisty was a warrior of Tethyr who attempted to bring an end to the anarchy within the region by any means available to him . Background . Along with Zaranda Star , Faneuil was a captain in King Azoun ' s crusade against the Tuigan Horde . They met again later when he became the most prominent member of the Council of Lords . Faneuil sought to restore the order within Tethyr by placing himself on the nation ' s throne . As it turned out , he was being used as a pawn by a creature known as the deepspawn . Allied with the Lords ' Council and the bureaucracies of Zazesspur , Faneuil crowned himself king and became prey for the deepspawn . Appearance . Baron Hardisty was handsome , with brown eyes and short , graying hair .

title: Fang
description: Fang The Fang was a large promontory extending north into the Sea of Fallen Stars from Aglarond . Geography . It was a mostly barren and rocky piece of land that jutted out from the northern coast of Aglarond , marking the beginning of the Sea of Dlurg .
description_long: Fang The Fang was a large promontory extending north into the Sea of Fallen Stars from Aglarond . Geography . It was a mostly barren and rocky piece of land that jutted out from the northern coast of Aglarond , marking the beginning of the Sea of Dlurg . The area was battered by storms almost constantly , and seas were often violent . Reefs surrounded the coastline . Government . The Fangers ruled themselves , wanting nothing to do with the Royal Council of Aglarond , but were still considered Aglarondan citizens . History . The Fang came to prominence in history after the humans of Velprin were defeated by the half - elves of the Yuirwood in the 1060s by Dalereckoning . While the majority of the defeated humans who rejected half - elven rule would soon found Altumbel , a few hundred went north instead to settle the Fang . Inhabitants . " Fangers " was a derogatory term given to the human inhabitants of the Fang . The vast majority of them were descendents of the wave of migrants from the fall of Velprin . Sea elves had several villages among the coastal reefs . Rumors and Legends .

title: Fang dragon
description: Fang dragon A fang dragon , also known as a gray dragon , was type of dragon found in Faerûn . Description . Fang dragons were poor flyers , with small muscled wings .
description_long: Fang dragon A fang dragon , also known as a gray dragon , was type of dragon found in Faerûn . Description . Fang dragons were poor flyers , with small muscled wings . Their eyes tended to be either red or orange . Their heads were edged with spikes or horns . Their bodies tended to be covered in bony plates that ended in spurs at the joints , and their tails were forked with scythe - like tips . Ecology . These dragons were also susceptible to bouts of seemingly random outbursts of rage and violence . They typically spoke a small handful of languages , and they used this ability in order to negotiate their way out of situations that could result in difficult or even deadly battles . They sometimes sealed up their lairs with boulders or other materials before leaving them , usually in the hunt for food , which they preferred to find far from their homes . Their diet consisted of flesh , of which they prefered that of intelligent animals . History . Fang dragons were first encountered in the ruins of Myth Drannor , which has led to speculation that they were connected to the demon ic inhabitants that resided there after its fall .

title: Fang in the Forest
description: Fang in the Forest The Fang in the Forest , formerly known as Daerlo ' s Rest , was a conical - shaped peak and the southernmost of the Earthfast Mountains . It was thought to have been an extinct volcano and was said to be partially hollow . Inhabitants .
description_long: Fang in the Forest The Fang in the Forest , formerly known as Daerlo ' s Rest , was a conical - shaped peak and the southernmost of the Earthfast Mountains . It was thought to have been an extinct volcano and was said to be partially hollow . Inhabitants . The peak was best known as the lair of the ancient green dragon Aglaraerose . Deep inside the mountain was her lair , which she named the Lure of Jaws . History . The peak was originally known as " Daerlo ' s Rest " after a local forester who was gored by a boar and laid to rest on the mountainside . In the later 14th century DR , Aglaraerose built a lair in the mountain and was still believed to inhabit the peak in the late 15th century DR , although she was never seen .

title: Fang scarab
description: Fang scarab A fang scarab was a medallion that gave any spider that wore it the ability to hear the dark whispers of Lolth and guide it in battle . However , any non - spider who wore the medallion found it would fuse to their neck and slowly transform them into a half - spider creature . Description .
description_long: Fang scarab A fang scarab was a medallion that gave any spider that wore it the ability to hear the dark whispers of Lolth and guide it in battle . However , any non - spider who wore the medallion found it would fuse to their neck and slowly transform them into a half - spider creature . Description . Made of crystal and shaped like a fang , a " fang scarab " typically hung from a finely crafted silver chain . The chain was designed to fit over a spider ' s head and body . Creation . They were crafted almost exclusively by worshipers of Lolth for their spider servants . However , occasionally a " fang scarab " fell into the hands of overly curious rogues or bards . Powers . The " fang scarab " granted its wearer access to the insidious whispers of Lolth , which would help to guide it in the midst of battle . However , as this item was primarily designed for spider s , it would only function for non - spiders if they could somehow unlock its secrets and fuse the scarab to their neck . Though the whispers of Lolth could still aid non - spiders , the process of fusing the scarab to their neck exacted a horrific price as they were transformed into a deformed spider - like creature .

title: Fangjaws Hold
description: Fangjaws Hold Fangjaws Hold was a collection of palisade stone lodges in Thar . Inhabitants . The hold was home to the Skullsmashers ogre tribe lead by Zar - Umak .
description_long: Fangjaws Hold Fangjaws Hold was a collection of palisade stone lodges in Thar . Inhabitants . The hold was home to the Skullsmashers ogre tribe lead by Zar - Umak . The tribe had numerous goblin guards who watched over a group of human and dwarven prisoners . History . Around , 1373 DR , Fangjaws Hold was named for the massive wooden gate which was covered with hundreds of bulette teeth making it look like a fearsome jaw .

title: Fangs of Night shuriken
description: Fangs of Night shuriken The Fangs of Night ninja clan of the city of Ojy - do in Koryo were known for a set of five magical stone shuriken , each carried by the five top warriors of the clan . Description . Strangely , these shuriken were carved of stone .
description_long: Fangs of Night shuriken The Fangs of Night ninja clan of the city of Ojy - do in Koryo were known for a set of five magical stone shuriken , each carried by the five top warriors of the clan . Description . Strangely , these shuriken were carved of stone . Powers . Once thrown , these shuriken never missed their targets . They inflicted greater injury than was typical , and victim could fall unconscious .

title: Fangs of retribution
description: Fangs of retribution Fangs of retribution was a divine evocation spell that dealt back all the injuries the caster had suffered . Effect . The spell created the ghostly jaws and fangs of a viper in front of the caster ' s face , who could then direct it to fly at and bite a foe of their choice .
description_long: Fangs of retribution Fangs of retribution was a divine evocation spell that dealt back all the injuries the caster had suffered . Effect . The spell created the ghostly jaws and fangs of a viper in front of the caster ' s face , who could then direct it to fly at and bite a foe of their choice . This bite dealt back all the injuries the caster had suffered from their chosen foe that day ; if the targeted creature had not harmed the caster that day , then the " fangs " had no effect . It functioned similarly to the " Ilmater ' s fist " spell . Components . The spell required the fang of any type of snake , venomous or not . History . The " fangs of retribution " spell appeared within the " Tome of Torment " , the holiest book of the church of Ilmater , which first appeared in the Realms in 848 DR .

title: Fangshields
description: Fangshields The Fangshields are a group of talking animals and good - aligned monsters who operate all over the wild areas of Faerûn . They seek out and stop evil monsters and organizations from carrying out their plans . Until very recently the group was not organized at all , simply a few monsters doing good deeds whenever they could but recently there has been an increase in the number of worshipers of Lurue and Nobanion , whom most of the group ' s members consider their patron deities .
description_long: Fangshields The Fangshields are a group of talking animals and good - aligned monsters who operate all over the wild areas of Faerûn . They seek out and stop evil monsters and organizations from carrying out their plans . Until very recently the group was not organized at all , simply a few monsters doing good deeds whenever they could but recently there has been an increase in the number of worshipers of Lurue and Nobanion , whom most of the group ' s members consider their patron deities . Also the number of evil monsters have gone up as well . In response , the Fangshields have banded together to concentrate their efforts , using humanoid messengers to impart their plans to cells that they , themselves couldn ' t reach as monsters tend to attract too much attention on human - built roads . Structure . Most members still operate on their own but in the face of greater threats they sometimes band together in small groups . They go about business in much the same way as the Harpers do , though they are more quick to retreat as increased interest from other parties could lead to an unacceptable loss in membership .

title: Fankiang
description: Fankiang The Fankiang were a tribe of nomadic human s living on the Plain of Horses in the Hordelands . Territory . The Fankiang lived in the eastern regions of the Endless Waste .
description_long: Fankiang The Fankiang were a tribe of nomadic human s living on the Plain of Horses in the Hordelands . Territory . The Fankiang lived in the eastern regions of the Endless Waste . Their lands bordered those of the Pazruki , Kashghun , Quirish , Zamogedi , and Gur tribes . Society . They spoke the Fankiang dialect of the Chuchian tongue . The Fankiang had no true allies among the tribes of the Endless Wastes , and they were particularly hostile to the Commani , the Quirish , the Tuigan , and the Dalat tribes . History . The Fankiang ' s feud with the Commani began long ago , during a " couralitai " , a grand council of the " khans " ( princes of the villages ) , when all the tribes were in attendance . During a heated argument at the council , the " khan " of the Commani and his sons were assassinated . The murderers were never discovered , but the Commani blamed the Fankiang for defending the attackers . This led to hatred between the two groups , which lasted even into the 14 century . Over the years , the Fankiang and Quirish raided each other , with the Quirish usually losing .

title: Fansa Windblossom
description: Fansa Windblossom Fansa Windblossom was one of the four Cloakmasters of Eshpurta for the Shadow Thieves around 1370 DR . History . Fansa was abandoned by her elven mother and grew up with a pair of married rangers .
description_long: Fansa Windblossom Fansa Windblossom was one of the four Cloakmasters of Eshpurta for the Shadow Thieves around 1370 DR . History . Fansa was abandoned by her elven mother and grew up with a pair of married rangers . One day , however , she tired of their preachings and killed them and stole all their valuables , which she sold . With the money , she enrolled in a wizard school . Later , she joined the Shadow Thieves , where she rose to the status of Cloakmaster . She was once seriously scarred fighting a mad efreeti . Personality . Fansa was very self - reliant and expected that all her underlings acted the same . She had only a minimal relationship with other local Cloakmasters .

title: Fantastic machine
description: Fantastic machine Fantastic machine is an illusion spell that creates an illusory and very noisy mechanical contraption . It is solely available to cleric s who worship deities of the craft or gnome domain s . Effect .
description_long: Fantastic machine Fantastic machine is an illusion spell that creates an illusory and very noisy mechanical contraption . It is solely available to cleric s who worship deities of the craft or gnome domain s . Effect . When cast , " fantastic machine " creates an illusory , many - armed , noisy mechanical construct of impressively - massive appearance . The caster can command the machine to perform any simple , physical task that they can describe in twenty - five words or less . They can order the machine to perform the same task over and over , but can ' t change the task . The caster must specify the task when he or she casts the spell . The machine is capable of swimming or flying , but does so clumsily ; its most common form of movement is walking or running . It can carry up to seven hundred pounds , but does so slowly , and can not fly or swim if carrying over two hundred and thirty pounds . It can lift a weight of up to one thousand , four hundred pounds to a height of fifteen feet ; push or drag thirty - five hundred pounds ; can excavate seven thousand pounds of loose rock each minute ; and can excavate sand or loose soil at twice that rate .

title: Fanya bint Parigar
description: Fanya bint Parigar Fanya bint Parigar was in charge of the Grand University of Huzuz located in the Pilgrims ' District of the City of Delights in 1367 DR . Activities . Fanya was a priest of Zann .
description_long: Fanya bint Parigar Fanya bint Parigar was in charge of the Grand University of Huzuz located in the Pilgrims ' District of the City of Delights in 1367 DR . Activities . Fanya was a priest of Zann . She was a proficient teacher who knew several languages , including Shou Lin from the distant northeast . She dreamed of the day that her school would be the grandest in all of Huzuz , though in reality she had a lot of work to do to accomplish such a feat .

title: Far Anchor
description: Far Anchor Far Anchor was a large inn on the north side of Far Rider Street in Scornubel . It was built in around 1365 DR by a retired sea captain and its name referred to the distance by river barge to the Sword Coast . Description .
description_long: Far Anchor Far Anchor was a large inn on the north side of Far Rider Street in Scornubel . It was built in around 1365 DR by a retired sea captain and its name referred to the distance by river barge to the Sword Coast . Description . It had large and bright rooms with simple furniture and baths and was full most of the time . It had the largest communal dining room in Scornubel and it was open to non - guests . The guests tended to be the wealthier visitors to the city . In addition to the baths in each room , there was a warm bath in the cellar of the building . Staff . The staff of the Far Anchor were all retired adventurers , and most carried hidden weapons . Rumors . The inn was said to be haunted by the spirit of a patron who was stabbed for his money , and the ghost was said to behave as though his stash of coins had not yet been found . Food and drink . The Far Anchor did not serve alcohol . Food consisted of roasts , stews , vegetables , and fried potatoes , as well as frogs , river clams , and eels , and cheeses and sausages from all over Faerûn . The Elturian gray cheese and the Corm Orp sausage made from squirrel meat , ground nuts , and hogmeat were both popular .

title: Far Forest
description: Far Forest The Far Forest was one of a group of three forests named the Triangle of Trees . Description . The Far Forest was full of small lakes , some of which had become stinking marshes infested by will - o ' - wisp s and a few chuul .
description_long: Far Forest The Far Forest was one of a group of three forests named the Triangle of Trees . Description . The Far Forest was full of small lakes , some of which had become stinking marshes infested by will - o ' - wisp s and a few chuul . The heart of the forest was populated by giant spider s and other creatures that were the result of cruel magical experiments conducted by the Netherese . Travelers who journeyed through the Forest faced many dangers : ettercap , bear s , owlbear s , spider s , giant beetle s , snake s and stirge s roamed among the trees . The eastern side of the forest was less dense than the rest of the forest . These woods had a handful of sites where ancient ruins were covered by roots and climbing plants . History . This was once a relatively peaceful forest much like the brighter parts of the nearby High Forest , but as dark creatures poured out of Hellgate Keep into these woods , the dryad s and treant s of the forest left . Over time , the forest itself became dark and twisted by the demonic forces from Hellgate Keep . Before the fall of Hellgate Keep there were no sylvan races left in these woods .

title: Far Hills
description: Far Hills The Far Hills were a group of high landrises located in the Western Heartlands . Geography . The area was a region of rocky hills , hidden valleys and thick strands of trees .
description_long: Far Hills The Far Hills were a group of high landrises located in the Western Heartlands . Geography . The area was a region of rocky hills , hidden valleys and thick strands of trees . The Far Hills formed the eastern border of Sunset Vale . Darkhold ' s control over the region is all but absolute .

title: Far Outpost
description: Far Outpost The Far Outpost was a large village and trading hub found on the very tip of the entrance to the Bay of Dancing Dolphins in Dambrath . Activities . The garrison of the Far Outpost was charged with defending the Bay of Dancing Dolphins from any attackers .
description_long: Far Outpost The Far Outpost was a large village and trading hub found on the very tip of the entrance to the Bay of Dancing Dolphins in Dambrath . Activities . The garrison of the Far Outpost was charged with defending the Bay of Dancing Dolphins from any attackers . All ships entering the bay were boarded and searched , but traders and merchants were allowed to go on their way without harm . All confiscated goods or riches were sent to Luenath . Armed Forces . A fighting force of 500 cavalry and 20 warships were stationed at the Far Outpost . Each warship carried a potent spellcaster who was typically used to question the captains of ship entering the Bay .

title: Far Payit
description: Far Payit The Far Payit Lands were a heavily forested jungle region of Maztica , occupying the peninsula east of the Sea of Azul . The region consisted of some arable land , disease - ridden swamps , and mountain crests that jutted just above the treetops . Otherwise , most of Far Payit was made up of vast miles of steaming , leaf - shrouded jungle in semi - darkness .
description_long: Far Payit The Far Payit Lands were a heavily forested jungle region of Maztica , occupying the peninsula east of the Sea of Azul . The region consisted of some arable land , disease - ridden swamps , and mountain crests that jutted just above the treetops . Otherwise , most of Far Payit was made up of vast miles of steaming , leaf - shrouded jungle in semi - darkness . The Far Payit was populated by communities of human s , known as the Itza s , and wild halfling s .

title: Far Quey
description: Far Quey The Far Quey were a martial tribe of Nar found in Narfell who were renowned for their toughness . There were 2 , 300 Far Quey in 1357 DR . Activities .
description_long: Far Quey The Far Quey were a martial tribe of Nar found in Narfell who were renowned for their toughness . There were 2 , 300 Far Quey in 1357 DR . Activities . Given their rugged lifestyle and fierce attitude toward outsiders , the Far Quey were one of the more dangerous tribes to encounter in Narfell . However , their habitat was not an area that received many travelers . Base of Operations . The warriors of the Far Quey inhabited the frigid lands between the northern shores of Icelace Lake and the Great Glacier .

title: Far Realm
description: Far Realm The Far Realm was a plane of madness situated very far from the planes of the standard cosmology . This maddening realm was feared for its power to twist unfortunate visitors into gruesome monsters , and it was from here that aberration s came . According to Malyanna , a servant of the Abolethic Sovereignty , all cosmologies are threatened by the same Far Realm .
description_long: Far Realm The Far Realm was a plane of madness situated very far from the planes of the standard cosmology . This maddening realm was feared for its power to twist unfortunate visitors into gruesome monsters , and it was from here that aberration s came . According to Malyanna , a servant of the Abolethic Sovereignty , all cosmologies are threatened by the same Far Realm . Geography and Characteristics . The Far Realm comprised an infinite number of layers . Unlike the layers of many Outer Planes , these layers were very thin , ranging from an inch to a mile in thickness , each separated from the next by around ten feet . These layers were also transparent , and travelers could glimpse through twenty or so , with each appearing increasingly blurred . The layers were also highly morphic . On the whim of the alien entities that drifted through them , the layers continually evaporated , divided , spawned , and breathed . Changes in the elemental and energy traits of the layers continuously occurred , creating the Far Realm equivalent of a storm . These changes could be seen from far off , moving from layer to layer rather like a storm drifting across a natural world .

title: Farad al - Meisal
description: Farad al - Meisal Farad al - Meisal was a janni inhabiting the Lost City of Ubar within the High Desert of Zakhara in 1367 DR . Activities . Farad served as Vizier to the Amir of Ubar .
description_long: Farad al - Meisal Farad al - Meisal was a janni inhabiting the Lost City of Ubar within the High Desert of Zakhara in 1367 DR . Activities . Farad served as Vizier to the Amir of Ubar . Since the Amir ' s health took a turn for the worse , Farad adopted the role of the de facto ruler of the city to ensure the daily needs of the city were met .

title: Fargas Rumblefoot
description: Fargas Rumblefoot Fargas Rumblefoot was a lightfoot halfling adventurer in the Silken Paths during the Rage of Demons . History . The halfling went to the Underdark with his adventuring party in search of the Lost Tombs of Khaem , but they were attacked by mad gnoll s .
description_long: Fargas Rumblefoot Fargas Rumblefoot was a lightfoot halfling adventurer in the Silken Paths during the Rage of Demons . History . The halfling went to the Underdark with his adventuring party in search of the Lost Tombs of Khaem , but they were attacked by mad gnoll s . He escaped alone into the Silken Paths and was captured and cocooned by a giant spider . During the Rage of Demons , a party of adventurers escaping drow slavers of Velkynvelve may have found and freed him .

title: Farid al - Nisr
description: Farid al - Nisr Farid al - Nisr was a Harper wizard in 1372 DR . History . Around 1369 DR , Farid was sent to New Waterdeep in Maztica by High Harper Khelben Arunsun together with his Harper fiancee Lady Syllia Adarbrent and fellow Harper Orist Moonbow .
description_long: Farid al - Nisr Farid al - Nisr was a Harper wizard in 1372 DR . History . Around 1369 DR , Farid was sent to New Waterdeep in Maztica by High Harper Khelben Arunsun together with his Harper fiancee Lady Syllia Adarbrent and fellow Harper Orist Moonbow . There he was chosen as one of the new Lords of the Borderlands for his integrity and his connections . Around 1371 DR , Farid and Syllia were back in Waterdeep and they impetuously married before going back to Maztica . Relationship . Known to few , Farid was the son of Fahd yn Sarsor al Nisr , a First Yrshelem of the Rundeen . Personality . Farid hated slavery .

title: Faridah bint Halah
description: Faridah bint Halah Faridah bint Halah was a person of note in Hawa . Description . She was tall and trim and had deep brown eyes that matched her sun - streaked brown hair .
description_long: Faridah bint Halah Faridah bint Halah was a person of note in Hawa . Description . She was tall and trim and had deep brown eyes that matched her sun - streaked brown hair . Faridah always smelled of rich perfume and was thought of as one of the prettier corsair captain ' s of Hawa . Most believed her to be a human , but Faridah was actually a lamia noble masquerading as a human in order to spread evil throughout the Corsair Domains . Personality . Rumors of her cruelty had led to substantial rewards being offered by Qudra for her capture . Abilities . Faridah ' s most implemented ability was her wisdom - drain . Possessions . Faridah ' s ship was " Dark Rover , " a notorious vessel among the Free Cities of Zakhara and the mamluk s of Qudra . She owned a secret fortified area on top of a portion of the Island of Firethorns . Activities . She actively sought prisoners while out on the seas in order to add to her crew . Faridah developed a plan to eventually enslave the entire population of the fishing village of Safe Cove , draining the wisdom of a few inhabitants on each of her visits . Relationships .

title: Farideh
description: Farideh Farideh ( pronounced " far - ee - duh " ) was a warlock who accidentally made a pact with the cambion Lorcan . She is the adopted daughter of a dragonborn warrior named Mehen and the twin sister of Havilar . Description .
description_long: Farideh Farideh ( pronounced " far - ee - duh " ) was a warlock who accidentally made a pact with the cambion Lorcan . She is the adopted daughter of a dragonborn warrior named Mehen and the twin sister of Havilar . Description . Farideh is tall and thin and has one golden and one silver eye . Relationships . Farideh has a love - hate relationship with her master Lorcan . She wants to get out of the pact that she never really wanted in the first place but is unwilling to take the necessary steps . She had at least one occasion to kill Lorcan which would have ended the pact but she chose not to . She loves her sister and adopted father although she frequently argues with both . History . In 1477 DR her twin was attempting to summon an imp when she accidentally summoned a cambion named Lorcan . The cambion was more interested in making Farideh rather than Havilar a warlock because Havilar had more of a warrior ’ s personality . Unbeknownst to Farideh , she was descended from Bryseis Kakistos , one of the Toril thirteen , the original thirteen tiefling warlocks who made pacts with Asmodeus .

title: Faril Laheralson
description: Faril Laheralson Faril Laheralson was a male human fighter and ranger and the Oversword of a 100 - strong contingent of Purple Dragons based in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the late 1360s and early 1370s DR . Activities . Laheralson cared deeply for his men but was concerned more with their morale and spirit than their discipline .
description_long: Faril Laheralson Faril Laheralson was a male human fighter and ranger and the Oversword of a 100 - strong contingent of Purple Dragons based in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the late 1360s and early 1370s DR . Activities . Laheralson cared deeply for his men but was concerned more with their morale and spirit than their discipline . Thus Laheralson and his troops were a rowdy bunch who enjoyed brawling and monster - slaying , and frequently got out of control . They acquired a bad reputation for causing trouble around town . Although Laheralson respected King Azoun IV , he paid only lip service to the Crown and thought little of the King ' s representatives , seeing them as soft bureaucrats not worth his time . He usually ignored the Crown clerk Hurm Thiodor . As the capital was so far away , they got away with a lot , and the Crown cared only that the town remained loyal . History . By the late 1360s DR , the folk of Thunderstone had once petitioned Lord Sarp Redbeard , the nominal ruler of the town , asking him to reprimand Laheralson over the behavior of his soldiers .

title: Farim
description: Farim Farim was a human mamluk who lived in Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . Farim was a handsome man .
description_long: Farim Farim was a human mamluk who lived in Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . Farim was a handsome man . Activities . He was a member of the Valiant Mamluk Society , but served as the bodyguard of the sha ' ir Qoha ' dar and was rarely seen apart from her . He disliked senseless violence , so only drew his weapon as a last resort . History . During a past adventure , Farim was accidentally splashed with a magical oil that caused Qoha ' dar to fall in love with him . Relationships . Though the magical oil wore off long ago , Qoha ' dar remained infatuated with Farim . Possessions . Farim owned a set of " armor of the desert evening " and a gold - hilted scimitar .

title: Farim al - Kanafi
description: Farim al - Kanafi Farim al - Kanafi was an inhabitant of Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Personality . Farim complained about his job to anyone who would listen .
description_long: Farim al - Kanafi Farim al - Kanafi was an inhabitant of Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Personality . Farim complained about his job to anyone who would listen . Activities . Farim was a member of the Dauntless and served as the commander of the Gate of Wealth . Bored with his job , and believing it was not befitting a man of his skills , Farim had no trouble taking bribes , though he referred to them as " tokens of esteem . " He never let smugglers into Huzuz , but his " friends " received far less scrutiny when passing through the gates .

title: Faris
description: Faris A faris ( plural farisan ; farisa for females ) was a holy warrior of Zakhara . Requirements . Farisan had no special requirements , though the vast majority of these warriors were good - natured .
description_long: Faris A faris ( plural farisan ; farisa for females ) was a holy warrior of Zakhara . Requirements . Farisan had no special requirements , though the vast majority of these warriors were good - natured . Role . Farisan were the mortal champions of their gods .
