description_long: Fetlock Court Fetlock Court was a large paved courtyard in the Castle Ward of Waterdeep , adjoining the stables of the Palace . It was used as the staging area for mounted guards before their departure on patrols , and was unofficially a concert area for bard s to practice . It was also possible to purchase horse s here .

title: Fevered certainty of Caiphon
description: Fevered certainty of Caiphon Fevered certainty of Caiphon is spell used by warlock s , most often those of the star pact . When cast , " fevered certainty of Caiphon " bestows upon its caster with dark and forbidden knowledge , giving them an advantage over others in various mundane or heroic tasks alike . However , the knowledge is intoxicating and flushes the warlock with a small touch of the madness of the Far Realm , which like the benefits gained , lasts only for a moment .
description_long: Fevered certainty of Caiphon Fevered certainty of Caiphon is spell used by warlock s , most often those of the star pact . When cast , " fevered certainty of Caiphon " bestows upon its caster with dark and forbidden knowledge , giving them an advantage over others in various mundane or heroic tasks alike . However , the knowledge is intoxicating and flushes the warlock with a small touch of the madness of the Far Realm , which like the benefits gained , lasts only for a moment . The spell is difficult to cast and warlocks can only call upon Caiphon ' s power in this way once per day .

title: Fey
description: Fey Fey were creatures from the Feywild , a parallel plane to the Prime . Many were typified as having supernatural abilities and a connection to nature or to some other force or place . The language of the fey was called Sylvan .
description_long: Fey Fey were creatures from the Feywild , a parallel plane to the Prime . Many were typified as having supernatural abilities and a connection to nature or to some other force or place . The language of the fey was called Sylvan . Fae , or faeries , as many liked to be called , were creatures of any size , shape , texture , or smell , that exemplified and inhabited natural wonder . They went by many names , like " Green Folk " , " Fair Folk " , " People of Peace " , sometimes " Wee folk " . They were ruled by noble eladrin s and other archfey . Legends . There were many unsubstantiated legends about fey on Toril , especially in the forested areas of the Dalelands , and the like . Faeries , in good and friendly lands , with warm lush forests and babbling brooks , were said to be short friendly folk , with a twinkle in their eye , pronouncing wealth and good luck on those deserving , who often happened to be the mortals who found them . In other places , blasted lands and choking swamps , fey were seen to be mad redcap s , devouring infants , corrupting youth , and bringing bad luck to any in whom they happened to take interest .

title: Fey ' ri
description: Fey ' ri Fey ' ri , or demonfey , were not a true elven subrace . They were to elves as tiefling s were to human s and tanarukk s were to orc s . The fey ' ri were the result of interbreeding between sun elves and tanar ' ri in an attempt to strengthen the sun elf bloodline .
description_long: Fey ' ri Fey ' ri , or demonfey , were not a true elven subrace . They were to elves as tiefling s were to human s and tanarukk s were to orc s . The fey ' ri were the result of interbreeding between sun elves and tanar ' ri in an attempt to strengthen the sun elf bloodline . Ecology . Physical characteristics . The fey ' ri resembled elves " the way tieflings resemble humans " , but generally rejected the notion of elven resemblance as offensive . Some fey ' ri had barbed tails , fangs , forked tongues or horns , or any combination . Some had multiple sets of arms and one or more sets of wings . Some fey ' ri were not visibly different to elves at all , and some were raised amongst elves , some never knowing their true nature . Abilities . Fey ' ri had a talent for the use of magic , and some would practice bladesong . Almost all fey ' ri had the ability to change shape , which aided in concealing themselves in society . Other abilities varied , including producing flames , draining life , or resisting spells . Society . Most fey ' ri became sorcerer s , rogue s or fighter s . Fey ' ri sought to reestablish the old elven realms of Cormanthor with themselves at their head .

title: Fey ' ri invasion of Evereska
description: Fey ' ri invasion of Evereska The hellspawn race of elves known as the fey ' ri were effectively entombed underneath Myth Drannor for 5000 years until some of the magical warding had eroded and they were able to escape to the surface . The fiendish race of elves were tainted and had acquired a great deal of power through the dark arts . High Fey ' ri mages had summoned 3500 demons and other minions of darkness to fortify their troops and begun a march south along the River Delimbiyr valley and into a narrow pass in the foothills to Evereska , the last elven stronghold .
description_long: Fey ' ri invasion of Evereska The hellspawn race of elves known as the fey ' ri were effectively entombed underneath Myth Drannor for 5000 years until some of the magical warding had eroded and they were able to escape to the surface . The fiendish race of elves were tainted and had acquired a great deal of power through the dark arts . High Fey ' ri mages had summoned 3500 demons and other minions of darkness to fortify their troops and begun a march south along the River Delimbiyr valley and into a narrow pass in the foothills to Evereska , the last elven stronghold . Key agents of an elite guild of rangers had spotted the invasion from the vantage of their base camp high on Mt . Evereska allowing time to call the archers into position . Using flying disks and formidable warriors of darkness , the Fey ' ri and their summoned troops marched up the pass . The sky went dark as thousands of elven archers ' arrow littered the sky stopping many and bringing down the enemies numbers , but the assault raged on . Fey ' ri mages flew over the ground assault on flying disks and rained - down fireballs and spells in an aerial strike .

title: Fey beguiler
description: Fey beguiler Fey beguilers are some of the greatest heroes in the folklore of gnome s . While most races would have powerful and fearless warriors as their heroes , in gnome legends the heroes outwit huge monsters , play great pranks without getting caught , and sneak past great magical guardians to get the treasures . Fey Beguilers bring these stories to a reality , using agility , stealth , and a little well - placed magic to achieve their goals .
description_long: Fey beguiler Fey beguilers are some of the greatest heroes in the folklore of gnome s . While most races would have powerful and fearless warriors as their heroes , in gnome legends the heroes outwit huge monsters , play great pranks without getting caught , and sneak past great magical guardians to get the treasures . Fey Beguilers bring these stories to a reality , using agility , stealth , and a little well - placed magic to achieve their goals . Abilities . Fey Beguilers abilities usually involve using powers commonly found among rogue s and wizard s . Also they use powers that allow them to strike with blinding fey magic before hiding with a cloak of invisibility

title: Fey crossroad
description: Fey crossroad Fey crossroads were magical portals , many of which led to the Feywild . They could be found all over Toril , but most were hidden from casual view . They often required the use of a ritual to operate , and after the Spellplague , many malfunctioned .
description_long: Fey crossroad Fey crossroads were magical portals , many of which led to the Feywild . They could be found all over Toril , but most were hidden from casual view . They often required the use of a ritual to operate , and after the Spellplague , many malfunctioned . Description . A fey crossroad , according to druid s , was where a fold in reality ' s ends touched each other , thus allowing instant travel by stepping in one end and coming out of the other . Each crossroad had a fey guardian , called a crossroad guardian , who had to be convinced to allow usage of the crossroad . Fey received automatic permission . As a general rule , entrances were hidden from sight and required the " detect crossroad " spell to find , though druids often marked them by arranging stones in circles , lines , or other ways . Most were large enough for a huge creature to fit through . They were mapped by druids and known to some bard s ; to other people , crossroads were more the stuff of legends than anything else . Usage . To use a crossroad , one needed to find one first , which required the aforementioned " detect crossroad " spell .

title: Fey domain
description: Fey domain The Fey domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters fey spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Exalted Deeds " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Fey Domain Powers .
description_long: Fey domain The Fey domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters fey spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Exalted Deeds " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Fey Domain Powers . The cleric gains resistance to the spell - like abilities of fey creatures , such as dryad s , nymph s , sprites , and telthor s .

title: Fey mound
description: Fey mound Fey mounds were hidden burial barrows of wild fey which often contained treasures buried with the fey . The soil from fey mounds was thought to be magical and was used in some ritual s to increase the fertility of fields . Individuals highly attuned to magic could sometimes sense a mound ' s presence .
description_long: Fey mound Fey mounds were hidden burial barrows of wild fey which often contained treasures buried with the fey . The soil from fey mounds was thought to be magical and was used in some ritual s to increase the fertility of fields . Individuals highly attuned to magic could sometimes sense a mound ' s presence . Mounds were often protected by illusionary magic which could charm trespassers or cause them to fall asleep . Living fey zealously guarded mounds and punished those who disturbed their kinsmens ' eternal rest .

title: Feytouched
description: Feytouched The feytouched are warlock s bound to pacts with powerful archfey , who have absorbed so much of the Feywild ’ s power so quickly as to have gone literally mad . However , the madness is only temporary for most who successfully take on the path , who learn to control their sanity , almost as if insanity itself were another weapon . With the power of the Feywild itself at their command , feytouched are not hindered by their temporary bouts of insanity .
description_long: Feytouched The feytouched are warlock s bound to pacts with powerful archfey , who have absorbed so much of the Feywild ’ s power so quickly as to have gone literally mad . However , the madness is only temporary for most who successfully take on the path , who learn to control their sanity , almost as if insanity itself were another weapon . With the power of the Feywild itself at their command , feytouched are not hindered by their temporary bouts of insanity . More the case , they are " aided " by it . Abilities . The feytouched gain several abilities from their newfound perspective . Initially , these new abilities simply make the feytouched more deadly , causing their spells to be cast with an uncanny degree of accuracy . Another consequence of a feytouched ’ s increased power is that their act of teleporting causes genuine harm to those nearby , acting as much as an attack as a mode of transportation .

title: Feywild
description: Feywild The Feywild , also known as the plane of Faerie , existed as an " echo " of the Prime Material Plane . It was from here that the fey originated , giving the Feywild its name , and it was also a place of unusually potent magic . Traits .
description_long: Feywild The Feywild , also known as the plane of Faerie , existed as an " echo " of the Prime Material Plane . It was from here that the fey originated , giving the Feywild its name , and it was also a place of unusually potent magic . Traits . As a parallel plane to the Prime , the Feywild ' s geography was similar , though not entirely identical , to the geography of the Prime . Similarly , just as the geography was reminiscent of Toril ' s , its inhabitants and many creatures existed as fey " echoes " of Prime creatures . Arcane magic ran more freely and powerfully in the Feywild than it did in the Prime and it was for this reason that so many of its inhabitants were magically gifted . The Feywild was also reputably beautiful compared with either the Shadowfell or the Prime . Territories . Though much of the Feywild was the same as the Prime geologically , there were differences , and more importantly , the lands answered to different powers than those on Toril . Much of the elven or eladrin civilizations had their earliest roots here and abandoned remnants of their culture littered the landscape .

title: Fflar Starbrow Melruth
description: Fflar Starbrow Melruth Fflar Starbrow Melruth is the former Captain of Myth Drannor in the Akh ' Velahr ( army of Cormanthor ) . He is around a hundred and fifty years old . Description .
description_long: Fflar Starbrow Melruth Fflar Starbrow Melruth is the former Captain of Myth Drannor in the Akh ' Velahr ( army of Cormanthor ) . He is around a hundred and fifty years old . Description . Fflar is tall with broad shoulders , russet hair and a broad , handsome face . He wears his hair in a braid . Relationships . Fflar had a wife , Sorenna Alydyrrin and son in the time of Myth Drannor . Both fled before the city fell . A " " Captain Fflar " " is credited as being a famed instructor on the School of Arms in Semberholme , in which he taught for eight years after his wife gave birth to their first child in the Year of Seven Stones ( 335 DR ) , but this one can ' t possibly be the same Fflar , according to his age . Possessions . Fflar carries the sword Keryvian . He has been known to be armoured with a lacquered breastplate and a kite - shaped shield . History . Fflar was killed on 15 Flamerule 714 DR in the Fall of Myth Drannor , after which he went to Arvandor , but he was resurrected by Seiveril Miritar on 20 Ches , 1374 DR , in order to take up Keryvian in battle against the daemonfey invasion of Faerûn .

title: Ffolk
description: Ffolk The Ffolk were a race of human s that inhabited the Moonshae Isles alongside the Northlanders . The Ffolk inhabited the southern parts of the Moonshaes , including Flamsterd , Moray , Snowdown and Sunset , and the southern parts of Alaron and Gwynneth . Their society was mainly agricultural and was ruled by a High King or Queen who resided in Caer Callidyrr , the capital of the Ffolk .
description_long: Ffolk The Ffolk were a race of human s that inhabited the Moonshae Isles alongside the Northlanders . The Ffolk inhabited the southern parts of the Moonshaes , including Flamsterd , Moray , Snowdown and Sunset , and the southern parts of Alaron and Gwynneth . Their society was mainly agricultural and was ruled by a High King or Queen who resided in Caer Callidyrr , the capital of the Ffolk . Culture and Heritage . Modern Ffolk were mostly of Tethyrian origin , following a large Tethyrian immigration in 467 DR . This caused the Ffolk to lose much of their original racial heritage , although their culture was quite distinct from their mainland cousins and they held to a strong druid ic tradition . The Ffolk spent most of their time on peaceful pasttimes such as farming , fishing , hunting , and trading . They were also accomplished ship builders , specializing in a type of ship that was designed to withstand some of the roughest seas . Religion . The Ffolk worshiped the Earthmother , and aspect of Chauntea . Religion primarily followed the Druidic traditions . Language . Modern Ffolk spoke Illuskan , although they employed the Thorass script . History .

title: Fhaornik
description: Fhaornik Fhaornik was a sun elf apprentice at Blackstaff Tower . On 28 Uktar 1374 DR , he was involved in the defence of the tower against Kemarn Darkthrush . He threw a " rod of absorption " into Kemarn ' s summoned nishruu , but it did not destroy the creature as he had hoped .
description_long: Fhaornik Fhaornik was a sun elf apprentice at Blackstaff Tower . On 28 Uktar 1374 DR , he was involved in the defence of the tower against Kemarn Darkthrush . He threw a " rod of absorption " into Kemarn ' s summoned nishruu , but it did not destroy the creature as he had hoped .

title: Fhazail
description: Fhazail Fhazail was a human bandit . Description . Fhazail was a fat man .
description_long: Fhazail Fhazail was a human bandit . Description . Fhazail was a fat man . He wore several rings of gold around one finger . Activities . He betrayed the White Shield Company to Graal , an orog , who also served as his master . Graal hated him because he would give up too easily and bow before anyone .

title: Fiddlehead soup
description: Fiddlehead soup Fiddlehead soup was a dish made in Faerûn , using the fiddlehead of a fern . Locations . Around 1370 DR , the village of Dead Tree Hollow in the Vast was famous for its fiddlehead soup when the fiddleheads were in season .
description_long: Fiddlehead soup Fiddlehead soup was a dish made in Faerûn , using the fiddlehead of a fern . Locations . Around 1370 DR , the village of Dead Tree Hollow in the Vast was famous for its fiddlehead soup when the fiddleheads were in season . It also made a fern - frond soup from older plants . A fern - and - fiddlehead soup was made at the Stag Steads royal hunting lodge in Cormyr around 1367 DR .

title: Field glass
description: Field glass A field glass was a popular export from the the Shining Lands in 1367 DR . It was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . History .
description_long: Field glass A field glass was a popular export from the the Shining Lands in 1367 DR . It was available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . History . A field glass was made by attaching special lenses , shaped by gnome artificers in Ormpe , to either end of a cylinder . Field glasses were coveted by captains sailing both the Sea of Fallen Stars and the Sword Coast . Usage . Field glasses were used to magnify the user ' s vision over great distances . They were extremely popular among sailors on the Great Sea , allowing them to spot pirates long before the pirates even knew they were there . A field glass typically at least doubled the distance vision of any scout or lookout .

title: Field of Triumph
description: Field of Triumph The Field of Triumph was a large outdoor stadium located in the Sea Ward of Waterdeep at the southern end of the Street of the Singing Dolphin , adjacent to the House of Heroes , and bordered by Julthoon Street , Jelzar ' s Stride , and Seaeye ' s March . The main entrance was at the end of Gulzindar Street , known as the Lion Gate because it was carved to give visitors the impression they were walking into the maw of a gigantic lion . The Field of Triumph was the venue for many public spectacles from late spring until late autumn , weather permitting .
description_long: Field of Triumph The Field of Triumph was a large outdoor stadium located in the Sea Ward of Waterdeep at the southern end of the Street of the Singing Dolphin , adjacent to the House of Heroes , and bordered by Julthoon Street , Jelzar ' s Stride , and Seaeye ' s March . The main entrance was at the end of Gulzindar Street , known as the Lion Gate because it was carved to give visitors the impression they were walking into the maw of a gigantic lion . The Field of Triumph was the venue for many public spectacles from late spring until late autumn , weather permitting . The Open Lord of Waterdeep used the Field as a public forum to give proclamations to the city , but most of the time it was host to exciting events such as horse races , shows of magic and illusion , martial displays of formation and skill , gladiatorial combats , and exhibitions of strange and wondrous creatures and monsters from all across Faerûn and beyond . Attendance often numbered in the thousands .

title: Fields of Mythal
description: Fields of Mythal The three Fields of Mythal were the way the powerful arcanist s of Netheril grouped their spells , similar to the nine schools of magic known to the wizard s of later ages . Each arcanist was a specialist in one Field , had minor insight into a second and could not cast spells from the third Field . Inventive .
description_long: Fields of Mythal The three Fields of Mythal were the way the powerful arcanist s of Netheril grouped their spells , similar to the nine schools of magic known to the wizard s of later ages . Each arcanist was a specialist in one Field , had minor insight into a second and could not cast spells from the third Field . Inventive . Inventives were spells used to create or destroy . A specialist in this Field was called an inventor . Mentalism . Mentalisms were spells designed to influence the minds of persons or creatures . They were used by mentalists . Variation . Variations were spells that changed and transformed things , energies and states , including other spells . A specialist in this Field was called a variator . < br >

title: Fields of Slaughter
description: Fields of Slaughter The Fields of Slaughter was a large plot of land running between the Spine of the World and the Severed Hand . History . The fields were named after a great battle that took place between elven and orc ish forces .
description_long: Fields of Slaughter The Fields of Slaughter was a large plot of land running between the Spine of the World and the Severed Hand . History . The fields were named after a great battle that took place between elven and orc ish forces . The blood was said to have been so much that the fields were red for months . Long after , however , the fields were used extensively as a pathway for merchants , travelers , and adventurers .

title: Fields of the Dead
description: Fields of the Dead The Fields of the Dead are the rolling hills east of Baldur ' s Gate between the Winding Water and the River Chionthar on the Sword Coast . Kings Strohm IV and Samyte of Tethyr were buried here . History .
description_long: Fields of the Dead The Fields of the Dead are the rolling hills east of Baldur ' s Gate between the Winding Water and the River Chionthar on the Sword Coast . Kings Strohm IV and Samyte of Tethyr were buried here . History . Centuries ago ( before the founding of Amn ) this land was a favored battleground for control of the lands north of Calimshan . Bones still litter the field and cairns of the dead are everywhere . Now used for farming and ranching , plows occasionally turn up skeletons in rusting armor , weapons , and other detritus . In 1264 DR , thieves stole the " Shield of Silvam " and the " Royal Masque Blades " from the tombs . Appendix . Notes . Map

title: Fiella Markin
description: Fiella Markin Warchief Fiella Markin was the ruler of Hethar in Dambrath . Personality . Due to her lack of priestly skills , Fiella was a fiercely determined individual who was not afraid to take risks in order to accomplish her goals .
description_long: Fiella Markin Warchief Fiella Markin was the ruler of Hethar in Dambrath . Personality . Due to her lack of priestly skills , Fiella was a fiercely determined individual who was not afraid to take risks in order to accomplish her goals . Activities . Fiella was loyal to Duchess Merial Luenath and Queen Yenandra . Relationships . Fiella was the sister of Grenai Markin and Herald Markin .

title: Fiend
description: Fiend A fiend is an evil creature from one of the Fiendish Planes . They are not just evil , but " born " of Evil ; primal malevolence is one of the roots of their nature , and the evil essence of the fiendish planes permeates every part of their bodies . Types of Fiends .
description_long: Fiend A fiend is an evil creature from one of the Fiendish Planes . They are not just evil , but " born " of Evil ; primal malevolence is one of the roots of their nature , and the evil essence of the fiendish planes permeates every part of their bodies . Types of Fiends . The tanar ' ri and the baatezu hold an eternal enmity for one another as they wage the Blood War . Demons . Demons are chaotic evil fiends , native to the Abyss . Tanar ' ri are the dominant species of demon , but there are a number of others . Devils . Devils are lawful evil in alignment and hail from the Nine Hells of Baator . The baatezu are the dominant species . Yugoloths . Also known as " daemons " . They are neutral evil in alignment and inhabit the Blood Rift . Demodands . Also known as " gehreleths " , demodands are said to have been fashioned by one of the primal creations of Evil , exiled because of their chaotic taint . They currently dwell in the Supreme Throne . Other fiendish races . While not all denizens of the Fiendish Planes are fiends as such , other inhabitants of the fiendish planes include :

title: Fiend ' s Wing
description: Fiend ' s Wing The Fiend ' s Wing was a large province of the Yikarian Empire in 1367 DR . Geography . This section of the Empire was found at a narrow section of the World Pillar Mountains that separated the jungles of the east from the barbarian lands of the west .
description_long: Fiend ' s Wing The Fiend ' s Wing was a large province of the Yikarian Empire in 1367 DR . Geography . This section of the Empire was found at a narrow section of the World Pillar Mountains that separated the jungles of the east from the barbarian lands of the west . The province sprawled from the mountains into the lowlands as it ran south for several hundred miles before reaching the border of the Bronze Falcon . Inhabitants . The powerful Cloud Wizard ruled this province with the help of marrash allies . Activities . Given its location , Fiend ' s Wing served to protect the heart of the Empire from any threats to the northeast and east .

title: Fiend of corruption
description: Fiend of corruption A fiend of corruption is an evil Outsider who specializes in tricking people into embracing the darker aspects of themselves . They do so out of the spitefulness of their nature . Known Fiends of Corruption .
description_long: Fiend of corruption A fiend of corruption is an evil Outsider who specializes in tricking people into embracing the darker aspects of themselves . They do so out of the spitefulness of their nature . Known Fiends of Corruption . Wendonai : A Balor in the Service of the Drow Demon Goddess , Lolth . He took possession of the Crescent Blade Halisstra Melarn had left behind in the Demonweb Pits to have easy access to the priestesses of Eilistraee opposing Lolth on the Material plane .

title: Fiend patron
description: Fiend patron A fiend patron was one possible sponsor for a warlock . If a bargain was made between a warlock and an archdevil , a demon lord , or some other member of the fiendish royalty , the warlock ' s patron gave them access to certain powers , including a suite of spells that expanded the choices to fill their spell slots .
description_long: Fiend patron A fiend patron was one possible sponsor for a warlock . If a bargain was made between a warlock and an archdevil , a demon lord , or some other member of the fiendish royalty , the warlock ' s patron gave them access to certain powers , including a suite of spells that expanded the choices to fill their spell slots .

title: Fiendish planes
description: Fiendish planes Fiendish planes was a collective term used to describe a subset of the Outer Planes in the World Tree cosmology model . The fiendish planes were generally associated with the evil deities whereas the celestial planes were generally associated with the good ones . The fiendish planes were : The River of Blood connected all of these planes except for the Demonweb Pits and the Supreme Throne .
description_long: Fiendish planes Fiendish planes was a collective term used to describe a subset of the Outer Planes in the World Tree cosmology model . The fiendish planes were generally associated with the evil deities whereas the celestial planes were generally associated with the good ones . The fiendish planes were : The River of Blood connected all of these planes except for the Demonweb Pits and the Supreme Throne . Navigating the river between planes was possible but very dangerous .

title: Fiendish resilience
description: Fiendish resilience Fiendish resilience is a spell used by many warlock s , both before and after the Spellplague , to enhance their durability . When a warlock , most typically one bound to the devil s of the Nine Hells , casts " fiendish resilience " , he or she imbues her flesh with the power of the Hells themselves , increasing his or her vitality substantially . This effect is not permanent , but nor does it wear down with time , and until this magical protection is stripped away from the warlock they retain it .
description_long: Fiendish resilience Fiendish resilience is a spell used by many warlock s , both before and after the Spellplague , to enhance their durability . When a warlock , most typically one bound to the devil s of the Nine Hells , casts " fiendish resilience " , he or she imbues her flesh with the power of the Hells themselves , increasing his or her vitality substantially . This effect is not permanent , but nor does it wear down with time , and until this magical protection is stripped away from the warlock they retain it . They can only cast the spell once per day , however , for it calls on much of their available power .

title: Fiertallin
description: Fiertallin Fiertallin was a cosmetic commonly used in Ulgarth . It was a white , chalky substance gathered from the river Xon and exported from the city of Suormpar to the rest of the realm . Around 1367 DR , women of Ulgarth used fiertallin to add artistic streaks of white to their typically dark hair , as hair was a prime area of fashion .
description_long: Fiertallin Fiertallin was a cosmetic commonly used in Ulgarth . It was a white , chalky substance gathered from the river Xon and exported from the city of Suormpar to the rest of the realm . Around 1367 DR , women of Ulgarth used fiertallin to add artistic streaks of white to their typically dark hair , as hair was a prime area of fashion . In the past , the king and princess of the neighboring realm of Doegan also bore similar streaks in their hair .

title: Fiery bolt
description: Fiery bolt Fiery bolt was a spell of the evocation school used most often by infernal pact warlock s , though other warlocks sometimes learned to use it . " Fiery bolt " , when cast , created a fiery ray of golden colored flame , which the warlock casting it shot toward a creature of their choosing within fifty feet . The spell , the potency of which was influenced by the caster ' s durability , if it hit , burned the target , as well as other creatures unfortunate enough to be nearby , with deadly ( but easily extinguished ) flames .
description_long: Fiery bolt Fiery bolt was a spell of the evocation school used most often by infernal pact warlock s , though other warlocks sometimes learned to use it . " Fiery bolt " , when cast , created a fiery ray of golden colored flame , which the warlock casting it shot toward a creature of their choosing within fifty feet . The spell , the potency of which was influenced by the caster ' s durability , if it hit , burned the target , as well as other creatures unfortunate enough to be nearby , with deadly ( but easily extinguished ) flames . The severity of the burns for those caught nearby depended , in the case of infernal pact warlocks , upon mental acuity of the warlock casting " fiery bolt " . " Fiery bolt " was relatively easy to cast and required only a short rest on the part of the caster before it could be used again .

title: Fiery fists
description: Fiery fists Fiery fists was a flame spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects .
description_long: Fiery fists Fiery fists was a flame spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects . Casting this spell caused the caster ' s hands to become engulfed in blue flames that were useful as weapons . Simple touching any opponent caused a fiery explosion that not only burned the target , but also released noxious smoke that caused them to cough uncontrollably for several minutes . Only a small amount of the smoke was released with each hit , causing only the single target to begin coughing . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a lump of coal to cast .

title: Fighter
description: Fighter Fighter was a descriptive term for a warrior skilled with a variety of weapons and trained in the arts of war . A skilled fighter defined the front line of any battle , breaking through enemy ranks and holding the line while their allies maneuvered . All fighters were trained to use virtually any armor or weapon the situation required ; a fighter could use an axe , a rapier , or a greatsword with roughly equivalent skill .
description_long: Fighter Fighter was a descriptive term for a warrior skilled with a variety of weapons and trained in the arts of war . A skilled fighter defined the front line of any battle , breaking through enemy ranks and holding the line while their allies maneuvered . All fighters were trained to use virtually any armor or weapon the situation required ; a fighter could use an axe , a rapier , or a greatsword with roughly equivalent skill . As well as being combat generalists , most fighter also specialized in a particular skillset , such as archery or combat magic . Artemis Entreri , Bruenor Battlehammer , Drizzt Do ' Urden and Azoun IV are all well - known fighters from Toril ' s history . Culture . Among the most common adventurers , fighters came from an innumerable set of backgrounds . Some were knight s in the service of a quest or elite foot soldiers whilst others were ambitious would - be overlords or hardened mercenaries . What brought fighters together , however , was their common roots as warriors who put themselves in the thick of battle , between their comrades and harm ' s way ; while many fighters could be called disreputable , few , if any , were true cowards .

title: Figurine of wondrous power
description: Figurine of wondrous power A figurine of wondrous power is a small statuette ranging in size from a grown man ' s hand to the size of a little finger , that is similar in shape to the extra - planar creature that it turns into . These rare items transform into many types of bestial planar creatures that understand common and follow the orders of the wielder of the statuette . These creatures are called by the name given to the creature upon the item ' s creation .
description_long: Figurine of wondrous power A figurine of wondrous power is a small statuette ranging in size from a grown man ' s hand to the size of a little finger , that is similar in shape to the extra - planar creature that it turns into . These rare items transform into many types of bestial planar creatures that understand common and follow the orders of the wielder of the statuette . These creatures are called by the name given to the creature upon the item ' s creation . They cannot reside on the prime material plane for large amounts of time and therefore are bound by the figurines to return to their home planes to rest after a set amount of time on the prime . If the creature is slain while on this plane it will revert back to statuette form and live on , but if the statuette is destroyed the item becomes worthless and loses all enchantment . Depending on the strength of the enchantment this artifact ' s effects should be permanent unless passed through an anti - magic field , which could disrupt the base structure of any magic item . Guenhwyvar . Guenhwyvar is a unique figurine in that the statuette summons its creature rather than transforms into it .

title: Fihelis
description: Fihelis Fihelis was a half - elf of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . Fihelis was a citizen of Neverwinter , whose daughter died during the Neverwinter plague .
description_long: Fihelis Fihelis was a half - elf of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . Fihelis was a citizen of Neverwinter , whose daughter died during the Neverwinter plague . He began working with the Watch as a spy in Smuggler ' s warehouse , to uncover Moire ' s plans . Gameplay . If the Kalach - Cha and the companions sided with the Watch , they needed to rescue Fihelis , who was being interrogated by Moire . Once done , the Kalach - Cha could threaten him for a reward , then bring him to Brelaina . If the Kalach - Cha and the compaions sided with the thieves , they needed to kill Fihelis . They could also kill the watchmen on the first floor for Moire or leave them alive for Axle .

title: Fiirnel ' ther Vandree
description: Fiirnel ' ther Vandree Fiinel ' ther Vandree was the matron mother of House Vandree in Menzoberranzan in 1480 DR and after . Personality . During the Rage of Demons , she and her house were considered vicious , vindictive , and determined to rise to the top .
description_long: Fiirnel ' ther Vandree Fiinel ' ther Vandree was the matron mother of House Vandree in Menzoberranzan in 1480 DR and after . Personality . During the Rage of Demons , she and her house were considered vicious , vindictive , and determined to rise to the top . History . She killed her mother and previous matron mother Troken ' ther Vandree in 1388 DR . Under Fiinel ' ther ' s guidance , the Vandree rose quickly to become the eighth house and thus a member of the Ruling Council .

title: Filani
description: Filani Filani of Tantras was a female human wizard and sage from the city of Tantras in the Vast who settled in Tilverton in Cormyr . History . Hailing from the city of Tantras in the Vast , Filani made her home in Tilverton before 1358 DR .
description_long: Filani Filani of Tantras was a female human wizard and sage from the city of Tantras in the Vast who settled in Tilverton in Cormyr . History . Hailing from the city of Tantras in the Vast , Filani made her home in Tilverton before 1358 DR . Filani of Tantras , as she was known , became one of the two most notable mages in the town , and was well respected there . She still lived there through 1367 DR , and by 1369 DR . Activities . Filani was a sage , specializing in the history and political affairs of the lands around the Dragonreach ( which included her home city of Tantras ) and the Moonsea North . However , she was no scholar ; rather , she was a businesswoman , dealing in information . Such information was reliable and came at a reasonable cost , though Filani ' s insight depended on the amount offered . She did not trade in scrolls , magical items , or spellcasting services . Filani could often be found in Tilverton ' s marketplaces and inns , speaking with caravan folk to learn news and local goings - on . In exchange , she bought them drinks and meals , and she had many regular sources who knew they could get a free feed while in town .

title: Filarion Filvendorson
description: Filarion Filvendorson Filarion Filvendorson was a grandson of Elorfindar Floshin in Daggerford around 1370 DR and 1485 DR . History . Filarion was the son of Filvendor Floshin .
description_long: Filarion Filvendorson Filarion Filvendorson was a grandson of Elorfindar Floshin in Daggerford around 1370 DR and 1485 DR . History . Filarion was the son of Filvendor Floshin . He trained as a thief but had a good reputation . Many in 1370 believed him the master of the local thieves ' guild . He disappeared from the town for many years in search of his missing father , resurfacing only around 1445 DR at Elorfindar Floshin ' s death hoping for an inheritance but the sole heir was Darfin Floshin . He lived training guards and militiamen .

title: Filfaeril Obarskyr
description: Filfaeril Obarskyr Queen Filfaeril Selzair Obarskyr ( the Dragon Queen ) was the queen of Cormyr and wife of King Azoun IV . Azoun was drawn to her more for her extremely sharp mind rather than her beautiful appearance . She was skilled at chess .
description_long: Filfaeril Obarskyr Queen Filfaeril Selzair Obarskyr ( the Dragon Queen ) was the queen of Cormyr and wife of King Azoun IV . Azoun was drawn to her more for her extremely sharp mind rather than her beautiful appearance . She was skilled at chess . Unbeknownst to her husband , Filfaeril was involved with the Harpers and acted as an agent on their behalf in Cormyr , regularly meeting with Dove Falconhand . Appearance . Filfaeril had ice - blue eyes and golden blonde hair . Her figure was slender and she had pale skin . She was extremely beautiful . Her everyday crown was a slim circlet with two brow spires , each with a sapphire at the end . Relatives . Filfaeril ' s husband was King Azoun IV . They had two daughters : Tanalasta and Alusair Obarskyr . Elminster was her sire making Laspeera , the Warden of the War Wizards , and Narnra Shalace her half - sisters . Background . Filfaeril was born on Mirtul 4 , 1311 DR . When Azoun was brought near death by the abraxus incident in 1369 DR , it was rumoured that Filfaeril was so stricken with grief that she was taken away to the Spires of the Morning in Eveningstar .

title: Filfaeril Stormbillow
description: Filfaeril Stormbillow Filfaeril Stormbillow was a wizard and ex - adventurer . History . She was born in Marsember , Cormyr , and retired there around 1338 DR .
description_long: Filfaeril Stormbillow Filfaeril Stormbillow was a wizard and ex - adventurer . History . She was born in Marsember , Cormyr , and retired there around 1338 DR . She became wealthy creating and selling magical items and potions . In turn , she bought the rare materials she needed to complete these items . She was pretty despite her age . Filfaeril survived two attacks . The first , by pirates , was an attempt to capture her for her skills . The second was by a group led by the Zhentarim , who tried to kill her and steal her magic items . She was protected both times by being enclosed in a magical healing sphere .

title: Filiare
description: Filiare Filiare was a retired fighter who ran the Inn of the Dripping Dagger in Trades Ward of Waterdeep . Description . The middle - aged human was quite jovial and Filiare had greying dark hair and a moustache .
description_long: Filiare Filiare was a retired fighter who ran the Inn of the Dripping Dagger in Trades Ward of Waterdeep . Description . The middle - aged human was quite jovial and Filiare had greying dark hair and a moustache . Personality . Using the inn as a base of his operations , Filiare sold used weapons and found work for down - on - their - luck mercenaries . It was throught this latter business that Filiare became a rival of Blazidon One - Eye .

title: Filina Shintar
description: Filina Shintar Filina Shintar was a half - elven priestess and Queen of Dambrath during the 11th century DR . Relationships . Filina was the daughter of Dambrath ' s first queen , Cathtyr Shintar .
description_long: Filina Shintar Filina Shintar was a half - elven priestess and Queen of Dambrath during the 11th century DR . Relationships . Filina was the daughter of Dambrath ' s first queen , Cathtyr Shintar . Activities . Filina grew tired of waiting for her mother to die of natural causes , so she decided to take matters into her own hands . She murdered her mother so she could become the queen of Dambrath . As fate would have it , Filina only ruled for 5 short years before her daughter , Cathakay did the same thing to her .

title: Filithan
description: Filithan Filithan was a male priest of Ilmater from Bormton , Amn , in the 3rd century DR , who held the title " Revered Brother " and helped create the legendary sword " Dornavver " , the " Demonbane " . History . To counter the growing spread of evil under the Shoon Imperium and a plethora of evil artifacts fashioned at the time , the Church of Ilmater sought a weapon to combat such evil .
description_long: Filithan Filithan was a male priest of Ilmater from Bormton , Amn , in the 3rd century DR , who held the title " Revered Brother " and helped create the legendary sword " Dornavver " , the " Demonbane " . History . To counter the growing spread of evil under the Shoon Imperium and a plethora of evil artifacts fashioned at the time , the Church of Ilmater sought a weapon to combat such evil . To this end , the sword " Dornavver " was completed in the Year of the Wrath Sword , 275 DR . On the night of the Feast of the Moon that same year , Filithan , along with Archsufferer Irmakul " Bloodthews " , Exalted Servant Volshur the Crooked and other senior clergy of Ilmater , took the sword and gathered at Allyn ' s Anvil in the Alimir Mountains east of Calimshan . There they conducted a holy ritual in which their impassioned prayers and howls of suffering enchanted the sword . These events were documented in the tome " Relics of the Righteous " .

title: Fillistrom Wunderkundoodle
description: Fillistrom Wunderkundoodle Fillistrom Wunderkundoodle was a healer in Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Fillistrom liked taking his time to do things but was a very competent healer .
description_long: Fillistrom Wunderkundoodle Fillistrom Wunderkundoodle was a healer in Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Fillistrom liked taking his time to do things but was a very competent healer . History . Fillistrom was a healer with a shop in Phlan . He was consulted by Aleyd Burral of the Knights of the Black Fist about a rumored dracolich or ghost ship ' s attack on a nearby village but found no definitive answers about the assailants .

title: Filsaelene Merwyst
description: Filsaelene Merwyst Filsaelene Merwyst was a sun elf cleric of Corellon Larethian rescued from captivity by the daemonfey in the ruins beneath Myth Glaurach by Araevin Teshurr and his party . Possessions . Filsaelene carried a longsword and wore a breastplate bearing the symbol of Corellon Larethian .
description_long: Filsaelene Merwyst Filsaelene Merwyst was a sun elf cleric of Corellon Larethian rescued from captivity by the daemonfey in the ruins beneath Myth Glaurach by Araevin Teshurr and his party . Possessions . Filsaelene carried a longsword and wore a breastplate bearing the symbol of Corellon Larethian . History . While traveling to Elvenport , Filsaelene ' s party was ambushed by fey ' ri near Hellgate Keep . The entire company was slain except Filsaelene , who was spared to be used as breeding stock . Later she joined for a timeAraevin ' s party in their search to destroy the fey ' ri . However she joined the Seiveril Miritar ' s Crusade in the Cormanthor War .

title: Filvendor Floshin
description: Filvendor Floshin Filvendor Floshin was the youngest son of Elorfindar Floshin in Daggerford around 1370 DR . History . Filvendor was the father of Kelson Darktreader and Filarion .
description_long: Filvendor Floshin Filvendor Floshin was the youngest son of Elorfindar Floshin in Daggerford around 1370 DR . History . Filvendor was the father of Kelson Darktreader and Filarion . At one point after 1370 he disappeared from the town . His son Filarion went to search him but with no success . Personality . Filvendor was the son who most resembled Elorfindar . He was spirited and untamed and didn ' t avoid stress in his daily routine , like his father . Elorfindar put much effort into guiding Filvendor , but the son always remained in control of his destiny and was trying to find his personal path .

title: Filzaur
description: Filzaur Filzaur was a male drow wizard and a student of the Inverted Tower in Szith Morcane . Description . An average - looking male drow , Filzaur distinguished himself by his atypical attire among drow society .
description_long: Filzaur Filzaur was a male drow wizard and a student of the Inverted Tower in Szith Morcane . Description . An average - looking male drow , Filzaur distinguished himself by his atypical attire among drow society . He wore gaudy attire of greens and yellows , typically sporting black boots and trousers , an emerald - green shirt , and a yellow sash around his waist . If he had cause to leave the Inverted Tower ( a rare occurrence ) , Filzaur wore a large black cloak over his lighter garments . Personality . Filzaur was particularly studious and tended to isolate himself to his room in the Inverted Tower where he could focus on creating vile " curses " . Abilities . A skilled wizard and the apprentice of Solom Ned ' razak , Filzaur had researched many spell s that caused disease s or inflicted curse s on a victim . In addition , he had studied alchemy and could create a number of magical potion s . Possessions . As an apprentice of the Inverted Tower , Filzaur was denied many possessions owing to the policy of austerity that his master , Solom , enforced .

title: Fimbrul
description: Fimbrul Fimbrul , also known as the Land of Giant s , was a small nation of giants located amid the northern Howling Mountains in Returned Abeir . Fimbrul was known for its few landmarks and the small communities hidden in the snowy mountains . Government .
description_long: Fimbrul Fimbrul , also known as the Land of Giant s , was a small nation of giants located amid the northern Howling Mountains in Returned Abeir . Fimbrul was known for its few landmarks and the small communities hidden in the snowy mountains . Government . Darrawn was the only proper Fimbran city , the rest of the settlements being small trade moots or strongholds not acknowledged by the giants . Because of that , every settlement was self - sufficient and ruled itself . Geography . Fimbrul was composed mostly by the Howling Mountains range . History . After the War of Fang and Talon , most of the surviving primordial s of Abeir went to the Howling Mountains to hide from the wrath of their dragon steeds , and eventually entered into a comma - like sleep . Most of those primordials , such as Blazing Rorn the Fury or Cirotralech , went to hide in the mountains that eventually will become part of Fimbrul . In 1469 DR , a group of oni appeared in Fimbrul and organized the usually scattered Fimbran orc tribes into formidable war bands . The oni then led them against the Fimbran giants .

title: Final Chord
description: Final Chord The Final Chord was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara dedicated to the teachings of Bala , the Zakharan goddess of music . The symbol of the Final Chord was a silver jambiya adorned with silver bells . Activities .
description_long: Final Chord The Final Chord was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara dedicated to the teachings of Bala , the Zakharan goddess of music . The symbol of the Final Chord was a silver jambiya adorned with silver bells . Activities . The Final Chord avoided unwanted attention by keeping an extremely low profile . Targets for their assassinations included supporters of the Pantheon and members of the Storm Which Destroys . History . Followers of Bala were persecuted by the Pantheist League for centuries . Because of this , representatives of the Pantheist League became important targets for the holy slayers of the Final Chord , particularly within the city of Mahabba . Organization . A rumor existed that members of the Final Chord were trained deep within the Grey Jungle . Base of Operations . Though they lacked a specific base , members of the Final Chord were found throughout the Cities of the Pantheon as well as the Ruined Kingdoms .

title: Finch
description: Finch Finch is described as a notorious bard , though perhaps infamous is a better word . Preferring his dulcet singing voice over instruments , Finch was at the very least also a fine lute and mandolin player , having taught Cain Lethellon , the popular Neverwintran lute player , as much as he could . However , despite his international fame as a musician , it would of course be Finch ' s many romantic liasons which made his name more widely known .
description_long: Finch Finch is described as a notorious bard , though perhaps infamous is a better word . Preferring his dulcet singing voice over instruments , Finch was at the very least also a fine lute and mandolin player , having taught Cain Lethellon , the popular Neverwintran lute player , as much as he could . However , despite his international fame as a musician , it would of course be Finch ' s many romantic liasons which made his name more widely known . Early in his career , Finch came to the aid of a monk of Torm named Mayram who was defending some travellers from bandits . The two travelled together for a while , becoming close friends , but Finch found himself falling in love . Knowing full well that the life of a travelling bard and that of an ascetic would not mesh well together , Finch gave her his magical cloak the night before they were due to part ways . Unfortunately , that very night , the pair were overwhelmed by a Malar ite beast cult and Finch was mortally wounded . Mayram fought until she too was near death and with her last moments , draped the cloak back onto Finch so that it ' s magic would save him .

title: Find familiar
description: Find familiar Find familiar was a conjuration ritual that bound a spirit to a warlock or wizard in the form of a familiar . Effects . Familiars summoned in this way were spirits of either celestial , fey or fiend ish nature , depending on the caster ' s choice , that took the form of an animal , also of the caster ' s choice .
description_long: Find familiar Find familiar was a conjuration ritual that bound a spirit to a warlock or wizard in the form of a familiar . Effects . Familiars summoned in this way were spirits of either celestial , fey or fiend ish nature , depending on the caster ' s choice , that took the form of an animal , also of the caster ' s choice . Subsequent castings of the ritual changed the form the spirit took to that of another animal . Typical choices included bat s , cat s , crab s , frog s , hawk s , lizard s , octopus es , owl s , snake s , fish , rat s , raven s , sea horse s , spider s , and weasel s , although warlocks could be granted other forms by their patrons , such as imp s , pseudodragon s , quasit s , or sprite s . Familiars thus summoned had the usual link with their masters , such as a telepathic link over some distance , which included the ability for the caster to see through the creature ' s eyes , the ability to relay touch - based spells and the ability to be temporarily or permanently dismissed . Only one familiar could be bound to a spellcaster at any given time . If a familiar summoned by this spell were killed , it could reappear by a subsequent casting of the ritual .

title: Find steed
description: Find steed Find steed was a conjuration spell for paladins s to call a spirit to take the form of a steed . Effects . The summoned steed could take any form , but most commonly it would take on the common forms of steeds ( warhorse , camel , or mastiff , for example ) .
description_long: Find steed Find steed was a conjuration spell for paladins s to call a spirit to take the form of a steed . Effects . The summoned steed could take any form , but most commonly it would take on the common forms of steeds ( warhorse , camel , or mastiff , for example ) . However , the spirit would have to be chosen from one of three types : celestial , fey , or fiend . The steed was loyal and would act in union with the caster , and commonly had a higher intelligence than a creature of the normal kind . If the spirit was within a mile of the caster , then they could communicate telepathically . If the steed " died " it would leave nothing behind but using the spell again would summon the same mount fully healed . Only one mount could be bound with this spell . While riding the mount , spells cast by the paladin that were normally " self only " could also encompass the steed . Components . The spell required verbal and somatic components .

title: Find the path
description: Find the path Find the path was a divination spell that found the most direct way from point A to point B . The reverse of this spell , lose the path , could completely confuse a creature and prevent it from finding any intended destination . Effects .
description_long: Find the path Find the path was a divination spell that found the most direct way from point A to point B . The reverse of this spell , lose the path , could completely confuse a creature and prevent it from finding any intended destination . Effects . This spell had a simple concept : show the way to a specific point . Non - specific requests like " a place where bulette s roam free " were not be accepted . The caster had to touch the recipient of this spell . All pre - Spellplague versions lasted about two hours ( more for casters with more experience ) but they showed traps , gave passwords for glyphs , and even cancelled the " maze " spell . The target location had to be on the same plane of existence . When cast in reverse , " lose the path " caused the recipient to be hopelessly lost and unable to find an intended destination without aid . The post - Second Sundering version worked much the same way , except it could not be granted to someone else and did not reveal traps , but could last a whole day . Components .

title: Find traps
description: Find traps Find traps was a divination spell that allowed the caster to detect traps . Effect . The oldest version of this spell functioned across an area and revealed all traps in a specific area around the caster .
description_long: Find traps Find traps was a divination spell that allowed the caster to detect traps . Effect . The oldest version of this spell functioned across an area and revealed all traps in a specific area around the caster . A newer version allowed the caster to search for traps like a rogue might within 100 ft ( 30 m ) or more , depending on skill , but it would not make the caster any better at finding them . The post Second Sundering version functioned by letting the caster know that a trap such as " glyph of warding " or " alarm " was within his or her line of sight out to a range of 120 ft ( 37 m ) .

title: Find water
description: Find water Find water was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . With this spell the caster could literally smell a supply of water within a broad expanse of territory depending on their level of power .
description_long: Find water Find water was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . With this spell the caster could literally smell a supply of water within a broad expanse of territory depending on their level of power . The caster was able to tell the direction , general distance , and whether or not the water was underground . This spell did not inform the caster if the water was potable or easily accessible . Components . This spell required a drop of the caster ' s sweat , tears , or spittle to cast .

title: Findar
description: Findar Findar was a human settlement in The Fang , containing the descendants of refugees from the conflict between the humans and the half - elves of the Yuirwood . It was situated on the coast on the west side of The Fang , beneath the cliffs , and the sandy ground made it difficult to grow crops . Findar ' s occupants made their living from the sea instead .
description_long: Findar Findar was a human settlement in The Fang , containing the descendants of refugees from the conflict between the humans and the half - elves of the Yuirwood . It was situated on the coast on the west side of The Fang , beneath the cliffs , and the sandy ground made it difficult to grow crops . Findar ' s occupants made their living from the sea instead . They were hostile towards any non - humans .

title: Finder Wyvernspur
description: Finder Wyvernspur Finder Wyvernspur ( pronounced " FIND - er " ) was a relatively new deity raised to divinity by acquiring the divine spark of the deceased god Moander . Originally he was a powerful bard named Finder Wyvernspur , though history would recall him as The Nameless Bard . Finder was the chaotic neutral demi - power of the cycles of life and transformation of art .
description_long: Finder Wyvernspur Finder Wyvernspur ( pronounced " FIND - er " ) was a relatively new deity raised to divinity by acquiring the divine spark of the deceased god Moander . Originally he was a powerful bard named Finder Wyvernspur , though history would recall him as The Nameless Bard . Finder was the chaotic neutral demi - power of the cycles of life and transformation of art . His symbol was a white harp on gray circle , and his divine realm was within Selûne ' s palace in the Gates of the Moon . Worshipers . Finder ' s church was very small , consisting primarily of younger bards and musicians , and those who sought to change and diversify the arts . His faith was strong only amongst the saurial s of the Lost Vale ( in the Dalelands ) , who owed him their freedom . The specialty priest s of Finder were called Finders . Relationships . Finder was tolerated by most of the good pantheon . His closest ally was Tymora , who sponsored his rise to godhood , and it was believed , as his old patron deity , helped him permanently slay Moander .

title: Fine Rugs
description: Fine Rugs Fine Rugs was a collection of three tents in the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz . It was operated by the shrewd merchant Alik Aksama . Description .
description_long: Fine Rugs Fine Rugs was a collection of three tents in the Grand Bazaar of Huzuz . It was operated by the shrewd merchant Alik Aksama . Description . Fine Rugs was not so much a permanent store as it was three large tents placed together . The first tent was filled with rugs fit for the common shopper . The second brimmed with tapestries of all qualities . The third tent only catered to clients with the heaviest purses . Fine Rugs was always busy , and few left one of the tents without purchasing anything .

title: Finellen
description: Finellen Finellen came from one of the dwarven groups who lived in Myrloch Vale . Description . As was the case of dwarven females , Finellen had a bristling beard that dropped past the beltline .
description_long: Finellen Finellen came from one of the dwarven groups who lived in Myrloch Vale . Description . As was the case of dwarven females , Finellen had a bristling beard that dropped past the beltline . She stood perhaps four feet tall , with a stocky body , short legs , and long arms . Her shoulders were broad and sturdy , and her legs ended in surprisingly large feet , protected by huge leather boots . History . Finellen was captured by firbolg s and was imprisoned alongside Keren Donnell . She was rescued by Tristan Kendrick and helped in their escape .

title: Finger of death
description: Finger of death Finger of death was a spell where the caster would attempt to cause instant death to a target . Effects . The oldest version of the spell would just attempt to kill the target .
description_long: Finger of death Finger of death was a spell where the caster would attempt to cause instant death to a target . Effects . The oldest version of the spell would just attempt to kill the target . The caster would incant the spell while pointing their finger at the target . A later version would also seek to destroy a person ' s life force , but it had the ability to also raise a human killed with the spell and , with an expensive ceremony , turn them into a ju - ju zombie under the caster ' s command . The victim could not to resurrected or raised from the dead in any other way . Only a " limited wish " could end this effect , or a " wish " that would fully resurrect the target . A newer version would again attempt to try and kill the target outright , unless the target managed to resist it , in which case they would take damage instead . The post Second Sundering version would attempt to cause a catastrophic amount of damage and if a target died they would after a few seconds be raised as a zombie , under the caster ' s command . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell . Early druids also needed their holy symbol . History .

title: Finguld Felloki
description: Finguld Felloki Finguld Boomer Felloki was a frost giant warrior in the late 15th century DR . History . Finguld was one of the most trusted warriors of Jarl Fimmel Orelson .
description_long: Finguld Felloki Finguld Boomer Felloki was a frost giant warrior in the late 15th century DR . History . Finguld was one of the most trusted warriors of Jarl Fimmel Orelson . In 1485 DR , during the late stages of the War of the Silver Marches , Finguld was with his jarl when Fimmel finally understood that the drow had deceived him about the brothers of the giant god Thrym and decided to stop his war with Luruar .

title: Fini ' they Tlabbar
description: Fini ' they Tlabbar Fini ' they Tlabbar was a drow priestess of House Faen Tlabbar in Menzoberranzan . Personality . Like her matron mother , Fini ' they was a devoted follower of Lolth and faithfully loyal .
description_long: Fini ' they Tlabbar Fini ' they Tlabbar was a drow priestess of House Faen Tlabbar in Menzoberranzan . Personality . Like her matron mother , Fini ' they was a devoted follower of Lolth and faithfully loyal . History . Before 1358 DR , Fini ' they was a member of a lower - ranking drow house until she was taken in by Ghenni ' tiroth Tlabbar . During the Time of Troubles , K ' yorl Odran took advantage of the loss of magic and attacked House Tlabbar . While making her way to Ghenni ' tiroth Tlabbar ' s chapel , K ' yorl ripped the heart out of Fini ' they .

title: Fior Botpur
description: Fior Botpur Fior Botpur was one of the elected Three Lords of Hlath in Chondath in 1358 DR . Activities . Lord Botpur ruled the city together with Lord Warkas and Lord Nybahn .
description_long: Fior Botpur Fior Botpur was one of the elected Three Lords of Hlath in Chondath in 1358 DR . Activities . Lord Botpur ruled the city together with Lord Warkas and Lord Nybahn . History . In 1358 DR , during an absence of both his colleagues , it was reported to Lord Botpur that a barbarian army from Kara - Tur threatened the city . Quickly he gathered all the prominent citizens to discuss the matter . Botpur wanted to hire an adventuring party for an exploration mission .

title: Firble
description: Firble Firble was a svirfneblin councilor of King Schnicktick in Blingdenstone , and had a secret relationship with Jarlaxle , who traded information . Description . The deep gnome had stubby fingers and was going bald .
description_long: Firble Firble was a svirfneblin councilor of King Schnicktick in Blingdenstone , and had a secret relationship with Jarlaxle , who traded information . Description . The deep gnome had stubby fingers and was going bald . Firble stood about 3 ft 6 in ( 1 . 07 m ) and weighed around 80 lb ( 36 . 29 kg ) . Personality . Firble could be impatient , and though he feared Jarlaxle , he was willing to press the mercenary for information , even if the dark elf pressed back . The deep gnome hated all types of light sources , including torchlight . Possessions . Instead of wearing metal armor , Firble dressed in long smooth robes . History . Around 1357 DR , Firble grew more and more suspicious and fearful of the drow creeping around in the Underdark . After " prompting " from Belwar Dissengulp , Firble agreed to escort Catti - brie to the drow city of Menzoberranzan . Death . After the Battle of Keeper ' s Dale , Belwar Dissengulp carried Firble ' s body away from the battlefield .

title: Firbolg
description: Firbolg The firbolg is a reclusive type of giant - kin that prefers to avoid contact with other sentient races . They are the most intelligent of the giant - kin . Amongst their own kind , they live in colonies , which are usually found in forests or caverns and watched by guard towers .
description_long: Firbolg The firbolg is a reclusive type of giant - kin that prefers to avoid contact with other sentient races . They are the most intelligent of the giant - kin . Amongst their own kind , they live in colonies , which are usually found in forests or caverns and watched by guard towers . Although they do farm , they prefer a more hunter - gatherer lifestyle , rather than the brigand / raider lifestyle of many other giants . A firbolg is usually lawful good in alignment , although they are seen as evil creatures by other giants . Description . Firbolgs resemble human s , and the males sport great , thick beards . Their skin is pink , and their hair , though it comes in many colors , is usually either red or blonde . Firbolgs see the wearing of armor as cowardly , and thus ; do not wear armor . Physiology . Firbolg pregnancies were about two years long . < ref name = " TToT - p16 " >

title: Fire
description: Fire The element of fire was one of the four fundamental building blocks of matter , both useful and dreadful , warming and consuming , changing and purifying . Despite elements generally playing a neutral role in the cosmos , fire was seen as aggressive and evil by many . Cosmology .
description_long: Fire The element of fire was one of the four fundamental building blocks of matter , both useful and dreadful , warming and consuming , changing and purifying . Despite elements generally playing a neutral role in the cosmos , fire was seen as aggressive and evil by many . Cosmology . Fire manifested its position in the cosmos as the Elemental Plane of Fire , one of the Inner Planes . The element was also represented there in living form as fire elemental s . The ruler over the portfolio of fire in Faerûn and Zakhara was the elemental lord Kossuth , while in the Maztica n pantheon it was held by Tezca . Moradin of the dwarves and Flandal Steelskin of the gnomes also had a special interest in fire as it was used in the forge . Talos , the draconic deity Garyx , and the giant power Surtr administered the destructive side of fire . The evil archomental Imix also worked to wrest the claim over the element of fire away from Kossuth , but the greater power remained firmly in control . Magic . School of elemental fire . Many magic al spells utilized the element of fire .

title: Fire Fountain
description: Fire Fountain The Fire Fountain was a fountain of flame at the center of the city of Myth Nantar , in Serôs . The mythal of the city allowed for surface - only effects , such as the fountain ' s ability to shoot flames , which would otherwise have been impossible underwater . The fountain also warmed the water inside the city .
description_long: Fire Fountain The Fire Fountain was a fountain of flame at the center of the city of Myth Nantar , in Serôs . The mythal of the city allowed for surface - only effects , such as the fountain ' s ability to shoot flames , which would otherwise have been impossible underwater . The fountain also warmed the water inside the city .

title: Fire Knives
description: Fire Knives The Fire Knives were a band of assassins that operated out of the city of Westgate , under the approval of the thieves guild known as the Night Masks . The group was led by Lord Tagreth Cormaeril , also referred to as the Grandfather of Assassins . Agents of the guild operated within all the major cities in Cormyr , as well as Chessenta , the Dalelands and Sembia .
description_long: Fire Knives The Fire Knives were a band of assassins that operated out of the city of Westgate , under the approval of the thieves guild known as the Night Masks . The group was led by Lord Tagreth Cormaeril , also referred to as the Grandfather of Assassins . Agents of the guild operated within all the major cities in Cormyr , as well as Chessenta , the Dalelands and Sembia . They were particularly dangerous because of their ability to blend in with high society along with their eagerness to accept almost any job , if only to hone their skills . History . Originally based in Cormyr , the Fire Knives were driven from that nation in 1341 DR when it was discovered they were involved with the assassination of a local lord and the death of a scullery maid . Forced to flee with only what they could carry , many of the remaining members that once operated in Cormyr still possessed some heirlooms from the realm . After this routing it was revealed that many of the members in the guild were members of the Bleth and Cormaeril families . They re - founded the organization at its current base of operations in Castle Cormaeril in 1357 DR . Agents .

title: Fire River
description: Fire River The Fire River was a river in the Vast that ran from the Earthspur Mountains to the Dragon Reach . Description . The Fire River was a wide and mostly placid river that flowed west across the southern Vast , north of the Earthfast Mountains , and into the Dragon Reach and ultimately the Sea of Fallen Stars .
description_long: Fire River The Fire River was a river in the Vast that ran from the Earthspur Mountains to the Dragon Reach . Description . The Fire River was a wide and mostly placid river that flowed west across the southern Vast , north of the Earthfast Mountains , and into the Dragon Reach and ultimately the Sea of Fallen Stars . Along its course , it was joined by a number of springs , which originated in dense stands of trees . The river had its headwaters in the Earthfast Mountains It ran down through the High Country and into the Vast lowlands . The only major cataract on the Fire River was a thundering waterfall near the village of Dragon Falls . There was a rope - pulled ferry across the river for merchant caravans going along the North Road , located a thousand yards above the village . However , the Dragon Falls themselves were actually a spring that cascaded over a bluff alongside the road and joined the Fire River . At the town of Mossbridges was the big multi - span bridge where the Coast Road crossed the Fire River . At its end , the Fire River ran between two large hills and emptied into the Dragon Reach .

title: Fire Wine
description: Fire Wine Fire Wine was a wine exported from the Old Empires . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description .
description_long: Fire Wine Fire Wine was a wine exported from the Old Empires . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description . Crafted in the Old Empires , this black wine burned the belly with its rich spices . Fire Wine was rumored to have a few medicinal properties . Prices . Fire Wine could be purchased in the following containers :

title: Fire agate
description: Fire agate Fire agate was a form of chalcedony which contained arranged in thin lines , giving this stone an iridescent quality . Description . These ornamental stones came in red , brown , gold , and green varieties and in the finest specimens the chalcedony was partially translucent , allowing the color to come through .
description_long: Fire agate Fire agate was a form of chalcedony which contained arranged in thin lines , giving this stone an iridescent quality . Description . These ornamental stones came in red , brown , gold , and green varieties and in the finest specimens the chalcedony was partially translucent , allowing the color to come through . A typical stone had a base value of 10 gp . Powers . Fire agates were used in creating the most potent base for " potions of fire resistance " by dissolving them in fire lizard or pyrolisk blood .

title: Fire arrows
description: Fire arrows Fire arrows was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell caused a regular campfire to spray flaming arrow s .
description_long: Fire arrows Fire arrows was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell caused a regular campfire to spray flaming arrow s . When the spell was cast the fire would immediately extinguish and explode into a shower of arrows . The caster determined the direction of the arrows , and stronger casters had more arrows to control versus weaker casters . Components . This spell required a handful of sand to cast .

title: Fire elemental
description: Fire elemental Fire elementals were elemental s formed from the element of fire . Description . They were fast and agile creatures whose touch could set objects aflame .
description_long: Fire elemental Fire elementals were elemental s formed from the element of fire . Description . They were fast and agile creatures whose touch could set objects aflame . Owing to their fiery nature , they were unable to enter water . They were capable of speaking Ignan although they rarely spoke . Physiology . Fire elementals had flowing through their bodies , which could be used as a magical ingredient . Combat . Fire elementals usually chose to burn opponents with their touch . They attacked ferociously , enjoying burning things in the material plane to cinders . The fire elemental might also slam an opponent , possibly causing them to catch fire . History . The fire elemental Jogaoh was forcibly transported from his home plane to the world of Toril by the extraplanar being Imgig Zu . Employing a Lockstone , Imgig Zu then trapped the powerful fire elemental in the form of a weak dwarf , which in turn bound him to Toril . In the Year of the Prince , 1357 DR , Vajra Valmeyjar and Priam Agrivar brought Jogaoh to the Lockstone , and the magical gem restored him to his true form . Jogaoh returned to his own plane .

title: Fire falcon
description: Fire falcon Fire falcons were small raptors that could be found around the Battle of Bones . Description . These falcons were small birds .
description_long: Fire falcon Fire falcons were small raptors that could be found around the Battle of Bones . Description . These falcons were small birds . Behavior . Fire falcons rarely traveled alone . Instead , they preferred to gather in flights of 2 – 6 birds . Combat . These birds favored swooping attacks on their prey , where they would launch small fiery spheres from their wingtips . All fire falcons were immune to fire - based attacks .

title: Fire gate
description: Fire gate Fire gate was an arcane alteration spell that allowed the caster to step into a large fire and teleport to another such fire . Effects . In order for this spell to work , there had to be at least two large fires ( a minimum of 2 to 4 ft ( 60 to 120 cm in diameter ) within range of each other .
description_long: Fire gate Fire gate was an arcane alteration spell that allowed the caster to step into a large fire and teleport to another such fire . Effects . In order for this spell to work , there had to be at least two large fires ( a minimum of 2 to 4 ft ( 60 to 120 cm in diameter ) within range of each other . The maximum range was 50 yd ( 46 m ) per level of the caster . If more than one such fire existed within range , then the caster could choose the destination . If no suitable destination was available , the spell fizzled and the caster was left standing in the fire . If the destination was blocked by a solid object such that the caster could not exit the fire , then he or she was stranded in the Elemental Plane of Fire and had to find another way out or be rescued .
