" Fire gate " only transported the caster and what he or she was carrying . This spell did not provide any protection from the flames , so it was highly recommended that the caster had some form of fire protection before stepping into a " fire gate " . Components . Only verbal incantations and two large fires were required to cast this spell . History .

title: Fire giant
description: Fire giant Fire giants were a type of giant . Description . Fire giants stood around eighteen feet ( five meters ) tall and were dwarf - like in appearance .
description_long: Fire giant Fire giants were a type of giant . Description . Fire giants stood around eighteen feet ( five meters ) tall and were dwarf - like in appearance . They tended towards orange or red hair and very dark skin . Adults weighed around 7 , 000 pounds ( 3 , 000 kilograms ) . Powers . Although fire giants were immune to fire , they were particularly vulnerable to cold . A fire giant ' s vision was well adapted to cope with the shimmering associated with high temperatures . Society . Fire giants lived in small family groups , called " huslyder " . They preferred to dwell in hot environments like volcanic areas , either in caverns or castles , and existed in societies often led by a king or a queen . Their clothing was usually flame - colored or black , and singed . Armor was generally made from steel . Fire Giants used magically flaming weapons whenever possible . They attacked with rocks heated in fire or lava to soften targets before engaging in melee . Fire Giants were hostage takers and often took payments from less powerful creatures in the surrounding area in exchange for not attacking them . Fire giants spoke Jotunild and Jotun .

title: Fire lichen
description: Fire lichen Fire lichen was a type of lichen that grew in the Underdark near sources of geothermal heat . It was recognizable by its stalks of pale orange - white . When ground to powder and fermented , it formed a paste that was very spicy but edible , added to soups and stews or spread on sporebread for flavor .
description_long: Fire lichen Fire lichen was a type of lichen that grew in the Underdark near sources of geothermal heat . It was recognizable by its stalks of pale orange - white . When ground to powder and fermented , it formed a paste that was very spicy but edible , added to soups and stews or spread on sporebread for flavor . Duergar were known to ferment fire lichen into an extremely hot alcoholic beverage .

title: Fire opal
description: Fire opal Fire opal was a rare gem stone usually found near hot springs and geysers . Description . Fire opal was a brilliant orange - red form of opal that was usually solid in color but could have golden or greenish flashes .
description_long: Fire opal Fire opal was a rare gem stone usually found near hot springs and geysers . Description . Fire opal was a brilliant orange - red form of opal that was usually solid in color but could have golden or greenish flashes . A typical specimen had a base value of 1 , 000 gp . Powers . They were the favored gems to use in " helms of brilliance " . Their affinity for igniting , releasing , and controlling fire made them useful in formulating inks to inscribe scrolls , enchanting immersions for making items , and mounting on devices as a focal point of discharge .

title: Fire purge
description: Fire purge Fire purge was an abjuration spell that prevented normal fires and dampened magical fires in an area . Effects . Within the protected area , normal fires refused to burn and magical fires were reduced to half intensity .
description_long: Fire purge Fire purge was an abjuration spell that prevented normal fires and dampened magical fires in an area . Effects . Within the protected area , normal fires refused to burn and magical fires were reduced to half intensity . Note that this spell did not affect fires that were already burning at the time of casting , it simply prevented ignition of new fires . Magical fires , including " burning hands " , " fire seeds " , " fireball " and even fiery dragon breath were dampened , allowing the targets of a fire attack a better chance to resist or avoid the fire and reducing any resulting damage . The area of effect was a 10 yd ( 9 . 1 m ) square and lasted ten minutes . This spell could be cast cooperatively with other priests , increasing the protected area exponentially and prolonging the duration . Components . Verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell as well as the priest ' s holy symbol and a sliver of wood that had been scorched by fire .

title: Fire sand
description: Fire sand Fire sand was a dangerous magical sand found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate , that created intense sheets of flame . Powers . " Fire sand " could be used in two ways : as a burning wall , or as an area spell .
description_long: Fire sand Fire sand was a dangerous magical sand found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate , that created intense sheets of flame . Powers . " Fire sand " could be used in two ways : as a burning wall , or as an area spell . " Fire sand " could be thrown up to 20 feet ( 6 m ) and covered a 10 foot by 10 foot square area . The magical sand ignited upon impact with the ground , burning everything within its effective area . If poured into a line , or any other shape , and then ignited with a flame or when struck , " fire sand " would create a burning wall that burned hotter than thrown " fire sand " . A 20 foot wall could be created per handful of sand used . Once activated , " fire sand " burned for 3 - 12 minutes .

title: Fire shield
description: Fire shield Fire shield , also known as Dragonflame mantle during the Spellplague , was an evocation spell used to immolate the caster in protective and offensive flames . Effects . When " fire shield " was cast , it enveloped the caster in a fiery shield that made it more difficult for enemies to attack the caster and burned any who came in contact .
description_long: Fire shield Fire shield , also known as Dragonflame mantle during the Spellplague , was an evocation spell used to immolate the caster in protective and offensive flames . Effects . When " fire shield " was cast , it enveloped the caster in a fiery shield that made it more difficult for enemies to attack the caster and burned any who came in contact . During the Spellplague , " fire shield " was called " dragonflame mantle " and was used by sorcerer s . The spell was somewhat difficult to cast and required a short rest of a few minutes or more before it could be cast again . Pre - and post - Second Sundering , it was used by wizard s as well as sorcerers and could call flames of hot or cold . It was also considered more powerful and not only protected the caster from attacks , but made them temporarily immune . There was an added versatility as well , as the flames protecting the caster could either be scorching hot or freezing cold when it contacted with an attacker ' s flesh . It gave off light by the flames , reaching up to 10 ft ( 3 m ) with half the illumination of a torch . The older versions also had shorter reach . Components .

title: Fire shroud
description: Fire shroud Fire shroud , originally named flame shroud and also published under the name shroud of flame , was an arcane evocation spell that caused one creature to be engulfed in flames and endanger those around it . Post - Spellplague , this spell attacked all enemies close to the caster , but with less intensity . Colloquially , it was called the " trollkiller " spell .
description_long: Fire shroud Fire shroud , originally named flame shroud and also published under the name shroud of flame , was an arcane evocation spell that caused one creature to be engulfed in flames and endanger those around it . Post - Spellplague , this spell attacked all enemies close to the caster , but with less intensity . Colloquially , it was called the " trollkiller " spell . Effects . The earliest versions of this spell could target a single creature up to 10 yd ( 9 . 1 m ) away . A later version increased this range relative to the level of the caster . The post - Spellplague version was centered on the caster themselves , but attacked all enemies ( and only enemies ) within a radius of 15 ft ( 4 . 6 m ) . Unless the target managed to resist the casting of this spell , it immediately started to burn . All flammable items worn or carried by the target also caught fire , although magical items had their own chance to resist the fire . Volatile oils were easily ignited by the flames and added their damage to the conflagration .

title: Fire spiral
description: Fire spiral Fire spiral was a flame and abjuration spell utilized by members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara . Effects . This spell created a spiral thread of flame that originated at the caster ' s feet and wound around their body before terminating above their head .
description_long: Fire spiral Fire spiral was a flame and abjuration spell utilized by members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara . Effects . This spell created a spiral thread of flame that originated at the caster ' s feet and wound around their body before terminating above their head . The " fire spiral " would flex to interrupt any incoming attack , both ranged and melee , directed at the caster . The " fire spiral " would block all attacks for the duration of the spell , which varied depending on the skill of the caster , but usually lasted for several minutes . All mundane missiles and weapons touched by the " fire spiral " were instantly vaporized . Magical weapons also had a chance of being destroyed , but their enchantments offered a degree of resistance . A magical weapon not destroyed by the " fire spiral " was deflected instead . Any attacker holding a weapon vaporized by a " fire spiral " suffered intense burns . Likewise , anyone attempting to touch the caster would also be burned horribly .

title: Fire storm
description: Fire storm Fire storm was an evocation spell that permeated a area of effect with sheets of flame . Effect . The target area would be drench all creatures within the area in flame similar to a " wall of fire " causing damage but usually not for a very long time but .
description_long: Fire storm Fire storm was an evocation spell that permeated a area of effect with sheets of flame . Effect . The target area would be drench all creatures within the area in flame similar to a " wall of fire " causing damage but usually not for a very long time but . Some older versions had the ability to reverse the spell to fire quench , extinguished an equal area of magical fire , or twice the area of normal fire . Components . This spell required vocal and somatic components . Realmslore . The arcane version of " fire storm " was originally common only to the Red Wizards of Thay .

title: Fire track
description: Fire track Fire track was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a spark that followed a target just like a hound on the scent .
description_long: Fire track Fire track was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a spark that followed a target just like a hound on the scent . The target was identified by the caster either by name or physical description . If the target was not within the spell ' s range for the last 24 hours , then the spark would fall to the ground and extinguish . If the target was within range , then the spark would land on the trail and begin to follow the target like a lit fuse . Scorch marks upon the ground clearly marked the path of the spark for the caster to see but these were easily swept clean . Anything that got in the way of the spark would get burned as if contacted by a torch . Flammable surfaces were also susceptible to the spark as it passed . The fire track could not cross water and would extinguish as soon as it made contact . Strong wind , rain , or sand could also extinguish the fire track if it was covered . Targets who escape via teleportation caused the fire track to circle the area where the target disappeared until the spell ended . Components .

title: Fire trap
description: Fire trap Fire trap was both an abjuration and evocation spell that could be used on any closeable item , causing a small fiery explosion upon unauthorized entry . History . This spell was invented by the arcanist and Fire Warden of Netheril Noanar in −2319 DR .
description_long: Fire trap Fire trap was both an abjuration and evocation spell that could be used on any closeable item , causing a small fiery explosion upon unauthorized entry . History . This spell was invented by the arcanist and Fire Warden of Netheril Noanar in −2319 DR . It was the first of his many fire - based spells , and originally called Noanar ' s trap .

title: Fire truth
description: Fire truth Fire truth was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects .
description_long: Fire truth Fire truth was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects . This spell was used to determine if someone was speaking the truth . The target was questioned by the wizard and spoke into a special candle while it was lit . Half - truths or slight deceptions caused the flame to gutter ; a lie extinguished the flame . This spell lasted for ten questions or until the candle was extinguished by a lie . If the target believed what they were saying was the truth then the candle read this as truth , even if it was false information . Components . This spell required a candle made from a rare desert bee ' s wax that cost 300 gold pieces .

title: Fireball
description: Fireball Fireball was an arcane spell that created a tiny ball of fire that flew forward from the caster , exploding in a huge fireball at a point designated by the caster . While an extremely potent spell , the caster had to take care to avoid catching allies in the explosion , or to accidentally strike an obstruction and detonate the spell early . Effects .
description_long: Fireball Fireball was an arcane spell that created a tiny ball of fire that flew forward from the caster , exploding in a huge fireball at a point designated by the caster . While an extremely potent spell , the caster had to take care to avoid catching allies in the explosion , or to accidentally strike an obstruction and detonate the spell early . Effects . Before the Spellplague , " fireball " at its weakest had a range of over four hundred feet , but after the collapse of the Weave its range was greatly reduced , only reaching a hundred feet . Components . In the Raumviran spellcasting tradition , the verbal component was the word " Kelenta " . Many versions had verbal and somantic components but also the need for a tiny amount of bat guano or sulphur . History . This spell was developed by the Fire Warden of Netheril Noanar and named Noanar ' s fireball in −2303 DR , two years after its more powerful companion " delayed blast fireball " . It was the arcanist ' s last invention , three years before his death at the hands of his long - time enemies and victims , the Canlespiere ogre s . Realmslore .

title: Firebead Elvenhair
description: Firebead Elvenhair Firebead Elvenhair was a mage who traveled the Sword Coast in search of books for the sages at Candlekeep , such as Gorion . That he made purchases for the monastery was a badly kept secret among the book dealers of Baldur ' s Gate and Beregost . Appearances .
description_long: Firebead Elvenhair Firebead Elvenhair was a mage who traveled the Sword Coast in search of books for the sages at Candlekeep , such as Gorion . That he made purchases for the monastery was a badly kept secret among the book dealers of Baldur ' s Gate and Beregost . Appearances . Firebead Elvenhair appeared twice in the " Baldur ' s Gate computer game " . First in the Candlekeep Inn were he tasked the player to retrieve a scroll from Tethtoril . He later appeared in Beregost , searching for " The History of the Fateful Coin " .

title: Firecam full - plate armor
description: Firecam full - plate armor The Firecam full - plate armor was the personal suit of armor of Sir Keldorn Firecam . It was designed specifically for him , so very few others could wear it . It was a " + 1 full plate armor " that granted the wearer to ability to move freely through hindrances such as webs , as well as boosted resistances to effects that assailed them .
description_long: Firecam full - plate armor The Firecam full - plate armor was the personal suit of armor of Sir Keldorn Firecam . It was designed specifically for him , so very few others could wear it . It was a " + 1 full plate armor " that granted the wearer to ability to move freely through hindrances such as webs , as well as boosted resistances to effects that assailed them .

title: Firedrake ( county )
description: Firedrake ( county ) County Firedrake was both the most populated and the most dangerous county on the Dragon ' s Neck Peninsula in Tethyr . Description . The waters around the peninsula were constantly full of pirates , which made life on this county risk for its citizens .
description_long: Firedrake ( county ) County Firedrake was both the most populated and the most dangerous county on the Dragon ' s Neck Peninsula in Tethyr . Description . The waters around the peninsula were constantly full of pirates , which made life on this county risk for its citizens . The many beaches provided perfect opportunities for the trades of glassblowing , fishing , and shipbuilding . Geography . Firedrake rested on the westernmost tip of the peninsula , known as the Dragon ' s Head . It was one of the counties of the of Cape Velen , along with Fyraven and Greenshores farther to the east . The county takes its name from Firedrake Bay , which rested between the Dragon ' s Neck and Starspire Peninsulas . Government . Firedrake was governed by Ondul Jarduth in 1370 DR from his manor house of Millvulthan in Velen , but he was often absent , working instead at Tordraken or Faerntarn . Notable Locations . The haunted city of Velen was the most notable settlement in the county .

title: Firedrake Bay
description: Firedrake Bay Firedrake Bay was the bay located between the Tethyr Peninsula and the Starspire Peninsula . Port Kir was located at its southeastern corner . Geography .
description_long: Firedrake Bay Firedrake Bay was the bay located between the Tethyr Peninsula and the Starspire Peninsula . Port Kir was located at its southeastern corner . Geography . The bay was relatively safe from storms and had calm waters . Flora & Fauna . The waters of the bay contained a wide variety of shellfish — clams , lobsters , and shrimp . A particular kind of lobster , the star lobster , was only found in this bay , in the region of Port Kir . Rumors & Legends . The " Amulet of Ioma " , a magical item once worn by the first Black Alaric , was believed to have been at the bottom of the bay .

title: Firedrinker ' s Inn
description: Firedrinker ' s Inn Firedrinker ' s Inn was an inn found in Yhaunn in 1358 DR . This famous establishment had a pristine reputation among the traveling folk of the Sea of Fallen Stars . Description .
description_long: Firedrinker ' s Inn Firedrinker ' s Inn was an inn found in Yhaunn in 1358 DR . This famous establishment had a pristine reputation among the traveling folk of the Sea of Fallen Stars . Description . Luxurious furnishings adorned Firedrinker ' s Inn , making it a popular resting place for those who could afford the expensive rates . Fine dining matched the furnishing , either brought directly to a patron ' s room or served in the dining room accompanied by music and dance .

title: Firefeed
description: Firefeed Firefeed was a strange wizard spell that combined the element of fire with healing . Effects . The caster of this spell could heal himself by physically touching a flame .
description_long: Firefeed Firefeed was a strange wizard spell that combined the element of fire with healing . Effects . The caster of this spell could heal himself by physically touching a flame . The intensity of the flame determined the amount of healing granted to the caster , with higher intensity fires granting more healing . The fire was immediately extinguished once the caster touched the flame to receive the healing effects .

title: Firefiend
description: Firefiend Firefiend was a unique magic weapon wielded by a tasked slayer genie called the Head Taker . " Firefiend " was one of two dangerous swords wielded by the Head Taker , with the other being " Widowmaker . " Description .
description_long: Firefiend Firefiend was a unique magic weapon wielded by a tasked slayer genie called the Head Taker . " Firefiend " was one of two dangerous swords wielded by the Head Taker , with the other being " Widowmaker . " Description . " Firefiend " was a massive great scimitar . Powers . Despite its size , this sword behaved as a scimitar of speed , allowing the wielder to strike before any opponent . Additional magical properties of " Firefiend " also made it much more likely for the wielder to strike and harm their opponent . Once per day , the wielder of " Firefiend " could self - immolate , causing intense flames to surround both the sword and their body . Anyone coming into contact with the flames , either by being struck by the sword or by touching the wielder ' s body , were instantly burned . Any metal object that touched the flames risked being melted . The flames also ignited all flammable objects , such as clothing , on contact . The wielder , and all of their possessions , were immune to these magical flames . Additionally , the wielder was completely immune to all normal and magical cold - based attacks while the flames were active .

title: Fireflow
description: Fireflow The Fireflow , also called Gaping Stream , was one of the watercourses of the Esmelflow in Amn . Description . The water in this stream was icy cold .
description_long: Fireflow The Fireflow , also called Gaping Stream , was one of the watercourses of the Esmelflow in Amn . Description . The water in this stream was icy cold . Geography . This creek began at the Gaping Face Cascade in the Qadim Hills and served as the western branch of upper Khalleshyr river . History . The famous ranger Vinnam once escaped from a band of troll s by plunging into this stream . Strangely , the trolls seemed to avoid the water as if it were fire , and so Vinnam named it the Fireflow .

title: Firefoam
description: Firefoam Firefoam was the famous war steed of the Knights of Myth Drannor leader , Florin Falconhand . Description . Florin ' s horse was a very intellectual white charger or heavy war horse .
description_long: Firefoam Firefoam was the famous war steed of the Knights of Myth Drannor leader , Florin Falconhand . Description . Florin ' s horse was a very intellectual white charger or heavy war horse . The beast could communicate through telepathy , recognize danger , and could fight alone with hooves and teeth . History . Gained by a magical wish , Firefoam was the equivalent of a paladin ' s war horse , who served Florin until 1373 DR .

title: Firelands
description: Firelands The Firelands was a region of the Underdark located beneath the jungles of Chult . Geography . The Firelands were located beneath the jungles of Chult .
description_long: Firelands The Firelands was a region of the Underdark located beneath the jungles of Chult . Geography . The Firelands were located beneath the jungles of Chult . Lava tubes to the Peaks of Flame provided connections to the surface . Description . The Firelands were full of lava tubes and other volcanic features . In the center of the Firelands was the Burning Rift , which contained innumerable " portal s " to the Elemental Plane of Fire . Inhabitants . The Firelands were home to azer , flamesnake s , magmin s , and salamander s that had migrated from the Plane of Fire through " portals " .

title: Firenewt
description: Firenewt Firenewts were reptilian humanoids native to volcanic regions , who evolved from lizardfolk and gained the ability to breathe fire . Description . Firenewts were about the size of a slim human .
description_long: Firenewt Firenewts were reptilian humanoids native to volcanic regions , who evolved from lizardfolk and gained the ability to breathe fire . Description . Firenewts were about the size of a slim human . They appeared like lizardfolk with simpler faces and larger , dark - colored eyes . Their speckled , smooth - scaled skin appeared eel - like and was colored dark reddish brown at their spines and faded to nearly white on their front sides . They had long feet , giving them the appearance of " reversed knees " , which gave them an advantage while running or leaping . Firenewt warriors typically wore chain mail and carried longsword s , battleaxe s , scimitar s , or longspear s . They were often seen riding upon the backs of giant strider s , creatures that they believed that Imix sent to aid them , as they were able to breath fire . The firenewts provided shelter and food for them and provided breeding grounds in their lairs for them . Habitat . Firenewts required a heated source of water in order to survive and breed . Separation from warm water for more than a tenday would cause a firenewt to slow mentally and physically , eventually entering hibernation .

title: Firepeaks
description: Firepeaks The Firepeaks were a series of mountains located in the Endless Wastes . Description . The Firepeaks , which received their name from the reddish glow seen at night , were located several hundred miles east of Almorel and were considered one of the most famous landmarks in the Endless Wastes .
description_long: Firepeaks The Firepeaks were a series of mountains located in the Endless Wastes . Description . The Firepeaks , which received their name from the reddish glow seen at night , were located several hundred miles east of Almorel and were considered one of the most famous landmarks in the Endless Wastes . An active geothermal basin surrounded by a circle of volcanic mountains , eruptions from at least one of the peaks occurred nearly weekly . The ash thrown into the air could be seen as far as the Spice Road , which passed within 100 miles of the mountain range . The nomadic tribes of the area considered the mountains sacred , calling them " Badara - Kharshi " , or " Land of the Fire God . " They could not be visited by the nomads until ritual preparations were made . Many outsiders came to the mountains to use their many hot springs , which were said to have healing and spiritual properties . Inhabitants . The Firepeaks were known to be inhabited by an ancient Dwarven kingdom , numbering at about 5 , 000 dwarves , known as the Siremun , ( the " Iron Men " ) , to the nomads .

title: Fireseed
description: Fireseed Fireseed was an alcohol ic beverage made by dwarves . It was a non - magic al liquor that had negligible effects on dwarves and gnome s . Fireseed was more potent to other races , however , either increasing natural resistances or debilitating drunkenness .
description_long: Fireseed Fireseed was an alcohol ic beverage made by dwarves . It was a non - magic al liquor that had negligible effects on dwarves and gnome s . Fireseed was more potent to other races , however , either increasing natural resistances or debilitating drunkenness . Dwarves and expert brewers could easily identify fireseed by its smell . It was stored in brown glass bottles that contained six shots .

title: Fireshear
description: Fireshear Fireshear was a mining city in the Frozenfar in Northwest Faerûn , on the coast west of the Iceflow river . Geography . The city ' s location was chosen because of the rich copper and silver veins in the area , exposed by a violent event such as a volcano or something falling from the sky .
description_long: Fireshear Fireshear was a mining city in the Frozenfar in Northwest Faerûn , on the coast west of the Iceflow river . Geography . The city ' s location was chosen because of the rich copper and silver veins in the area , exposed by a violent event such as a volcano or something falling from the sky . Government . The large city was ruled by three merchants , one each from Mirabar , Neverwinter and Waterdeep . These merchants were responsible for the hiring of adventurers when patrols or information was needed . The city ' s emblem was a crossed blade , pick and shovel underneath an orange flame , on an ice - blue field . Inhabitants . The city ' s miners were hired from the Sword Coast populace , and shipped into the city along with other workers such as healers . Miners were paid 100 gold pieces per month as of 1366 DR . For half the year , " lock - in " keeps the city cut off by the ice . Defense . Fireshear ' s miners made up the military , which numbered 10 , 000 . Attacks from bear s , crag cat s , and orc s happened occasionally , and when the city kept sheep as an extra food source , this would attract wolves .

title: Firesoul genasi
description: Firesoul genasi A firesoul genasi , also known as an fire genasi , was a type of genasi that was able to harness the power of fire . Description . Many firesoul genasi carried obvious traits from the Elemental Plane of Fire , such as coal - colored skin , flame - like hair , and fiery eyes .
description_long: Firesoul genasi A firesoul genasi , also known as an fire genasi , was a type of genasi that was able to harness the power of fire . Description . Many firesoul genasi carried obvious traits from the Elemental Plane of Fire , such as coal - colored skin , flame - like hair , and fiery eyes . Personality . Firesoul genasi were generally energetic and quick to act . They were impatient and dressed flamboyantly . Abilities . Firesoul genasi could summon nonmagical flame . They were also resistant to fire . Religion . Firesoul genasi could worship any deity , but clerics were devotees of Gond , Talos , or Kossuth . Locations . Firesoul genasi could be found anywhere , but were most commonly found in Calimshan , Chult , the Lake of Steam , and Unther . Most firesoul genasi in Faerûn were descended from efreet , particularly those that ruled Calimshan .

title: Firespiders
description: Firespiders Firespiders creates 240 tiny fire elemental s in form of small burning spiders . History . Thousands of years ago drow used this spell to set afire large parts of what is now the Border Forest and separated it from Cormanthor .
description_long: Firespiders Firespiders creates 240 tiny fire elemental s in form of small burning spiders . History . Thousands of years ago drow used this spell to set afire large parts of what is now the Border Forest and separated it from Cormanthor . Effects . The spell creates a swarm of spiders which search the area for something or someone to attack and ignite . The elementals are immune to fire but vulnerable to water or other nonflammable liquids . They will not die after the attack . Instead they will stay until they are slain or banished or the spell expires . Material components . The caster needs rubys or ruby dust worth at least 500gp . The spell needs also a somatic and vocal component .

title: Firesteap Mountains
description: Firesteap Mountains The Firesteap Mountains stretched from the edge of the Lake of Steam to the forest of Chondalwood , then go on to the northern border of the Shaar , meeting the land beyond . The mountains do not have many monsters but the Shaaryan tribes claimed there were ancient tombs and killed or captured anyone that did not have traditional rights . The northern mountains had a couple of thieves and monsters that struck at caravans .
description_long: Firesteap Mountains The Firesteap Mountains stretched from the edge of the Lake of Steam to the forest of Chondalwood , then go on to the northern border of the Shaar , meeting the land beyond . The mountains do not have many monsters but the Shaaryan tribes claimed there were ancient tombs and killed or captured anyone that did not have traditional rights . The northern mountains had a couple of thieves and monsters that struck at caravans .

title: Firestorm Cabal
description: Firestorm Cabal The Firestorm Cabal was a loosely organized organization of genasi with chapters in Airspur , Calimport and Memnon . The Airspur chapter was dedicated to protecting Akanûl and the chapter often did Queen Arathane ' s dirty work for her . The organization was disliked by many of the lower classes in Airspur but was viewed favorably by the upper classes .
description_long: Firestorm Cabal The Firestorm Cabal was a loosely organized organization of genasi with chapters in Airspur , Calimport and Memnon . The Airspur chapter was dedicated to protecting Akanûl and the chapter often did Queen Arathane ' s dirty work for her . The organization was disliked by many of the lower classes in Airspur but was viewed favorably by the upper classes . The Calimshan chapters were more interested in maintaining the purity of genasi souls . That is , they wanted to prevent Airsoul and Firesoul genasi from mixing with genasi of other manisfestations . While the Airspur chapter had a few non - genasi members the Calimshan chapters were open to only genasi . History . The Firestorm Cabal was founded in Calimshan and the organization later expanded into Airspur . Cabal members were among the first to take up arms during the Second Era of Skyfire . In 1479 DR the Airspur chapter was infiltrated by the Cult of the Elder Elemental Eye . The cult ' s leader ( Murmur ) possessed a high ranking officer while she was sleeping and recruited many low - ranking members of the cabal into the cult .

title: Firethorn
description: Firethorn Firethorn , or Sea Rose , was a naturally occurring plant on the Island of the Firethorns within the Genie ' s Turban off the coast of mainland Zakhara . Description . The presence of firethorn gave the Island of the Firethorns a lovely red coloration .
description_long: Firethorn Firethorn , or Sea Rose , was a naturally occurring plant on the Island of the Firethorns within the Genie ' s Turban off the coast of mainland Zakhara . Description . The presence of firethorn gave the Island of the Firethorns a lovely red coloration . Though beautiful , the firethorn plant ' s thorns carried a dangerous poison , creating a natural barrier that surrounded most of the lower portions of the island since the plants grew so close together . Firethorn plants also gave off natural heat and glowed softly .

title: Firetrees
description: Firetrees Firetrees was a small town located in the Greenfields of Unther , East Faerûn , as of 1357 DR . Background . The town was named after its red - colored trees , that shone in the night with unnatural phosphorescence .
description_long: Firetrees Firetrees was a small town located in the Greenfields of Unther , East Faerûn , as of 1357 DR . Background . The town was named after its red - colored trees , that shone in the night with unnatural phosphorescence . Firetrees was known for its feasts and festivals , and for being one of the most important centers were the cult of Tiamat had most influence than the cult of Gilgeam . Government . As of 1357 DR , Firetrees was ruled by Lord Tukulti , a wizard loyal to Gilgeam . However , most people ignored his edicts or openly insulted him . Economy . Firetrees was a farming community and a popular stop for trading caravans . History . Firetrees was destroyed alongside the rest of Unther during the Spellplague .

title: Firetrees ( Returned Abeir )
description: Firetrees ( Returned Abeir ) Firetrees , originally named Durlyndbold and later Raurokh , was a ruined fortress located in eastern Eskorn , Returned Abeir . Description . The fortress was located in a scorched land of tumbled stones , amid a forest of burned tree trunks and fire - blackened rocks where no new plants could grow , hence its name .
description_long: Firetrees ( Returned Abeir ) Firetrees , originally named Durlyndbold and later Raurokh , was a ruined fortress located in eastern Eskorn , Returned Abeir . Description . The fortress was located in a scorched land of tumbled stones , amid a forest of burned tree trunks and fire - blackened rocks where no new plants could grow , hence its name . The fortress was enveloped in a powerful magic that warped the senses , abilities , and shapes of any living creatures , and mysterious eerie lights drifted about its ruins . Inhabitants . Terrible monsters plagued the land and scholars also believed the place was cursed with a mysterious sentient spell . Unknown to most people , a few tribes of dragonborn also lived in the subterranean ruins of Firetrees since centuries before the Spellplague . History . The fortress was built by dwarves in the ancient past of the world of Abeir , and originally was named Durlyndbold . When a sentient spell appeared and began to spread a plague that rotted flesh , the dwarves abandoned Durlyndbold and scattered across Abeir .

title: Firewine Bridge
description: Firewine Bridge Firewine Bridge was once an elven trading town , but it was destroyed around 1168 DR in a sorcerous battle . By 1368 DR , " Firewine Bridge " was a fallow field of overgrown rubble dominated by a large area of wild magic . The sorcerous battle was so mighty that it not only leveled the elven town , it also altered the course of the stream over which the bridge crossed .
description_long: Firewine Bridge Firewine Bridge was once an elven trading town , but it was destroyed around 1168 DR in a sorcerous battle . By 1368 DR , " Firewine Bridge " was a fallow field of overgrown rubble dominated by a large area of wild magic . The sorcerous battle was so mighty that it not only leveled the elven town , it also altered the course of the stream over which the bridge crossed . The small settlement of Gullykin rested hard up against the rubble field and was partially affected by the area of wild magic . Legend . The bard Poe wrote a lay , telling of the fate of the Elven Knights of Firewine : " I ' ve a tale , a tale to tellof Knights so bold and dungeons hell , and slumber broke upon the shoreof nightmare ' s reef when dawn no more . A story true of courage lack , and footing lost on virtues track , and trailing far but near to feara vengeance scream through night to ear . The swordsmen came by two and fourto take their fight to evil ' s core with confidence in might and right " went bravely forward spreading light . But light alone canst clear the pathwhen suffers all a hellish wrath from deep below whence fires came , still none above dare speak the name .

title: Firkraag
description: Firkraag Firkraag , also known as Lord Jierdan Firkraag , was a red dragon living in the Windspear Hills in Amn and masquerading as a human noble . He took over the area after financially ruining the rightful owner of the lands , Garren Windspear , and made his lair in an old temple / tomb complex nearby . Firkraag surrounded himself with such minions as orc s , hobgoblin s , ogrillon s , wolfwere s and golems s .
description_long: Firkraag Firkraag , also known as Lord Jierdan Firkraag , was a red dragon living in the Windspear Hills in Amn and masquerading as a human noble . He took over the area after financially ruining the rightful owner of the lands , Garren Windspear , and made his lair in an old temple / tomb complex nearby . Firkraag surrounded himself with such minions as orc s , hobgoblin s , ogrillon s , wolfwere s and golems s . Another notable follower of the dragon was Tazok , previously a minion of Sarevok . Having been in the past wounded by Gorion and " his Harper friends , " Firkraag plotted revenge against Gorion ' s adopted child — the protagonist of the - when he or she arrived in Amn . The player can meet the polymorphed " Lord Jierdan " in The Copper Coronet in Athkatla , and he will make a generous - seeming offer for them to come and help clear out the monsters infesting the lands supposedly belonging to him .

title: First Age
description: First Age The First Age of Netheril began in - 3859 DR when the human communities of Fenwick , Gers , Gilan , Gustaf , Moran , Nauseef , and Janick all banded together to protect themselves . Description . At first , the community was known as Seventon , but Nether the Elder renamed the alliance " Netheril " .
description_long: First Age The First Age of Netheril began in - 3859 DR when the human communities of Fenwick , Gers , Gilan , Gustaf , Moran , Nauseef , and Janick all banded together to protect themselves . Description . At first , the community was known as Seventon , but Nether the Elder renamed the alliance " Netheril " . Over the years , Netheril learned the knowledge of magic from the Eaerlanni elves and soon all the inhabitants were becoming arcanist s . Timeline . - 3859 DR - 3856 DR - 3848 DR - 3847 DR - 3845 DR - 3830 DR - 3827 DR - 3772 DR

title: First Crown War
description: First Crown War - 12 , 000 . Aryvandaar , lead by the Vyshaan clan , invades Miyeritar and pressures Shantel Othreier to accept occupation or suffer the same fate . - 11 , 800 .
description_long: First Crown War - 12 , 000 . Aryvandaar , lead by the Vyshaan clan , invades Miyeritar and pressures Shantel Othreier to accept occupation or suffer the same fate . - 11 , 800 . Aryvandaar occupies Miyeritar but has to deal with dark and sylvan elf resistance fighters . Illefarn provides safe havens for elves fleeing Miyeritar . - 11 , 300 . Aryvandaar fully conquers Miyeritar , ending the First Crown War .

title: First Flowering
description: First Flowering The First Flowering was a period in Faerûn ' s history between - 24000 DR and - 12000 DR . At the start of this period , the elves had split into five major realms : Aryvandaar , Illefarn , Keltormir , Miyeritar and Shantel Othreier , as well as several smaller ones such as Eiellûr , Ilythiir , Orishaar , Syòrpiir and Thearnytaar . During the First Flowering , the last of the winged elven race Avariel are believed to have left Faerûn .
description_long: First Flowering The First Flowering was a period in Faerûn ' s history between - 24000 DR and - 12000 DR . At the start of this period , the elves had split into five major realms : Aryvandaar , Illefarn , Keltormir , Miyeritar and Shantel Othreier , as well as several smaller ones such as Eiellûr , Ilythiir , Orishaar , Syòrpiir and Thearnytaar . During the First Flowering , the last of the winged elven race Avariel are believed to have left Faerûn .

title: First Lancers
description: First Lancers The First Lancers , also called the Blazes , was part of the standing army of the efreet in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire . Organization . Noble efreet led these medium cavalry who numbered 1 , 000 strong .
description_long: First Lancers The First Lancers , also called the Blazes , was part of the standing army of the efreet in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire . Organization . Noble efreet led these medium cavalry who numbered 1 , 000 strong . Nightmares served as their mounts . Activities . The First Lancers were used against fallen nobles or to quell small rebellions . Their noble efreeti commanders enjoyed lording their position of power over others . Base of Operations . The City of Brass served as the base of the First Lancers .

title: First Sundering
description: First Sundering The First Sundering ( sometimes simply The Sundering ) or Ever ' Sakkatien ( as called by the Tel - quessir ) , was a High Magic ritual cast by the greatest High Mage s of the Tel - quessir during the period of The First Flowering , around – 17600 DR . The ritual resulted in the creation of the Isle of Evermeet , but also resulted in widespread disaster which destroyed or altered much of Faerûn and may even be the cause of much of the non - uniformity of the Weave throughout the continent . Ever ' Sakkatien is somehow connected to the more recent Second Sundering , an event that takes place in the 1480s DR .
description_long: First Sundering The First Sundering ( sometimes simply The Sundering ) or Ever ' Sakkatien ( as called by the Tel - quessir ) , was a High Magic ritual cast by the greatest High Mage s of the Tel - quessir during the period of The First Flowering , around – 17600 DR . The ritual resulted in the creation of the Isle of Evermeet , but also resulted in widespread disaster which destroyed or altered much of Faerûn and may even be the cause of much of the non - uniformity of the Weave throughout the continent . Ever ' Sakkatien is somehow connected to the more recent Second Sundering , an event that takes place in the 1480s DR . History . Place of the Gathering . Hundreds of years before the ritual began , elves prepared the place for the casting of the magic . The place was surrounded by small villages , where the elves lived . The gathering place itself was at a special place in the heart of the continent Faerûn . They built there a tower of white granite which reflected the colors of the sky . It was higher than any tower built by elves before .

title: First Tymanther - Unther War
description: First Tymanther - Unther War The First Tymanther – Unther War was a conflict between the nations of Tymanther and Unther that took place in the Year of the Rune Lords Triumphant , 1487 DR . < ref name = " TDYK / Hardcover - p109 - 115 " > < / ref > History . At some point in 1486 DR , while on the world of Abeir , the god - king Gilgeam contacted the demon lord Graz ' zt and asked him to aid Unther in their war against the genasi forces of Shyr .
description_long: First Tymanther - Unther War The First Tymanther – Unther War was a conflict between the nations of Tymanther and Unther that took place in the Year of the Rune Lords Triumphant , 1487 DR . < ref name = " TDYK / Hardcover - p109 - 115 " > < / ref > History . At some point in 1486 DR , while on the world of Abeir , the god - king Gilgeam contacted the demon lord Graz ' zt and asked him to aid Unther in their war against the genasi forces of Shyr . Graz ' zt provided Gilgeam with an army of demon s to bolster his forces in exchange for powerful Abeiran magic item s . < ref name = " TDYK / Hardcover - p94 , 141 , 310 " > < / ref > On Nightal 15 of 1486 DR , members of the Liberators of the Steel Sky accomplished the impossible and opened a portal to Abeir in the Catacombs of Djerad Thymar , believing they would save the dragonborn inhabitants of that world . < ref name = " AotT / Hardcover - p9 - 11 " > < / ref > However , one of the maurezhi granted to Gilgeam , whose mission was to infiltrate and debilitate the Shyran defenses , < ref name = " TDYK / Hardcover - p32 , 310 " > < / ref > was accidentally sent to Toril through the portal .

title: First flensing
description: First flensing The First Flensing was a powerful ritual that , if completed , would allow the evil god Asmodeus to enter Waterdeep . Wizards and clerics at the House of Wonder in Waterdeep first attempted the ritual around 1180 DR in exchange for immortality . However , they reneged on the deal and were cursed into lich form and became the Circle of Skulls .
description_long: First flensing The First Flensing was a powerful ritual that , if completed , would allow the evil god Asmodeus to enter Waterdeep . Wizards and clerics at the House of Wonder in Waterdeep first attempted the ritual around 1180 DR in exchange for immortality . However , they reneged on the deal and were cursed into lich form and became the Circle of Skulls . In 1480 DR , several parties , including the Circle of Skulls , attempted to complete the ritual but the deva Jinnaoth Ir ' Gadohn halted the attempt . Effects . The exact effect of the ritual was unknown . However , it appeared that the ritual would allow the god Asmodeus to enter Waterdeep and create Hell on earth . Because other deities were unlikely to allow Asmodeus free entry to the Prime Material Plane , completion of the ritual would probably lead to a war between the gods .

title: First inter - dale war
description: First inter - dale war The first inter - dale war occurred in 1232 DR between Archendale and Sessrendale , and lasted three weeks . It ended in victory for Archendale , and the annihilation of Sessrendale . The forces of Archendale led an invasion of Sessrendale after the " mysterious " Dusk Lord , ruler of Sessrendale , was judged to be using necromancy and that " evil raiders " were being harbored there .
description_long: First inter - dale war The first inter - dale war occurred in 1232 DR between Archendale and Sessrendale , and lasted three weeks . It ended in victory for Archendale , and the annihilation of Sessrendale . The forces of Archendale led an invasion of Sessrendale after the " mysterious " Dusk Lord , ruler of Sessrendale , was judged to be using necromancy and that " evil raiders " were being harbored there . Although " powerful magic " was used by Sessrendale in the conflict , it led to the slaying of the Dusk Lord , and the Swords of Archendale ordered an annihilation of Sessrendale by burning its buildings and salting its earth .

title: Firstpeak
description: Firstpeak Firstpeak was a mountain in the Spine of the World mountain range . History . It was formerly known as Ironstar Mountain since it was once home to the Ironstar clan of shield dwarves .
description_long: Firstpeak Firstpeak was a mountain in the Spine of the World mountain range . History . It was formerly known as Ironstar Mountain since it was once home to the Ironstar clan of shield dwarves . By 1370 DR , it was abandoned by the dwarves and the silver dragon Dargentum took up residence . Geography . The svirfneblin city of Blingdenstone was located deep beneath the mountain .

title: Fish - spice paste
description: Fish - spice paste Fish - spice paste was a condiment applied to in Faerûn . It was made of fish with spice and also had a salty flavor , and came in several varieties . Elgath ' s Provisions in Archenbridge in Archendale , in the Dalelands , sold fish - spice pastes to add flavor to their traveling rations , in addition to their hot sauces .
description_long: Fish - spice paste Fish - spice paste was a condiment applied to in Faerûn . It was made of fish with spice and also had a salty flavor , and came in several varieties . Elgath ' s Provisions in Archenbridge in Archendale , in the Dalelands , sold fish - spice pastes to add flavor to their traveling rations , in addition to their hot sauces .

title: Fist
description: Fist The Fist was the best assassin member of the Assassins Guild of the Galenas in 1357 DR . History . In 1357 DR , the Grandfather of Assassins sent the Fist and a squad of assassins to kill Gareth Dragonsbane and his party .
description_long: Fist The Fist was the best assassin member of the Assassins Guild of the Galenas in 1357 DR . History . In 1357 DR , the Grandfather of Assassins sent the Fist and a squad of assassins to kill Gareth Dragonsbane and his party . The Fist died in the mission .

title: Fist of the adder
description: Fist of the adder Fist of the adder was a potent offensive spell used in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was favored by the Red Eyes sorcerous society . Effects .
description_long: Fist of the adder Fist of the adder was a potent offensive spell used in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was favored by the Red Eyes sorcerous society . Effects . This spell caused the caster ' s arm to change into a long tentacle tipped with the head of an adder . The attack range of the arm was quite long depending on the power of the caster . The adder struck with deadly accuracy and could even harm creatures that were only harmed by magical weapons . Casters with more power were able to strike with more force , causing devastating physical damage . For more powerful wizards , attacks by the adder were also complimented with venom . Components . This spell required the skin of a venomous snake to cast .

title: Fistandantilus ' s firequench
description: Fistandantilus ' s firequench Fistandantilus ' s firequench , also shortened to just firequench , was an abjuration and alteration spell that extinguished fires and prevented flammable materials from igniting . Effects . This spell protected a spherical volume with a radius of 40 ft ( 12 m ) for a duration of four minutes .
description_long: Fistandantilus ' s firequench Fistandantilus ' s firequench , also shortened to just firequench , was an abjuration and alteration spell that extinguished fires and prevented flammable materials from igniting . Effects . This spell protected a spherical volume with a radius of 40 ft ( 12 m ) for a duration of four minutes . The center of the effect could be set at a distance of 210 ft ( 64 m ) . More experienced casters could increase this range . During this time , all normal fires were extinguished and magical fires had one chance to resist the spell or be snuffed out . New fires could not be started inside the designated sphere for the duration of the spell . All creatures got one chance to resist the spell . Creatures with a fire - creating power had to overcome the magic of this spell each time they attempted to use their powers . Magically created fires ( which included fire elemental s and " fireball s " ) were prevented or extinguished by random chance , with the odds decreasing as the level of the fire - causing effect increased . Note that fires started by " fireball " and similar agents were considered normal fires after the magical effect dissipated .

title: Five Great Terraces
description: Five Great Terraces The Five Great Terraces was a large enclosure found in Manass in Khazari . Description . A graveled square surrounded the Five Great Terraces , which were stacked upon one another .
description_long: Five Great Terraces The Five Great Terraces was a large enclosure found in Manass in Khazari . Description . A graveled square surrounded the Five Great Terraces , which were stacked upon one another . Barracks for troops were positioned along three of the sides . Uses . The governor of Manass used this area to review his troops as well as entertain elite guests and dignitaries . It was a crime to visit the Five Great Terraces unless specifically invited by the governor .

title: Fives Council
description: Fives Council The Fives Council served as the ruling body of government of Yhaunn in 1358 DR . This organization derived its name because each table of a council session seated five people . Activities .
description_long: Fives Council The Fives Council served as the ruling body of government of Yhaunn in 1358 DR . This organization derived its name because each table of a council session seated five people . Activities . Aside from dealing with current events topics , the Fives Council was responsible for electing the Nessarch , or mayor . Organization . Composed of wealthy property owners and merchants , the Fives Council was open to those who arrived early to claim the 75 seats . Seated individuals were permitted to vote on current topics .

title: Fizmorayen Fitzmoran
description: Fizmorayen Fitzmoran Fizmorayen Fitzmoran was an exiled high artificer and a cleric of Gond who lived in the fortress known as Throne Rock . Relationships . Living with Fizmorayen within his sanctuary was a few dwarves , tinkerers , and an alchemist .
description_long: Fizmorayen Fitzmoran Fizmorayen Fitzmoran was an exiled high artificer and a cleric of Gond who lived in the fortress known as Throne Rock . Relationships . Living with Fizmorayen within his sanctuary was a few dwarves , tinkerers , and an alchemist . History . Around 1370 DR , Fizmorayen was known to purchase adamantite ore and resell it to merchants from Waterdeep .

title: Flaergon
description: Flaergon Flaergon was a follower of Ilmater who lived in Glister in Thar , in the mid – 13th century DR . History . Flaergon devoted his efforts to assisting and ensuring the safety of miners and caravan - workers in the frozen north of the Moonsea .
description_long: Flaergon Flaergon was a follower of Ilmater who lived in Glister in Thar , in the mid – 13th century DR . History . Flaergon devoted his efforts to assisting and ensuring the safety of miners and caravan - workers in the frozen north of the Moonsea . " Circa " 1267 DR , Althea the Abased , the leader of the House of the Broken God temple in Keltar , selected Blaermon the Blessed to take away the " Tome of Torment " , the holiest book of the faith , to the " wild places " of the Realms and bestow it upon the first " needy and worthy " Ilmatari he met , someone who worked or fought for the benefit of the common people and their faith , not merely for wealth and adventure . Blaermon obeyed and , in the Year of the Daystars , 1268 DR , he gave the " Tome " to Flaergon of Glister . Aided by the " Tome " over the next three decades , Flaergon worked hard to improve the lives of travellers in the Moonsea . He finally died of a fall in a rocky chasm near Whitehorn , in the Year of the Claw , 1299 DR . Daern of Hawksroost , one of Flaergon ' s most devoted companions , took the " Tome of Torment " back to Althea at the House of the Broken God . Activities .

title: Flagon Held High
description: Flagon Held High The Flagon Held High was the only tavern in Tilverton . History . In 1372 DR , the town of Tilverton was completely destroyed during an attack by Thultanthar forces .
description_long: Flagon Held High The Flagon Held High was the only tavern in Tilverton . History . In 1372 DR , the town of Tilverton was completely destroyed during an attack by Thultanthar forces . Presumably , the Flagon Held High was destroyed too . Geography . It was located in the Old Town section of the city on the hilltop at the dead end street , Phorn ' s Lane . Atmosphere . The tavern was something of an ongoing festival , where people of all types came to meet , drink , and eat . The crowd spilled out into Phorn ' s Lane every night and the law was known to look the other way here . Structure . The tavern had smooth stone walls .

title: Flail
description: Flail A flail is a one - handed , martial melee weapon . Description . A flail consists of a haft about two feet ( 60cm ) long with a heavy metal ball or rod attached by chain to the end of the haft .
description_long: Flail A flail is a one - handed , martial melee weapon . Description . A flail consists of a haft about two feet ( 60cm ) long with a heavy metal ball or rod attached by chain to the end of the haft . The ball or rod is often spiked . An average flail costs 8gp and weighs 5lbs ( 2 . 3kg ) . In 1st and 2nd edition D & D , this weapon is called the horseman ' s flail . Weaponology . Military flails evolved from tools used to thresh grain . These lighter flails are typically used as one - handed weapons from horseback but there is a heavy flail and a dire flail for infantry that require two hands . Flails can be used to trip an opponent and the flexible chain increases the chance of entangling an enemy weapon and disarming them . Realmslore . Flails are often used by priests although several warriors of note , including the genasi Cephas preferred the flail to other weapons .

title: Flail of Ages
description: Flail of Ages The Flail of Ages was a powerful multi - headed flail , each of whose heads did different kinds of damage . It also grew in power according to the number of heads currently on it . History .
description_long: Flail of Ages The Flail of Ages was a powerful multi - headed flail , each of whose heads did different kinds of damage . It also grew in power according to the number of heads currently on it . History . It was originally created by a group of rakshasa for use in different sorts of battles . Around 1368 DR , it was in the possession of Lord de ' Arnise ( the father of Nalia de ' Arnise ) . He was in possession of the handle and the fire , ice , and acid heads , which he kept hidden separately in his castle . If Gorion ' s Ward embarked on the quest to free de ' Arnise Keep from troll s , they would have the chance to assemble the flail at a magical forge also hidden in the castle ; its acid and fire heads made it useful against trolls . The handle could then be combined with any number of heads in any combination . Each head added its own kind of damage and to the magical strength of the weapon , and once all were attached , the flail also gained a chance to slow opponents . Later , a further two heads for the flail could be found , and attached by Cespenar , doing electrical and poison damage and further increasing the weapon ' s potency .

title: Flail snail
description: Flail snail Flail snails were earth - based creatures that produced a number of valuable resources . The residue they left behind as they moved could be harvested to produce glass , and their colorful shells could be used to produce protective magical items , such as spellguard shield s and robes of scintillating colors .
description_long: Flail snail Flail snails were earth - based creatures that produced a number of valuable resources . The residue they left behind as they moved could be harvested to produce glass , and their colorful shells could be used to produce protective magical items , such as spellguard shield s and robes of scintillating colors .

title: Flamberge
description: Flamberge A flamberge sword was a two - handed weapon with an undulating blade . The name literally meant " flame blade " . Used during medieval times , this two - handed sword could be used in such ways that it would send vibrations down an opponent ' s weapon , much to their discomfort .
description_long: Flamberge A flamberge sword was a two - handed weapon with an undulating blade . The name literally meant " flame blade " . Used during medieval times , this two - handed sword could be used in such ways that it would send vibrations down an opponent ' s weapon , much to their discomfort . Wounds inflicted with this blade also created much wider lacerations .

title: Flame ( province )
description: Flame ( province ) The province of flame in the Zakhara n view of magic was a group of spells related to the element of fire . Use . The four elemental provinces played a very similar role for Zakharan magic - users as the eight ( or nine ) schools of magic did for Faerûn ian ones .
description_long: Flame ( province ) The province of flame in the Zakhara n view of magic was a group of spells related to the element of fire . Use . The four elemental provinces played a very similar role for Zakharan magic - users as the eight ( or nine ) schools of magic did for Faerûn ian ones . Elemental mage s in Zakhara specialized exclusively in one province , like flame , while sorcerers took spells from two provinces , shunning the other two . Unlike elementalist s , magic - users from the Land of Fate recognized no opposition between flame and sea . Cultural significance . The flame was associated with wrath and other burning emotions in Zakharan culture , and most flame mages showed a disposition towards evil . The Brotherhood of the True Flame was the ultimate example of this proclivity toward evil . Paths of power . Zakharan practicioners of path magic recognized four paths of power within the province of flame :

title: Flame blade
description: Flame blade Flame blade was an evocation spell that created a sword - like beam of fire that extended from the caster ' s hand and performed similar to a scimitar . Effects . The blade inflicted fire damage , could ignite items , and gave off light .
description_long: Flame blade Flame blade was an evocation spell that created a sword - like beam of fire that extended from the caster ' s hand and performed similar to a scimitar . Effects . The blade inflicted fire damage , could ignite items , and gave off light . Strangely enough , this flaming blade was not a magical weapon but unsurprisingly , it wouldn ' t work underwater . Components . All versions required verbal and somatic components , but the oldest version and the post - Second Sundering version required the caster to have a leaf of .

title: Flame cyclone
description: Flame cyclone Flame cyclone is an evocation spell used by inexperienced swordmage s , particularly those of the assault style . When " flame cyclone " is cast a tempest of magical flame shoots from the swordmage ' s blade , towards a nearby location , exploding into a flaming storm of fifteen feet in diameter . Creatures caught within are scorched by this blast , which dissipates within a few seconds and which is powered primarily by the strength and intelligence of the swordmage casting it .
description_long: Flame cyclone Flame cyclone is an evocation spell used by inexperienced swordmage s , particularly those of the assault style . When " flame cyclone " is cast a tempest of magical flame shoots from the swordmage ' s blade , towards a nearby location , exploding into a flaming storm of fifteen feet in diameter . Creatures caught within are scorched by this blast , which dissipates within a few seconds and which is powered primarily by the strength and intelligence of the swordmage casting it . " Flame cyclone " wears somewhat heavily on its caster ' s power , meaning that before a swordmage can cast the spell again he or she must rest at least a few minutes .

title: Flame knife
description: Flame knife Flame knives were special weapons used by holy slayer assassin s in Zakhara . Description . These knives had a wavy blade .
description_long: Flame knife Flame knives were special weapons used by holy slayer assassin s in Zakhara . Description . These knives had a wavy blade . Uses . Members of the Flamedeath Fellowship used these wicked blades smeared with pitch or even oil of liquid stars . The oil was set aflame and wielded in combat . Members of the Flamedeath Fellowship preferred using this tactic at night to intimidate their opponents . The dagger was often left behind as a warning sign to keep others from straying from the path the fellowship endorsed . Price . Flame knives cost 2 gold piece s .

title: Flame of justice
description: Flame of justice Flame of justice was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell was a more powerful version of the " fire truth " spell and was cast in the same manner using a special lit candle .
description_long: Flame of justice Flame of justice was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell was a more powerful version of the " fire truth " spell and was cast in the same manner using a special lit candle . When the target of this spell spoke falsely , part of their body would burst into flame . For this spell , the idea of truth is based on the caster ' s ideal , not the target ' s . If something is incorrect yet the caster believed it to be the truth , then the target would suffer accordingly if they " lied . " This spell expired after ten questions were asked . Components . This spell required a candle made from a rare form of desert bees wax to cast .

title: Flame shield
description: Flame shield Flame shield was a divine magic spell available to druid s of Eldath , the Goddess of Singing Waters . It created an intangible barrier attached to the caster ' s hand that extinguished normal and magical fires . The " shield " could be passed to others .
description_long: Flame shield Flame shield was a divine magic spell available to druid s of Eldath , the Goddess of Singing Waters . It created an intangible barrier attached to the caster ' s hand that extinguished normal and magical fires . The " shield " could be passed to others . Effects . When cast , this spell caused a shield that pulsated with darkness to come into existence at the tips of the caster ' s fingers on one hand . The " flame shield " was 6 ft ( 1 . 8 m ) tall , similar to a tower shield , and lasted for five minutes ( longer for more experienced casters ) . The " shield " was intangible , weightless , and transparent enough to see through . The " flame shield " extinguished small normal fires ( candles , torches , flaming oil , flaming arrows , campfires ) when touched . Larger fires were reduced in size wherever the " shield " came in contact , but if not completely extinguished , could resurge . The " flame shield " snuffed out a " flame blade " on contact and absorbed half the damage of a " fireball " that engulfed the " shield " . At least some versions of " flame strike " could be completely canceled if the " shield " was held overhead to intercept the pillar of fire .

title: Flame spiral
description: Flame spiral Flame spiral , also known as fireburst , is an evocation spell used by many sorcerer s early on in their careers . When a sorcerer casts " flame spiral " , they create a vortex of flame that spins around them , shooting outwards into a burst of ten feet in diameter . Any three creatures caught within are scorched , the degree depending largely on how quick their reflexes are , as well as the sorcerer ' s charisma .
description_long: Flame spiral Flame spiral , also known as fireburst , is an evocation spell used by many sorcerer s early on in their careers . When a sorcerer casts " flame spiral " , they create a vortex of flame that spins around them , shooting outwards into a burst of ten feet in diameter . Any three creatures caught within are scorched , the degree depending largely on how quick their reflexes are , as well as the sorcerer ' s charisma . " Flame spiral " , while powerful , is not particularly difficult to cast and the sorcerer requires a rest of only a few minutes or so before they can cast it again . Before the Spellplague , " flame spiral " was more commonly known as " fireburst " and was slightly less powerful . At this time , the range of " flame spiral " was five feet , rather than ten feet , and it was used by both wizard s and sorcerers . At this time " flame spiral " , like nearly all spells , required either preparation from a wizard or a substantial portion of a sorcerer ' s spellcasting energy to be cast , limiting its uses substantially . " Flame spiral " also grew in potency as its caster did , like most spells of the time .

title: Flame strike
description: Flame strike Flame strike was an evocation spell that blasted a target with divine fire . Effects . A vertical column of fire was called down by the caster on the exact spot indicated when the spell was cast .
description_long: Flame strike Flame strike was an evocation spell that blasted a target with divine fire . Effects . A vertical column of fire was called down by the caster on the exact spot indicated when the spell was cast . Those caught in the target area were engulfed in flames but could partially resist the spell if they were lucky or escape part of the damage if they were dexterous . There were at least two distinct versions of this spell through the ages . The older version filled a cylinder 10 ft ( 3 m ) wide by 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) tall with fire and did an average amount of damage regardless of the level of the caster . The newer version blasted an area 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) wide by 40 ft ( 12 . 2 m ) tall and the average damage increased with the experience of the caster . The divine fire was made up of half fire and half divine power , so protections like " fire shield ( chill shield ) " and " protection from energy ( fire ) " only applied to the fire half . Components . The newer version required verbal and somatic components as well as a holy symbol or divine focus for casting . The older version and the post - Second Sundering version also required a pinch of sulfur .

title: Flamebeard ' s Firebrandy
description: Flamebeard ' s Firebrandy Flamebeard ' s Firebrandy was a fiery liquor and the signature drink from Kelvin ' s Comfort in Bryn Shander . Description . A few warm shots of Firebeard ' s Firebrandy were advertised by Augrek Brighthelm to help in keeping the cold at bay .
description_long: Flamebeard ' s Firebrandy Flamebeard ' s Firebrandy was a fiery liquor and the signature drink from Kelvin ' s Comfort in Bryn Shander . Description . A few warm shots of Firebeard ' s Firebrandy were advertised by Augrek Brighthelm to help in keeping the cold at bay . The liquor was in fact a cheap rotgut from Mirabar that Ogden Flamebeard , proprietor of the tavern , purchased in bulk and then relabeled and resold at a considerably higher price . History . Sometime after the War of the Silver Marches , the dwarven criminal Worvil Forkbeard was known to be addicted to Flamebeard ' s Firebrandy . Sir Baric Nylef hoped to use Worvil ' s cravings for it as an opportunity to catch him .

title: Flamedance
description: Flamedance Flamedance was the name in the Realms for . Description . This precious stone was translucent and ranged in color from pale yellow to green .
description_long: Flamedance Flamedance was the name in the Realms for . Description . This precious stone was translucent and ranged in color from pale yellow to green . It was usually found in fragments and small crystals . Because it did not cleave well , it was mainly used for carving . Only crystals that could yield faceted gems were cut . A typical specimen had a base value of 500 gp . Powers . These stones and any item on which they were mounted always resisted attacks from normal or magical fire . A creature wearing one or more of these gems gained a significant improvement in the chance to resist normal or magical fire - based attacks .

title: Flamedeath Fellowship
description: Flamedeath Fellowship The Flamedeath Fellowship was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara dedicated to the teachings of Najm , the Zakharan god of adventure , or Kossuth , the Lord of Flames . Activities . This group of holy slayers was closely involved with the Brotherhood of the True Flame .
description_long: Flamedeath Fellowship The Flamedeath Fellowship was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara dedicated to the teachings of Najm , the Zakharan god of adventure , or Kossuth , the Lord of Flames . Activities . This group of holy slayers was closely involved with the Brotherhood of the True Flame . Newer members followed the teaching of Najm , but the senior members tended to follow Kossuth . Holy slayers of the Flamedeath Fellowship were supplied with Greek fire or " oil of liquid stars . " They used this deadly substance to burn their enemies and their homes to ash . A small group of holy slayers from the Fellowship protected a secret temple to Kossuth located within the Court District of Huzuz . A particularly nefarious sect of the Fellowship existed in Umara within the Free Cities of Zakhara .

title: Flameling
description: Flameling Flamelings were small elemental vermin native to the Elemental Plane of Fire that could also be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These creatures resembled small alligators .
description_long: Flameling Flamelings were small elemental vermin native to the Elemental Plane of Fire that could also be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These creatures resembled small alligators . Their forward - facing eyes were bulbous and a crown of tentacles surrounded their head . The tentacles served as sensory organs . A flameling ' s body was covered with red scales . Their club - shaped tail was used for defense . Ecology . Though they were weak fire elemental s , flamelings could still manipulate fire and were inherently immune to that element . When threatened , flamelings could toss miniature " fireball s " at their assailants . They consumed any flammable material as a food source .

title: Flameproof
description: Flameproof Flameproof was an abjuration spell that granted a subject immunity to fire . Effects . When cast , this spell fully protected the recipient from normal fires and offered limited protection from magical ones .
description_long: Flameproof Flameproof was an abjuration spell that granted a subject immunity to fire . Effects . When cast , this spell fully protected the recipient from normal fires and offered limited protection from magical ones . The recipient became completely immune to normal fire , lava , etc . Breath weapons , or other fire - related attacks , from creatures and fire - based spells did not cause as much harm to the recipient . This spell could not be combined with any other spell or magical item that granted resistance to fire . When cast upon an inanimate object , the spell made the object completely immune to all forms of fire both normal and magical . Components . This spell required a bit of candle wax to cast . History . The spell was once unique to the mages of Zakhara , the Land of Fate . However , it was eventually propagated to Faerûn by the Halruaan mage Daltim Flamefist some time in the mid – 14th century DR . He included it in his spellbook " Daltim ' s Tome of Fire " , which he lost in Tethyr in the 1360s DR . It remained a unique spell at the time .

title: Flameran Verminbane
description: Flameran Verminbane Flameran Verminbane was a halfling during the Elemental Evil crisis . Activitivies . Flameran worked in the great Dellmon farm in the Dessarin Valley .
description_long: Flameran Verminbane Flameran Verminbane was a halfling during the Elemental Evil crisis . Activitivies . Flameran worked in the great Dellmon farm in the Dessarin Valley . He was also an agent of the Emerald Enclave . History . In 1491 DR , the Iceshield orc s attacked many farms around the Dellmon property . However , Kerbin Dellmon refused to abandon his farm and flee to Yartar , instead deciding to fight with the aid of his family and workers , including Flameran . Flameran helped Dreena Dellmon to ask the help of the elves of the High Forest . With the lucky arrival of some adventurers , the Dellmons managed to defend the farm .

title: Flames of Phlegethos
description: Flames of Phlegethos Flames of Phlegethos , sometimes known as brimstone blast , is a moderately powerful warlock invocation learned by young or inexperienced warlock s , particularly those who forge pacts with the powers of the Nine Hells . When " flames of Phlegethos " is cast , the warlock casting it summons from the plane of Phlegethos burning streams of liquid fire , which he bathes a target of his or her choice within fifty feet , causing them immense pain and burning at their flesh . Even if the creature survives the initial onslaught , the flames continue to burn , causing continuous pain to the warlock ' s victim .
description_long: Flames of Phlegethos Flames of Phlegethos , sometimes known as brimstone blast , is a moderately powerful warlock invocation learned by young or inexperienced warlock s , particularly those who forge pacts with the powers of the Nine Hells . When " flames of Phlegethos " is cast , the warlock casting it summons from the plane of Phlegethos burning streams of liquid fire , which he bathes a target of his or her choice within fifty feet , causing them immense pain and burning at their flesh . Even if the creature survives the initial onslaught , the flames continue to burn , causing continuous pain to the warlock ' s victim . The power of " flames of Phlegethos " is largely dependent on the constitution of the warlock casting it and the spell is so powerful that it can only be cast once per day . Prior to the Spellplague , " flames of Phlegethos " was known primarily as " brimstone blast " and was castable at - will , like all warlock invocations . " Flames of Phlegethos " was also slightly more powerful , but at the cost of being too much for inexperienced warlocks to master .

title: Flamesight Mosque
