description: Foresters ' Hall Foresters ' Hall was a long , low meeting hall used by the Foresters : an elite part of the Aglarond an army . The hall was decorated in the style of the Yuir elves , with runes and artifacts . It is used for long celebrations , feasting and drinking .
description_long: Foresters ' Hall Foresters ' Hall was a long , low meeting hall used by the Foresters : an elite part of the Aglarond an army . The hall was decorated in the style of the Yuir elves , with runes and artifacts . It is used for long celebrations , feasting and drinking .

title: Forgefires
description: Forgefires Forgefires was a small dwarven stronghold located in Fimbrul , Returned Abeir . Background . The dwarves of Forgefires were xenophobic and only allowed other dwarves to enter in their domain .
description_long: Forgefires Forgefires was a small dwarven stronghold located in Fimbrul , Returned Abeir . Background . The dwarves of Forgefires were xenophobic and only allowed other dwarves to enter in their domain . Even so , unfamiliar dwarves were treated with suspicion as well . Architecture . Forgefires was built in tunnels too small for giant s or dragon s to enter them . The stronghold had hundreds of hidden tunnels and doors , and the deeper cellars were located in volcanic rifts where the dwarves forged all manner of stuff .

title: Forgotten Forest
description: Forgotten Forest The Forgotten Forest lies in a vale between Evereska ' s Shaeradim to the east , and the Graypeak Mountains forty miles to the west . The Marsh of Chelimber is south of the forest , and to the north are the Lonely Vale and the Graycloak Hills .
description_long: Forgotten Forest The Forgotten Forest lies in a vale between Evereska ' s Shaeradim to the east , and the Graypeak Mountains forty miles to the west . The Marsh of Chelimber is south of the forest , and to the north are the Lonely Vale and the Graycloak Hills .

title: Forgotten God
description: Forgotten God The Forgotten God was a mysterious deity worshiped at a temple in the Spine of the World mountains . Worshipers . Nothing was known about the Forgotten God except that his priests , referred to as acolytes , gained priestly powers from someone .
description_long: Forgotten God The Forgotten God was a mysterious deity worshiped at a temple in the Spine of the World mountains . Worshipers . Nothing was known about the Forgotten God except that his priests , referred to as acolytes , gained priestly powers from someone . Giant statues of a robed hooded figure stood outside the temple and another sat in meditation inside the entrance to the temple . This figure could be the Forgotten God , or someone else .

title: Forgotten Realms
description: Forgotten Realms The Forgotten Realms is a fictional alternate world that has been published as a campaign setting for " Advanced Dungeon & Dragons " ( " AD & D " ) , " Dungeons & Dragons " ( D & D ) , 3 Edition " Dungeons & Dragons " ( 3e ) , and 4 Edition " Dungeons and Dragons " ( 4e ) , by TSR , Inc . and Wizards of the Coast ( WotC ) . The setting is also referenced in the 5 edition " Dungeons and Dragons " core books , though it has not yet been published as its own separate setting .
description_long: Forgotten Realms The Forgotten Realms is a fictional alternate world that has been published as a campaign setting for " Advanced Dungeon & Dragons " ( " AD & D " ) , " Dungeons & Dragons " ( D & D ) , 3 Edition " Dungeons & Dragons " ( 3e ) , and 4 Edition " Dungeons and Dragons " ( 4e ) , by TSR , Inc . and Wizards of the Coast ( WotC ) . The setting is also referenced in the 5 edition " Dungeons and Dragons " core books , though it has not yet been published as its own separate setting . It was originally created in 1967 as a setting for short stories by Ed Greenwood , but it has since become one of the most enduring campaign settings for " D & D " . The primary focus of the setting is the continent of Faerûn , part of the world of Abeir - Toril , an Earth - like planet with certain obvious influences and similarities from the real world and fantasy fiction . The Forgotten Realms setting owes a lot of its popularity to the many novels using the setting , like R . A . Salvatore ' s works detailing the life and adventures of the famed drow Drizzt Do ' Urden , as well as computer games like Pool of Radiance , Baldur ' s Gate , Icewind Dale and Neverwinter Nights . History .

title: Forgotten Realms : Demon Stone
description: Forgotten Realms : Demon Stone Forgotten Realms : Demon Stone is a game with a story written by R . A . Salvatore about three adventurers who get involved in an inter - planar war .
description_long: Forgotten Realms : Demon Stone Forgotten Realms : Demon Stone is a game with a story written by R . A . Salvatore about three adventurers who get involved in an inter - planar war . Story . Orc armies and the red dragon Caminus are raiding the Gemspark Mine in Damara . Three adventurers , Rannek , Zhai , and Illius take it upon themselves to save the civilians in the area and secure the mines . They join up and eventually defeat the warlord controlling the dominant army . Searching the area , they come across a mysterious stone and accidentally release the prisoners it contains : the Githyanki general Cireka and the slaad Ygorl . They summon their armies and resume an old fight . Zhai takes them to her home , Cedarleaf , a wood elf village , only to find it under attack by Cireka ' s Gith . Ygorl intervenes , trying to steal Cireka ' s Silver Sword . The party escape to Blackstaff Tower to meet with Illius ' mentor , Khelben " Blackstaff " Arunsun , who tells them that they need to go to a yuan - ti temple to Merrshaulk in Chult to find a demon stone that will re - imprison Cireka and Ygorl .

title: Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide
description: Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide Contents . The " Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide " is the first portion , followed by the " Forgotten Realms Player ' s Guide " of the 4th edition release of the " Forgotten Realms " campaign setting for the " Dungeons & Dragons " roleplaying game . Unlike previous releases , like the 3rd edition variant , the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide " , or FRCG , focuses solely on proving information for rules referees and storytellers known as DMs , rather than for players .
description_long: Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide Contents . The " Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide " is the first portion , followed by the " Forgotten Realms Player ' s Guide " of the 4th edition release of the " Forgotten Realms " campaign setting for the " Dungeons & Dragons " roleplaying game . Unlike previous releases , like the 3rd edition variant , the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide " , or FRCG , focuses solely on proving information for rules referees and storytellers known as DMs , rather than for players . This information is meant to help a DM build a campaign , either within the " Realms " , or in a homebrewed setting , rather than for players to use to enhance their characters . Information for building characters is instead provided in the " Forgotten Realms Player ' s Guide " . Partially as a consequence , the FRCG is slightly slimmer than the 3rd edition FRCS in page number , a fact which has given the false assumption that is undetailed . However , if one were to add the two books together , as is intended , the total page number exceeds that of the FRCS by more than a hundred page , though the word count per page is lower given the 4th edition formatting standards .

title: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition
description: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition The Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition was the " original " second edition campaign setting , published in 1993 . This version features an image of a horse on a plain background on the box . This campaign setting was revised and re - released in 1996 .
description_long: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition The Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition was the " original " second edition campaign setting , published in 1993 . This version features an image of a horse on a plain background on the box . This campaign setting was revised and re - released in 1996 .

title: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition ( revised )
description: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition ( revised ) The Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition is the " revised " version of the original boxed second edition campaign setting , which was originally released in 1993 . This boxed set depicts Elminster Aumar on top of a rock on the cover .
description_long: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition ( revised ) The Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition is the " revised " version of the original boxed second edition campaign setting , which was originally released in 1993 . This boxed set depicts Elminster Aumar on top of a rock on the cover .

title: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition
description: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition The Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting was published in 2001 by Wizards of the Coast , Inc . It is a Forgotten Realms campaign sourcebook for use with the 3rd edition of the " Dungeons & Dragons " role - playing game . The book was written by Ed Greenwood , Sean K .
description_long: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition The Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting was published in 2001 by Wizards of the Coast , Inc . It is a Forgotten Realms campaign sourcebook for use with the 3rd edition of the " Dungeons & Dragons " role - playing game . The book was written by Ed Greenwood , Sean K . Reynolds , Skip Williams , and Rob Heinsoo , with the contributions of members of the Wizards company ' s staff . The book is 320 pages in length ; illustrated in color , and hardbound . In 2002 , the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting " won the for Best Role - Playing Game Supplement of 2001 . Contents . This is the third edition release of the " Forgotten Realms " campaign setting for " Dungeons & Dragons " and a number of changes have been made since the previous books were published by the former TSR , Inc . The most important update was to incorporate the significant revisions to the game system with the 3rd edition update . Various regional feats , character attributes , prestige classes , spells , and NPC statistics all use the new rule set .

title: Forgotten Realms Interactive Atlas
description: Forgotten Realms Interactive Atlas The Forgotten Realms Interactive Atlas was developed by ProFantasy Software , the creators of for Wizards of the Coast . The developers created vector versions of the published maps for the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting " and included many new maps , including a globe of Abeir - Toril . There have been three updates published for the application that deliver over 800 maps .
description_long: Forgotten Realms Interactive Atlas The Forgotten Realms Interactive Atlas was developed by ProFantasy Software , the creators of for Wizards of the Coast . The developers created vector versions of the published maps for the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting " and included many new maps , including a globe of Abeir - Toril . There have been three updates published for the application that deliver over 800 maps . The maps were hyperlinked within a customized viewer , or could be accessed via an interactive globe . The product was discontinued after selling through its entire print in its first year , perhaps because of an electronic rights transfer between Wizards of the Coast and . It is still found to be purchased at prices over the original purchase price on . The license to the software has now reverted to the publisher , although the maps and other rights are owned by Wizards of the Coast .

title: Forgotten Realms Player ' s Guide
description: Forgotten Realms Player ' s Guide Contents . This is , along with the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide " , the most recent release of the " Forgotten Realms " campaign setting for " Dungeons & Dragons " . Unlike the " Campaign Guide " , which focuses on lore ( commonly refered as " fluff " ) and background information for so - called " dungeon masters " game referees and storytellers to use , the " Player ' s Guide " , or FRPG , focuses on " crunch , " that is to say , information immediately relevant to the game such as new player races , a new class , new paragon paths , and a number of other materials for players to make use of in their game .
description_long: Forgotten Realms Player ' s Guide Contents . This is , along with the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide " , the most recent release of the " Forgotten Realms " campaign setting for " Dungeons & Dragons " . Unlike the " Campaign Guide " , which focuses on lore ( commonly refered as " fluff " ) and background information for so - called " dungeon masters " game referees and storytellers to use , the " Player ' s Guide " , or FRPG , focuses on " crunch , " that is to say , information immediately relevant to the game such as new player races , a new class , new paragon paths , and a number of other materials for players to make use of in their game . The book does contain a small amount of lore , though only what each player is expected to know , such as details on the nation from which their character hails as well as basic details on each of the races , etc . The book is organized into seven chapters , as follow :

title: Foril Obarskyr I
description: Foril Obarskyr I King Foril Obarskyr was a member of the Obarskyr s , the ruling family of Cormyr . He was born in the Year of True Omens , 1409 DR to King Azoun V and Nalara Marliir and named after his great - grandfather ' s only son who perished at the hands of a Fire Knives assassin at the age of two . He married Jemra Rhindaun , niece to Queen Sybille of Tethyr , in the Year of the Stalking Horses , 1430 DR and she gave birth to Irvel Obarskyr in the Year of the Lashing Tail , 1431 DR .
description_long: Foril Obarskyr I King Foril Obarskyr was a member of the Obarskyr s , the ruling family of Cormyr . He was born in the Year of True Omens , 1409 DR to King Azoun V and Nalara Marliir and named after his great - grandfather ' s only son who perished at the hands of a Fire Knives assassin at the age of two . He married Jemra Rhindaun , niece to Queen Sybille of Tethyr , in the Year of the Stalking Horses , 1430 DR and she gave birth to Irvel Obarskyr in the Year of the Lashing Tail , 1431 DR . He was coronated in the Year of the Godly Invitation , 1449 DR after the death of his father .

title: Forjia Chase
description: Forjia Chase Forjia Chase was a rogue and operative of the Zhentarim in 1375 working within the city of Melvaunt . Background . In 1361 DR , at the young age of seven , Forija fled Zhentil Keep as it was assaulted by the armies of Cyric .
description_long: Forjia Chase Forjia Chase was a rogue and operative of the Zhentarim in 1375 working within the city of Melvaunt . Background . In 1361 DR , at the young age of seven , Forija fled Zhentil Keep as it was assaulted by the armies of Cyric . Orphaned from the conflict , she was to be sold into bondage at a slave camp near Phlan by Zhent slavers . Forija escaped however , able to carve out a life on the street through thievery . Later , after working for her former captors for a time as a messenger and a runner , Forjia was able to set out on her own . Appearance . Forjia had short , curly dark hair that was unevenly cut , and her face seemed to always have a layer of dirt covering it .

title: Fork
description: Fork The Fork was located where the trail east from Sundabar split to go north along the Adbar Road toward Citadel Adbar , and east along the Fork Road toward Ascore . Geography . The lonely and wild spot seemed like the end of Faerûn , splitting toward the dwarfholds of the Ice Mountains , and the nameless track heading east to the ruins of Ascore .
description_long: Fork The Fork was located where the trail east from Sundabar split to go north along the Adbar Road toward Citadel Adbar , and east along the Fork Road toward Ascore . Geography . The lonely and wild spot seemed like the end of Faerûn , splitting toward the dwarfholds of the Ice Mountains , and the nameless track heading east to the ruins of Ascore . Few traveled the way , but the gnome s of Graevelwood sometimes used the road .

title: Fork Road
description: Fork Road Fork Road was an east - to - west road joining Sundabar at the western end to Ascore at the eastern end . Starting at Sundabar , Fork Road passed by Newfort just before the road entered the gap between the Nether Mountains and the Rauvin Mountains . Just before the Fork , where Fork Road met Adbar Road , down a narrow cart track was the village of Deadsnows .
description_long: Fork Road Fork Road was an east - to - west road joining Sundabar at the western end to Ascore at the eastern end . Starting at Sundabar , Fork Road passed by Newfort just before the road entered the gap between the Nether Mountains and the Rauvin Mountains . Just before the Fork , where Fork Road met Adbar Road , down a narrow cart track was the village of Deadsnows . After the Fork , Fork Road continued to end at Ascore .

title: Formian
description: Formian Formians were an ant - like race of outsider s . Description . Formians were brown and resembled a cross between an ant and a centaur .
description_long: Formian Formians were an ant - like race of outsider s . Description . Formians were brown and resembled a cross between an ant and a centaur . . Their size and appearance otherwise depended on the rank they were born into : Society . Formians were dedicated to spreading their colonies wherever they could . Colonies , also called " hive - cities , " consisted of a ruling queen and different hierarchies of workers , from worker ( lowest ) to taskmaskers , from warriors to myrmarchs ( highest below the queen ) . Formians had a hive mind based on the queen ; any formian within 50 miles of a queen could communicate telepathically with any other formian within that range . The most prestigious of myrmarchs was responsible for guarding the queen . Combat . Colonies relied on their warriors ' fighting abilities to defend the hive . Myrmarchs and taskmasters were also proficient fighters and had limited spell - like abilities , such as " dominate monster " or " charm monster " .

title: Forsyl Filarfar
description: Forsyl Filarfar Forsyl Filarfar was an accomplished abjurer living in Yhaunn in 1358 DR . Personality . Forsyl was a gentle , quiet man .
description_long: Forsyl Filarfar Forsyl Filarfar was an accomplished abjurer living in Yhaunn in 1358 DR . Personality . Forsyl was a gentle , quiet man . Activities . Skilled in abjuration magic , it was rumored that Forsyl placed many protective enchantment on his tower so he could pursue his academic studies in peace .

title: Fort Agis
description: Fort Agis Fort Agis , also known as Memnonnar Citadel , was one of the border keeps of Tethyr , collectively known as the Calimmon Garrisons . Location . This fort was located two miles north of Memnon on the edge of the ruins of Memnonnar .
description_long: Fort Agis Fort Agis , also known as Memnonnar Citadel , was one of the border keeps of Tethyr , collectively known as the Calimmon Garrisons . Location . This fort was located two miles north of Memnon on the edge of the ruins of Memnonnar . Structure . Like most of the Calimmon Garrisons , this non - elaborate fortress was built from huge stones . Its walls were ten - to - fifteen - feet thick ( 3 . 0 – 4 . 6 meters ) and 20 feet high ( 6 . 1 meters ) with a deep , empty moat around them . Defenses . Due to its proximity to one of Calimshan ' s major cities and one of its most dangerous ruins , Fort Agis was defended with a greater complement of troops than its sister garrisons . Around 300 Tethyrian soldiers were stationed there . History . As of 1370 DR , the fort was approximately 600 years old . See also . The four primary Calimmon Garrisons were :

title: Fort Arran
description: Fort Arran Fort Arran is an outpost that guards the Golden Road between Sespech and Arrabar , the capital of Chondath . The fort serves as a warning of sorts for the people of Sespech should a war break out with their neighbors . As such , messengers are ready to be dispatched to Mimph , Elbulder and Ormpetarr with warning for the rest of the country .
description_long: Fort Arran Fort Arran is an outpost that guards the Golden Road between Sespech and Arrabar , the capital of Chondath . The fort serves as a warning of sorts for the people of Sespech should a war break out with their neighbors . As such , messengers are ready to be dispatched to Mimph , Elbulder and Ormpetarr with warning for the rest of the country . The thousand men serving at the fort consider it a great honor to do so .

title: Fort Beluarian
description: Fort Beluarian Fort Beluarian was a trade outpost in northern Chult that was run by the Flaming Fist and later belonged to the city - state of Baldur ' s Gate . Geography . Fort Beluarian was located on the northern tip of Chult , northeast of Port Nyanzaru and near the eastern shore of the Bay of Chult .
description_long: Fort Beluarian Fort Beluarian was a trade outpost in northern Chult that was run by the Flaming Fist and later belonged to the city - state of Baldur ' s Gate . Geography . Fort Beluarian was located on the northern tip of Chult , northeast of Port Nyanzaru and near the eastern shore of the Bay of Chult . Trade . The fort was a place of refuge for weary explorers or adventurers as a last resort , at least for a night or two . Defenses . The fort was well supplied and well defended against the monsters of the jungle . History . Originally , the fort belonged to the Flaming Fist Mercenary Company . When that group later became integrated into the government of Baldur ' s Gate , ownership transferred , and the outpost grew to the size of a small town . The fort was destroyed twice by native uprisings and rebuilt . In the late 15th century DR , Amn attempted to purchase the fort from Baldur ' s Gate . Inhabitants . The Flaming Fist would hire out its mercenaries from the fort for the right price , provided the task was not evil . In the late 14th century DR , the outpost was home to a small assortment of ranger s , wizard s , cleric s , and rogue s and numerous fighter s .

title: Fort Ilbratha
description: Fort Ilbratha " Fort Ilbratha " was the name given to an abandoned fort in the eastern foothills of the Troll Mountains , Amn . Location . The fort once controlled the quickest east – west pass through the Troll Mountains .
description_long: Fort Ilbratha " Fort Ilbratha " was the name given to an abandoned fort in the eastern foothills of the Troll Mountains , Amn . Location . The fort once controlled the quickest east – west pass through the Troll Mountains . This was the only one that didn ' t lead into the Snakewood . History . The fort was built to be the northernmost defense of the 4th century realm of Valashar . However , on King Ashar Tornamn ' s push north in the Year of the Woeful Resurrection , 375 DR , the Calishite garrison there was left with a bare skeleton staff . Following Valashar ' s defeat to Cormyrean forces in the Year of the Leaping Hare , 376 DR , Prince Azoun I of Cormyr pushed on through Amn , Valashar , and Tethyr , pillaging many garrisons . With the magical sword " Ilbratha " in hand , Azoun overran the few remaining defenders of this fort and razed it to the ground . The garrison ' s original name was lost ; history recorded it as " Fort Ilbratha " after the famed sword that destroyed it . Description . The log palisade that once ringed the fort was burned to the ground and entirely erased , but the stone foundations survived into the mid – 14th century DR .

title: Fort Locke
description: Fort Locke Fort Locke was a garrison southern end of the Mere of Dead Men along the Sword Coast . Geography . Located between Highcliff and West Harbor , Fort Locke was built as a garrison .
description_long: Fort Locke Fort Locke was a garrison southern end of the Mere of Dead Men along the Sword Coast . Geography . Located between Highcliff and West Harbor , Fort Locke was built as a garrison . It was a point where the patrolls would report for duty . Inhabitants . Most of inhabitants of the Fort are Greycloak soldiers , though the Fort also accepted refugees and those willing to help . History . It is the place where the King of Shadows fought his first and second battle . In the first battle , the warriors pushed his forces to West Harbor . The dead soldiers were buried in a graveyard near the Fort . In the second battle , however , the Fort was destroyed .

title: Fort Morninglord
description: Fort Morninglord Fort Morninglord was an Elturgardian fortress located a day ' s ride from Elturel . In 1476 DR the entire garrison of paladin s disappeared overnight and every stone in the fort was blackened and fused . The High Overseer of Torm feared the fort was contaminated by some evil and ordered all entrances sealed and declared that anyone entering the fort would be outlawed .
description_long: Fort Morninglord Fort Morninglord was an Elturgardian fortress located a day ' s ride from Elturel . In 1476 DR the entire garrison of paladin s disappeared overnight and every stone in the fort was blackened and fused . The High Overseer of Torm feared the fort was contaminated by some evil and ordered all entrances sealed and declared that anyone entering the fort would be outlawed .

title: Forthar Helvenstron
description: Forthar Helvenstron Forthar Helvenstron was a Zhentilar commander involved in the Zhent invasion of Shadowdale in 1375 DR . History . Forthar was a Zhentilar commander who was part of the Zhentarim Occupation Army in Shadowdale in 1375 DR .
description_long: Forthar Helvenstron Forthar Helvenstron was a Zhentilar commander involved in the Zhent invasion of Shadowdale in 1375 DR . History . Forthar was a Zhentilar commander who was part of the Zhentarim Occupation Army in Shadowdale in 1375 DR . When the fighting in the dale increased , he gathered as many villagers as possible . In order to terrify the population , his plan was to slaughter them all in the debased Shrine of Mystra . However , his troops were attacked at the bridge on the River Ashaba by some adventurers and he was killed .

title: Fortify
description: Fortify Fortify was a cooperative magic spell allowing one priest to enhance the healing powers of another . Effects . The priest casting " fortify " had to touch another priest casting " cure light wounds " , " cure serious wounds " , or " cure critical wounds " on a subject , and both spells had to be cast simultaneously .
description_long: Fortify Fortify was a cooperative magic spell allowing one priest to enhance the healing powers of another . Effects . The priest casting " fortify " had to touch another priest casting " cure light wounds " , " cure serious wounds " , or " cure critical wounds " on a subject , and both spells had to be cast simultaneously . At the completion of both spells , the maximum possible healing effect was granted to the subject for the cure spell being cast . It is unknown if " fortify " worked with other " cure " spells , including the " mass cure " variety . Components . Verbal and somatic components , and the priest ' s holy symbol , were all that were required to cast this spell .

title: Fortress of Jorhat
description: Fortress of Jorhat The Fortress of Jorhat , or Jorhat Citadel , was a fortification located in the Hordelands . Location . The ruins of this fortress sat halfway up the mountain of Jorhat Shan .
description_long: Fortress of Jorhat The Fortress of Jorhat , or Jorhat Citadel , was a fortification located in the Hordelands . Location . The ruins of this fortress sat halfway up the mountain of Jorhat Shan . Structure . Though a mess of ruins , the Fortress of Jorhat covered several acres of the mountainside . Tightly packed buildings , alleys , and walls were in various state of disrepair . Much of them had collapsed and tumbled down the steep cliff faces . Interior . Many tunnels and passageways were carved into the rock beneath the fortress , most of which were only accessible from the ruins . Rumors and Legends . Locals believed the fortress was initially constructed by rebels engaged in a conflict with Mulhorand , serving as their main base from which they executed raids through the Howling Gap and Teyla Shan . The rebels were eventually cornered by a force of wizard s , priests , and soldiers and were slaughtered to the last man . Inhabitants . Most sane people avoided the ruins of the Fortress of Jorhat . Passing caravans on the Iron Road hurried quickly by the mass of crumbling buildings , choosing to camp far from the ruins which were believed to be haunted .

title: Fortress of the Five Vultures
description: Fortress of the Five Vultures The Fortress of the Five Vultures was a castle in the city of Calaunt in the Vast . Calauntans jokingly called it " the Sevensroost " . Description .
description_long: Fortress of the Five Vultures The Fortress of the Five Vultures was a castle in the city of Calaunt in the Vast . Calauntans jokingly called it " the Sevensroost " . Description . It lay on the eastern end of Calaunt , and was the largest structure in the city . It was a massive baronial - style castle . The fortress was joined by a weathered , flying stone bridge to the Keep of the Scepter . Activities . During the 14th century DR , the fortress served as the headquarters of the Supreme Scepter and the Merchant Duke s , as well as a barracks and jail . History . Prior to Calaunt ' s rise as a city , it was held by a band of robber - barons . They constructed the Fortress of the Five Vultures , and it was named for them . Around the 1330s DR , Bellas ' s Band , an adventuring company , took over Calaunt , and occupied the Fortress as their headquarters . Thereafter , locals called it " the Sevensroost " . Inhabitants . Supreme Scepter Bellas Thanatar dwelled in the Keep of the Scepter . The Merchant Dukes lived in palatial houses close to the fortress .

title: Fortress of the Half - Demon
description: Fortress of the Half - Demon The Fortress of the Half - Demon is a ruined stone fort located north of Rashemen . It was built thousands of years ago by the Nar and has a huge iron gate fashioned into the face of a leering demon . One of the gates is ajar which is the source of the name " Half - Demon " The fortress is square in shape and has a huge stone keep in the center of the courtyard .
description_long: Fortress of the Half - Demon The Fortress of the Half - Demon is a ruined stone fort located north of Rashemen . It was built thousands of years ago by the Nar and has a huge iron gate fashioned into the face of a leering demon . One of the gates is ajar which is the source of the name " Half - Demon " The fortress is square in shape and has a huge stone keep in the center of the courtyard . Underneath the fortress are a huge number of catacombs and passages , at least some of which lead to pocket planes which were used as extra burial space long ago . In 1479 DR a group of undead Durthan allied with an unknown force , possibly Nar , used the fortress as their base of operations . An army consisting of Rashemi bersekers and fey and led by Aoth Fezim attacked the fortress and drove the Durthan and their undead minions into the tunnels under the fort in the Battle of the Fortress of the Half - Demon .

title: Fortune candle
description: Fortune candle A fortune candle was a special magic item made by mystic s in the Realms . It granted the subject ( s ) a modicum of luck ( similar to a " luckstone " ) when the vagaries of life could not be avoided . Description .
description_long: Fortune candle A fortune candle was a special magic item made by mystic s in the Realms . It granted the subject ( s ) a modicum of luck ( similar to a " luckstone " ) when the vagaries of life could not be avoided . Description . " Fortune candles " were green in color and intended to be burned in ten - minute intervals . The longest - lasting candle that could be manufactured burned for ninety minutes . This was the sixth type of candle mystics learned to make when studying candle magic . Powers . After burning for the desired amount of time and then being extinguished ( either by blowing , snuffing , dousing , or reaching the end of its wick ) , this candle granted a small amount of good luck that lasted one day for every ten minutes the candle was allowed to burn . The recipient ( s ) enjoyed slightly better odds when dodging falling flowerpots , avoiding slippery mud , crafting items , testing their abilities , resisting hostile magic , or performing feats of skill that were not related to combat .

title: Fossil
description: Fossil Fossil was a remnant of an angel in service to the god Cyric . In 1479 DR , he existed in the form of a sentient mask . He recalled the spirit of Madri from the dead and manipulated her into plotting against the deva Demascus .
description_long: Fossil Fossil was a remnant of an angel in service to the god Cyric . In 1479 DR , he existed in the form of a sentient mask . He recalled the spirit of Madri from the dead and manipulated her into plotting against the deva Demascus . Description . Fossil appeared to be a plain mask . As an angel , he was 8 feet ( 2 . 4 meters ) tall and had black wings .

title: Foulwing
description: Foulwing Foulwings were huge , monstrous aberration s . Description . They were very large with black , leathery wings , toad - like bodies , and horse - like heads .
description_long: Foulwing Foulwings were huge , monstrous aberration s . Description . They were very large with black , leathery wings , toad - like bodies , and horse - like heads . Their skin was black and covered in " horn - shaped , wriggling skin growths . " They were clumsy fliers . Their most distinctive feature was their three jaws filled with razor - sharp teeth and centered around a single snout . Their eyes glowed red in infravision . Behavior . Foulwings were generally considered lazy . They were carnivorous , preferring to feed on carrion , though they hunted live prey and sometimes kept creatures captive for food . They often lived alone , but occasionally they could be found in flocks of up to four creatures . Foulwings sometimes mated with wyvern s , creating a foulvern . Foulwings communicated with each other through animal - like grunts and calls . Combat . Foulwings preferred to use their weight to pin prey or enemies under their bodies . They had the ability to breathe out ammonia , causing irritation to the eyes and nose of their targets . They used their sharp teeth to pierce the flesh of a target and suck its blood . Ecology . Habitat .

title: Founder
description: Founder The Founder was a female Red Wizard of Thay . History . She was the lover of the Chosen of Myrkul , Akachi .
description_long: Founder The Founder was a female Red Wizard of Thay . History . She was the lover of the Chosen of Myrkul , Akachi . However , she was Faithless and one day she died as a result of accidental spell backfire and was condemned to the Wall of the Faithless . Akachi was distraught over her fate and went so far as to turn against his faith and god and led a crusade to save her . In the end , Akachi was captured and punished by Myrkul but not before he saved the Founder from the Wall . Thus it was now the Founder who needed a plan to save her lover from the wrath of Myrkul . She founded the Academy of Shapers and Binders in Thaymount , hence her title . The Founder created Nefris , Lienna , and Safiya from fragments of her own soul in order to attract the Kalach - Cha to Rashemen in order to save Akachi . However , she permitted Akachi ' s brother Araman to enter the academy , unaware that he was under a " geas " by Myrkul to destroy her . Araman led a coup in the academy and captured the Founder but , before he could kill her , the Kalach - Cha arrived and saved her .

title: Foundry
description: Foundry The Foundry was located in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire . Description . This area of the City of Brass had many plazas , wide streets , and opulent homes .
description_long: Foundry The Foundry was located in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire . Description . This area of the City of Brass had many plazas , wide streets , and opulent homes . Inhabitants . Some of the wealthiest and most powerful efreet lived within the Foundry .

title: Fountain of Happiness Inn
description: Fountain of Happiness Inn The Fountain of Happiness Inn was the largest inn found in the city of Manass in Khazari . Structure . Located near the Jade Gate , the inn was complete with a full courtyard , stable and additional guest houses located around a Shou - style garden .
description_long: Fountain of Happiness Inn The Fountain of Happiness Inn was the largest inn found in the city of Manass in Khazari . Structure . Located near the Jade Gate , the inn was complete with a full courtyard , stable and additional guest houses located around a Shou - style garden . Activities . The Fountain of Happiness catered to the many caravans passing through the city . The city guards of Manass were given free meals to ensure their prompt attention with dealing with local thieves . Inhabitants . Ba Salnang was the inn ' s owner .

title: Fountain of Stars
description: Fountain of Stars The Fountain of Stars was a white fountain in Leuthilspar on the island of Evermeet . Description . The white fountain depicted birds , flowers , trees and other icons of nature .
description_long: Fountain of Stars The Fountain of Stars was a white fountain in Leuthilspar on the island of Evermeet . Description . The white fountain depicted birds , flowers , trees and other icons of nature . History . The fountain was said to have been given to Zaor Moonflower as a gift by Sehanine Moonbow . Rumors and legends . It was rumored the fountain offered a glimpse of the future to those who looked into it .

title: Fountains of Memory
description: Fountains of Memory The Fountains of Memory were a mysterious source of water that permitted one to see inside pieces of the history selected by the observer . Description . Originally , they were a series of pools located somewhere in the Northdark .
description_long: Fountains of Memory The Fountains of Memory were a mysterious source of water that permitted one to see inside pieces of the history selected by the observer . Description . Originally , they were a series of pools located somewhere in the Northdark . After the Spellplague , the pools were destroyed but the springs that fed the pools remained . They mingled with ordinary springs , so the waters were not as powerful as before . History . Originally the Fountains of Memory were a sacred place for deep gnome s , who jealously kept the secret of their location . Once in 1379 DR , it was permitted to Q ' arlynd Melarn to use them , thanks to his friendship with Flinderspeld . After the Spellplague , the Fountains were altered . The shadovar managed to claim them and relocated them to their secret village for captured Chosen in the Lost Peaks . In 1486 DR , Farideh often used it . It was presumed destroyed in the fall of the village .

title: Four
description: Four The Four were adventurers from Waterdeep . Activities . The organization was banned from working in Cormyr and Amn , but did business in the North and Tethyr .
description_long: Four The Four were adventurers from Waterdeep . Activities . The organization was banned from working in Cormyr and Amn , but did business in the North and Tethyr . History . Around 1357 DR , Khelben Arunsun banished the group from operating in the City of Splendors for assassinating nobles .

title: Fourteenth Skull
description: Fourteenth Skull The Fourteenth Skull was the legendary " extra " skull in Skullport . Personality . Although he was similar in nature to the Skulls of Skullport , he operated independently unlike the Skulls who seemed to behave collectively .
description_long: Fourteenth Skull The Fourteenth Skull was the legendary " extra " skull in Skullport . Personality . Although he was similar in nature to the Skulls of Skullport , he operated independently unlike the Skulls who seemed to behave collectively . The Fourteenth Skull was rarely seen and when a person saw him it was usually discounted as a drunk ' s hallucinations . Activities . His true purpose in Skullport was to strengthen the mythal around Skullport known as the Mantle . He was aided by thirteen mage s that he hand selected , known as the Fray . History . The Fourteenth Skull ' s background was similar to that of the other skulls . At one time he was a drow known as the Rag Mage who moved to the Netherese enclave that became Skullport and was apparently caught in the magical backlash during Karsus ' s Folly .

title: Fourthpeak
description: Fourthpeak Fourthpeak was one of the many mountains which rested along the huge range known as the Spine of the World . Geography . Fourthpeak was one of four mountains whose peaks , when standing in the correct place , aligned perfectly .
description_long: Fourthpeak Fourthpeak was one of the many mountains which rested along the huge range known as the Spine of the World . Geography . Fourthpeak was one of four mountains whose peaks , when standing in the correct place , aligned perfectly . The other three mountains were named Firstpeak , Secondpeak , and Thirdpeak respectively . It was beneath Fourthpeak mountain that Mithral Hall was carved out .

title: Fox ' s cunning
description: Fox ' s cunning Fox ' s cunning was a transmutation spell that increased the chance to perform any skill requiring intelligence . Effects . The caster had to touch the target of this spell in order to cast it .
description_long: Fox ' s cunning Fox ' s cunning was a transmutation spell that increased the chance to perform any skill requiring intelligence . Effects . The caster had to touch the target of this spell in order to cast it . The recipient was granted a few minutes of mental acuity , perception , and quick thinking . Spellcasters that relied on intelligence were not able to gain more spell capacity , but the spells they cast while under the influence of " fox ' s cunning " were harder to resist . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required the use of a holy symbol or divine focus for bards , and a pinch of fox dung or a bit of fox fur for arcane spellcasters .

title: Fox - at - Twilight
description: Fox - at - Twilight The Fox - at - Twilight ( real name : Ilira ) was a swashbuckler and con artist , the moon elf called " Light " by her friends was an enigma at best . Description . Twilight was often described as having an athletic build , slight and lithe ( sensual ) with a kind of allure not entirely like that of an elf .
description_long: Fox - at - Twilight The Fox - at - Twilight ( real name : Ilira ) was a swashbuckler and con artist , the moon elf called " Light " by her friends was an enigma at best . Description . Twilight was often described as having an athletic build , slight and lithe ( sensual ) with a kind of allure not entirely like that of an elf . Some found her beautiful , while others did not , but hers was not a forgettable face or frame . Human men who found themselves drawn to her seemed to do so for what they see as her “ elf ” nature . Elf men were drawn to her for much the same reason they were drawn to humans : her vibrancy did not seem entirely like other elf women ( like Yldar ) . Twilight did not exhibit the patience of elves and was as lusty as a human woman . Twilight had pale skin and raven blue - black hair that she usually wore in a tail to the small of her back . The color of her eyes depended upon the light and her mood , and she was often described as having " pale eyes " . She also has alabaster skin and delicate features .

title: Fox Ridge
description: Fox Ridge Fox Ridge was a rise of ground on the east side of the Ashaba in Shadowdale . Geography . The ridge was north of the temple of Chauntea and south of Storm ' s Farm .
description_long: Fox Ridge Fox Ridge was a rise of ground on the east side of the Ashaba in Shadowdale . Geography . The ridge was north of the temple of Chauntea and south of Storm ' s Farm . The north side of Fox Ridge was a cliff about the height of an average human male . This cliff - side was pockmarked with cavern entrances ranging from burrows to small caverns . Rumors and legends . It was said the caves on the north side of Fox Ridge led to an old tomb dating to before the times when Shadowdale was ruled by the drow . These caverns were used by adventurer s as a hiding place for weapons , gold , food , and former comrades . Further past the tomb was a great cavern known as the Grinding Gulf where flying boulders cascaded in magical vertical dances . History . Fox Ridge was named for the abundance of foxes living here .

title: Foxberry
description: Foxberry Foxberry was a snaky vine that grew in the midwood area of the forest of Cormanthor , often near beech trees . It had yellow , greasy , grape - like berries that smelled like meat . These berries could even be eaten by the meat - eaters in the forest .
description_long: Foxberry Foxberry was a snaky vine that grew in the midwood area of the forest of Cormanthor , often near beech trees . It had yellow , greasy , grape - like berries that smelled like meat . These berries could even be eaten by the meat - eaters in the forest .

title: Foxe
description: Foxe Foxe was a priest of Deneir at the temple of Deneir in the city of Procampur in the Vast in the early 1360s DR . Foxe was the eldest in his family . The lama Koja of Khazari could not pronounce his family name , and so called him " Firstborn Foxe " in honor of this position .
description_long: Foxe Foxe was a priest of Deneir at the temple of Deneir in the city of Procampur in the Vast in the early 1360s DR . Foxe was the eldest in his family . The lama Koja of Khazari could not pronounce his family name , and so called him " Firstborn Foxe " in honor of this position . He was a portly man . Foxe was appointed as secretary and aide to Koja while he was a guest at the temple . He helped him with the writing of " A History of the Tuigan " , negotiated with Forgemaster Inkstain for its printing , and kept his appointments with people such as Duke Jozul Piniago . During their time together , Foxe developed an interest in Koja ' s faith and learning inner harmony , but was not very good at it . He also had trouble understanding Koja ' s desire to have his book mass - published . When Koja decided to travel to Waterdeep , he invited Foxe to accompany him .

title: Foxilon Cardluck
description: Foxilon Cardluck Foxilon Cardluck , better known as Foxy , was a crew - member of the Halruaan caravel " Realms Master " in 1370 DR . History . Foxy was born in Luiren but soon left in search of adventures with some halfling companions .
description_long: Foxilon Cardluck Foxilon Cardluck , better known as Foxy , was a crew - member of the Halruaan caravel " Realms Master " in 1370 DR . History . Foxy was born in Luiren but soon left in search of adventures with some halfling companions . However , Foxy and his fellows were tricked by Joribel into becoming addicted to a narcotic substance known as cheeeese . So they became Joribel ' s pawns — stealing , raiding and even killing for a piece of cheeeese . However , when a bully took Foxy ' s cheeeese , Foxy briefly regained lucidity , managing to escape together with a halfling girl . In their escape , they met Dwalimar Omen and Minder . Foxy explained his situation and Omen destroyed Joribel . Afterward the wizard trained Foxy in stealing magical items . When Omen launched the " Realms Master " , Foxy became his first mate . Personality . Foxy was a buoyant and charming individual . He was protective of his crew members and considered it his mission to keep their spirits up . Foxy was friendly and liked almost all people but was not naive . Sometimes he still felt a craving for cheeeese but resisted the temptation .

title: Foxmantle
description: Foxmantle The Foxmantles were one of the merchant - noble families of Sembia . Their businesses included farming , pressing wine , growing dyestuffs , salting meat , and tanning hides and furs . Their family crest was three vigilant eyes in purple set on a slant .
description_long: Foxmantle The Foxmantles were one of the merchant - noble families of Sembia . Their businesses included farming , pressing wine , growing dyestuffs , salting meat , and tanning hides and furs . Their family crest was three vigilant eyes in purple set on a slant . Properties . The Foxmantle family home overlooks Rauthauvyr ' s Road .

title: Fraasz
description: Fraasz Fraasz was a duergar city located deep under the Sunrise Mountains in eastern Rashemen . History . The city was originally located in a vault beneath Thay but earthquakes caused by the Spellplague nearly destroyed the old city and the duergar relocated .
description_long: Fraasz Fraasz was a duergar city located deep under the Sunrise Mountains in eastern Rashemen . History . The city was originally located in a vault beneath Thay but earthquakes caused by the Spellplague nearly destroyed the old city and the duergar relocated . Fraasz was relatively isolated and faced no real threats from rival cities .

title: Fracto - Nimbuli
description: Fracto - Nimbuli Fracto - Nimbuli was a cloud giant ally of Yrkhetep in Chondath in 1358 DR . Activities . Usually Fracto - Nimbuli was in his main room with three spotted lion s as pets .
description_long: Fracto - Nimbuli Fracto - Nimbuli was a cloud giant ally of Yrkhetep in Chondath in 1358 DR . Activities . Usually Fracto - Nimbuli was in his main room with three spotted lion s as pets . History . In 1358 DR , Fracto - Nimbuli agreed to help the arcanaloth Yrkhetep in exchange for gold and power . He transported a portion of Yrkhetep ' s troops — including the Skykillers , the Dark Watch , and others — to the Five Crown inn in Arrabar using his flying castle in order to battle the combined forces of the Sisterhood of the Oaks , the Lightblades , the Sunshafts , and the Windriders . Personality . Fracto - Nimbuli was a greedy and vain individual .

title: Fraeyer Illance
description: Fraeyer Illance Fraeyer Illance , tall thin darkly handsome and soft - spoken cold heart , one of the younger and better - traveled members of his family , now most energetic in promoting family interests , unscrupulous and follows the motto " Freedom from all laws , and a spur to all profits , daggers for our foes , and a pox on all lawmakers and keepers . " ( hinted to be a family motto )
description_long: Fraeyer Illance Fraeyer Illance , tall thin darkly handsome and soft - spoken cold heart , one of the younger and better - traveled members of his family , now most energetic in promoting family interests , unscrupulous and follows the motto " Freedom from all laws , and a spur to all profits , daggers for our foes , and a pox on all lawmakers and keepers . " ( hinted to be a family motto )

title: Franko Olbert
description: Franko Olbert Franko Olbert was a man from Nesme in the late 15th century DR . History . Franko born in Nesmè from an Uthgardt mother and a Nesmè man .
description_long: Franko Olbert Franko Olbert was a man from Nesme in the late 15th century DR . History . Franko born in Nesmè from an Uthgardt mother and a Nesmè man . He managed to escape the fall of his home city in 1484 DR after an attack by drow and orc armies led by Tiago Baenre . In 1485 DR , Franko plotted to gather an Uthgardt army to reclaim the city when Tiago found him and dueled with him for sport . Franko was defeated and eaten by the white dragon Amaunathor .

title: Fraternity of Tharos
description: Fraternity of Tharos The Fraternity of Tharos was a demon - worshiping cult based in New Sarshel in Impiltur . The group took its name from the ancient Nar capital of Dun - Tharos . The group conducted bloody rituals that required members to kidnap innocent victims and then sacrifice them on the Demonstone which lay in a tower in New Sarshel .
description_long: Fraternity of Tharos The Fraternity of Tharos was a demon - worshiping cult based in New Sarshel in Impiltur . The group took its name from the ancient Nar capital of Dun - Tharos . The group conducted bloody rituals that required members to kidnap innocent victims and then sacrifice them on the Demonstone which lay in a tower in New Sarshel .

title: Fray
description: Fray The Fray were thirteen mage s who helped the Fourteenth Skull maintain the weakened mythal around Skullport known as the Mantle in the 15th century DR . Members of the Fray were given great power by the Fourteenth Skull but it drove them mad . They were promised that once the mythal was restored to its former power they would become the new Skulls of Skullport .
description_long: Fray The Fray were thirteen mage s who helped the Fourteenth Skull maintain the weakened mythal around Skullport known as the Mantle in the 15th century DR . Members of the Fray were given great power by the Fourteenth Skull but it drove them mad . They were promised that once the mythal was restored to its former power they would become the new Skulls of Skullport . Organization . Most of the Fray ' s duties were rather mundane such as tracking down and stealing minor magic items which they used to strengthen the mythal . Occasionally , the Fourteenth Skull required the Fray to capture visiting mages and kill them to add their essence to the mythal .

title: Fraz - Urb ' luu
description: Fraz - Urb ' luu Fraz - Urb ' luu , styled the Prince of Deception , was a demon lord . Abilities . His vision was excellent and piercing with both darkvision and " true seeing " .
description_long: Fraz - Urb ' luu Fraz - Urb ' luu , styled the Prince of Deception , was a demon lord . Abilities . His vision was excellent and piercing with both darkvision and " true seeing " . His ability to fly was average . History . In −181 DR , the ruler of Narfell , Ilithkar , was overthrown by his cousin Rheligaun " the Horned " , a half - fiend ish son of Fraz - Urb ' luu .

title: Fredegar Rockcrusher
description: Fredegar Rockcrusher Fredegar Rockcrusher , also known as Fret , was a dwarf sage under the charge of Alustriel in Silverymoon . He was a trusted advisor to both Alustriel and her sister Dove Falconhand . Description .
description_long: Fredegar Rockcrusher Fredegar Rockcrusher , also known as Fret , was a dwarf sage under the charge of Alustriel in Silverymoon . He was a trusted advisor to both Alustriel and her sister Dove Falconhand . Description . Fredegar had a snow white hair and beard . He dressed in the finest cloth and had an elflike musical voice . Fret was a very clean and tidy dwarf , who liked things and people around him to be clean and tidy also . While Catti - brie was in Silverymoon , Fret helped her to clean herself up . Despite his curious and awkward nature of being the most pampered and clean dwarf in all of Faerûn , he proved himself more than once in battle when his favorite vestments were dirtied by a mind flayer ' s brain matter after going into a fit of rage against a drow onslaught . History . Fret was born in Citadel Adbar , but spent many years in Silverymoon . Around 1340 DR , Fret was one of the members of a group alongside Dove Falconhand who hunted Drizzt Do ' Urden when he first came to the surface .

title: Fredegast
description: Fredegast Fredegast was the young sheriff of the halfling town of Waukeshire in Bloodstone Barony in 1357 DR . History . In 1357 DR , Fredegast and his people met Gareth Dragonsbane ' s party .
description_long: Fredegast Fredegast was the young sheriff of the halfling town of Waukeshire in Bloodstone Barony in 1357 DR . History . In 1357 DR , Fredegast and his people met Gareth Dragonsbane ' s party . In 1359 DR , Fredegast was a key member of the Alliance of Belt Watchers with local dwarves and centaur s . Personality . Fredegast was an able , bright and charismatic military leader .

title: Free Cities of Zakhara
description: Free Cities of Zakhara The Free Cities of Zakhara were a group of city - states along the north coast of that continent . Geography . Each of these city - states was located at the mouth of a river .
description_long: Free Cities of Zakhara The Free Cities of Zakhara were a group of city - states along the north coast of that continent . Geography . Each of these city - states was located at the mouth of a river . The cities were Hafayah , Liham , Muluk , Qadib , Umara , and Utaqa . They swore fealty to the Grand Caliph in Huzuz , but maintained a larger degree of independence than other parts of Zakhara . Government . The Free Cities ' independence was limited mainly by the nearby city of staunch Qudra and its mamluks . The Free Cities seemed less civilized than other Zakharan urban centers , as they had to contend with wild tribes on land to the south and pirates on sea . They were also the first stopping point for travellers from Faerûn . Trade . Main products of the Free Cities included clothing , rice , agate s , semi - precious stones , pottery , coffee , indigo dye , purple cloth and clothing , and trade in northern goods .

title: Free Cities of the Vilhon Reach
description: Free Cities of the Vilhon Reach The Free Cities of the Vilhon Reach were a collection of independent city - states that separated themselves from Chondath . Hlondeth , Lachom , Nimpeth , Reth , and Surkh were considered the five key free cities but the villages of Elupar and Nun were often grouped with them as well . History .
description_long: Free Cities of the Vilhon Reach The Free Cities of the Vilhon Reach were a collection of independent city - states that separated themselves from Chondath . Hlondeth , Lachom , Nimpeth , Reth , and Surkh were considered the five key free cities but the villages of Elupar and Nun were often grouped with them as well . History . After the Rotting War in 902 DR , the Chondathian Empire became weak and lost its hold on several territories . The cities that would become known as the free cities , gained their independence during this time . Politics . Despite no official allegiances , the free cities often supported each other and worked together to prevent Arrabar from regaining the strength it once held . The free cities did have disputes and small conflicts from time to time but military might was rarely employed . Culture . The free cities all shared a strong military culture and dependence on slavery . Nimpeth made use of slave s more than the other free cities . Military service was also a shared expectation within the city - states . When a boy reached adulthood , he was expected to serve in his local militia . Slaves rarely served in armies unless they were absolutely needed .

title: Free action
description: Free action Free action was a divine abjuration and enchantment spell that allowed an individual to move normally while under water or against magic that impeded movement . Effects . The caster was required to touch the target of this spell and it lasted for over an hour , with even longer duration for more experienced casters .
description_long: Free action Free action was a divine abjuration and enchantment spell that allowed an individual to move normally while under water or against magic that impeded movement . Effects . The caster was required to touch the target of this spell and it lasted for over an hour , with even longer duration for more experienced casters . The recipient of " free action " was able to move and fight normally ( as if on dry land ) while under water using melee weapons held in the hands . Ranged weapons were subject to movement reduction immediately upon being hurled or fired . Note that this spell did not confer any ability to breathe while submerged . This spell was also proof against " web " , " slow " , " hold person " , " paralyze " , " iron bands of Bilarro " , and other magical hindrances to movement . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , the caster was required to touch the recipient of this spell . The material component was a leather thong tied around an arm , leg , or similar appendage of the recipient . The leather thong turned to dust when the spell expired .

title: Freedale
description: Freedale Though far from other towns , Freedale remains a busy place . Elves traveling west often stop in Freedale for supplies , as do other travelers from the east . Freedale is also a stop for those traveling up or down the River Ashaba , docking their boats or barges at the wharfs south of town .
description_long: Freedale Though far from other towns , Freedale remains a busy place . Elves traveling west often stop in Freedale for supplies , as do other travelers from the east . Freedale is also a stop for those traveling up or down the River Ashaba , docking their boats or barges at the wharfs south of town .

title: Freedom
description: Freedom Freedom is an abjuration spell that releases a creature from imprisonment . Effects . The subject is freed from spells and effects that restrict his movement , including " entangle " , " hold " , " imprisonment " , " paralysis " , " petrification " , " sleep " , " slow " , stunning , " temporal stasis " , and " web " .
description_long: Freedom Freedom is an abjuration spell that releases a creature from imprisonment . Effects . The subject is freed from spells and effects that restrict his movement , including " entangle " , " hold " , " imprisonment " , " paralysis " , " petrification " , " sleep " , " slow " , stunning , " temporal stasis " , and " web " . To free someone from " imprisonment " , you must know his name and background , and you must cast this spell at the spot where he was entombed . " Freedom " was the reversed form of the spell " imprisonment " .

title: Freedom Riders
description: Freedom Riders The Freedom Riders were the military forces organized by Randal Morn to expel the Zhentarim from Daggerdale . After victory in 1369 DR , they became the official army of the dale . History .
description_long: Freedom Riders The Freedom Riders were the military forces organized by Randal Morn to expel the Zhentarim from Daggerdale . After victory in 1369 DR , they became the official army of the dale . History . Randal Morn had been fighting for Daggerdale ' s liberty since 1339 DR , when he was a young man of about sixteen winters . Gathering a small band of outcasts , he formed the Freedom Riders , a rebel force whose single goal was to overthrow the Zhentarim - sponsored government that had ruled Daggerdale since 1316 DR . Their numbers increased to a hundred in the early 1350 DR s . About half of them were cavalrymen who fought on horseback ; the rest were mounted infantrymen who could quickly dismount and fight on foot . Being mounted provided them with the mobility to strike at Zhent - controlled hamlets hard and fast . As a guerrilla - style unit , the Freedom Riders never established a permanent headquarters , but they often used Castle Daggerdale and the surrounding hills as a base of operations .

title: Freedom domain
description: Freedom domain The two deities who hold influence over the freedom domain are Ilmater and Mielikki . Ilmater ' s primary mission is to keep others from feeling the weight of hardship , pain and being controlled against ones wish . The freedom the crying god grants comes from his own suffering .
description_long: Freedom domain The two deities who hold influence over the freedom domain are Ilmater and Mielikki . Ilmater ' s primary mission is to keep others from feeling the weight of hardship , pain and being controlled against ones wish . The freedom the crying god grants comes from his own suffering . Mielikki believes that freedom is a natural state , and that just as the animals of the forest , who are free to roam how ever they will , so should people be . Power of freedom Domain . Any divine caster that worships a deity who claims the freedom domain may choose to channel the deities powers within the domain . When the caster chooses this domain , she will become more acrobatic and gain the ability to use " path of freedom " . When she uses a power that is associated the domain that hits an enemy , she or an ally near her will , for a short time , become more protected against magic and poison . The powers of the freedom Domain include :

title: Freedom of movement
description: Freedom of movement Freedom of movement is a common abjuration spell that allows the subject to move normally despite impediments . Effect . This spell enables you or the creature you touch to move and attack normally for the duration of the spell , even under the influence of magic that usually impedes movement , such as " hold person " , " paralysis " , " solid fog " , " slow " , and " web " spells .
description_long: Freedom of movement Freedom of movement is a common abjuration spell that allows the subject to move normally despite impediments . Effect . This spell enables you or the creature you touch to move and attack normally for the duration of the spell , even under the influence of magic that usually impedes movement , such as " hold person " , " paralysis " , " solid fog " , " slow " , and " web " spells . The spell also allows a character to move and attack normally while underwater , even with cutting weapons such as axes and swords and with bludgeoning weapons such as flails , hammers , and maces , provided that the weapon is wielded in the hand rather than hurled . The " freedom of movement " spell does not , however , allow water breathing . Material Component . A leather thong , bound around the arm or a similar appendage .

title: Freeze
description: Freeze Freeze was a divine magic spell available to priests of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It could attack a creature with biting cold and possibly encase the target in ice . Effects .
description_long: Freeze Freeze was a divine magic spell available to priests of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It could attack a creature with biting cold and possibly encase the target in ice . Effects . This spell could be cast at a single target , in sight , up to 170 ft ( 52 m ) away ( more experienced casters could extend this range ) . When cast , a white beam of light shot from the caster ' s outstretched hand and , if the attack on the target succeeded , caused the victim to suffer damage from intense cold . A creature struck by " freeze " had one chance to avoid the second , more devastating effect of this spell — being encased in a sheath of solid ice 5 inches ( 13 centimeters ) thick that continuously subjected the individual to the same cold damage as the white ray . While a victim was frozen in ice , he or she was awake , aware , and could breathe normally , but could not move or speak except to try and break free using brute strength . Flying creatures immediately fell from the sky , swimming creatures bobbed like a small iceberg .

title: Freezing cloud
description: Freezing cloud Freezing cloud is a spell of the evocation school used by wizard s early in their studies . When cast , " freezing cloud " creates a tiny pellet of ice , which shoots from the hand of its caster to a spot within fifty feet of him or her . There , the pellet explodes into a cloud of freezing mist over an area of ten feet in radius .
description_long: Freezing cloud Freezing cloud is a spell of the evocation school used by wizard s early in their studies . When cast , " freezing cloud " creates a tiny pellet of ice , which shoots from the hand of its caster to a spot within fifty feet of him or her . There , the pellet explodes into a cloud of freezing mist over an area of ten feet in radius . Creatures within are subjected to deadly temperatures , the deadliness depending upon how durable the creature in question is . The cloud dissipates on its own after a moment , but the wizard can , if he or she wishes , dismiss it sooner with a little effort . " Freezing cloud " requires a great deal of concentration on the wizard ' s part and as such , can only be cast once per day .

title: Frenzy dog
description: Frenzy dog The frenzy dog is a magical transformation of almost any other animal , created by the special " create frenzy dog " spell , used by the druid s of Chondalwood to protect their environment . The spell that creates these creatures is barely known outside this forest , and the druids use it sparingly , creating a pack of only around a dozen frenzy dogs at one time , wary of their ability to ruin forest environments if left unchecked . A frenzy dog gains a certain amount of magical intelligence , but only enough for hunting .
description_long: Frenzy dog The frenzy dog is a magical transformation of almost any other animal , created by the special " create frenzy dog " spell , used by the druid s of Chondalwood to protect their environment . The spell that creates these creatures is barely known outside this forest , and the druids use it sparingly , creating a pack of only around a dozen frenzy dogs at one time , wary of their ability to ruin forest environments if left unchecked . A frenzy dog gains a certain amount of magical intelligence , but only enough for hunting . Description . The frenzy dog is around 4 feet ( 1 . 2m ) tall at the shoulder and has black coat with tan and white swirls . It has a face similar to a pit bull . It has a protrusion of 7 " ( 18cm ) bony spikes from its neck that has the appearance of a spiked collar . Diet . A frenzy dog eats three times the amount that a normal dog of the same size would eat . They will eat any type of animal flesh . Combat . In combat , the frenzy dog attacks without fear and attempts to rip its victims apart ( although not necessarily to eat ) .

title: Freona
description: Freona madame Freona was an halfling businesswoman in Phlan . Personality . Freona has a keen taste for finer things in life .
description_long: Freona madame Freona was an halfling businesswoman in Phlan . Personality . Freona has a keen taste for finer things in life . She was a good cook , a terrible gossip hound and a very skilled entrepreneur . She loved her city and hated the dragon usurper . Activities . Freona managed the Madame Freona ' s Tea Kettle with the help of her five daughters History . Freona ' s tea house was one of the most famous place in Phlan in 1489 DR . After Vorgansharax ' s coup she hid in her shop many individuals sought after by the Tears of Virulence For this the dragon ordered to burn the tea house but an adventuring party hired by the resistance managed to help Freona to escape from the city .

title: Friary of St . Amahl
description: Friary of St . Amahl The Friary of St . Amahl was an Ilmatari monastery in the middle of the Calim Desert .
description_long: Friary of St . Amahl The Friary of St . Amahl was an Ilmatari monastery in the middle of the Calim Desert . Location . The friary was 75 miles ( 120 . 7 kilometers ) south of the city of Memnon , along the Trade Way . Structure . A former , the Friary of St . Amahl had heavily shuttered windows to protect against the desert storms . It contained a well that had never gone dry . Rumors and legends . This safehouse was named after St . Amahl , the Ilmatari saint of desert nomads . The local legend of the place was that their well would never run dry as long as they continued to be watched over by their patron saint .

title: Fried Rat
description: Fried Rat The Fried Rat was a restaurant on Rat Alley in Luskan established by two retired shiphands who had developed a taste for rat after long periods at sea , and wanted to serve it . History . The restaurant burned down long before 1370 DR .
description_long: Fried Rat The Fried Rat was a restaurant on Rat Alley in Luskan established by two retired shiphands who had developed a taste for rat after long periods at sea , and wanted to serve it . History . The restaurant burned down long before 1370 DR . Two theories existed : one was that flaming grease was responsible for the fire , and the other was that discontented wererat s were to blame .

title: Friendly Arm Inn
description: Friendly Arm Inn The Friendly Arm Inn was a walled hamlet on the Coast Way between Baldur ' s Gate and the town of Beregost . Interior . The most prominent building around the hamlet was the stone keep which housed the titular inn , which was run by Bentley Mirrorshade .
description_long: Friendly Arm Inn The Friendly Arm Inn was a walled hamlet on the Coast Way between Baldur ' s Gate and the town of Beregost . Interior . The most prominent building around the hamlet was the stone keep which housed the titular inn , which was run by Bentley Mirrorshade . This establishment was a popular stop for people traveling on the Coast Road . The rooms were airy , the food was good , and everything was clean . The barmaids were rumored to be iron golem s camouflaged as women by illusory means . Apart from the inn , the wall surrounded a temple , a handful of houses , and stables . Atmosphere . At the Friendly Arm Inn , peace was secured by the guards , who insisted that all weapons be left at the gate and that all wizard s and cleric s tie one thumb to their belts , a practice that spilled over to fighting monks as well . History . The keep was once the stronghold of an evil cleric of Bhaal , but the gnome Bentley Mirrorshade and his adventuring party , including his wife Gellana Mirrorshade cleaned out the keep and renovated it . The Friendly Arm became a safe haven for travellers . Appendix . Notes . Baldur ' s Gate the novel .

title: Friendly Word
description: Friendly Word The Friendly Word was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara whose members followed the teaching of Zann , the Zakharan god of learning and intelligence . Symbol . Though they did not use unique weapons , members of the Friendly Word left a pen - shaped dagger in the pillow of their target as a calling card and warning .
description_long: Friendly Word The Friendly Word was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara whose members followed the teaching of Zann , the Zakharan god of learning and intelligence . Symbol . Though they did not use unique weapons , members of the Friendly Word left a pen - shaped dagger in the pillow of their target as a calling card and warning . Activities . Holy slayers from this organization rarely committed murder , preferring instead to attack the reputation or station of their targets . They accomplished this by carefully researching their targets , spreading rumors , and destroying the wealth and holdings of their targets . Their favorite tactic was to create an accusation of which the target could only be proved innocent by confessing to some other crime or incriminating situation . Base of Operations . The stronghold for the Friendly Word was located within the Ghost Mountains northwest of Halwa .

title: Friends
description: Friends Friends was an arcane enchantment spell that could influence the mood of a creature in favor of the caster . Effects . While the caster concentrated , for up to one minute , the target creature became more inclined to believe , be persuaded or otherwise influenced by the caster .
description_long: Friends Friends was an arcane enchantment spell that could influence the mood of a creature in favor of the caster . Effects . While the caster concentrated , for up to one minute , the target creature became more inclined to believe , be persuaded or otherwise influenced by the caster . Once the effect of the spell wore off , the target creature immediately realized that magic was used to influence its mood , and could react violently . Components . The spell needed somatic and material components . As the material component , a bit of makeup was applied to the caster ' s face , but this could be replaced by the use of an arcane focus .

title: Frigid blade
description: Frigid blade Frigid blade is a transmutation spell used by swordmage s , particularly those who prefer to use fire and ice together in their spells . When a swordmage casts " frigid blade " they fill their weapon with icy power , freezing the flesh of its target and the air around it . When used on a creature , this causes the said creature to slow down substantially , the exact percentage dependent upon how durable the swordmage ' s own flesh is .
description_long: Frigid blade Frigid blade is a transmutation spell used by swordmage s , particularly those who prefer to use fire and ice together in their spells . When a swordmage casts " frigid blade " they fill their weapon with icy power , freezing the flesh of its target and the air around it . When used on a creature , this causes the said creature to slow down substantially , the exact percentage dependent upon how durable the swordmage ' s own flesh is . This effect only lasts a brief moment , though " frigid blade " can be recast at will and the power of the spell increases with the swordmage ' s own .

title: Frigid darkness
description: Frigid darkness Frigid darkness , is an invocation of the evocation school used by many warlock s , particularly those of the star pact . When a warlock casts " frigid darkness " he or she summons to a spot within fifty feet of him or herself a pool of freezing shadow . These shadows cling to any creature unfortunate enough to be within their grasp , bestowing them with a sample of the dark cold of the night sky .
description_long: Frigid darkness Frigid darkness , is an invocation of the evocation school used by many warlock s , particularly those of the star pact . When a warlock casts " frigid darkness " he or she summons to a spot within fifty feet of him or herself a pool of freezing shadow . These shadows cling to any creature unfortunate enough to be within their grasp , bestowing them with a sample of the dark cold of the night sky . The shadow not only injures a warlock ' s foes , but distracts them and obscures their vision for a moment , giving both the warlock and his or her allies a short - lasting advantage against the victim . Those of the star pact summon shadow of such power that they are able to reduce the effectiveness of an enemy ' s armor , at least for a brief moment . " Frigid darkness " is not enormously complex and a warlock need only rest a few minutes or more before casting the spell a second time .

title: Frisky chest
description: Frisky chest Frisky chest was an enchantment spell that enabled an object to avoid being approached by anyone other than the caster . Effects . The caster had to touch the object to cast this spell , and the object had to be movable , non - living , and fit inside a 10 ft ( 3 m ) cube .
description_long: Frisky chest Frisky chest was an enchantment spell that enabled an object to avoid being approached by anyone other than the caster . Effects . The caster had to touch the object to cast this spell , and the object had to be movable , non - living , and fit inside a 10 ft ( 3 m ) cube . For the duration of the spell , the object would grow feet or legs , wings , or fins ( whichever would provide the best escape ) whenever someone other than the caster got within 3 ft ( 1 m ) .
