Although many scholars have come to believe that roots of gray renders can be traced back to the Elemental Chaos , the truth of the matter is that gray renders were created thousands of years ago by a small conclave of silver dragon wizards who spent most of their time in elven form and developed gray renders primarily as bodyguards for their loyal minions . The method for creating new gray renders was passed from the silver dragons to several elven communities , and from them to numerous like - aligned wizards of various races over the following centuries . Today , the knowledge of how to create a gray render is not uncommon among wizardly scholars , although the origins of the race are largely forgotten . Physical description . A gray render stands about 9 feet tall in spite of its hunched posture and is about 4 feet wide . It weighs about 4 , 000 pounds . It has very thick skin which protects it from the bites and stings of insects . Its six eyes have insect - like structure , each being composed of hundreds of tiny ocelli .

title: Gray slaad
description: Gray slaad Gray slaadi were powerful slaad shapechangers and spellcasters . Description . Gray slaadi were the result of a green slaad having learned a magical procedure to transform permanently into a stronger form , while retaining all their memories from their previous forms .
description_long: Gray slaad Gray slaadi were powerful slaad shapechangers and spellcasters . Description . Gray slaadi were the result of a green slaad having learned a magical procedure to transform permanently into a stronger form , while retaining all their memories from their previous forms . They could wield greatsword s and imbue them with their own magic . Grey slaadi were servants of the death slaad i and often carried out their errands in the Prime Material Plane , often disguised as humanoid s . If a gray slaad devoured the corpse of a death slaad it would become a death slaad itself .

title: Gray wolf
description: Gray wolf The gray wolf was the most common variety of wolf to be found . Combat . While wolves were often blamed for attacks on stray wanderers and children , they were actually quite afraid of humans .
description_long: Gray wolf The gray wolf was the most common variety of wolf to be found . Combat . While wolves were often blamed for attacks on stray wanderers and children , they were actually quite afraid of humans . Most wolves stayed away from areas inhabited by humanoids , only attacking if they were extremely hungry or desperate . Ecology . A wolf was a common canine predator found in many parts of the world , but especially in northern climates . They were apex predators who hunted in well - organized packs using tactics honed over millions of years of evolution . Behavior . A wolf pack was a highly - structured society , commanded by an alpha male and his alpha female . Subordinate wolves were in a beta class , while the bottom of the social order was an omega wolf . Packs often hunted together . Their tactics included harrying their prey into an area where the pack could surround it and slowly weaken it with attacks that come one at a time from each wolf until the prey was dropped to the ground . At this time , the entire pack converged in for the final kill and feasting .

title: Grayclaws
description: Grayclaws The Grayclaws were a thieves ' guild located in the city of Tantras in the Vast in the 14th century DR . Organization . The Grayclaws were composed of thieves and smugglers .
description_long: Grayclaws The Grayclaws were a thieves ' guild located in the city of Tantras in the Vast in the 14th century DR . Organization . The Grayclaws were composed of thieves and smugglers . Most thieves and other rogues in Tantras were Grayclaws . Those who were not either made an arrangement with the guild or were soon killed . Around 1358 DR , the Grayclaws were commanded by two men : Amlithor Harlguss , a thief , and Othniir Xalast , a priest of Mask . Activities . An effective thieves ' guild , the Grayclaws were largely engaged in both theft and smuggling . Being somewhat loyal to their city , they mostly only preyed upon visitors to Tantras and those native Tantrans whom they felt to have grown too wealthy , too arrogant , or too immoral . The Grayclaws watched each other and made certain that they did not attract undue attention , not wishing to making many enemies nor to raise the ire of the High Council of Tantras . Possessions . The Grayclaws were named for the claw - like weapons they favored in combat , also called grayclaws . Armed with these blades , Grayclaws could deliver a devastating sneak attack on their targets , though they were less effective with other weapons .

title: Grayclaws ( weapon )
description: Grayclaws ( weapon ) Grayclaws were a set of claw - like weapons favored by the Grayclaws thieves ' guild of Tantras , who took their name from these blades . Description . Grayclaws consisted of a set of leather gauntlets that strapped to the hand fitted with brass knuckles , from which projected razor - sharp blades .
description_long: Grayclaws ( weapon ) Grayclaws were a set of claw - like weapons favored by the Grayclaws thieves ' guild of Tantras , who took their name from these blades . Description . Grayclaws consisted of a set of leather gauntlets that strapped to the hand fitted with brass knuckles , from which projected razor - sharp blades . They were similar to the bagh nakh wielded in some eastern lands . Abilities . Grayclaws were a slashing weapon , lightly damaging but fast . A trained user could be dangerous in battle , and Grayclaws thieves , specialized in their use , could deliver a devastating sneak attack on their targets . The claws had another use , in gripping surfaces while climbing , enabling to climb faster and more surely . A Grayclaws thief could use them to scale a wall with ease . However , they tended to hamper the wearer ' s hand movements in other areas , and they could not be donned or doffed quickly . Availability . A set of grayclaws typically cost 3 gold piece s , though they were rarely available on the open market .

title: Graycloak ' s Wolves
description: Graycloak ' s Wolves Graycloak ' s Wolves was an adventuring company active in 1343 DR , and led by Irmar Graycloak . Activities . Graycloak ' s Wolves were active in the city of Hlondeth in the Vilhon Reach in the Year of the Boot , 1343 DR , when they were requested to deliver the " Tome of Torment " — the most holy book of the church of Ilmater — to Master Sufferer Olbedan in Aralent .
description_long: Graycloak ' s Wolves Graycloak ' s Wolves was an adventuring company active in 1343 DR , and led by Irmar Graycloak . Activities . Graycloak ' s Wolves were active in the city of Hlondeth in the Vilhon Reach in the Year of the Boot , 1343 DR , when they were requested to deliver the " Tome of Torment " — the most holy book of the church of Ilmater — to Master Sufferer Olbedan in Aralent . However , during the harsh winter , Graycloak ' s Wolves fell prey to doppelganger s and leucrotta preying on travellers . The " Tome " was thought lost in the winter snows .

title: Grayling
description: Grayling The Grayling was a ship that sailed its last voyage in 1399 DR . The Grand Council of Impiltur chartered the ship to carry Bayel Droust on a mission to map the post - spellplague shoreline of the Sea of Fallen Stars . Droust carried two rare books that the eladrin Caelynna wanted and she sunk the ship in order to get the books and to capture Droust .
description_long: Grayling The Grayling was a ship that sailed its last voyage in 1399 DR . The Grand Council of Impiltur chartered the ship to carry Bayel Droust on a mission to map the post - spellplague shoreline of the Sea of Fallen Stars . Droust carried two rare books that the eladrin Caelynna wanted and she sunk the ship in order to get the books and to capture Droust . Bayel Droust was imprisoned on the ship for many years and forced to work at translating the books .

title: Graystaff
description: Graystaff A graystaff , or a staff of frost , was a mundane staff used by bheur s as a magical focus for powerful spells . Description . A graystaff was a gnarled wooden staff taller than a bheur .
description_long: Graystaff A graystaff , or a staff of frost , was a mundane staff used by bheur s as a magical focus for powerful spells . Description . A graystaff was a gnarled wooden staff taller than a bheur . It was not inherently magical and only had powers when held by the bheur who had crafted it . Abilities . When held by a bheur , the staff allowed her to create powerful magical effects , including " cone of cold " , " hold person " , " ice storm " , " solid fog " , and " wall of ice " . Unless she held her graystaff , she could not cast these spells . Construction . A graystaff was made from a wood that could not be found on the Prime Material Plane . It took at least a year for a bheur to craft her staff .

title: Grayth Holmfast
description: Grayth Holmfast Grayth Holmfast was a human priest of Lathander and a member of the Company of the White Star . His squire was Brant Rethalshield . He lived in Waterdeep .
description_long: Grayth Holmfast Grayth Holmfast was a human priest of Lathander and a member of the Company of the White Star . His squire was Brant Rethalshield . He lived in Waterdeep . Description . Grayth had silvery - gray hair ( once dark ) in a close - cropped fringe with a receding hairline and a gray goatee . He was of lean build , although he used to be athletic . He was tall with square shoulders . He spoke with a deep , gravelly voice . Relatives . Grayth was married for a time , although was no longer married as of Alturiak , 1374 DR . His two sons of ten and seven years resided with their mother . Equipment . Grayth wore a suit of light gold mail underneath a white coat with the sunrise symbol of Lathander . He carried a broadsword . History . Grayth took part in King Azoun ' s crusade against the Tuigan Horde in Thesk . On Tarsakh 7 , 1374 DR , Grayth was stabbed in the neck by Nurthel Floshin in retribution for Araevin Teshurr ' s refusal to cooperate with Sarya Dlardrageth .

title: Graz ' zt
description: Graz ' zt Graz ' zt , called The Dark Prince , is a demon lord and one of the most powerful fiends in the Abyss . Description . Standing nine feet tall , Graz ' zt appears as a lithe , muscular humanoid .
description_long: Graz ' zt Graz ' zt , called The Dark Prince , is a demon lord and one of the most powerful fiends in the Abyss . Description . Standing nine feet tall , Graz ' zt appears as a lithe , muscular humanoid . His skin shines like polished obsidian , and his eyes glitter with malevolent green light . He has yellowed fangs , pointed ears , and six slender fingers decorating each hand . He is sometimes described as having six small black horns half - hidden amid his thick black hair . These fiend ish traits are apparent , regardless of whatever form Graz ' zt chooses to take . He is considered the comeliest demon in the Abyss , and dresses in the most expensive and elegant finery on the entire plane . Wielding an acid - drenched greatsword in one hand and a profane tower shield in the other , the Dark Prince is a veritable killing machine when loosed upon the hordes of the Abyss . What ' s more , he has a vast repertoire of spell - like abilities at his disposal , making him a deadly magical opponent . Graz ' zt ' s greatest weapons , however , are his mastery of seduction and guile .

title: Grazilaxx
description: Grazilaxx Grazilaxx was a mind flayer member of the Society of Brilliance during the Rage of Demons . History . Grazilaxx and all the other members of the society went on a pilgrimage to Gravenhollow some years before the Rage of Demons .
description_long: Grazilaxx Grazilaxx was a mind flayer member of the Society of Brilliance during the Rage of Demons . History . Grazilaxx and all the other members of the society went on a pilgrimage to Gravenhollow some years before the Rage of Demons . During the late phase of the Rage of Demons , Grazilaxx surprisingly helped Regis and Drizzt Do ' Urden in fighting the demon lord Demogorgon near Mantol - Derith .

title: Grease
description: Grease Grease ( originally called Shan ' s tallow ) was a low - powered conjuration spell of the creation subschool used by arcane casters to cover a solid surface in an oily film . Some cleric s of Ghaunadaur , Ilsensine , Laogzed , and Moander were granted the power of " grease " by their deities , and ooze genasi could create a similar effect . Effects .
description_long: Grease Grease ( originally called Shan ' s tallow ) was a low - powered conjuration spell of the creation subschool used by arcane casters to cover a solid surface in an oily film . Some cleric s of Ghaunadaur , Ilsensine , Laogzed , and Moander were granted the power of " grease " by their deities , and ooze genasi could create a similar effect . Effects . This spell would coat a single object or a ten - foot - square surface within a close range with a layer of slippery grease , which would last for a number of seconds depending on the power of the caster . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic component s , the caster required a piece of butter or a bit of pork rind to cast this spell , which disappeared . History . The spell was invented by the Netherese arcanist Shan in −644 DR .

title: Great Bhaerynden
description: Great Bhaerynden Great Bhaerynden was a domain located in the south - central region of Faerûn beneath the vast plains of Shaar . History . This Underdark region was the first homeland of the dwarves , but was conquered by the drow when they first ventured in the Underdark in search of a realm of their own .
description_long: Great Bhaerynden Great Bhaerynden was a domain located in the south - central region of Faerûn beneath the vast plains of Shaar . History . This Underdark region was the first homeland of the dwarves , but was conquered by the drow when they first ventured in the Underdark in search of a realm of their own . The drow called their new home Telantiwar , but this kingdom didn ' t last . For reasons that are still unknown , the domed ceilings of the enormous vaults in which Telantiwar was established collapsed down on the kingdom during civil war around - 7600 DR . Many of the drow were crushed beneath rocks and rubble from the rock layer above . This great collapse laid ruin to many of the drow cities of Telantiwar , and created the Great Rift . Inhabitants . Gold dwarves live in the Great Rift and a lot of the adjoining caves . Drow and half - drow held the city of T ' lindhet , and halflings lived in Deepburrow in Great Bhaerynden .

title: Great Chain Bridge of Ra - Khati
description: Great Chain Bridge of Ra - Khati The Great Chain Bridge of Ra - Khati was the only known crossing of the Jumpa River . Location . Located in Ra - Khati , the bridge crossed the Jumpa River and the Jumpa River Gorge into the city of Kushk .
description_long: Great Chain Bridge of Ra - Khati The Great Chain Bridge of Ra - Khati was the only known crossing of the Jumpa River . Location . Located in Ra - Khati , the bridge crossed the Jumpa River and the Jumpa River Gorge into the city of Kushk . Description . This bridge was made from iron chains , wood and hemp . The bridge would constantly sway with air churned from the pounding current of the Jumpa River .

title: Great Codex
description: Great Codex The Great Codex was a compendium of all the laws of the city of Procampur in the Vast . It was compiled in the 13th century DR , as a grand project to copy all of Procampur ' s existing laws into a single tome , which would be installed in a grand library . Scribes and legal scholars accompanied the city ' s ruling Thultyrl everywhere to continue the work .
description_long: Great Codex The Great Codex was a compendium of all the laws of the city of Procampur in the Vast . It was compiled in the 13th century DR , as a grand project to copy all of Procampur ' s existing laws into a single tome , which would be installed in a grand library . Scribes and legal scholars accompanied the city ' s ruling Thultyrl everywhere to continue the work . They even worked on it while on campaign , such as in the Year of Burning Steel , 1246 DR , when the Thultyrl led an army to liberate the allied city of Tsurlagol from an orc and goblinoid horde . However , his Hamayarch , the Pearl , predicted that he was destined to die young and in battle . Believing that he would go on to become a good king and complete the Great Codex , she may have orchestrated a wound he suffered on a hunting trip and secretly prevented his wounds from healing to keep him away from the frontlines .

title: Great Dale
description: Great Dale The Great Dale is governed by a druid ic hierarchy , under rule of Nentyarch . It is a human land , of 200 , 000 inhabitants . According to rumours , The Great Dale is the place from which Dalelanders come .
description_long: Great Dale The Great Dale is governed by a druid ic hierarchy , under rule of Nentyarch . It is a human land , of 200 , 000 inhabitants . According to rumours , The Great Dale is the place from which Dalelanders come . History . The Great Dale was part of the Narfell Empire and it was originally settled by human folk fleeing the fall of Jhaamdath . 1 , 500 years ago the war between Narfell and Raumathar caused the abandonment of the area . Nowadays is a frontier for the expanding tendencies of the kingdom of Impiltur . Major Geographic Features . The Dale . The Dale is a large gap between the Forest of Lethyr and the Rawlinswood . This area created long ago by an arm of the Great Glacier . The Dalefolk legends saying that a great dragon divided the forest with his breath while others state that Silvanus and Shaundakul held a contest to decide whether wood or wind will rule this land when Auril the Frostmaiden intervened to set winter over both . One long road crosses The Dale connecting Uthmere with the cold road , known by the name The Great Road or simply The Road ( since it is the only major road of the area ) . Climate is harsh with furious winter winds .

title: Great Dismal Delve
description: Great Dismal Delve The Great Dismal Delve was the home of all dao living on the Elemental Plane of Earth . Description . The Great Dismal Delve was actually a massive labyrinth located deep underground .
description_long: Great Dismal Delve The Great Dismal Delve was the home of all dao living on the Elemental Plane of Earth . Description . The Great Dismal Delve was actually a massive labyrinth located deep underground . The area it covered was larger than most continents on the Prime Material Plane . Location . Located deep within the Elemental Plane of Earth , the Great Dismal Delve was pocketed with links to a wide array of elemental materials , allowing the Great Khan of the dao to summon allies and resources at will . Geography . All tunnels within the Great Dismal Delve ultimately led to the Sevenfold Mazework , the heart of dao power . Inhabitants . In addition to the dao , the Great Dismal Delve housed many kinds of slaves who spent much of their time clearing debris caused by planequakes . The exact number of dao and their slaves inhabiting the Great Dismal Delve was unknown .

title: Great Door
description: Great Door The Great Door was a massive door hidden on the outskirts of Waterdeep on the Sword Coast North . It served as a " gate " to the planes . Defenses .
description_long: Great Door The Great Door was a massive door hidden on the outskirts of Waterdeep on the Sword Coast North . It served as a " gate " to the planes . Defenses . The Great Door was constructed inside a huge pit in the ground , covered over with an illusion of solid ground . After it was tampered with , the Door could shoot bolts of magic at those outside , and release monsters from other planes . It could also levitate into the air , tearing up the ground with it . Description . The Great Door was a colossal pair of doors set into the cliff - face of the pit , bearing many human and monstrous faces and topped by a statue of a winged , dragon - like creature that looked down on those below . Powers . The Great Door contained a " gate " that unlocked an interdimensional wormhole to the planes . History . The Great Door was constructed by two great wizard s , Ostus Agrivar and Parwyyd Hanifar , who worked together to explore the frontiers of magic . They built the Door as a means to easily enter the planes . Each wizard needed the other to control the Door , however , so it remained closed after Ostus ' s death in the Year of the Dragon , 1352 DR .

title: Great Garden
description: Great Garden The Great Garden was a wonder found within the fortress of Krak al - Mazhar in the Great Anvil of the Haunted Lands in 1367 DR . Descriptions . The garden was found deep underground beneath the fortress .
description_long: Great Garden The Great Garden was a wonder found within the fortress of Krak al - Mazhar in the Great Anvil of the Haunted Lands in 1367 DR . Descriptions . The garden was found deep underground beneath the fortress . It was filled with beautiful flora and a bubbling marble fountain , all of which were real . The pristine blue sky and bird and insect sounds filling the garden were all an elaborate illusion . The garden measured roughly 100 feet in diameter , but cleverly designed illusions made it appear endless . The paths traversing the garden had a " maze - like " effect upon occupants . Only those who knew the secret command word were immune to this effect . The " sky " over the garden mimicked the same cycles that occurred above the fortress . A constant gentle breeze caressed every area of the Great Garden . Inhabitants . Nar - Aidiya enjoyed relaxing in the garden when he was able to find time . A tasked slayer genie named Mujibur served as caretaker and guardian of the garden .

title: Great Glacier
description: Great Glacier The Great Glacier , also called Pelvuria was a large mass of frozen land in northeast Faerûn . History . It was created in - 2550 DR when the god Ulutiu laid himself to rest in his ice barge in the Cold Ocean , a favourite inland sea of his .
description_long: Great Glacier The Great Glacier , also called Pelvuria was a large mass of frozen land in northeast Faerûn . History . It was created in - 2550 DR when the god Ulutiu laid himself to rest in his ice barge in the Cold Ocean , a favourite inland sea of his . The barge sank soon after and the " Necklace of Ulutiu " , an artifact that he wore , encased his body in ice when his divinity had departed to the Astral Sea . The Cold Ocean became completely frozen by the necklace ' s magic over the next seventy five years then , due to a lack of interference from the giant kingdom of Ostoria , encroached upon the land as well . The glacier eventually destroyed the remains of Ostoria ( the city of Gharreil was a testimony to its former existence ) but was held in check by the High Magic of the elves of Lethyr . Over three thousand years later , the Ice Queen Iyraclea was granted the power to overcome the High Magic by Auril and the glacier began to grow larger once more .

title: Great Library of Perpustakaan
description: Great Library of Perpustakaan The Great Library of Perpustakaan , or simply Perpustakaan , was a library in Perpustakaan in Kesasar Valley in Shou Lung . It was one of the most magnificent depositories of knowledge in all of Kara - Tur . Unfortunately , most of the people outside the Shao Mountains had forgotten the existence of Perpustakaan History .
description_long: Great Library of Perpustakaan The Great Library of Perpustakaan , or simply Perpustakaan , was a library in Perpustakaan in Kesasar Valley in Shou Lung . It was one of the most magnificent depositories of knowledge in all of Kara - Tur . Unfortunately , most of the people outside the Shao Mountains had forgotten the existence of Perpustakaan History . Perpustakaan was built in ancient times by the Shao Mountains Empire . After the fall of that civilization , the existence of the library was forgotten in the rest of Shou Lung . In 1358 DR , however , an adventuring party rediscovered the library and told the Emperor ' s Wu Jen about it . Description . Perpustakaan was made of black granite . It was a huge building with a tall pagoda stretching into the sky . Inside , the library was divided in many Reference Sections , one specific section for each of these topics : literature , astrology , geography , ancient history , military history , philosophy , biography , mathematics , arcane lore , and one section for each member of the Nine Immortals . There also a conference room , a rotunda , rooms and cubicles for visiting scholars , a foyer , and residences for staff members .

title: Great Mother
description: Great Mother The Great Mother was the monstrous goddess of beholder s and a chaotic evil greater deity . Her symbol was an egg with an eye . Her areas of influence included magic , fertility , and tyranny .
description_long: Great Mother The Great Mother was the monstrous goddess of beholder s and a chaotic evil greater deity . Her symbol was an egg with an eye . Her areas of influence included magic , fertility , and tyranny . Her main interests were her beholder children and their safety , particularly against the drow . The Great Mother made her home in the Realm of a Million Eyes , the sixth layer of the Abyss .

title: Great Old One patron
description: Great Old One patron A Great Old One patron was one possible sponsor for a warlock . If a bargain was made between a warlock and a being from the Far Realm , an elder evil , or some other ancient and mysterious being , the warlock ' s patron gave them access to certain powers , including a suite of spells that expanded the choices to fill their spell slots .
description_long: Great Old One patron A Great Old One patron was one possible sponsor for a warlock . If a bargain was made between a warlock and a being from the Far Realm , an elder evil , or some other ancient and mysterious being , the warlock ' s patron gave them access to certain powers , including a suite of spells that expanded the choices to fill their spell slots .

title: Great Padishate of the Marid
description: Great Padishate of the Marid The Great Padishate of the Marid , or the Marid Padishate , was the collective term referring to the ruling body of government of the marid s . Marids were less organized as an official government when compared to the djinn , but their greater power ensured that they held greater control over the Elemental Plane of Water than the djinn did on the Elemental Plane of Air . Organization .
description_long: Great Padishate of the Marid The Great Padishate of the Marid , or the Marid Padishate , was the collective term referring to the ruling body of government of the marid s . Marids were less organized as an official government when compared to the djinn , but their greater power ensured that they held greater control over the Elemental Plane of Water than the djinn did on the Elemental Plane of Air . Organization . The Great Padisha of the Marid , Kalbari al - Durrat al - Amwaj ibn Jari , ruled over all of the noble marid s comprising the Padishate . Each and every marid claimed nobility of some sort , but only the truly noble marid served the Padisha and schemed to replace her one day . Base of Operations . The Citadel of Ten Thousand Pearls on the Elemental Plane of Water served as the seat of power for the Marid Padishate .

title: Great Raven Pueblo
description: Great Raven Pueblo Great Raven Pueblo was a settlement of 900 Azuposi nestled between the north bank of the Pasocada River above Raven Falls and Mesa Bovara . It marked the boundary between the Azuposi territory to the north and the Metahel territory to the south , and a large staircase carved from the rock descended from the settlement to the lands below . The Metahel settlement of Lomaraj was just a few miles down the river .
description_long: Great Raven Pueblo Great Raven Pueblo was a settlement of 900 Azuposi nestled between the north bank of the Pasocada River above Raven Falls and Mesa Bovara . It marked the boundary between the Azuposi territory to the north and the Metahel territory to the south , and a large staircase carved from the rock descended from the settlement to the lands below . The Metahel settlement of Lomaraj was just a few miles down the river .

title: Great Reflecting Pool
description: Great Reflecting Pool The Great Reflecting Pool was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Rumors and Legends . Accessible only from the Public Gardens , the reflecting pool was believed to have mystical properties .
description_long: Great Reflecting Pool The Great Reflecting Pool was part of the complex of the Palace of the Enlightened Throne in Huzuz in 1367 DR . Rumors and Legends . Accessible only from the Public Gardens , the reflecting pool was believed to have mystical properties . If visited on a crystal clear day , a visitor with a precise question might see the answer within the waters of the pool . Some even believed that the water reflected the nature of a person ' soul . Though the reflecting pool did indeed posses magical qualities , the soul reflection was actually an elaborate prank set in place by Ambassador Jiraad . Jiraad placed spells at popular viewing locations around the pool , showing different images to viewers at random intervals . Inhabitants . The pool was maintained and guarded by a pair of marid who lived under the water .

title: Great Rift
description: Great Rift The Great Rift is the traditional home of Faerûn ' s gold dwarves , though there is also a human city nearby , called Khôltar . The country of 1 , 300 , 000 dwarves , gnome s , halfling s and humans is ruled by a monarchy from the capital of Eartheart . Geography .
description_long: Great Rift The Great Rift is the traditional home of Faerûn ' s gold dwarves , though there is also a human city nearby , called Khôltar . The country of 1 , 300 , 000 dwarves , gnome s , halfling s and humans is ruled by a monarchy from the capital of Eartheart . Geography . The wide canyon known as the Great Rift lies near the western end of the Eastern Shaar , not far from the Landrise . The bottom of this chasm lies more than 1 , 000 feet below the plains , surrounded by sheer cliff walls on every side . The arid , hilly ground that serves as the floor of the Great Rift is split down the middle by the Riftlake , a deep , icy - cold body of clear water that is often shrouded in morning mists . The lake is fed by the numerous small streams and rivers that flow throughout the Great Rift , as well as some very deep springs , which rumors suggest are fed by portal s from the Elemental Plane of Water . The lake in turn drains into the River Shaar , which snakes along the valley floor before disappearing into a spray - filled gorge on the north end of the canyon .

title: Great Spire of the Ice Sea
description: Great Spire of the Ice Sea The Great Spire of the Ice Sea was a giant structure found on an uncharted island located near the middle of Yal Tengri . Geography . This cold , desolate place was windy around the year .
description_long: Great Spire of the Ice Sea The Great Spire of the Ice Sea was a giant structure found on an uncharted island located near the middle of Yal Tengri . Geography . This cold , desolate place was windy around the year . Scant vegetation grew on the island . Description . A lone towering spire jutted upward from the island ' s surface , appearing like a tower from a great cathedral . The spire was visible from anywhere on the island . The spire sparkled in the sun , and sailors used this landmark when sailing the frigid waters nearby . History . The Great Spire was the work of gnomish engineers . A small group of gnomes who worshiped Gond lived on the island in half - buried communities around the base of the spire . The gnomes busied themselves with constructing the special glass used to maintain the spire . The gnomes believed an ancient prophecy that stated that the world would be returned to the glory of Gond when the spire was completed . This ancient prophecy was lost after the time of the Raumathar empire , but was rediscovered during the 11th century DR .

title: Great Swamp of Rethild
description: Great Swamp of Rethild The Great Swamp of Rethild , also known simply as the Great Swamp or Rethild , was a swamp in Dambrath . Geography . The Great Swamp was located on the western border of Dambrath .
description_long: Great Swamp of Rethild The Great Swamp of Rethild , also known simply as the Great Swamp or Rethild , was a swamp in Dambrath . Geography . The Great Swamp was located on the western border of Dambrath . It was separated from Halruaa by the East Wall mountains . Description . The Great Swamp was filled with moss , cypress trees , and zalantar trees . It was always muggy and full of biting insects . Noxious vapors came up through the water and hung above the ground in great clouds of yellow , brown , or green gas . Some of these gases were poisonous or carried diseases , such as cackle fever and mindfire . History . The Great Swamp was cursed by an ancient wizard . It was once home to a city of sarrukh s . In 1372 DR , the lizardfolk were united in the kingdom of Kethid under the ruler Ghassis . A hundred years later , they called their kingdom Ilimar . Inhabitants . The Great Swamp was home to numerous tribes of lizardfolk , bullywug s , and tasloi , as well as giant leeches , toads , and snakes . The black dragon Valraxxath dwelt in the center of the swamp in a ruined city . Shambling mound s could also be found in the swamp .

title: Great Vale
description: Great Vale The Great Vale , also known as Asanibis , was considered the breadbasket of Mulhorand , and included the lands that lie between the Dragonsword Mountains and the Alamber Sea . Geography . The area that made up the Great Vale accounted for the majority of Mulhorand ' s farmland .
description_long: Great Vale The Great Vale , also known as Asanibis , was considered the breadbasket of Mulhorand , and included the lands that lie between the Dragonsword Mountains and the Alamber Sea . Geography . The area that made up the Great Vale accounted for the majority of Mulhorand ' s farmland . The region was heavily irrigated , and the annual flooding of the River of Spears provided the soil with an infusion of sediment on a regular basis . Inhabitants . The population of the Great Vale was composed primarily of humans . The majority of these individuals made their homes in the towns of Surbroar , Klondor , Ulzel , and Mishtan , though a fair number resided at the farms of the region . Rumors also indicated that intelligent storms known as Skriaxit may have once been found in the area around Klondor .

title: Great Wheel cosmology
description: Great Wheel cosmology Great Wheel is the cosmology model in which the world of Toril was said to exist during the first and second editions of the " Advanced Dungeons & Dragons " game , although the actual term " Great Wheel " didn ' t mean the cosmology as a whole until the 3rd edition of the " D & D " game and its " Manual of the Planes 3rd edition " . In second edition , " Great Wheel " or " Great Ring " meant the Outer planes only . The cosmology as a whole didn ' t require a name other than " the Planes " or " the Multiverse , " as there weren ' t any formally named alternatives in the " AD & D " game .
description_long: Great Wheel cosmology Great Wheel is the cosmology model in which the world of Toril was said to exist during the first and second editions of the " Advanced Dungeons & Dragons " game , although the actual term " Great Wheel " didn ' t mean the cosmology as a whole until the 3rd edition of the " D & D " game and its " Manual of the Planes 3rd edition " . In second edition , " Great Wheel " or " Great Ring " meant the Outer planes only . The cosmology as a whole didn ' t require a name other than " the Planes " or " the Multiverse , " as there weren ' t any formally named alternatives in the " AD & D " game . Ed Greenwood created the Faerûnian pantheon by choosing deities from the first edition " Deities & Demigods " book , sometimes renaming and modifying them , with the aim of ending up with one deity for every Outer plane or Outer planar layer in what we now call the Great Wheel cosmology . In this sense , the Faerûnian pantheon was created with the Great Wheel in mind .

title: Great Worm Cavern
description: Great Worm Cavern Great Worm cavern , the traditional ancestor mound of the Great Worm tribe , was said to reside at the base of a mountain in the Spine of the World range , part of a vast underground complex . Given great reference by the tribes through the lineage of Uthgar ' s still living son , Elrem the Wise . Little is known of the inside of the caves but stories abound of a large altar depicting stylised represntations of a great spiralling winged snake .
description_long: Great Worm Cavern Great Worm cavern , the traditional ancestor mound of the Great Worm tribe , was said to reside at the base of a mountain in the Spine of the World range , part of a vast underground complex . Given great reference by the tribes through the lineage of Uthgar ' s still living son , Elrem the Wise . Little is known of the inside of the caves but stories abound of a large altar depicting stylised represntations of a great spiralling winged snake . The adventurer Athelyare spoke tales that the caves connection with other parts of the Underdark such as lost Gauntlgrym .

title: Great galley
description: Great galley A great galley was a large ship used for both war and commerce on the Sea of Fallen Stars , primarily by the nations of Chessenta and Mulhorand . Description . The great galley was an improvement on the design of the dromond , having more sails and fewer oars and rowers .
description_long: Great galley A great galley was a large ship used for both war and commerce on the Sea of Fallen Stars , primarily by the nations of Chessenta and Mulhorand . Description . The great galley was an improvement on the design of the dromond , having more sails and fewer oars and rowers . It was about 130 ft ( 40 m ) along the keel and 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) across the beam , with three masts and 140 rowers . Under sail , the minimum crew size was 40 . When fully loaded for war , the maximum crew size including rowers was 200 . The great galley had a higher sailing speed and better maneuvering ability than the dromond , but could not match the dromond ' s speed when all oarsmen were engaged . When used for war , a ram was built into the bow and up to three large weapons ( such as catapults or ballistae ) could be mounted fore , aft , and amidships . The great galley was not particularly seaworthy and its large crew size and cramped quarters usually kept them close to shore .

title: Great ghul
description: Great ghul Great ghuls were undead cousins of genie s who occupied the lowest rung in the hierarchy of the jann . Description . Great ghuls had one interesting feature — their feet were always donkey hooves , although they often tried to hide this shortcoming by wearing long robes or boots .
description_long: Great ghul Great ghuls were undead cousins of genie s who occupied the lowest rung in the hierarchy of the jann . Description . Great ghuls had one interesting feature — their feet were always donkey hooves , although they often tried to hide this shortcoming by wearing long robes or boots . Ghuls adored eating the flesh from corpses and then drinking the bone marrow . They often had long hair and bushy eyebrows . They had clawed fingers and well developed muscles . Their white skin was always sticky and cold . Great ghuls knew that their looks were repulsive , so they often tried to hide their ugliness with lush " sarafans " and jewelry . Combat . Great ghuls attacked enemies with sharp claws and teeth . Only magical weapons could injure or kill a great ghul . Great ghul magicians were much more dangerous than their simple relatives . Great ghuls could use various spell s including " bestow invisibility " , " polymorph self " , and " shocking grasp " . Being undead , great ghuls had a special immunity to poison and many mind - affecting spells . They were much weaker during the daytime than at night and could be injured with holy water . Habitat / Society .

title: Great revenance
description: Great revenance Great revenance was a spell researched by Irae T ' sarran that could raise an army of revenant s slaved to the caster ' s will . Effects . The magic of this spell could potentially animate thousands of creatures as revenant s under the command of the caster .
description_long: Great revenance Great revenance was a spell researched by Irae T ' sarran that could raise an army of revenant s slaved to the caster ' s will . Effects . The magic of this spell could potentially animate thousands of creatures as revenant s under the command of the caster . The undead horde would retain the capabilities each creature had in life but also bring them under a shared will . However , this unifying power could only be achieved if used in conjunction with a potent source of negative energy , such as that projected by the Undying Temple in Maerimydra . Components . For the " great revenance " spell to perform as it was originally intended , it required the empowering negative energy of the Undying Temple and a great number of recently deceased bodies . History . In 1372 DR , on Marpenoth 2 , Irae T ' sarran began researching the " great revenance " spell under Kiaransalee ' s guidance in Maerimydra . Irae summoned the Undying Temple to Castle Maerimydra on Marpenoth 17 and moved her spell research there . By Marpenoth 27 , she was devoting most of her time to developing the spell and had made plans to use the spell on the Dalelands above .

title: Great shout
description: Great shout Great shout was an arcane evocation spell that produced a tremendous sonic force similar to a " horn of blasting " from the mouth of the caster . Effects . There were at least two distinct versions of this spell .
description_long: Great shout Great shout was an arcane evocation spell that produced a tremendous sonic force similar to a " horn of blasting " from the mouth of the caster . Effects . There were at least two distinct versions of this spell . The original , presumably invented by a wizard named Daimos , was dangerous to the caster , requiring some of his or her own vitality in the casting , with possibly fatal results . It also required an item that radiated magic as a material component . A later version was much less taxing , did more damage , had a bigger area of effect , and only needed an arcane focus ( which was not consumed in the casting ) . " Great shout " had two areas of effect , one inside the other . The primary area of devastation was a narrow corridor emanating straight out from the caster . The secondary region of sonic punishment also emanated from the caster in the same direction as the primary but was in the shape of a widening cone that surrounded the primary on both sides . For the earliest version of the spell , the primary area was only 1 ft ( 30 cm ) wide by 8 ft ( 2 . 4 m ) long , while the later version had a 5 ft ( 1 .

title: Great shout ( evocation )
description: Great shout ( evocation ) Great shout was a barbarian evocation that briefly hindered the attacking ability of foes . Effects . Upon a successful hit , a barbarian could tap into the rage of his or her ancestors and give a furious battle cry .
description_long: Great shout ( evocation ) Great shout was a barbarian evocation that briefly hindered the attacking ability of foes . Effects . Upon a successful hit , a barbarian could tap into the rage of his or her ancestors and give a furious battle cry . All enemies within 25 ft ( 7 . 6 m ) were intimidated and their next attack was less skillful because of this temporary lack of conviction .

title: Greataxe
description: Greataxe A greataxe is a double - bladed , two - handed melee weapon in the axe family . Description . The greataxe is a large , heavy battleaxe with a double - bladed head .
description_long: Greataxe A greataxe is a double - bladed , two - handed melee weapon in the axe family . Description . The greataxe is a large , heavy battleaxe with a double - bladed head . The haft is usually stout wood and longer than even a dwarven waraxe . The grip is about half the length of the haft . The greataxe weighs about twice as much as a regular battleaxe . An average greataxe costs 20gp and weighs 12lbs ( 5 . 5kg ) . Use . Barbarians tend to favor the greataxe for the tremendous amount of damage it can deliver . Wielded two - handed , the double blades allow an alternating forward / backswing attack with devastating results . It requires some training to use the greataxe effectively , therefore this is classified as a martial weapon .

title: Greatclub
description: Greatclub The greatclub , a two - handed version of the club , is a martial melee weapon . Description . A greatclub is bigger and heavier than a regular club and usually augmented with spikes , nails and / or bands of iron .
description_long: Greatclub The greatclub , a two - handed version of the club , is a martial melee weapon . Description . A greatclub is bigger and heavier than a regular club and usually augmented with spikes , nails and / or bands of iron . An average greatclub costs 5gp and weighs 8lbs ( 3 . 6kg ) . Weaponology . The greatclub is classified as a two - handed martial weapon because the extra weight and the spikes make it a bit more difficult to wield without hurting yourself or your allies . The greatclub is not listed in the 1st or 2nd edition player handbooks .

title: Greater command
description: Greater command Greater command was an arcane evocation spell that compelled multiple subjects to follow a single order as long as they were given in a language they understood . Effect . This spell functioned in the same manner as " command " , except that more creatures could be affected and the effects lasted longer .
description_long: Greater command Greater command was an arcane evocation spell that compelled multiple subjects to follow a single order as long as they were given in a language they understood . Effect . This spell functioned in the same manner as " command " , except that more creatures could be affected and the effects lasted longer . Components . Only verbal components were necessary to cast this spell .

title: Greater dispelling
description: Greater dispelling Greater dispelling was an abjuration spell that dispelled magic . Effects . This spell functioned in the same manner as " dispel magic " , except that the maximum bonus on the dispel check was + 20 instead of + 10 .
description_long: Greater dispelling Greater dispelling was an abjuration spell that dispelled magic . Effects . This spell functioned in the same manner as " dispel magic " , except that the maximum bonus on the dispel check was + 20 instead of + 10 . Additionally , " greater dispelling " had a chance to dispel any effect that " remove curse " could remove , even if " dispel magic " couldn ' t dispel that effect .

title: Greater fantastic machine
description: Greater fantastic machine Greater fantastic machine was an illusion spell exclusive to cleric s with the Craft domain . It called into being a large illusory mechanical contraption that was controlled by the caster to perform simple tasks . Effect .
description_long: Greater fantastic machine Greater fantastic machine was an illusion spell exclusive to cleric s with the Craft domain . It called into being a large illusory mechanical contraption that was controlled by the caster to perform simple tasks . Effect . The machine was imposingly large and noisy , with wheels and many arms with tool appendages , and was constructed of adamantine to be extremely tough and strong . The machine could roll on its wheels , swim , or fly . The movement speed was as fast as an unencumbered human on land but one third the rate when swimming or flying . The maximum load it could carry was 1 , 560 lb ( 709 kg ) on land and one third that amount when swimming or flying . Standing still , it could lift double its maximum load to a height of 15 ft ( 4 . 6 m ) . It could push or drag a 7 , 800 lb ( 3 , 550 kg ) load over land . It could also excavate a 5 ft ( 1 . 5 m ) cube of rock and dirt ( about 20 , 000 lb or 9 , 100 kg worth ) in one minute . The machine was similar to an " animated object " and could perform simple tasks autonomously or have each movement controlled by the caster .

title: Greater glyph of warding
description: Greater glyph of warding Greater glyph of warding is an abjuration spell that creates a glyph that causes damage when triggered . Effect . This spell functions in the same manner as " glyph of warding " , except that the blast deals up to 10d8 damage , and the " greater glyph " can store a harmful spell of up to 6th level .
description_long: Greater glyph of warding Greater glyph of warding is an abjuration spell that creates a glyph that causes damage when triggered . Effect . This spell functions in the same manner as " glyph of warding " , except that the blast deals up to 10d8 damage , and the " greater glyph " can store a harmful spell of up to 6th level . Material Component . Diamond dust worth at least 400 gp .

title: Greater invisibility
description: Greater invisibility Greater invisibility or improved invisibility was an illusion spell that functioned exactly like " invisibility " except the recipient could attack and not break the spell . History . The spell was attributed to the Netherese arcanist Pockall in - 1478 DR and was known then as " Pockall ' s invisibility plus " .
description_long: Greater invisibility Greater invisibility or improved invisibility was an illusion spell that functioned exactly like " invisibility " except the recipient could attack and not break the spell . History . The spell was attributed to the Netherese arcanist Pockall in - 1478 DR and was known then as " Pockall ' s invisibility plus " .

title: Greater ironguard
description: Greater ironguard Greater ironguard was an arcane abjuration spell that temporarily granted one creature immunity from all non - magical metals and some enchanted metals . It was an improved version of " ironguard " . Effects .
description_long: Greater ironguard Greater ironguard was an arcane abjuration spell that temporarily granted one creature immunity from all non - magical metals and some enchanted metals . It was an improved version of " ironguard " . Effects . The effects of this spell were the same as for " lesser ironguard " except that it also granted immunity and transparency to metals that had been enchanted up to a certain degree . Components . In addition to the verbal , somatic , and material components required for " lesser ironguard " , this spell needed an arcane focus in the form of a small piece of raw adamantine costing about 100 gp .

title: Greater planar ally
description: Greater planar ally Greater planar ally was a conjuration spell that called up to three outsider s or elemental s from their home plane to aid the caster in exchange for payment . Effect . This spell functioned in the same manner as " lesser planar ally " , except that the caster could call three such creatures , or two somewhat larger creatures , or one very large creature .
description_long: Greater planar ally Greater planar ally was a conjuration spell that called up to three outsider s or elemental s from their home plane to aid the caster in exchange for payment . Effect . This spell functioned in the same manner as " lesser planar ally " , except that the caster could call three such creatures , or two somewhat larger creatures , or one very large creature . The creature ( s ) agreed to help the caster in return for payment or a favor . When a creature was called of the good , evil , chaotic , lawful , air , earth , fire , or water types , " greater planar ally " was a spell of that type . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a holy symbol or divine focus to cast . When cast , this spell stole a small portion of the caster ' s life experience .

title: Greater restoration
description: Greater restoration Greater restoration is a necromancy spell that completely heals the subject . Effect . This spell functions in the same manner as " lesser restoration " , except the spell dispels all negative levels afflicting the healed creature , restoring the creature to the highest level it had previously achieved .
description_long: Greater restoration Greater restoration is a necromancy spell that completely heals the subject . Effect . This spell functions in the same manner as " lesser restoration " , except the spell dispels all negative levels afflicting the healed creature , restoring the creature to the highest level it had previously achieved . This reverses level drains by a force or creature . The drained levels are restored only if the time since the creature lost the level is no more than 1 week per caster level . " Greater restoration " also dispels all magical effects penalizing the character ' s abilities , cures all temporary ability damage , and restores all points permanently drained from all ability scores . It also removes all forms of insanity , confusion , and similar mental effects . " Greater restoration " does not restore levels or Constitution points lost due to death . XP Cost . 500 XP .

title: Greater scrying
description: Greater scrying Greater scrying is a divination spell that spies on a subject from a distance . Effects . This spell functions in the same manner as " scrying " , except as noted above .
description_long: Greater scrying Greater scrying is a divination spell that spies on a subject from a distance . Effects . This spell functions in the same manner as " scrying " , except as noted above . All of the following spells can be cast reliably through the sensor : " comprehend languages " , " darkvision " , " detect chaos " , " detect evil " , " detect good " , " detect law " , " detect magic " , " message " , " read magic " , and " tongues " .

title: Greater spell immunity
description: Greater spell immunity Greater spell immunity , also known as Serten ' s spell immunity , was an abjuration spell that was identical to " spell immunity " except that it bestowed complete resistance against one or more particular spells , spell - like effects of magic items , or spell - like abilities of creatures of 8th level or below .
description_long: Greater spell immunity Greater spell immunity , also known as Serten ' s spell immunity , was an abjuration spell that was identical to " spell immunity " except that it bestowed complete resistance against one or more particular spells , spell - like effects of magic items , or spell - like abilities of creatures of 8th level or below .

title: Greater touchsickle
description: Greater touchsickle Greater touchsickle was a divine magic spell available to druid s , cleric s , and crusader s of Eldath , the Mother Guardian of Groves . It was a more potent version of " touchsickle " . Effects .
description_long: Greater touchsickle Greater touchsickle was a divine magic spell available to druid s , cleric s , and crusader s of Eldath , the Mother Guardian of Groves . It was a more potent version of " touchsickle " . Effects . This spell was identical to the " touchsickle " spell except that the caster ' s hand became a " sickle + 2 " that could damage any and all creatures that were immune to normal weapons . The duration of " greater touchsickle " was eighteen minutes , with more experienced casters able to extend this time limit . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell . Users . Peacemen and peacewomen , the specialty priests of Eldath , were not granted this spell . For druids , the " touchsickle " was equivalent to a gold en or silver sickle for the purpose of harvesting mistletoe at its greatest potency .

title: Greatsword
description: Greatsword A greatsword is a two - handed , martial , melee weapon . Description . The greatsword is the largest member of the sword family requiring two hands to wield .
description_long: Greatsword A greatsword is a two - handed , martial , melee weapon . Description . The greatsword is the largest member of the sword family requiring two hands to wield . The hilt is elongated to accommodate the extra grip and the blade is doubled - edged . Some versions have parrying hooks ( " Parierhaken " ) on the blade about 4 - 8in ( 10 - 20cm ) away from the guard . The blade is dull between the parrying hooks and the guard so it can be gripped there . An average greatsword costs 50gp and weighs 8lbs ( 3 . 6kg ) . Weaponology . The greatsword is large and heavy for a sword , and takes good training to wield effectively , therefore it is classified as a martial weapon . Greatswords with the parrying hooks may be gripped with one hand between the hooks and the guard and the other on the hilt , allowing this weapon to be used in pole arm fashion . The greatsword is recognized by adventurers as a reliable , powerful weapon .

title: Greed domain
description: Greed domain The Greed domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters greed spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Exalted Deeds " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Greed Domain Powers .
description_long: Greed domain The Greed domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters greed spell powers . It originated in the " Book of Exalted Deeds " , and was added to the Forgotten Realms setting by the " Player ' s Guide to Faerûn " . Greed Domain Powers . The cleric gains skill at appraising and picking locks and pockets .

title: Green Calishite cheese
description: Green Calishite cheese Green Calishite was a spicy cheese crafted in Calimshan . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description .
description_long: Green Calishite cheese Green Calishite was a spicy cheese crafted in Calimshan . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description . The Calishites added curry to give this cheese some extra kick while preserving it at the same time . The spice also added a greenish tint to the cheese . Prices . Green Calishite cheese could be purchased in the following sizes :

title: Green Fields
description: Green Fields Green Fields was the celestial home of the halfling pantheon . It was also the home of the souls of deceased good halflings . Description .
description_long: Green Fields Green Fields was the celestial home of the halfling pantheon . It was also the home of the souls of deceased good halflings . Description . As its name aptly implied , Green Fields consisted of a green field expanding ever outward in every direction . It was home to winged halflings . History . In 1372 DR , Gromph Baenre unintentionally visited the Green Fields during a spell battle with the Lichdrow Dyrr . Notable inhabitants . Dietr was a halfling from Luiren who dwelt in Green Fields after his death . When Gromph left the plane , he saw an opportunity to return to Faerûn to help his mother and followed the drow back to Menzoberranzan , where he was promptly turned into an undead huecuva . Gromph had no sympathy for Dietr and forced him to go up against the Lichdrow ; Dietr was easily destroyed .

title: Green Folk
description: Green Folk The Green Folk were one of the four basic people groups of Maztica , living in the low jungles south of the desert known as the House of Tezca . Description . The Green Folk were short like the Payit .
description_long: Green Folk The Green Folk were one of the four basic people groups of Maztica , living in the low jungles south of the desert known as the House of Tezca . Description . The Green Folk were short like the Payit . They were dexterous but not overly strong . Personality . As a rule , the Green Folk were private people . In fact , few who entered their forests were ever seen again . They would shoot first with their arrows and ask questions later . However , it was possible to impress them with displays of supernatural power . Society . The Green Folk were organized into separate villages and did not have a nation of their own although the nation of Kolan , which was found on the western coast of Maztica , included inhabitants of Green Folk stock . These villages were scattered through the jungles of the Southern Wilds . Religion . The Green Folk worshiped gods of nature , such as Maztica , Nula , Qotal , or Watil , but they did not practice human sacrifice . Combat . They were highly skilled in the use of bow and arrow , and they often tipped their arrows with kurari poison . When they took prisoners , they only rarely let them live .

title: Green Goddess Falls
description: Green Goddess Falls The Green Goddess Falls were a series of waterfalls in Amn . Description . The Falls were part of the River Rimril , as its waters flowed out of the Troll Mountains .
description_long: Green Goddess Falls The Green Goddess Falls were a series of waterfalls in Amn . Description . The Falls were part of the River Rimril , as its waters flowed out of the Troll Mountains . The largest of the falls was 400 feet ( 120 meters ) in height and poured over the cliffs on the west side of Eldath ' s Mount and into Duskwood Dell . Afterward , the waters continued cascading in a number of smaller falls and pools called the Steps .

title: Green Imsa
description: Green Imsa Green Imsa was a traveler just before the Tyranny of Dragons . Personality . Imsa was a quiet and friendly individual .
description_long: Green Imsa Green Imsa was a traveler just before the Tyranny of Dragons . Personality . Imsa was a quiet and friendly individual . She became frustrated if people bothered her about her condition . History . Imsa was a human who was afflicted with an unknown condition that turned her skin , eyes , hair , teeth , and nails green . At the start of the Tyranny of Dragons , in 1489 DR Imsa sought to travel to Waterdeep in search of a cure for herself . She boarded a great caravan , which unknown to her was full of Cult of the Dragon agents transporting treasures for the Hoard of the Dragon Queen .

title: Green Lady
description: Green Lady " The Lady " or " The Green Lady " was a female human druid and follower of Eldath who lived in the Brynwood forest in the Vast in the 1350s and 1360s DR . History . Going by her age , the Lady was born around 1289 DR .
description_long: Green Lady " The Lady " or " The Green Lady " was a female human druid and follower of Eldath who lived in the Brynwood forest in the Vast in the 1350s and 1360s DR . History . Going by her age , the Lady was born around 1289 DR . Both her real name and her history were unknown to others , and she was known only as the Lady or the Green Lady for many years . It was known , however , that she settled in the Misty Vale in Brynwood in the Vast around 1349 DR , where she went into semi - retirement and lived in seclusion . On 28th Eleasias of the Year of the Gauntlet , 1369 DR , Dura Gerathu , a ranger friend of the Lady , visited her to tell how he ' d discovered the Vipers ' Nest . She advised him to watch the place longer and learn all he could , but this led to Dura being murdered by the Vipers bandits . The bandits followed Dura ' s writings and came after the Lady next . Forewarned by the sprites she lived with , she conjured obscuring mists and illusory forests to drive the terrified bandits off . Calispar Delgorth , the leader of the assault , vowed to return and finish her later . Afterwards , the Lady sent two sprites to check on Dura , who reported his death .

title: Green Lady ' s Keep
description: Green Lady ' s Keep The Green Lady ' s Keep was a long , low temple to Chauntea in Velprintalar , Aglarond . History . In 1368 DR , the abbey included a granary where twelve monks were led by Abbot Dalmar .
description_long: Green Lady ' s Keep The Green Lady ' s Keep was a long , low temple to Chauntea in Velprintalar , Aglarond . History . In 1368 DR , the abbey included a granary where twelve monks were led by Abbot Dalmar . By 1374 DR , the monks had increased in number to over one hundred . Inhabitants . The monks worked to produce a green ale said to include fermented , which was one of the city ' s most popular exports .

title: Green Regent
description: Green Regent The Green Regent enjoyed many of the abilities of a Chosen of Mielikki . Their powers however , were limited to a period of four years — from Shieldmeet to Shieldmeet ( unless of course the Regent was killed in the meantime ) . The Green Regent was tasked with the protection of Mielikki ' s Dream : the perfect balance between civilization and nature that was found in the Delimbiyr Crescent .
description_long: Green Regent The Green Regent enjoyed many of the abilities of a Chosen of Mielikki . Their powers however , were limited to a period of four years — from Shieldmeet to Shieldmeet ( unless of course the Regent was killed in the meantime ) . The Green Regent was tasked with the protection of Mielikki ' s Dream : the perfect balance between civilization and nature that was found in the Delimbiyr Crescent . The city of Loudwater and its environs — built on the fringes of the High Forest — became dear to the goddess while she maintained a home on the Material Plane and continued to be so after she left it to join her fellow nature deities in the House of Nature after the Time of Troubles .

title: Green Shield
description: Green Shield In the Heralds of Faerûn organization , the office of Green Shield was one of two unique positions ( Gauntlet being the other one ) that were temporary . While most Herald offices were a lifetime appointment , Green Shield was given a four - year term that began and ended just before consecutive Shieldmeet s . Green Shield presided over the particular quadrennial festival at which was convened the Heralds ' Round — an open court wherein the High Heralds publicly spoke and voted on various aspects of Herald business .
description_long: Green Shield In the Heralds of Faerûn organization , the office of Green Shield was one of two unique positions ( Gauntlet being the other one ) that were temporary . While most Herald offices were a lifetime appointment , Green Shield was given a four - year term that began and ended just before consecutive Shieldmeet s . Green Shield presided over the particular quadrennial festival at which was convened the Heralds ' Round — an open court wherein the High Heralds publicly spoke and voted on various aspects of Herald business . Green Shield was responsible for the docket of the Round as well as most other aspects of the Shieldmeet : seeing the rituals were properly performed , the organization , logistics , and scheduling of events were carried out , security provided for the distinguished attendees , proper precedence observed , and all of it done with diplomacy . For the next four years , Green Shield followed up on any business conducted that day , consulted with the High Heralds , and prepared for the next Shieldmeet . This office was usually filled from the ranks of the Heralds Pursuivant and never by a sitting High Herald .

title: Green Sirene
description: Green Sirene The Green Sirene was an inn in the city of Tantras in the Vast . Location . The Green Sirene lay on Whistleturn War , close to the Market in the center of the city .
description_long: Green Sirene The Green Sirene was an inn in the city of Tantras in the Vast . Location . The Green Sirene lay on Whistleturn War , close to the Market in the center of the city . Description . It was a good - quality establishment with moderate prices and favored by sailors . History . During the Time of Troubles of the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR , the Green Sirene was commandeered by the Tantran navy . They used it as a barracks and a recruiting post .

title: Green Sword
description: Green Sword The Green Sword was a tavern in Leuthilspar , Evermeet . Description . The establishment took its name from an extremely heavy green metal sword mounted behind the counter , which supposedly belonged to a green dragon .
description_long: Green Sword The Green Sword was a tavern in Leuthilspar , Evermeet . Description . The establishment took its name from an extremely heavy green metal sword mounted behind the counter , which supposedly belonged to a green dragon . It was too heavy for most medium humanoid s to lift . Atmosphere . The tavern was more rowdy than the norm for elven taverns . History . In 1367 DR , the proprietor was Halanaestra .

title: Green dragon
description: Green dragon Green dragons are master manipulators who revel in corrupting lesser creatures and hoarding them like possessions . Physical description . Green dragons are most notable for the large , waving crest or fin that starts at the dragon ' s nose and runs the entire length of the dragon ' s body .
description_long: Green dragon Green dragons are master manipulators who revel in corrupting lesser creatures and hoarding them like possessions . Physical description . Green dragons are most notable for the large , waving crest or fin that starts at the dragon ' s nose and runs the entire length of the dragon ' s body . They also have exceptionally long , slender forked tongues . Breath weapon . Green dragons expel a cone of corrosive chlorine gas . Personality . These dragons love intrigue and secrets . They put up a front of diplomacy and deceit when dealing with stronger foes , but they reveal their cruel and petty nature when intimidating lesser beings or when gaining the upper hand . They delight in stalking their enemies and listening in for any information they can gather before moving to attack . Green dragons especially enjoy corrupting or consuming elves and fey creatures . Ecology . Society . Green dragons value their territory , but only as a means to gain as much power as possible without expending considerable effort . They will sometimes trade safe passage for a worthy item to add to their hoards .

title: Green hag
description: Green hag Green hags , also known as swamp hags and river hags , use their magical powers to lure innocents into their traps . They will assume the form of beautiful women and enter a populated area to find a young man or woman to corrupt with vices . They will use their ability to mimic animal noises to lure children into the swamp , where they are captured and devoured .
description_long: Green hag Green hags , also known as swamp hags and river hags , use their magical powers to lure innocents into their traps . They will assume the form of beautiful women and enter a populated area to find a young man or woman to corrupt with vices . They will use their ability to mimic animal noises to lure children into the swamp , where they are captured and devoured . Description . A green hag is about the same height and weight as a female human . They appear to be ugly crones with twisted bodies and wretched features . Their mouths are filled with rotten teeth , often coming to points which are used to eat humanoid flesh . Their fingers end in long , blackened claws . Lair . Green hags are horrible , cruel , fey - like women found in desolate swamps and dark forests . They delight in destroying beauty and purity , wanting to match it to their own ugly , debased selves . Locations . Green hags were found in Ashanath , the North Country , the Forest of Lethyr , and the Yuirwood in the Unapproachable East .

title: Green slaad
description: Green slaad Green slaadi were unusually intelligent slaad shapechangers and spellcasters . Description . Green slaadi appeared as the result of an infection of a humanoid spellcaster by a red slaad egg or a blue slaad ' s chaos phage .
description_long: Green slaad Green slaadi were unusually intelligent slaad shapechangers and spellcasters . Description . Green slaadi appeared as the result of an infection of a humanoid spellcaster by a red slaad egg or a blue slaad ' s chaos phage . If the infected humanoid could cast sufficiently powerful spell s , instead of a red or blue slaad , a green slaad appeared . Beside their spellcasting abilities , green slaadi were also shapechangers and could assume the form of other humanoids . They usually chose to assume the form of their former hosts . After some time , a green slaad could learn how to magically transform permanently into the stronger gray slaad . Learning this process could take decades .

title: Green sleeping dust
description: Green sleeping dust Green sleeping dust was a drug that caused a creature to fall asleep . It was made from parts of the bija tree , which was found in the Quang Muku Forest in Koryo , Kara - Tur . It was incredibly potent — a person who inhaled the dust could not resist falling asleep .
description_long: Green sleeping dust Green sleeping dust was a drug that caused a creature to fall asleep . It was made from parts of the bija tree , which was found in the Quang Muku Forest in Koryo , Kara - Tur . It was incredibly potent — a person who inhaled the dust could not resist falling asleep . Around 1357 DR , its main users were ninja in service to the Soretyo family of Foo Nakar , a city within the Quang Muku . Some merchants with illicit dealings could purchase it as well , though it was very expensive . Green sleeping dust may have been used by the " nameless ones " — ninja — who kidnapped Meo Li around 1350 DR . She recalled a " magic powder " , blown like a " puff of smoke " in her face , and knew nothing more .

title: Green warder
description: Green warder Green warders were plant creature s programmed by elves to guard their woodland secrets . Description . Green warders were humanoid - shaped topiary bushes pruned to look like tall elves , but if untended , they grew bushy and scraggly .
description_long: Green warder Green warders were plant creature s programmed by elves to guard their woodland secrets . Description . Green warders were humanoid - shaped topiary bushes pruned to look like tall elves , but if untended , they grew bushy and scraggly . They bore sharp thorns on their forearms for defense , if needed . Behavior . Green warders had limited intelligence and minimal personalities . They were generally peaceful and benign beings and only in extreme circumstances would they shed blood , even if directly ordered to do so . Combat . Warders were generally programmed to avoid shedding blood ; their purpose was to guard . If intruders approached , they would first raise an alarm and then use their magical powers to confuse the invaders or send them into a deep sleep until elven reinforcements could arrive . If under attack , a green warder would typically flee but if trapped could use its thorns to defend itself . History . When the elves left Cormanthor during the Retreat , thousands of green warders were left behind , guarding the old sacred sites .

title: Greenest
description: Greenest Greenest was the only sizable town along the Uldoon Trail in the Greenfields area of the Western Heartlands . Ravenforge . A respected group of mercenaries whose ideals and aims are unknown to many .
description_long: Greenest Greenest was the only sizable town along the Uldoon Trail in the Greenfields area of the Western Heartlands . Ravenforge . A respected group of mercenaries whose ideals and aims are unknown to many . The organization was founded by the House Amberarms , a family of dwarves that found residency in the small village . They hold the largest forge and weapons trading post in town that was coincidentally named Raven Forge . The family fought against dragons and their cults for ages that eventually lead to their demise . History . The mercenary group was almost wiped out after the attack of the Cult of the Dragon . The entire Amberarms and their mercenaries were slain , but one managed to survive . Hiding behind the name , " Big Boss , " he slowly rebuilt the group by recruiting creatures of all shape and sizes that he met during their adventures . Now the group has expanded their connection to almost every corner of the Northern Swordcoast . They have been slowly expanding ever since .

title: Greenfields ( Unther )
description: Greenfields ( Unther ) Greenfields or the Green Lands was a region of Unther , and later Tymanther , < ref name = " AotT / Hardcover - p248 " > < / ref > south of the River Alamber and including the River Angol . It was considered the breadbasket of Unther , and later Tymanther , with many productive farms .
description_long: Greenfields ( Unther ) Greenfields or the Green Lands was a region of Unther , and later Tymanther , < ref name = " AotT / Hardcover - p248 " > < / ref > south of the River Alamber and including the River Angol . It was considered the breadbasket of Unther , and later Tymanther , with many productive farms .

title: Greenflame blade
description: Greenflame blade Greenflame blade is a transmutation spell most often used by assault swordmages , though swordmage s of other styles are also known to cast it . When cast " greenflame blade " ignites the swordmage ' s weapon with viridian flames , which add to the deadliness of the swordmage ' s attacks for an instant . " Greenflame blade " , which can be cast at will uses the swordmage ' s intellect and physical strength as the basis for its power , though a swordmage of greater experience will cast a significantly more powerful version of the spell .
description_long: Greenflame blade Greenflame blade is a transmutation spell most often used by assault swordmages , though swordmage s of other styles are also known to cast it . When cast " greenflame blade " ignites the swordmage ' s weapon with viridian flames , which add to the deadliness of the swordmage ' s attacks for an instant . " Greenflame blade " , which can be cast at will uses the swordmage ' s intellect and physical strength as the basis for its power , though a swordmage of greater experience will cast a significantly more powerful version of the spell .

title: Greengrass
description: Greengrass Greengrass was a festival to welcome in the first day of spring in the Calendar of Harptos . It occured annually on a special day between Tarsakh 30 and Mirtul 1 . Traditionally , the wealthier people brought out flowers to give to the less wealthy , who either wore them or spread them on the ground to encourage the deities to usher in the summer .
description_long: Greengrass Greengrass was a festival to welcome in the first day of spring in the Calendar of Harptos . It occured annually on a special day between Tarsakh 30 and Mirtul 1 . Traditionally , the wealthier people brought out flowers to give to the less wealthy , who either wore them or spread them on the ground to encourage the deities to usher in the summer .

title: Greenmeadow
description: Greenmeadow Greenmeadow was a grassy meadow north of Leuthilspar on the island of Evermeet . Geography . The meadow was separated from the city by the River Ardulith .
description_long: Greenmeadow Greenmeadow was a grassy meadow north of Leuthilspar on the island of Evermeet . Geography . The meadow was separated from the city by the River Ardulith .
