Heafstaag bore many wounds from his time on the harsh tundra . He had only one eye , lost to a reindeer ' s antler , and his left hand was left useless from an attack by a polar bear . He hated wizards , but nonetheless allied with Akar Kessel . History . Heafstaag was the son of Hrothulf the Strong and grandson of Angaar the Brave . His mother was a woman from Luskan who had been captured as a child during a caravan raid and who had been raised by the Tribe of the Elk . Heafstaag was seriously wounded by Drizzt in the battle of Ten Towns . When Akar Kessel fought against the Ten Towns , Heafstaag ' s tribe would have followed Kessel to battle but Wulfgar claimed the throne using the Right of Challenge and killed Heafstaag beforehand .

title: Heal
description: Heal Heal was a conjuration , evocation , or necromancy spell that cured many ailments and restored health . The reverse of this spell , harm , could drain health away , bringing a creature to near unconsciousness and death . Effects .
description_long: Heal Heal was a conjuration , evocation , or necromancy spell that cured many ailments and restored health . The reverse of this spell , harm , could drain health away , bringing a creature to near unconsciousness and death . Effects . The caster had to touch the recipient of this spell for it to work . The necromantic version of this spell restored a creature to full health , cured all diseases , restored sight , and cured mental disorders caused by brain injury or magic such as " feeblemind " . The conjuration version delivered a charge of positive energy that had an upper limit on how much health it could restore , but it also cured blindness , deafness , disease , insanity , poison , sickness of all sorts , and the effects of spells such as " confusion " , and " feeblemind " . If cast in reverse , " harm " brought a living creature to the brink of unconsciousness and inflicted a disease on the victim . If either version was successfully cast on an undead creature , it acted like the corresponding " harm " spell . Components . The spell needed only verbal and somatic components to be cast .

title: Healing candle
description: Healing candle A healing candle was a special magic item made my mystic s in the Realms . It healed the wounds of one individual . The longer the candle was allowed to burn , the more healing it could provide .
description_long: Healing candle A healing candle was a special magic item made my mystic s in the Realms . It healed the wounds of one individual . The longer the candle was allowed to burn , the more healing it could provide . Description . " Healing candles " were gold in color and intended to be burnt in ten - minute intervals . The longest - lasting candle that could be made burned for ninety minutes . This was the fourth type of candle mystics learned to make when studying candle magic . Powers . After burning for the desired amount of time and then being extinguished ( either by blowing , snuffing , dousing , or reaching the end of its wick ) , the creature that extinguished the candle or was closest to it when it went out received an amount of healing that , on average , was proportional to the length of time ( in ten - minute segments ) the candle burned . The recipient had to remain within ten feet ( three meters ) of the burning candle for the entire time it was lit and when it was extinguished , or that application of the " candle " was wasted . The healing effect only worked on beings that were susceptible to magical healing .

title: Healing hand
description: Healing hand Healing hand was a divine necromancy spell that boosted the healing provided by a previously cast healing spell . Effect . The " healing hand " spell supplied additional healing to a creature that had already been healed within the previous 24 hours .
description_long: Healing hand Healing hand was a divine necromancy spell that boosted the healing provided by a previously cast healing spell . Effect . The " healing hand " spell supplied additional healing to a creature that had already been healed within the previous 24 hours . If the intended recipient was not present , then the caster of " healing hand " could work with the caster of the previous healing spell , who concentrated on and visualized the recipient . Any on these three people could be the same if required . A full 48 hours was required before another casting of " healing hand " could be applied . Components . The spell required a scrap of skin and a sliver of bone , of any type , size , age , and species . History . The " healing hand " spell appeared within the " Tome of Torment " , the holiest book of the church of Ilmater , which first appeared in the Realms in 848 DR .

title: Healing sphere
description: Healing sphere The Healing sphere was a group of spells granted to cleric s , crusader s , and druid s without limitations , and to monk s and shaman s with minor access only . Spells in this sphere could cure or cause damage to health , but not bring beings back to life . Spells in normal text were listed in the Tome of Magic 2nd edition .
description_long: Healing sphere The Healing sphere was a group of spells granted to cleric s , crusader s , and druid s without limitations , and to monk s and shaman s with minor access only . Spells in this sphere could cure or cause damage to health , but not bring beings back to life . Spells in normal text were listed in the Tome of Magic 2nd edition . Spells in italics were added to the Healing Sphere in the sourcebook .

title: Healing word
description: Healing word Healing word was a healing spell or prayer cast by bard s , cleric s , and druid s . Among the most basic forms of magic al healing , " healing word " uses some of one creature ' s life force to heal said creature a small amount . This creature must be within a nearby area of twenty - five feet in diameter or the caster themselves .
description_long: Healing word Healing word was a healing spell or prayer cast by bard s , cleric s , and druid s . Among the most basic forms of magic al healing , " healing word " uses some of one creature ' s life force to heal said creature a small amount . This creature must be within a nearby area of twenty - five feet in diameter or the caster themselves . As a cleric grows in power and skill , the power of " healing word " increases , to as much as six times its initial utility . " Healing word " is fairly basic in casting and can be cast twice without the need for a short rest , though it requires a short " cool off " time of several seconds before it can be recast .

title: Heart of All Mountains
description: Heart of All Mountains The Heart of All Mountains comprised the bulk of the armed forces of the dao within the Great Dismal Delve . Organization . Nine thousand dao heavy infantry made up the Heart of All Mountains .
description_long: Heart of All Mountains The Heart of All Mountains comprised the bulk of the armed forces of the dao within the Great Dismal Delve . Organization . Nine thousand dao heavy infantry made up the Heart of All Mountains . Activities . The infantry was drilled and indoctrinated in loyalty to the Great Khan on a regular basis . The khan used them to deal with noble dao who troubled him . They also hunted down merchants who owed taxes . Base of Operations . The Sevenfold Mazework within the Great Dismal Delve served as base of all dao military organizations .

title: Heart of Wine
description: Heart of Wine Heart of Wine was a special alcoholic beverage found in Zakhara . It was made by aging wine in the desert heat or mountain snows until all of the water evaporated or froze , leaving behind a potent substance . As with all alcoholic drinks , Heart of Wine was forbidden in any area controlled by moralist s .
description_long: Heart of Wine Heart of Wine was a special alcoholic beverage found in Zakhara . It was made by aging wine in the desert heat or mountain snows until all of the water evaporated or froze , leaving behind a potent substance . As with all alcoholic drinks , Heart of Wine was forbidden in any area controlled by moralist s . Prices . A half gallon ( 1 . 89 liters ) pitcher sold for 2 gp .

title: Heart of ice
description: Heart of ice Heart of ice was a divine magic spell available to cleric s and crusader s of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It caused massive internal damage to the creature touched , often fatally shattering the heart . Effects .
description_long: Heart of ice Heart of ice was a divine magic spell available to cleric s and crusader s of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It caused massive internal damage to the creature touched , often fatally shattering the heart . Effects . It took a full minute of intense concentration to build up the fury of this spell , and then it required the caster to successfully touch the target . When touched , the victim ' s skin turned black as the sky of the Negative Energy plane itself , and their body was rimed with white frost . If the creature failed to resist the magic of this spell , it froze and shattered the heart , causing immediate death . If the victim was able to resist , he or she still suffered a large amount of cold damage to their internal organs which could also prove fatal . If they survived , the victim could do nothing except yell and choose which direction to fall down as their body was wracked with uncontrollable shivering , leaving them helpless . As an ironic side effect , survivors of this spell were immune to further cold damage for over two hours ( even longer when " heart of ice " was cast by more experienced priests ) .

title: Heart of the Eagle
description: Heart of the Eagle The Heart of the Eagle was located within the fortress of Sarahin in the Haunted Lands . Description . Carved from the rock of the ridge upon which Sarahin stood , the Heart of the Eagle was a tight chamber decorated with several tapestries .
description_long: Heart of the Eagle The Heart of the Eagle was located within the fortress of Sarahin in the Haunted Lands . Description . Carved from the rock of the ridge upon which Sarahin stood , the Heart of the Eagle was a tight chamber decorated with several tapestries . Windows provided a splendid view of the river gorge below . History . One of the tapestries was actually a " tapestry of folded existence " housing the entire treasure horde of the Everlasting .

title: Heart of the Lion
description: Heart of the Lion The Heart of the Lion was a holy relic that could be found in the fortress of Sarahin in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . The Heart of the Lion was actually a carnelian of bright red coloration .
description_long: Heart of the Lion The Heart of the Lion was a holy relic that could be found in the fortress of Sarahin in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . The Heart of the Lion was actually a carnelian of bright red coloration . The stone was large , measuring at least a foot across . History . Casting " detect magic " upon the stone would cause it to radiate strong necromantic magic . This occurred because Akim al - Kalaas used the stone as the receptacle for his " lifeproof " spell . Akim tasked his personal dao servant to kill anyone who lifted a finger against the stone . Three smaller fragments sat beside the Heart of the Lion on the sacred altar of the Lion ' s Shrine . If held by devout followers of Hajama , these fragments granted them the ability to use " bless " , " cloak of bravery " , " cure disease " , " dispel evil " , and " heal " . Rumors and Legends . The founder of the Everlasting was said to have ripped the Heart from the body of the Lion of Suja .

title: Heartblood River
description: Heartblood River The Heartblood River was a tributary of the Delimbiyr in the Savage Frontier . It found its source on the north face of the Star Mounts and wound its way east and south through the Dire Wood . There it gained its name from the red tinge its waters took on as they passed the ruined city of Karse .
description_long: Heartblood River The Heartblood River was a tributary of the Delimbiyr in the Savage Frontier . It found its source on the north face of the Star Mounts and wound its way east and south through the Dire Wood . There it gained its name from the red tinge its waters took on as they passed the ruined city of Karse . By the time it joined the Delimbiyr , its waters returned to a normal hue . It was said that drinking from the waters when they still flowed red could grant an increase to magical powers , or help stave off adverse magical effects . The red color was attributed simply to soil deposits picked up as the river passed through the Dire Wood . However , other sources mentioned contamination from the blood of the still - beating heart of the dead god Karsus .

title: Heartstone Gem
description: Heartstone Gem The Heartstone Gem was a powerful artifact kept in the village of Kuldahar . Description . The Heartstone Gem was a red stone , appearing like a gemstone .
description_long: Heartstone Gem The Heartstone Gem was a powerful artifact kept in the village of Kuldahar . Description . The Heartstone Gem was a red stone , appearing like a gemstone . Powers . Long range divination and the power to see what is hidden from standard divination . It requires tremendous magical och priestly power to use it . History . The origin of the Heartstone Gem is unknown . It resided for a long time in the druids shrine in Kuldahar , the druids used its powers of divination to see the surrounding lands and look into the affairs of people throughout the realms . A young druid had grown tired of the humble teachings of his mentor the archdruid , and hungered for power of his own . He stole the Heartstone Gem and it eventually ended up in a temple dedicated to the mysterious Forgotten God . The priests of the same god placed it on an altar deep within their temple , but the part it played in their religion like anything else of their faith is unknown . The Heartstone Gem was stolen by snake worshipping cultists , apparently tainted one s who were agents of the marilith Yxunomei .

title: Heartwarder
description: Heartwarder Heartwarders are devoted spellcasters devoted to the worship of the god dess Sune . Heartwarders follow the teachings of their patron goddess and seek to encourage love and enjoyment of all things in life . Heartwarders often serve wealthy patrons and in turn are served by others to help bring together men and women seeking love and intimacy , as well as to bring pure pleasure through art , music , and other enjoyable pursuits .
description_long: Heartwarder Heartwarders are devoted spellcasters devoted to the worship of the god dess Sune . Heartwarders follow the teachings of their patron goddess and seek to encourage love and enjoyment of all things in life . Heartwarders often serve wealthy patrons and in turn are served by others to help bring together men and women seeking love and intimacy , as well as to bring pure pleasure through art , music , and other enjoyable pursuits . Sometimes , heartwarders are forced to take a less peaceful route and members of the order oppose all forms of cruelty and tyranny . Although heartwarders do not relish battle , they are thrilled by the pursuit of beauty or joy and are accepting of the fact that sometimes these goals cannot be obtained by any other means . Even so , Sune ' s Heartwarders are rarely soldiers by choice and prefer instead to shield others from harm . Abilities . Because of Sune ' s love of joy and distaste for violence many of the abilities learned and used by heartwarders avoid direct harm , instead charming opponents or healing allies .

title: Heat leech
description: Heat leech Heat leech was a necromantic divine magic spell available to cleric s of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It drained vitality from all creatures in a small area and transferred that vitality to the caster , even to the point of gaining temporary health beyond normal limits . Effects .
description_long: Heat leech Heat leech was a necromantic divine magic spell available to cleric s of Auril , the Frostmaiden . It drained vitality from all creatures in a small area and transferred that vitality to the caster , even to the point of gaining temporary health beyond normal limits . Effects . This spell could be cast at a creature or group of creatures up to 45 ft ( 14 m ) away ( higher level casters could extend this range ) . It affected all creatures except the caster that fit within a 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) diameter circle or other regular shape as long as no two individuals were more than 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) apart . Each creature had a chance to resist the magic of this spell , and if they had sufficient fortitude , no harm was done to them . Those that failed to resist were subjected to extreme cold that sucked the life force from their bodies , possibly causing unconsciousness or death . The sum of all life force stolen by " heat leech " was transferred to the caster as health , first healing any wounds he or she may have sustained . Any surplus vitality granted the caster a temporary health boost beyond the normal limit that acted like a damage shield .

title: Heat metal
description: Heat metal Heat metal is a transmutation spell that heats metal to damage those who touch it . Effect . This spell is identical to " chill metal " except that it makes metal warm , hot , and searing instead of cold , icy , and freezing .
description_long: Heat metal Heat metal is a transmutation spell that heats metal to damage those who touch it . Effect . This spell is identical to " chill metal " except that it makes metal warm , hot , and searing instead of cold , icy , and freezing . If cast underwater , heat metal does less damage and boils the surrounding water . " Heat metal " counters and dispels " chill metal " .

title: Heat mirage
description: Heat mirage Heat mirage was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell enhanced the desert ' s natural abilities to create mirages .
description_long: Heat mirage Heat mirage was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell enhanced the desert ' s natural abilities to create mirages . If cast upon an area of the desert already creating a mirage , this spell added olfactory and auditory components to the mirage . Heat mirage was particularly useful for luring victims into an ambush . The mirage illusion was not dispelled until something actually tried to drink from the oasis , allowing bandits to hide in plain sight . Components . This spell did not require physical components to cast .

title: Heatwave
description: Heatwave Heatwave was a flame spell that combined the schools of alteration and evocation . It was used by members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara . Effects .
description_long: Heatwave Heatwave was a flame spell that combined the schools of alteration and evocation . It was used by members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara . Effects . " Heatwave " created an intense blast of heat that radiated outward from the caster for 20 feet ( 6 m ) . Anything caught in the area of effect suffered painful burns until they were able to move away from the heat . The caster was immune to this heat . Additionally , the heat warped the air within the area of effect , granting everything caught within the area , including the caster , the effects of a " cloak of displacement " . This effect could be negated by those using a " true seeing " spell . A " heatwave " could melt ice or snow , or evaporate water , at a rate of 10 cubic feet per minute . This included ice or water created by other spells such as " wall of ice " . Casting " heatwave " before a " wall of ice " spell was cast halved the production of the " wall of ice " . If " heatwave " and " ice storm " were cast they would cancel each other out . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , " heatwave " required a small folding fan and a drop of mercury to cast .

title: Heaven ' s trumpet
description: Heaven ' s trumpet Heaven ' s trumpet is an evocation spell that sounds a blast of music to paralyze foes . Only casters with the archon subtype can use this spell . Effect .
description_long: Heaven ' s trumpet Heaven ' s trumpet is an evocation spell that sounds a blast of music to paralyze foes . Only casters with the archon subtype can use this spell . Effect . You produce a blast of music of utter clarity , piercing beauty , and paralyzing awe . All foes within 120 feet of you must succeed on a Fortitude save or be paralyzed for up to 24 seconds . Focus . A masterwork trumpet , which you must blow .

title: Heavenly lightning
description: Heavenly lightning Heavenly lightning is an evocation spell that electrocutes targets with divine lightning . Effect . You create a leaping bolt of radiant lightning that arcs from one target to the next , avoiding other creatures in its path .
description_long: Heavenly lightning Heavenly lightning is an evocation spell that electrocutes targets with divine lightning . Effect . You create a leaping bolt of radiant lightning that arcs from one target to the next , avoiding other creatures in its path . Each target struck by an arc takes up to eighteen points of special celestial electricity damage . Creatures normally immune to electricity take full damage from this spell , and the celestial lightning is not subject to being reduced by " protection from energy ( electricity ) " or similar magic .

title: Heavy aspergillum
description: Heavy aspergillum A heavy aspergillum was a weapon that combined the features of an aspergillum and a heavy mace . It was only used by the Ilmaterans of the kingdom of Impiltur . Description .
description_long: Heavy aspergillum A heavy aspergillum was a weapon that combined the features of an aspergillum and a heavy mace . It was only used by the Ilmaterans of the kingdom of Impiltur . Description . Like the ordinary aspergillum , the heavy aspergillum took the form of a metal club or mace , with a reservoir inside that could contain up to three flask ' s worth of holy water . Pressing a button on the shaft opened up the perforations in the head , allowing holy water to leak out . In this way , the aspergillum could spray holy water over a short distance or on anything struck by it , using one flask ' s worth per shot . Unlike the ordinary aspergillum , the heavy aspergillum was designed as a melee weapon , with the effectiveness of a heavy mace . Uses . In addition to its ritual uses , the heavy aspergillum could be used as a weapon as well as a means of spraying monsters with holy water . " Circa " 1372 DR , it was used almost exclusively by the worshipers of Ilmater the Crying God in the kingdom of Impiltur against the demon s that terrorized that realm .

title: Heavy flail
description: Heavy flail A heavy flail is a two - handed , martial melee weapon , a larger version of the flail . Description . A heavy flail is a flail with a longer haft ( about four feet or 1 .
description_long: Heavy flail A heavy flail is a two - handed , martial melee weapon , a larger version of the flail . Description . A heavy flail is a flail with a longer haft ( about four feet or 1 . 2 meters ) and chain and a heavier spiked ball or rod on the end of the chain . The top spike may be elongated to give the weapon even more reach . An average heavy flail costs 15gp and weighs 10lbs ( 4 . 5kg ) . In 1st and 2nd edition D & D , this weapon is called the footman ' s flail . Weaponology . Heavy flails are typically used as two - handed weapons . Flails can be used to trip an opponent and the flexible chain increases the chance of entangling an enemy weapon and disarming them .

title: Heavy mace
description: Heavy mace A heavy mace is a simple , one - handed melee weapon , much like a club made from metal . Description . The heavy mace is the larger brother of the light mace .
description_long: Heavy mace A heavy mace is a simple , one - handed melee weapon , much like a club made from metal . Description . The heavy mace is the larger brother of the light mace . It has a longer and thicker metal haft and a larger head than the light mace . The flanges on the striking head are bigger and often more elaborate . Heavy maces are not to be confused with the morning star which is even longer and has spikes protruding out of the head . An average heavy mace costs 12gp and weighs 8lbs ( 3 . 6kg ) . Use . The mace is the natural development of the club and is made completely out of metal , making it a heavy but difficult to break weapon . This weapon is intended to be used one - handed and is simple enough for most character classes to use without any training . Mounted horsemen often use maces with slightly longer hafts to reach both mounted and unmounted opponents . Realmslore . The weapon is often found in the hands of adventurers from Cormyr , the Savage Frontier and Vaasa .

title: Heavy pick
description: Heavy pick A heavy pick is a one - handed , martial melee weapon . Description . The heavy pick is similar to a miner ' s pick but specifically designed for war .
description_long: Heavy pick A heavy pick is a one - handed , martial melee weapon . Description . The heavy pick is similar to a miner ' s pick but specifically designed for war . The haft is about 4 feet ( 1 . 2m ) long and can be made of wood or metal . The metal weapon head is a slightly curved thick spike backed by either a smaller spike or a hammer head . Some heavy picks are indistinguishable from a light hammer with a pick on the back . An average heavy pick costs 8gp and weighs 6lbs ( 2 . 7kg ) . Weaponology . The heavy pick is also known as a horseman ' s pick as they were often wielded from horseback . Picks are intended to pierce plate armor but can get stuck if swung too hard . Some training is required to wield effectively , therefore the heavy pick is classified as a martial weapon . Other editions . The second edition player ' s handbook does not mention picks , but first edition and 3 . 5 edition do .

title: Hebopbe
description: Hebopbe Hebopbe was a myconid leader of a Circle in Neverlight Grove during the Rage of Demons . Personality . Hebopbe had no interest in the feud between sovereigns Basidia and Phylo .
description_long: Hebopbe Hebopbe was a myconid leader of a Circle in Neverlight Grove during the Rage of Demons . Personality . Hebopbe had no interest in the feud between sovereigns Basidia and Phylo . It did not like Phylo ' s innovations but thought that Basidia had exaggerated the danger . History . Hebopbe was the leader of the Circle of Growers in Neverlight Grove . When , with the Rage of Demons , Zuggtmoy ' s will twisted most of the Circle , Hebopbe partially resisted the evil ' s influence .

title: Hector
description: Hector Hector was an oni night hunter in the ruin of Spellgard in 1479 DR . History . Thanks to a partial array of alabaster pillar s , Thoran managed to summon and bind an oni , who often disguised himself as a human prisoner called Hector .
description_long: Hector Hector was an oni night hunter in the ruin of Spellgard in 1479 DR . History . Thanks to a partial array of alabaster pillar s , Thoran managed to summon and bind an oni , who often disguised himself as a human prisoner called Hector . The oni planned to kill Thoran and enslave Lady Saharel .

title: Hedrun Arnsfirth
description: Hedrun Arnsfirth Hedrun Arnsfirth was the Chosen of Auril in Icewind Dale in 1484 DR . History . Hedrun was born into the Tribe of the Elk as the daughter of Soren Arnsfirth .
description_long: Hedrun Arnsfirth Hedrun Arnsfirth was the Chosen of Auril in Icewind Dale in 1484 DR . History . Hedrun was born into the Tribe of the Elk as the daughter of Soren Arnsfirth . At a young age , she was promised to Olaf Tormhaalt , son of the tribe ' s shaman . However , when her Chosen powers first manifested , Hedrun accidentally killed Olaf and was banished from the tribe . Her powers permitted her to survive in the winter and , in her fury and desire for vengeance , Hedrun gladly embraced the will of Auril . She started gathering an army of animals and monsters . Soon , even the Tribe of the Bear pledged themselves to the Ice Witch . They started to construct a temple to Auril in the old lair of Ingeloakastimizilian . Hedrun then started a war in Icewind Dale with her troops attacking all of its communities . The Ten Towns defended themselves but in response , she sent an army to attack Bryn Shander . In the meantime , she sent her captured father as her envoy to the Elk Tribe demanding their submission . In the end , however , an adventuring party defeated her .

title: Hedweck
description: Hedweck Hedweck was a male human barbarian of the White Worm tribe in Vaasa in north Faerûn in the mid – 14th century DR . He was the tribe ' s spirit hunter around 1359 DR . History .
description_long: Hedweck Hedweck was a male human barbarian of the White Worm tribe in Vaasa in north Faerûn in the mid – 14th century DR . He was the tribe ' s spirit hunter around 1359 DR . History . At some point , Hedweck had proved himself as the mightiest warrior of the tribe and was chosen as the next spirit hunter , the champion of White Worm . He was magically strengthened and hypnotized by the tribe shaman and was equipped with enchanted weapons like Bonecrusher and the sacred white - worm - skin armor . He was then sent into the wilds to battle " evil spirits " invading the tribe ' s territory , his first task being to avenge the death of the last spirit hunter . In 1359 DR , he wandered the Vaasan bog south of the Great Glacier . Abilities . As a spirit hunter , Hedweck had been magically strengthened and hypnotized by the tribe ' s shaman . He fought in a terrible battle - rage , hitting faster and harder and more often . The spirit hunter ' s purpose was to battle " evil spirits " , but in his altered state , anyone Hedweck saw was an evil spirit . Fanatically determined , he would throw himself at superior foes and numbers , without fear of death .

title: Heidar Qan
description: Heidar Qan Heidar Qan was an Amir of the Jann of the Haunted Lands in Zakhara in 1367 DR . History . Heidar Qan was credited with constructing the great fortress of Sarahin within the Haunted Lands .
description_long: Heidar Qan Heidar Qan was an Amir of the Jann of the Haunted Lands in Zakhara in 1367 DR . History . Heidar Qan was credited with constructing the great fortress of Sarahin within the Haunted Lands . During a hunting trip , he released his prized golden eagle . The eagle settled on a rock , drawing the Amir ' s attention to the tranquil beauty and inherent strength of the site . He commanded his servants to build his fortress upon that very site , later naming it Sarahin , which meant " wolves ' den " . After the construction of his fortress , Heidar stopped paying fealty to the Grand Caliph in Huzuz and disappeared without a trace . As of 1367 DR , Heidar Qan had not been seen for 50 years , causing much unrest among the jann . Rumors & Legends . In reality , the rumors of Heidar ' s illness or death were false . Heidar was captured and held by the Brotherhood of the True Flame and their sinister master , The Bonfire . The motive behind his kidnapping remained unclear .

title: Hekaton
description: Hekaton Hekaton was the storm giant king until sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Hekaton ruled the storm giants but asserted his authority over all races of giants .
description_long: Hekaton Hekaton was the storm giant king until sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Hekaton ruled the storm giants but asserted his authority over all races of giants . Just before the time of the shattering of the ordning , receiving no more answers from the giant pantheon , he come to believe that the time of giants was over . After the end of the ordning , Hekaton was greatly shocked but his wife Neri said to him that the future was in the hands of the small folk . Thank to Neri ' s belief and some omens , Hekaton decided to appoint his youngest daughter Serissa , who agreed with Neri ' s ideas , as his heir , angering his older daughters Mirran and Nym . When , in the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Neri ' s dead body was found , Hekaton exploded in rage but Serissa managed to calm her father . Hekaton decided to find Neri ' s assassin but Mirran and Nym , with the help of the disguised Iymrith , managed to deceive Hekaton . He was lured into a trap devised by Kraken Society agents who , posing as Lords ' Alliance agents , captured him and placed him in a stasis sphere in a shielded ship constantly at sea . Personality .

title: Heladar Longspear
description: Heladar Longspear Heladar Longspear was a male warrior member of the Zhentilar in High Dale . History . Heladar fought for Zhentil Keep in Daggerdale and in the conquest of the Citadel of the Raven .
description_long: Heladar Longspear Heladar Longspear was a male warrior member of the Zhentilar in High Dale . History . Heladar fought for Zhentil Keep in Daggerdale and in the conquest of the Citadel of the Raven . In 1358 DR , Heladar commanded a small Zhent occupation army that secretly conquered High Dale . However , Elminster Aumar and Sharantyr casually discovered the Zhent plot regarding the dale and started an insurrection in which Heladar was killed by the Harpers Itharr and Belkram .

title: Helbareim Alanasker
description: Helbareim Alanasker Helbareim Alanasker was in 1373 DR the king of Ormpur , the Lapaliiyan town holy to Tiamat . He came to power by overthrowing Queen Maerildarraine who , in 1306 DR , had rebelled against Tiamat and killed her father . Helbareim defeated the heretic queen with the help of the church of Tiamat but at the price of falling under the power of the Overking of Lapaliiya .
description_long: Helbareim Alanasker Helbareim Alanasker was in 1373 DR the king of Ormpur , the Lapaliiyan town holy to Tiamat . He came to power by overthrowing Queen Maerildarraine who , in 1306 DR , had rebelled against Tiamat and killed her father . Helbareim defeated the heretic queen with the help of the church of Tiamat but at the price of falling under the power of the Overking of Lapaliiya . Helbarein ' s daughter Alabhansree Alanasker went missing in 1357 DR destroying his spirit , especially after adventurers hired by him no found her as slave in Llurth Dreir , as from informations . In truth without anyone knowing Alabhansree escaped with her lover the pirate Cairak Redbeard and lived in a small tower in the Moonshaes . In 1370 DR yuan - ti agents plotted to use this information to gain control of the city .

title: Helda Silverstream
description: Helda Silverstream Helda Silverstream was a dwarf just returned to Icewind Dale in 1485 DR . History . Helda was born in Kelvin ' s Cairn in the union of Clan Silverstream and Clan Battlehammer and was the niece of Stokely Silverstream .
description_long: Helda Silverstream Helda Silverstream was a dwarf just returned to Icewind Dale in 1485 DR . History . Helda was born in Kelvin ' s Cairn in the union of Clan Silverstream and Clan Battlehammer and was the niece of Stokely Silverstream . At a young age , full of stories from her mother about the Companions of the Hall , she traveled to Mithral Hall . Helda later settled in Mirabar , where she joined the Axe of Mirabar , but usually wandered from Waterdeep to Icewind Dale to sell her works . In 1485 DR , alarmed by strange rumors about dissent against her uncle , Helda returned to the dale to check on the situation . She was probably involved in the conflict between Stokely and Baerick Hammerstone . Appendix . Behind the scenes . Helda can recruit the adventurers in Bryn Shander as bodyguards .

title: Heldapan
description: Heldapan Heldapan was the capital of Durpar located toward the center of the country . Description . Heldapan was situated on the eastern coast of the River Heldar near the Golden Water .
description_long: Heldapan Heldapan was the capital of Durpar located toward the center of the country . Description . Heldapan was situated on the eastern coast of the River Heldar near the Golden Water . Large docks were suited to handle the countless arrival of ships carrying goods . Inhabitants . The Council of Merchants was based in Heldapan . Each of the Chakas of 31 also had some kind of establishment here . History . Heldapan was known throughout the Shining South for its splendid markets where nearly anything imaginable could be purchased .

title: Heldatha Dhussta
description: Heldatha Dhussta Heldatha Dhussta was a female human and a Painbearer of Ilmater . She was the Revered Mother of the House at the Towers of Willful Suffering in Eshpurta , Amn , in the Year of the Shield , 1367 DR through at least early 1370 DR , the Year of the Tankard
description_long: Heldatha Dhussta Heldatha Dhussta was a female human and a Painbearer of Ilmater . She was the Revered Mother of the House at the Towers of Willful Suffering in Eshpurta , Amn , in the Year of the Shield , 1367 DR through at least early 1370 DR , the Year of the Tankard

title: Helder Mornstone
description: Helder Mornstone Helder Mornstone was the commander of Xantharl ' s Keep in 1370 DR . Activities . Helder was the leader of the garrison of Xantharl ' s Keep .
description_long: Helder Mornstone Helder Mornstone was the commander of Xantharl ' s Keep in 1370 DR . Activities . Helder was the leader of the garrison of Xantharl ' s Keep . He disliked troublemakers but appreciated adventurers in times of need . His goal in 1370 was to unveil Zhentarim and Cult of the Dragon spies inside Xantharl . Personality . Helder dreamed of the day when Xantharl would be an oasis of peace dedicated to Mielikki , but knew he was too old to see his dream become reality . He accepted his duty to defend the keep until his death .

title: Heldorm
description: Heldorm Heldorm was a member of the Cult of the Black Earth at the Temple of the Black Earth in Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Heldorm was an unbalanced individual .
description_long: Heldorm Heldorm was a member of the Cult of the Black Earth at the Temple of the Black Earth in Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Heldorm was an unbalanced individual . He normally spoke with himself and tittered at a series of black jests he only partially shared aloud . History . In 1491 DR , Heldorm and three fellow cultists acted as jailers in the temple ' s jail until some adventurers infiltrated the temple and confronted and defeated them .

title: Heldorn Thaerntyl
description: Heldorn Thaerntyl Heldorn " Goldsun " Thaerntyl was a human fighter , wizard , thief and a member of the Council of Sparkling Stones in Mirabar . Description . The adventurer gained his nickname because he had long curly blond hair , and he used two sun blade s in combat .
description_long: Heldorn Thaerntyl Heldorn " Goldsun " Thaerntyl was a human fighter , wizard , thief and a member of the Council of Sparkling Stones in Mirabar . Description . The adventurer gained his nickname because he had long curly blond hair , and he used two sun blade s in combat .

title: Helgabal
description: Helgabal Helgabal , formerly known as Heliogabalus , was the largest city in Damara , and was once the seat of government until King Gareth moved the capital to Bloodstone Village . Government . 14th Century DR .
description_long: Helgabal Helgabal , formerly known as Heliogabalus , was the largest city in Damara , and was once the seat of government until King Gareth moved the capital to Bloodstone Village . Government . 14th Century DR . Since the crowning of Gareth Dragonsbane as the King of Damara , the power of many long - standing baronies was reduced . On the surface it seemed he was loved and respected by all , but Baron Dimian Ree still maintained a large amount of loyalty in central Damara where Helgabal lay . Publicly , Baron Ree proclaimed to be a public servant of the crown , but Grandmaster Kane of Spysong suspected Ree to be in cahoots with the Citadel of Assassins . 15th Century DR . Lord Yarin Frostmantle ruled as a tyrannical king in the late 15th century DR . Trade . Various independent merchant and trade guilds allowed Helgabal to heavily influence the supply of goods to all of Damara . Helgabal was the farthest stop north for most merchants traveling north into the Bloodstone Lands . Independent , and loyal to no one outside their respective guilds , the people here rarely objected to anything unless it interfered with day - to - day business . Defense .

title: Helgar Hoaraxe
description: Helgar Hoaraxe Helgar Hoaraxe was the head carpenter in Skullport . Once a sailor , Helgar settled in Skullport around 1340 DR , starting a new career in repairing and refitting damaged ships that arrived in the port . In times of slow work , he and his squad could be hired by captains as on - board carpenters or sailmasters .
description_long: Helgar Hoaraxe Helgar Hoaraxe was the head carpenter in Skullport . Once a sailor , Helgar settled in Skullport around 1340 DR , starting a new career in repairing and refitting damaged ships that arrived in the port . In times of slow work , he and his squad could be hired by captains as on - board carpenters or sailmasters .

title: Helgre
description: Helgre Helgre served as the first mate on the " Orcsblood " , a pirate ship that terrorized the Moonsea in the mid – 15th century DR . She managed to escape when the " Orcsblood " was attacked and destroyed by deva s in 1460 DR . Helgre correctly reasoned that two shipmates , Gareth Jadaren and Ivor Beguine , who had recently jumped ship , were the ones responsible for betraying the " Orcsblood " ' s location to the devas .
description_long: Helgre Helgre served as the first mate on the " Orcsblood " , a pirate ship that terrorized the Moonsea in the mid – 15th century DR . She managed to escape when the " Orcsblood " was attacked and destroyed by deva s in 1460 DR . Helgre correctly reasoned that two shipmates , Gareth Jadaren and Ivor Beguine , who had recently jumped ship , were the ones responsible for betraying the " Orcsblood " ' s location to the devas . She dedicated the following months to tracking down Gareth and Ivor and found them near Erlkazar in 1461 DR . Rather than attempt to kill the two men , she slew Ivor ' s lover , Jandi M ' baren , and staged the crime so that it appeared Gareth was responsible . At some point after 1461 DR , Helgre became a vampire . She participated in the assault on Jadaren Hold in 1600 DR but was killed by the deva Lakini . Appearance . Helgre had a horrible scar on the side of her face .

title: Heliodor
description: Heliodor Heliodor was a variety of and considered a precious stone for jewelry and ornamentation . It has some magical uses as well . Description .
description_long: Heliodor Heliodor was a variety of and considered a precious stone for jewelry and ornamentation . It has some magical uses as well . Description . Heliodor had a deep yellow hue with tints from greenish yellow to reddish yellow and yielded medium to large facet - cut gems . A typical specimen had a base value of 500 gp . Powers . Heliodor gems could be substituted for other naturally - occurring material components ( " i . e . " , those that did not require manufacturing or special construction ) in all priest spells of the sun sphere . Crushed heliodor was a required reagent when forging a " sun blade " .

title: Heliopolis
description: Heliopolis Heliopolis was a plane where the deities of the Mulhorandi pantheon resided . Great Wheel cosmology . In the Great Wheel cosmology , Heliopolis was more specifically the name of a joint realm of three Mulhorandi deities in Arcadia ' s second layer of Buxenus .
description_long: Heliopolis Heliopolis was a plane where the deities of the Mulhorandi pantheon resided . Great Wheel cosmology . In the Great Wheel cosmology , Heliopolis was more specifically the name of a joint realm of three Mulhorandi deities in Arcadia ' s second layer of Buxenus . It was comprised of Thekele - Re , ruled by Horus - Re , Gizekhtet by Isis , and Memphiria , governed by Osiris .

title: Helisa Ithcanter
description: Helisa Ithcanter Helisa Ithcanter was a cleric of Azuth in Westbridge in 1370 DR . Activities . Helisa can ' t stay still , she always need did something .
description_long: Helisa Ithcanter Helisa Ithcanter was a cleric of Azuth in Westbridge in 1370 DR . Activities . Helisa can ' t stay still , she always need did something . Helisa was thirsty for informations about her hometown of Baldur ' s Gate and her friends there . She was worried by the Ghaliver Longstocking ' s rise to the top , fearing this attired the Zhentarim over Westbridge . Anyone that knew how damage Ghaliver ' s or the Zhent was welcomed .

title: Hell hound
description: Hell hound A hell hound was a big , powerfully built dog with short , rust - red fur ; its markings , teeth , and tongue were sooty black . Description . Hell hounds were the dogs of the Nine Hells .
description_long: Hell hound A hell hound was a big , powerfully built dog with short , rust - red fur ; its markings , teeth , and tongue were sooty black . Description . Hell hounds were the dogs of the Nine Hells . They appeared to be canines with emaciated features , fire spouting from their red glowing eyes , and smoke pouring from their fanged mouths . The average hell hound stood four and a half feet ( 1 . 4 meters ) at the shoulder and weighed about 120 pounds ( 54 . 4 kilograms ) . Combat . Hell hounds preferred to hunt in packs and would use their fiery breath on an opponent first and then close in for the kill . Ecology . While hell hounds were found in the Plane of Hell , they were also regularly seen in the Plane of Fire and the mortal world . Fire giant s and other fiery creatures made use of hell hounds as guard dogs and hunting beasts . Society . Hell hounds used wolf - like tactics . They organized in packs , surrounding their prey , and attacked one at a time until the target became fatigued or fell to the ground . If singular attacks did not seem to be effective , the pack would each breathe a gout of flame at the target .

title: Hellborn shadow
description: Hellborn shadow A hellborn shadow is a tiefling ranger who has learned to tap into his or her fiend ish heritage as a way to enhance their natural abilities . Instead of turning away from their ancestry , hellborn shadows embrace it , for good or evil , and use it to battle the supernatural threats they face , becoming dark and often feared monster slayers . The brings hellborn shadows dangerously close to the evil taint that haunts them , sometimes blurring the line between good and evil .
description_long: Hellborn shadow A hellborn shadow is a tiefling ranger who has learned to tap into his or her fiend ish heritage as a way to enhance their natural abilities . Instead of turning away from their ancestry , hellborn shadows embrace it , for good or evil , and use it to battle the supernatural threats they face , becoming dark and often feared monster slayers . The brings hellborn shadows dangerously close to the evil taint that haunts them , sometimes blurring the line between good and evil . Hellborn shadows , like most tieflings , often face a great degree of prejudice and misunderstanding from others . However , this prejudice is intensified by the fact that they willingly embrace their inner darkness , often using the very fear they evoke as a weapon . While all tieflings have supernatural qualities , hellborn shadows push these to their limits , using ancient knowledge or natural ability to enhance their combat prowess and to even transform themselves into a fiend - like form . Such power does not come without a cost , however , and a fair number of hellborn shadows give in to the evil urges that their abilities bring , though others manage to fight them off . Abilities .

title: Hellcat
description: Hellcat Hellcats , also called " bezekira " , are quiet hunters of the Nine Hells . Physical description . In total darkness , hellcats appear to be a massive feline monsters with hot , ethereal wisps coming from their bodies .
description_long: Hellcat Hellcats , also called " bezekira " , are quiet hunters of the Nine Hells . Physical description . In total darkness , hellcats appear to be a massive feline monsters with hot , ethereal wisps coming from their bodies . Their eyes burn with hellfire , hunger , and anger . The average hellcat is about 9 feet long and weighs about 900 pounds . Combat . These fierce devil - cats move about in virtual silence , constantly on the prowl for any opportunity to do evil . They enjoy setting ambushes and outwitting enemies . While their appearance suggests they are incorporeal , hellcats have corporeal bodies and can be harmed by physical attacks . Abilites . Invisible in any light , bezekira are only visible in total darkness . Hellcats use a natural telepathy to communicate with one another and those they encounter .

title: Hellenhild
description: Hellenhild Hellenhild was a frost giant jarl sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Hellenhild was one of the giant lords at the time of the shattering of the ordning .
description_long: Hellenhild Hellenhild was a frost giant jarl sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . Hellenhild was one of the giant lords at the time of the shattering of the ordning . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Hellenhild was one of the giant lords who had arrived in the Maelstrom citadel in search of news about Princess Serissa ' s plans for the future . Personality . Hellenhild respected battle prowess above all .

title: Hellenrae
description: Hellenrae Hellenrae was a high - ranking member of the Cult of the Black Earth during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Hellenrae simply hated everyone , even her fellow cultists , so she tried to avoid contact with others .
description_long: Hellenrae Hellenrae was a high - ranking member of the Cult of the Black Earth during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Hellenrae simply hated everyone , even her fellow cultists , so she tried to avoid contact with others . She greatly despised weakness . Activities . Hellenrae usually remained in her quarters unless orders cane from Marlos Urnrayle . History . In her youth , Hellenrae was an orphan who lost her sight . She was accepted by a monastic order , where was she trained as a monk , but she distorted the monks ' philosophy of self - denial and emptiness of mind to extremes , seeking to fill herself with the dark power she sensed sleeping in the earth and rock around her . So , insteadm , Hellenrae joined the Cult of the Black Earth and rose to become the chief lieutenant of Marlos Urnrayle . In 1491 DR , Hellenrae , Qarbo , and their minions disguised themselves as monks occupying the Sacred Stone Monastery . Soon after , however , some adventurers infiltrated the monastery and in the end confronted and defeated Hellenrae .

title: Hellfire warlock
description: Hellfire warlock A Hellfire Warlock is able to enhance the power of their eldritch blasts by harnessing hellfire , a mysterious magical energy found in the Nine Hells . They often gain this power by interacting with the Baatezu , summoning them in order to make infernal contracts or forcibly capturing and interrogating them . Abilities .
description_long: Hellfire warlock A Hellfire Warlock is able to enhance the power of their eldritch blasts by harnessing hellfire , a mysterious magical energy found in the Nine Hells . They often gain this power by interacting with the Baatezu , summoning them in order to make infernal contracts or forcibly capturing and interrogating them . Abilities . Hellfire Blast : Whenever a hellfire warlock unleashes an eldritch blast , they have the option of converting it into a ' hellfire blast ' . The hellfire blast inflicts greater damage than a standard blast , but drains a portion of the caster ' s lifeforce in exchange . The extra damage inflicted is not fire damage ; hellfire burns hotter than any fire normally found on the Prime Material Plane . A warlock cannot utilize hellfire blasts if they are physically unhealthy . Hellfire Shield : The hellfire warlock may surround themselves with a shield formed from hellfire . The shield provides no protection , but will launch hellfire blasts at any opponent who moves too close to the warlock . The warlock ' s lifeforce will be drained whenever the shield launches a hellfire blast .

title: Hellfire wyrm
description: Hellfire wyrm Hellfire wyrms were dragons sponsored by the hells to influence events on the Material Plane . Description . Large bone spikes jutted from the head and shoulders of these dragons , while smoke was continually emitted from their scales , seeming to flow like molten lava across their massive bodies .
description_long: Hellfire wyrm Hellfire wyrms were dragons sponsored by the hells to influence events on the Material Plane . Description . Large bone spikes jutted from the head and shoulders of these dragons , while smoke was continually emitted from their scales , seeming to flow like molten lava across their massive bodies . Their eyes burned bright yellow , and they reeked of brimstone . However , when they appeared before humanoids , they usually took the form of a tiefling . Combat . Hellfire wyrms preferred to manipulate people and politics from behind the scenes ; however , if they should be forced into a combat situation , they excelled at tactical maneuvers , able to turn enemies into friends and blast the rest with their powerful breath weapon . They also had the ability to temporarily summon baatezu allies and burn anything that got close to them .

title: Hellgate Dell
description: Hellgate Dell Hellgate Dell was the area where Hellgate Keep once stood . All that remained of Hellgate Keep was a craggy and mishapen hill covered with small bushes and moss . A ring of twenty - five huge oak trees , of which five were treant s , surrounded and guarded the hill from strangers .
description_long: Hellgate Dell Hellgate Dell was the area where Hellgate Keep once stood . All that remained of Hellgate Keep was a craggy and mishapen hill covered with small bushes and moss . A ring of twenty - five huge oak trees , of which five were treant s , surrounded and guarded the hill from strangers .

title: Hellgate Keep
description: Hellgate Keep Hellgate Keep , formerly Ascalhorn , was a city of evil on the northeast edge of the High Forest . It was destroyed in 1369 DR when the Harpers used the Gatekeeper ' s Crystal , and is now overseen by the treant Turlang and his fellows . History .
description_long: Hellgate Keep Hellgate Keep , formerly Ascalhorn , was a city of evil on the northeast edge of the High Forest . It was destroyed in 1369 DR when the Harpers used the Gatekeeper ' s Crystal , and is now overseen by the treant Turlang and his fellows . History . Ascalhorn . Ascalhorn was founded by the Eaerlann i elves in the northeast of the High Forest on an area known as Ascal ' s Horn , to protect the boundaries of the kingdom . They gave it to the Netherese refugees after Netheril fell . Wulgreth , a Netherese wizard , summoned devil s to the city in 820 DR . In 880 DR , this prompted other wizards , with the guidance of the fey ' ri , to summon demon s to counteract the devils and in 882 DR the demons won the battle and subsequently conquered the city . The demons continued their rampage , destroying Eaerlann and Ammarindar . Hellgate . In 886 DR , Harpers placed wards around the keep to prevent demons from using their gate abilities . In 1368 DR , the Blue Bear tribe , led by shaman and chieftain Tanta Hagara , marched on the fiend - ridden fortress .

title: Hellish rebuke
description: Hellish rebuke Hellish rebuke was a basic spell known to all warlock s of the infernal pact , and available to all warlocks after the Second Sundering . Effects . When cast , " hellish rebuke " caused a creature of the warlock ' s choosing within fifty feet of him or her to burst into flames channeled straight from the Nine Hells by the warlock ' s pain and rage .
description_long: Hellish rebuke Hellish rebuke was a basic spell known to all warlock s of the infernal pact , and available to all warlocks after the Second Sundering . Effects . When cast , " hellish rebuke " caused a creature of the warlock ' s choosing within fifty feet of him or her to burst into flames channeled straight from the Nine Hells by the warlock ' s pain and rage . The intensity of the flames was , for the most part , determined by the capacity of the warlock themselves to take damage , and with more experience the spell grew in power substantially . As the most basic of all spells used by warlocks in the service of devil s , " hellish rebuke " could be cast as many times per day as the warlock wished . Components . THe spell needed only somatic and verbal components to be cast . History . After the Second Sundering , warlocks of other pacts and sufficiently experienced tiefling s were able to cast the spell as well .

title: Hellriders
description: Hellriders The Hellriders were a group of skilled horsemen who acted as the primary armed force of the city of Elturel . Skilled soldiers who fought from horseback , they were typically proficient with spears , composite bows , and a curved saber similar to a scimitar . Activities .
description_long: Hellriders The Hellriders were a group of skilled horsemen who acted as the primary armed force of the city of Elturel . Skilled soldiers who fought from horseback , they were typically proficient with spears , composite bows , and a curved saber similar to a scimitar . Activities . In addition to policing the city itself , they patrolled the nearby reaches of the Chionthar River and those regions of the Fields of the Dead that were within Elturel ' s jurisdiction .

title: Hellwasp devil
description: Hellwasp devil Hellwasp devils are members of a huge colony that makes its home in the Garden of Delight s in Malbolge . Ruthless and logical , with an alien intelligence and the unquestioning instincts of a colony insect , these devil s live to serve the whims of their queen . Hellwasp devils were once demons akin to mezzodemon s .
description_long: Hellwasp devil Hellwasp devils are members of a huge colony that makes its home in the Garden of Delight s in Malbolge . Ruthless and logical , with an alien intelligence and the unquestioning instincts of a colony insect , these devil s live to serve the whims of their queen . Hellwasp devils were once demons akin to mezzodemon s . While in the Abyss , Glasya defeated their master and took them back to the Nine Hells . There , she transformed them into devils , making them shock troops and bodyguards . Lore . Hellwasp devils were once demons in service to a wasplike demon lord . During the Blood War , Glasya defeated the demon lord , and its curious spawn flocked to her as their new queen . Now , the hellwasp devil colony is an unwavering implement of Glasya ' s will . Unlike many of her other minions , hellwasps do not need to be seduced or manipulated . They see service to Glasya as an honor and a reward . When encountered outside Malbolge , hell wasp devils are either on a mission for their queen or on loan to one of Glasya ' s allies . Encounters .

title: Helm
description: Helm Helm ( pronounced " HELM " ) , also known as the Vigilant One and The Watcher , was the god of guardians , protection , and protectors . He was worshiped by guards and paladin s both , long being seen as a cold and focused deity who impartially took the role of defender and sometimes also enforcer . His activities in the Time of Troubles caused the folk of Faerûn to look differently on the Watcher .
description_long: Helm Helm ( pronounced " HELM " ) , also known as the Vigilant One and The Watcher , was the god of guardians , protection , and protectors . He was worshiped by guards and paladin s both , long being seen as a cold and focused deity who impartially took the role of defender and sometimes also enforcer . His activities in the Time of Troubles caused the folk of Faerûn to look differently on the Watcher . Personality . A very old deity , Helm was the eternal sentry and was always seen wearing a full suit of armor that represented the weight of his heavy responsibility . Yet Helm always got the job at hand done without complaint . The people of the Realms widely admired these qualities in what they saw as a humble and reassuring god . Relations . Far back in time , the deity Lathander caused a divine purge known as the Dawn Cataclysm in which Helm ' s lover , a lesser deity of pragmatism called Murdane , was a victim . Helm begrudged the Morninglord for this . However , Helm reserved his real opposition for deities whose plots threatened the people and stability of Faerûn , especially Bane , Cyric , Mask , and Shar .

title: Helm ' s Hold
description: Helm ' s Hold Helm ' s Hold was a fortified city and cathedral located near Neverwinter . Location . Helm ' s Hold was located around twenty miles ( less than a day ' s travel ) south east of the the city of Neverwinter , not far from the edge of Neverwinter Wood , in fact , a section of the Wood , known as the Watcher ' s Forest , was cared for by the Hold ' s residents , historically because of a wild magic area within .
description_long: Helm ' s Hold Helm ' s Hold was a fortified city and cathedral located near Neverwinter . Location . Helm ' s Hold was located around twenty miles ( less than a day ' s travel ) south east of the the city of Neverwinter , not far from the edge of Neverwinter Wood , in fact , a section of the Wood , known as the Watcher ' s Forest , was cared for by the Hold ' s residents , historically because of a wild magic area within . Government . Originally , the Hold ' s founder , Dumal Erard , led the Hold as First Guardian - a position that could only be passed on through martial combat . Eventually though , a democratically elected City Council was chosen from among the populace . This council was composed of ' Speakers ' who were frequently loud , individualistic and sometimes obnoxious during their debates , often using intimidation against each other to try and pass legislation . The Chief Speaker led this forum and had final say on policy - making decisions . Eventually , when the Ashmadai revealed themselves , The Prophet , as their leader , temporarily became de facto ruler of the Hold until she showed her true colours and fled to the Crypts .

title: Helm Dwarf - Friend
description: Helm Dwarf - Friend Helm Dwarf - Friend was the ruler of Sundabar < ref name = " N : GSF / Cities - p56 " > < / ref > and a member of the Council of the Marches . Personality . Helm was known as a wise and fair leader .
description_long: Helm Dwarf - Friend Helm Dwarf - Friend was the ruler of Sundabar < ref name = " N : GSF / Cities - p56 " > < / ref > and a member of the Council of the Marches . Personality . Helm was known as a wise and fair leader . History . Helm first gained notoriety when he was a the war - captain of the Bloodaxe Mercenary Company , his valiant campaigns earned him popularity in Sundabar . In 1355 DR , Helm became the sixth Ruling Master of the city of Sundabar . In Sojourn , around 1340 DR , Helm already is the Master of Sundabar , as Dove Falconhand is waiting to have an audience with him when called to hunt Drizzt .

title: Helm Stoneblade
description: Helm Stoneblade Helm Stoneblade was a knight serving the Stag King of Athalantar , Uthgrael Aumar , and the new king of the kingdom after 240 DR . History . Helm was a knight serving the kingdom of Athalantar and his king Uthgrael .
description_long: Helm Stoneblade Helm Stoneblade was a knight serving the Stag King of Athalantar , Uthgrael Aumar , and the new king of the kingdom after 240 DR . History . Helm was a knight serving the kingdom of Athalantar and his king Uthgrael . When the king died in 216 DR and his sons , the Warring Princes of Athalantar , started a bloody contest for the throne , Helm and many of his fellows abandoned the court and started lives as outlaws , especially after power was seized by Belaur Aumar and the magelord s . Helm tried to fight the usurpers but with little hope . In 222 DR , he made friends with young Elminster Aumar . Later , the magelords killed Elminster ' s parents , and he helped him in all things . Many years later , Elminster , by now a powerful wizard , came back in his country to defeat the magelords and recruit Helm and his fellows as allies . Elminster , the only remaining heir of Uthgrael , then nominated Helm to be king for his valor and integrity .

title: Helm and Cloak
description: Helm and Cloak The Helm and Cloak is a high - end inn and feasting hall in the city of Baldur ' s Gate . It is highly popular both with travelers and with local residents , who enjoy its dining room . It is also home to the majority of the Knights of the Unicorn , who currently rent the majority of an upper floor .
description_long: Helm and Cloak The Helm and Cloak is a high - end inn and feasting hall in the city of Baldur ' s Gate . It is highly popular both with travelers and with local residents , who enjoy its dining room . It is also home to the majority of the Knights of the Unicorn , who currently rent the majority of an upper floor . Its " signboard " consists of a weathered cloak draped over an exterior balcony on one side and an enormous helm hanging over the door on the other . Patronage . The Helm is much favored by individuals of power in Baldur ' s Gate . Numerous business deals are negotiated in its dining alcoves every day . Its clientele largely fall into two categories : locals coming to dine in the festhall and well - to - do travelers coming to enjoy the elegant accommodations . There is an entire floor set up for long - term occupancy , largely occupied at present by the Knights of the Unicorn . These Knights are romantic adventurers , commonly described as " elegant buffoons . " They make pleasant if slightly absurd company for any patron with good manners and a sense of humor . Architecture and Decor . The inn actually consists of two connected buildings .

title: Helm at Highsun
description: Helm at Highsun The Helm at Highsun was a tavern in the town of Red Larch owned by a mage named Yather Indaglol . Interior . The tavern was shadowy and quiet .
description_long: Helm at Highsun The Helm at Highsun was a tavern in the town of Red Larch owned by a mage named Yather Indaglol . Interior . The tavern was shadowy and quiet . Most customers were caravan guards , adventurers , retired people , people who want to just be alone , and merchants looking for relaxation . Staff . The motto of the Helm at Highsun was enforced by a silent , attentive , and menacing helmed horror that was under the mental control of Indaglol . The horror was known as Araldyk , and served as waiter , usher , bouncer , and sometimes a cloak rack .

title: Helm of reflection
description: Helm of reflection The helm of reflection was a magic item that could be found within the Hordelands . Description . This item was available in a variety of helmet types .
description_long: Helm of reflection The helm of reflection was a magic item that could be found within the Hordelands . Description . This item was available in a variety of helmet types . Powers . Especially useful to warriors , this helm reflected " any " magic used against the wearer of the helm back upon the caster .

title: Helmed horror
description: Helmed horror A helmed horror is an animated construct often found as a guardian . Physical description . A helmed horror as an empty suit of armor , with purple magical light flickering between the joints .
description_long: Helmed horror A helmed horror is an animated construct often found as a guardian . Physical description . A helmed horror as an empty suit of armor , with purple magical light flickering between the joints . They often carry a greatsword and a heavy crossbow . Combat . Helmed Horrors fight intelligently . They go after soft foes first and use their magic to outmaneuver foes . Magical Abilities . Helmed Horrors can move through the air , as the spell air walk . They can see unseen creatures and objects , as the spell see invisibility . They are immune to several spells . They can imbue a melee weapon they hold with a magical attack power . History . Helmed Horrors are over 5 , 000 years old . Both Netheril and Imaskar are well known to use helmed horrors . Creation . The process of creating helmed horrors was something of a bad secret for many years . While unknown to the magical community at large , a great number of cleric s of Bane , lich es and evil wizards knew well how to create these constructs . It is now uncommon knowledge .

title: Helmgrove
description: Helmgrove Helmgrove was a wooded area north of the city of Myth Drannor . It is most notable for its use as a watchpost by the Shield of Myth Drannor , in the events leading up to the Fall of Myth Drannor . It no longer exists and its exact location has been lost .
description_long: Helmgrove Helmgrove was a wooded area north of the city of Myth Drannor . It is most notable for its use as a watchpost by the Shield of Myth Drannor , in the events leading up to the Fall of Myth Drannor . It no longer exists and its exact location has been lost .

title: Helmsdale
description: Helmsdale Helmsdale was a small farming town found in Soravia on the border with Brandiar . Description . Helmsdale rested on the banks of the Goliad River south of Ironspur .
description_long: Helmsdale Helmsdale was a small farming town found in Soravia on the border with Brandiar . Description . Helmsdale rested on the banks of the Goliad River south of Ironspur . History . Zhengyi used Helmsdale as his base of operations for the entire duration of the Bloodstone Wars . Because of this many Damarans often referred to the town as " the cursed village " . Inhabitants . This small farming community hosted a population of 500 inhabitants who produced food in support of the dwarves of Ironspur . The population swelled to 4 , 000 when Zhengyi ' s forces occupied the town . Only 78 of the original inhabitants survived to see the Witch - King ' s defeat .

title: Helmsport
description: Helmsport Helmsport was an Amn ian fort on the shore of Payit established by Captain - General Cordell in 1361 DR . It had an anchorage for ships and served as the Golden Legion ' s main base in Maztica . The fort was located on the ocean several miles from the native city of Ulatos .
description_long: Helmsport Helmsport was an Amn ian fort on the shore of Payit established by Captain - General Cordell in 1361 DR . It had an anchorage for ships and served as the Golden Legion ' s main base in Maztica . The fort was located on the ocean several miles from the native city of Ulatos . A full year after Cordell ' s conquest , the town still only had a dozen permanent buildings with many tents and lean - tos .

title: Helmthorn
description: Helmthorn Helmthorn was a hardy , vine - like shrub . Description . The helmthorn got its name from large , imposing black thorns .
description_long: Helmthorn Helmthorn was a hardy , vine - like shrub . Description . The helmthorn got its name from large , imposing black thorns . The thorns could grow as large as a man ' s hand . Its indigo berries were often harvested to be either eaten or fermented into a helmthorn wine . Occasionally , the plant would sprout a spring of red berries . Usage . Helmthorn thorns were used as needles and dart points . Red helmthorn berries could be sold for 1 sp each . When the spell " goodberry " was cast on these berries , it lasted a day longer than usual . Locations . Helmthorn was common throughout Faerûn . Helmthorn brush grew dense in the Forest of Wyrms . It was also common in the High Thorog valley in the Nether Mountains .

title: Helping hand
description: Helping hand Helping hand was an evocation spell that called a spectral hand to lead the subject to the caster . Effects . This spell could be used to summon help or to direct a person within five miles ( 8 km ) to the caster ' s location .
description_long: Helping hand Helping hand was an evocation spell that called a spectral hand to lead the subject to the caster . Effects . This spell could be used to summon help or to direct a person within five miles ( 8 km ) to the caster ' s location . Upon casting the spell , a spectral hand appeared about 1 ft ( 30 cm ) tall and lasted for an hour per level of the caster . The caster then gave a description of the person or creature that the hand was to seek out and the hand flew away at an extremely rapid pace in search of a being that matched the description . The description had to be of the physical likeness of the target , not ambiguous things like profession . The farther the subject was from the caster the longer the search took ; from a few seconds up to four hours at maximum range . If a being matching the description was found , the hand appeared before it and beckoned . If the target followed the hand , it led the the target on the most direct feasible path , hovering 10 ft ( 3 m ) in front and pointing in the direction of the caster . If the subject did not follow the hand , it beckoned until the subject changed their mind or until the spell ran out .

title: Heltharn Dynasty
description: Heltharn Dynasty The Heltharn Dynasty was the fourth of the ruling dynasties of Impiltur . Overview . House Heltharn was the family of paladin war - captain Imphras Heltharn the Great , who united what were four independent cities against a hobgoblin horde in 1095 DR .
description_long: Heltharn Dynasty The Heltharn Dynasty was the fourth of the ruling dynasties of Impiltur . Overview . House Heltharn was the family of paladin war - captain Imphras Heltharn the Great , who united what were four independent cities against a hobgoblin horde in 1095 DR . After his victory the second realm of Impiltur was formed . The dynasty included many paladins as kings and its queens were sorceresses or wizard esses . It included six kings , one queen , two regents , and five others who never ruled but were marked for succession . Its last king was Imbrar II , who died without an heir in the Year of Blue Fire , 1385 DR .

title: Helve ' s Trail
description: Helve ' s Trail Helve ' s Trail was a road in the southern Vast . It ran from Maerstar in the south , where it met the North Road , then into the Earthfast Mountains , where it ended at High Haspur and connected with the High Trail .
description_long: Helve ' s Trail Helve ' s Trail was a road in the southern Vast . It ran from Maerstar in the south , where it met the North Road , then into the Earthfast Mountains , where it ended at High Haspur and connected with the High Trail .

title: Helve Moonstar
description: Helve Moonstar Helve Moonstar was a member of House Moonstar in Waterdeep in 1372 DR . Personality . Helve was rebellious in his past , but matured over time .
description_long: Helve Moonstar Helve Moonstar was a member of House Moonstar in Waterdeep in 1372 DR . Personality . Helve was rebellious in his past , but matured over time . Helve secretly feared that his heir , Rober Moonstar , didn ' t have the qualities needed to lead the house , so he tested all his nieces and nephews hoping to find a better candidate . History . Helve was an officer in the City Guard ' s cavalry until an accident ended his career . To the delight of his father , he devoted himself to his family ' s businesses . The business prospered thanks to his wife ' s guidance .

title: Helve Urtrace
description: Helve Urtrace Helve Urtrace was a City Watch officer in Waterdeep in 1372 DR . Personality . Helve was a old , bald , and quiet man .
description_long: Helve Urtrace Helve Urtrace was a City Watch officer in Waterdeep in 1372 DR . Personality . Helve was a old , bald , and quiet man . Activities . Helve ' s duty as Armsmaster was to manage all weapons used by City Watch officers . If a weapon disappeared , he investigated . He was an expert in weapons and street fighting . Usually , Helve led the second wave of reinforcements if there was danger , usually accompanied by his daughter Lassree Urtrace , a watch - wizard .

title: Helvur Tharnlar
description: Helvur Tharnlar Helvur Tharnlar was a shopkeeper in Red Larch during the Elemental Evil crisis , who once provided a favor for the Lords ' Alliance . Personality . Helvur was a snob .
description_long: Helvur Tharnlar Helvur Tharnlar was a shopkeeper in Red Larch during the Elemental Evil crisis , who once provided a favor for the Lords ' Alliance . Personality . Helvur was a snob . He disliked the local gossip and was always remarking that his hats were trendy in Silverymoon or that his boots were made for Neverwinter aristocrats , despite the fact that he had no idea about those places . Relationship . Helvur was married to Maegla and ran his clothier shop with her .

title: Helyos
description: Helyos Helyos was a mercenary in Chessenta . History . Helyos was one of the best fighters in Chessenta .
description_long: Helyos Helyos was a mercenary in Chessenta . History . Helyos was one of the best fighters in Chessenta . Once he nearly won the throne of Mourktar during a military tournament . He also led the Renegades , a military unit of Akanax , the town of soldiers , who had deserted with dreams of gold and glory .

title: Hematite
description: Hematite Hematite was an ornamental stone that was favored by fighters . Description . When polished , hematite was a shiny gray - black stone .
description_long: Hematite Hematite was an ornamental stone that was favored by fighters . Description . When polished , hematite was a shiny gray - black stone . It was often tumbled to make beads or cut in a baguette fashion ( rectangular with beveled sides ) . Powers . Hematite was not magical itself , but it was responsive to enchantments related to blood and life force and was used in necromancy and the healing arts . Specifically , it was used to create magical periapts for healing and foul rotting . A typical stone had a base value of 10 gp . Only a handful of people ( mostly powerful mages that kept the secret to themselves ) knew that this common stone was one of the " nine secrets " — minerals that could be enchanted to become " ioun stones " .

title: Hemeth
description: Hemeth Hemeth was a duergar arms dealer in Sloobludop until the Rage of Demons . History . Hemeth was originally from Gracklstugh .
description_long: Hemeth Hemeth was a duergar arms dealer in Sloobludop until the Rage of Demons . History . Hemeth was originally from Gracklstugh . During the Rage of Demons , the dwarf heard that the village of Sloobludop had started a civil war , so he went there in order to sell his weapons to both factions . However , Hemeth was captured by cultists , led by Bloppblippoodd , who wanted to sacrifice him to a new god named Leemooggoogoon , the Deep Father ( who was , in truth , the demon lord Demogorgon ) .

title: Hendle
description: Hendle Hendle was a druid from Rashemen and an old member of the Emerald Enclave in 1489 DR . Personality . Hendle was saddened by the loss of treant s in forests .
description_long: Hendle Hendle was a druid from Rashemen and an old member of the Emerald Enclave in 1489 DR . Personality . Hendle was saddened by the loss of treant s in forests . History .
