Patrons included visiting nobles , wealthy merchants , and local notables such as Darfin and Lady Belinda Anteos of the Sword Coast Trader ’ s Bank . Atmosphere . The Council of Guilds used the private dining chambers of the River Shining for many of their meetings , appreciating the air of importance the tavern lended to their affairs . Tavern prices were rather steep but were backed by fantastic service and atmosphere .

title: River Soshenstar
description: River Soshenstar The River Soshenstar was one of the three great rivers of Chult . The river was in the north - central region of the jungle and flowed from the Swamp of Sorrows into the Bay of Chult . The town of Port Nyanzaru was located at its mouth .
description_long: River Soshenstar The River Soshenstar was one of the three great rivers of Chult . The river was in the north - central region of the jungle and flowed from the Swamp of Sorrows into the Bay of Chult . The town of Port Nyanzaru was located at its mouth . The aldani lived in this river , and dragon turtle s were also common near its mouth .

title: River Surbrin
description: River Surbrin The River Surbrin was a river in the Silver Marches . It flowed from the Spine of the World , after which it was joined by the River Rauvin , and later the Goblintide River , the Laughingflow , and Horn Stream . The River Surbrin then fed into the River Dessarin .
description_long: River Surbrin The River Surbrin was a river in the Silver Marches . It flowed from the Spine of the World , after which it was joined by the River Rauvin , and later the Goblintide River , the Laughingflow , and Horn Stream . The River Surbrin then fed into the River Dessarin . The River Surbrin flowed only a few miles to the east of Mithral Hall , north to south along the eastern edge of the Spine of the World . The town of Nesmé sat on the eastern side of the River Surbrin , with a large fortified bridge across it to the stronghold of the Riders of Nesmé .

title: River Talar
description: River Talar The River Talar flowed along the southern fringe of the Shaar plains , providing access to Sheirtalar on the Shining Sea . Geography . The River Talar was fed by both the Shaar and Channath rivers near Shaareach .
description_long: River Talar The River Talar flowed along the southern fringe of the Shaar plains , providing access to Sheirtalar on the Shining Sea . Geography . The River Talar was fed by both the Shaar and Channath rivers near Shaareach . From this joining , the Talar flowed west and north above the Misty Vale to meet the Shining Sea at Talar Bay . The capital of Lapaliiya , Sheirtalar , sat on its north bank .

title: River Tamthew
description: River Tamthew The River Tamthew was a small river found in southern Luiren in the Shining South . Geography . The River Tamthew originated in the heart of the Southern Lluirwood .
description_long: River Tamthew The River Tamthew was a small river found in southern Luiren in the Shining South . Geography . The River Tamthew originated in the heart of the Southern Lluirwood . It flowed on a southern course before emptying into the vast expanse of the Great Sea east of the Dambrathan city of Hazuth .

title: River Tath
description: River Tath The River Tath was one of the three great rivers of Chult . The river was in the western region of the jungle and flowed from the Swamp of Sorrows into the Trackless Sea between the Kobold Mountains and the Mistcliffs . The aldani lived in this river , as in the other large rivers of Chult .
description_long: River Tath The River Tath was one of the three great rivers of Chult . The river was in the western region of the jungle and flowed from the Swamp of Sorrows into the Trackless Sea between the Kobold Mountains and the Mistcliffs . The aldani lived in this river , as in the other large rivers of Chult .

title: River Umber
description: River Umber The River Umber was a fast flowing river , full of cascades , that formed part of the natural border between Aglarond and Thesk . The river has its headwaters in the high glaciers of Thaymount and flowed west . At the town of Nethentir if flowed down the First Escarpment and into Lake Umber , and from there it flowed through the Dragonjaw Mountains into the Sea of Dlurg .
description_long: River Umber The River Umber was a fast flowing river , full of cascades , that formed part of the natural border between Aglarond and Thesk . The river has its headwaters in the high glaciers of Thaymount and flowed west . At the town of Nethentir if flowed down the First Escarpment and into Lake Umber , and from there it flowed through the Dragonjaw Mountains into the Sea of Dlurg . Trade . Vessels could move up and down the river , all the way to the eastern end of Lake Umber . Thay often sent trade ships down the river into the Sea of Dlurg and onto the Sea of Fallen Stars .

title: River Valashar
description: River Valashar The River Valashar was a river in Amn , in the region of the former kingdom of the same name . Geography . The river started in the lower peaks of the Snowflake Mountains in the east of Amn , within the forest of Shilmista .
description_long: River Valashar The River Valashar was a river in Amn , in the region of the former kingdom of the same name . Geography . The river started in the lower peaks of the Snowflake Mountains in the east of Amn , within the forest of Shilmista . The headwaters included three sets of waterfalls , as they poured over cliffs to end in a deep forest pool . From this pool the river continued to the west , leaving the forest and growing larger and faster . It joined with the mighty Amstel River near Trollford , after itself being joined by the Khalleshyr . Description . The Valashar was a wide river that was shallow and calm for up to 20 miles after leaving Shilmista . It picked up volume from springs along its course and deepened . By within 40 miles of Trollford its speed picked up before joining the Amstel River , which was uncrossable . Rumors & Legends . The pool near the headwaters of the River Valashar was said to be inhabited by nereid s .

title: River Vesper
description: River Vesper The River Vesper was a river in the Vast that ran from the Earthspur Mountains to the Dragon Reach . Geography . The River Vesper began in the Earthspur Mountains and descended through the High Country down a long series of heavy waterfalls and rocky cascades .
description_long: River Vesper The River Vesper was a river in the Vast that ran from the Earthspur Mountains to the Dragon Reach . Geography . The River Vesper began in the Earthspur Mountains and descended through the High Country down a long series of heavy waterfalls and rocky cascades . Here the waters were cold and clear . The town of King ' s Reach marked the highest navigable point on the river . Afterwards , the Vesper was wide , slow , and generally calm . It lay in a broad , gradually sloping river valley as it ran by the Troll Mountains , and also left floodplains . These lands made for fertile farmland . The river had several tributaries . The River Vesper could be forded at Viperstongue Ford . As this coincided with the Viperstongue pass through the mountains , it was a strategic crossing . The river emptied into the Dragon Reach in a wide delta , called the Vespermouth . In high summer , its banks turned into fields of stinking mud , producing clams and worms . The city of Calaunt , formerly a village known as " Vespermouth " , sat at the mouth of the Vesper . Activities . The Vesper was a major trade route for goods exported from the Vast .

title: River Xon
description: River Xon The River Xon was a river that lay along the border between Durpar and Ulgarth in southeast Faerûn . To the folk of the Hordelands and followers of the Padhra , it was the Gaya , called the River of Life and the Sacred River . Geography .
description_long: River Xon The River Xon was a river that lay along the border between Durpar and Ulgarth in southeast Faerûn . To the folk of the Hordelands and followers of the Padhra , it was the Gaya , called the River of Life and the Sacred River . Geography . The Gaya was the end point of the great Jumpa River that ran through the Hordelands . The Jumpa ran through the Great Pass of the Yehimal , and there joined the Gaya . As the Xon , it emerged from the Ice Peaks of the Dustwall Mountains . It ran past the Durpari city of Flyndagol on the west bank . At its mouth , it flowed into Xontuil Bay , which emptied into the Golden Water , which joined the Great Sea in the south . Politics . The heavily defended and fortified border between Durpar and Ulgarth lay along the Xon . Industry . The river Xon was where the cosmetic fiertallin — a chalky white material — was gathered . It was exported from Suormpar , a city 20 miles ( 32 kilometers ) down the bay . It was popular in Ulgarth . Significance . The Gaya was sacred to followers of the Padhran religion in the Hordelands .

title: River of Blood
description: River of Blood The River of Blood was a cross - planar feature in the World Tree cosmology of the plane s . It was a huge and stinking river that flowed through many of the fiendish planes , connecting them similarly to how the World Tree connected the celestial planes . The source of the River of Blood was thought to lie somewhere in the Abyss .
description_long: River of Blood The River of Blood was a cross - planar feature in the World Tree cosmology of the plane s . It was a huge and stinking river that flowed through many of the fiendish planes , connecting them similarly to how the World Tree connected the celestial planes . The source of the River of Blood was thought to lie somewhere in the Abyss . The river ran strongest through the Abyss , Blood Rift , and the Nine Hells . It also wound its way through the Barrens of Doom and Despair , Clangor , Fury ' s Heart , Hammergrim , and Nishrek , and ultimately poured out into the Fated Depths . The only fiendish planes not connected by the River of Blood were the Supreme Throne and the Demonweb Pits . Appendix . Notes . The River of Blood is very similar to the River Styx of the Great Wheel cosmology , as described on page 86 of the " Manual of the Planes " .

title: River of Gold
description: River of Gold The River of Gold was a beautiful waterway located on the Island of Gardens within the Corsair Domains off the coast of northwest Zakhara . Description . The river originated atop a high cliff on the island , splitting to the south into two majestic waterfalls .
description_long: River of Gold The River of Gold was a beautiful waterway located on the Island of Gardens within the Corsair Domains off the coast of northwest Zakhara . Description . The river originated atop a high cliff on the island , splitting to the south into two majestic waterfalls . The eastern portion of the river flowed smoothly through jungles as it traveled to the southern regions of the island . Inhabitants . The River of Gold was inhabited by a zin named Zthyz al - Zin who would confront anyone trying to take water .

title: River of Shadows
description: River of Shadows The River of Shadows is a rocky and treacherous waterway located in the nation of Mulhorand . Geography . The River of Shadows flows west from its origin near the Dragonsword Mountains .
description_long: River of Shadows The River of Shadows is a rocky and treacherous waterway located in the nation of Mulhorand . Geography . The River of Shadows flows west from its origin near the Dragonsword Mountains . Its waters empty into the Alamber Sea near the nation ' s capital city of Skuld , from which the river derives its name . Inhabitants . Slave farms can be found near the delta of the River of Shadows , where they produce flax , papyrus , and sheep . The waterway passes the cities of Skuld and Jhalhoran as it flows towards the sea .

title: River of Spears
description: River of Spears The River of Spears provides water to the majority of the farms located in the nation of Mulhorand . Geography . The River of Spears flows west from the Dragonsword Mountains , across the Great Vale , and eventually empties into the Alamber Sea at the city of Gheldaneth .
description_long: River of Spears The River of Spears provides water to the majority of the farms located in the nation of Mulhorand . Geography . The River of Spears flows west from the Dragonsword Mountains , across the Great Vale , and eventually empties into the Alamber Sea at the city of Gheldaneth . Along with its two tributary flows , the Mishtan and the Klondor , this river is heavily irrigated for the purpose of farming ; annual flooding enriches the soil of the surrounding regions with valuable nutrients . Inhabitants . The River of Spears flows past the cities of Gheldaneth , Ulzel , and Surbroar .

title: River of Swords
description: River of Swords The River of Swords served as the border between the lands of Mulhorand and Unther . This river is divided into upper and lower portions at the ruins of Sekras . Upper Sword .
description_long: River of Swords The River of Swords served as the border between the lands of Mulhorand and Unther . This river is divided into upper and lower portions at the ruins of Sekras . Upper Sword . The Upper Sword flows from the ruins of Sekras to the Alamber Sea . Many farms can be found on the river ' s banks , which flood annually . Flat - bottomed boats navigate the Upper Sword , serving as transport between the settlements on both sides . Lower Swords . The Lower Swords refer two two seperate rivers , the Blue Sword and the Green Sword , that converge at the ruins of Sekras . The Blue Sword is composed of fresh water , and lies entirely in the nation of Unther . The Green Sword flows from the Great Salt Lake , and is considered too salty to drink . Inhabitants . The banks of the Upper Sword are inhabited primarily by farmers . The Lower Swords are sparsely populated , home to a handful of hermits and wizards , as well as a small yet notable quantity of sphinxes . The ruins of Sekras are known for its population of werecrocodiles .

title: River of sand
description: River of sand River of sand was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . The spell created a barreling river of sand that was 80 feet ( 24 .
description_long: River of sand River of sand was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . The spell created a barreling river of sand that was 80 feet ( 24 . 4 m ) long . The caster cast the spell with a mouthful of sand and spat it in the direction they wished the river to flow . The caster could not control the length of the river ; it always formed the same length . Nor could the caster change the direction of the river . Once formed , the river of sand rushed over anything in its path . The river struck with enough force to rip clothing and hair from creatures , lift large wagons , or batter objects like a ram . Living creatures engulfed by the river of sand risked suffocation . Components . This spell required a mouthful of sand and a little spittle to cast .

title: River of the Dawn
description: River of the Dawn The River of the Dawn lay between the lands of Mulhorand and Thay . Both nations claimed this waterway as their own , and combat between the forces of both sides erupted on occasion . Geography .
description_long: River of the Dawn The River of the Dawn lay between the lands of Mulhorand and Thay . Both nations claimed this waterway as their own , and combat between the forces of both sides erupted on occasion . Geography . Though both bordering nations claimed land on the opposite shore of the River of the Dawn , this rapid - flowing waterway followed what is generally accepted as the boundary between Mulhorand and Thay . The river ' s waters were crossed at only a single point , a bridge constructed as part of the great eastern trading road . Inhabitants . A single Thayan outpost served to cement the nation ' s claim on the lands surrounding the River of the Dawn , while military patrols in the region provided a similar claim for Mulhorand . In addition , merchants could often be found traveling along the eastern trading road .

title: Rivermoot
description: Rivermoot Rivermoot was a very small town in the Lower Rauvin Vale in the Silver Marches , nestled on the trail between the High Hold and Nesme . It sat between the northern bank of the River Rauvin and the River Surbrin , at the foot of the Frost Hills south of the Spine of the World mountains . It was protected by a sturdy palisade on its east side , and by the two rivers on its south and north - west sides , making it defensible .
description_long: Rivermoot Rivermoot was a very small town in the Lower Rauvin Vale in the Silver Marches , nestled on the trail between the High Hold and Nesme . It sat between the northern bank of the River Rauvin and the River Surbrin , at the foot of the Frost Hills south of the Spine of the World mountains . It was protected by a sturdy palisade on its east side , and by the two rivers on its south and north - west sides , making it defensible . However , during spring , it suffered destructive floods from the two rivers . Therefore , the majority of buildings were built standing on pilings at least 10 feet ( 3 meters ) off the ground . The town was officially a part of Silverymoon ' s lands and a protectorate of the League of the Silver Marches . In this capacity , it benefited from the League ' s common defense and trade agreements , while being unable to support the League itself .

title: Rivershire
description: Rivershire Rivershire was one of the counties of Tethyr and a major agricultural territory . In 1370 DR , it was the most stable of Tethyr ' s counties . Geography .
description_long: Rivershire Rivershire was one of the counties of Tethyr and a major agricultural territory . In 1370 DR , it was the most stable of Tethyr ' s counties . Geography . County Rivershire was located in the Crown Lands , between the Sulduskoon River and the River Ith , east of county Ithmonn and west of county Varyth . Trade . Rivershire was a large producer of pipeweed , fish , and table wines . Nearly all the land and businesses were owned by seven rich families . Government . Zelphar Thann , the Estate Chancellor of Tethyr and relative of Danilo Thann , was the appointed Count of Rivershire . His estate was Lhestyn ' s Hearth , ( named after Zelphar ' s grandmother , ) which was twelve miles north of the capital . Zelphar was not a well - received count — only two of the seven merchant families approved of his leadership . Rumors . While on the surface , this county was stable , political instability seemed on the horizon in 1370 DR , due to rumored schemes among five of the seven Rivershire families to remove Zelphar Thann from power . One such plan involved rumors that Zelphar was courting the Court Vizera , Perendra Raslemtar , solely to gain favor from the queen .

title: Riviar Darkwind
description: Riviar Darkwind Riviar Darkwind was the second - in - command of the Zhentarim military forces of Darkhold and the leader of the elite Storm Watch company in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . Personality . Riviar disliked wizard s ( even Sememmon , though she kept this secret in her heart ) .
description_long: Riviar Darkwind Riviar Darkwind was the second - in - command of the Zhentarim military forces of Darkhold and the leader of the elite Storm Watch company in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . Personality . Riviar disliked wizard s ( even Sememmon , though she kept this secret in her heart ) . She became attracted to Dag Zoreth and hoped he would gain preeminence against the wizards of Darkhold .

title: Riyas
description: Riyas Old Riyas lived atop the highest peaks on the island of Kaff in the Djinni ' s Claws in 1367 DR . Description . Old Riyas was an aging great roc .
description_long: Riyas Old Riyas lived atop the highest peaks on the island of Kaff in the Djinni ' s Claws in 1367 DR . Description . Old Riyas was an aging great roc . Activities . In his youth Old Riyas could pluck whale s from the sea , but as of 1367 DR spent most of his time sleeping .

title: Rizzen Do ' Urden
description: Rizzen Do ' Urden Rizzen , later known as Rizzen Do ' Urden , was the patron of House Do ' Urden until his death . Description . Rizzen was described as " handsome but otherwise unremarkable .
description_long: Rizzen Do ' Urden Rizzen , later known as Rizzen Do ' Urden , was the patron of House Do ' Urden until his death . Description . Rizzen was described as " handsome but otherwise unremarkable . " Personality . Rizzen was very submissive to Matron Mother Malice Do ' Urden and her cruel daughter Briza Do ' Urden . It was no wonder , as they often beat him and threw him into the dungeon on a whim . History . Rizzen was a commoner of House Do ' Urden until he was made patron and allowed to carry the family name . He became patron after the previous patron , Zaknafein Do ' Urden , was stripped of his title . As patron , he was granted a two - room suite inside the complex of House Do ' Urden . In about 1339 DR , Malice tricked Rizzen into engaging the spirit - wraith ( Zin - carla ) Zaknafein in a fight , in which Rizzen was promptly killed . Malice claimed that it was no great loss as she had already chosen her next patron from amongst the soldiers of House Do ' Urden . Skills . Rizzen was trained as a fighter under Zaknafein , but he also had limited wizardly abilities . Relationships . Rizzen was the known father of Nalfein , Dinin , and Maya Do ' Urden .

title: Ro ' kolor
description: Ro ' kolor Ro ' kolor was a drow rogue of Menzoberranzan and a member of Bregan D ' aerthe in 1479 DR . Personality . Ro ' kolor could be influenced by those who showed to him how gain the biggest profit for himself and Bregan D ' aerthe .
description_long: Ro ' kolor Ro ' kolor was a drow rogue of Menzoberranzan and a member of Bregan D ' aerthe in 1479 DR . Personality . Ro ' kolor could be influenced by those who showed to him how gain the biggest profit for himself and Bregan D ' aerthe . He appreciated solutions that maximized gains and minimized losses . History . Ro ' kolor was his organization ' s representative for an alliance with House Xorlarrin and House Melarn in handling a party of adventurer s . They first sent the team to gain power for Lolth ' s Demon Weave scheme . For the expedition , he asked adventurers loyal to his organization to find and capture alive the traitor among the previous party . The traitor was discovered to be the priestess Iyelle Tlabbar . After the adventurers returned from their first mission , Hoshtar Xorlarrin was invited to meet with members of the Council of Spiders by his cousin , Raelaryn Xorlarrin . At the meeting , a Jaezred Chaulssin assassin killed Raelaryn and captured Hoshtar . The alliance ' s hired team managed to rescue him .

title: Road of the Patriarch
description: Road of the Patriarch Road of the Patriarch is the third and final novel of The Sellswords trilogy by R . A . Salvatore .
description_long: Road of the Patriarch Road of the Patriarch is the third and final novel of The Sellswords trilogy by R . A . Salvatore . Summary . Ilnezhara and Tazmikella have ceased their working relationships with Jarlaxle and Artemis . The pair have attracted the attention of both the Citadel of Assassins ( especially Entreri ) and Spysong . Entreri is becoming more confused and self - reflective about himself which is complicated by the fact that he has taken Calihye as his lover . Jarlaxle is more interested in his surface empire , hoping to use the Zhengyian construct as the center of his new realm . Athrogate the dwarf takes to spending the harsh Damaran winter drinking himself into a stupor , planning on resuming his monster hunting in the spring .

title: Road to Enlightenment
description: Road to Enlightenment The Road to Enlightenment , or the Enlightened Way , was located in Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . The Road to Enlightenment was one of the largest streets in Golden Huzuz .
description_long: Road to Enlightenment The Road to Enlightenment , or the Enlightened Way , was located in Huzuz , the City of Delights , in 1367 DR . Description . The Road to Enlightenment was one of the largest streets in Golden Huzuz . It entered the city for the southwest corner at the Gulf Gate , then traveled directly northeast to the courtyard that housed the Golden Mosque and other mosques to the Enlightened gods . The Enlightened Way served as the main boundary between the South District and Peasants ' District before entering the Pilgrims ' District on its approach to the mosques .

title: Roalgan
description: Roalgan Roalgan was the leader of the Shields of the Highland adventuring company in 1370 DR . Description . Roalgan was a very large man with long red hair and a heavy beard .
description_long: Roalgan Roalgan was the leader of the Shields of the Highland adventuring company in 1370 DR . Description . Roalgan was a very large man with long red hair and a heavy beard . He wore chainmail . Personality . Roalgan kept an emotionless expression in the midst of grief . History . Roalgan hailed from one of the villages near the Forest of Mir like all his companions . On Uktar 8 , 1370 DR , the Shields of the Highland lost two of their members while guarding a caravan . Unexpected cold weather led to snow , and a band of fourteen gnoll s were able to track them and attack them , killing two of them during the ensuing battle . At dusk two days later , Roalgan and the other three survivors went to the Blue Badger Inn in the village of Toralth to grieve their loss . They found a bard in the tavern , calling himself Fylson Tarasp , and demanded that he compose a dirge for their two fallen friends . They had no idea that this man was actually a secret agent of the sea elf Gantar Kraok .

title: Roaoum
description: Roaoum Roaoum was a subchief of the Tiger Coral tribe of locathah and a member of the Nantarn Council . Relashionship . Roaoum was the son of chief Cuvis and a long - time acquaintance of merfolk prince Mirol .
description_long: Roaoum Roaoum was a subchief of the Tiger Coral tribe of locathah and a member of the Nantarn Council . Relashionship . Roaoum was the son of chief Cuvis and a long - time acquaintance of merfolk prince Mirol . Activities . Roaoum was the quietest of the councilors , speaking only if requested . Normally he found the discussions boring , caring only for the harvesting of kelp , hunting of fish , food stores for winter , and similar arguments like all his fellow locathah . In truth , Chief Cuvis waited to obtain improved weapons before he would help the alliance more .

title: Roaring Griffon
description: Roaring Griffon The Roaring Griffon ( once The Drowning Fish ) was an inn in Marsember , Cormyr . Location . The inn stood in the south central portion of the westernmost islet , north of its docks .
description_long: Roaring Griffon The Roaring Griffon ( once The Drowning Fish ) was an inn in Marsember , Cormyr . Location . The inn stood in the south central portion of the westernmost islet , north of its docks . The Leaping Eel tavern was located across the street to the west . Structure . The Roaring Griffon was a three - story building . The common room , game room , and a tavern area were located on the first floor , along with a couple of private dining areas . The second floor housed most of the bedrooms , which were of good quality , but the uppermost floor contained truly excellent accommodations . The bedrooms were only accessible via staircases that were always protected by locked doors . Every room key also unlocked the correct stairwell door . Fare . The inn was open from sunrise to midnight and tended to have a steady stream of business . After the name change , its first proprietor was Szwentil , who did a fine job of making the place respectable . Gregarious and chatty sailors and merchants were the normal clientele and it was said that Szwentil , a powerful merchant himself , bought the place mostly so that his customers would have a decent place to stay .

title: Roaring Lion Inn
description: Roaring Lion Inn The Roaring Lion Inn was an inn found in the city of Tantras in the Vast . It was located just off Whistleturn Way , near the Market . It was known as the best inn in the city around 1358 DR , with excellent accommodations but a high price to match .
description_long: Roaring Lion Inn The Roaring Lion Inn was an inn found in the city of Tantras in the Vast . It was located just off Whistleturn Way , near the Market . It was known as the best inn in the city around 1358 DR , with excellent accommodations but a high price to match . However , it was commandeered by the Guard of Tantras for use as an army barracks during the Time of Troubles of that year .

title: Roaringhorn ( Waterdeep )
description: Roaringhorn ( Waterdeep ) Roaringhorn was a noble house of Waterdeep . They bred horses in Amphail , where they owned an estate and personal guard . The head of the family had six nieces , all of whom were wizard s .
description_long: Roaringhorn ( Waterdeep ) Roaringhorn was a noble house of Waterdeep . They bred horses in Amphail , where they owned an estate and personal guard . The head of the family had six nieces , all of whom were wizard s . These nieces used their magic to keep watch for thieves or other ill - doers .

title: Rob Heinsoo
description: Rob Heinsoo Rob Heinsoo is a game developer for Wizards of the Coast . He helped write the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting " and is the designer of Three - Dragon Ante , a unique card game . Other Forgotten Realms works include the sourcebook " Monsters of Faerûn " .
description_long: Rob Heinsoo Rob Heinsoo is a game developer for Wizards of the Coast . He helped write the " Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting " and is the designer of Three - Dragon Ante , a unique card game . Other Forgotten Realms works include the sourcebook " Monsters of Faerûn " . Appendix . External links . Wizards of the Coast profile

title: Robe of gentle repose
description: Robe of gentle repose A robe of gentle repose was a garment that when worn would halt the decomposition process . This was especially valued by undead who wished to maintain the appearance of still being a living creature . Description .
description_long: Robe of gentle repose A robe of gentle repose was a garment that when worn would halt the decomposition process . This was especially valued by undead who wished to maintain the appearance of still being a living creature . Description . The " robe of gentle repose " was an unassuming garment . It appeared as an open - fronted robe of light green . Powers . Especially prized by undead who wished to masquerade as living creatures or simply did not want their bodies to decay , the robe could halt all decay and decomposition of a creature ' s corporeal form whilst worn , operating in much the same fashion as a permanent " gentle repose " spell . History . Around 1372 DR , an example of this item had come into the hands of the lich Umaerh . Thanks to the robe he could still pass for a healthy male drow while he resided in Irae T ' sarran ' s Undying Temple .

title: Roben
description: Roben Roben was a kensai adventurer in Miyama Province in Kozakura in 1357 DR . History . Roben born to a shipping merchant and lived a comfortable life indulging in harmless pleasures .
description_long: Roben Roben was a kensai adventurer in Miyama Province in Kozakura in 1357 DR . History . Roben born to a shipping merchant and lived a comfortable life indulging in harmless pleasures . An old kensai in his village noted Roben ' s talent and offered to teach him . Unsatisfied with his life , Roben accepted . In 1357 DR , his master had taught Roben all he knew and so Roben went to Miyama Province following a rumor about a talented master of the naginata . Appendix . Behind the scenes . Roben is a pre - generated PC for use in adventures in Miyama .

title: Robert J . Kuntz
description: Robert J . Kuntz Robert J . Kuntz is a game designer and one of the first people ever to play Gary Gygax ' Dungeons & Dragons .
description_long: Robert J . Kuntz Robert J . Kuntz is a game designer and one of the first people ever to play Gary Gygax ' Dungeons & Dragons . Career . Kuntz was TSR ' s sixth employee . He was initially hired into the shipping department , yet he was still able to do design work , and he co - authored " Gods , Demi - Gods & Heroes " . Later , he was an author for " Deities and Demigods " , and he wrote for " Dragon " magazine as well . After leaving TSR , Kuntz started his own publishing company , Pied Piper Publishing , which was in existence until 2010 .

title: Robert J . Schwalb
description: Robert J . Schwalb Robert J . Schwalb is a writer in the roleplaying game industry .
description_long: Robert J . Schwalb Robert J . Schwalb is a writer in the roleplaying game industry . His works for " Dungeons & Dragons " include : " " ( 2006 , with Robin Laws ) , " Drow of the Underdark " ( 2007 , with Ari Marmell , Anthony Pryor , and Greg A . Vaughan ) , " Elder Evils " ( 2007 ) , " Exemplars of Evil " ( 2007 ) , " Tome of Magic " ( 2006 , with Matthew Sernett , Dave Noonan , and Ari Marmell ) , " Players Handbook II " ( 2006 ) He has also done work for and , and contributed to " " for ( 2007 ) . Schwalb became the writer for the online version of the popular " Dragon " column " Demonomicon of Iggwilv " in 2008 , having thus far contributed articles for Yeenoghu and Baphomet .

title: Robert Lazzaretti
description: Robert Lazzaretti Robert Lazzarettii ( also credited as Rob Lazzaretti ) is an American fantasy cartographer . He took up strategy gaming during high school , and attended Lincoln College and Illinois State University . He took up a path to Game Designers Workshop and took to map illustration mainly because nobody else in his department enjoyed the role .
description_long: Robert Lazzaretti Robert Lazzarettii ( also credited as Rob Lazzaretti ) is an American fantasy cartographer . He took up strategy gaming during high school , and attended Lincoln College and Illinois State University . He took up a path to Game Designers Workshop and took to map illustration mainly because nobody else in his department enjoyed the role . He moved to TSR in 1993 and ended up at Wizards of the Coast after the 1997 acquisition . Due to budget cuts in the years that followed , Lazzaretti was forced into a freelance career , and regularly contributes for Paizo Publishing and Hasbro Games .

title: Robert Wiese
description: Robert Wiese Robert Wiese is a biochemist and a former game designer for Wizards of the Coast . Career . Wiese was a long - time player in the RPGA who eventually worked for the RPGA for seven years .
description_long: Robert Wiese Robert Wiese is a biochemist and a former game designer for Wizards of the Coast . Career . Wiese was a long - time player in the RPGA who eventually worked for the RPGA for seven years . He has written over 60 adventures , several articles , and several web enhancements for Forgotten Realms sourcebooks . He left the gaming industry and , as of 2005 , was working as a biochemist for the University of Nevada .

title: Robillard
description: Robillard Robillard was a powerful wizard and close ally of Deudermont . He served as the second - in - command on Deudermont ' s vessel , the " Sea Sprite " and was a former member of the Arcane Brotherhood . He was a capable magic user and was even skilled in the art of healing , aiding Deudermont after an assassination attempt , an act which helped save the life of Wulfgar the barbarian ; had Deudermont not woken , Wulfgar would have been falsely executed for the alleged assassination attempt , a crime which Deudermont confirmed he did not commit .
description_long: Robillard Robillard was a powerful wizard and close ally of Deudermont . He served as the second - in - command on Deudermont ' s vessel , the " Sea Sprite " and was a former member of the Arcane Brotherhood . He was a capable magic user and was even skilled in the art of healing , aiding Deudermont after an assassination attempt , an act which helped save the life of Wulfgar the barbarian ; had Deudermont not woken , Wulfgar would have been falsely executed for the alleged assassination attempt , a crime which Deudermont confirmed he did not commit . Robilliard ' s power became even more evident when he singlehandedly defeated Arklem Greeth , a lich and the former Archmage Arcane of the Arcane Brotherhood . This battle , however , pulled the wizard from his captain ' s side , allowing High Captain Kensidan of Luskan to bait and kill Captain Deudermont .

title: Robyn Kendrick
description: Robyn Kendrick Robyn Kendrick was the ward of the king of Caer Corwell . Description . Robyn was a beautiful young lady with bright green eyes and thick black hair .
description_long: Robyn Kendrick Robyn Kendrick was the ward of the king of Caer Corwell . Description . Robyn was a beautiful young lady with bright green eyes and thick black hair . Possessions . Unlike most ladies on Corwell , Robyn wore a rust - colored over her dark green . She also wore a torque that she found in a firbolg stronghold while rescuing Keren Donnell . Abilities . At the beginning of her adventures , Robyn used the spells " entangle " and " heat metal " , both while fighting firbolgs . Relationships . Robyn was friends with the halfling Pawldo and felt a strong connection to Tristan Kendrick . History . Robyn found out by accident she had druid ic powers while fighting a group of firbolgs in Llaryth Forest .

title: Roc
description: Roc Rocs were gargantuan eagle - like birds that inhabited the highest mountains in warm regions . As large as these great birds were , they paled in both size and ferocity to the mighty Zakharan roc s of the Land of Fate . Ecology .
description_long: Roc Rocs were gargantuan eagle - like birds that inhabited the highest mountains in warm regions . As large as these great birds were , they paled in both size and ferocity to the mighty Zakharan roc s of the Land of Fate . Ecology . Rocs were birds of such immense size that they were known to snatch horses ( and their riders ) , elephants , and even whales to feed upon . They preyed upon large creatures such as cattle , horses , and elephants . The roc swept down upon prey , seized it in its powerful talons , and carried it off to its lair to feed . If the prey resisted , the roc would strike with its beak . The lair of a roc was be a vast nest of trees , branches , and the like . Its treasure was strewn about , for the creature did not place any value upon it . Rocs were occasionally tamed and used by giant s . Rocs often guarded the nests of simurgh s until they were mature . Rocs were usually solitary , but sometimes found in mated pairs . History . Lord Charles Frederik LaVerne Blacktree IV was known for wearing a roc feather in his hat .

title: Rock crab
description: Rock crab Rock crabs were a variety of crabs endemic to the River Esmur , in Returned Abeir . Because of this , rock crabs were coveted in many other regions of the continent , and the merchants and fishers of Tarsith made lots of money exporting the crabs to other regions . Rock crabs were prepared by rolling its flesh into balls and later baking them .

title: Rock crystal
description: Rock crystal Rock crystal was another name for colorless , transparent . Description . This clear semi - precious stone was considered lower grade if it was soft or brittle , but was frequently used to adorn furniture or decorative head gear .
description_long: Rock crystal Rock crystal was another name for colorless , transparent . Description . This clear semi - precious stone was considered lower grade if it was soft or brittle , but was frequently used to adorn furniture or decorative head gear . High grade samples free from impurities were used for optics , eyeglasses , magnifying glasses , and prisms . A typical specimen had a base value of 50 gp . Powers . When a spell required an unspecified gem of a certain value , rock crystals were generally used . There was a process that could turn a quantity of rock crystals into a molten glass - like state that allowed it to be worked into weapons and other implements . When it cooled , the rock crystal was hard enough to be used for mace heads , spear heads , ram heads , or even climbing spikes . The process required three spells ; two of which were minor but kept secret , and " Veladar ' s vambrace " .

title: Rock gnome
description: Rock gnome Rock gnomes are a curious , childlike race very much unlike their cousins , the " svirfneblin " or deep gnomes and the forest gnome s . When most people think of gnome s , they are thinking of the rock gnome . Rock gnomes embody the characteristics of their creator and patron deity , Garl Glittergold , choosing to spend their long lives by filling each day with as much fun and enjoyment as possible .
description_long: Rock gnome Rock gnomes are a curious , childlike race very much unlike their cousins , the " svirfneblin " or deep gnomes and the forest gnome s . When most people think of gnome s , they are thinking of the rock gnome . Rock gnomes embody the characteristics of their creator and patron deity , Garl Glittergold , choosing to spend their long lives by filling each day with as much fun and enjoyment as possible . Description . Rock gnomes are typically between 3 to 3½ feet tall and weigh anywhere from 40 to 45 lbs . They possess a natural brownish tint to their skin ; the presence or absence of light has little effect upon it . Young rock gnomes possess any of a large number of hair colors that fades to gray or white upon reaching adulthood . Male gnomes typically keep beards groomed in a neat manner . Personality . Rock gnomes possess many of the traits other races , particularly humans , attribute to children . Most rock gnomes enjoy life to their very fullest ; asking questions endlessly , playing pranks on friends and strangers , and finding new and interesting hobbies are just a few of the countless chores that rock gnomes burden each day with .

title: Rock of Bral
description: Rock of Bral The Rock of Bral was one of the asteroids making up the Tears of Selûne , which orbited the planet Toril behind its moon Selûne . Government . The Rock was ruled by Prince Andru , grandson of a bandit king named Cozar , but several other factions wielded power as well .
description_long: Rock of Bral The Rock of Bral was one of the asteroids making up the Tears of Selûne , which orbited the planet Toril behind its moon Selûne . Government . The Rock was ruled by Prince Andru , grandson of a bandit king named Cozar , but several other factions wielded power as well . People . Gamalon Idogyr of Tethyr lived on Bral for several decades in the 14th century and met and married his wife Mynda there . Gamalon maintained a curio shop on the Rock . Elminster Aumar and Haedrak Rhindaun III had also traveled there on occasion to visit him . Locations . Despite the Rock being a haven for pirates , it was also home to the only temple to Tyr , god of justice , in Realmspace that did not lie on the planet of Toril . The Pantheist Temple of Tyr was home to priests who held a number of non - standard religious views , but nevertheless they felt compelled to fight crime and injustice wherever they found it . Thus , they waged a number of crusades and wars on crime on the Rock of Bral . Needless to say , the Tyrrans and their god were not popular on Bral . Miscellaneous . Rock of Bral cuisine had some unique dishes .

title: Rock of Fasting
description: Rock of Fasting The Rock of Fasting was located within the fortress of Sarahin in the Haunted Lands . Description . This 600 ft .
description_long: Rock of Fasting The Rock of Fasting was located within the fortress of Sarahin in the Haunted Lands . Description . This 600 ft . ( 180m ) pillar of stone was only accessible by a single narrow rope bridge . Activities . The Rock of Fasting served as the prison for Sarahin . It was scorching hot under the rays of the sun , and freezing during the night when frost formed on every surface . Inhabitants . The rope bridge leading to the Rock of Fasting was guarded by a wind walker . In the event of a rescue attempt , the wind walker would destroy the bridge . Prisoners attempting to escape would be buffeted until they fell to their deaths on the rocks below .

title: Rockbottom
description: Rockbottom Rockbottom was a dwarf cleric . He was part of an expedition that accompanied the Companions of the Hall to Shallows in 1370 DR , only to be attacked by orc s and frost giant s , and did what he could to heal Withegroo Seian ' Doo and Bruenor Battlehammer .
description_long: Rockbottom Rockbottom was a dwarf cleric . He was part of an expedition that accompanied the Companions of the Hall to Shallows in 1370 DR , only to be attacked by orc s and frost giant s , and did what he could to heal Withegroo Seian ' Doo and Bruenor Battlehammer .

title: Rocktappers
description: Rocktappers The Rocktappers of the Earthfasts were an association of people who worked and explored the Earthfast Mountains in the Vast and Impiltur . They consisted largely of lone prospectors , fur trappers , and other mountain folk , and were often hermits or outcasts of mainstream society . Their numbers were highly variable and difficult to estimate , and fluctuated as new people ventured into mountains , old members gave up and returned to civilization , and others died in the wilderness .
description_long: Rocktappers The Rocktappers of the Earthfasts were an association of people who worked and explored the Earthfast Mountains in the Vast and Impiltur . They consisted largely of lone prospectors , fur trappers , and other mountain folk , and were often hermits or outcasts of mainstream society . Their numbers were highly variable and difficult to estimate , and fluctuated as new people ventured into mountains , old members gave up and returned to civilization , and others died in the wilderness . They formed a very loose and disconnected group , always traveling alone . However , they left signs and supplies for fellow Rocktappers , not out of a real desire to aid one another but to ensure that they themselves could be similarly aided in future . One thing they did together was to gather every autumn on a particular outcrop of the southwest flank of the Earthfasts , from which they could view the city of Lyrabar and Tower Pureheart . They spent a week enjoying a rough and noisy party before finally wandering into Lyrabar to sell their goods . Rocktappers acquired colorful nicknames such as Bearface Giltch and Goldsniffin ' Hoots .

title: Rocnest
description: Rocnest Rocnest was a high , rocky outcrop and natural citadel in Evereska that had housed elven garrisons for nearly a thousand years since the Crown Wars . Though the fortress was abandoned after the fall of Aryvandaar , its location between Evereska and the Greycloak Hills meant that the elves of Evereska continued to maintain it as a watch post . History .
description_long: Rocnest Rocnest was a high , rocky outcrop and natural citadel in Evereska that had housed elven garrisons for nearly a thousand years since the Crown Wars . Though the fortress was abandoned after the fall of Aryvandaar , its location between Evereska and the Greycloak Hills meant that the elves of Evereska continued to maintain it as a watch post . History . Around 1371 DR , Nightal 30 , Rocnest was lost when forces from Waterdeep led by Khelben " Blackstaff " Arunsun were too late to turn the tide against the phaerimm in the Battle of Rocnest .

title: Rod
description: Rod A rod is a scepterlike magical device that have unique magical powers . Anyone can use a rod . Realmslore .
description_long: Rod A rod is a scepterlike magical device that have unique magical powers . Anyone can use a rod . Realmslore . Rods are popular in Mulhorand Dreadmaster s of Bane have a special affinity for rods , and often create them . It ' s known that some spellcasters carry rods in sheaths on their hips . After the Spellplague . The Spellplague changed the nature of rods in the Realms . Rods , which are much like larger wand s , are a type of magical implement most commonly used by warlock s but sometimes by artificer s as well . Infused with dark , eldritch energy rods often possess the touch of some creature with which a warlock has formed a pact . As such , many rods are particularly potent in the hands of specific warlocks , who have forged the appropriate pacts with outsider s .

title: Rod of Four Moons
description: Rod of Four Moons The Rod of Four Moons was the favored weapon of the Faerûn ian moon goddess Selûne . Uses . The weapon was a " + 5 defending disruption holy heavy mace " .
description_long: Rod of Four Moons The Rod of Four Moons was the favored weapon of the Faerûn ian moon goddess Selûne . Uses . The weapon was a " + 5 defending disruption holy heavy mace " . Notes . In the Faiths & Avatars sourcebook , the " Rod of Four Moons " was an actual rod and the wielder could fight with it or use it as a wand of paralyzation , a wand of polymorphing , a wand of lightning , a wand of security , or a rod of resurrection .

title: Rod of cats
description: Rod of cats A rod of cats is a black wooden rod seven feet ( 2 . 1m ) in length , with a carved cat ' s head at one end . It is a magic + 1 quarterstaff and when held , it improves the wielder ' s ability to " climb " , " hide " , " move silently " and see in the dark or low light .
description_long: Rod of cats A rod of cats is a black wooden rod seven feet ( 2 . 1m ) in length , with a carved cat ' s head at one end . It is a magic + 1 quarterstaff and when held , it improves the wielder ' s ability to " climb " , " hide " , " move silently " and see in the dark or low light . Once per day , the wielder can use the rod to cast " darkness " , and anyone holding the rod is immune to this spell ' s effects . There is a hidden compartment in the rod but it is only large enough to hold a scroll or some thieves ' tools . The rod is worth around 25 , 000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of displacement
description: Rod of displacement The rod of displacement was invented when Myth Drannor was in its prime and it acts like a " minor globe of displacement " when held . It allows the wielder to use " jump " and " knock " twice per day . Once a day , the wielder can create a sphere five feet ( 1 .
description_long: Rod of displacement The rod of displacement was invented when Myth Drannor was in its prime and it acts like a " minor globe of displacement " when held . It allows the wielder to use " jump " and " knock " twice per day . Once a day , the wielder can create a sphere five feet ( 1 . 5m ) in radius that will displace water , so it can be used to cross rivers or travel underwater . The sphere constantly generates air , and expires after ten minutes . The rod is worth around 48 , 000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of divergence
description: Rod of divergence A rod of divergence is constructed to act against one type of energy , and provides " resist energy " for that type of energy . It can produce " faerie fire " at will , and once per day , the rod will automatically spell turn any incoming spell of the rod ' s energy type , provided it can be turned . The rod is worth around 33 , 000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of fury
description: Rod of fury Rods of fury were the creation of the wizard s of Mulhorand and usually have the end carved into the shape of a Mulhorandi deity . The rods give varying levels of protection between + 1 and + 5 , and once per day , the rod can use " Empower Spell " . Depending on the quality of the rod , it can be worth between 27 , 000 gold pieces and 96 , 000 gold pieces .

Depending on the quality of the rod , it can be worth between 27 , 000 gold pieces and 96 , 000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of leadership
description: Rod of leadership The rod of leadership was a magical item that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . This item appeared as a stout rod that could actually be used as a potent melee weapon .
description_long: Rod of leadership The rod of leadership was a magical item that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . This item appeared as a stout rod that could actually be used as a potent melee weapon . Powers . Coveted by warriors and priests alike , the " rod of leadership " inspired all those within 120 yards ( 110 m ) of the wielder with fanatical loyalty and morale . Those within 30 yards ( 27 m ) of the wielder were completely immune to all forms of magically induced " fear " . When wielded as a weapon , the rod of leadership could paralyze targets at the will of the wielder , though using this power drained the rod of all magical properties .

title: Rod of mirrors
description: Rod of mirrors A rod of mirrors gives the holder the ability to make an insubstantial round mirror at its end , two feet ( 0 . 6m ) in diameter , which lasts for eleven minutes , and when the holder looks through the back , sees as the spell " true seeing " . The holder is also immune to all gaze attacks and illusion effects coming from the other side of the mirror .
description_long: Rod of mirrors A rod of mirrors gives the holder the ability to make an insubstantial round mirror at its end , two feet ( 0 . 6m ) in diameter , which lasts for eleven minutes , and when the holder looks through the back , sees as the spell " true seeing " . The holder is also immune to all gaze attacks and illusion effects coming from the other side of the mirror . The first of these rods was created by the wizard Glendar , and each is worth around 40 , 000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of rulership
description: Rod of rulership A rod of rulership enabled its wielder to impose his or her will to would - be subjects . They felt a wave of compulsion washing over them , a telepathic call to fall to their knees and obey the wielder . Persons of strong mind could withstand its effect though .
description_long: Rod of rulership A rod of rulership enabled its wielder to impose his or her will to would - be subjects . They felt a wave of compulsion washing over them , a telepathic call to fall to their knees and obey the wielder . Persons of strong mind could withstand its effect though . The rod appeared as a jeweled scepter wrought of solid gold . It was often favored by chieftains and tribal leaders .

title: Rod of silence
description: Rod of silence A rod of silence was carved with symbols of cat s ' paws and owl s . Powers . It gave the holder the ability to cast " silence " once per day on himself or herself , although the silence affected nobody else .
description_long: Rod of silence A rod of silence was carved with symbols of cat s ' paws and owl s . Powers . It gave the holder the ability to cast " silence " once per day on himself or herself , although the silence affected nobody else . Unless the silence was in effect , the holder could also use " shout " once per day . While the rod was being held , the holder was better able to resist sonic effects . It was worth around 24 , 000 gold piece s .

title: Rod of smiting
description: Rod of smiting Rods of smiting were magical item s that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Rods by the same name could be found elsewhere in Toril . Powers .
description_long: Rod of smiting Rods of smiting were magical item s that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Rods by the same name could be found elsewhere in Toril . Powers . These rods had all of the powers of their non - Zakharan counterparts , but also had the chance to completely destroy copper automaton s or living idol s .

title: Rod of spheres
description: Rod of spheres A rod of spheres allows its wielder to create up to three spheres per day . These spheres are four feet ( 1 . 2m ) in diameter and float a few feet off the ground .
description_long: Rod of spheres A rod of spheres allows its wielder to create up to three spheres per day . These spheres are four feet ( 1 . 2m ) in diameter and float a few feet off the ground . They can be used to carry items up to 200lbs ( 91kg ) and they will follow their creator for up to two hours until they disappear , or they will disappear immediately if they take any damage . The items within a destroyed sphere will float to the ground just like they were affected by a " feather fall " spell . The rod is worth around 3000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of surprises
description: Rod of surprises A rod of surprises is a magic rod that can be extended up to 60 feet ( 20m ) and support up to 800 pounds ( 363kg ) . It is worth around 22 , 000 gold pieces . A rod of surprises can store a message up to 25 words , and works like the " magic mouth " spell .
description_long: Rod of surprises A rod of surprises is a magic rod that can be extended up to 60 feet ( 20m ) and support up to 800 pounds ( 363kg ) . It is worth around 22 , 000 gold pieces . A rod of surprises can store a message up to 25 words , and works like the " magic mouth " spell . It can also transform into a + 1 version of any of the following weapons :

title: Rod of the monolith
description: Rod of the monolith The rod of of the monolith was a magical item that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . This item resembled a short staff .
description_long: Rod of the monolith The rod of of the monolith was a magical item that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . This item resembled a short staff . Powers . The wielder of this item could control the creature released by the powerful " unleash monolith " spell . The wielder could issue commands to the summoned monolith and even dismiss the creature back to its elemental plane . The elemental monolith had a chance to resist the commands of the wielder . Maintaining control of a monolith drained power from the rod during each minute of control .

title: Rod of the twisted Weave
description: Rod of the twisted Weave The rod of the twisted Weave was an item with properties similar to a " rod of absorption " except instead of storing spell energy it released it as a backlash of negative energy . Description . A " rod of the twisted Weave " was a long scepter that tapered to a point at one end made of a black - colored material .
description_long: Rod of the twisted Weave The rod of the twisted Weave was an item with properties similar to a " rod of absorption " except instead of storing spell energy it released it as a backlash of negative energy . Description . A " rod of the twisted Weave " was a long scepter that tapered to a point at one end made of a black - colored material . The other end of the rod was constructed with intricate strands that had been woven loosely together . Nestled amid this basket of strands was a plume of pale green raw magical energy . Powers . Similar to a " rod of absorption " , the " rod of the twisted Weave " could absorb incoming spells and spell - like abilities that targeted the wielder or the wielder ' s possessions . However , unlike a " rod of absorption " , the " rod of the twisted Weave " did not store spell energy for later use . Instead it immediately released is as a backlash of negative energy that targeted the original caster of the spell . Furthermore , certain spells , like " negative energy protection " , could ward an individual against the negative energy backlash and undead spellcasters were even healed by this effect . History .

title: Rod of tuning
description: Rod of tuning A rod of tuning can produce any tuning note , which is useful for bard s or clerics of Milil when tuning musical instruments , but it is also capable of creating other , magical notes , with powerful effects . Once per day it can create a note that acts as a " holy word " spell to any evil creatures within 30 feet ( 10m ) . Also , once per day it can create a note that acts as a " banishment " spell to outsider s within 30 feet .
description_long: Rod of tuning A rod of tuning can produce any tuning note , which is useful for bard s or clerics of Milil when tuning musical instruments , but it is also capable of creating other , magical notes , with powerful effects . Once per day it can create a note that acts as a " holy word " spell to any evil creatures within 30 feet ( 10m ) . Also , once per day it can create a note that acts as a " banishment " spell to outsider s within 30 feet . This note has three aspects that the creature hates . The rod can act as a focus for any song - based or sonic spell . It is worth around 85 , 000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of viscid globs
description: Rod of viscid globs A rod of viscid globs was a silver rod that could fire up to five sticky spheres per day , up to 100 feet ( 30m ) . These spheres acted like tanglefoot bag s , and the spheres dissolved quickly in alcohol . The rod was worth around 6 , 000 gold pieces .
description_long: Rod of viscid globs A rod of viscid globs was a silver rod that could fire up to five sticky spheres per day , up to 100 feet ( 30m ) . These spheres acted like tanglefoot bag s , and the spheres dissolved quickly in alcohol . The rod was worth around 6 , 000 gold pieces .

title: Rod of whips
description: Rod of whips A rod of whips was a magic rod that could be commanded to transform into a " + 1 dancing whip " by sprouting a tendril of force . It functioned three times per day , with each transformation lasting for an hour . This whip acted as a " spiritual weapon " against incorporeal creatures .
description_long: Rod of whips A rod of whips was a magic rod that could be commanded to transform into a " + 1 dancing whip " by sprouting a tendril of force . It functioned three times per day , with each transformation lasting for an hour . This whip acted as a " spiritual weapon " against incorporeal creatures . The rod was worth around 21 , 600 gold piece s . It could be created with " animate objects " and " spiritual weapon " spells .

title: Roddy McGristle
description: Roddy McGristle Roddy McGristle was a human bounty hunter . He wielded an axe named Bleeder , and was usually accompanied by a pair of hunting dogs . After the deaths of the Thistledown farming family at the hands of the barghest whelp Ulgulu ( who was disguised as a drow during the act ) , a bounty was placed on the head of the Drizzt Do ' Urden .
description_long: Roddy McGristle Roddy McGristle was a human bounty hunter . He wielded an axe named Bleeder , and was usually accompanied by a pair of hunting dogs . After the deaths of the Thistledown farming family at the hands of the barghest whelp Ulgulu ( who was disguised as a drow during the act ) , a bounty was placed on the head of the Drizzt Do ' Urden . Roddy McGristle left Maldobar to find Drizzt , eventually finding and attacking him with Bleeder and his two dogs . During the fight the agile drow killed one of the dogs in self - defense and McGristle lost an ear . McGristle eventually tracked Drizzt to Mooshie ' s Grove , the haven of the famous ranger Montolio Debrouchee . There , he allied himself with the local orcs ( led by their king , Graul ) in the hopes of revenging himself on the drow . Montolio and Drizzt repelled their subsequent assault on Mooshie ' s Grove , and McGristle was captured by the elf Kellindill , an associate of the ranger Dove Falconhand . The quickling Tephanis , searching for a new master ( the previous three having been killed by Drizzt or his associates ) , cut McGristle ' s bonds , allowing the bounty hunter to overpower and murder his elven captor .

title: Roderick Tem
description: Roderick Tem Roderick Tem was a male human leader of the Fire Knives during the Time of Troubles . History . Roderick was the leader of the Fire Knives during the Time of Troubles in 1358 .
description_long: Roderick Tem Roderick Tem was a male human leader of the Fire Knives during the Time of Troubles . History . Roderick was the leader of the Fire Knives during the Time of Troubles in 1358 . Roderick and his men had just occupied Dembling Castle when the god Bane called to him the souls of all assassin s and Roderick and his men all died instantly .

title: Roderik Hilltopple
description: Roderik Hilltopple Roderik Hilltopple was a strongheart halfling shepherd sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Roderik was captured by the hill giant s of Chief Guh and taken as a prisoner to Grudd Haug .
description_long: Roderik Hilltopple Roderik Hilltopple was a strongheart halfling shepherd sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Roderik was captured by the hill giant s of Chief Guh and taken as a prisoner to Grudd Haug . There , the goblin cooks wanted to roast Roderik alive and serve it up to Guh . However , he was saved by an adventuring party but refused to escape without taking some sheep for his trouble .

title: Roderin Obarskyr
description: Roderin Obarskyr King Roderin Obarskyr , or Roderin the Bastard , was crowned the king of Cormyr after the reign of Gantharla Obarskyr in 261 DR . He succeeded her despite his illegitimacy due to the support of the Silver families and Baerauble . Unfortunately , he did not have an heir when he died and was succeeded by his mother ' s cousin Thargreve .
description_long: Roderin Obarskyr King Roderin Obarskyr , or Roderin the Bastard , was crowned the king of Cormyr after the reign of Gantharla Obarskyr in 261 DR . He succeeded her despite his illegitimacy due to the support of the Silver families and Baerauble . Unfortunately , he did not have an heir when he died and was succeeded by his mother ' s cousin Thargreve .

title: Rodolfo
description: Rodolfo Rodolfo was the most veteran navigator of the Trackless Sea . History . Rodolfo was a sailor who knew the Trackless Sea very well .
description_long: Rodolfo Rodolfo was the most veteran navigator of the Trackless Sea . History . Rodolfo was a sailor who knew the Trackless Sea very well . He once acted as fleet commander for the Golden Legion . Afterward he retired but , in 1361 DR , Rodolfo accepted an offer to act as fleet commander for Don Vaez ' s expedition after the Council of Six offered him a large amount of money .

title: Roe
description: Roe Roe was a male human Watch lieutenant of the city of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . Activities . Roe was the lieutenant of the Watch .
description_long: Roe Roe was a male human Watch lieutenant of the city of Neverwinter on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . Activities . Roe was the lieutenant of the Watch . History . Roe was Neverwinter Watch ' s lieutenant . He served the Watch with a great loyalty . If the Kalach - Cha sided with the watch , Roe would eventually die in a fire at the city guardhouse made by Moire .

title: Roejan Benster
description: Roejan Benster Roejan Benster was a Veteran Thief of the Shadowmasters of Telflamm in 1370 DR . Personality . Roejan was a scheming man with an ugly appearance but an agreeable personality .
description_long: Roejan Benster Roejan Benster was a Veteran Thief of the Shadowmasters of Telflamm in 1370 DR . Personality . Roejan was a scheming man with an ugly appearance but an agreeable personality . By 1370 DR , his devotion to Mask began to wane . His supreme goal was the position of Guildmaster , but Roejan had too few cronies under him . He wanted to expand the ranks of those loyal to him , hoping to challenge Keshna Finlothleer one day or to be in the right place in case she encountered an " accident " . History . In 1370 , Roejan was a powerful member of the Shadowmasters , with a retinue of a dozen followers .

title: Rog ' osto
description: Rog ' osto Located about 250 miles up the Nogaro River from Dihliz , the Zakhara n city of Rog ' osto was famed for its strange and lofty towers of bright metal . It was believed that this was once the site of the capital of the now - fallen kingdom of Nog .
description_long: Rog ' osto Located about 250 miles up the Nogaro River from Dihliz , the Zakhara n city of Rog ' osto was famed for its strange and lofty towers of bright metal . It was believed that this was once the site of the capital of the now - fallen kingdom of Nog .

title: Roge Applewink
description: Roge Applewink Roge Applewink was a large halfling farmer in the Moonsea . Activities . Roge regularly sold his products to Reyill Werned .
description_long: Roge Applewink Roge Applewink was a large halfling farmer in the Moonsea . Activities . Roge regularly sold his products to Reyill Werned . History . His partnership with Reyill was very good for Roge ' s businesses during the years . During the Rage of Demons in 1491 DR Roge was drinking with his halfling s friends and Reyill at the Plodding Plow , in the village of The Stop . Relationship . Roge was friend of Narder Ulthub and Guylian Stundter . He had good dealing with Reyill Werned .

title: Roger E . Moore
description: Roger E . Moore Roger E . Moore is a writer of roleplaying games best known for his long - running tenure as editor of Dragon magazine , and was the founding editor of Dungeon magazine .
description_long: Roger E . Moore Roger E . Moore is a writer of roleplaying games best known for his long - running tenure as editor of Dragon magazine , and was the founding editor of Dungeon magazine . Background . Moore discovered roleplaying games in the late 1970s while writing gaming articles for various magazines while he was with the U . S . Army . He joined TSR , Inc . as a magazine editor in May 1983 , progressing through the ranks to become the editor of both Dungeon and Dragon magazines . He later moved to the games division and became creative director of the AD & D core rules product group . He joined Wizards of the Coast in 1997 when TSR , Inc . was acquired and continued to write and edit gaming materials of all sorts , finally leaving the company in late 2000 . Roger Moore is also a past member of the Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers of America .

title: Rogrotus
description: Rogrotus Rogrotus was a black dragon living near the Well of Dragons . History . When the Cult of the Dragon attempted to summon Tiamat into the world at the Well of Dragons , Rogrotus was one of the chromatic dragon heralds sent to ensure the coming of the Dragon Queen .
description_long: Rogrotus Rogrotus was a black dragon living near the Well of Dragons . History . When the Cult of the Dragon attempted to summon Tiamat into the world at the Well of Dragons , Rogrotus was one of the chromatic dragon heralds sent to ensure the coming of the Dragon Queen .

title: Rogue
description: Rogue Rogues were versatile masters of stealth , combat , and various skillful tricks . Where other adventurers had the power to defeat their enemies , rogues used their wits and their natural resourcefulness to exploit their foes ' vulnerabilities as well as to lead their allies safely through dangerous environments , disarming traps and opening lock along the way . Several well - known rogues of Toril include Ravenscar of Baldur ' s Gate , Regis of the Companions of the Hall , and Mirt of Waterdeep .
description_long: Rogue Rogues were versatile masters of stealth , combat , and various skillful tricks . Where other adventurers had the power to defeat their enemies , rogues used their wits and their natural resourcefulness to exploit their foes ' vulnerabilities as well as to lead their allies safely through dangerous environments , disarming traps and opening lock along the way . Several well - known rogues of Toril include Ravenscar of Baldur ' s Gate , Regis of the Companions of the Hall , and Mirt of Waterdeep . Culture . Common to most cities in Faerûn , rogues were an incredibly diverse group , included burglars , assassins , and con artists as well as more lawfully employed persons , like locksmiths , investigators , exterminators , or treasure hunters . To a large extent , the criminal sort of rogue was considered more typical and both thieves ' and assassins ' guild s were found widely throughout the world , some of which were incredibly powerful , such as the Shadow Thieves . Regardless of their specific occupation , rogues shared a common affinity for cunning and daring feats of skill , as well as for getting into things others would rather be left unfound or unopened .

title: Rogue stone
description: Rogue stone A rogue stone ( sometimes written roguestone ) was a small , extremely rare magical gemstone with a tendency to cause wild magic . Description . Rogue stones were filled with rainbow colors that flowed as if in liquid , slowly swirling iridescently , when exposed to sunlight .
description_long: Rogue stone A rogue stone ( sometimes written roguestone ) was a small , extremely rare magical gemstone with a tendency to cause wild magic . Description . Rogue stones were filled with rainbow colors that flowed as if in liquid , slowly swirling iridescently , when exposed to sunlight . They were extremely rare and seemed to repel each other — no two rogue stones where ever found in the same place at the same time . Single stones have been found in treasure hoards , cold regions , and sunk in swamps , but evidence about what type of rock they occurred in was inconclusive . Rogue stones were easily faceted along natural planes and the resulting faces gave the stones their iridescent property . A typical specimen had a base value of 5 , 000 gp but was likely to be worth much more to wizards who knew of its uses . There were more than sixty known rogue stones throughout the Realms . Powers . Rogue stones were used to cast the " gemjump " spell . Rogue stones did not have a detectable magic aura except at the time " gemjump " spell was being cast , and they were not destroyed or consumed by the initial enchantment or the activation of the spell .

title: Rohini
description: Rohini Rohini is a succubus currently living with the Abolethic Sovereignty in Neverwinter . In the late 1470s she was sent to Neverwinter on a mission by her master , the Erinyes Invadiah , to attempt to create conflict between the Sovereignty and the god Asmodeus . Rohini was able to seduce the head priest of Oghma ' s House of Knowledge in Neverwinter .
description_long: Rohini Rohini is a succubus currently living with the Abolethic Sovereignty in Neverwinter . In the late 1470s she was sent to Neverwinter on a mission by her master , the Erinyes Invadiah , to attempt to create conflict between the Sovereignty and the god Asmodeus . Rohini was able to seduce the head priest of Oghma ' s House of Knowledge in Neverwinter . The Oghman priests had developed a method for using the spellplague Chasm in Neverwinter to give creatures spellscar s without some of the nasty side effects . Rohini began sending spellscarred creatures to the Abolethic Sovereignty for their use as servitors . Rohini ' s mind was enslaved by the Sovereinty using a powerful relic of the Spellplague known as the Hex Locus . Unfortunately for Rohini , her plans were derailed when a clanless dragonborn warrior named Mehen and his adopted tiefling twin daughters arrived in Neverwinter and stayed at the House of Knowledge . Rohini dominated Mehen but his daughters uncovered her plot and stirred up enough trouble to catch Invadiah ' s attention . Invadiah travelled through a portal from Malbolge to Neverwinter and defeated Rohini , whom she now regarded as a traitor .

title: Roi Uxio
description: Roi Uxio Roi Uxio was a soldier of the Red Plumes in Yulash . Activities . Roi was stationed at the Red Plumes camp in Yulash .
description_long: Roi Uxio Roi Uxio was a soldier of the Red Plumes in Yulash . Activities . Roi was stationed at the Red Plumes camp in Yulash . A silkroot addict , he often went to a secluded spot to indulge in his vice . History . Roi bought the silkroot from a man named Ventria Greenglass of Hillsfar ' s Rogues ' Guild . During the Rage of Demons in 1491 DR , during the visit of Torin Nomerthal to the city , Roi was worried he would have only one dose of silkroot left . Personality . Roi was a coward at heart . He was scared that his superiors would discover his vice and severely punished him .

title: Rokthorl
description: Rokthorl Rokthorl was a dragonborn settlement and the capital of Relmaur , Returned Abeir . Background . Rokthorl was a " mobile " city .
description_long: Rokthorl Rokthorl was a dragonborn settlement and the capital of Relmaur , Returned Abeir . Background . Rokthorl was a " mobile " city . Whichever cavern the High Crown of Relmaur was inhabiting at any given moment was named Rokthorl . The Relmorn always tried to maintain the cave - settlements of Harone Thar and Aranghthal near the current location of Rokthorl .

title: Roldilar
description: Roldilar Roldilar , or the Realm of Glimmering Swords , was a shield dwarf kingdom that occupied the lands later known as the Vast , between Cormanthyr and Impiltur in north Faerûn , both below and above ground . It was founded in 610 DR and fell in 649 DR . History .
description_long: Roldilar Roldilar , or the Realm of Glimmering Swords , was a shield dwarf kingdom that occupied the lands later known as the Vast , between Cormanthyr and Impiltur in north Faerûn , both below and above ground . It was founded in 610 DR and fell in 649 DR . History . The rise of Roldilar . Formerly , the land had been held by the orc nation of Vastar , but it fell into civil war in the Year of Writhing Darkness , 572 DR . Meanwhile , underground , dwarves from the north and east expanded their mines into the mountains of Vastar . After initial clashes with the orcs in their tunnels , the dwarves decided to let no orc who ' d seen a dwarf remain alive , to prevent any word reaching orcish chieftains of their nature of their enemy . The dwarves were subtly aided by the downtrodden goblin and kobold slaves of the orcs : the dwarves left them alone , and so they never told the orcs about the dwarves they saw , nor helped them in battle . The unexplained deaths of large numbers of orcs in the mountains were blamed on the civil war . Even as the civil war ended , the dwarves continued to encroach from the west , spreading underground and applying increasing pressure on the orcs .

title: Rolf Sunriver
description: Rolf Sunriver Rolf Sunriver was the Chief Constable of Ravens Bluff from 1352 DR - - ? Appearance . Rolf is 5 ' 9 " tall and weighs 180 pounds ; compact and muscular .
description_long: Rolf Sunriver Rolf Sunriver was the Chief Constable of Ravens Bluff from 1352 DR - - ? Appearance . Rolf is 5 ' 9 " tall and weighs 180 pounds ; compact and muscular . His elvish heritage shows in the slight point to his ears and his unusually bright green eyes , otherwise he looks human . His skin is tanned from many years of outdoor life . He wears elven chain mail but does not carry a shield . His badge of office is displayed predominantly on his surcoat and on the back of his hooded cape . Personality . The moniker " Sunny " is satirical because Rolf is usually quiet , watchful , and impassive . He has a sense of humor which ranges from dry to bawdy depending on his mood . He pays close attention to detail and is a good investigator . He dislikes paperwork and would rather make the rounds , checking on his men and keeping a finger on the pulse of the city .
