After her capture by drow in Port Llast in 1484 DR , the mace fell into the hands of the drider Yerrininae . It was unclear whether Ambergris was able to retrieve it .

title: Skullport
description: Skullport Skullport , also known as the Port of Shadows , was a teeming hive of evil lying deep beneath Waterdeep on the third underground level of Undermountain . Geographical features . Sargauth , Portals , and Port .
description_long: Skullport Skullport , also known as the Port of Shadows , was a teeming hive of evil lying deep beneath Waterdeep on the third underground level of Undermountain . Geographical features . Sargauth , Portals , and Port . Skullport lay along the subterranean river Sargauth , which was used as a trade route to the outside world . Over the centuries , several magical portals large enough for entire ships to pass through were built in the cavern walls along this waterway . One such portal , about 400 feet ( 122 m ) east of Skull Island , is only faintly visible as a scratched outline in the stone . Triggering the portal required no special key , just extraordinary confidence on the part of the ship ' s pilot , since the vessel had to be steered bow - first into the wall . When the bowsprit made contact with the portal , the vessel and all its contents were transported instantly to the middle of the Lapal Sea . The Keepers were hired mages who raised ships through the magical locks that led from the port to the Sea Caves south of Waterdeep and from there to the open sea . These portals are said to have been established by Halaster .

title: Skulls of Skullport
description: Skulls of Skullport In the chaotic underground of Skullport , a city of thieves , murderers and slave traders , the Skulls imposed some semblance of order when things get out of hand . They are magically powerful floating skulls believed to be the spiritual embodiment of the arcanists who created the Mythallar . The Mythallar or mantle is a sentient and powerful arcane relic capable of generating nearly limitless power .
description_long: Skulls of Skullport In the chaotic underground of Skullport , a city of thieves , murderers and slave traders , the Skulls imposed some semblance of order when things get out of hand . They are magically powerful floating skulls believed to be the spiritual embodiment of the arcanists who created the Mythallar . The Mythallar or mantle is a sentient and powerful arcane relic capable of generating nearly limitless power . The Mythallar in Skullport was created to support the immense weight of the world surrounding it , but at some point it seems that the magic had faltered , and Skullport was in danger of complete destruction . Only through the efforts of the arcanists did the caverns survive but at the cost of their own lives . The thirteen most powerful were reborn shortly after as the Skulls , guardians of the mantle . They however were bound to the mantle and can ' t move more than 300 feet beyond . In centuries they lost their individual identities and started act as a collective hive mind . Each Skull retained few aspect of his original identity but in objective and purpose they were really a single entity .

title: Skullsmashers
description: Skullsmashers The Skullsmashers were a tribe of unusually strong and fierce ogre s , led by Guld , who made their base in Fangjaws Hold in Thar . They enslaved " lesser " neighbors such as goblin s and even human s and dwarves , working them hard , usually to death in just a few months .
description_long: Skullsmashers The Skullsmashers were a tribe of unusually strong and fierce ogre s , led by Guld , who made their base in Fangjaws Hold in Thar . They enslaved " lesser " neighbors such as goblin s and even human s and dwarves , working them hard , usually to death in just a few months .

title: Skultan
description: Skultan Skultan was a village near Daerlun in Sembia . As of 1368 DR , it was known as a place where goods could be fenced , currency could be exchanged between Cormyr eans and Sembia ns , and things could be repaired . The Tumbling Goblets and The Winking Wemic , two gnome - run festhall s , were staffed by attractive human females , and were sites of underhand dealings .
description_long: Skultan Skultan was a village near Daerlun in Sembia . As of 1368 DR , it was known as a place where goods could be fenced , currency could be exchanged between Cormyr eans and Sembia ns , and things could be repaired . The Tumbling Goblets and The Winking Wemic , two gnome - run festhall s , were staffed by attractive human females , and were sites of underhand dealings . A rumor existed that Purple Dragon s would permit these dealings to continue , accepting bribes in the form of discounted " services " in these establishments .

title: Skulto Mreth
description: Skulto Mreth Skulto Mreth was a wizard and a member of the slavery and crime syndicate known as the Tarntar . His specialty was illusion spells . Description .
description_long: Skulto Mreth Skulto Mreth was a wizard and a member of the slavery and crime syndicate known as the Tarntar . His specialty was illusion spells . Description . He was hard to describe because he used disguises and illusions to mask his rather ordinary features . Personality . Skulto was a very private man because he led a very dangerous life , and protecting his secrets was of utmost importance to prevent his many enemies from getting revenge . He was always prepared in case disaster should strike and looked at everything with a dispassionate eye . He was cool under pressure and not easily excited . Abilities . He was a master of disguise and coupled this with his skill as an illusionist to create personas throughout the Moonsea region for his many secret business investments . Possessions . He collected enchanted whip s to use on his slaves . History . Sometime around the Year of the Turret , 1360 DR , Skulto was traveling with some other members of the Tarntar and had stopped at the Whistling Wizard inn in Voonlar . While observing the small - town milieu of the common room , in walked none other than Elminster himself , bantering with his compatriots in a most familiar manner .

title: Skum Lord
description: Skum Lord The Skum Lord was an aboleth prominent in Skullport in 1370 DR . Activities . The Skum Lord was the primary agent of the Kraken Society in Skullport .
description_long: Skum Lord The Skum Lord was an aboleth prominent in Skullport in 1370 DR . Activities . The Skum Lord was the primary agent of the Kraken Society in Skullport . It owned almost forty percent of Skullport ' s buildings and inhabitants . If a person refused or could not pay their monthly rent , the Skum Lord ' s skum servitors would drag them off to the monster ' s lair for sinister purposes . In his spying actives , the Skum Lord used many normal citizens of Skullport as informants , communicating with them through telepathic links .

title: Skurge
description: Skurge Skurge was an ancient female black dragon who laired in the Marsh of Tun . Personality . She was especially intelligent for her kind , knowing not to despoil the area she lived in , but otherwise shared the traits common to other black dragons , being petty , cruel and aggressive .
description_long: Skurge Skurge was an ancient female black dragon who laired in the Marsh of Tun . Personality . She was especially intelligent for her kind , knowing not to despoil the area she lived in , but otherwise shared the traits common to other black dragons , being petty , cruel and aggressive . Her advanced age made her irritable due to pain caused by the strain of her own body weight upon her bones and joints but this was tempered by a surprisingly patient nature . Lair . Through many years of magical effort , Skurge built several underwater lairs and ambush spots throughout the Marsh of Tun and when she was not occupying them , they were guarded by lizardfolk servitors drawn from one of the four tribes living in the Marsh , who believed her to be an emissary of Semuanya . At least one of these lairs was a brood chamber where she kept her unhatched offspring . The brood chamber was magically heated and as long as it was occupied by an egg ( about 12 – 18 months every decade ) , Skurge would also live in that lair , leaving only to hunt when she needed to . Relationships .

title: Skuthosiin
description: Skuthosiin Skuthosiin " the Venomous " was a fiend ish green dragon and one of Tiamat ' s chosen . History . He was invested with a third of Tiamat ' s divine power during the Time of Troubles but was devoured , along with Gestaniius , by the bearer of another third , Tchazzar .
description_long: Skuthosiin Skuthosiin " the Venomous " was a fiend ish green dragon and one of Tiamat ' s chosen . History . He was invested with a third of Tiamat ' s divine power during the Time of Troubles but was devoured , along with Gestaniius , by the bearer of another third , Tchazzar . During the Dracorage , he was resurrected by Tiamat and sent to the Methwood to create an army for Tchazzar , who was now his ally . In 1479 DR , Skuthosiin organized the ash giant s of the Black Ash Plain into an army to invade Tymanther . The army was driven back into the plain and Skuthosiin was killed by dragonborn led by the paladin Medrash .

title: Sky Home
description: Sky Home Sky Home was a plane in the Elemental Chaos and was home to the primordial Akadi . The plane was a broad expanse of sky , clouds and storms . In some places the winds coalesced to form structures which the planes inhabitants resided in .
description_long: Sky Home Sky Home was a plane in the Elemental Chaos and was home to the primordial Akadi . The plane was a broad expanse of sky , clouds and storms . In some places the winds coalesced to form structures which the planes inhabitants resided in . Sky Home had connections to Arvandor in the Astral Sea .

title: Skydrop
description: Skydrop Skydrop was the common name given to material ; fragments of glass of meteoric origin found beneath the shifting dunes of Anauroch and other deserts . Description . Skydrop stones were usually clear to lightly shaded with a glassy luster .
description_long: Skydrop Skydrop was the common name given to material ; fragments of glass of meteoric origin found beneath the shifting dunes of Anauroch and other deserts . Description . Skydrop stones were usually clear to lightly shaded with a glassy luster . These stones were left uncut and merely polished and mounted in a claw setting as earrings and pendants . A typical specimen had a base value of 50 gp . Powers . A creature touching , wearing , or carrying a skydrop gemstone was immune to petrification .

title: Skykillers
description: Skykillers The Skykillers were a disbanded mercenary company based in Chondath around 1358 DR . History . They fought during the war against the arcanaloth Yrkhetep at the yugoloth ' s side .
description_long: Skykillers The Skykillers were a disbanded mercenary company based in Chondath around 1358 DR . History . They fought during the war against the arcanaloth Yrkhetep at the yugoloth ' s side . They were destroyed by the Windriders at the Battle of Five Crowns . Membership . The Skykillers were hippogriff - mounted cavalry . Leadership . Their leader , Sir Lehakin , was a mortal enemy of Bren Wingblade , leader of the Windriders .

title: Slaad
description: Slaad Slaadi were bipedal , frog - like creatures native to Limbo and to the Supreme Throne . Description . Their base form was that of a large bipedal frog , though some of the more powerful slaadi had polymorph self or shapechange abilities and sometimes appeared as humanoid s .
description_long: Slaad Slaadi were bipedal , frog - like creatures native to Limbo and to the Supreme Throne . Description . Their base form was that of a large bipedal frog , though some of the more powerful slaadi had polymorph self or shapechange abilities and sometimes appeared as humanoid s . In frog form their heads were huge and their claws were extremely sharp . They spoke their own language and , occasionally , some additional evil languages . Telepathy , however , allowed them to understand and converse with all things . There were many types of slaadi depending on their place of origin and rank within their society . The most common types of slaadi were blue slaad i , green slaad i , red slaad i , gray slaad i ( the executioners ) and death slaad i ( the lesser masters ) . Some were even chalk - white slaad i like Chourst , and very rarely did they turn into black slaad i . Size also varied between the different subtypes , from human - sized to several feet taller . Most Slaadi were almost always chaotic neutral , with the exception of death slaadi , which were usually chaotic evil , and the gormeel slaad i , which were usually lawful neutral .

title: Sladis Vadir
description: Sladis Vadir Sladis Vadir was a druid and a member of the Emerald Enclave during the Rage of Demons . Personality . Sladis was always fascinated by the Underdark , but the madness spread by the demon lord s broke his sanity .
description_long: Sladis Vadir Sladis Vadir was a druid and a member of the Emerald Enclave during the Rage of Demons . Personality . Sladis was always fascinated by the Underdark , but the madness spread by the demon lord s broke his sanity . However , it was not too late for him to be cured . History . Sladis was one of the students of Morista Malkin in Gauntlgrym . However , at the start of Rage of Demons , he was driven mad and he disappeared into the Underdark . Driven by madness , he started to kill and eat other humanoids he encountered until he arrived in Mantol - Derith . There , Sladis worked as a guide to Menzoberranzan , Gracklstugh , Neverlight Grove , and Blingdenstone

title: Slan Thurbel
description: Slan Thurbel Slan Thurbel was the leader of the mercenaries and enforcers of the Xanathar Thieves ' Guild of Skullport . Activities . Slan commanded all the fighter s of the guild , including the punitive squads incaricated to kill those that cross the ways of the guild .
description_long: Slan Thurbel Slan Thurbel was the leader of the mercenaries and enforcers of the Xanathar Thieves ' Guild of Skullport . Activities . Slan commanded all the fighter s of the guild , including the punitive squads incaricated to kill those that cross the ways of the guild . Personality . The reorganization of the guild ( and the secret change of the guild master ) greatly made him happy because the old Xanathar did not " respect his talents " ; on contrary , the Eye greatly praised him in order to assure his loyalty . This praise however boostered Slan ' s ego so he considered himself the most important follower of his master . The Eye ordered Avaereene to keep an eye on Slan in order to control Slan if he moved against the guild .

title: Slanya
description: Slanya Slanya was a monk of Kelemvor living at the monastery in the city of Ormpetarr . Appearance . Slanya was tall and lithe .
description_long: Slanya Slanya was a monk of Kelemvor living at the monastery in the city of Ormpetarr . Appearance . Slanya was tall and lithe . Her head was shaven , except for a characteristic sidelock of blonde hair wrapped in thin white leather straps that barely reaches her shoulder . At the base of her skull where it met the spine was a blue outlined and filled with red and green inked tattoo depicting the sign of Kelemvor , a skeletal hand holding a set of scales . After she traveled into the Plaguewrought Land with Duvan , she acquired a spellscar that permeated her entire body . History . Slanya was orphaned at an early age and was sent to live with her aunt in Impiltur . Slanya ' s aunt abused her and she set a fire that killed her aunt although she has no conscious memory of the event . After her aunt ' s death , Brother Gregor took Slanya to the Kelemvoran monastery for training . She journeyed with the monks to Ormpetarr when Gregor convinced the monastery to relocate . She served under high priestess Kaylinn in Ormpetarr . Her primary duty was to tend the funeral pyres of pilgrims who died from exposure to the spellplague .

title: Slarkrethel
description: Slarkrethel Slarkrethel was a huge kraken wizard and Chosen of Umberlee , who also founded the Kraken Society . History . Born in the Year of the Kraken , 151 DR , it wasn ' t until Slarkrethel found the submerged ruins of Ascarle in 244 DR that he began building his undersea empire .
description_long: Slarkrethel Slarkrethel was a huge kraken wizard and Chosen of Umberlee , who also founded the Kraken Society . History . Born in the Year of the Kraken , 151 DR , it wasn ' t until Slarkrethel found the submerged ruins of Ascarle in 244 DR that he began building his undersea empire . There , he was inspired by legends of his ancestors ' past , and his studies left him aspiring to godhood and to regain some of his race ' s former glory . Centuries later , he had extended his tentacles all over the Trackless Sea , and created the web of informants and spies called the Kraken Society . He was adopted by Umberlee as her chosen in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR .

title: Slater
description: Slater Slater was a female human soldier of the Zhentilar Company of the Scorpions during the Time of Troubles in 1358 DR . Slater was one of the first to befriend Cyric when he decided to join the Scorpions . She helped and followed him loyally .
description_long: Slater Slater was a female human soldier of the Zhentilar Company of the Scorpions during the Time of Troubles in 1358 DR . Slater was one of the first to befriend Cyric when he decided to join the Scorpions . She helped and followed him loyally . She explained to Cyric that she liked him and his vision of power , and she wanted to rise through the ranks as his lieutenant . When in Scardale , the Company was reorganized as an elite force under the god Bane himself . Slater was nominated as captain of one of the ships arranged for the assault against Tantras .

title: Slaughtertusk
description: Slaughtertusk Slaughtertusk was a nalfeshnee agent of Baphomet in the Labyrinth during the Rage of Demons . Personality . Slaughtertusk was a bully at heart , pleading for its life against enemies stronger than it .
description_long: Slaughtertusk Slaughtertusk was a nalfeshnee agent of Baphomet in the Labyrinth during the Rage of Demons . Personality . Slaughtertusk was a bully at heart , pleading for its life against enemies stronger than it . It was bored by the task assigned to it but knew not to disobey the Horned King . History . During the Rage of Demons , the demon lord Baphomet established himself in the Labyrinth . When he found the Maze Engine inside , he ordered Slaughtertusk to watch over the crevasse and prevent any creature from approaching the device .

title: Slavery
description: Slavery Slavery was a practice among certain cultures that forced a sentient creature to serve another , often against their will . Slavery differed from other forms of service such as indentured servitude or apprenticeship in that slavery was of an indefinite duration and the slave rarely had any choice in the arrangement . Slavery in the Realms .
description_long: Slavery Slavery was a practice among certain cultures that forced a sentient creature to serve another , often against their will . Slavery differed from other forms of service such as indentured servitude or apprenticeship in that slavery was of an indefinite duration and the slave rarely had any choice in the arrangement . Slavery in the Realms . Athkatla . Slavery was legal in Athkatla . High Imaskar . Slavery was illegal in the realm of High Imaskar . Hulburg . Slavery was outlawed in the city of Hulburg on the Moonsea . Mulhorand . The majority of Mulhorandi were slaves . Slaves in Mulhorand were guaranteed humane treatment by law and were treated better than slaves in other lands . Procampur . Slavery was illegal in Procampur and any slaves brought into the city were freed . Ravens Bluff . Slavery was illegal in Ravens Bluff but there was an active slave trade with the drow in the Underdark beneath the city . Thay . Slavery was legal and commonplace in Thay . Thayan enclave s brought slavery ( though only inside the enclave grounds ) to several settlements all over Faerûn . Though not permitted to trade in slaves out of the enclave , this did sometimes occur . Underdark .

title: Slavin ' krath ' magaal
description: Slavin ' krath ' magaal Slavin ' krath ' magaal , also known as Slavin , was a young brown dragon living in Unther . History . Slavin was a young brown dragon part of a dragon generation with good dealing with Tiamat ; for this she agreed to collaborate with the cleric of Tiamat Malise in exchange for rituals that improve her power .
description_long: Slavin ' krath ' magaal Slavin ' krath ' magaal , also known as Slavin , was a young brown dragon living in Unther . History . Slavin was a young brown dragon part of a dragon generation with good dealing with Tiamat ; for this she agreed to collaborate with the cleric of Tiamat Malise in exchange for rituals that improve her power . From this rituals she acquire the fiendish archetype . She arrived to the point to agreed to mate with Malise giving birth to a half - dragon offspring , Braeden . In 1374 DR possibly she was killed by an adventures ' band raiding the underground Temple of Tiamat .

title: Slay living
description: Slay living Slay living was a necromancy spell that could kill a single creature . The older versions of this spell were also reversible , known as " raise dead " . Effects .
description_long: Slay living Slay living was a necromancy spell that could kill a single creature . The older versions of this spell were also reversible , known as " raise dead " . Effects . The target had to be a living creature for this spell to be effective . The newer version of " slay living " required a successful melee touch attack in order to cast , but the older versions operated at a range of 90 ft ( 27 . 4 m ) . In this respect , they were very similar to " finger of death " . If the target was able to overcome the death magic , they were not killed outright but were then subject to damage on the order of an " inflict serious wounds " spell , which still might have been fatal . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell . The somatic component for the older versions was to point at the intended victim .

title: Slayer genie
description: Slayer genie Slayer genies were tasked genie s who served to commit murder as often as possible . All tasked genies ran the risk of eventually becoming slayers if they were not able to retain their sanity while repeatedly performing their given tasks . Slayer genies were initially used by powerful genie lords to intimidate their enemies and rivals , but were later used by noble genie s to eliminate targets .
description_long: Slayer genie Slayer genies were tasked genie s who served to commit murder as often as possible . All tasked genies ran the risk of eventually becoming slayers if they were not able to retain their sanity while repeatedly performing their given tasks . Slayer genies were initially used by powerful genie lords to intimidate their enemies and rivals , but were later used by noble genie s to eliminate targets . Description . Slayer genies had four muscular arms and dark skin . One pair of their hands resembled lion ’ s paws and the other pair resembled clawed human hands . They had red eyes that burned like fire . A third green eye sat on their forehead in between two horns . Two wings protruded from their backs . Slayer genies stood 10 feet ( 3 m ) tall . Combat . Stealth was a slayer genie ’ s favored method of attack . They could cast " blindness " , " silence 15 ' radius " , " darkness " , " improved invisibility " , " ventriloquism " , " misdirection " , " assume gaseous form " , " polymorph self " , and " dimension door " . They could attack with all four arms and their strength added terrible power to their strikes . Habitat / Society .

title: Sleep
description: Sleep Sleep was a spell of the enchantment school used by wizard s , bard s and sorcerer s , as well as warlock s with Archfey patron s . Effects . " Sleep " , as the name of the spell implies , placed its targets into a light slumber when cast successfully , overcoming the creatures ' willpower .
description_long: Sleep Sleep was a spell of the enchantment school used by wizard s , bard s and sorcerer s , as well as warlock s with Archfey patron s . Effects . " Sleep " , as the name of the spell implies , placed its targets into a light slumber when cast successfully , overcoming the creatures ' willpower . It affected a number of creatures that depended on the caster ' s power . Between the Spellplague and the Second Sundering , because of the complexity and energy involved in the spell , it could typically be cast only once per day and affected an area of roughly five feet in radius within a distance of 100 feet from the caster . Creatures that managed to stave off the intended effects of the spell nonetheless found their body fatigued , slowing their movements and thought processes . Components . The spell needed verbal , somatic and material components to be cast . The materials required were either a pinch of fine sand , rose petals or a cricket , any of which could be replaced by the use of an arcane focus . History . The spell was credited to the Netherese arcanist Efteran in - 1772 DR and was originally called " Efteran ' s sleep " .

title: Sleep - smoke
description: Sleep - smoke Sleep - smoke was a dark - gray , smoky gas that caused those who inhaled it to fall unconscious for up to 4 minutes . When released into the air , it quickly dissipated , and affected an area 20 feet ( 6 m ) in diameter . It was known to be used primarily by members of Xanathar Thieves ' Guild , specifically when they attempted to capture or kidnap a target .
description_long: Sleep - smoke Sleep - smoke was a dark - gray , smoky gas that caused those who inhaled it to fall unconscious for up to 4 minutes . When released into the air , it quickly dissipated , and affected an area 20 feet ( 6 m ) in diameter . It was known to be used primarily by members of Xanathar Thieves ' Guild , specifically when they attempted to capture or kidnap a target .

title: Sleeping Cat
description: Sleeping Cat The Sleeping Cat was a tavern and restaurant located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . Its proprietor was Whelgar Taerncole . History .
description_long: Sleeping Cat The Sleeping Cat was a tavern and restaurant located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . Its proprietor was Whelgar Taerncole . History . The Sleeping Cat was originally just a tavern , and a rowdy place that enjoyed nightly brawls , until it was bought by Whelgar Taerncole . Sick of the brawling , Whelgar got rid of both taproom and wine cellar , and developed the place as a restaurant instead . In 1358 DR , the Sleeping Cat operated as both tavern and restaurant . By around 1369 DR , the Sleeping Cat had steadily become a proper , quality restaurant , with an improving menu . It was a favorite of Volothamp Geddarm . Services . The Sleeping Cat had only a small menu , but the cooks dedicated themselves to mastering the recipes and slowly improving it . The " Volo ' s Guide " would give the restaurant a top rating but for the limited menu . Among its offerings were roast venison , fried eel soup , pork pastries , chicken and pheasant pies , stewed hare , wine - simmered goose , and aged brandycake . The only alcohol ic beverages were a small quantities of brandy , clarry , and mead .

title: Sleeping Dragon
description: Sleeping Dragon The Sleeping Dragon was an inn near Rassalantar on the Long Road north of Waterdeep . Structure . The inn was equipped with stables and privies , and both the east and west walls of the main building had chimneys .
description_long: Sleeping Dragon The Sleeping Dragon was an inn near Rassalantar on the Long Road north of Waterdeep . Structure . The inn was equipped with stables and privies , and both the east and west walls of the main building had chimneys . The roof was thatched . Interior . Its main door was at the southeast corner , and the main fireplace was on the west wall . A bar with high stools ran halfway along the northern wall , with a rare large mirror behind it . The kitchen was on the east side of the building , accessible through an archway . The east wall of the main room had cloak pegs , crates , barrels and stairs up to the upper floor . Up against the southern wall were nine long tables with benches , and the middle of the room was filled with round tables and chairs . The upper level consisted of a short hallway with doors to seven rooms , and windows overlooking the entrance . Inhabitants . The innkeeper of the Sleeping Dragon was Thrun " Spider " Samallahan . There were rumors that a female employee of the inn was a gold dragon in human form . Services . The inn served Spider ' s own brew , called Sleeping Dragon dark . History .

title: Sleeping gas
description: Sleeping gas Sleeping gas was a tool used by some rogue s to deal with pesky guards . Uses . Sleeping gas was stored in easily breakable flasks that would put most guards to sleep as soon as they smelled it .
description_long: Sleeping gas Sleeping gas was a tool used by some rogue s to deal with pesky guards . Uses . Sleeping gas was stored in easily breakable flasks that would put most guards to sleep as soon as they smelled it . Transporting the gas could be a risky venture for careless thieves if the flask broke while in their possession . Prices . The cost of sleeping gas depended on the size . A flask of sleeping gas suitable to knock - out a smaller guard cost 5 gold . A flask for a regular sized guard cost 10 gold . Any kind of guard over 7 ft . ( 2 . 1 m ) tall required a large flask costing 20 gold .

title: Sleeping poison
description: Sleeping poison Sleeping poison was an extremely potent poison that put the victim to sleep . The drow were renowned for their sleeping poison , also known as drow knockout poison or simply drow poison . It was hard to find outside of drow areas .
description_long: Sleeping poison Sleeping poison was an extremely potent poison that put the victim to sleep . The drow were renowned for their sleeping poison , also known as drow knockout poison or simply drow poison . It was hard to find outside of drow areas . The drow coated the tips of their hand crossbow bolt s in this poison and sometimes imbued their weapons with it . There were few antivenins , but Regis was able to brew an antivenin that lasted half a day , and drinking Gutbuster was a surefire way to prevent falling asleep ( assuming the drinker survived the Gutbuster itself ) . Locations . Drow sleeping poison was available from certain drow vendors in the Underdark . In Menzoberranzan , it could be obtained from Shimmerdark ' s Decanter in the Bazaar .

title: Sleeping potion
description: Sleeping potion Sleeping potions were magical potion s that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . They were only carried or used by holy slayer s . Description .
description_long: Sleeping potion Sleeping potions were magical potion s that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . They were only carried or used by holy slayer s . Description . Sleeping potions had a tart taste . Powers . After imbibing this potion , the imbiber fell into a peaceful sleep for a few hours . Sleep from this potion had the safe positive effects of a full night ' s rest ; thus , this potion was often used by spellcasters to rapidly increase the rate at which they could re - memorize spell s . Being woken during this sleep nullified any of these positive effects .

title: Sleet storm
description: Sleet storm Sleet storm is a conjuration spell that summons a rain of partially frozen water to hamper vision and movement . Effects . Driving sleet blocks all sight ( even darkvision ) within it and causes the ground in the area to be icy , slowing movement to one - half normal .
description_long: Sleet storm Sleet storm is a conjuration spell that summons a rain of partially frozen water to hamper vision and movement . Effects . Driving sleet blocks all sight ( even darkvision ) within it and causes the ground in the area to be icy , slowing movement to one - half normal . Additionally , any creature in sleet that attempts to move must succeed at a Reflex save or fall down instead . The sleet extinguishes torches and small fires . Components . A pinch of dust and a few drops of water .

title: Slim
description: Slim Slim was a wererat of Ship Rethnor in Icewind Dale in 1485 DR . History . Slim was a wererat fighter member of Ship Rethnor in Luskan .
description_long: Slim Slim was a wererat of Ship Rethnor in Icewind Dale in 1485 DR . History . Slim was a wererat fighter member of Ship Rethnor in Luskan . He and his friend Marek the Shank were the main leaders of the Rethnor men that followed Vaelish Gant in Icewind Dale . They started a protection racket in Bryn Shander and supported Vaelish in his political plot . Slim stole animals from Aglonell ' s traps on Eleint 6 . Some days later , Slim and Marek stole silver weapons ordered by the Harper Aarun from Dunavan ' s warehouse . On Highharvestide , Silm and Marek kidnapped the Speaker of Bryn Shander , Duvessa Shane , on the day of an election and Vaelish proposed himself as substitute , pretending to appear reluctant . Appendix . Gameplay . In order to fight Akar Kessell and Hedrun Arnsfirth , the adventurers could potentially allow to Vaelish to succeed in his plan .

title: Slime Clan
description: Slime Clan The Slime Clan were a tribe of derro living in the Underdark near Delzimmer in southern Faerûn . The tribe lived in a huge cave and had crude stone huts as dwellings . The only building of substance was a large stone building in which their leader lived and in which the derro performed bizarre experiments .
description_long: Slime Clan The Slime Clan were a tribe of derro living in the Underdark near Delzimmer in southern Faerûn . The tribe lived in a huge cave and had crude stone huts as dwellings . The only building of substance was a large stone building in which their leader lived and in which the derro performed bizarre experiments . The cavern contained portals to the Far Realm through which denizens passed only to be captured by the derro . Leadership . The clan was ruled by the Slime King . In the past , an aboleth and a mind flayer had been the Slime King . As of 1479 DR , the Slime King was a yuan - ti pureblood named Iraska who had been enslaved by the derro but managed to manipulate her way to leadership .

title: Slime domain
description: Slime domain The Slime domain was a deity domain that granted divine spellcasters spell s related to slime . They also gained the ability to rebuke and command ooze s much as an evil cleric could rebuke and command undead . Slime domain spells .
description_long: Slime domain The Slime domain was a deity domain that granted divine spellcasters spell s related to slime . They also gained the ability to rebuke and command ooze s much as an evil cleric could rebuke and command undead . Slime domain spells . These spells were considered in the Slime domain although some of them were not normally divine spells :

title: Sling
description: Sling A sling is a missile weapon consisting of a cord with a pouch to hold a stone ( called a bullet ) . The cord may be made of leather or cloth . The user swings the sling in a circle and then releases the stone which flies at a high speed at his opponent .
description_long: Sling A sling is a missile weapon consisting of a cord with a pouch to hold a stone ( called a bullet ) . The cord may be made of leather or cloth . The user swings the sling in a circle and then releases the stone which flies at a high speed at his opponent . A sling can be a deadly weapon in the hands of a trained slinger , especially halfling s .

title: Slink Monteskor
description: Slink Monteskor Slink Monteskor was the main spymaster of the Xanathar Thieves ' Guild of Skullport . Slink was a potbellied fellow with an eidetic memory , allowing him to remember all that he read . The Xanathar used him as bookkeeper and information storehouse .
description_long: Slink Monteskor Slink Monteskor was the main spymaster of the Xanathar Thieves ' Guild of Skullport . Slink was a potbellied fellow with an eidetic memory , allowing him to remember all that he read . The Xanathar used him as bookkeeper and information storehouse . Slink also commanded Xanathar ' s network of spies and had information about all the guild ' s operations , and all the other masters sent reports to him . The Xanathar trusted him and knew , by use of spells , that Slink was loyal but kept a very close eye on him ; if someone captured him , they could learn all about the Xanathar Guild .

title: Sloopdilmonpolop
description: Sloopdilmonpolop Sloopdilmonpolop was a minor Underdark city of the kuo - toa . The city was home to the Sacred Pool of the Sea Mother , a square , subterranean lake occupying a cavern nearly 1 , 000 feet long and wide . It was dedicated to the worship of Blibdoolpoolp .
description_long: Sloopdilmonpolop Sloopdilmonpolop was a minor Underdark city of the kuo - toa . The city was home to the Sacred Pool of the Sea Mother , a square , subterranean lake occupying a cavern nearly 1 , 000 feet long and wide . It was dedicated to the worship of Blibdoolpoolp . Dagagoorg served both as Priest - King ( Va - Poolgol ) of Sloopdilmonpolop and high priest of the Sacred Pool of the Sea Mother . History . Circa - 3000 DR , Sloopdilmonpolop was founded by Sloopdilmonpol , a great kuo - toa prophet , as a temple - city in the Underdark off the coast of Tethyr . Eventually the temple grew into a theocratic city - state , with priest - king rulers . After an increasing number of expansionist raids by the city ' s denizens , the dwarves of Sondarr and Xothaerin dispatched scouts who eventually discovered the City of Pools . This touched off a centuries - long war of mutual extinction , known as the Axe and Fin Wars . The city was never taken , but the long conflict ushered in a period of decline from which the city never recovered . The only benefit to this was the city ' s emergence as a mercantile hub .

title: Sloth strike
description: Sloth strike Sloth strike is a transmutation spell used by several swordmage s of relatively low experience and power . When " sloth strike " is cast it infuses the flesh of a creature struck by a swordmage ' s weapon in melee with icy power , partially freezing their muscles and blood . In addition to causing the target great pain , this slows their movements for a brief moment .
description_long: Sloth strike Sloth strike is a transmutation spell used by several swordmage s of relatively low experience and power . When " sloth strike " is cast it infuses the flesh of a creature struck by a swordmage ' s weapon in melee with icy power , partially freezing their muscles and blood . In addition to causing the target great pain , this slows their movements for a brief moment . " Sloth strike " can be recharged after a short rest of a few minutes , at which point it can be cast again .

title: Slow
description: Slow Slow ( originally Quantoul ' s slowmorph ) was a transmutation spell used by arcane spellcasters that caused one or more targets to move more slowly . Some creatures , such as stone golem s and mindwitness es , had innate magical abilities that mimicked this spell . Ocular adept s , humanoid servants of the Great Mother , the beholder goddess , also had the power of " slow " .
description_long: Slow Slow ( originally Quantoul ' s slowmorph ) was a transmutation spell used by arcane spellcasters that caused one or more targets to move more slowly . Some creatures , such as stone golem s and mindwitness es , had innate magical abilities that mimicked this spell . Ocular adept s , humanoid servants of the Great Mother , the beholder goddess , also had the power of " slow " . Effects . One or more creatures within close range both from the caster and each other were magically made slower in their actions and reflexes . Targets with high strength of will could resist the effects of the spell , which otherwise lasted for about a third of a minute or longer . Several spells countered or negated the effects of this spell , including " haste " , " freedom " , " freedom of movement " , and " remove paralysis " . Components . The spell required verbal and somatic component s and a drop of molasses . History . The spell was invented by prolific Netherese arcanist Quantoul in −2026 DR ( 1833 NY ) . It was also recorded in the " Book of Bats " .

title: Slow Spout
description: Slow Spout Slow Spout was a Duergan ale that was thick and bitter . It was so named because it tended to swirl around in one ' s insides until it was " spouted " back up . Availability .
description_long: Slow Spout Slow Spout was a Duergan ale that was thick and bitter . It was so named because it tended to swirl around in one ' s insides until it was " spouted " back up . Availability . In Menzoberranzan , it was mostly enjoyed by goblin s and kobold s , but it was not unknown for drow to drink it .

title: Slow boon
description: Slow boon Slow boon was a divine necromancy spell that slowly healed injuries that the subject had suffered . Effect . The " slow boon " spell simply applied a slow rate of healing to the subject until the spell expired .
description_long: Slow boon Slow boon was a divine necromancy spell that slowly healed injuries that the subject had suffered . Effect . The " slow boon " spell simply applied a slow rate of healing to the subject until the spell expired . If the subject was fully healed before this time , then they could transfer the remainder of the spell to another willing creature by skin - to - skin contact . Components . The spell required a fragment of bone painted with the holy symbol of Ilmater the Broken God . This piece could come from any creature and be of any size . History . The " slow boon " spell appeared within the " Tome of Torment " , the holiest book of the church of Ilmater , which first appeared in the Realms in 848 DR .

title: Slow rot
description: Slow rot Slow rot was an abjuration spell that prevented spoilage of fruits , vegetables , and grains for a few weeks . Effects . Up to 100 ft ( 2 .
description_long: Slow rot Slow rot was an abjuration spell that prevented spoilage of fruits , vegetables , and grains for a few weeks . Effects . Up to 100 ft ( 2 . 83 m ) of plants , crops , or harvested goods per level of the caster could be kept free from decay for weeks . This spell did not work on meat , and pests could still consume the preserved plant material . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a pinch of sugar to cast . History . " Slow rot " dates back to the time of the first Netherese empire where it was known as a third - level druid spell of the terrestrial winds . It was also granted to specialty priests and favored servants of Moander to prolong their life as they were slowly corrupted from within . Appendix . Notes . This spell also had an opposite known as " speed rot " . This was not the " reverse " of " slow rot " but rather a separate spell that had the opposite effect .

title: Slow sand
description: Slow sand Slow sand was a powerful magical sand from Zakhara that literally had the power to stop time . Powers . When thrown , this sand could affect up to three man - sized creatures so long as they stood within 10 feet ( 3 m ) of each other , freezing each of them for up to 5 minutes similar to a " hold person " spell .
description_long: Slow sand Slow sand was a powerful magical sand from Zakhara that literally had the power to stop time . Powers . When thrown , this sand could affect up to three man - sized creatures so long as they stood within 10 feet ( 3 m ) of each other , freezing each of them for up to 5 minutes similar to a " hold person " spell . Affected individuals entered a special stasis where they were unaffected by anything transpiring around them . A second handful of " slow sand " tossed on an individual in stasis increased the duration for one hour . Any creature able to resist the sand was merely slowed down for one minute .

title: Slowtooth Weaponry
description: Slowtooth Weaponry Slowtooth Weaponry was a weapon shop located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . Its proprietor was Nym " Slowtooth " Nindar . Location .
description_long: Slowtooth Weaponry Slowtooth Weaponry was a weapon shop located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . Its proprietor was Nym " Slowtooth " Nindar . Location . The store stood on the southwest corner of where the Way of the Manticore crossed the Westbank March in Wheloon . Defenses . Because the store was stocked with weapons , the local Purple Dragons guarded it as if it was an armory . Regardless , Nindar ( a retired Dragon himself ) operated his own defenses against thieves . He was skilled with throwing axe s and had cords under his desk with which he could open shutters in the windows and door from a distance . Thus he could bury an axe in a thief anywhere in or outside his store . History . Slowtooth Weaponry was in business by 1358 DR . It was still in business through 1369 DR , and in 1374 DR . Services . Slowtooth Weaponry sold , of course , all kinds of weapons , and was the best in town . It also bought and sold magical weapons . When not otherwise busy , Nindar had a side - business instructing other warriors and young folk in how to wield specific weapons , and in their proper maintenance .

title: Slub
description: Slub Slub was a hill giant sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Slub was one of the minions of Chief Guh in Grudd Haug .
description_long: Slub Slub was a hill giant sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Slub was one of the minions of Chief Guh in Grudd Haug . He lived in a very dirty room together with his pet otyugh .

title: Sluuguth
description: Sluuguth Sluuguth was a roaming illithid who in 1372 DR tried to take advantage of the Siege of Menzoberranzan by duergar s and tanarukk . He discovered in Lake Donigarten the Archmage of Menzoberranzan , Gromph Baenre , imprisoned in a magical sphere after his defeat in a battle with Lichdrow Lord Dyrr . Sluuguth was convinced by Gromph to free him from the sphere using his psionic powers in exchange for great recompense .
description_long: Sluuguth Sluuguth was a roaming illithid who in 1372 DR tried to take advantage of the Siege of Menzoberranzan by duergar s and tanarukk . He discovered in Lake Donigarten the Archmage of Menzoberranzan , Gromph Baenre , imprisoned in a magical sphere after his defeat in a battle with Lichdrow Lord Dyrr . Sluuguth was convinced by Gromph to free him from the sphere using his psionic powers in exchange for great recompense . Gromph and Sluuguth traveled to the Archmage ' s quarters in Sorcere , and Sluuguth tried to trick Gromph using " thought bottles " of his own design . Gromph defeated Sluuguth , sealing his soul into a magical axe .

title: Small Teeth
description: Small Teeth The Small Teeth were a small mountain range that made up the border between Amn to the north and Muranndin to the south . Geography . The Small Teeth were a relatively small cluster of mountains .
description_long: Small Teeth The Small Teeth were a small mountain range that made up the border between Amn to the north and Muranndin to the south . Geography . The Small Teeth were a relatively small cluster of mountains . The average peak height was 8 , 000 feet above sea level . They were lightly forested , except for on the tallest peaks . The southern foothills were a good area for growing grapes . A large amount of snow fell in the mountains . The melts from these snows form the Imnestream and the River Specie , which flow through the Zehoarast Floodplains and into the sea . Inhabitants . The mountains were home to the blue dragon Iryklathagra . The lair of a mated pair of bronze dragon s once resided in the Teeth as well , but they were driven away or slain by Iryklathagra in 1369 DR . The surviving mate , Arellaxerrontoal , plotted her revenge from the Forest of Tethir . In 1095 DR , the Skeletal Finger maintained several hideouts in the mountains . Historically , the Teeth were home to hill giants .

title: Smallfry
description: Smallfry Smallfry was a tavern owner in Skullport . Personality . Smallfry was an irritable , short - tempered , and pushy individual .
description_long: Smallfry Smallfry was a tavern owner in Skullport . Personality . Smallfry was an irritable , short - tempered , and pushy individual . The smallest criticism of his cooking made him furious , and he would quickly order his staff to eject or dispose of anyone uncultured enough to find fault with one of his meals . Activities . Smallfry managed , owned , and cooked for his restaurant , the Smallfry ' s Pantry . History . Smallfry was a good - natured adventurer in Undermountain until he found a bejeweled " helm of opposite alignment " in a kuo - toa temple . His fellow adventurers immediately noted the change in Smallfry ' s behavior , and tried to reverse the effect . What happened next is unknown , save that Smallfry returned to Skullport some time later , and never spoke on the matter again . Later in life , he opened an innovative restaurant .

title: Smelting
description: Smelting Smelting was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects .
description_long: Smelting Smelting was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects . With this spell the caster could transform raw ore into fine ingots of pure metal . " Smelting " took 30 minutes to cast and the effects were permanent . The results of the spell depended greatly on the initial quality of ore . The following yields could be expected : Gems or semi - precious stones were unaffected by this spell . The spell would fail if cast upon rock that did not contain ore . Interrupting the spell at any point would cease the transformation process , but even successfully dispelling the magic would not cause the ingots to revert to their ore state . " Smelting " had no effect on metal or rock - based creatures . The reverse of this spell , sometimes called hide normal metal , caused metal ingots to meld back with the earth and was an effective method of hiding wealth or material . Components . This spell only required verbal and somatic components to cast .

title: Smile
description: Smile Smile was a female halfling rogue in Wheloon in 1374 DR . Description . She wore a black hood .
description_long: Smile Smile was a female halfling rogue in Wheloon in 1374 DR . Description . She wore a black hood . Abilities . Smile preferred to snipe at her victims with her bow . Possessions . Smile wielded a " + 1 composite shortbow " and a masterwork rapier , wore studded leather armor , and carried " potion of invisibility " and a " potion of cure light wounds " . History . Smile was the sister of Smote , a rogue and wizard of similar bent . In 1374 DR , Smile and her partner , Londal Fen , were employed by Lady Arthas of the Temple of Mystra . Smile persuaded Smote to attend the temple and participate in the rite of Mystra ' s Sacred Trust there . This ended in Smote being " dominated " by the " Starry Gnosis " and abducted as part of a secret Shar ran plot . Smote later wasn ' t sure if he should take revenge on his sister for this or not . If adventurers investigating the strange behavior of the cleric s of Mystra there attacked the temple , then she would pay the pair 830 gp to ambush them . Smile and Londal would lure the adventurers into an ambush among the waterfront warehouses at 23 Impil Street , or otherwise keep tabs on them to ambush and murder them out of sight .

title: Smiling Satyr
description: Smiling Satyr The Smiling Satyr was a rather good quality tavern just outside of the city of Loudwater . Geography . It was located eight farms southwest of Loudwater on the top of a hill with oaks and beeches .
description_long: Smiling Satyr The Smiling Satyr was a rather good quality tavern just outside of the city of Loudwater . Geography . It was located eight farms southwest of Loudwater on the top of a hill with oaks and beeches . Description . Exterior . In the lane that led to the tavern , there was a wooden statue of a dancing satyr with pipes ( that " played " piping tunes when someone approached , due to a permanent magic spell ) . There was a stream on a nearby field that offered water . Merchant and adventurers ' caravans occasionally camped on the surrounding fields , two of which were also owned by the tavern ' s proprietor . Interior . The floor was made of flagstone . There were two hearths , one at each side of the taproom . The walls were decorated with weapons ( including two magic battle axe s that could animate when ordered by the tavern ' s owner ) , animal skulls and other hunting trophies . History . It was run by Arvyn Umbryl , a former adventurer , even before 1365 DR and at least until 1370 DR .

title: Smiling Siren
description: Smiling Siren The Smiling Siren was a bawdy tavern / nightclub and theater in Waterdeep that later became a festhall run by the church of Sune . Description . Tavern / theater .
description_long: Smiling Siren The Smiling Siren was a bawdy tavern / nightclub and theater in Waterdeep that later became a festhall run by the church of Sune . Description . Tavern / theater . The nightclub and theater was housed in a plain stone and mudbrick building . It was home to a local troupe of actors , who often put on ( somewhat risque ) private shows for Waterdhavian nobles . Traveling troupes , bards , comedians , and nearly nude dancers also performed regularly . The proprietor in the 1360s DR was Perendel Wintamer , a young mage . Festhall . Many years later in 1479 , the Smiling Siren had been turned into festhall that primarily functioned as a brothel for the prostitute priestesses of Sune . A female dwarf named Sanchel was the proprietress . Sanchel was able to deduce the preferences of customers just by looking at them . The Siren ' s entry room featured elaborate , extremely life - like murals of nymphs and other woodland creatures frolicking in the forest . A magical golden basin sat in the entry room . Customers tossed donations into the basin to pay for the privilege of spending time with the ladies . If the donation was sufficient , the water in basin glowed .

title: Smoke ( ninja )
description: Smoke ( ninja ) Smoke was one of the three ninja in the service of Daisake Mayazato in the town of Aru in Wa . History . Smoke trained in the ninja arts in the Warazama clan together with Moonlight and Snake , until that clan was destroyed by internal dissent .
description_long: Smoke ( ninja ) Smoke was one of the three ninja in the service of Daisake Mayazato in the town of Aru in Wa . History . Smoke trained in the ninja arts in the Warazama clan together with Moonlight and Snake , until that clan was destroyed by internal dissent . He and his fellows entered into the service of Daisake Mayazato to repay him for previous services .

title: Smoke Wyrm
description: Smoke Wyrm The Smoke Wyrm was a tavern in Ravens Bluff run by the dwarf Tharzon Brewhammer and his son . The tavern was best known for its excellent stout known as Old Smokey , which was shipped all over the Vast . Structure .
description_long: Smoke Wyrm The Smoke Wyrm was a tavern in Ravens Bluff run by the dwarf Tharzon Brewhammer and his son . The tavern was best known for its excellent stout known as Old Smokey , which was shipped all over the Vast . Structure . The tavern had a sign that depicted a sleeping dragon blowing smoke out his nose . A storeroom had a secret entrance to a location in the sewers close to the entrance to Sarbreen .

title: Smoke bridge
description: Smoke bridge Smoke bridge was a clerical spell from the elemental fire sphere . Effects . With this spell a priest or cleric shaped smoke into a desired form up to a maximum length of 300 yards ( 275 m ) .
description_long: Smoke bridge Smoke bridge was a clerical spell from the elemental fire sphere . Effects . With this spell a priest or cleric shaped smoke into a desired form up to a maximum length of 300 yards ( 275 m ) . When the desired shape was created , it became as hard as stone for the duration of the spell . Components . This spell required smoke from a large open flame to cast .

title: Smoke drake
description: Smoke drake A Smoke drake ( also known as a fumarandi ) is a careful , sly predator that hunts its prey for miles before attacking with surprise . Physical description . A smoke drake ' s polished , overlapping scales are charcoal gray mixed with the occasional highlight of dark red and a dorsal ridge of ebony .
description_long: Smoke drake A Smoke drake ( also known as a fumarandi ) is a careful , sly predator that hunts its prey for miles before attacking with surprise . Physical description . A smoke drake ' s polished , overlapping scales are charcoal gray mixed with the occasional highlight of dark red and a dorsal ridge of ebony . Its eyes glow red like hot coals , especially when the beast is angry or in battle . The smoke drake has a tongue the color of charred wood and it has black claws and horns . Its horns curve back from its skull . It emits heat , and is hot to the touch , but not to the extent where it is not possible for a normal humanoid to sit on it , but the creature shows up distinctly to infravision . Combat . Once it hunts down its prey , the smoke drake opens battle with its smoky breath , which causes blindness , and its teeth and claws . It attacks lone or separated targets , focusing on that creature until it is incapacitated . If fighting an opponent , it cannot easily defeat , it will flee to safety , but will follow and attack again later . The smoke drake has two forms of breath weapon : a hazy cloud , and an incendiary cloud .

title: Smokepowder
description: Smokepowder Smokepowder was the " Realms " magical alchemical equivalent of black powder . History . The difference was in the composition of the powder .
description_long: Smokepowder Smokepowder was the " Realms " magical alchemical equivalent of black powder . History . The difference was in the composition of the powder . The secret to making smokepowder was given by Gond to the Lantan ese for sheltering him during the Time of Troubles in 1358 DR . The church of Gond are one of the few manufacturers of smokepowder . It was banned on many cities and a source of friction as it is considered dangerous to use and a threat to the status quo .

title: Smokespire
description: Smokespire The Smokespire was an extinct volcano in the Troll Mountains of Amn famed for being the home of the great dragon Balagos . It was the westernmost mountain in the range . History .
description_long: Smokespire The Smokespire was an extinct volcano in the Troll Mountains of Amn famed for being the home of the great dragon Balagos . It was the westernmost mountain in the range . History . The Smokespire was once the home of Hulrundrar until Balagos slew her . In Tarsakh of 1374 DR , Daelegoth Orndeir led an assault on Balagos ' lair to retrieve the " Shard of the Sun " , a relic of Amaunator captured by Hulrundrar .

title: Smoking Hammer Shrine
description: Smoking Hammer Shrine The Smoking Hammer Shrine was a temple located in the City of Brass in 1367 DR . Description . Though scant information was available on the Smoking Hammer Shrine , it was said to be quite ugly and strange .
description_long: Smoking Hammer Shrine The Smoking Hammer Shrine was a temple located in the City of Brass in 1367 DR . Description . Though scant information was available on the Smoking Hammer Shrine , it was said to be quite ugly and strange . Activities . This temple was dedicated to Surtr , a giant god of fire and steel . The genie s of the City of Brass did not worship Surtr , but they allowed some of their servants to erect the shrine nonetheless . Inhabitants . The Shrine was guarded night and day by attentive fire giant s .

title: Smoking Mountains
description: Smoking Mountains The Smoking Mountains were a range of mountains with active volcanoes at its western end . They were located in the Old Empires area of Faerûn , between the nations of Unther and Tymanther . < ref name = " TDYK / Hardcover - p185 " > < / ref > The equivalent region of the Smoking Mountains in the world of Abeir were the Dead Stone Mountains .
description_long: Smoking Mountains The Smoking Mountains were a range of mountains with active volcanoes at its western end . They were located in the Old Empires area of Faerûn , between the nations of Unther and Tymanther . < ref name = " TDYK / Hardcover - p185 " > < / ref > The equivalent region of the Smoking Mountains in the world of Abeir were the Dead Stone Mountains . History . At some point of the first years of the Wailing Years , dragonborn of Tymanther used rooks from the Smoking Mountains to construct Djerad Thymar .

title: Smoky quartz
description: Smoky quartz Smoky Quartz , also known as cairngorm or moorland topaz , was a variety of that was often found in massive deposits . The black variety of this stone was called morion and was used in necromancy . Description .
description_long: Smoky quartz Smoky Quartz , also known as cairngorm or moorland topaz , was a variety of that was often found in massive deposits . The black variety of this stone was called morion and was used in necromancy . Description . Smoky quartz ranged in color from brownish - yellow to brown to black and was usually into faceted gems regularly used to decorate weapons . Morion was used in magical inks and as a necromantic spell component . A typical specimen had a base value of 50 gp . Smoky quartz was considered sacred by followers of Mask — appropriate for sacrifice , or to be consecrated for use , or recognized as boons or omens when found . Powers . When bones were immersed in a solution that included morion they became hard as steel and immune to hostile necromantic effects . For example , a magic item made with morion - treated bone could not be affected by a rival necromancer who attempted to disrupt its magical function by targeting the bone material .

title: Smylla Nathos
description: Smylla Nathos Smylla Nathos was a human sorceress , psionicist , and broker of knowledge in the Braeryn in Menzoberranzan . History . Smylla came to Menzoberranzan from the surface and dwelt for a time with House Faen Tlabbar , until they grew tired of her novelty .
description_long: Smylla Nathos Smylla Nathos was a human sorceress , psionicist , and broker of knowledge in the Braeryn in Menzoberranzan . History . Smylla came to Menzoberranzan from the surface and dwelt for a time with House Faen Tlabbar , until they grew tired of her novelty . She ended up in the Braeryn and became ill . She lived in a crowded house of goblinoid s and worked as a broker of knowledge . In 1372 DR , Pharaun Mizzrym and Ryld Argith approached Smylla for information about missing drow males and a possible uprising of undercreatures . In exchange for the information , Pharaun promised to cure Smylla ' s illness by changing her into a drow , but he lied about the spell ' s efficacy and turning her into a drow killed her .

title: Snail - and - eel soup
description: Snail - and - eel soup Snail - and - eel soup was a dish made by the lizardfolk of the Vast Swamp of Cormyr , made from snails and eel s . In the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR , the Sharptooth tribe brewed snail - and - eel soup in a hot spring at their encampment in the swamp . The chieftain Kessessek offered this concoction to adventurers investigating Shar ran activities there as they parlayed .
description_long: Snail - and - eel soup Snail - and - eel soup was a dish made by the lizardfolk of the Vast Swamp of Cormyr , made from snails and eel s . In the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR , the Sharptooth tribe brewed snail - and - eel soup in a hot spring at their encampment in the swamp . The chieftain Kessessek offered this concoction to adventurers investigating Shar ran activities there as they parlayed .

title: Snake
description: Snake Snakes were natural reptiles that had no legs . They slithered along the ground or in trees in search of food , which consisted of small mammals , insects , and birds . In many parts of the world , snakes were seen as helpful creatures , due to their feeding on unwanted vermin .
description_long: Snake Snakes were natural reptiles that had no legs . They slithered along the ground or in trees in search of food , which consisted of small mammals , insects , and birds . In many parts of the world , snakes were seen as helpful creatures , due to their feeding on unwanted vermin .

title: Snake ( ninja )
description: Snake ( ninja ) Snake was one of the three ninja in the service of Daisake Mayazato in the town of Aru in Wa . History . Snake trained in ninja arts inside the Warazama clan together with Moonlight and Smoke , until that clan was destroyed by internal dissent .
description_long: Snake ( ninja ) Snake was one of the three ninja in the service of Daisake Mayazato in the town of Aru in Wa . History . Snake trained in ninja arts inside the Warazama clan together with Moonlight and Smoke , until that clan was destroyed by internal dissent . He and his fellows entered into the service of Daisake Mayazato to to repay him for previous services .

title: Snake - dog
description: Snake - dog A snake - dog was a cross - breed of a venomous snake and a dog domesticated by the yuan - ti that lived in the jungles of Chult . Description . Snake - dogs were around 2 ft ( 0 .
description_long: Snake - dog A snake - dog was a cross - breed of a venomous snake and a dog domesticated by the yuan - ti that lived in the jungles of Chult . Description . Snake - dogs were around 2 ft ( 0 . 6 m ) tall at the shoulder , with an elongated body and a snake - like tail . Its body was about 4 ft ( 1 . 2 m ) long and its neck the same length again . It has an elongated , flattened snake - like head except for the ears . The snake - dog can unhinge its own jaw to allow it to swallow larger objects than would normally fit , and has rows of sharp fangs . It is covered in snake - like jungle - coloured scales which help its disguise in a jungle environment . Behavior . The snake - dog is aggressive , but not overly so , fiercely protecting its own kind , especially females and the young . It is able to swim well thanks to its snake - like qualities , helping it through the water . It has a venomous bite which it will use in a confrontation , as well as the ability to trip bipeds using its long neck . They can be trained to become effective defensive pets . Diet . Snake - dogs eat small rodents , mammals and vermin . The long neck helps it to capture prey inside burrows . History .

title: Snake Road
description: Snake Road The Snake Road was a road in the Dragon Coast . The snake road ran from Elversult south across the Horse Prairie to the town of Wyrm ' s Hamlet on the Lake of the Snake . Blacknight Manor and the Ginger Palace were both on the Snake Road .
description_long: Snake Road The Snake Road was a road in the Dragon Coast . The snake road ran from Elversult south across the Horse Prairie to the town of Wyrm ' s Hamlet on the Lake of the Snake . Blacknight Manor and the Ginger Palace were both on the Snake Road .

title: Snakewood
description: Snakewood The Snakewood was a relatively small forest located in eastern Amn . Etymology . It was given the name " Snakewood " because of the great number of black and green snakes that lived there .
description_long: Snakewood The Snakewood was a relatively small forest located in eastern Amn . Etymology . It was given the name " Snakewood " because of the great number of black and green snakes that lived there . Geography . The forest was located west of the Troll Mountains , south of the Green Fields , north of the Amstel and Splendarrllur rivers and east of the Cloud Peaks . Flora & Fauna . Other than snakes , the forest was known to be the home of small pockets of giant spider s History . The Snakewood was once part of the great forest of Shantel Othreier . The forest was split off from Shantel Othreier by dragon fires as early as −11 , 700 DR . By −1100 DR , elves had slain the last great dragon from the forest , then known as the Wyrmwood , and they founded a kingdom there , which they called Arundath , the Quiet Wood . The elves were nearly eradicated by human s during the last one hundred years of the Shoon Imperium , ( the late 350s DR ) . This was because the elves tried to protect a small herd of seven unicorn s in the woods from the evil emperor Shoon VII , who wanted their horns for his magic , in particular for the powerful artifact known as the Tome of the Unicorn .

title: Snapjaw
description: Snapjaw Snapjaw was a lizardfolk of the Scaly Death tribe in the Mere of Dead Men during the Tyranny of the Dragons . Snapjaw was a proud lizardfolk warrior . However , like the other members of his tribe , he was recruited to work as a labourer and hunter for the Cult of the Dragon .
description_long: Snapjaw Snapjaw was a lizardfolk of the Scaly Death tribe in the Mere of Dead Men during the Tyranny of the Dragons . Snapjaw was a proud lizardfolk warrior . However , like the other members of his tribe , he was recruited to work as a labourer and hunter for the Cult of the Dragon . Under orders of Dralmorrer Borngray , the lizardfolk were put under control of the bullywug , who previously killed the tribe ' s leader Suncaller . Behind the Scenes . In the " Hoard of the Dragon Queen " adventure , if the players meet and befriend him , Snapjaw can be a powerful ally , helping them to enter Castle Naerytar in exchange for helping him defeat the bullywug .

title: Snare
description: Snare Snare was a transmutation or enchantment spell that created a magical booby trap . Effects . A loop at the end of some strong , supple material ( rope , cord , a vine , a leather thong , etc .
description_long: Snare Snare was a transmutation or enchantment spell that created a magical booby trap . Effects . A loop at the end of some strong , supple material ( rope , cord , a vine , a leather thong , etc . ) became a magical trap that constricted around any creature stepping inside or passing through the loop . The loose end of the snare could be tied to something solid or , if tied to a strong , flexible tree nearby , the spell would cause the tree to bend down and then snap back to original shape when the snare was triggered , likely hoisting the prey up by an appendage . The snare was very difficult to detect by even those skilled in locating traps because the spell caused the snare to blend in with its surroundings , giving it nearly perfect camouflage . The trap was magical and could be detected by magical methods , but could not be escaped except by very strong creatures or those dexterious enough to wiggle out of it . A magical blade easily cut the cord , or a mundane sharp blade carefully inserted into the constricting circle and sufficient force applied was also effective in releasing captives . A successful escape by any means broke the loop and the spell .

title: Snilloc
description: Snilloc Snilloc was an adventuring wizard who lived some time in the 13th century by Dalereckoning . Biography . Snilloc traveled with a party of adventurers , allegedly fighting beholder s , dinosaur s , pirates , spirits , and vampire s .
description_long: Snilloc Snilloc was an adventuring wizard who lived some time in the 13th century by Dalereckoning . Biography . Snilloc traveled with a party of adventurers , allegedly fighting beholder s , dinosaur s , pirates , spirits , and vampire s . He wrote a book full of anecdotes on how to defeat such monsters . Snilloc gained fame among his fellow wizards by developing several cold - based evocation s and more general fame when he helped save Procampur from a horde of hobgoblin s . Rumor had it that Snilloc spent his final years living in Zakhara . Legacy . Snilloc was the inventor of three known spells in the Realms , " Snilloc ' s snowball " , " Snilloc ' s snowball swarm " and " Snilloc ' s major missile " , as well as a rumored fourth , " Snilloc ' s cream pie " . There also existed a path of power based on Snilloc ' s magic , a so - called lost path which was not publicly known . Personality . If Snilloc ' s writings represented his personality in person , then he was apparently a patronizing and overly self - confident individual . Relationships .

title: Snilloc ' s major missile
description: Snilloc ' s major missile Snilloc ' s major missile was an arcane evocation spell that improved upon the " magic missile " spell by increasing the possible damage for high - level casters . Effects . This spell produced a single missile and could only be aimed at one target within 60 yd ( 55 m ) plus 10 yd ( 9 .
description_long: Snilloc ' s major missile Snilloc ' s major missile was an arcane evocation spell that improved upon the " magic missile " spell by increasing the possible damage for high - level casters . Effects . This spell produced a single missile and could only be aimed at one target within 60 yd ( 55 m ) plus 10 yd ( 9 . 1 m ) per level of the caster . The possible damage of the missile increased in proportion to the caster ' s level until a maximum was reached . All spells and effects that negated " magic missile " also affected " Snilloc ' s major missile " . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell . History . The Avatar Crisis prompted intense research into improving the " magic missile " spell , and this spell was the result . " Snilloc ' s major missile " was first published in " The Collected Wisdom of Snilloc " and then later published in " Volo ' s Guide to All Things Magical " , where it became generally known to the magical community .

title: Snilloc ' s snowball
description: Snilloc ' s snowball Snilloc ' s snowball was an evocation spell in general use throughout the Realms . Effects . This spell caused one ball of magical snow to instantly appear in the caster ' s hand which could then be thrown at any creature or object within the range of the spell ' s effect .
description_long: Snilloc ' s snowball Snilloc ' s snowball was an evocation spell in general use throughout the Realms . Effects . This spell caused one ball of magical snow to instantly appear in the caster ' s hand which could then be thrown at any creature or object within the range of the spell ' s effect . The frigid projectile struck unerringly , like a " magic missile " , and could be deflected or negated by the same methods that worked against " magic missile " . At higher levels , the range of this spell was much greater than for " magic missile " , but it was limited to just the one snowball . Creatures with an affinity for fire were particularly susceptible to damage from this spell , taking up to twice as much damage as a non - fire - using creature . Components . Verbal and somatic components were necessary to cast this spell , as well as a chip of ice or a fleck of ivory . Appendix . Origins . Dave Collins created this spell in Jeff Grubb ' s original campaign setting and it eventually became " Snilloc ' s snowball " in the Forgotten Realms Adventures sourcebook .

title: Snilloc ' s snowball swarm
description: Snilloc ' s snowball swarm Snilloc ' s snowball swarm , also just snowball swarm , was a spell that generated an explosion of snowballs that covered a 10 ft ( 3 m ) radius area . An older version of this spell covered a 30 ft ( 9 m ) radius but did less damage . Effect .
description_long: Snilloc ' s snowball swarm Snilloc ' s snowball swarm , also just snowball swarm , was a spell that generated an explosion of snowballs that covered a 10 ft ( 3 m ) radius area . An older version of this spell covered a 30 ft ( 9 m ) radius but did less damage . Effect . The caster could choose the center of the explosion and was subject to being struck if within the area of effect . Snowballs were normal missiles , but there were so many moving so fast that only the very dexterous could even hope to avoid getting hit as snowballs spattered on every solid object , such as walls and ceilings . Components . Verbal , somatic and material components were required to cast this spell , including a piece of ice or a small chip of white rock . The material component of the earlier version of the spell was either ice or a single pearl . History . This spell was created by the mage Snilloc . He placed this spell in the tome " The Collected Wisdom of Snilloc " . Eventually the tome was stolen and this spell was copied and appeared throughout the Realms . This spell was also in the pamphlet " Volo ' s Guide to All Things Magical " published at the start of 1369 DR .

title: Snowdown
description: Snowdown Snowdown was an island of the Moonshae Isles . It lay to the east of Gwynneth . Inhabitants .
description_long: Snowdown Snowdown was an island of the Moonshae Isles . It lay to the east of Gwynneth . Inhabitants . The Ffolk and colonists from Amn live on the island . History . During the 1400s , Snowdown became a colony of Amn . As of 1479 DR , Snowdown was ruled by Lady Erliza Daressin , Viceroy of Caer Westphal .

title: Snowdrift Inn
description: Snowdrift Inn The Snowdrift Inn was an inn in Easthaven within the Ten - Towns of Icewind Dale . Structure . Located near Pomab ' s Emporium in the eastern part of Easthaven , the wooden building looked inviting to many a cold traveler .
description_long: Snowdrift Inn The Snowdrift Inn was an inn in Easthaven within the Ten - Towns of Icewind Dale . Structure . Located near Pomab ' s Emporium in the eastern part of Easthaven , the wooden building looked inviting to many a cold traveler . The inn was surrounded on the outside by racks of drying knucklehead trout , which gave the surrounding area a fishy smell . Interior . The one - story inn was a comfortable sight with a warm common room and three rooms where adventurer s from the Frozenfar could rest for an evening or two . Inhabitants . The Snowdrift was owned by Quimby , who would share tales of Easthaven with newcomers . History . In Eleint , 1281 DR , an elven wanderer named Erevain Blacksheaf from Evereska stayed at the inn after his travels from Kuldahar in the Spine of the World .

title: Snowflake Mountains
description: Snowflake Mountains The Snowflake Mountains were a range of mountains in West Faerûn , forming the borders between Tethyr , Amn , and what was once the barony of Impresk within Erlkazar . They included some of the tallest mountains in Faerûn . Geography .
description_long: Snowflake Mountains The Snowflake Mountains were a range of mountains in West Faerûn , forming the borders between Tethyr , Amn , and what was once the barony of Impresk within Erlkazar . They included some of the tallest mountains in Faerûn . Geography . These mountains were part of the Iltkazar Range , a chain that stretched all the way to the Shining Sea in the south .
