description_long: Star sapphire Star Sapphire was a very rare form of sapphire that exhibited . Description . Asterism is a reflective optical effect that highlights a white six - pointed star on the surface of cabochon - cut stones . Star sapphires were more opaque than regular gem - quality sapphire s . About one in a thousand sapphires was a star sapphire . A typical specimen had a base value of 5 , 000 gp or 1 , 000 gp depending on market conditions . Star sapphires were considered sacred by followers of Callarduran Smoothhands , Corellon Larethian , Deneir , Gaerdal Ironhand , and Luthic — appropriate for sacrifice , or to be consecrated for use , or recognized as boons or omens when found . Powers . Star sappires were often used in making and decorating devices and objects to ward off hostile magic , such as " globes of invulnerability " , allowing them to be effective against stronger spells . Many spells could be enhanced by adding a star sapphire to the material component . For example , the duration of an " antimagic shell " could be extended for more than two hours beyond the usual time limit .

title: Stardeep
description: Stardeep Stardeep was a small dungeon complex sited in a small demiplane in the Ethereal Plane in a tenuous pocket near Sildëyuir . Stardeep was linked to Faerûn by a portal called the Causeway , appearing as a stone bridge over the Mere river , a tributary of the Chubala River . History .
description_long: Stardeep Stardeep was a small dungeon complex sited in a small demiplane in the Ethereal Plane in a tenuous pocket near Sildëyuir . Stardeep was linked to Faerûn by a portal called the Causeway , appearing as a stone bridge over the Mere river , a tributary of the Chubala River . History . Stardeep was created by the star elves as a prison for the Traitor and to guard against the Abolethic Sovereignty and the city of Xxiphu . Inhabitants . Stardeep was normally inhabited by two star elven Keepers of the Cerulean Sign and around two hundred Empyrean Knight s , as well as the sentient construct Cynosure .

title: Stargazer
description: Stargazer The Stargazer refers to a female elf who , thousands of years ago , picked up One Thousand Broken Dreams after the death of Datharian Mistwatcher and used it to slay hundreds of drow . Her true identity is not known . She died of grief over the death of her sister , after the Battle of Nine Arrows .
description_long: Stargazer The Stargazer refers to a female elf who , thousands of years ago , picked up One Thousand Broken Dreams after the death of Datharian Mistwatcher and used it to slay hundreds of drow . Her true identity is not known . She died of grief over the death of her sister , after the Battle of Nine Arrows .

title: Starleaf
description: Starleaf Starleaf was a Wild elf and High Mage of enormous power . She served as center in a high magic ritual , known as the First Sundering . Her role was revealed to the elves by a gathering of elven priests , who got her role revealed from the Seldarine .
description_long: Starleaf Starleaf was a Wild elf and High Mage of enormous power . She served as center in a high magic ritual , known as the First Sundering . Her role was revealed to the elves by a gathering of elven priests , who got her role revealed from the Seldarine . At that time she was still a small girl in the woods of Faerûn but she accepted her fate and left the forests to train as a mage . At the day of the ritual she stood at the center of the tower in the middle of many other high mages . She controlled the powers of the spell and formed the will of the gathered elves to create the promised land . When the spell took form she saw the other mages die and felt the tremors ripping Faerûn apart . She was the only one of the gathered mages that survived this day . That accomplished Starleaf awoke on the island of Evermeet before the Tree of Souls and was greeted by the gods Angharradh and Corellon Larethian . Both gods revealed to her that they had their part in the spell and that Evermeet and the destruction of Faerûn was also their blame too . They made Starleaf the guardian of the artifact , which should one day bring high magic to the elves when it was lost to the world .

title: Starless Night
description: Starless Night Starless Night is the second book in the Legacy of the Drow series by R . A . Salvatore .
description_long: Starless Night Starless Night is the second book in the Legacy of the Drow series by R . A . Salvatore . It was later reissued as book eight of the Legend of Drizzt series . Summary . In the first part of the book , Drizzt Do ' Urden leaves Mithral Hall directed to Menzoberranzan . He is afraid that the drow still represent a threat to his friends and he is ready to do anything to stop them . He meets Ellifain , an elf he saved from a drow raid when he was still living among his kin , and then he reaches Mooshie ' s Grove , which he finds now inhabited by a unicorn . Meanwhile , Catti - brie sets up in pursuit as soon as she learns of the drow ' s departure , starting to realize that she has been harboring feelings for him . She reaches Silverymoon where Lady Alustriel helps her with directions and equipment . In the meantime Matron Mother Yvonnel Baenre is carrying out preparations for her long planned conquest of Mithral Hall . In the second part of the book Drizzt sneaks and fights his way through the tunnels of the Underdark . He comes close to the svirfneblin city of Blingdenstone where he helps some of the deep gnomes against a drow party , but he is knocked unconscious .

title: Starling house
description: Starling house Starling house was one of the houses in the village of West Harbor on the Sword Coast North . It was inhabited by the Starling family . Location .
description_long: Starling house Starling house was one of the houses in the village of West Harbor on the Sword Coast North . It was inhabited by the Starling family . Location . Located near the edge of the village , the Starling house was located next to Tarmas ' home . Structure . Like the other houses in West Harbor , the Starling house was wooden . Interior . This was the largest building in West Harbor . It was composed of a children ' s bedroom , a hall , and a living room . History . Retta Starling and the Kalach - Cha ' s friend , Bevil Starling ( as well as his siblings ) , lived in this house . When duergar and bladeling s attacked the village in 1374 DR , some of the duergar went into the house . The Kalach - Cha could ' ve helped Bevil to come to his house and attack the duergar , with the help of his dogs : Muttonchop , Locke , and Nasher .

title: Starmantle
description: Starmantle Starmantle was a small city located on the Dragon Coast . It was one of Westgate ' s main rivals for trade across the Sea of Fallen Stars . History .
description_long: Starmantle Starmantle was a small city located on the Dragon Coast . It was one of Westgate ' s main rivals for trade across the Sea of Fallen Stars . History . In the mid - to - late fourteenth century DR , Starmantle was inundated by flood of Shou human s from Thesk . Starmantle was destroyed in 1385 DR by the Spellplague . , and just over a decade later , the city was little more then ruins . Large man - sized , gemstone - hard , emerald - colored outcrops that hummed with a single flute - like note covered the ruins and the surrounding land . A flickering blue glow passed between the outcrops . Obsidian masses slowly drifted across the open ground . The only inhabitants were plaguechanged ghoul s .

title: Starry Gnosis
description: Starry Gnosis The Starry Gnosis was a minor artifact of Shadow Weave magic imbued by the goddess Shar with powers of mental domination . Purported to be a relic of the goddess Mystra instead , it was used to abduct petitioners at the false Temple of Mystra in Wheloon in the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR . Description .
description_long: Starry Gnosis The Starry Gnosis was a minor artifact of Shadow Weave magic imbued by the goddess Shar with powers of mental domination . Purported to be a relic of the goddess Mystra instead , it was used to abduct petitioners at the false Temple of Mystra in Wheloon in the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR . Description . The " Starry Gnosis " was a crystal sphere about the size of a ( 3 . 9 – 5 . 9 in , or 10 – 15 cm ) . It had a dark inner core that no light could penetrate , yet tiny points of light twinkled like stars at the edge of this dark heart . When the full power of the " Starry Gnosis " was called upon , these stars disappeared as if swallowed up , until it was ready to use again three days ' hence . It was rather like a crystal ball gone dark . Powers . When the " Starry Gnosis " was held and the command phrase " Knowledge lies between the stars " was uttered , it produced a terrible bewitching effect on all within 30 feet ( 9 . 1 meters ) who were not allied with the bearer . Those whose wills faltered in the face of it would struggle to strike the holder of the " Starry Gnosis " .

title: Starspire
description: Starspire The Starspire was a large peak in northern Melabrauth . Background . The Starspire was so large that its peak reached the sky .
description_long: Starspire The Starspire was a large peak in northern Melabrauth . Background . The Starspire was so large that its peak reached the sky . People believed that inside its caverns were hidden fabulous treasures , but most of the caves were rigged by traps to hold adventurers at bay .

title: Starspire Mountains
description: Starspire Mountains The Starspire Mountains were a range of low mountains in Tethyr . Geography . The Starspires began gradually in the highlands of eastern Tethyr and ran from east to west .
description_long: Starspire Mountains The Starspire Mountains were a range of low mountains in Tethyr . Geography . The Starspires began gradually in the highlands of eastern Tethyr and ran from east to west . A spur of the Starspire Mountains extended into the Sea of Swords , forming the Starspire Peninsula . The average height of the mountains in this range were only 4 , 500 feet above sea level . Four of the peaks were above 5 , 000 feet . The summit of the tallest was at 7 , 200 feet , making this range among the smallest of the Lands of Intrigue . Hawkwing ' s Brook , a major tributary to the Sulduskoon River , flowed down from the eastern slopes . Climate . The Starspires were very humid ; they received a large amount of rain during the summer months and snow during the winter months . The snow could remain on the taller peaks even into the summer . The peaks were nearly tree - covered , growing more dense in greenery as the slopes met the Forest of Tethir to the north or the waters of the Sulduskoon River to the south . Fauna . Sheeps and goats belonging to local farmers of counties Starspur and Uluran dotted the foothills of the Starspires .

title: Starspur
description: Starspur Starspur was the county of Tethyr encompassing the Starspire Peninsula . It was known for the city of Zazesspur , the sometime capital of that kingdom . Description .
description_long: Starspur Starspur was the county of Tethyr encompassing the Starspire Peninsula . It was known for the city of Zazesspur , the sometime capital of that kingdom . Description . Unlike the lowlands of Tethyr , the county of Starspur was infested with a variety of monsters , because there were so many mountains , hills , cliffs , and sea caves for them to inhabit . Geography . Starspur was part of the of Kamlann . It was isolated from the rest of Tethyr by its position on the Starspire Peninsula , its only significant border being with County Uluran to the east . Inhabitants . The wild lands of Starspur were home to goblinoid s , cyclopskin , urd s , and flind s . Peryton s , hippogriff s , fire drake s , and possibly dragon s also lived in the region . Government . In 1370 DR , Starspur was ruled over by the Countess and Royal Admiral Corinna Dezlentyr . Her castle was named Battles ' End and was situated atop high foothills .

title: Starwater River
description: Starwater River The Starwater River was a river in Cormyr . It flowed south from the Storm Horns mountain range , through the King ' s Forest , to the Dragonmere . The city of Marsember was situated on the western bank of the mouth of the river .
description_long: Starwater River The Starwater River was a river in Cormyr . It flowed south from the Storm Horns mountain range , through the King ' s Forest , to the Dragonmere . The city of Marsember was situated on the western bank of the mouth of the river . Description . The Starwater was populated by treacherous sandbars , which made it dangerous to those who were not familiar with them . The most southerly rapids were in Redhand Pool in Eveningstar , although boats needed to be fairly narrow to navigate the Mouth O ' Gargoyles .

title: Starym
description: Starym House Starym was an ultraconservative and powerful elven noble family that once inhabited the city of Cormanthor ( later Myth Drannor ) in the elven empire of Cormanthyr . Comprised chiefly of Gold elves but with some Moon elves as well , they became discontent when Coronal Eltargrim Irithyl allowed races such as gnomes , halflings and dwarves to inhabit the city . Their reputation as a trusted influential house was destroyed after they attacked the Elven Court , subsequently most of the gold elves emigrated from Myth Drannor .
description_long: Starym House Starym was an ultraconservative and powerful elven noble family that once inhabited the city of Cormanthor ( later Myth Drannor ) in the elven empire of Cormanthyr . Comprised chiefly of Gold elves but with some Moon elves as well , they became discontent when Coronal Eltargrim Irithyl allowed races such as gnomes , halflings and dwarves to inhabit the city . Their reputation as a trusted influential house was destroyed after they attacked the Elven Court , subsequently most of the gold elves emigrated from Myth Drannor . History . The Starym Clan of elves had been in the city of Cormanthor for quite sometime , as a member of the 12 First Houses of Cormanthyr , ( in fact , even their rivals admit to Starym being the First house , pinnacle of all that is noble and fine among the elves ) but their notable history begins after the Dalereckoning . Starym , along with other old noble houses , put forward much resistance to the forward - thinking Coronal Eltargrim Irithyl , and vehemently opposed his liberal ideas of opening the capital city to the N ' Tel ' Quess ( the " Not - People " ; anyone not an elf ) , where formerly it was barred against all but the elves .

title: Stasis sphere
description: Stasis sphere The stasis sphere was a magical item . When touched by its owner and commanded , one nearby creature could be placed in " temporal stasis " and confined inside the sphere , similar to the " imprisonment " spell . Description .
description_long: Stasis sphere The stasis sphere was a magical item . When touched by its owner and commanded , one nearby creature could be placed in " temporal stasis " and confined inside the sphere , similar to the " imprisonment " spell . Description . The sphere was a greenish and glowing sphere made of crystal , around 8 feet ( 2 . 4 meters ) in diameter and weighing 1000 pounds ( 453 kilograms ) . Inside the sphere , there was an extra - dimensional space in which as many as fifty creatures could be confined . With a second command , a creature could be freed . Once the sphere has been used fifty times , it could no longer confine new creatures . History . It was created in the age of Netheril . It was used by Telkoun Adranther in the Telkoun ' s Tower for his creepy experiments .

title: Statue
description: Statue Statue was an arcane alteration spell that changed the recipient together with anything worn to stone , but kept their faculties and senses intact . In older versions the magical transformation carried a certain risk of immediate death , but if successfull , all versions allowed the affected person or creature to hide in plains sight as a statue , with all the resiliency of stone . The recipient could turn back to their normal form at will .
description_long: Statue Statue was an arcane alteration spell that changed the recipient together with anything worn to stone , but kept their faculties and senses intact . In older versions the magical transformation carried a certain risk of immediate death , but if successfull , all versions allowed the affected person or creature to hide in plains sight as a statue , with all the resiliency of stone . The recipient could turn back to their normal form at will . Components . Apart from verbal and somatic components , the caster had to stir some lime , sand and water with a rodlike piece of iron . History . The " statue " spell was first introduced in the time of Netheril , in 1839 NY ( −2020 DR ) , under the name Quantoul ' s statue , after famous variator arcanist Quantoul . " Statue " was an uncommon spell to the magical community of Faerûn by 1358 DR .

title: Statue of Mystra
description: Statue of Mystra The statue of Mystra was a magical statue of the goddess Mystra standing in the Stoneyard of the false Temple of Mystra in Wheloon in the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR . History . To aid in their deception , the false priests of the temple bought up a large quantity of religious paraphernalia , but chose to destroy much of what they did not need or found to be against the faith of Shar .
description_long: Statue of Mystra The statue of Mystra was a magical statue of the goddess Mystra standing in the Stoneyard of the false Temple of Mystra in Wheloon in the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR . History . To aid in their deception , the false priests of the temple bought up a large quantity of religious paraphernalia , but chose to destroy much of what they did not need or found to be against the faith of Shar . Among these was a statue of Mystra , whose holy and miraculous nature surprised them . No matter how they damaged it each day , it was whole again the next night . It then exuded a disturbing glow . The Sharrans then tried to hide it by heaping the debris about it , but this was always shed again . Though the temple was a front for followers of Shar , and thus within her dark power , Mystra ' s holy image had given her influence and the chance to oppose their sacrilege . When adventurers in service to Mystra investigating the temple passed through on Eleint 6 , the statue of Mystra could well have come alive to battle the dark earth elemental that rose out of the shattered statuary in the Stoneyard . It would give a motion of blessing before falling dormant again .

title: Status
description: Status Status is a divination spell that allows one to monitor the position and condition of one ' s allies . Effect . When a cleric needs to keep track of comrades that may get separated , " status " allows him to mentally monitor their relative position and general condition .
description_long: Status Status is a divination spell that allows one to monitor the position and condition of one ' s allies . Effect . When a cleric needs to keep track of comrades that may get separated , " status " allows him to mentally monitor their relative position and general condition . The cleric is aware of direction and distance to the creatures and their status : unharmed , wounded , disabled , staggered , unconscious , dying , dead , etc . Once the spell has been cast upon the subjects , the distance between them and the caster does not affect the spell as long as they are on the same plane of existence . If they leave it , the spell ceases to function for them .

title: Staunt Pools
description: Staunt Pools The Staunt Pools referred to a succession of deep holes located in the River Rauvin to the west of Jalanthar . Description . The pools were the lair of a freshwater giant squid .
description_long: Staunt Pools The Staunt Pools referred to a succession of deep holes located in the River Rauvin to the west of Jalanthar . Description . The pools were the lair of a freshwater giant squid . Many barge guards swore to have met and killed the squid , but others reported attacks by another identical example . The legend of the " Treasure of the Holes " was very well known in the region . History . According to the rumor , a barge carrying a dwarf - treasure full of silver bullion was sunk somewhere between the sludge of one of these pools . The pools were named for the ruined village of Staunt ' s Hold that once stood nearby .

title: Steaming Isles
description: Steaming Isles The Steaming Isles , located in the southeast of Zakhara ' s Crowded Sea , were very unusual . Unexplored by denizens of the mainland , these islands , shrouded in mist and covered in sub - tropical forest , were inhabited and ruled by intelligent , talking animals . Geography .
description_long: Steaming Isles The Steaming Isles , located in the southeast of Zakhara ' s Crowded Sea , were very unusual . Unexplored by denizens of the mainland , these islands , shrouded in mist and covered in sub - tropical forest , were inhabited and ruled by intelligent , talking animals . Geography . The chain was made up of six large island surrounded by numerous smaller islands . From west to east these were Jaqal ( Jackal ) , Baz ( Hawk ) , Gazal ( Gazelle ) , Hayyat ( Snake ) , Sunn ( Swallow ) and Nimr ( Tiger ) . Society . The animal inhabitants of the Steaming Isles in general acted like normal animals , but still had formed society structures similar to those found in Enlightened Zakhara , with a Shah ruling over each island . Each Shah was of the species of the island ' s name . The supreme ruler was Padishah Jaqal .

title: Stedd Whitehorn
description: Stedd Whitehorn Stedd Whitehorn was a young boy Chosen and prophet of Lathander during the Second Sundering . History . Stedd was chosen by the god Lathander to announce his return to the people of the Realms .
description_long: Stedd Whitehorn Stedd Whitehorn was a young boy Chosen and prophet of Lathander during the Second Sundering . History . Stedd was chosen by the god Lathander to announce his return to the people of the Realms . Unfortunately , this attracted the ire of many factions that opposed this event . First , Stedd was captured by the Shadovar and imprisoned in a secret village in the Lost Peaks together with many other Chosen . He was freed from the camp by the Harpers and Farideh . Afterward , Stedd was pursued by the Chosen of Umberlee , Evendur Highcastle and the Red Wizards of Thay . At last , Stedd fulfilled his mission of curing the leader of the Emerald Enclave from a Shar - induced - madness .

title: Steel dragon
description: Steel dragon Steel dragons , sometimes known as Waterdeep dragons , were metallic dragon s who were rarely seen in their natural form , instead living clandestine lives in human cities , observing art , culture , history , and politics . Description . Steel dragons in their natural forms were especially feline in their movements and stature .
description_long: Steel dragon Steel dragons , sometimes known as Waterdeep dragons , were metallic dragon s who were rarely seen in their natural form , instead living clandestine lives in human cities , observing art , culture , history , and politics . Description . Steel dragons in their natural forms were especially feline in their movements and stature . They had scales that shone like burnished steel as adults and usually smelled like wet metal . Younge dragons ' scales were a darker blue - gray and less lustrous . Their faces were particularly expressive , sometimes giving the illusion of a human - like face . They had many long spines surrounding their faces , which gave the appearance of hair . In humanoid forms , steel dragons usually kept their true identities secret ; however , they always had at least one visual indication of their true nature in the form of steel - gray hair , eyes , tattoos , or another feature . Abilities . Steel dragons were immune to acid and resistant to poison and especially magic . They had innate abilities to enchant and charm individuals . Personality . Steel dragons , as a rule , were amiable , curious , and witty .

title: Steeping Falls
description: Steeping Falls Steeping Falls was an ancient barony that encompassed the lands surrounding modern - day Daggerford . History . Founded by the Shoon outlaw , Artor Morlin in 133 DR , the barony was located just to the west of Athalantar but between the Realm of the Stag and Halangorn Forest on the north bank of the Delimbiyr .
description_long: Steeping Falls Steeping Falls was an ancient barony that encompassed the lands surrounding modern - day Daggerford . History . Founded by the Shoon outlaw , Artor Morlin in 133 DR , the barony was located just to the west of Athalantar but between the Realm of the Stag and Halangorn Forest on the north bank of the Delimbiyr . It served as a crossroads for traders travelling on and along the river . Morlin eventually allowed his realm to fall , preferring the life of a mercenary captain battling the forces of the Imperium . By 403 DR Artor ' s home - Morlin Castle - had fallen into ruin and had gained a reputation for being haunted by undead and other monsters . It would take more than five hundred years for people to stop avoiding the castle and Castle Daggerford was built upon Morlin Castle ' s foundations . However a remnant of Morlin Castle could be accessed via the Ethereal Plane that was used by Artor Morlin as an emergency redoubt .

title: Steersissk
description: Steersissk Steersissk was a lizardfolk in the Vast Swamp in 1374 DR . History . Stersissk was a warrior of the Sharptooth tribe .
description_long: Steersissk Steersissk was a lizardfolk in the Vast Swamp in 1374 DR . History . Stersissk was a warrior of the Sharptooth tribe . In 1374 the fellow lizardfolk tribe of the Shadowscale allied with the Church of Shar and began to act strangely . They eventually started a war with the Sharptooth . In fighting Steersissk was captured as many others to be converted to Shar thank to a ritual in the Plane of Shadow . Stersissk escaped just entered in the Plane of Shadows but was recaptured by a sharran patrol soon after . However was at this time that an adventurers party assaulted the keep where he was prisoner . Gameplay . If free Steersissk fought alongside the adventurers against his Sharran captors .

title: Stegosaurus
description: Stegosaurus A stegosaurus was a gargantuan , herbivorous , herd dinosaur found in Chult . Description . These dinosaurs were immense and had many defenses to protect them from their many predators .
description_long: Stegosaurus A stegosaurus was a gargantuan , herbivorous , herd dinosaur found in Chult . Description . These dinosaurs were immense and had many defenses to protect them from their many predators . Along their spine from head to tail were a set of alternating bone plates . Their tails ended with a collection of sharp spikes , which were a yard ( one meter ) long . They had short legs with hoof - like feet . Behavior . A stegosaurus would use the plates on its back to distribute heat from the sun . They walked on four legs but could rear up to reach the leaves on tall trees . They had very tiny brains and so were not very intelligent . They tended to stick together in herds of five to eight animals . Combat . If threatened , a stegosaurus would continuously turn away from the threat , keeping its spiked tail toward the potential enemy . If attacked , a stegosaurus would kick with its forelegs , much like a horse , or it would thrash out with its spiked tail . A stegosaurus was particularly dangerous if charging , and it could easily trample smaller creatures underfoot . History . Stegosauruses , like most dinosaurs , originated in Chult .

title: Stellaga Brightstar
description: Stellaga Brightstar Mornmaster Stellaga Brightstar is the soft - spoken and diplomatic high priestess of the Morning temple in Archenbridge . Dedicated to her work , Stellaga encourages growth among the Arkhenfolk while taking little time to indulge in her more secret indulgences . These include dancing , adventuring and becoming romantic with people from far away .
description_long: Stellaga Brightstar Mornmaster Stellaga Brightstar is the soft - spoken and diplomatic high priestess of the Morning temple in Archenbridge . Dedicated to her work , Stellaga encourages growth among the Arkhenfolk while taking little time to indulge in her more secret indulgences . These include dancing , adventuring and becoming romantic with people from far away . Personality . Typically a gentle and resserved leader , Stellaga can occasionally be quite an upstart . On one occasion , Belorn " Battleaxe " the barbarian spent an exhausting night trying to escort both her and Jalia Mossgreen through a party thrown by the Arkhen clan at the gardens of Halanthaver House . The two ladies almost came to blows over Belorn , who bore bruises for months after the night when he foolishly tried to protect them from each other .

title: Stellephosa
description: Stellephosa Lady Stellephosa was a paladin of Kelemvor in Undermountain in 1479 DR . History . In 1479 DR , she went into Undermountain after hearing rumors of undead activities there .
description_long: Stellephosa Lady Stellephosa was a paladin of Kelemvor in Undermountain in 1479 DR . History . In 1479 DR , she went into Undermountain after hearing rumors of undead activities there . However , Stellephosa was instead captured by the goblin and kobold followers of the mad half - elf mercenary Zarr . Zarr forced her to fight as a gladiator against the bugbear Smurgle .

title: Stelwyn Russlewood
description: Stelwyn Russlewood Stelwyn Russlewood was a female human cleric of Iyachtu Xvim and an agent of Zhentil Keep based in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the late 1360s DR . Personality . Stelwyn was forthright in speech and tended to be destructive .
description_long: Stelwyn Russlewood Stelwyn Russlewood was a female human cleric of Iyachtu Xvim and an agent of Zhentil Keep based in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the late 1360s DR . Personality . Stelwyn was forthright in speech and tended to be destructive . She was cruel and enjoyed bullying those weaker or less fortunate than herself . Although not shy of her faith in Iyachtu Xvim , she preferred to keep quiet her affiliation to Zhentil Keep . Description . A young woman , she had midnight - black eyes and hair . Powers . In addition to commanding the prayers of a cleric , Stelwyn was an authlim , a specialty priest of Xvim . As such , she was immune to " fear " spells but could surround herself with an aura of " fear " once a day ; she could conjure an aura of " protection from good " and freely call upon Xvim to heal her wounds , once each a day . Equipment . Stelwyn wore " bracers of defense " , a " cloak of protection + 2 " , a " girdle of hill giant strength " , a " ring of free action " , and " ring of protection + 3 " , and swung a " + 3 footman ' s mace " in a fight . She carried a holy symbol of her god Xvim , and typically had six vials of unholy water .

title: Stephan
description: Stephan Stephan was the innkeeper of Bloodstone Village in 1357 DR . Activities . Stephan managed the Inn of the Clowns with his barmaids , Racquel and Carlotta .
description_long: Stephan Stephan was the innkeeper of Bloodstone Village in 1357 DR . Activities . Stephan managed the Inn of the Clowns with his barmaids , Racquel and Carlotta . They knew virtually everything about the community . People could win his respect by beating him at a drinking contest . History . Around 1345 DR , Stephan won the inn in a gambling match . He abandoned his career as a mercenary and settled in the village . Despite fewer people arriving at the inn over the years , Stephan was happy with his life .

title: Steploe Nestletoe
description: Steploe Nestletoe Steploe Nestletoe was a halfling member of the Cellarers ' & Plumbers ' Guild in Undermountain in 1479 DR . History . In 1479 DR , he was with his crew in the city ' s sewers when their lights suddenly went dark and he was struck on the head .
description_long: Steploe Nestletoe Steploe Nestletoe was a halfling member of the Cellarers ' & Plumbers ' Guild in Undermountain in 1479 DR . History . In 1479 DR , he was with his crew in the city ' s sewers when their lights suddenly went dark and he was struck on the head . Steploe woke up in Undermountain as a prisoner of the goblin and kobold followers of the mad half - elf mercenary Zarr . However , he believed he knew of a sure escape and he could learn something from this experience . Personality . Steploe was an eternal optimist .

title: Steps of Istishia
description: Steps of Istishia The Steps of Istishia was the most impressive structure within the city of Keltar . This monolithic shrine to the Water Lord was built thousands of years before the 14th century DR . Water from the Calim River was diverted by sluice gate and pumped to the top of the structure by hidden screw pumps .
description_long: Steps of Istishia The Steps of Istishia was the most impressive structure within the city of Keltar . This monolithic shrine to the Water Lord was built thousands of years before the 14th century DR . Water from the Calim River was diverted by sluice gate and pumped to the top of the structure by hidden screw pumps . The water was then magically guided down the monolith in four stair - like patterns to reach a pool of water surrounding the Steps . To ensure that this pool of water was always clear and clean , it was magically returned to the river twice a day to be replaced with fresh water .

title: Steve Kurtz
description: Steve Kurtz Steve Kurtz is an author and game designer who has written for TSR , Inc . , with several works published in the Al - Qadim setting . Background .
description_long: Steve Kurtz Steve Kurtz is an author and game designer who has written for TSR , Inc . , with several works published in the Al - Qadim setting . Background . Kurtz worked for TSR while in graduate school . After achieving his degree , he went on to develop medical devices .

title: Steve Miller
description: Steve Miller Steve Miller is a game designer who has worked for TSR , Inc . and Wizards of the Coast . Education .
description_long: Steve Miller Steve Miller is a game designer who has worked for TSR , Inc . and Wizards of the Coast . Education . Miller received his degree in English with a Creative Writing influence from the . Works . Miller was one of the authors of the first 3 edition Forgotten Realms adventure book , " Into the Dragon ' s Lair " .

title: Steve Winter
description: Steve Winter Steve Winter is a game designer who has worked for TSR , Inc . and Wizards of the Coast . Education .
description_long: Steve Winter Steve Winter is a game designer who has worked for TSR , Inc . and Wizards of the Coast . Education . Winter received a degree in Journalism from . Works . Winter worked as editor and game designer on many Dungeons & Dragons products , including " Oriental Adventures " and the " Pool of Radiance " game .

title: Steven E . Schend
description: Steven E . Schend Steven E . Schend is a fantasy writer and game designer .
description_long: Steven E . Schend Steven E . Schend is a fantasy writer and game designer . Background . Schend was born in 1967 and his childhood was heavily fantasy - influenced . He previously worked as a teacher , a street sweeper , a curb builder and a landscaper before gaining employment in fantasy , where he has worked for over fifteen years . He is a former game designer and editor for TSR , Inc . , Wizards of the Coast , Bastion Press , Green Ronin , and Goodman Games , as well as a former substitute teacher in Washington and Wisconsin . He is currently an adult instructor of World Building for Writers and Game & Adventure Design workshops / seminars . He also teaches college classes at various venues , including Kendall College of Art & Design . He claims his favorite role is spokesperson for the denizens of the " Forgotten Realms " . He is also currently working on a novel in his " Vanguard " universe and a non - fiction World - Building book for writers . Undermountain adventures ;

title: Sticks to snakes
description: Sticks to snakes Sticks to snakes was an alteration spell that turned appropriate non - magical wooden items into snakes for a few minutes . The reverse of this spell , snakes to sticks countered " sticks to snakes " or turned ordinary - sized snakes temporarily into sticks . Effects .
description_long: Sticks to snakes Sticks to snakes was an alteration spell that turned appropriate non - magical wooden items into snakes for a few minutes . The reverse of this spell , snakes to sticks countered " sticks to snakes " or turned ordinary - sized snakes temporarily into sticks . Effects . This spell could be cast on unenchanted wooden items that were significantly longer than their width , e . g . , sticks , torches , staves , planks , spears , etc . If an item was in the possession of a being , the being had a chance to resist the spell . The number of snakes that could be produced was somewhat random and increased with the level of the spellcaster , but at least eight snakes could be created if sufficient materials were at hand . The type of snakes produced was also variable but could be of the constricting or poisonous varieties . The chance for venomous snakes increased with the level of the caster . The snakes were under the command of the caster and would attack designated targets . When cast in reverse , " snakes to sticks " dismissed snakes created by " sticks to snakes " , returning them to their original form .

title: Stig
description: Stig Stig was a male human fighter and a bouncer at the tavern called The Furniture ' s Fate in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the late 1360s DR . He was very strong . When brawls broken out , Boffo the tavern owner often had Stig lift him up and hurl the gnome into the fray .
description_long: Stig Stig was a male human fighter and a bouncer at the tavern called The Furniture ' s Fate in the town of Thunderstone in Cormyr in the late 1360s DR . He was very strong . When brawls broken out , Boffo the tavern owner often had Stig lift him up and hurl the gnome into the fray .

title: Stiletto
description: Stiletto A stiletto , also known as a stylet is a slender dagger used for piercing leather and plated armor , and mail such as chain mail . Description . The slim blade of a stiletto is triangle or square in shape and ends in a sharp point .
description_long: Stiletto A stiletto , also known as a stylet is a slender dagger used for piercing leather and plated armor , and mail such as chain mail . Description . The slim blade of a stiletto is triangle or square in shape and ends in a sharp point . History . Many cities prohibited the use of stilettos because they could be easily concealed on the body , such as one used by the bandit known as Shadowhawk who operated within the King ' s Forest in 1335 DR .

title: Still Waters
description: Still Waters Still Waters was an inn located in the eastern part of the village of Elmwood on the southern side of the Moonsea . Structure . It was a two - story building run by master brewer , Enrad Daleborn , a friendly man whose was sought after in the area and a favorite of the River Lis ferry crewmen .
description_long: Still Waters Still Waters was an inn located in the eastern part of the village of Elmwood on the southern side of the Moonsea . Structure . It was a two - story building run by master brewer , Enrad Daleborn , a friendly man whose was sought after in the area and a favorite of the River Lis ferry crewmen . Inhabitants . The inn was owned by Enrad Daleborn , an honest hardworking man of plain looks , who loved to brew the finest amber drink in the region . Elenawen , one of his serving girls , aspired to become an acolyte of Selûne . While a serious - minded woman , Elenawen loved to flirt with charming human and half - elf men who frequented the establishment .

title: Stilmus
description: Stilmus Stilmus was a mercenary in Chessenta and the leader of the Society of the Sword . Personality . Stilmus was obsessed with honor and he never broke his word .
description_long: Stilmus Stilmus was a mercenary in Chessenta and the leader of the Society of the Sword . Personality . Stilmus was obsessed with honor and he never broke his word . For Stilmus , someone cheating him or his company was a challenge to his honor , a very serious matter . He fought many duels over this and sometimes drove the company on a quest for vengeance . Stilmus hated Helyos and hoped there would come a day when the Society of the Sword crush the Renegades and Helyos . History . Stilmus fought in many conflicts . During one of those conflicts he was in the same mercenary company as Helyos but Helyos tried to kill him . Later , Stilmus joined the Society of the Sword and by 1358 DR he was the leader of the Company .

title: Stinking cloud
description: Stinking cloud Stinking cloud , originally called Tolodine ' s stinking cloud , was a conjuration spell that created a cloud bank of nauseating vapors . Moon - horse s of Evermeet often used this spell . Effects .
description_long: Stinking cloud Stinking cloud , originally called Tolodine ' s stinking cloud , was a conjuration spell that created a cloud bank of nauseating vapors . Moon - horse s of Evermeet often used this spell . Effects . The cloud created by this spell had a 20 - foot ( six meter ) radius and was equally high . It could be formed anywhere within medium range . Creatures breathing in its fumes felt sick to the stomach . Components . This spell required verbal and somatic component s and a rotten egg , a handful of leaves , or yochlol essence , which were consumed in the casting process . When this spell was magically inscribed unto a scroll , ink made from yochlol essence or smoke drake eggs was often used . History . This spell and the similar " death fog " spell were invented by the Netherese arcanist Tolodine in −2363 DR , early in the history of Netheril .

title: Stirge
description: Stirge A stirge is a tiny magical beast that feeds on the blood of other creatures . A group of stirges is known as a " thirst " . Stirges have been known to be used as familiar s .
description_long: Stirge A stirge is a tiny magical beast that feeds on the blood of other creatures . A group of stirges is known as a " thirst " . Stirges have been known to be used as familiar s . Appearance . A stirge resembles a monstrous cross between a large hummingbird and a mosquito . Ecology . Stirges lurk in forests , caves , and swamps until a living creature passes near . They then fly down and attempt to subtly attach themselves to the creature and feed off its warm blood . While one stirge may not seem to be a threat , these creatures often cluster in large swarms , which can quickly slay a creature from all the stirges feeding at once on the same body . As of 1372 DR , stirges inhabited Velarswood in Harrowdale , the Duskwood in the Lake of Steam , the Umber Marshes in Aglarond , and Ardeep Forest . Cormanthor . Stirges in Cormanthor live in colonies that have a roaming area of around one square mile , and they sleep by day . At night , they pick on weaker or smaller animals such as dog s , goat s or pheasant s and suck their blood .

title: Stival Chergoba
description: Stival Chergoba Stival Chergoba was a warrior of Sossal during the Rage of Dragons of 1373 DR . History . Stival was a commander in the contingent led by Madislak Pemsk during the war against the Ice Witch Iyraclea and the white dragon dracolich Zethrindor .
description_long: Stival Chergoba Stival Chergoba was a warrior of Sossal during the Rage of Dragons of 1373 DR . History . Stival was a commander in the contingent led by Madislak Pemsk during the war against the Ice Witch Iyraclea and the white dragon dracolich Zethrindor . He was chosen alongside Natali Dormetsk to join Madislak in the duel against Zethrindor .

title: Stojanow
description: Stojanow The Stojanow river began high in the Dragonspine Mountains and flowed south into the Moonsea . There was fertile ground along this river allowing for farming of some grains and hardy vegetables . To the west of the river was the Grass Sea .
description_long: Stojanow The Stojanow river began high in the Dragonspine Mountains and flowed south into the Moonsea . There was fertile ground along this river allowing for farming of some grains and hardy vegetables . To the west of the river was the Grass Sea . On most of the east bank was the Quivering Forest . Circa 100 DR a pyramid was built on a large island in the middle of the river . Known as the Sorcerer ' s Isle this was used a wizard ' s school until it was later abandoned . There were several fortified hamlets along the Stojanow River , of which Kabel ' s Hill was one . The city of Phlan covered both banks of the river as it entered the Moonsea .

title: Stokely Silverstream
description: Stokely Silverstream Stokely Silverstream was the leader of the dwarven Clan Battlehammer that dwelt in Kelvin ' s Cairn in Icewind Dale . History . In his position as leader of the Clan Battlehammer dwarves , Stokely sometimes met with various humans , including Darby Snide , at a tavern in Bremen .
description_long: Stokely Silverstream Stokely Silverstream was the leader of the dwarven Clan Battlehammer that dwelt in Kelvin ' s Cairn in Icewind Dale . History . In his position as leader of the Clan Battlehammer dwarves , Stokely sometimes met with various humans , including Darby Snide , at a tavern in Bremen . Stokely was apparently killed in 1484 DR by Tiago Baenre during the Battle of Kelvin ' s Cairn when Tiago ' s forces attacked Clan Battlehammer . in truth he remained prisoner of the House Xorlarrin until 1485 DR when was freed after the dwarven victory in the War of the Silver Marches .

title: Stolvor
description: Stolvor Stolvor was a fire giant sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR Stolvor with his hell hound went in search of pieces of the Vonindod near the Stone Bridge ; however , secretly he was simply in search of a good fight .
description_long: Stolvor Stolvor was a fire giant sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR Stolvor with his hell hound went in search of pieces of the Vonindod near the Stone Bridge ; however , secretly he was simply in search of a good fight .

title: Stone Bridge
description: Stone Bridge Stone Bridge was a bridge located along the River Dessarin , connecting the Red Larch and the Long Road to the High Forest . The bridge , which was also a temple to Moradin , was a single arch , 3 . 2km ( two miles ) in length and 122m ( 400ft ) high , made of granite , roughly six paces wide , with no railings or barriers .
description_long: Stone Bridge Stone Bridge was a bridge located along the River Dessarin , connecting the Red Larch and the Long Road to the High Forest . The bridge , which was also a temple to Moradin , was a single arch , 3 . 2km ( two miles ) in length and 122m ( 400ft ) high , made of granite , roughly six paces wide , with no railings or barriers . It was originally built to connect the two halves of the realm of Besilmer , and was wide enough to cope with the broadest flow of the river in times of flooding . As of 1368 DR , it was a site of pilgrimage for dwarves of lawful good alignment . History . The bridge was the site of a fight between Torhild Flametongue , founder of the dwarven realm of Besilmer , and a hill giant , resulting in Torhild ' s death . During the final days of the Ironstar clan of dwarven , their king , Daurvos Frostbeard , was cut down on the bridge by orc s while the clan was attempting to flee south . While mortally wounded , he cried to Moradin for aid and died . Moradin ' s avatar , a 6m - high ( 20ft ) armoured dwarf , appeared on the bridge , rallying the fleeing dwarves and leading them to victory over the orcs .

title: Stone Guard
description: Stone Guard The Stone Guard was a military corp in Gracklstugh . They served Deepking Horgar Steelshadow V as bodyguards , elite troops , and secret police . History .
description_long: Stone Guard The Stone Guard was a military corp in Gracklstugh . They served Deepking Horgar Steelshadow V as bodyguards , elite troops , and secret police . History . The Stone Guard was first reformed as a strong organization of veteran soldiers under Horgar Steelshadow . During the Rage of Demons , corrupt members like Gorglak were present within their organization , but their high - ranking members and their commander Errde Blackskull were busy dealing with the corruption from the city .

title: Stone Stand
description: Stone Stand The Stone Stand was a stone circle in the High Forest in the Silver Marches . It contained a large oak tree , grown from a cutting from the Grandfather Tree . The site was sacred to the Tree Ghost tribe .
description_long: Stone Stand The Stone Stand was a stone circle in the High Forest in the Silver Marches . It contained a large oak tree , grown from a cutting from the Grandfather Tree . The site was sacred to the Tree Ghost tribe . Description . In the past this ancestral mound belonged to the Blue Bear Tribe . Afterward the Blue Bear Tribe became extinct . The mound was guarded by ghost s of many warriors of the tribe , each of whom had been in life a fierce and bloodthirsty fighter . The site was then consecrated to Malar the Beast - Lord .

title: Stone flyer
description: Stone flyer Stone flyers were magical beast s which hunted prey deep in the Underdark . Description . These creatures looked like wolves with large wings .
description_long: Stone flyer Stone flyers were magical beast s which hunted prey deep in the Underdark . Description . These creatures looked like wolves with large wings . Most stone flyers were earth tones , such as black , brown , or gray . Combat . Stone flyers moved through stone as if it was air and attacked victims with surprise . These earth elemental beasts worked in packs while hunting for prey .

title: Stone fountain
description: Stone fountain Stone fountain was a powerful arcane spell that could not just knock over stone towers and walls , but also lift and hurl them too . Effects . " Stone fountain " was a variant spell of " towerfall " , which quite simply lifted and knocked over huge stone structures , like castle towers , bridges , and city walls .
description_long: Stone fountain Stone fountain was a powerful arcane spell that could not just knock over stone towers and walls , but also lift and hurl them too . Effects . " Stone fountain " was a variant spell of " towerfall " , which quite simply lifted and knocked over huge stone structures , like castle towers , bridges , and city walls . " Stone fountain " extended this power to hurling the debris across the land . For example , a stone structure could be lifted up to three times its height into the air and thrown back down again , launching stone blocks in all directions except a 120° arc selected by the caster . History . Inhil " Hurler - of - Stars " Lauthdryn , the Magister from 154 to 1294 DR , had a special love of blowing up castles , hence his creation of " towerfall " and " stone fountain " . He took the secrets of the spells to his grave in the Year of Deep Moon , 1294 DR .

title: Stone giant
description: Stone giant A stone giant was a type of giant . Description . Adult stone giants averaged about 18 feet in height and weighed 1 , 700 pounds .
description_long: Stone giant A stone giant was a type of giant . Description . Adult stone giants averaged about 18 feet in height and weighed 1 , 700 pounds . Stone giants preferred to fight using ranged weapons such as boulders but if forced into melee they wielded gigantic stone club s . Abilities . Stone giants had an excellent sense of smell and had infravision to 200 feet ( 60 m ) . They spoke Jotunstein and Jotun . Stone giants were the longest living of the giants , despite their low position in the " ordning " . Ecology . Stone giants preferred temperate mountain ranges as their habitat . Stone giants were powerful enough to survive and make a living in the Underdark in the face of competition . They had a tendency to gather in larger individual groups as deeper the given group was located , but were primarily denizens of the Upperdark , though even there their number wasn ' t large . They carved their homes out of the rock and had a reputation as good artisans , though they generally maintained an uncaring stance towards other denizens of the Underdark and expected the same stance from the others . Society .

title: Stone golem
description: Stone golem Stone golems were constructed from either a single piece of carefully - chiseled stone or from a collection of specially - fitted stone blocks . The most elegant stone golems were used as both guardians and art pieces in a magical building . They appeared to be beautiful statues until commanded by their master to move and act .
description_long: Stone golem Stone golems were constructed from either a single piece of carefully - chiseled stone or from a collection of specially - fitted stone blocks . The most elegant stone golems were used as both guardians and art pieces in a magical building . They appeared to be beautiful statues until commanded by their master to move and act . Appearance . The average stone golem was 9 ft . ( 2 . 7 m ) tall and weighed 2 , 000 pounds ( 907 kg . ) . Sogi - nora . Sogi - nora were rare stone golems that could be found in the Hordelands . These golems were created by wu jen and given a mind of their own . They were adept at implementing martial arts maneuvers like throws during combat .

title: Stone hull
description: Stone hull Stone hull was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell strengthened a ship ' s hull with a magical aura , helping it withstand attacks from sea monsters , hidden reefs , or bombardment .
description_long: Stone hull Stone hull was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell strengthened a ship ' s hull with a magical aura , helping it withstand attacks from sea monsters , hidden reefs , or bombardment . This spell countered the effects of " warp wood " and " turn wood " . It did not offer additional protection from fire . Any ship under the influence of this spell had its movement speed cut in half . Components . This spell required a bit of pumice to cast .

title: Stone maiden
description: Stone maiden Stone maidens were beautiful damsels who dwelt in standing stones , rock formations , and secluded cavern walls in Zakhara . Description . These women appeared to be elven or human and wore simple , loose - fitting clothing .
description_long: Stone maiden Stone maidens were beautiful damsels who dwelt in standing stones , rock formations , and secluded cavern walls in Zakhara . Description . These women appeared to be elven or human and wore simple , loose - fitting clothing . The kind of stone these creatures lived in was reflected in the coloring of their clothing . Combat . Stone maidens were shy creatures , and they fled from most confrontational situations . They would attack if angered or provoked , using weapons or magic . Their special powers over stone provided interesting ways of trapping or attacking hostiles . Stone maidens could cast " animate rock " , " meld into stone " , " spike stones " , " stone shape " , " stone tell " , and " suggestion " . Stone maidens preferred attacking with magic while they remained safely enclosed within stone . All stone maidens were immune to earth - affecting magic . Habitat / Society . Stone maidens were mystically bonded with the rock where they lived , never straying more than a quarter mile ( 0 . 4 km ) from the rock . If removed from this area by force , a stone maiden suffered physical pain until they died or were returned .

title: Stone of Tymora
description: Stone of Tymora The Stone of Tymora was an artifact sacred to the goddess of good fortune , Tymora . The stone bound itself to the soul of a creature of its own choosing , usually someone who was already naturally lucky . When the stone was in close proximity to the one it had chosen , that mortal could perform feats of extraordinary luck , such as taking a leap off of a tall building in a city , only to hit every piece of laundry out to dry on the way down , and then conveniently to land on something reasonably soft , thereby turning a certainly lethal fall into a mildly painful bump .
description_long: Stone of Tymora The Stone of Tymora was an artifact sacred to the goddess of good fortune , Tymora . The stone bound itself to the soul of a creature of its own choosing , usually someone who was already naturally lucky . When the stone was in close proximity to the one it had chosen , that mortal could perform feats of extraordinary luck , such as taking a leap off of a tall building in a city , only to hit every piece of laundry out to dry on the way down , and then conveniently to land on something reasonably soft , thereby turning a certainly lethal fall into a mildly painful bump . Unfortunately , the nature of luck was that where there was good luck , there must also be bad , so when it altered the luck of its wielder , somewhere another soul would experience an equal amount of bad luck .

title: Stone of Tymora ( omnibus )
description: Stone of Tymora ( omnibus ) Stone of Tymora was the published omnibus of the Stone of Tymora trilogy by Geno Salvatore and R . A . Salvatore .
description_long: Stone of Tymora ( omnibus ) Stone of Tymora was the published omnibus of the Stone of Tymora trilogy by Geno Salvatore and R . A . Salvatore . It combined " The Stowaway " , " The Shadowmask " , and " The Sentinels " into one book .

title: Stone of Tymora trilogy
description: Stone of Tymora trilogy The Stone of Tymora trilogy is a trilogy of novels by R . A . Salvatore and his son Geno Salvatore intended for younger readers and published by Mirrorstone .
description_long: Stone of Tymora trilogy The Stone of Tymora trilogy is a trilogy of novels by R . A . Salvatore and his son Geno Salvatore intended for younger readers and published by Mirrorstone . The series follows a character named Maimun instead of Drizzt Do ' Urden ( who appears throughout the series ) . Omnibus . The trilogy is also available as the " Stone of Tymora " omnibus , released by Wizards of the Coast in 2012 .

title: Stone shape
description: Stone shape Stone shape was a transmutation spell or alteration spell that reshaped stone objects . Effects . Fine detail was not possible , but natural or worked stone could be manipulated by means of this spell to form most any shape the caster desired — an arch , a statue , a door , or a wall with a hole in it , for example .
description_long: Stone shape Stone shape was a transmutation spell or alteration spell that reshaped stone objects . Effects . Fine detail was not possible , but natural or worked stone could be manipulated by means of this spell to form most any shape the caster desired — an arch , a statue , a door , or a wall with a hole in it , for example . If small moving parts were required , there was a chance the mechanism just wouldn ' t function . Components . Verbal and somatic components were necessary , plus arcane casters required a lump of clay that had to be crudely molded into the desired shape and then brought into contact with the stone to be reshaped . Some druids also required mistletoe .

title: Stone sphere
description: Stone sphere Stone sphere is an evocation spell that conjures a spherical stone that can crush enemies . Effect . You create a smoothly polished , 5 - foot - diameter sphere of stone that moves under your control at a speed of 30 feet .
description_long: Stone sphere Stone sphere is an evocation spell that conjures a spherical stone that can crush enemies . Effect . You create a smoothly polished , 5 - foot - diameter sphere of stone that moves under your control at a speed of 30 feet . The stone sphere can be destroyed with weapons or spells , but this can take a while . On the round in which you cast the spell , the stone sphere appears at the spot you designate within the spell ’ s range , and you may direct its movement as a free action . On subsequent rounds , you must actively direct the stone sphere in order to move it ; otherwise , it remains motionless . Directing the movement of the stone sphere in the rounds after its initial appearance requires a move action . If you move the stone sphere into an enemy creature ' s square , it deals damage to every creature in that square based on their size . The sphere cannot roll into any square occupied by a Gargantuan or Colossal creature . The sphere must stop moving after it rolls over one occupied square , finishing its move in an adjacent square .

title: Stone spiders
description: Stone spiders Stone spiders was a transmutation spell unique to cleric s who commanded the Spider domain . It turned pebbles into enormous spider s , or gave insectoid vermin carapaces of stone . Effect .
description_long: Stone spiders Stone spiders was a transmutation spell unique to cleric s who commanded the Spider domain . It turned pebbles into enormous spider s , or gave insectoid vermin carapaces of stone . Effect . When cast , " stone spiders " turned up to three pebbles into stone construct s that took the form of monstrous spider s . These constructs could be of any size chosen by the spellcaster , provided they were all of the same size . The constructs were just like natural monstrous spiders , but had enhanced natural armor and were more resistant to damage . They even had a spider ' s strength - draining poison bite . The stone spiders attacked enemies of the caster as well as they could , unless given other orders while the caster was in earshot . An alternative use of the " stone spiders " spell was to grant up to three insectoid vermin of any size or type the effects of a " stoneskin " spell . Components . This spell required a cleric to use a divine focus .

title: Stone sword
description: Stone sword The stone sword was a unique weapon that could be found within the Rainbow Monastery in the Hordelands . History . The stone sword was ancient , forged long ago during a period of conflict in Solon ' s history .
description_long: Stone sword The stone sword was a unique weapon that could be found within the Rainbow Monastery in the Hordelands . History . The stone sword was ancient , forged long ago during a period of conflict in Solon ' s history . Description . This sword looked as if it were made entirely out of stone . However , it was much sharper that most steel swords . Powers . When wielded , the stone sword behaved like many other magical swords , making it much easier for the wielder to hit their opponent . However , if a single word of anger was uttered by the wielder while the stone sword was in their possession , the sword would instantly spring into their hand and they would be magically compelled to battle the source of their anger to the death . Once the first word of anger was invoked , the sword became a cursed weapon , making it more difficult to strike targets . The cursed stone sword would always leap into the wielder ' s hand during combat , disallowing the use of any other weapons . The only way to get rid of the stone sword once an angry word was spoken was through a " remove curse " spell or a " wish " .

title: Stone tell
description: Stone tell Stone tell was a divination spell that allowed the caster to speak with stones . Effects . This spell operated on any type of stone or rock , natural or worked .
description_long: Stone tell Stone tell was a divination spell that allowed the caster to speak with stones . Effects . This spell operated on any type of stone or rock , natural or worked . Early versions of this spell required the caster to touch the stones to be questioned , while later versions of this spell worked on the caster , allowing conversation with any stone addressed . In either case , the stones were able to answer questions about who or what touched them in the past , and what the stone might be concealing . However , the stones had particularly limited knowledge and understanding . For example , a rock might have revealed that a snake was hiding beneath it , but could not tell if it was a poisonous snake . Components . Old versions of the spell required verbal , somatic and material components , including a drop of mercury and a pinch of clay . Newer versions of the spell worked with the caster ' s holy symbol or divine focus as the material component .

title: Stone walk
description: Stone walk Stone walk is a transmutation spell unique to Banite cleric s . It creates what is effectively a portal between one stone area and another . Effect .
description_long: Stone walk Stone walk is a transmutation spell unique to Banite cleric s . It creates what is effectively a portal between one stone area and another . Effect . You magically link one location to another so that you or another may speak a command word at one end and be teleported to the other end . Before you cast the spell you must prepare the ends of the link , both of which must be areas of stone 5 feet square . This preparation takes 1 hour , and functions for repeated castings of the spell as long as the stones are not damaged . When the spell is cast , the stones become attuned to a command word you designate . Any creature that speaks the command word while standing upon one of the stones is teleported without error to the other end instantaneously . The stones function once for every four caster levels , and can carry 50 pounds per caster level each time . Creatures that exceed the weight limitation are not transported and count as one of the uses of the spell . Material Component . The preparation of each of the ends of the link requires a paste made from rubies and amber worth 2 , 500 gp . Casting the spell requires a 2 , 500 gp diamond .

title: Stonecliff
description: Stonecliff The Stonecliff was a perilous , rocky , craggy limestone escarpment that formed a natural wall along the north side of The High Road . The Eveningstar Gorge or Starwater Gorge along the Starwater River was the only route that mount s and livestock couldn take up or down the Stonecliff . Rumors .
description_long: Stonecliff The Stonecliff was a perilous , rocky , craggy limestone escarpment that formed a natural wall along the north side of The High Road . The Eveningstar Gorge or Starwater Gorge along the Starwater River was the only route that mount s and livestock couldn take up or down the Stonecliff . Rumors . It is said that once many mage s dwelt in caves in or north of the Stonecliff .

title: Stonefire
description: Stonefire Stonefire was a liquid material that could burn nearly any material , including stone . Stonefire bombs , called firepots , could be lobbed at structures and enemies to cause great damage . History .
description_long: Stonefire Stonefire was a liquid material that could burn nearly any material , including stone . Stonefire bombs , called firepots , could be lobbed at structures and enemies to cause great damage . History . Stonefire was used extensively in the drow cities of Menzoberranzan and Ched Nasad during the Silence of Lolth ( 1372 – 1373 DR ) . Drow rebels and slaves led by Syrzan used it during the uprising in Menzoberranzan . Clan Xornbane used them on the attack on House Melarn and later upon Ched Nasad itself , causing the complete destruction of the city when the stonefire brought down the cities calcified web layers , creating a cascading effect as the city ' s structures plummeted to the bottom of the chasm . The duergar army of Gracklstugh also used firepots during the Siege of Menzoberranzan , damaging parts of Tier Breche . It was revealed that the Jaezred Chaulssin had secretly been providing the firepots in order to weaken drow society .

title: Stonekiller
description: Stonekiller Stonekiller was a dwarf adventurer in Maztica . History . Stonekiller was going about his business when he was snatched by a cadre of riders and dragged back to Ulatos .
description_long: Stonekiller Stonekiller was a dwarf adventurer in Maztica . History . Stonekiller was going about his business when he was snatched by a cadre of riders and dragged back to Ulatos . There he met newcomers from Faerûn . When he was finally put back out on the street , he was full of curiosity about these strangers . He wanted answers to all his questions and believed that he could find it in Nexal . Personality . Stonekiller was fascinated by the Amn ians , whom he believed were crazier than Nexalan s , for their love of gold and their blinding curiosity . He also did not understood why the newcomers knew about the ancient dwarf gods and why the newcomers knew about the Viperhands monsters . Appendix . Behind the Scenes . Stonekiller is a pre - generated Maztican PC for use in adventures in Maztica .

title: Stonelands
description: Stonelands The Stonelands was a rocky and hilly region of terrain north of the Storm Horns mountain range , to the north of Cormyr . Politics . Although Cormyr claimed this land as part of its territory , it could not control it beyond where its soldiers marched .
description_long: Stonelands The Stonelands was a rocky and hilly region of terrain north of the Storm Horns mountain range , to the north of Cormyr . Politics . Although Cormyr claimed this land as part of its territory , it could not control it beyond where its soldiers marched . It was an inhospitable place for civilized humanoid s and was home to orc s , goblinoid s , and other creatures . Cormyr ' s monarchs long offered generous rewards for those who could establish and maintain settlements in the region . Geography . It was a rocky land of many valleys and hills , but it had a harsh beauty . Startop Crag was a peak in the Stonelands . High meadows ran north of it . History . Many legends told that the Stonelands were created circa −200 DR when Asram and Anauria attacked a magical realm that existed above the clouds of the region in order to escape the encroachment of the ever - expanding Anauroch desert on their kingdoms . The castles built above the clouds crashed down to the earth from the sky , creating the Stonelands .

title: Stoneplague
description: Stoneplague The Stoneplague was a disease that began afflicting dwarves in the East Rift region of Faerûn in 1480 DR . History . At first , it was feared the disease was spread person - to - person .
description_long: Stoneplague The Stoneplague was a disease that began afflicting dwarves in the East Rift region of Faerûn in 1480 DR . History . At first , it was feared the disease was spread person - to - person . However , the plague was actually spread by handling cursed gold . The duergar of Drik Hargunen used powerful earth magic to inscribe a rune inside a giant geode near their city . The rune was connected to Moradin ' s Vein , Moradin ' s tangible link to Toril . The intent was to poison Moradin himself and cause the death of the god . Several unscrupulous dwarves stole a powerful rune from Drik Hargunen that would teleport the user to the River of Gold and mined cursed gold from the river . The tainted gold found its way into the economy of the East Rift region and soon many dwarves were infected . Dwarven clerics were powerless to stop the spread of the plague and the cleric s of the Temple of the Lady of Mercy in Hammergate may have even spread the plague further through their practice of accepting offerings of gold in their ritual cleansing pool . The plague was ended when the dwarven ally Torrin Ironstar used a Duergar rune to teleport to Drik Hargunen .

title: Stoner ' s Needle
description: Stoner ' s Needle Stoner ' s Needle , also called Needle Rock , was a rocky spire in the Sword Coast lands . History . The extraplanar monster Imgig Zu placed a Lockstone with a frozen greater basilisk as guardian on the summit of Stoner ' s Needle .
description_long: Stoner ' s Needle Stoner ' s Needle , also called Needle Rock , was a rocky spire in the Sword Coast lands . History . The extraplanar monster Imgig Zu placed a Lockstone with a frozen greater basilisk as guardian on the summit of Stoner ' s Needle . This Lockstone would restore Jogaoh , who had escaped Imgig Zu ' s captivity , to his original form , but Jogaoh feared the basilisk too much to make the climb up and take the Lockstone . Instead , Jogaoh made his home close to the spire , and made a name for himself as a smith who could work magic . In the Year of the Prince , 1357 DR , Vajra Valmeyjar , Cybriana , Timoth Eyesbright , Onyx the Invincible , and Priam Agrivar sought out the famed dwarf smith Jogaoh for his services . Jogaoh agreed to help , provided the companions retrieved the Lockstone from atop Stoner ' s Needle . Jogaoh accompanied the heroes to the stony spire . They camped for the night at the base of the Needle , but close to dawn they were attack by ghoul warriors that clawed their way out of the earth . After defeating the undead , Vajra , Priam , and Jogaoh ascended the rocky tower , with Vajra carrying Jogaoh on her back and pulling up the weakened Priam .

title: Stoneskin
description: Stoneskin Stoneskin was an abjuration spell that turned a subject ' s skin stony in order to block blows , cuts , stabs , and slashes . Effects . The target creature felt a brief tingling sensation before their skin , clothes , and hair took on a gray , stone - like appearance .
description_long: Stoneskin Stoneskin was an abjuration spell that turned a subject ' s skin stony in order to block blows , cuts , stabs , and slashes . Effects . The target creature felt a brief tingling sensation before their skin , clothes , and hair took on a gray , stone - like appearance . A creature warded by " stoneskin " was able to resist much of the damage caused by bludgeoning , cutting , stabbing , and slashing attacks . Only adamantine weapons , " + 5 " weapons , and magical assaults could overcome it . Once the spell had blocked a certain amount of damage according to the caster ' s level of power , it was discharged . Components . In addition to the usual verbal and somatic components , casting " stoneskin " required a dust of granite and diamond ( worth at least 250 gp ) to be sprinkled over the skin of the being to be warded . History . " Stoneskin " was published in " Volo ' s Guide to All Things Magical " and became generally known to the magical community . It was a commonly used spell in the mid – 14th century DR . In Waterdeep in the Year of the Prince , 1357 DR , Kyriani cast " stoneskin " on Onyx the Invincible to protect him from the raking talons of the marauding Aviss .

title: Stonesmith Hammerhand
description: Stonesmith Hammerhand Stonesmith Hammerhand was a dwarf noble and commander of the city guard of the city of Orvyltar in Ulgarth around 1367 DR . Stonesmith was one of the few dwarven nobles in the kingdom . Stonesmith commanded 500 men - at - arms and three cavalry troops , as well as the city ' s defenses .
description_long: Stonesmith Hammerhand Stonesmith Hammerhand was a dwarf noble and commander of the city guard of the city of Orvyltar in Ulgarth around 1367 DR . Stonesmith was one of the few dwarven nobles in the kingdom . Stonesmith commanded 500 men - at - arms and three cavalry troops , as well as the city ' s defenses . Stonesmith lovingly maintained the powerful ballistae mounted on the towers that overlooked Copper Bay . Appendix . Notes . Stonesmith might be a distant member of Clan Hammerhand , but " Hammerhand " is also a common nickname for dwarves according to " Dwarves Deep " . Stonesmith might have been intended to be the sixth baron of Ulgarth , as only five out of sixth were mentioned .

title: Stonesulder wine
description: Stonesulder wine Stonesulder wine took its name from the merchant Arlast Stonesulder who popularized its use . This wine was produced by crushing berries and vines found in the Abyss . It was yellow in color and had a sharp flavor .
description_long: Stonesulder wine Stonesulder wine took its name from the merchant Arlast Stonesulder who popularized its use . This wine was produced by crushing berries and vines found in the Abyss . It was yellow in color and had a sharp flavor . Stonesulder wine was often used in cooking because it could bind sauces and gravies to food .

title: Stool
description: Stool Stool was a myconid sprout living in the Underdark during the Rage of Demons . History . Stool lived in Neverlight Grove with all its people .
description_long: Stool Stool was a myconid sprout living in the Underdark during the Rage of Demons . History . Stool lived in Neverlight Grove with all its people . During the Rage of Demons , it was captured by Sarith Kzekarit , who took it to the drow outpost of Velkynvelve . Personality . Stool ' s main concern was to return to its fellows . If it grew attached to humanoid people , it acted like a curious and enthusiastic younger brother . At the hands of the drow , it felt lonely and frightened . Powers . Thank to its spores , it could communicate telepathically with other creatures and could also act as bridge between two creatures without a common language in order to communicate .

title: Storm ' s Front Tavern
description: Storm ' s Front Tavern The Storm ' s Front Tavern was a tavern in Waterdeep ' s Sea Ward . Structure . The tavern was decorated with a nautical theme so it looked like a faux Dock Ward tavern .
description_long: Storm ' s Front Tavern The Storm ' s Front Tavern was a tavern in Waterdeep ' s Sea Ward . Structure . The tavern was decorated with a nautical theme so it looked like a faux Dock Ward tavern . History . In 1480 DR , the Storm ' s Front Tavern was burned to the ground during a confrontation between the deva Jinnaoth Ir ' Gadohn and the dark angel Sathariel .

title: Storm Horns
description: Storm Horns The Storm Horns was the name given to the mountains that marked the western and northern frontier of Cormyr . They were wild and untamed , the cliffs and crags teeming with monsters . Geography .
description_long: Storm Horns The Storm Horns was the name given to the mountains that marked the western and northern frontier of Cormyr . They were wild and untamed , the cliffs and crags teeming with monsters . Geography . The mountains formed an unbroken line of jagged peaks , except for High Horn Pass and Gnoll Pass , the only easy routes , both of which were defended by Cormyr . History . These mountains were once home to several strongholds of an ancient goblin empire . The empire fell to dwarven attacks , long before humans appeared in Cormyr . In the 14th century DR , the tribes of the mountains occasionally launched raids , although some had learned to trade peacefully . When the extra - dimensional city of Grodd was drawn closer to the Prime Material Plane , gates started to open and close in these mountains . Notable locations . As of 1372 DR , there were two human settlements in the mountains : Eagle Peak and Skull Crag . These settlements were usually bounded behind log palisades to protect them from the dangers outside .
