description: Suld Suld was a member of the Cult of the Dragon . History . In the Year of the Prince , 1357 DR , Suld and Arkuel were servants of the Cult ' s archmage , Malark Himbruel , on a mission to capture Shandril Shessair inside the Twisted Tower of Ashaba .
description_long: Suld Suld was a member of the Cult of the Dragon . History . In the Year of the Prince , 1357 DR , Suld and Arkuel were servants of the Cult ' s archmage , Malark Himbruel , on a mission to capture Shandril Shessair inside the Twisted Tower of Ashaba .

title: Suldanessellar
description: Suldanessellar Suldanessellar was an elven city in the Forest of Tethir . It was ruled by Queen Ellesime and housed the Tree of Life . The city was a meeting place for elves and their tribes ; a location all elves of the forest called home at one time or another .
description_long: Suldanessellar Suldanessellar was an elven city in the Forest of Tethir . It was ruled by Queen Ellesime and housed the Tree of Life . The city was a meeting place for elves and their tribes ; a location all elves of the forest called home at one time or another . Nestled around and above the Swanmay ' s Glade , the settlement ' s lowest dwellings were 50 feet above the ground and the first bridges among the branches began another 50 feet above that . There were only three entrances to the settlement above from the forest floor and these tree - trunk secret doors were well hidden . Inhabitants . While elves regularly patrolled the areas surrounding Suldanessellar , they did not stop local animals , especially fey , from entering . Among the types of creatures that regularly wandered within the city ' s borders were dryad s , centaur s and satyr s .

title: Suldax Tampcoin
description: Suldax Tampcoin Suldax Tampcoin was a member of the Shadow Council of Shadow Thieves and the Shade of the Caravan Sect around 1370 DR . History . Suldax started his career in the Shadow Thieves as a thief and moneylender .
description_long: Suldax Tampcoin Suldax Tampcoin was a member of the Shadow Council of Shadow Thieves and the Shade of the Caravan Sect around 1370 DR . History . Suldax started his career in the Shadow Thieves as a thief and moneylender . Soon , he proved so talented that he was promoted to guildmaster of racketeers and then even guildmaster of con artists and tricksters ( nobody had ever before held two different guildmaster positions ) . At last , Suldax ascended to the Shadow Council . Abilities . Suldax had an uncanny knack for estimating weight and balance . He could estimate the weight of precious metals to within five percent of its actual value without any particular efforts . If the metal was pure , he could even determine how much it was worth .

title: Sulduskoon River
description: Sulduskoon River The Sulduskoon River was a major river in the kingdom of Tethyr . This spring - fed river flowed west from the highlands all the way into the ocean at the Bay of Bormul in Zazesspur . Etymology .
description_long: Sulduskoon River The Sulduskoon River was a major river in the kingdom of Tethyr . This spring - fed river flowed west from the highlands all the way into the ocean at the Bay of Bormul in Zazesspur . Etymology . The river received its name from the tribe of Suldusk elves living within the Forest of Tethir . History . Circa - 2600 DR , the last survivors of High Shanatar were slain by Calishite s on the shore of the Sulduskoon .

title: Sulesdeg
description: Sulesdeg Sulesdeg the Pole was a very tall guard working on the Sword Coast just before the Tyranny of Dragons . Personality . Sulesdeg did not talk much , but when he did , people listened .
description_long: Sulesdeg Sulesdeg the Pole was a very tall guard working on the Sword Coast just before the Tyranny of Dragons . Personality . Sulesdeg did not talk much , but when he did , people listened . History . A native of the Shaar , where in his native language his name meant " tall as a lodge pole " , he traveled to the Sword Coast and found work as a guard . At the start of the Tyranny of Dragons in 1489 DR he worked as a guard for a great caravan that , unknown to him , was full of agents of the Cult of the Dragon transporting treasures for the Hoard of the Dragon Queen .

title: Suliyar
description: Suliyar Suliyar was a rakshasa rajah in service of Set in Mulhorand in 1357 DR . Activities . Suliyar was a member of The Fangs of Set .
description_long: Suliyar Suliyar was a rakshasa rajah in service of Set in Mulhorand in 1357 DR . Activities . Suliyar was a member of The Fangs of Set . He was always accompanied by four rakshasa bodyguards , one that Hodkamset wanted use in his plot . He usually stalked the streets of Skuld in search of humans to kill . Suliyar posed as a mercenary History . Suliyar was exiled from his homeland east of Raurin , where he had ruled a great rakshasa tribe . He was found by Nekiset to recruited him to the service of Set . Personality . Suliyar was a proud and savage creature . He believed that helping Set would grant him the rule of a great empire . He enjoyed killing humans , especially initiates of Horus - Re . Relationship . Suliyar no cared much for his companions in the Fang of Set but sometimes found deviousness amusing .

title: Suljack
description: Suljack Suljack was the leader of Ship Suljack and one of the five High Captains of the city of Luskan . Along with the others he was an experienced adventurer and a former pirate . Suljack was killed by Athrogate in " The Pirate King " for siding with Deudermont over Kensidan ; it was not clear what happened to his territory .
description_long: Suljack Suljack was the leader of Ship Suljack and one of the five High Captains of the city of Luskan . Along with the others he was an experienced adventurer and a former pirate . Suljack was killed by Athrogate in " The Pirate King " for siding with Deudermont over Kensidan ; it was not clear what happened to his territory .

title: Sull ( the butcher )
description: Sull ( the butcher ) Sull is a semi - skilled fighter who works as a butcher in the South Ward of Waterdeep . After Icelin Tearn ' s great - uncle was killed by Cerest Elenithil ' s men , Sull agreed to take Icelin to Mistshore to hide from Cerest and the City Watch . He protected Icelin from Cerest and was seriously wounded in a battle with Cerest ' s henchmen .
description_long: Sull ( the butcher ) Sull is a semi - skilled fighter who works as a butcher in the South Ward of Waterdeep . After Icelin Tearn ' s great - uncle was killed by Cerest Elenithil ' s men , Sull agreed to take Icelin to Mistshore to hide from Cerest and the City Watch . He protected Icelin from Cerest and was seriously wounded in a battle with Cerest ' s henchmen . Later , Sull journeyed out of Waterdeep with Icelin and Ruen Morleth on a quest to find a cure for Icelin ' s spellscar . Equipment . Sull uses his butcher cleavers as his primary weapons . Appearance . Sull is a huge man with frizzy red hair and muttonchop sideburns .

title: Sultan ' s Own
description: Sultan ' s Own The Sultan ' s Own , or the Jackals , were located in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire . Organization . This light infantry unit was comprised of 4 , 000 salamander s .
description_long: Sultan ' s Own The Sultan ' s Own , or the Jackals , were located in the City of Brass on the Elemental Plane of Fire . Organization . This light infantry unit was comprised of 4 , 000 salamander s . Activities . These security troops were infamous for their sadistic nature . They were used when the Illuminated were not successfully able to quell a mob . Base of Operations . The City of Brass served as the base of the Sultan ' s Own .

title: Suluq
description: Suluq Suluq was an enslaved efreeti in Zakhara in 1367 DR . Activities . Suluq was trapped within a ring of genie summoning and did his master ' s bidding whenever he was called .
description_long: Suluq Suluq was an enslaved efreeti in Zakhara in 1367 DR . Activities . Suluq was trapped within a ring of genie summoning and did his master ' s bidding whenever he was called . Relationships . Contrary to most enslaved genie s , Suluq actually liked his master , Fasim Kaldur . Suluq and Fasim got along quite well since Fasim treated him fairly and frequently allowed him to exercise his thirst for committing violence .

title: Sumber Hills
description: Sumber Hills The Sumber Hills were a range of hills in the middle of the Dessarin Valley . The River Dessarin flowed through the hills , providing a source of water travel between Yartar and downstream communities such as Beliard , Bargewright Inn , and Womford . The Larch Path and the Dessarin Road provided passage through the hills .
description_long: Sumber Hills The Sumber Hills were a range of hills in the middle of the Dessarin Valley . The River Dessarin flowed through the hills , providing a source of water travel between Yartar and downstream communities such as Beliard , Bargewright Inn , and Womford . The Larch Path and the Dessarin Road provided passage through the hills . History . One of the first settlements in the Sumber Hills was the underground city of Tyar - Besil , a part of the shield dwarf kingdom of Besilmer . Tyar - Besil was abandoned and fell into ruin in −4190 DR , after the king of Besilmer died in battle . The Sumber Hills were left alone until the Knights of the Silver Horn started clearing the area of its native inhabitants in 893 DR . The knights attempted to set up fortresses in the hills but were stopped by Uruth Ukrypt . These events eventually played a part in the Orcfastings War , and the First and Second Trollwars . Around 1000 DR , settlements started springing up around the Sumber Hills , creating roads and trails that bisected the hills .

title: Sumcha
description: Sumcha Sumcha was a human thief who claimed to be a merchant prince when he moved to Velprintalar in Aglarond around 1358 DR . His real occupation was as a burglar in Sembia , but he was forced to flee to Aglarond after stealing goods belonging to Zhentil Keep . He adopted Velprintalar as his new home , building and living in Sumcha ' s Tower with his family and servants .
description_long: Sumcha Sumcha was a human thief who claimed to be a merchant prince when he moved to Velprintalar in Aglarond around 1358 DR . His real occupation was as a burglar in Sembia , but he was forced to flee to Aglarond after stealing goods belonging to Zhentil Keep . He adopted Velprintalar as his new home , building and living in Sumcha ' s Tower with his family and servants .

title: Sumcha ' s Tower
description: Sumcha ' s Tower Sumcha ' s Tower was a tower in Velprintalar , Aglarond . It was built around 1358 DR by Sumcha , who claimed to be a merchant prince who moved to the city from Sembia . He lived in the tower with his family and servants .
description_long: Sumcha ' s Tower Sumcha ' s Tower was a tower in Velprintalar , Aglarond . It was built around 1358 DR by Sumcha , who claimed to be a merchant prince who moved to the city from Sembia . He lived in the tower with his family and servants .

title: Sumi - ko
description: Sumi - ko Sumi - ko was the younger daughter of Funada Toyoo in Nakamaru around 1357 DR . History . Sumi - ko was promised in marriage by her father to the son of a daimyo of a far place but this son died and from then she was free from arranged marriage until her father not found an other good candidate .
description_long: Sumi - ko Sumi - ko was the younger daughter of Funada Toyoo in Nakamaru around 1357 DR . History . Sumi - ko was promised in marriage by her father to the son of a daimyo of a far place but this son died and from then she was free from arranged marriage until her father not found an other good candidate . At a a moon - viewing party Sumi - ko met the handsome Nagoya Kenko and fall in love for him . They started a illicit romance . However Funada Genzo discovered the matter and in order to protect his half - sister payed a visit to Kenko menacing him but this only made Kenko angry Personality . Sumi - ko was impetuous and foolishness like most girl , she was naive enough to believed the advances of any handsome man who might court her . Sumi - ko only fear was becoming an old maid . She fall in love with Kenko but in time she will understand that he not love her .

title: Sumitomo Toyo
description: Sumitomo Toyo Sumitomo Toyo was the heir and chef of Doi No Fugu in 1360 DR . History . Toyo was the younger son of Sumitomo Koji , master of the Doi No Fugu , and the second male .
description_long: Sumitomo Toyo Sumitomo Toyo was the heir and chef of Doi No Fugu in 1360 DR . History . Toyo was the younger son of Sumitomo Koji , master of the Doi No Fugu , and the second male . In his youth , he was very close to his older brother , Sumitomo Yoichi , who was always fascinated by stories of travelers , and his younger sister Sumitomo Skoshi . When as tradition dictated Yoichi was sent outside Maeshi Province for training as a chef , Toyo and Skoshi knew he would never come back . He didn ' t , and Toyo became the heir . With the turmoil in the province between the Michimori clan and the Korimori clan , he undertook his training at home . In 1359 arrived at the inn the ronin Haka Kinnori that after a talk with their father Sumitomo Koji started t live with them . Soon Toyo and Skoshi befriend Haka that also teach them karate

title: Sumitomo Yoichi
description: Sumitomo Yoichi Sumitomo Yoichi was the former heir of Doi No Fugu and a ninja in 1360 DR . History . Yoichi was the older son of Sumitomo Koji , master of the Doi No Fugu , destined to inherit the inn and the position of chef .
description_long: Sumitomo Yoichi Sumitomo Yoichi was the former heir of Doi No Fugu and a ninja in 1360 DR . History . Yoichi was the older son of Sumitomo Koji , master of the Doi No Fugu , destined to inherit the inn and the position of chef . However Yoichi always dreamed of adventures and samurai , fascinating by stories of travelers , that he told to younger Sumitomo Toyo and Sumitomo Skoshi . When his father decided as tradition dictated to send him outside Maeshi Province for training as a chef Yoichi disappeared . He somehow become a ninja in the Ono Kumi in north Kozakura under the new name of Ono Arieki . In 1360 his boss Ono Noburo told him of a special mission : went in Maeshi in the Doi No Fugu inn to recover the Seven Swords from an adventuring party . Noburo explained that for cover trails he must kill all people inside the inn . He planned a very meticulous plan , capturing the Sumitomos and with his ninja posing as them before the adventurers ' arrive . However the adventurers , also thank to Haka Kinnori , defeated the ninja Personality . Yoichi was resigned to the death of his family , now his family were the Ono ninja .

title: Summer Palace
description: Summer Palace The Summer Palace is the second home of Queen Amlaruil Moonflower of Evermeet and lies in the centre of the Lake of Dreams . The palace itself rivals the Moonstone Palace for beauty and is an enchanted structure of alabaster , marble , crystal and gems resting on four pyramids , 200 ' ( 60m ) above the lake . The queen uses this location to consider important issues with her Council of Matrons .
description_long: Summer Palace The Summer Palace is the second home of Queen Amlaruil Moonflower of Evermeet and lies in the centre of the Lake of Dreams . The palace itself rivals the Moonstone Palace for beauty and is an enchanted structure of alabaster , marble , crystal and gems resting on four pyramids , 200 ' ( 60m ) above the lake . The queen uses this location to consider important issues with her Council of Matrons .

title: Summer in the City
description: Summer in the City " Summer in the City " is the 33rd issue of the " Advanced Dungeons & Dragons " comics series set in the " Forgotten Realms " and published by . It was written by Dan Mishkin , drawn by Jan Duursema , and edited by Kim Yale . Appendix .
description_long: Summer in the City " Summer in the City " is the 33rd issue of the " Advanced Dungeons & Dragons " comics series set in the " Forgotten Realms " and published by . It was written by Dan Mishkin , drawn by Jan Duursema , and edited by Kim Yale . Appendix . Reprints . This issue was reprinted in the Dungeons & Dragons Classics , Vol . 4 trade paperback by in February 2013 .

title: Summer rhymer
description: Summer rhymer Summer rhymers are cunning bard s who seek to evoke the power of the Feywild and the Summer Queen ' s lively spirit . Summer rhymers claim a deep connection to the power of the mystical Plane of Faerie , seeking to earn the blessing of the Summer Fey , reflecting the power of the fey in their own training , be it through teleportation or the life - enhancing powers of the Feywild . Culture .
description_long: Summer rhymer Summer rhymers are cunning bard s who seek to evoke the power of the Feywild and the Summer Queen ' s lively spirit . Summer rhymers claim a deep connection to the power of the mystical Plane of Faerie , seeking to earn the blessing of the Summer Fey , reflecting the power of the fey in their own training , be it through teleportation or the life - enhancing powers of the Feywild . Culture . Tiandra the Summer Queen is among the most powerful archfey of the Feywild , full of lifegiving power and surrounded by unearthly beauty . A powerful arcane spellcaster , Tiandra ' s approval is sought by many and among the few who actually receive it are the summer rhymers . Not all summer rhymers begin their path with the Queen ' s blessing , but all seek it and likely obtain it before their training is done . Touched by the power of the fey , summer rhymers have a long tradition of service to the Summer Fey , using their musical talents as bards to spread the influence and power of the Feywild throughout the world . For their efforts , some summer rhymers actually obtain the favor of the Summer Queen , and with it other rewards .

title: Summon fire dragons
description: Summon fire dragons Summon fire dragons was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects .
description_long: Summon fire dragons Summon fire dragons was a spell used commonly in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects . The name of this spell was a little misleading considering that it did not summon any kind of creature . Instead it allowed the caster to create up to 10 fiery snake - like tongues of flame that were called " fire dragons " or " flame dragons " . Each " fire dragon " measured 6 ft . ( 1 . 8 m ) in diameter and moved according to the will of the caster so long as they concentrated . The " flame dragons " would dissipate if the caster was struck or their attention was diverted in another manner . Additionally , each " flame dragon " could stretch across 180 ft . ( 55 m ) of ground and reach 30 ft . ( 9 m ) into the air . " Fire dragons " could not strike against anything standing in water or anything situated higher than 30 ft . off of the ground . Components . In addition to verbal components , this spell required a strip of paper that was soaked in oil , coal , saltpeper , and sulfur to cast .

title: Summon monster
description: Summon monster Summon monster , or monster summoning , ( originally called Lucke ' s monster summons ) was a series of increasingly more powerful summoning spell s commonly in use by both arcane and divine spellcasters . Effects . A " summon monster " spell conjured one or more creatures from another plane and made them appear within close range of the caster .
description_long: Summon monster Summon monster , or monster summoning , ( originally called Lucke ' s monster summons ) was a series of increasingly more powerful summoning spell s commonly in use by both arcane and divine spellcasters . Effects . A " summon monster " spell conjured one or more creatures from another plane and made them appear within close range of the caster . These " monsters " were usually native magical beasts , outsider s , or elemental creature s . Whatever creature was summoned was magically compelled to fight for the caster to the best of its ability . A summoned being could not be truly destroyed ; instead , an attack that would otherwise destroy it instead sent it back to the plane from which it was summoned , where it reformed over the next twenty - four hours . It was impossible to summon a creature into an environment that could not support its life . Summoned beings lost any powers to themselves summon other entities or to use any sort of planar travel . Divine casters could only someone creatures whose alignments were not in conflict with either their own or their deities alignment .

History . This was the first " summon monster " spell developed by the Netherese arcanist Lucke . He completed it in −1994 DR .

description: Summon monster II Summon monster II , or monster summoning II , ( originally called Lucke ' s 2nd monster summons ) was one of the series of " summon monster " spells available to spellcasters . Effects . This spell functions just as all " summon monster " spells .

Effects . This spell functions just as all " summon monster " spells . Alternatively , it could summon one to three dog s , owl s , giant fire beetle s , porpoise s , badger s , or monkey s from the celestial planes or the same number of dire rat s , raven s , medium - sized monstrous centipede s , small monstrous scorpion s , hawk s , small monstrous spider s , octopus es , or small viper s from one of the fiendish planes — provided they were within 30 feet of each other . History .

description: Summon monster III Summon monster III , or monster summoning III , ( originally called Lucke ' s 3rd monster summons ) was one of the series of " summon monster " spells available to spellcasters . Effects . This spell functioned just as all " summon monster " spells .

Effects . This spell functioned just as all " summon monster " spells . Alternatively , it could summon one to three giant bee s , giant bombardier beetle s , riding dog s , or eagle s from the celestial planes or the same number of lemure s , squid s , wolves , large monstrous centipedes , medium - sized monstrous scorpion s , medium - sized shark s , medium - sized monstrous spider s , or medium - sized vipers from one of the fiendish planes . One to three kaorti from the Far Realm could also be summoned .

title: Summon sha ' ir
description: Summon sha ' ir Summon sha ' ir was a conjuration spell used by genie wizard s to compel service from an abusive sha ' ir . This spell was useless when cast upon any target who was not a sha ' ir . Typically genies would only use this spell against sha ' irs who abused their gen , created too many magical items , bound an excessive number of genies within genie prison s , or if the sha ' ir displayed similar malcontent toward geniekind .
description_long: Summon sha ' ir Summon sha ' ir was a conjuration spell used by genie wizard s to compel service from an abusive sha ' ir . This spell was useless when cast upon any target who was not a sha ' ir . Typically genies would only use this spell against sha ' irs who abused their gen , created too many magical items , bound an excessive number of genies within genie prison s , or if the sha ' ir displayed similar malcontent toward geniekind . Genies could not use this spell against a sha ' ir simply because they wanted to . The spell would not take effect unless several warning signs were triggered by the sha ' ir ' s behavior . Effects . For this spell to work , the genie caster needed to possess one of the sha ' ir ' s personal items . This item was usually acquired by intimidating the sha ' ir ' s gen while it was traveling on the native elemental plane of the genie caster while fetching a spell for its master . A gen who agreed to help the genie acquire the item delivered on the promise the next time the sha ' ir sent it off in search of a spell . Any personal belonging of the sha ' ir would satisfy the requirements of the spell .

title: Summon swarm
description: Summon swarm Summon swarm is a conjuration spell that conjures a swarm of small crawling or flying creatures . It requires as a material component a square of red cloth . Effect .
description_long: Summon swarm Summon swarm is a conjuration spell that conjures a swarm of small crawling or flying creatures . It requires as a material component a square of red cloth . Effect . When cast , " summon swarm " causes a swarm of little creatures to carpet an area , viciously attacking all other creatures there . Spellcasting or concentrating on spells within the swarm is impossible . The caster has no choice as to what type of creature he summons ; typical swarms include rat s , bat s , poisonous spider s , centipedes , and flying beetles . The swarm cannot be fought effectively with weapons , but fire and damaging area effects can force it to disperse . Certain area or effect spells , such as " gust of wind " and " stinking cloud " , disperse a swarm immediately if appropriate to the swarm summoned . ( For example , only fliers are affected by a " gust of wind " . ) The swarm is stationary once summoned , not leaving the original area . A druid caster , however , can direct the swarm to move up to thirty feet every few seconds ( or ninety feet if she has summoned bats or beetles ) .

title: Summon undead
description: Summon undead Summon undead was a series of increasingly more powerful , evil summoning spell s commonly in use by sorcerer s and wizard s of the Realms . Effects . Like other summoning spells , a " summon undead " spell conjured one or more undead creatures from another place and made them appear within close range of the caster .
description_long: Summon undead Summon undead was a series of increasingly more powerful , evil summoning spell s commonly in use by sorcerer s and wizard s of the Realms . Effects . Like other summoning spells , a " summon undead " spell conjured one or more undead creatures from another place and made them appear within close range of the caster . The summoned creature appeared in a burst of fog and smoke , in which some claimed they could see the residual image of screaming faces . An undead being was magically compelled to fight for the caster . A summoned undead could not be truly destroyed ; instead , an attack that would otherwise destroy it instead sent it back to the place from which it was summoned where it reformed over the next day . Summoned undead beings would serve the caster until the duration of the spell ended , which was anywhere from mere seconds to several minutes , depending on the power level of the caster . Components . Like other arcane summoning spells , " summon undead " spells required verbal and somatic component s and a tiny bag and an unlit candle as magical foci . They uniquely required a third magical focus , the carved bone from any humanoid creature .

title: Summon undead I
description: Summon undead I Summon undead I was the weakest of the series of " summon undead " spells available to arcane casters in the Realms . This spell could summon a medium - sized skeleton or small zombie . Usually , the skeleton of a human warrior or a kobold zombie were chosen .

title: Summon wind dragons
description: Summon wind dragons Summon wind dragons was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created 1 - 10 small wind vortices called wind dragons .
description_long: Summon wind dragons Summon wind dragons was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created 1 - 10 small wind vortices called wind dragons . These wind dragons had a 6 foot ( 1 . 8 m ) diameter and were mentally controlled by the caster . They would disappear if the caster was struck or otherwise distracted from concentrating . The caster could direct no more than two wind dragons at any one target , but could attack multiple targets at the same time . Wind dragons could not lift targets , but caused buffeting damage and made spellcasting impossible . This spell could only be cast if air was present . It could not be cast underwater . Components . This spell required a cup to cast .

These spells could bring aid in the form of creatures from distant places and planes , or transport the caster to safety . Spells in normal text were listed in the " Tome of Magic 2nd edition " .

title: Sun ' s Eye
description: Sun ' s Eye The Sun ' s Eye was the northern most province of the Yikarian Empire in 1367 DR . Geography . This province was unique among others of the Empire in that most of its terrain was not dominated by the sprawling World Pillar Mountains .
description_long: Sun ' s Eye The Sun ' s Eye was the northern most province of the Yikarian Empire in 1367 DR . Geography . This province was unique among others of the Empire in that most of its terrain was not dominated by the sprawling World Pillar Mountains . The Sun ' s Eye covered a wide area of land leading from the mountains in the east to the coast of the Great Sea in the west while also bordering much of Konigheim to the north . Inhabitants . The albino Coral Princess was the governor of the Sun ' s Eye province . Activities . Because of its position along the Great Sea and Konigheim , the Sun ' s Eye province offered distinct strategical advantages over the other provinces of the Yikarian Empire . Mainly , it connected the yak - folk with the outside world , exposing them to sailors from the sea and barbarians from the north , allowing access to vital trade items as well as slaves . Goods smuggled into the Empire often entered through the Sun ' s Eye province . The navy of the Yikarian Empire was based in Lipo .

title: Sun Canyon
description: Sun Canyon Sun Canyon is a canyon in the Pasocada Basin that runs southwest from the Dunobo Springs into the Pasocada River . The canyon is filled and carved out by the Danozi Wash , which is the floodwater coming from the mountains every spring . It is the spiritual centrepoint of the Azuposi civilization and the City of Gold , Michaca , is located here .

title: Sun Ya Sen
description: Sun Ya Sen Sun Ya Sen was the Chancellor of Shou Lung in 1358 DR . History . Sun Ya Sen was appointed Chancellor in 1348 DR and from then on she always commanded respect from all the bureaucracy .
description_long: Sun Ya Sen Sun Ya Sen was the Chancellor of Shou Lung in 1358 DR . History . Sun Ya Sen was appointed Chancellor in 1348 DR and from then on she always commanded respect from all the bureaucracy . Activities . The Chancellor decided which reports and petitions from the minister and other officials were worthy of attention by the Emperor . The power to decide who met Kai Tsao Shou Chin made Sun Ya Sen one of the most powerful individuals of the Empire but she was fundamentally a honest woman , despite her blunt manner . Her main concern was the Emperor ' s trust in the Society of the Kuo - Tan . Sun Ya Sen mistrusted the Kuo - Tan and feared that one day they would betray the Son of Heaven and in order to prevent this she would do anything . Sun Ya Sen regularly spied upon the Kuo - Tan .

title: Sun domain
description: Sun domain The Sun domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters sun spell powers . Once per day , the user can perform a " greater turning " against undead in place of a normal turn / rebuke , which destroys undead that it would normally have turned / rebuked . Deities with the Sun domain .
description_long: Sun domain The Sun domain is a deity domain that grants divine spellcasters sun spell powers . title: Sun elf
description: Sun elf The sun elves , also sometimes known as gold elves , sometimes as high elves due to their stereotypically elitist ways , and Ar - tel - quessir in their own language are a subrace of eladrin historically rare in Faerûn due to the Retreat , in which the majority abandoned the continent for Evermeet , although during the Era of Upheaval they began return to the mainland . Haughty and arrogant , sun elves typically feel themselves superior to most other races , including other Tel - quessir . Ecology .
description_long: Sun elf The sun elves , also sometimes known as gold elves , sometimes as high elves due to their stereotypically elitist ways , and Ar - tel - quessir in their own language are a subrace of eladrin historically rare in Faerûn due to the Retreat , in which the majority abandoned the continent for Evermeet , although during the Era of Upheaval they began return to the mainland . Haughty and arrogant , sun elves typically feel themselves superior to most other races , including other Tel - quessir . Ecology . Physical characteristics . Like all of the Tel - quessir , the sun elves are close to the height of human s , but with notable differences . Sun elves have bronze - colored skin and hair most often of copper , golden blond , and black , with red more uncommon but not unheard of . Sun elves , like other eladrin , typically have green eyes , though golden ones are also common , often with a liquid appearance , and silver , black , hazel , or copper hues have also been heard of . Like their moon elven brethren , male sun elves are typically taller and heavier than females , sometimes by as much as five inches or twenty pounds .

title: Sun scepter
description: Sun scepter Sun scepter was a conjuration spell that created a magical scepter of light . Effects . When cast , this spell created a scepter made from light that had a mace - like shape .
description_long: Sun scepter Sun scepter was a conjuration spell that created a magical scepter of light . Effects . When cast , this spell created a scepter made from light that had a mace - like shape . Usable as a weapon only by the caster , it struck with the powers of axiomatic , disruption , and flaming burst weapons .

title: Sun sphere
description: Sun sphere The Sun sphere was a group of spells granted to druid s . These spells focus light and heat for comfort or for destruction . Spells in normal text were listed in the Tome of Magic 2nd edition .
