description: Tayanulchi The Tayanulchi , also spelled Tayanuchi , were a tribe of human s living in the Ama Basin in the Northern Wastes of Kara - Tur . They split from the Issacortae and disappeared into the Land of the Snow Demons centuries before the 14th century DR . Society .
description_long: Tayanulchi The Tayanulchi , also spelled Tayanuchi , were a tribe of human s living in the Ama Basin in the Northern Wastes of Kara - Tur . They split from the Issacortae and disappeared into the Land of the Snow Demons centuries before the 14th century DR . Society . Having broken off from the Issacortae , the Tayanulchi likely spoke the Issacortae language .

title: Tayrom Onetry
description: Tayrom Onetry Tayrom Onetry was a human man who lived in the town of Elmwood in the Moonsea in the mid – 14th century . He was proprietor of the Grange trading emporium . History .
description_long: Tayrom Onetry Tayrom Onetry was a human man who lived in the town of Elmwood in the Moonsea in the mid – 14th century . He was proprietor of the Grange trading emporium . History . Tayrom was born " circa " 1334 DR . He lived in Elmwood . At age 22 , around 1356 DR , Tayrom took up as an adventurer and joined a band of explorers travelling to Ravens Bluff in the Vast . But , on the way , they were attacked by kobold s , who beat them all up and stole all their valuables . Tayrom , however , had fled screaming at the first sight of them , and ran all the back to Elmwood . This was his " one try " at the adventurer ' s life , hence his nickname . Tayrom later became a merchant , managing the Grange trading emporium in Elmwood . He still managed the store by 1367 DR . Personality . In later years , Tayrom " Onetry " enjoyed telling the tale of his brief adventuring career , but claimed he killed several kobolds before he fled . The kobolds seemed to grow in size with every telling . Activities . Tayrom managed the Grange , a trading emporium in Elmwood . It stocked almost every mundane item one could need , bar arms and armor .

title: Tazlan Rilzeer
description: Tazlan Rilzeer Tazlan Rilzeer was a sea - captain in Waterdeep sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . Activities . Zaldar was the captain of the " Coin Toss " , of propriety of the noble Arilosa Adarbrent , a financier of the Order of the Gauntlet .
description_long: Tazlan Rilzeer Tazlan Rilzeer was a sea - captain in Waterdeep sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . Activities . Zaldar was the captain of the " Coin Toss " , of propriety of the noble Arilosa Adarbrent , a financier of the Order of the Gauntlet . He had a priest of Helm as ship ' s medic . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR eventually Tazlan was hired by the Order of the Gauntlet to travel in search of the " Morkoth

title: Tazmikella
description: Tazmikella Tazmikella was a copper dragon who lived in the Bloodstone Lands . Appearance . Her human form was that of a rather ordinary looking , middle - aged woman with once - strawberry - blond , mostly soft - gray hair , dressed in simple clothes .
description_long: Tazmikella Tazmikella was a copper dragon who lived in the Bloodstone Lands . Appearance . Her human form was that of a rather ordinary looking , middle - aged woman with once - strawberry - blond , mostly soft - gray hair , dressed in simple clothes . She was also known to take the form of a young blond female elf , but still kept her human name . She had wide shoulders and a smallish head . Personality . Tazmikella was considered friendly by her customers and neighboring merchants . She hated wearing clothes and couldn ' t understand the need of humans to hide their natural forms . To her that showed a level of shame and modesty reflective of a race that couldn ' t elevate itself above its apparent limitations . History . By the 14th century DR , Tazmikella was centuries old . She had a sister , Ilnezhara , with whom she crawled from her egg in the great deserts of Calimshan . She and her sister were once approached by Zhengyi , the Witch - King , with the offer of immortality in lichdom if they served beside his conquering armies . The dragon sisters declined that offer .

title: Tazok
description: Tazok Tazok was a half - ogre bandit leader and an important follower of Sarevok . History . Tazok was already the leader of a band of brigands .
description_long: Tazok Tazok was a half - ogre bandit leader and an important follower of Sarevok . History . Tazok was already the leader of a band of brigands . He and his band captured and tortured Kivan and Deheriana , and only the former made it out alive , swearing revenge . Years later , during the iron crisis , Tazok was the leader of the bandit groups that had been organized to steal what iron they could find on travelers . He was a major agent in Iron Throne ' s plans to gain a monopoly on iron and political power during the crisis , but was also in on Sarevok ' s more secret plans to attain godhood . He was also Mulahey ' s superior , and thus involved in the sabotage of the Nashkel mine .

title: Tazu - ei
description: Tazu - ei Tazu - ei was a barbarian in Machukara around 1357 DR . History . Tazu - ei born from a noble family in Nakamaru on isle of Tsukishima .
description_long: Tazu - ei Tazu - ei was a barbarian in Machukara around 1357 DR . History . Tazu - ei born from a noble family in Nakamaru on isle of Tsukishima . However disgusted by the plots of his relatives over supremacy he decided to renounced his status and went to Machukara . All considered him dead . However Tazu - ei prospered in the savage island , he had also befriended a race of intelligent orange gorillas who will make him their king if he teaches them to build and use ships . Personality . Tazu - ei was a hot - tempered and fearless individual . He now was considering the gorillas ' offer , intrigued to led a band of pirate gorilla .

title: Tchandrae Euinwood
description: Tchandrae Euinwood Tchandrae Euinwood was a girl with strange powers in Kheldell in 1370 DR . She possessed unusual powers : simply by touching an item , Tchandarae would know things about it , similarly to the " legend lore " spell . She was examined by Elminster Aumar in person , who said her powers had no clear origin but he was sure she was blessed by Mystra .
description_long: Tchandrae Euinwood Tchandrae Euinwood was a girl with strange powers in Kheldell in 1370 DR . She possessed unusual powers : simply by touching an item , Tchandarae would know things about it , similarly to the " legend lore " spell . She was examined by Elminster Aumar in person , who said her powers had no clear origin but he was sure she was blessed by Mystra .

title: Tchazar
description: Tchazar Tchazar was the " Realms " name for which occurred in long , prism - shaped crystals that were straw - yellow and very fragile . Description . A of great skill was required to cut gems from this semi - precious stone .
description_long: Tchazar Tchazar was the " Realms " name for which occurred in long , prism - shaped crystals that were straw - yellow and very fragile . Description . A of great skill was required to cut gems from this semi - precious stone . tchazar was much less valuable ( treated as an ornamental stone ) . A typical specimen had a base value of 50 gp . Powers . This gemstone was important to those who feared magical scrying because tchazar interfered with scrying devices and spells , rendering anything within 2 ft ( 60 cm ) of a tchazar stone blurry and indistinguishable . The effect was the same regardless of how the tchazar was cut ( cabochon , facted , or natural crystal ) so it was used to adorn many personal items and locations where privacy was of utmost importance . This magical smoke screen effect was lost if the tchazar stone was shattered .

title: Tchazzar
description: Tchazzar Tchazzar ( pronounced cha - zar ) was a red dragon mythic sovereign who posed as a human warlord and eventually became a god for a time . Appearance . Despite his age , Tchazzar had the vigor of a red dragon in its prime .
description_long: Tchazzar Tchazzar ( pronounced cha - zar ) was a red dragon mythic sovereign who posed as a human warlord and eventually became a god for a time . Appearance . Despite his age , Tchazzar had the vigor of a red dragon in its prime . His scales were as bright as a wyrmling ' s except along his wings where they were black as obsidian . His eyes and horns were completely black and the horns themselves were sharp and serrated . In human form Tchazzar was a large , handsome man with an angular face and slightly pointed ears . He had yellow eyes and flawless white teeth . Personality . Tchazzar was a force of pure chaos and evil . He was convinced of his superiority over all living things , even more so than a typical red dragon . He cared not for his subjects or allies except as expendable resources , but at the same time made efforts to ensure their loyalty . After his return to Chessenta in 1479 DR Tchazzar behaved extremely erratically . It ' s unknown whether his madness was caused by his imprisonment in the Shadowfell or if his participation in Xorvintaal was responsible .

title: Tea
description: Tea Tea was a traditional beverage from Shou Lung . Two varieties were available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description .
description_long: Tea Tea was a traditional beverage from Shou Lung . Two varieties were available for purchase through " Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue " . Description . Tea was similar in concept to other herbal infusions popular in the Realms . However , tea drinking was made into a refined art by the Shou , and teas from Shou Lung were known for being both invigorating and soothing .

title: Tear of Selûne
description: Tear of Selûne The Tear of Selûne was a major artifact of both great value and power that naturally made any magic in its vicinity more intense and dangerous . When combined with three other magical items , it could also be used to bring about great destructive force against evildoers . Description .
description_long: Tear of Selûne The Tear of Selûne was a major artifact of both great value and power that naturally made any magic in its vicinity more intense and dangerous . When combined with three other magical items , it could also be used to bring about great destructive force against evildoers . Description . This artifact was quite massive in size , comparable to an ogre ' s clenched fist , its surface formed of rough , unpolished crystal . Unlike other meteorites , it was in fact a great diamond . Anyone attuned to magical doings could feel that it radiated incredible energy . Powers . Simply by its own passive nature , the Tear had a significant effect on magic in its vicinity , for any spell cast within a hundred feet ( 30 meters ) of it would act at maximum effect , as well as if cast by a caster much greater in power . Any bearer of the Tear who also possessed the two steel keys was capable of unleashing stunning power from the skies , as they could summon a " meteor swarm " at will , which could strike anywhere in the Realms within their sight ( whether directly or by scry ing ) .

title: Teardrops
description: Teardrops The Teardrops was the name given to a series of small lakes found within the eastern half of Narfell as well as the western borderlands of Rashemen . Geography . The lakes of the Teardrops were strewn in a roughly linear pattern found due east of Hark ' s Finger .
description_long: Teardrops The Teardrops was the name given to a series of small lakes found within the eastern half of Narfell as well as the western borderlands of Rashemen . Geography . The lakes of the Teardrops were strewn in a roughly linear pattern found due east of Hark ' s Finger . The individual lakes of the Teardrops are listed below : Description . The Teardrops supported a bounty of fish and game , attracting hunters from the various tribes of Nar inhabiting the region .

title: Tearfall
description: Tearfall The Tearfall , also known as ileleste ( falling rain , in Elven ) , the changing of the stars , the seven - turn winter , or the month of mist , was a planet - wide disaster that struck Abeir - Toril in the final millennium of the Days of Thunder . It was widely believed dragonkind was created as a consequence of the Tearfall . History .
description_long: Tearfall The Tearfall , also known as ileleste ( falling rain , in Elven ) , the changing of the stars , the seven - turn winter , or the month of mist , was a planet - wide disaster that struck Abeir - Toril in the final millennium of the Days of Thunder . It was widely believed dragonkind was created as a consequence of the Tearfall . History . According to the " Parwiccan Cycle " , a devastating meteor rain fell in - 31000 DR , creating a series of natural catastrophes across the planet that destroyed whole continents in earthquakes , fires , and windstorms , rearranging even the positions of the seas . Ancient sarrukh accounts called this event the " changing of the stars " . Due to the catastrophe , the four Inner Seas merged together to form the Sea of Fallen Stars . In both the " Parwiccan Cycle " and the giant s ' traditions , the meteors were actually dragon eggs from which the varied races of dragonkind were born .

title: Tears of Selûne
description: Tears of Selûne The Tears of Selûne is an asteroid cluster , visible from the surface of Abeir - Toril that follows the moon Selûne in its orbit around the planet . Description . From Toril , although Selûne appears to be about the size of a human fist an arm ' s length away , the Tears of Selûne span almost three handspans wide and three fingers deep at the same distance .
description_long: Tears of Selûne The Tears of Selûne is an asteroid cluster , visible from the surface of Abeir - Toril that follows the moon Selûne in its orbit around the planet . Description . From Toril , although Selûne appears to be about the size of a human fist an arm ' s length away , the Tears of Selûne span almost three handspans wide and three fingers deep at the same distance . From the ground , the Tears appear as stars and are often identified as nine stars ( the other bodies are too indistinct to make out ) . The Tears are only bright enough to be seen at night , and even then they are not seen every night . The first tear appears above the horizon about four hours after Selûne rises , and it takes about three hours for the entire set of Tears to rise or set . History . Circa - 3500 DR an astronomer from Shou Lung , Tu Pi Chei , reported seeing many objects ' pop ' into existence . Soon , all of Toril ' s oceans were wracked by massive tidal waves . The Emperor was informed and the next night he too looked at the sky and saw the new objects . Twenty astrologers were tasked with determining their meaning .

title: Tears of fire
description: Tears of fire Tears of fire was a flame evocation spell used by members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara . Effects . This spell created 2 - 5 spheres of fire .
description_long: Tears of fire Tears of fire was a flame evocation spell used by members of the Brotherhood of the True Flame in Zakhara . Effects . This spell created 2 - 5 spheres of fire . Each sphere measured roughly 6 inches ( 15 cm ) in diameter . The fire spheres followed the caster for the duration of the spell by circling around their head . These spheres radiated the same amount of illumination as a " light " spell and gave off the heat of a regular fire , making them capable of providing warmth and comfort for the caster and anyone close to them . The fire spheres moved about the caster without their concentration , leaving them free to cast other spells or perform similar actions unhindered . With a mere thought the caster could send any or all of the spheres to unerringly strike any visible foe , so long as they were within 20 yards ( 18 m ) , burning them with flame . When struck with a sphere , combustible garments or items also burst into flame . The caster could direct the spheres at a single target or multiple targets at the same time . If the caster chose to send only a single sphere at a target , they were able to simultaneously perform other actions such as spellcasting .

title: Tebryn Dhialael
description: Tebryn Dhialael Tebryn Dhialael , also known as Dalael ) or the Shadowstalker , was a vampire and member of the Night Masters , the cabal of vampires who led the Night Masks . Description . Tebryn ' s skin was not as dark as a normal drow ' s but enough to betray his origin , as did his white hair .
description_long: Tebryn Dhialael Tebryn Dhialael , also known as Dalael ) or the Shadowstalker , was a vampire and member of the Night Masters , the cabal of vampires who led the Night Masks . Description . Tebryn ' s skin was not as dark as a normal drow ' s but enough to betray his origin , as did his white hair . Contrary to this , his blue eyes were clearly a gift from his human parent . He had a strong and slender build like most half - elves . History . Tebryn was born into slavery in the Underdark drow city of Sschindylryn . His opportunity to escape came when a duergar army from Underspires attacked the mining outpost where he toiled . The outpost was destroyed and Tebryn killed his masters and fled . He emerged from the Underdark in the tunnels under Westgate and lived as a thief . Tebryn accidentally discovered the Lair of the Night Masters and stole some items from there . Discovering the theft , Orbakh and Dahlia Vhammos easily caught Tebryn . He became the last vampire slave of Orbakh and the last victim of the " Winged Teeth " artifact . Tebryn was considered a perfect fit as master of the guild ' s thieves .

title: Teelah
description: Teelah Teelah was a dancer at the Moonstone Mask . Biography . She had aspirations to study dance at the conservatory in Waterdeep , but lacked the money to pay for it .
description_long: Teelah Teelah was a dancer at the Moonstone Mask . Biography . She had aspirations to study dance at the conservatory in Waterdeep , but lacked the money to pay for it . Until then , she worked for Ophala Cheldarstorn . If the Kalach - Cha came with Elanee , Teelah and Elanne would make some agressive comments . The Kalach - Cha could ' ve stood with Elanee to gain influence with her .

title: Teeth
description: Teeth Teeth were an ogre mercenary company based in Stonelands . Organization . The Teeth were organized in units of 19 warriors and a sergeant , all reporting to Jadron , that decided if merge the units or no .
description_long: Teeth Teeth were an ogre mercenary company based in Stonelands . Organization . The Teeth were organized in units of 19 warriors and a sergeant , all reporting to Jadron , that decided if merge the units or no . They preferred quickly and decisive combat and often stroke from several directions at once to confuse and frighten their foes . The Teeth ' s mark was their habit of bite their opponents . Contracts . the Teeth charged 2 gold piece s per week for each warrior for their services . Leadership . They were led by the the very infamous mercenary Jadron the Fang . History . In 1375 DR , they were recruited by the Zhentarim who ' d occupied Shadowdale . They attacked and destroyed the village of Oakwood Knoll with the Skull and Club mercenaries . Later , the two mercenary groups argued about the spoils .

title: Teeth of the Wind
description: Teeth of the Wind The Teeth of the Wind was an armed militia from the djinn freehold s and the Citadel of Ice and Steel . Organization . The exact numbers of the Teeth of the Wind was unknown , though it was believed to be in the tens of thousands .
description_long: Teeth of the Wind The Teeth of the Wind was an armed militia from the djinn freehold s and the Citadel of Ice and Steel . Organization . The exact numbers of the Teeth of the Wind was unknown , though it was believed to be in the tens of thousands . It was made - up of djinni and their elemental allies . Activities . This combined force worked as a gigantic cloud of flying combatants , reigning missiles down from above with archers and skirmishers . Base of Operations . The Citadel of Ice and Steel within the Elemental Plane of Air served as base of all djinni military organizations .

title: Tegan
description: Tegan Tegan was an escaped slave in the Deep Wastes . History . Tegan and her brother Drystan were two farmers in the Dalelands until , five years before the Rage of Demons , they were captured in an orc raid .
description_long: Tegan Tegan was an escaped slave in the Deep Wastes . History . Tegan and her brother Drystan were two farmers in the Dalelands until , five years before the Rage of Demons , they were captured in an orc raid . They were sold to the yugoloth Maram il Vass as a slave in its lair in the Deep Wastes . During the Rage of Demons , they managed to escape but were in very poor condition until they met an adventuring party that saved Tegan . Personality . Tegan had a desperate need for help but her time with a yugoloth caused her to not trust anyone . Tegan was proud and stubborn .

title: Tehrinna
description: Tehrinna Tehrinna was a human female and the proprietor of The Lake Spirits , a bathhouse and inn in Amnwater , Amn , circa 1368 DR . She had a sweet nature and flame red hair , and was only 1 . 37m ( 4 ' 6 " ) tall , but she was muscular and was able to eject most troublemakers .
description_long: Tehrinna Tehrinna was a human female and the proprietor of The Lake Spirits , a bathhouse and inn in Amnwater , Amn , circa 1368 DR . She had a sweet nature and flame red hair , and was only 1 . 37m ( 4 ' 6 " ) tall , but she was muscular and was able to eject most troublemakers .

title: Teirflin Armgo
description: Teirflin Armgo Teirflin Armgo was the son of Sinnafain and Tos ' un Armgo . Description . Teirflin kept his head shaved .
description_long: Teirflin Armgo Teirflin Armgo was the son of Sinnafain and Tos ' un Armgo . Description . Teirflin kept his head shaved . He fought with two swords . History . In 1484 DR , Teirflin and his sister Doum ' wielle Armgo held a duel to see who would inherit their father ' s sentient sword , " Khazid ' hea " . Doum ' wielle won the duel by using a spell , which Teirflin considered cheating . Enraged and fueled on by the sword ' s psychic intrusions , Teirflin stole " Khazid ' hea " and tried to kill Doum ' wielle with it as she slept . She awoke and managed to wrest the sword from his hands , but , at the urging of the sword , impaled her brother .

title: Tekinjo Gasahan
description: Tekinjo Gasahan Tekinjo Gasahan was the daimyo of Kurahito around 1357 DR . History . Tekinjo was the daimyo of the coastal Kurahito province and as the brother - in - law of the shogun one of the Three House daimyos .
description_long: Tekinjo Gasahan Tekinjo Gasahan was the daimyo of Kurahito around 1357 DR . History . Tekinjo was the daimyo of the coastal Kurahito province and as the brother - in - law of the shogun one of the Three House daimyos . He was devastated when in 1352 DR he discovered his wife , his only brother , and two senior members of the tairo were plotting his assassination . Tekinjo had all of them executed and afterward did not trust anyone . Only recently by 1357 DR he had found a friend in young Ionoi . Personality . Tekinjo had become withdrawn and cynical but he still possessed a sharp mind and was very perceptive . He knew that the shogunate wanted him to remarry to produce an heir but he totally disagreed with this .

title: Tekinjo Yojairo
description: Tekinjo Yojairo Tekinjo Yojairo was a samurai in Wa around 1357 DR . History . Yojairo was the son of Tekinjo Gasahan , one of the Three House daimyos , and for this , from around 1347 DR , he was appointed as military governor of the imperial residence at Rukimbaru , acting as liaison between the emperor and the shogun .
description_long: Tekinjo Yojairo Tekinjo Yojairo was a samurai in Wa around 1357 DR . History . Yojairo was the son of Tekinjo Gasahan , one of the Three House daimyos , and for this , from around 1347 DR , he was appointed as military governor of the imperial residence at Rukimbaru , acting as liaison between the emperor and the shogun . Around 1356 DR , he started a secret relationship with Kisha Yunoko , the emperor ' s concubine and the shogun ' s granddaughter . Personality . Tekinjo was a very efficient administrator . His service had shown him the true miseries of Wa ' s poor people and the hypocrisies of the shogunate . At first , he was disgusted by Yunoko ' s situation , but soon his sympathy for her blossomed into love .

title: Tekir
description: Tekir Tekir was a sahuagin malenti living in the Great Sea near a zaratan around the Corsair Domains in 1367 DR . Activities . Tekir guarded the island formed by the zaratan ' s shell from intruders , questioning any who approached .
description_long: Tekir Tekir was a sahuagin malenti living in the Great Sea near a zaratan around the Corsair Domains in 1367 DR . Activities . Tekir guarded the island formed by the zaratan ' s shell from intruders , questioning any who approached . They tried to enlist aid when they were able to help cleanse the isle of a self - proclaimed caliph named Nuri al - Zaratani

title: Tekthyrios
description: Tekthyrios Tekthyrios was a storm dragon living in a temple on Celestia . History . A portal was located in Tekthyrios ' s belly that was connected to the inside of a giant snake in the City of Brass in the Elemental Plane of Fire .
description_long: Tekthyrios Tekthyrios was a storm dragon living in a temple on Celestia . History . A portal was located in Tekthyrios ' s belly that was connected to the inside of a giant snake in the City of Brass in the Elemental Plane of Fire . A priest of Cyric named Zasian Menz and the cambion Kaanyr Vhok used this portal to enter Celestia from the City of Brass ; Kaanyr escaped from within Tekthyrios by means of purgative mushrooms delivered by the alu - fiend Aliisza , though in the journey they lost 12 years . Zasian instead possessed the dragon , as was his plan all along . The draconic hobgoblin Myshik Morueme followed Zasian and Vhok and , once emerging from the dragon ' s maw , swore to serve the storm dragon , having no awareness of Zasian ' s possession . Though Tekthyrios fought Zasian for control , the priest was easily able to keep him at bay while using the dragon ' s body to wreak havoc on Celestia . Once Tekthyrios was no longer useful , Zasian forced the storm dragon to impale himself on a broken tree and returned to his own body . Zasian emerged from the dragon ' s gullet as Tekthyrios died , swearing revenge on the priest with his last breath .

title: Tel ' kiira
description: Tel ' kiira A tel ' kiira ( also telkiira , plural tel ' kiira or telkiira ) is a small gemstone that can be used to magically store the thoughts or memories of an individual , or arcane lore or knowledge . Usually one merely needs to touch the stone to reveal its contents , but it is also possible to guard the contents against casual access . Some elven wizard s use these stones as spellbooks .
description_long: Tel ' kiira A tel ' kiira ( also telkiira , plural tel ' kiira or telkiira ) is a small gemstone that can be used to magically store the thoughts or memories of an individual , or arcane lore or knowledge . Usually one merely needs to touch the stone to reveal its contents , but it is also possible to guard the contents against casual access . Some elven wizard s use these stones as spellbooks .

title: Tel - quessir
description: Tel - quessir Tel - quessir ( also Tel ' Quessir or Tel ' Quess ) are a number of closely related , long - lived fey races commonly known as elves , though this term is now acknowledged to be technically inaccurate . Nonetheless , the name is common and many of the Tel - quessir consider themselves as one larger culture , an attitude not unjustified given that nearly all Tel - quessir speak Elven and share a common history together . Perhaps more importantly , the Tel - quessir were once one race , generally assumed to have been the eladrin or “ high elves .
description_long: Tel - quessir Tel - quessir ( also Tel ' Quessir or Tel ' Quess ) are a number of closely related , long - lived fey races commonly known as elves , though this term is now acknowledged to be technically inaccurate . Nonetheless , the name is common and many of the Tel - quessir consider themselves as one larger culture , an attitude not unjustified given that nearly all Tel - quessir speak Elven and share a common history together . Perhaps more importantly , the Tel - quessir were once one race , generally assumed to have been the eladrin or “ high elves . ” For these reasons and others , the Tel - quessir are often considered as though they were one race and called “ elves . ” Except when stated otherwise , the word “ elf ” and “ elven ” are used in this context throughout the article . Ecology . Physical characteristics . Although individual Tel - quessir races exhibit a number of unique traits , there are some features which are common to all of the races . Tel - quessir tend to be fair , beautiful and graceful , though they are very often frail as well .

title: Telamont Tanthul
description: Telamont Tanthul Telamont Tanthul the Most High was the ruler of Thultanthar , also known as Shade Enclave . He was a powerful Shade Archmage and Netherese Arcanist of the Shadow Weave . Description .
description_long: Telamont Tanthul Telamont Tanthul the Most High was the ruler of Thultanthar , also known as Shade Enclave . He was a powerful Shade Archmage and Netherese Arcanist of the Shadow Weave . Description . Tall and hardy , Telamont had diminished little in stature over his millennia long existence . In public , he cultivated his imposing figure by proudly wearing the traditional dark armor of the Netherese Empire . He wore robe of deep purple over the draconic overmantle and artistic vambraces of the armor . Personality . Telamont has a great love of Netherese culture and has sought to preserve it even when his subjects and he were forced onto the Demiplane of Shadow . His unwavering determination to rule the city means that he considers himself to be the true embodiment of the city ' s culture , laws and beliefs . Telamont ' s composure was such that it was near impossible to get a bead on what he was truly thinking or feeling and he had an unwavering eye for easily seeing through the facades of others . History . Early Life . Born in - 645 DR , Telamont became a student at the Academy of Mentalist Study in Eileanar under the moniker , Shadow .

title: Telantiwar
description: Telantiwar Telantiwar was an ancient drow city . History . When the drow first descended into the Underdark , they invaded and conquered the Dwarven city of Bhaerynden and renamed it Telantiwar .
description_long: Telantiwar Telantiwar was an ancient drow city . History . When the drow first descended into the Underdark , they invaded and conquered the Dwarven city of Bhaerynden and renamed it Telantiwar . The Drow bore two generations within the city , being host to Four Matriarchal noble houses . The main export of Telantiwar was copper and laves . The cavern housing the city later collapsed in on itself during the uprising of House Alean ' viir . Civil war erupted between the House of Alean ' viir and the three other noble houses within the city . The cave in buried and crushed the city , forming the Great Rift . Noble Houses House Rilyn ' val was the ruling noble house of Telantiwar , claiming to be direct descendants of the very first Illythri followers of Lolth . They pridied themselves on their abundant trade of slaves as well as their strong , dreadful priestesses . The Arch Priestess of Telantiwar was also the Matron of House Rilyn ' val . Their colors were black and maroon . House Zau ' tyl was the house of mages . They prided themselves in their skilled mages . The Ul ' faeruk of the city was also the Qu ' el ' faeruk of House Zau ' tyl . Their colors were silver and orange .

title: Telbran Nelarn
description: Telbran Nelarn Telbran Nelarn was a sorcerer in Waterdeep in 1372 DR . Personality . Telbran was a quiet man .
description_long: Telbran Nelarn Telbran Nelarn was a sorcerer in Waterdeep in 1372 DR . Personality . Telbran was a quiet man . He saw Waterdeep as a garden , and his actions against evildoers as that of a weeder tending the garden . Abilities . Telbran was a sorcerer of tremendous power . He could read and write many languages and knew more lore about Faerûn than most sages ever learned . Activities . By 1372 DR , Telbran lived quietly , usually under the alias of the book collector Hurlblar Corthyn . History . Telbran was born in the days of ancient Netheril . He was working as a scullery knave in the kitchens of the Netherese scholar Ensul Thruin , when a rival of his master destroyed the tower and his sorcerous powers were activated . He fled with a stolen tome containing the spell " Ensul ' s soultheft " , which he used to survive . Afterward , he adopted the life of a traveling trader , using this spell to kill foes or prolong his life . In time , Telbran decided to only target with his spell evil spellcasters whom he viewed as preying on others . Finally , Telbran arrived in Waterdeep , which he soon came to love , and so he decided to live there .

title: Teldar
description: Teldar Teldar was an old pirate in 1359 DR . History . Teldar was a pirate officer under Laershala , the last pirate lord of Earthspur .
description_long: Teldar Teldar was an old pirate in 1359 DR . History . Teldar was a pirate officer under Laershala , the last pirate lord of Earthspur . He was the de - facto leader of the pirates thank to his old age and his record of successful raids . Many believed he no ruled openly for no attire unnecessary attentions . teldar always gave wise advise to new pirates . He was renown for his supply of magical item s that saved him many times in over the years like when he using his necklace of missiles ended the career of Cheves the Scourge . In 1363 DR Vurgrom managed to defeat Teldar becoming the pirate lord . Teldar exiled himself in Thesk . Personality . Teldar had few leadership abilities

title: Teldartham
description: Teldartham Teldartham was the new captain of the guard of Skuld in Mulhorand in 1357 DR . History . In 1357 the clerics of Horus - Re managed to appoint Teldartham , a champion of Horus - Re , as captain of the guard of Skuld despite was a position usually covered by worshipers of Anhur .
description_long: Teldartham Teldartham was the new captain of the guard of Skuld in Mulhorand in 1357 DR . History . In 1357 the clerics of Horus - Re managed to appoint Teldartham , a champion of Horus - Re , as captain of the guard of Skuld despite was a position usually covered by worshipers of Anhur .

title: Teldorn Darkhope
description: Teldorn Darkhope Teldorn Darkhope was the ruler of the city of Mintar , having conquered it with a Zhentarim - sponsored army of Iyachtu Xvim . After the conquest on Mintar , Teldorn , and Fzoul Chembryl forged the artifact known as the Scepter of the Tyrant ' s Eye .
description_long: Teldorn Darkhope Teldorn Darkhope was the ruler of the city of Mintar , having conquered it with a Zhentarim - sponsored army of Iyachtu Xvim . After the conquest on Mintar , Teldorn , and Fzoul Chembryl forged the artifact known as the Scepter of the Tyrant ' s Eye .

title: Telekinesis
description: Telekinesis Telekinesis was an arcane transmutation spell that allowed a caster to telekinetically move , manipulate , or forcefully hurl objects or creatures . Effects . The spell gave the caster the power of telekinesis , allowing them to move an object or creature in a variety of possible ways , as they wished .
description_long: Telekinesis Telekinesis was an arcane transmutation spell that allowed a caster to telekinetically move , manipulate , or forcefully hurl objects or creatures . Effects . The spell gave the caster the power of telekinesis , allowing them to move an object or creature in a variety of possible ways , as they wished . According to the power of the caster , it worked up to a distance of hundreds of feet , could move an object weighing up to 375 pounds ( 170 kilograms ) , thrust a number of creatures or objects , and last for a brief time so long as the caster concentrated . The first application exerted a sustained force on an object , rotating it or moving it in any direction at a speed of up to 3 . 3 feet ( 1 meter ) per second . A creature had to resist the spell in order to hold back or hold onto the object . This application allowed a degree of fine manipulation , such as pulling a rope or level , turning a key , or even untying a simple knot , if such tasks could be performed with one hand . The second application exerted a short force on a creature .

title: Telepathic broadcast
description: Telepathic broadcast Telepathic broadcast was a divine magic alteration spell that was available to priests of the Red Knight . It allowed the caster to telepathically convey verbal information to all allies within range . Effects .
description_long: Telepathic broadcast Telepathic broadcast was a divine magic alteration spell that was available to priests of the Red Knight . It allowed the caster to telepathically convey verbal information to all allies within range . Effects . When cast , this spell connected the mind of the caster to the mind of all allies within 270 ft ( 82 m ) in a one - way mental link for nine minutes . More experienced casters could extend this range and duration . Any information that could be expressed verbally could be broadcast , and only the caster ' s allies could receive it — no one hostile to the caster could overhear or intercept the mental speech . The caster could choose to broadcast in any language that he or she knew and the recipients heard the words in that language whether or not they spoke that tongue . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components and the priest ' s holy symbol , a material component was required to help power " telepathic broadcast " ( and was consumed in the casting ) .

title: Telepathy
description: Telepathy Telepathy was a psionic mental ability that enabled one intelligent creature to send and receive thoughts to another intelligent creature and communicate without words or a shared language . A creature must know a language to use telepathy . The use of magic was a common way to use telepathy .
description_long: Telepathy Telepathy was a psionic mental ability that enabled one intelligent creature to send and receive thoughts to another intelligent creature and communicate without words or a shared language . A creature must know a language to use telepathy . The use of magic was a common way to use telepathy . Some creatures possessed telepathy as a supernatural ability . Some intelligent magic item s could also communicate using telepathy . Mental Discipline . Telepathy was also a mental discipline or psionic sub - class . Any psion who focused on this discipline gained experience and power dealing with psionic messages and control of other beings .

title: Telepathy candle
description: Telepathy candle A telepathy candle was a special magic item made by mystic s in the Realms . It allowed a mystic to read thoughts and communicate mind to mind with those under its influence . Description .
description_long: Telepathy candle A telepathy candle was a special magic item made by mystic s in the Realms . It allowed a mystic to read thoughts and communicate mind to mind with those under its influence . Description . " Telepathy candles " were yellow and , unlike other candles made by mystics , operated continuously for as long as they remained lit . The longest - lasting candle that could be made burned for ninety minutes . This was the fifth type of candle mystics learned to make when studying candle magic . Powers . Only mystics could utilize the power of these candles . Unwilling subjects had one chance to resist the magic of this candle and , if they succeeded , were unaffected and their thoughts remained private . Those that failed to resist , and " charmed " or willing subjects opened their minds to examination by the mystic and could communicate with him or her at a level that transcended any language barrier . The mystic could detect lies , half - truths , and evasive answers to questions and could read the conscious thoughts of all those affected by the " telepathy candle " .

title: Teleport
description: Teleport Teleport was a conjuration spell that allowed the caster to transit instantly between two points . Effect . This spell instantly transported the caster to a designated destination .
description_long: Teleport Teleport was a conjuration spell that allowed the caster to transit instantly between two points . Effect . This spell instantly transported the caster to a designated destination . Distance was not a factor , but interplanar travel was not possible . The caster could bring along objects and willing creatures . The amount of weight a caster could bring with him increased as he became more powerful . The caster had to have a clear idea of the location and layout of the destination . The clearer the mental image , the more likely the teleportation was to work . Areas of strong physical or magical energies could make teleportation more hazardous or even impossible . Teleportation was instantaneous travel through the Astral Plane . Anything that blocked astral travel also blocked teleportation . There was a chance the caster would end up off target or in an area that was visually similar to the desired destination . The teleporation could occasionally result in a " mishap " which injured or even killed the caster and companions .

title: Teleport dead
description: Teleport dead Teleport dead was an alteration and necromancy spell that could instantly transport a single dead or undead body to anywhere on the plane of the caster . Effects . The oldest version of this spell was easier to learn and only worked on the undead .
description_long: Teleport dead Teleport dead was an alteration and necromancy spell that could instantly transport a single dead or undead body to anywhere on the plane of the caster . Effects . The oldest version of this spell was easier to learn and only worked on the undead . The newer version was more difficult to learn but also worked on an unanimated corpse and could be used to remove a fallen comrade from the battlefield to a safer location . The caster had to touch the corpse or undead creature ( including gaseous vampire s , specter s , and other intangible undead ) . All undead creatures had a chance to resist the magic of this spell and , if successful , remained in place . Spellcasting undead had a much better chance of resisting this spell . Accuracy was the same as for the " teleport " spell and improved with increasing familiarity of the destination . Arriving high meant a fall of 10 ft ( 3 m ) at the very least , while arriving low meant 10 ft ( 3 m ) underground and was usually , though not necessarily , " fatal " to an undead creature .

title: Teleport without error
description: Teleport without error Teleport without error , or greater teleport , is a transmutation spell that lets one instantly transit from one location to another . Effects . This spell is like " teleport " , except there is no chance you arrive off target .
description_long: Teleport without error Teleport without error , or greater teleport , is a transmutation spell that lets one instantly transit from one location to another . Effects . This spell is like " teleport " , except there is no chance you arrive off target . You must have at least a reliable description of the place to which you are teleporting . If you attempt to teleport with insufficient information ( or with misleading information ) , you disappear and simply reappear in your original location .

title: Teleportation circle
description: Teleportation circle Teleportation circle was a conjuration spell that created a circle that teleported any creature inside to a designated spot . Effects . The teleportation circles appeard on the floor or other horizontal surface .
description_long: Teleportation circle Teleportation circle was a conjuration spell that created a circle that teleported any creature inside to a designated spot . Effects . The teleportation circles appeard on the floor or other horizontal surface . It functioned like the " teleport without error " spell . Any creature who stood within the circle was teleported to a designated spot . This designated spot could only be set once . The spell failed if the caster attempted to set the circle to teleport creatures into a solid object , to a place with which they were not familiar and had no clear description , or to another plane . The circle itself was subtle and nearly impossible to notice . The caster needed to mark the circle in some way to keep creatures from activating it accidentally . Teleportation circles were extremely difficult to detect and disarm . Material components . This spell required amber dust to cover the area of the circle .

title: Telescope of fantastic vision
description: Telescope of fantastic vision A telescope of fantastic vision was a bizarre magical spyglass that originated in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These spyglasses were cylindrical and often made of precious metal such as gold .
description_long: Telescope of fantastic vision A telescope of fantastic vision was a bizarre magical spyglass that originated in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These spyglasses were cylindrical and often made of precious metal such as gold . Powers . For the first several uses , this spyglass functioned exactly like a " telescope of true vision " , magnifying images and granting the user the ability to pierce illusions and see things as they truly were . However , after the first several uses , the " telescope of fantastic vision " showed the viewer weird images that usually proved to appear the opposite of what they actually were . For instance , the telescope might make the viewer think a distant caravan was actually a war - party of orc s .

title: Telescope of true vision
description: Telescope of true vision Telescopes of true vision were incredibly useful magic spyglasses that originated in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These spyglasses were cylindrical and often made of precious metal such as gold .
description_long: Telescope of true vision Telescopes of true vision were incredibly useful magic spyglasses that originated in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Description . These spyglasses were cylindrical and often made of precious metal such as gold . Powers . A " telescope of true vision " provided the mundane ability of magnifying a viewed object by a factor of 50 . Thus a ship at sea from 5 , 000 feet away would appear to be 100 feet away when viewed through the spyglass . The enchantment upon these spyglasses pierced illusions and other magical misdirection , allowing the viewer to see an object in its true form . A " telescope of true vision " had 20 charges . Upon using the last charge the lens would crack and the item would be ruined .

title: Telflamm
description: Telflamm Telflamm was usually considered to be the biggest and most important city in Thesk ; however , Telflamm was actually an independent city - state but wielded so much power and influence over the country that it might as well have been the capital . Telflamm was officially founded in 926 DR by Windyn Balindre , who moved his base of operations from Impiltur to this newly - built settlement and declared himself ' Merchant Prince ' , a hereditary title . Situated at the start the incredibly profitable Golden Way trading route , Telflamm quickly became the biggest trading station in the region , with most trade concerning the products of Kara - Tur which was in wide demand across Faerûn .
description_long: Telflamm Telflamm was usually considered to be the biggest and most important city in Thesk ; however , Telflamm was actually an independent city - state but wielded so much power and influence over the country that it might as well have been the capital . Telflamm was officially founded in 926 DR by Windyn Balindre , who moved his base of operations from Impiltur to this newly - built settlement and declared himself ' Merchant Prince ' , a hereditary title . Situated at the start the incredibly profitable Golden Way trading route , Telflamm quickly became the biggest trading station in the region , with most trade concerning the products of Kara - Tur which was in wide demand across Faerûn . Sometime in the early part of the fourteenth century DR , the most wealthy and influential merchants in the city set up a regulating body to check any excesses of the prince . This Merchant ' s Council was viewed as the real power in the city by most outsiders . This was not actually the case , however . Once the merchants began squabbling with Thesk and becoming too worried about their own profits , things started to go downhill .

title: Telkoun ' s Tower
description: Telkoun ' s Tower Telkoun ' s Tower was a wizard stronghold located in High Thorog in the Nether Mountains . Description . The stronghold consisted of one building with two double towers .
description_long: Telkoun ' s Tower Telkoun ' s Tower was a wizard stronghold located in High Thorog in the Nether Mountains . Description . The stronghold consisted of one building with two double towers . Several gargoyle s defended the tower , paid and also charmed by Telkoun Adranther . There was a " stasis sphere " at the last floor of the tower .

title: Telkoun Adranther
description: Telkoun Adranther Telkoun Adranther was an evil sorcerer who constantly sought magical power . Relationships . His parents were an evil sorceress and a powerful demon .
description_long: Telkoun Adranther Telkoun Adranther was an evil sorcerer who constantly sought magical power . Relationships . His parents were an evil sorceress and a powerful demon . History . Circa 1352 DR , together with his fellows , Telkoun came across the ancient Netherese tower of High Thorog . After driving away all the creatures that were occupying the tower , Telkoun enslaved his fellows and proclaimed himself absolute master of the tower . He spent years of his life trying to solve the mysteries of the tower . The most intriguing was certainly the " stasis sphere " . He believed that a demon lord had been imprisoned within the sphere . His purpose was to free the demon and gain a dark reward . Powers . Telkoun used his powerful spells , such as " charm monster " to subjugate large groups of monsters and creatures living near the tower . Under Telkoun ' s control , these creatures watched the lands around the tower and reported intruders ' movements . These creatures were in the majority peryton s .

title: Tellectus
description: Tellectus Tellectus was a city founded by the Ariser Creed of Oryndoll in the Upperdark near Beregost . Long before the mid - 14th century DR , a band of adventurers launched a devastating raid on the city . They discovered the sword " Taragarth " , which had been being studied there .
description_long: Tellectus Tellectus was a city founded by the Ariser Creed of Oryndoll in the Upperdark near Beregost . Long before the mid - 14th century DR , a band of adventurers launched a devastating raid on the city . They discovered the sword " Taragarth " , which had been being studied there . In addition to the legendary bastard sword , the adventurers also found a series of stone tablets with illithid writing on them . When they deciphered the tablets , it was found that the colony had a safe passage to Oryndoll , but its location was not on the tablets . It was also revealed that the colony was built to gain access to Candlekeep ' s library , by ambushing travelers coming and going with new knowledge . It had one other purpose , and that was to document Candlekeep ' s defenses , for the possibility of a future plundering by the Arisers of Oryndoll . However , due to the raid , the efforts at Tellectus were abandoned by the Arisers , though their efforts to plunder Candlekeep continued from Oryndoll . Their mozgriken servitors still lived in the ruins , abandoned by the Arisers and not wanted among their svirfneblin ancestors .

title: Tellik Melarn
description: Tellik Melarn Tellik Melarn was the brother of Q ' arlynd Melarn . He was also a Nightshadow , a term to describe a cleric of Vhaeraun . Relationship .
description_long: Tellik Melarn Tellik Melarn was the brother of Q ' arlynd Melarn . He was also a Nightshadow , a term to describe a cleric of Vhaeraun . Relationship . Tellik was Q ' arlynd ' s younger brother . They were very close to each other , enough for Q ' arlynd to think first his brother when asked about close family members . History . Tellik was a cleric of Vhaeraun and invited his brother to attend a meeting of fellow members of the church of Vhaeraun . At some point , he made a major transgression against his faith by impersonating his god ' s avatar . He was punished for it . The punishment consisted of the illusion to be made permanent , so he couldn ' t switch it off anymore , which was dangerous because it would have revealed his link to the church of Vhaeraun for everyone in the Lolth dominated city of Ched Nasad . He came to his brother , who was a wizard and begged him for help . Q ' arlynd wasn ' t able to lift the curse , due to his lack of skill . So the next suggestion was to turn Tellik invisible to allow his escape out of the city .

title: Telmyz
description: Telmyz Telmyz was a priest of Vhaeraun . History . In 1377 DR , Telmyz was one of the six nightshadow s chosen for an assault led by Kâras on the main temple of Kiaransalee .
description_long: Telmyz Telmyz was a priest of Vhaeraun . History . In 1377 DR , Telmyz was one of the six nightshadow s chosen for an assault led by Kâras on the main temple of Kiaransalee . Together with the conjurer Mazeer , he was polymorph ed into an insect when a sudden flood hit them , them killing Telmyz .

title: Telnarquel
description: Telnarquel Telnarquel was an Underdark city , called The Hidden City . It was so well concealed that some drow explorers refused to believe that it actually existed . In truth , it did indeed exist but was abandoned for an unknown reason at some point in the 14th century DR .
description_long: Telnarquel Telnarquel was an Underdark city , called The Hidden City . It was so well concealed that some drow explorers refused to believe that it actually existed . In truth , it did indeed exist but was abandoned for an unknown reason at some point in the 14th century DR . It lay empty for a few decades until an alhoon made the city its lair . Dove Falconhand once used being from Telnarquel as a cover identity while " polymorph ed " as a drow infiltrating a large group of Vhaeraun - worshipers who were covertly invading Scornubel in 1369 DR .

title: Telornym
description: Telornym Telornym was a human male cleric of Mystra and the Lord of Mystery at the Tower of Mysteries in Saerloon , Sembia . He was the second - in - command of the Tower of Mysteries , assisting the Mage Arcane Tanthala . He was also a senior member of the Moonstars in 1370 DR .
description_long: Telornym Telornym was a human male cleric of Mystra and the Lord of Mystery at the Tower of Mysteries in Saerloon , Sembia . He was the second - in - command of the Tower of Mysteries , assisting the Mage Arcane Tanthala . He was also a senior member of the Moonstars in 1370 DR . Telornym and his wife Shaal , a priestess of Azuth , lived in a house in Saeloon owned by Khelben Arunsun but rented to Telornym for thirty years .

title: Telos
description: Telos The Master of the Iron Sky , known as Telos in most tongues , was a primordial who fell to the tundra of Vaasa during the Spellplague . He remained there , comatose , while the Warlock Knights mined what they called ironfell or " the iron " from his body . This material , which regenerated quickly , was used by the Knights to fashion items and construct s they called shardsoul s .
description_long: Telos The Master of the Iron Sky , known as Telos in most tongues , was a primordial who fell to the tundra of Vaasa during the Spellplague . He remained there , comatose , while the Warlock Knights mined what they called ironfell or " the iron " from his body . This material , which regenerated quickly , was used by the Knights to fashion items and construct s they called shardsoul s .

title: Telos ( city )
description: Telos ( city ) Telos was located in the crater created when the primordial Telos , whom the city takes its name from , fell to Vaasa . The city was fortress - like and the Ironfell Council ruled from the Citadel of the Iron Sky in the center of the city . There were no houses of worship in Telos but some sects worshiped in secret .
description_long: Telos ( city ) Telos was located in the crater created when the primordial Telos , whom the city takes its name from , fell to Vaasa . The city was fortress - like and the Ironfell Council ruled from the Citadel of the Iron Sky in the center of the city . There were no houses of worship in Telos but some sects worshiped in secret .

title: Telpi
description: Telpi Telpi was a language spoken by the inhabitants of the Dragon Coast and the Pirate Isles , from Proskur in the north to Nathlekh in the south , and from Iriaebor in the west to the Pirate and Whamite Isles in the east . Telpi was the only East Thorass language , but it included three dialects — Dragonsmere , Pirate / , and Whamite . The dialect of the pirates of the Sea of Fallen Stars was strongly influenced by other languages of the region .
description_long: Telpi Telpi was a language spoken by the inhabitants of the Dragon Coast and the Pirate Isles , from Proskur in the north to Nathlekh in the south , and from Iriaebor in the west to the Pirate and Whamite Isles in the east . Telpi was the only East Thorass language , but it included three dialects — Dragonsmere , Pirate / , and Whamite . The dialect of the pirates of the Sea of Fallen Stars was strongly influenced by other languages of the region . They used it as a sort of secret language for carrying on their illegal activities .

title: Telshazz
description: Telshazz Telshazz was a demon in the balor Errtu ' s service . Personality . The small demon was obedient and very submissive to its masters .
description_long: Telshazz Telshazz was a demon in the balor Errtu ' s service . Personality . The small demon was obedient and very submissive to its masters . History . Errtu appointed Telshazz with the task of retrieving the Crenshinibon artifact . However , the relic was found by Al Dimeneira , but its power overwhelmed that of the angelic being , burning its hands . Al Dimeneira managed to throw Crenshinibon across the planes of existence , putting it far away from Errtu ' s grasp . When Telshazz reported all this to its master , Errtu tore its throat out in rage .

title: Telthukiilir
description: Telthukiilir A telthukiilir ( or " high seeing orb " ) was an extremely powerful version of a crystal ball . It was lit faintly from within , emanating emerald - colored light . By speaking a command , the large orb could show the whereabouts of any individual .
description_long: Telthukiilir A telthukiilir ( or " high seeing orb " ) was an extremely powerful version of a crystal ball . It was lit faintly from within , emanating emerald - colored light . By speaking a command , the large orb could show the whereabouts of any individual . It was capable of scrying despite even powerful magical barriers , but its more powerful abilities used its charge more rapidly , and it took time to recover from this . Sarya Dlardrageth recovered a telthukiilir originating from Aryvandaar from the ruins of Nar Kerymhoarth .

title: Telvannah
description: Telvannah Telvannah was the White Worm high shaman in Vaasa in 1479 DR . Powers . Telvannah could summon the Spirit of the Remorhaz , gaining great control over heat and fire .
description_long: Telvannah Telvannah was the White Worm high shaman in Vaasa in 1479 DR . Powers . Telvannah could summon the Spirit of the Remorhaz , gaining great control over heat and fire . Relationship . Telvannah was the wife of chieftain Tor - Rem . She had a tundra yeti as a spirit companion .

title: Temerity
description: Temerity Temerity was a tiefling descendant of the Toril thirteen . Activities . Temerity ran a shop in Proskur .
description_long: Temerity Temerity was a tiefling descendant of the Toril thirteen . Activities . Temerity ran a shop in Proskur . History . In 1478 DR , Farideh and Lorcan went to Temerity ' s shop . Lorcan asked for Temerity ' s assistance for his plan . However , Temerity had made a pact with Sairché and informed her of the presence of Farideh and Lorcan in the city . Powers . Temerity had made a warlock ' s pact with Lorcan but later transferred to Sairche .

title: Temigast
description: Temigast Temigast was the steward of Auckney , serving under the Lord of Auckney since 1339 DR , the Year of the Weeping Moon . Description . Temigast essentially ran Auckney from beside the scene , advising Lord Feringal Auck in all important matters of state .
description_long: Temigast Temigast was the steward of Auckney , serving under the Lord of Auckney since 1339 DR , the Year of the Weeping Moon . Description . Temigast essentially ran Auckney from beside the scene , advising Lord Feringal Auck in all important matters of state . He was quite the gentleman , one of the few in Auckney knowledgeable of places and events outside the fiefdom . His hobby was painting seascapes . History . Temigast was originally from Waterdeep . He came to Auckney as a merchant , but he then settled there and became a counselor for the then lord of Auckney , Tristan Auck . Relationships . Temigast helped raise Feringal and Priscilla Auck after their parents died . He secretly shared his bed with Feringal ' s sister , Priscilla Auck , who took care of the flower garden outside the palace . He was friendly towards Auck ' s fiance , Meralda Ganderlay , even though she had been lying with other men , more specifically another man , Jaka Sculi . It was revealed that he knew Meralda ' s secret all along , but kept it for her sake . Meralda considered him a source of support .

title: Temmenische
description: Temmenische Temmenische was a monk and a member of the Disciples of St . Sollars the Twice - Martyred at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose in the 13th and 14th centuries DR . History .
description_long: Temmenische Temmenische was a monk and a member of the Disciples of St . Sollars the Twice - Martyred at the Monastery of the Yellow Rose in the 13th and 14th centuries DR . History . Temmenische was born " circa " 1264 DR . In the Year of the Serpent , 1359 DR , Grand Master Poke died suddenly . This necessitated that Kane , a Master of Spring and next - in - line for the position of Grand Master , hurry back to the monastery and manage affairs until a new Grand Master could be trained and selected . However , Kane had no wish to remain in the position . Temmenische was the next most senior monk , but at 95 years of age , he was hardly a practical choice . Thus Kane and Temmenische chose Cantoule , who was much younger and more suitable , to succeed Poke as Grand Master . They put Cantoule through accelerated training in advanced techniques to ready him for the post .

title: Temmi Dharimm
description: Temmi Dharimm Temmi Dharimm ( pronounced " TEHM - ee DARR - imm " or " TEH - mee DAH - rimm " ) , known simply as " Temmi the Slaver " , was a human man from Tsurlagol in the Vast . He was a bandit and slaver . History .
description_long: Temmi Dharimm Temmi Dharimm ( pronounced " TEHM - ee DARR - imm " or " TEH - mee DAH - rimm " ) , known simply as " Temmi the Slaver " , was a human man from Tsurlagol in the Vast . He was a bandit and slaver . History . Temmi Dharimm was native to Tsurlagol . However , he went on to spend many years working hard as a bandit around the Moonsea . In that time , he accumulated by some means his force of trained monsters . By 1357 DR , Temmi had based himself in the Elven Woods near Hillsfar and began taking captives and selling them into slavery . They were sold to the Zhentarim or other agents of Zhentil Keep , who took them north in covered wagons . Temmi was still carrying on his cruel trade ten years later . He intended to expand his business and was on the look - out for employees with similar ways . Activities . Temmi the Slaver was highly discreet and very careful . The humans and demihuman s he caught were securely bound in manacles , blindfolded and gagged , then chained by collars around their throats to a coffle - bar ( a long tree - trunk that a group of slaves were forced to carry ) . He operated around the Elven Woods , the Moonsea , the Dalelands , and the Vast .

title: Tempest
description: Tempest Tempest was the murdered lover of Ren o ' the Blade . Description . Tempest was a very beautiful and muscular woman with fiery red hair .
description_long: Tempest Tempest was the murdered lover of Ren o ' the Blade . Description . Tempest was a very beautiful and muscular woman with fiery red hair . With her emerald green eyes and facial features , she resembled Shal Bal . Personality . Bawdy and quick as a street courtesan , Tempest was wonderfully talented in all her exploits . Possessions . When hunting and stealing , Tempest preferred to wear black leather armor . History . In 1339 DR , Ren and Tempest stole a pair of magical dagger s and ioun stone s from an assassin ' s guild in Waterdeep . Later that year , the killers found Ren and Tempest in their Waterdhavian home and stabbed Tempest through her left breast . The dagger was coated in a vile poison which caused Tempest to convulse and spasm in her death throes ; Ren had no choice but to put her out of her misery .

title: Tempest breath
description: Tempest breath Tempest breath , also known as Mestil ' s acid breath was a spell of the conjuration school used by some sorcerer s , particularly dragon sorcerers . When a sorcerer cast " tempest breath " he or she exhaled a green mist of acidic vapors that burned and disoriented any creatures within a nearby zone 15 ft ( 4 . 6 m ) in diameter .
description_long: Tempest breath Tempest breath , also known as Mestil ' s acid breath was a spell of the conjuration school used by some sorcerer s , particularly dragon sorcerers . When a sorcerer cast " tempest breath " he or she exhaled a green mist of acidic vapors that burned and disoriented any creatures within a nearby zone 15 ft ( 4 . 6 m ) in diameter . Creatures affected by " tempest breath " were prevented , for a moment , from taking advantage of their enemies ' weaknesses , so disoriented were they by the spell . Dragon sorcerers who used " tempest breath " were able to , in addition , conceal themselves from sight for a moment through use of the remaining mist . The spell was not particularly easy to cast , it required a few minutes of rest to be recharged . Before the Spellplague , " tempest breath " was more commonly known as " Mestil ' s acid breath " and was used by both sorcerers and wizard s . The area of effect was a cone emanating from the caster ' s mouth for a distance of at least 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) .

title: Tempest domain
description: Tempest domain The Tempest domain was a set of spells that were granted by deities whose portfolio included the destructive power of nature . Clerics who chose this domain were granted free access to these spells ( they could cast them at any time without having to prepare them in advance ) .
description_long: Tempest domain The Tempest domain was a set of spells that were granted by deities whose portfolio included the destructive power of nature . Clerics who chose this domain were granted free access to these spells ( they could cast them at any time without having to prepare them in advance ) .

title: Temple Hill
description: Temple Hill Temple Hill was a rocky hill rising from the center of the city of Elversult . Description . Crowded on top of the hill was a temple to Waukeen and a temple to Lathander .
description_long: Temple Hill Temple Hill was a rocky hill rising from the center of the city of Elversult . Description . Crowded on top of the hill was a temple to Waukeen and a temple to Lathander . At the hill ' s northern base was the open space for the city ' s marketplace .

title: Temple of Corellon Larethian
description: Temple of Corellon Larethian The Temple of Corellon Larethian was a temple in Leuthilspar on the island of Evermeet . Structure . The temple was dedicated to the worship of Corellon Larethian , head of the Seldarine .
description_long: Temple of Corellon Larethian The Temple of Corellon Larethian was a temple in Leuthilspar on the island of Evermeet . Structure . The temple was dedicated to the worship of Corellon Larethian , head of the Seldarine . The building was set in its own grounds and featured two spires . Inside was a large statue of Corellon Larethian . History . As of 1369 DR , the temple was run by High Priest Rathal Evanara , who was assisted by two acolytes .

title: Temple of Deneir ( Procampur )
description: Temple of Deneir ( Procampur ) A temple of Deneir lay in the Temple District of the city of Procampur in the Vast . Structure & Interior . The temple structure included a main hall .
description_long: Temple of Deneir ( Procampur ) A temple of Deneir lay in the Temple District of the city of Procampur in the Vast . Structure & Interior . The temple structure included a main hall . The front entrance consisted of a portico with a very loud doorknocker , attended to by a clay golem porter . There was also a small side - door . Inside the hall was a shrine to Deneir , and upon the altar were arranged a thousand votive candles . It also had a tower , accessed with a winding staircase , with small rooms with single small windows . They had good views over the city of Procampur . These rooms were inhabited by priests and guests of the temple . Attached to the temple were a number of secure vaults , for the storage of books and for working on projects such as the creation of golem s . History . At some point , the Hierarch of the temple commanded the scholar - monk Vilhiard of Procampur to set out on a number of lengthy and hazardous journeys into the East . The Hierarch was , in turn , thought to have received commands from the Thultyrl of Procampur . The Thultyrl granted Vilhiard a supply of wealth for expenses .

title: Temple of Lolth ( Cathtyr )
description: Temple of Lolth ( Cathtyr ) The Temple of Lolth was the second largest temple in the metropolis of Cathtyr in Dambrath . Description . The temple sat on one side of the queen ' s palace .
description_long: Temple of Lolth ( Cathtyr ) The Temple of Lolth was the second largest temple in the metropolis of Cathtyr in Dambrath . Description . The temple sat on one side of the queen ' s palace . It had flying buttresses shaped to resemble spider ' s legs , and its main entrance was carved to resemble the spider ' s head and mouth . Inhabitants . The Temple of Lolth in Cathtyr was led by High Priestess Chaladra Sse ' blis .

title: Temple of Mystra ( Wheloon )
description: Temple of Mystra ( Wheloon ) The Temple of Mystra was a false temple in the town of Wheloon in Cormyr . Constructed in 1374 DR on the ruins of an old citadel on the edge of town , it was dedicated to Mystra , goddess of magic , but was in fact a front for worshipers of Shar , goddess of shadows , and Cyric , god of lies . Under the guise of a holy ritual , they kidnapped , murdered , and sacrificed true followers of Mystra , wielders of magic , and ordinary people who ' d become caught up in the snare .
description_long: Temple of Mystra ( Wheloon ) The Temple of Mystra was a false temple in the town of Wheloon in Cormyr . Constructed in 1374 DR on the ruins of an old citadel on the edge of town , it was dedicated to Mystra , goddess of magic , but was in fact a front for worshipers of Shar , goddess of shadows , and Cyric , god of lies . Under the guise of a holy ritual , they kidnapped , murdered , and sacrificed true followers of Mystra , wielders of magic , and ordinary people who ' d become caught up in the snare . This was all part of a plot by Esvele Graycastle and the black dragon Despayr to rend a hole in the Weave of magic . The nefarious scheme was unveiled and thwarted by adventurers in service to Mystra . History . Citadel . Well before the founding of Wheloon , a so - called citadel was built on the site . It was later ruined , and nothing more than the crumbling foundations remained by the 1370s DR . The ruins became home to displacer serpent s . Founding . In around Ches of the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR , the priestess Naedaenya Arthas met with Lord Sarp Redbeard to request the construction of a temple of Mystra in Wheloon , the first in the whole kingdom of Cormyr .

title: Temple of Ten Thousand Gods
description: Temple of Ten Thousand Gods The Temple of Ten Thousand Gods was an unusual faith in Zakhara . Its adherents believed in the enlightened gods , but held the opinion that they , and each deity represented there , were only facets of one supreme divine being . The credo of the Ten Thousand also included that there was a divine spark in every creature , and that the variety of mortals also reflected the theme of diversity in unity .
description_long: Temple of Ten Thousand Gods The Temple of Ten Thousand Gods was an unusual faith in Zakhara . Its adherents believed in the enlightened gods , but held the opinion that they , and each deity represented there , were only facets of one supreme divine being . The credo of the Ten Thousand also included that there was a divine spark in every creature , and that the variety of mortals also reflected the theme of diversity in unity . The ideals of the Temple of Ten Thousand Gods were therefore tolerance and acceptance . < br > Its symbol was a nautilus shell . < br > This faith bore a strong resemblance to the philosophy of the planar faction called the Believers of the Source and had some common ground with the Durpar i belief in Adama .

title: Temple of Tyr ( Dagger Falls )
description: Temple of Tyr ( Dagger Falls ) A temple of Tyr lay in Dagger Falls and was occasionally known to lend its services to adventurers who aided Randal Morn . Location . It was situated in Dagger Falls , in northern Daggerdale .
description_long: Temple of Tyr ( Dagger Falls ) A temple of Tyr lay in Dagger Falls and was occasionally known to lend its services to adventurers who aided Randal Morn . Location . It was situated in Dagger Falls , in northern Daggerdale . Services . The temple of Tyr in Dagger Falls offered a few services to those willing and able to pay . Healing and spellcasting services were provided , if necessary . History . In 1372 DR , the temple of Tyr had a good working relationship with the Lord of Daggerdale , Randal Morn , with a senior cleric of Tyr , Tunfer the Stout , operating as the Lord ' s advisor .

title: Temple of Wisdom
description: Temple of Wisdom The Temple of Wisdom was a house of worship dedicated to the gnomish god Garl Glittergold at the Friendly Arm Inn on the Sword Coast . Structure . It was a low building with its interior walls decorated with gems and gold nuggets .
description_long: Temple of Wisdom The Temple of Wisdom was a house of worship dedicated to the gnomish god Garl Glittergold at the Friendly Arm Inn on the Sword Coast . Structure . It was a low building with its interior walls decorated with gems and gold nuggets . Appendix . Appearances . In the game Baldur ' s Gate , the player can visit the temple to buy potions and receive healing . It is run by Gellana Mirrorshade , the wife of Bentley Mirrorshade .

title: Temple of the Faceless God
description: Temple of the Faceless God The Temple of the Faceless God was dedicated to the Faceless God of the Yikarian Empire in 1367 DR . Location . The temple was located in the yikarian capital of Nathong in the heart of the Land of the Yak - Men .
description_long: Temple of the Faceless God The Temple of the Faceless God was dedicated to the Faceless God of the Yikarian Empire in 1367 DR . Location . The temple was located in the yikarian capital of Nathong in the heart of the Land of the Yak - Men . Activity . The Temple of the Faceless God was the site where the ritual sacrifice of the Lotus Emperor occurred once every 20 years .

title: Temple of the Lady of Mercy
description: Temple of the Lady of Mercy The Temple of the Lady of Mercy was a temple located in Hammergate dedicated to the dwarven goddess Sharindlar . The temple had a tall statue of the goddess carved from a single huge fire opal as well as a ritual cleansing pool . During the stoneplague in 1480 DR , the temple inadvertently spread the plague by accepting offerings of tainted gold from worshipers .
description_long: Temple of the Lady of Mercy The Temple of the Lady of Mercy was a temple located in Hammergate dedicated to the dwarven goddess Sharindlar . The temple had a tall statue of the goddess carved from a single huge fire opal as well as a ritual cleansing pool . During the stoneplague in 1480 DR , the temple inadvertently spread the plague by accepting offerings of tainted gold from worshipers .

title: Temple of the Nine Travelers
description: Temple of the Nine Travelers The Temple of the Nine Travelers was one of the newer buildings in Manass in 1367 DR . It was a temple devoted to the Faith of the Nine Travelers , in particular to the Giants in Gray . Faith .
description_long: Temple of the Nine Travelers The Temple of the Nine Travelers was one of the newer buildings in Manass in 1367 DR . It was a temple devoted to the Faith of the Nine Travelers , in particular to the Giants in Gray . Faith . It was home to a small sect of the Nine Travelers faith originating from Shou Lung that worshiped the Giants in Gray themselves . Visitations of the Giants in Gray were said to presage immense tragedies . Inhabitants . A Shou settler named Li Dawchyuan managed the temple . Many Shou travelers made a point to stop and visit the temple since it was a good place to catch up on gossip from Shou Lung . Activities . The Yellow Mountain Sect in Manass kept a careful eye on the Temple of the Nine Travelers since they were not sure if this " new " religion from the east was a threat to their goals .

title: Temple of the Red Mountain
description: Temple of the Red Mountain The Temple of the Red Mountain was a rundown building in Manass in Khazari in 1367 DR . Description . The Temple of the Red Mountain was a small structure in need of repair because of an assortment of attacks from rivals .
description_long: Temple of the Red Mountain The Temple of the Red Mountain was a rundown building in Manass in Khazari in 1367 DR . Description . The Temple of the Red Mountain was a small structure in need of repair because of an assortment of attacks from rivals . Inhabitants . The temple was home to nineteen shukenja of the Red Mountain Sect . Activities . The temple was constantly attacked and harassed by sohei of the Yellow Mountain Sect .
