description_long: Water form Water form was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell transformed the caster or recipient into a creature made from elemental water . The recipient ' s mind remained the same . While in water form , the recipient could go through any location that water would fit through including small cracks and crevices . The recipient was invisible when submerged in water . Piercing or slashing weapons did not cause nearly as much damage while in water form , but blunt weapons caused regular damage . Exposure to full sunlight caused minor evaporation damage . The recipient was immune to poison or gas attacks and did not need to eat or breathe while in water form . Fire - based attacks against the recipient were not as effective , but lighting - based attacks were more effective . Components . This spell required an eyedropper to cast .

title: Water naga
description: Water naga Water nagas lived within oceans and rivers , protecting hidden treasures claimed by these waterways . They preferred solitude and isolation . Appearance .
description_long: Water naga Water nagas lived within oceans and rivers , protecting hidden treasures claimed by these waterways . They preferred solitude and isolation . Appearance . Water nagas were about ten feet long and weighed about 250 pounds . They had scales the color of the waters in which they lived — greens , blues , and all the colors in between . Their bodies were lined with frilled spines that stood on edge when excited or agitated .

title: Water of Eldath
description: Water of Eldath Water of Eldath was a divine magic spell available to priests of Eldath , the Goddess of Singing Waters . It created three flasks of a potion that had many curative and purification abilities . Effects .
description_long: Water of Eldath Water of Eldath was a divine magic spell available to priests of Eldath , the Goddess of Singing Waters . It created three flasks of a potion that had many curative and purification abilities . Effects . When cast , this spell filled three potion bottles with " water of Eldath " that could be used topically or taken internally . The potion had the following properties : Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required three drops of water blessed by Eldath herself , one of her servitors , or one of her high - ranking priests ( known as an Exalted of Eldath ) . One drop was placed in each of the three flasks to be filled by the resulting potion .

title: Water opal
description: Water opal Water opal was a rare and valuable gem stone . Description . Water opal was a clear to translucent gemstone with small flashes of color .
description_long: Water opal Water opal was a rare and valuable gem stone . Description . Water opal was a clear to translucent gemstone with small flashes of color . Opals without any color were considered plain , an inferior stone , and were nearly worthless . Water opal was rare and highly prized for use in decorating mirrors and windows and in the creation of scry ing devices such as " crystal balls " . A typical specimen had a base value of 1 , 000 gp . Powers . An " elixir of health " could be made without any spellcasting by grinding a water opal to powder and mixing it with holy water .

title: Water walk
description: Water walk Water walk was a transmutation or alteration spell that allowed one or more creatures to stride upon liquids or semi - liquids such as water ( flowing or still ) , oil , snow , mud , or quicksand . Effects . While walking on a liquid , the subject ' s feet did not touch the surface but floated one or two inches ( 2 .
description_long: Water walk Water walk was a transmutation or alteration spell that allowed one or more creatures to stride upon liquids or semi - liquids such as water ( flowing or still ) , oil , snow , mud , or quicksand . Effects . While walking on a liquid , the subject ' s feet did not touch the surface but floated one or two inches ( 2 . 5 to 5 cm ) above . Appendages made appropriate - sized oval displacements in the surface , thus leaving peculiar footprints in semi - liquids . The recipient could even walk on lava if they could stand the intense heat . If cast while submersed , the recipient would quickly float to the surface . Components . Verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell , as well as the priest ' s holy symbol or divine focus .

title: Waterbane
description: Waterbane Waterbane was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects .
description_long: Waterbane Waterbane was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects . With this spell the caster or target would not get wet from fresh water or saltwater only . This spell had no effect on creatures from the Elemental Plane of Water and did not prevent drowning . Once cast , this spell lasted for one full day . Components . This spell required a bit of wax and some paper to cast .

title: Waterclock Guild
description: Waterclock Guild The Waterclock Guild was a guild founded in Neverwinter by the wizard Lucan Greenharrow and the clockmaker Saborn Rendel . Using the former ' s magic and the latter ' s clockmaking skill , the guild produced clocks that were both accurate and beautiful . Over time , Lucan built the crypts beneath the guild , expanding them using the magic he had learned during his time at the Hosttower of the Arcane in Luskan .
description_long: Waterclock Guild The Waterclock Guild was a guild founded in Neverwinter by the wizard Lucan Greenharrow and the clockmaker Saborn Rendel . Using the former ' s magic and the latter ' s clockmaking skill , the guild produced clocks that were both accurate and beautiful . Over time , Lucan built the crypts beneath the guild , expanding them using the magic he had learned during his time at the Hosttower of the Arcane in Luskan . This included the secrets of binding water elemental s , and the crypt walls were covered in translucent veins through which sea water flowed .

title: Waterdeep
description: Waterdeep Waterdeep , also known as the City of Splendors or the Crown of the North , was the most important and influential city in the North and perhaps in all Faerûn . For this reason it was considered part of the Western Heartlands of the Realms , even though it lay 150 miles north of Daggerford on the shores of the Sword Coast . The city sat " slightly above the 45 degree north latitude line on Toril .
description_long: Waterdeep Waterdeep , also known as the City of Splendors or the Crown of the North , was the most important and influential city in the North and perhaps in all Faerûn . For this reason it was considered part of the Western Heartlands of the Realms , even though it lay 150 miles north of Daggerford on the shores of the Sword Coast . The city sat " slightly above the 45 degree north latitude line on Toril . " The road to Waterdeep was well paved and well patrolled . The city was the hub of trading from the mineral - rich lands to the north , the merchant kingdoms of Amn and Calimshan to the south , the kingdoms of the Inner Sea to the east , and the sea kingdoms and traders to the west . Waterdeep ' s authority extended between thirty to forty miles from its walls . The surrounding region had a population density of over 200 people per square mile . Waterdeep was named for its outstanding natural deep - water harbor , and the city that grew up at this site became the commercial crossroads of the northern Realms . More than 100 , 000 people made their home in Waterdeep .

title: Waterdeep ( series )
description: Waterdeep ( series ) Waterdeep ( or Ed Greenwood Presents Waterdeep ) is a series of six stand - alone novels , each written by a different author , that takes place in the city of Waterdeep in 1479 DR , the year in which the fourth edition of the Forgotten Realms takes place . Forgotten Realms creator Ed Greenwood oversaw the project .
description_long: Waterdeep ( series ) Waterdeep ( or Ed Greenwood Presents Waterdeep ) is a series of six stand - alone novels , each written by a different author , that takes place in the city of Waterdeep in 1479 DR , the year in which the fourth edition of the Forgotten Realms takes place . Forgotten Realms creator Ed Greenwood oversaw the project .

title: Waterdhavian ( cheese )
description: Waterdhavian ( cheese ) Waterdhavian cheese was pale with holes and came from Waterdeep . Geography . The cheese was available in most bars in the city and was commonly eaten by the nobility also .
description_long: Waterdhavian ( cheese ) Waterdhavian cheese was pale with holes and came from Waterdeep . Geography . The cheese was available in most bars in the city and was commonly eaten by the nobility also . Description . It had a sharp and tangy bite . Prices . As of 1368 DR , a 450 g ( 1 lb ) wheel was around four silver pieces , and 45 kg ( 100lb ) was available for around 35 gold pieces .

title: Waterfall Kiss
description: Waterfall Kiss Waterfall Kiss was a scented facial wash invented by Jhamanthra Tsathree around the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR . Description . Waterfall Kiss was a secret blend of herbs brewed with water that was clear with a slightly oily feel and a strong scent .
description_long: Waterfall Kiss Waterfall Kiss was a scented facial wash invented by Jhamanthra Tsathree around the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR . Description . Waterfall Kiss was a secret blend of herbs brewed with water that was clear with a slightly oily feel and a strong scent . It was sold in " handbottles " for 3 gp each at Tsathree ' s Comforts on Golden Serpent Street in the North Ward of Waterdeep . While in demand for faddish reasons , the resale value of a full bottle was reported to be double or triple the original price . Powers . This hygiene product was purported to cleanse the skin , remove " tired skin " , and leave a pleasant scent after rinsing . It was soon found to have another , probably unintended , property . After washing with Waterfall Kiss and applying certain rouges and powders that were in fairly common use among the matrons of Waterdeep , the treated skin began to glow a vivid green . This effect came on suddenly some hours after the application of makeup and lasted for a few more hours .

title: Watermaster
description: Watermaster The Watermaster was a hobgoblin sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , the Watermaster was one of the minions of the hill giant Chief Guh in Grudd Haug .
description_long: Watermaster The Watermaster was a hobgoblin sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , the Watermaster was one of the minions of the hill giant Chief Guh in Grudd Haug . His duty was to catch fish from the river , take care of the dam , and guard the den ' s supply of rations .

title: Waterorb
description: Waterorb Waterorb was a fungus that grew in the Underdark in shallow water . When mature , it was bulbous in shape and bigger than a human head . If squeezed and wrung out , it yielded about a gallon ( almost four liters ) of potable water .
description_long: Waterorb Waterorb was a fungus that grew in the Underdark in shallow water . When mature , it was bulbous in shape and bigger than a human head . If squeezed and wrung out , it yielded about a gallon ( almost four liters ) of potable water . The remaining husk was bland and chewy like a sponge , but edible , providing about a pound ( almost a half kilogram ) of food .

title: Waters of devotion
description: Waters of devotion Waters of devotion was a potion that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Powers . The imbiber of this potion was placed under the control of the person who gave it to them .
description_long: Waters of devotion Waters of devotion was a potion that could be found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Powers . The imbiber of this potion was placed under the control of the person who gave it to them . The imbiber ' s mental capacities were still intact , but they remained loyal to the giver . The potion ' s effects lasted for one month , but could be dispelled by magical means at any time .

title: Watersoul genasi
description: Watersoul genasi Watersoul genasi , also known as water genasi , are one of five most common subraces or " manifestations " within the genasi race . Like all genasi manifestations they can be manifested by experienced genasi who have a different primary manifestation but have trained themselves otherwise or have acquired the manifestation as a result of hidden ancestry or environmental conditions . Ecology .
description_long: Watersoul genasi Watersoul genasi , also known as water genasi , are one of five most common subraces or " manifestations " within the genasi race . Like all genasi manifestations they can be manifested by experienced genasi who have a different primary manifestation but have trained themselves otherwise or have acquired the manifestation as a result of hidden ancestry or environmental conditions . Ecology . Physical characteristics . Most watersoul genasi are descended from marid genie s , although a few have other origins , including some who are descended from the goddess Umberlee . Like other genasi , watersoul genasi look generally human except for some distinguishing features . Watersoul genasi " szuldar " are often bright blue in color and most of the race is bald , though there are exceptions . The skin of the watersoul genasi is usually sea - foam green or blue . A few other , rarer , features are found amongst watersoul genasi , such as lightly scaled skin , clammy flesh , blue - green hair , excessive perspiration , blue - black eyes , or a muffled voice that sounds as if drowned in water .

title: Waterspout
description: Waterspout Waterspout was a divine magic spell available to priests of Umberlee , the Bitch Queen , and cleric s of other deities that claimed the ocean as their domain . It created a towering column of water that could pick up objects and creatures , pummel them mercilessly , and then eject them high above the water level . A rare arcane conjuration / summoning version of this spell also existed , mainly used by water elementalist s .
description_long: Waterspout Waterspout was a divine magic spell available to priests of Umberlee , the Bitch Queen , and cleric s of other deities that claimed the ocean as their domain . It created a towering column of water that could pick up objects and creatures , pummel them mercilessly , and then eject them high above the water level . A rare arcane conjuration / summoning version of this spell also existed , mainly used by water elementalist s . Effects . There were two divine versions of this spell , an earlier one used by priests of Umberlee and a later version that had more wide - spread use among followers of deities associated with oceans . The spells were very similar with minor differences in range and duration , but with one major difference : the later spell required a source of water at least 10 ft ( 3 m ) across by 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) deep and could create enough water to form a column 10 ft ( 3 m ) wide by 80 ft ( 24 m ) tall , whereas the earlier version required a body of water large enough to supply all the water for such a column . Both versions required a water depth of at least 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) below the surface of the water source to support the " waterspout " .

title: Waterstar
description: Waterstar Waterstar , also called achroite or colorless tourmaline , was a rare fancy stone . Description . Waterstar was a colorless and transparent gemstone .
description_long: Waterstar Waterstar , also called achroite or colorless tourmaline , was a rare fancy stone . Description . Waterstar was a colorless and transparent gemstone . Gem - quality stones had to be flawless and could yield large faceted jewels that sparkled . A typical specimen had a base value of 100 gp . Powers . Waterstar , like all tourmalines , could absorb any spell cast upon it and immediately convert it into three " lightning bolt s " that blasted outward from the crystal facets . This act consumed the gem in the process .

title: Watery death domain
description: Watery death domain Watery Death was a prestige domain granted to certain high - level divine spellcasters , such as kuo - toa n sea mother whip s of Blibdoolpoolp . It bestowed the power to " smite " any non - aquatic creature once a day , and a range of killing water - themed spells . Deities with the Watery Death domain .
description_long: Watery death domain Watery Death was a prestige domain granted to certain high - level divine spellcasters , such as kuo - toa n sea mother whip s of Blibdoolpoolp . It bestowed the power to " smite " any non - aquatic creature once a day , and a range of killing water - themed spells . Deities with the Watery Death domain . The following deities would grant the watery death domain to their followers :

title: Watery form
description: Watery form Watery form was an arcane alteration spell that transformed the caster and anything being worn into a quantity of water . Effects . For 50 minutes ( or longer , for higher level casters ) , the caster of " watery form " became essentially a sentient , mobile , puddle of water .
description_long: Watery form Watery form was an arcane alteration spell that transformed the caster and anything being worn into a quantity of water . Effects . For 50 minutes ( or longer , for higher level casters ) , the caster of " watery form " became essentially a sentient , mobile , puddle of water . While in this form , the caster could see , hear , breathe , and move at his or her normal speed , either on land , on a ship , or in water . Movement included climbing or swimming to any depth , but all strenuous movement was just as physically taxing in this form as in the caster ' s normal form . The caster also had the same strength as normal . The caster ' s " body " could not be absorbed by a sponge or separated into smaller quantities of water , but weapons and magic could injure or effect the caster normally . For the duration of this spell , " watery form " provided camouflage that was undetectable by normal means in a body of water or in places where water was expected , such as wet spots on the deck of a ship , but climbing a rope was likely to draw attention . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell . History .

title: Watson Nettlebee
description: Watson Nettlebee Watson Nettlebee was the oldest son and heir of Bertram Nettlebee during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Watson was brave , honest , and forthright .
description_long: Watson Nettlebee Watson Nettlebee was the oldest son and heir of Bertram Nettlebee during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Watson was brave , honest , and forthright . He had more in common with his mother than his father or grandfather , and he was angry about the mistreatment of the cattle . Watson knew about Wiggan and Bertram ' s new religion , but thought it was only folklore . Relationships . His father Bertram slowly instructed Watson about the Cult of the Black Earth . History . In 1491 DR , he was unwittingly involved in a trap set by his family for some adventurers who had defeated the Cult of the Black Earth at the Sacred Stone Monastery .

title: Waukeen
description: Waukeen Waukeen ( pronounced wau - KEEN or wah - KEEN ) was a lesser deity of the Faerûnian pantheon known as the Merchant ' s Friend , Liberty ' s Maiden , and the Golden Lady . Her portfolio included everything related to commerce and the accumulation of wealth through free and fair trade , as well as the beneficial use of wealth to improve civilization . Those that venerated and appeased her included merchants from lowly peddlers to the wealthy owners of trading companies , investors , accountants , entrepreneurs , caravan guides , warehouse owners , philanthropists , deal - makers , moneylenders , and so on .
description_long: Waukeen Waukeen ( pronounced wau - KEEN or wah - KEEN ) was a lesser deity of the Faerûnian pantheon known as the Merchant ' s Friend , Liberty ' s Maiden , and the Golden Lady . Her portfolio included everything related to commerce and the accumulation of wealth through free and fair trade , as well as the beneficial use of wealth to improve civilization . Those that venerated and appeased her included merchants from lowly peddlers to the wealthy owners of trading companies , investors , accountants , entrepreneurs , caravan guides , warehouse owners , philanthropists , deal - makers , moneylenders , and so on . Waukeen was also the goddess of illicit trade and the patron of many smugglers , fences , black marketeers , and " businessmen " on the shady side of commerce . Collectively , her worshipers were known as Waukeenar . Description . Waukeen was portrayed as a slender , young woman with long , lustrous golden hair ; always splendidly dressed . Some depictions included a pair of golden lions resting at her feet . Her avatar was 10 ft ( 3 m ) tall and typically had eyes that appeared as solid gold .

title: Waukeen ' s Promenade
description: Waukeen ' s Promenade Waukeen ' s Promenade is one of the most impressive structures in Athkatla . It is a huge marketplace , twice the size of Waterdeep ' s market and built as an oval stadium surrounded by terraced 50 - foot walls . The Promenade has 75 - foot - wide levels for consumer and mercantile traffic .
description_long: Waukeen ' s Promenade Waukeen ' s Promenade is one of the most impressive structures in Athkatla . It is a huge marketplace , twice the size of Waterdeep ' s market and built as an oval stadium surrounded by terraced 50 - foot walls . The Promenade has 75 - foot - wide levels for consumer and mercantile traffic . From the upper levels falls some shade to the lower ones . The most expansive areas for merchants is the entry level on the ground or the first terrace over the entry arches . Greater guilds and merchant houses have monopolized that area of the market . Wide ramps lead up to the terraces where additional stalls and booths provide anything and everything from across the Realms . The city guards are constantly patrolling the market and therefore only a few illegal or magical items can be found at Waukeen ' s Promenade . But the Promenade is also a place where clandestine meetings are often planned for unlawful business , which actually takes place elsewhere . Baldur ' s Gate II : Shadows of Amn . In the game Baldur ' s Gate II : Shadows of Amn the Promenade is one of the main areas at the beginning of the adventure .

title: Waukeen ' s silver tongue
description: Waukeen ' s silver tongue Waukeen ' s silver tongue was a divine spell , or Channel Divinity prayer , given to worshipers of Waukeen that granted them a second chance at a more favorable outcome in situations requiring diplomacy or when attempting to bluff or intimidate . Better or worse , the second outcome was final .
description_long: Waukeen ' s silver tongue Waukeen ' s silver tongue was a divine spell , or Channel Divinity prayer , given to worshipers of Waukeen that granted them a second chance at a more favorable outcome in situations requiring diplomacy or when attempting to bluff or intimidate . Better or worse , the second outcome was final .

title: Wave Echo Cave
description: Wave Echo Cave Wave Echo Cave was a great cavern complex within the Sword Mountains . The cavern was known for its mineral wealth as well as its magical properties . Wave Echo Cave was connected to an underground hot spring that continuously boiled near the cavern .
description_long: Wave Echo Cave Wave Echo Cave was a great cavern complex within the Sword Mountains . The cavern was known for its mineral wealth as well as its magical properties . Wave Echo Cave was connected to an underground hot spring that continuously boiled near the cavern . The cavern got its name from the booming sounds created every time the waves crashed against the cavern . History . In approximately 900 DR , clans of dwarves and gnomes made a pact that would later be known as Phandelver ' s Pact . The pact allowed both of the races to share the riches within the mine of Wave Echo Cave . Many gained from this agreement , including the nearby human settlement of Phandalin . However , in 951 DR , the orcs of Uruth Ukrypt came from the north and laid waste to the region . The orcs were aided by mercenary wizards when they attacked Wave Echo Cave , adamant in seizing its riches . The human spellcasters of Phandalin fought alongside the gnomes and dwarves to defend the cave . However , the battle of magic destroyed much of Wave Echo Cave . Few survived the battle and so the location of the cave was lost to history .

title: Wavecrest
description: Wavecrest Wavecrest is one of two islands that make up the Eyes of Silvanus on the Sea of Fallen Stars . It is situated close to the mouth of the Vilhon Reach . It benefits from the protection of reefs and also the magic of the Emerald Enclave .
description_long: Wavecrest Wavecrest is one of two islands that make up the Eyes of Silvanus on the Sea of Fallen Stars . It is situated close to the mouth of the Vilhon Reach . It benefits from the protection of reefs and also the magic of the Emerald Enclave . The Eyes of Silvanus were formed from mountains when Jhaamdath fell .

title: Waves of sand
description: Waves of sand Waves of sand was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . With this spell the caster caused the sand surrounding a wagon , or similar vehicle , to undulate like water .
description_long: Waves of sand Waves of sand was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . With this spell the caster caused the sand surrounding a wagon , or similar vehicle , to undulate like water . The wagon could be carried along as if it were riding a tide . Living creatures surrounding the wagon , such as pack animals , could not pull the wagon while the spell was active . The wagon could travel at a rate of 3 miles ( 4 . 8 km ) per hour and the direction was controlled by a mental urging from the caster or anyone else whom the caster designated . The spell would automatically end if the wagon stopped for more than one minute . Components . This spell required the presence of sand to cast .

title: Waves of weariness
description: Waves of weariness Waves of weariness was an enchantment spell that could cause a person or creature to either pause in their attack or fall to the ground completely , depending on the target ' s wisdom or intellect . Effects . This spell could affect one creature up to 40 yd ( 36 .
description_long: Waves of weariness Waves of weariness was an enchantment spell that could cause a person or creature to either pause in their attack or fall to the ground completely , depending on the target ' s wisdom or intellect . Effects . This spell could affect one creature up to 40 yd ( 36 . 6 m ) away . If the target had sufficient resistance to spells , then this spell failed with no ill effects . Otherwise , creatures of above average intelligence or wisdom were suddenly fatigued enough to cause them to delay their next action , hopefully giving the caster or the caster ' s allies an advantage . Creatures of below average intelligence or wisdom were overcome with exhaustion and vertigo , causing them to collapse immediately for one minute . After the spell wore off , the target recovered just as quickly . This spell only affected creatures that normally sleep . Undead and elemental s , for example , were immune . Components . In addition to somatic gestures , this spell required the caster to read aloud from a small book of poetry , such as " Translations from Kara - Tur Haiku " by Lhaeo of Shadowdale . History .

title: Way of Lost Power
description: Way of Lost Power The Way of Lost Power was a small twenty - two page hand written chapbook which contained cryptic hints to guide the reader to sites containing lost magic . Description . The original book was a rather ordinary looking , slim chapbook with the title on the cover .
description_long: Way of Lost Power The Way of Lost Power was a small twenty - two page hand written chapbook which contained cryptic hints to guide the reader to sites containing lost magic . Description . The original book was a rather ordinary looking , slim chapbook with the title on the cover . History . The book was copied as many as seventy times although the content in some of the copies may have been altered as most of the copies had fewer than the original twenty - two pages . Many mage s suspected the copies contained erroneous information intended to lead the reader astray . The original author was unknown although the book was attributed variously to Velahoondar , " Old Elminster " , Volo and Khelben the Younger .

title: Way of the Manticore
description: Way of the Manticore The Way of the Manticore was a long road that connected the nations of Cormyr and Sembia . The westernmost point of the Way of the Manticore was located at the town of Hilp , where it met Calantar ' s Way . The easternmost part of the Way of the Manticore was the city of Selgaunt in Sembia .
description_long: Way of the Manticore The Way of the Manticore was a long road that connected the nations of Cormyr and Sembia . The westernmost point of the Way of the Manticore was located at the town of Hilp , where it met Calantar ' s Way . The easternmost part of the Way of the Manticore was the city of Selgaunt in Sembia . Route . From west to east , the Way of the Manticore ran through :

title: Way of the Powrie
description: Way of the Powrie The Way of the Powrie was a road in the Moonsea North . Starting at a bridge crossing the Telstang Brook , north of the village of Ilinvur , it stretched over 100 miles further north , skirting the eastern edge of the Ride before crossing into the Tortured Land s then ending at a bridge over the River Pelauvir near Frozen Flindyke .
description_long: Way of the Powrie The Way of the Powrie was a road in the Moonsea North . Starting at a bridge crossing the Telstang Brook , north of the village of Ilinvur , it stretched over 100 miles further north , skirting the eastern edge of the Ride before crossing into the Tortured Land s then ending at a bridge over the River Pelauvir near Frozen Flindyke .

title: Wayfork Village
description: Wayfork Village A growing village that is located just North of Trollbark Forest . Its fate is unknown as it either was destroyed by the Spellplague , or like the rest of the civilizations around its area , it was relatively untouched . It is likely still growing into a larger city .
description_long: Wayfork Village A growing village that is located just North of Trollbark Forest . Its fate is unknown as it either was destroyed by the Spellplague , or like the rest of the civilizations around its area , it was relatively untouched . It is likely still growing into a larger city . History . The Dark Alliance . The village was almost destroyed by the Zhentarim ' s Red Fang Marauder Goblin Gang . It was very quickly saved by a band of five adventurers .

title: Waymoot
description: Waymoot Waymoot was a small town in the King ' s Forest in Cormyr . Locations . It the location of The Moon and Stars , which was , according to Volo , one of the greatest taverns in all of the Realms .
description_long: Waymoot Waymoot was a small town in the King ' s Forest in Cormyr . Locations . It the location of The Moon and Stars , which was , according to Volo , one of the greatest taverns in all of the Realms . History . In 1368 DR , Waymoot , along with Espar , Eveningstar , and Tyrluk , was plagued by rogue dragons . Trade . Animal pelts from the Thunder Peaks and the Storm Horns did very good business in Waymoot as of 1368 DR .

title: Wayrock
description: Wayrock Wayrock is both an island and an 11 , 000 ft . ( 3 , 400 m ) mountain in the Sea of Fallen Stars . It is visible from up to 100 miles ( 161km ) away .
description_long: Wayrock Wayrock is both an island and an 11 , 000 ft . ( 3 , 400 m ) mountain in the Sea of Fallen Stars . It is visible from up to 100 miles ( 161km ) away . The only man - made structures are a ruined keep on the eastern slope and a temple of Cyric which was stripped , stolen and placed upon the wayrock by the githvyrik sorcerer Vhostym . It is now a temple to Mask , guarded closely by his exarch Drasek Riven .

title: Wean mother
description: Wean mother The task of being a Wean mother is delegated to a noble daughter of a noble drow house . Their job is to tend to the needs of a drow infant for 10 years , teaching it language ( low drow , High Drow , Drow Sign Language and undercommon ) , how to manifest it ' s spell - like abilities , and above all to teach it it ' s place in drow society .
description_long: Wean mother The task of being a Wean mother is delegated to a noble daughter of a noble drow house . Their job is to tend to the needs of a drow infant for 10 years , teaching it language ( low drow , High Drow , Drow Sign Language and undercommon ) , how to manifest it ' s spell - like abilities , and above all to teach it it ' s place in drow society .

title: Weapon - black
description: Weapon - black Weapon - black was a useful substance used by some rogue s and other nocturnal adventurers . Uses . When smeared on metal this substance eliminated the chance of light reflecting off of a blade and alerting guards .
description_long: Weapon - black Weapon - black was a useful substance used by some rogue s and other nocturnal adventurers . Uses . When smeared on metal this substance eliminated the chance of light reflecting off of a blade and alerting guards . Weapon - black was not harmful to metal and did nothing but dull a blade . Weapon - black was not flammable . A vial of weapon - black contained enough of the substance for 25 applications . Prices . A single vial of weapon - black cost 3 gold pieces .

title: Weapon master
description: Weapon master For a weapon master , perfection is found in the mastery of a single melee weapon . A weapon master seeks to unite this weapon of choice with the body to make them one and to use the weapon as naturally and without thought as any other limb . Source of Power .
description_long: Weapon master For a weapon master , perfection is found in the mastery of a single melee weapon . A weapon master seeks to unite this weapon of choice with the body to make them one and to use the weapon as naturally and without thought as any other limb . Source of Power . Like other classes such as the monk , red avenger , and master samurai , the weapon master uses an esoteric force known as " ki " to increase his lethality in combat . His goal is to unite his weapon of choice with his body , and be able to use it without conscious effort as naturally as he would use any other limb . Individual weapon masters are often named for their weapons : for instance , a weapon master who uses longsword s would be a " longsword master , " a warhammer wielder would be a " warhammer master , " etc .

title: Weapon of concealed wizardry
description: Weapon of concealed wizardry A weapon of concealed wizardry referred to any type of magic weapon where the enchantments were undetectable by magical means . These weapons originated in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Powers .
description_long: Weapon of concealed wizardry A weapon of concealed wizardry referred to any type of magic weapon where the enchantments were undetectable by magical means . These weapons originated in Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Powers . A " weapon of concealed wizardry " could have the enchantment of any other magic weapon found on Al - Toril . Additionally , casting " detect magic " , " legend lore " , " identify " , and similar spells , revealed nothing about the weapon ' s magical nature . Rawun s and barber s were able to use their special skills to determine the basic magical nature of these weapons .

title: Weather sphere
description: Weather sphere The Weather sphere was a group of spells granted to druid s . These spells could temporarily alter the weather or local conditions for good or ill . Appendix .
description_long: Weather sphere The Weather sphere was a group of spells granted to druid s . These spells could temporarily alter the weather or local conditions for good or ill . Appendix . Background . Spells in normal text were listed in the " Tome of Magic 2nd edition " . Spells in italics were added to the Weather Sphere in the " " sourcebook .

title: Weather stasis
description: Weather stasis Weather stasis was an abjuration spell that preserved the weather conditions in a given area for a few hours . Effects . The area of effect for this spell was a cube whose sides were of length 10 ft ( 3 .
description_long: Weather stasis Weather stasis was an abjuration spell that preserved the weather conditions in a given area for a few hours . Effects . The area of effect for this spell was a cube whose sides were of length 10 ft ( 3 . 1 m ) times the level of the caster . Inside this volume , the prevailing weather conditions remained constant regardless of changes in the surrounding area . Normal or magical changes in the weather did not occur within the protected area , even with the rising or setting of the sun . Components . A drop of rain was required to cast this spell , along with verbal and somatic components and the priest ' s holy symbol .

title: Weathercote Wood
description: Weathercote Wood Weathercote Woods is a woodland located just west of Anauroch , north of the Lonely Moor , east of the Graypeak Mountains and south of the Fallen Lands in the Savage Frontier . Blue mists and strange lights are often see in the woods . History .
description_long: Weathercote Wood Weathercote Woods is a woodland located just west of Anauroch , north of the Lonely Moor , east of the Graypeak Mountains and south of the Fallen Lands in the Savage Frontier . Blue mists and strange lights are often see in the woods . History . Weathercote Wood has existed from before the rise of Netheril and continues to exist today despite the advancing of the desert of Anauroch . Some legends claim Nobanion originally entered the Realms through one of the portals in Weathercote Woods . Trade . The Zhentarim s Black Road runs just south of Weathercote Woods . Rumors . According to the elves , Weathercote wood is full of Gate s to other worlds , as well as Wizard s that guard the gates from casual use . Neither spells nor psionics can penetrate the woods and those that enter are not heard from again .

title: Weathertell
description: Weathertell Weathertell was an arcane divination spell that allowed the caster to foresee natural weather conditions a few hours ahead . Effects . This spell had to be cast outdoors where the caster was able to see and hear the current weather conditions .
description_long: Weathertell Weathertell was an arcane divination spell that allowed the caster to foresee natural weather conditions a few hours ahead . Effects . This spell had to be cast outdoors where the caster was able to see and hear the current weather conditions . When cast , he or she instantly gained knowledge of prevailing wind direction and speed , precipitation type and strength , and any unusual weather conditions ( such as cyclones ) that would naturally occur in the very near future . The extent of this knowledge was the surrounding area of the caster and a number of hours into the future equal to the caster ' s level . The path of phenomena such as tornadoes could not be predicted accurately enough to know where they would touch down or what they would hit , just whether or not they would appear in the general area . Only natural weather could be predicted by this spell . Any manipulation by other magical forces could not be foreseen . Components . This spell required verbal , somatic , and unspecified material components . History . This spell was associated with the pirates roaming the Sea of Fallen Stars .

title: Weave
description: Weave The Weave , controlled by Mystryl or one of her successors , was a way through which raw magic was accessed , tapped into and used by casters of magic . The Weave was the way in which magic presented itself to beings for their use , and it flowed throughout the world , touching almost every corner of existence , with exception of dead - magic zone s . The Weave coexisted with the Shadow Weave .
description_long: Weave The Weave , controlled by Mystryl or one of her successors , was a way through which raw magic was accessed , tapped into and used by casters of magic . The Weave was the way in which magic presented itself to beings for their use , and it flowed throughout the world , touching almost every corner of existence , with exception of dead - magic zone s . The Weave coexisted with the Shadow Weave . The Weave did not exist on Abeir , making casting magic in that world more difficult than in Toril . Nature of the Weave . The Weave was considered many things , including Mystra ' s body , the source of magic , all the studies of casters , arcane and divine alike , and the many energies and forces that existed around the plane s . Many saw it as a " fabric " on which magic was " drawn " , and damaging the fabric caused magic to go awry . Some textbooks deliberately falsified the nature of the Weave , as an attempt to limit the knowledge associated with spellcasting . In the years after the Spellplague , the term Weave also became a synonym of the use of magic . Casting a spell was equivalent to telling the Weave to rearrange itself to create an effect .

title: Web
description: Web Web , formerly known as Shan ' s web , was a spell that filled an area with sticky spider - webs that ensnared those caught in the area . Users . The " web " spell could be learned and cast by wizard s and sorcerer s with access to the conjuration school of magic .
description_long: Web Web , formerly known as Shan ' s web , was a spell that filled an area with sticky spider - webs that ensnared those caught in the area . Users . The " web " spell could be learned and cast by wizard s and sorcerer s with access to the conjuration school of magic . In the time of Netheril , it could be cast by arcanist s of the Inventive specialization . In Zakhara , elemental mage s and sorcerers could learn it as part of the universal province . Effects . After the Year of Wild Magic , 1372 DR , a caster could , up to a distance of 100 ft ( 30 m ) or more depending on their level , create a multi - layered collection of strong and sticky strands or fibers . These were rather like spider webs , but were much thicker and tougher . These spread over an area 40 ft ( 12 m ) wide , but the strands had to be anchored to stable , diametrically opposite objects ; a part of the " web " that was not so anchored would collapse in on itself and vanish . These strands entangled creatures caught within the " web " , hampering their movements . One had to either force their way or slip nimbly between the strands in order to pass through them .

title: Web - of - bells
description: Web - of - bells A web - of - bells was a costume originating from Thay typically worn by dancers . History . When Volothamp Geddarm visited Elgath ' s Provisions in Archenbridge in Archendale , in the Dalelands , he tested proprietor Elgath ' s claim that he could locate any desired item for sale within a day by requesting a Thayan web - of - bells dancer ' s costume .
description_long: Web - of - bells A web - of - bells was a costume originating from Thay typically worn by dancers . History . When Volothamp Geddarm visited Elgath ' s Provisions in Archenbridge in Archendale , in the Dalelands , he tested proprietor Elgath ' s claim that he could locate any desired item for sale within a day by requesting a Thayan web - of - bells dancer ' s costume . By the next meal that day , Elgath had found a Sembian collector willing to part with a spare , and even offered to have a fast rider collect it . Volo declined on the basis that it was not his size or shape .

title: Webb Mossfeld
description: Webb Mossfeld Webb Mossfeld was a male human of the village of West Harbor on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . Activities . Webb , like his brothers , was the member of West Harbor militia .
description_long: Webb Mossfeld Webb Mossfeld was a male human of the village of West Harbor on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . Activities . Webb , like his brothers , was the member of West Harbor militia . History . Webb was the bully of the West Harbor , who would tease Kalach - Cha , Bevil Starling and Amie Fern . They were the champions of the Harvest Fair several years . During the Harvest Fair , Webb and his brothers were the winners of the Harvest Brawl . The Kalach - Cha , after defeating the Lannon siblings , would ' ve faced him and his brothers , Wyl and Ward . If the Kalach - Cha , Amie and Bevil were defeated , they could ' ve asked Merring for a rematch or submit that Mossfelds won . During the attack of bladeling s and duergar , the Kalach - Cha could ' ve encountered Webb , who would fight the attackers . Once finished , he could ' ve been asked to go to the field to defend the town . When the Kalach - Cha returns to the village to craft the Sword of Gith , he / she encountered Ward and his brothers . However , it was an ambush , as they were shadows .

title: Webstone
description: Webstone Webstone was the " Realms " name for spiderweb obsidian . Description . This ornamental stone was an obsidian variety formed by small pieces of the stone cemented together by heat and pressure in a globular mass , the joints showing as wispy , web - like lines .
description_long: Webstone Webstone was the " Realms " name for spiderweb obsidian . Description . This ornamental stone was an obsidian variety formed by small pieces of the stone cemented together by heat and pressure in a globular mass , the joints showing as wispy , web - like lines . It was usually black , the seams sometimes showing white , but brown , reddish brown , and rust - red varieties with lighter - hued web lines were known . A typical stone had a base value of 10 gp . Powers . This stone offered a wearer protection against airborne pollutants and gasses if worn in direct contact with the skin . Some jewelers fashioned tumbled webstones into armpit bands that were worn around the shoulder to maintain skin contact . When the wearer was exposed to poisonous gas , smoke , or airborne spores , the webstone would vaporize in irregular bursts , protecting the wearer from the harmful effects until the supply was depleted or until the exposure ended . Unfortunately the efficacy of this protection varied greatly — from complete protection to no protection at all — between samples of webstone , seemingly at random . This unreliability prevented webstone from having a much higher value .

title: Weeping Desert
description: Weeping Desert The Weeping Desert was a desert located in the Haunted Lands of interior Zakhara . It was a sandy expanse running from limestone hills at the base of the Furrowed Mountains to massive dunes separating it from the Burning Land . By 1367 DR , the Weeping Desert earned its name from the prevalence of undead spirits , such as ghost s , ghost horses , and the undead giant s known as rom .
description_long: Weeping Desert The Weeping Desert was a desert located in the Haunted Lands of interior Zakhara . It was a sandy expanse running from limestone hills at the base of the Furrowed Mountains to massive dunes separating it from the Burning Land . By 1367 DR , the Weeping Desert earned its name from the prevalence of undead spirits , such as ghost s , ghost horses , and the undead giant s known as rom . A large set of ruins was believed to be the source of the keening sounds that kept travelers awake at night . A large clan of rom was hidden beneath this ruin at the magical underground spring known as the Well of Despair .

title: Weeping Friars
description: Weeping Friars The Weeping Friars were an informal group of quasi - ascetics known throughout most of the Savage Frontier . They claimed to believe that there was only a finite amount of pain and suffering in the world , and the more suffering they took upon themselves , the less suffering others would have to endure . They would offer to undergo suffering on a person ' s behalf in exchange for money or items , usually taking the form of alcohol or trinkets .
description_long: Weeping Friars The Weeping Friars were an informal group of quasi - ascetics known throughout most of the Savage Frontier . They claimed to believe that there was only a finite amount of pain and suffering in the world , and the more suffering they took upon themselves , the less suffering others would have to endure . They would offer to undergo suffering on a person ' s behalf in exchange for money or items , usually taking the form of alcohol or trinkets . To outsiders , they were generally regarded as masochists . Drizzt Do ' Urden traveled with the group for a while , acting as a bodyguard and companion . They were the ones who gave him the idea of traveling to Ten Towns , Brother Jankin , being drunk at the time , mentioned it as a place where rogues can find their place . When the Quickling Tephanis trapped them in Hephaestus ' s lair , Drizzt was the one to save them , however once the drow left the group for the Dale , they were tracked down by Roddy McGristle who tortured them all for Drizzt ' s whereabouts . Drizzt later discovered that the friars were followers of Ilmater . Members . From Drizzt Do ' Urden ' s party there were five members in total .

title: Weeping Garden
description: Weeping Garden The Weeping Garden was a planar location in the House of the Triad , provided by the god Ilmater to provide relief and aid to his most dedicated followers . Access . Only the god Ilmater allowed entry to the Weeping Garden , and he allowed only a select and faithful few , those who demonstrated supreme dedication and selflessness in his name and were themselves in great need of relief .
description_long: Weeping Garden The Weeping Garden was a planar location in the House of the Triad , provided by the god Ilmater to provide relief and aid to his most dedicated followers . Access . Only the god Ilmater allowed entry to the Weeping Garden , and he allowed only a select and faithful few , those who demonstrated supreme dedication and selflessness in his name and were themselves in great need of relief . Such people were priests , knights , monks or other devout worshipers of Ilmater , and they had to be in a crisis or grim situation , such as facing overwhelming odds or too many people in need of help . Some examples were of an Ilmatari defending helpless people against an enormous force , or exhausting themself and expending all their magic to heal a plague , or standing against powerful followers of Loviatar , or travelling the length of Faerûn in a kind and just quest , all without regard for danger or self - advancement . At such rare times , Ilmater provided them with relief and sanctuary in the Garden , though ultimately no release from their task . For the blessed Ilmatari , to be invited into the Weeping Garden was a tremendous honor as well a great responsibility .

title: Weeping Rock ( Ilmater )
description: Weeping Rock ( Ilmater ) Weeping Rock was a site related to the faith of Ilmater the Crying God . In the autumn of the Year of the Groaning Hart , 1267 DR , Weeping Rock was the site of a bloody battle between feuding factions of the church of Ilmater . The holy war had broken out around 1265 DR when Archsufferer Bloirt Waelarn of the House of the Broken God in Keltar had denounced his fellow Ilmatari priests of the House of Holy Suffering in Mussum for refusing to relinquish the " Tome of Torment " , the holiest book of the faith .
description_long: Weeping Rock ( Ilmater ) Weeping Rock was a site related to the faith of Ilmater the Crying God . In the autumn of the Year of the Groaning Hart , 1267 DR , Weeping Rock was the site of a bloody battle between feuding factions of the church of Ilmater . The holy war had broken out around 1265 DR when Archsufferer Bloirt Waelarn of the House of the Broken God in Keltar had denounced his fellow Ilmatari priests of the House of Holy Suffering in Mussum for refusing to relinquish the " Tome of Torment " , the holiest book of the faith . On one side were the Mussum priests and the Companions of the Noble Heart paladin order , and on the other were Waelarn , his followers , the Holy Warriors of Suffering , and the Knights of the Bleeding Shield .

title: Weeping Unicorn
description: Weeping Unicorn The Weeping Unicorn was an inn and tavern in the city of Calaunt in the Vast , operating around 1358 DR . It was a quiet and comfortable place located by the docks , and of good quality for moderate prices . It was oft - used to do business by villainous sorts .
description_long: Weeping Unicorn The Weeping Unicorn was an inn and tavern in the city of Calaunt in the Vast , operating around 1358 DR . It was a quiet and comfortable place located by the docks , and of good quality for moderate prices . It was oft - used to do business by villainous sorts . The house rule was strictly " no fighting " , which all patrons obeyed , as those who didn ' t tended to run into a cockatrice . Their petrified forms adorned the cellar .

title: Weeping War
description: Weeping War The Weeping War was a battle that culminated on 15 Flamerule , 714 DR , in which the Akh ' Velahr ( the army of Cormanthor ) were defeated by the invading demonic forces named the Army of Darkness , leading to the fall of the elven city of Myth Drannor , the greatest and most powerful bastion of civilisation by far at the time . Origins . The exact power responsible for the original demonic summoning is unknown , but it is believed to have been a flind or orc shaman , or a human archmage .
description_long: Weeping War The Weeping War was a battle that culminated on 15 Flamerule , 714 DR , in which the Akh ' Velahr ( the army of Cormanthor ) were defeated by the invading demonic forces named the Army of Darkness , leading to the fall of the elven city of Myth Drannor , the greatest and most powerful bastion of civilisation by far at the time . Origins . The exact power responsible for the original demonic summoning is unknown , but it is believed to have been a flind or orc shaman , or a human archmage . This unknown individual summoned yugoloth s to raid the lands of the Dragonreach , but Aulmpiter , Gaulguth and Malimshaer broke free of their master ' s control and rounded up huge numbers of goblinkin in the surrounding area . Helmgrove . Word of this large army reached Captain Fflar of Myth Drannor , who set a watchpost north of the city at Helmgrove , appointing the company named the Shield of Myth Drannor to it . The entire company was destroyed by the demonic forces . Burnt Ridge . A second pre - battle stand was made at Burnt Ridge , where hundreds of the defending wizard s were killed . Evacuation .

title: Weeping Willow Inn
description: Weeping Willow Inn Weeping Willow Inn was an inn in the Mere of Dead Men . It was the only inn for miles around , so was a frequent stop for travellers of that part of the High Road . Location .
description_long: Weeping Willow Inn Weeping Willow Inn was an inn in the Mere of Dead Men . It was the only inn for miles around , so was a frequent stop for travellers of that part of the High Road . Location . The Weeping Willow Inn was located between West Harbor and Fort Locke . Structure . Like most swamp buildings , this inn was built from wood and stone . Interior . The inn is built in two layers : the first one had a bar , while the second floor had rooms for travelers to rest . History . The Weeping Willow had gained a certain unpleasant reputation amongst its visitors . Some said it was the pine forest , that the owner had built it too close to the trees and the wild crept in on snowy nights , others that a young girl had been strangled under the floorboards of the cellar . Either way , it was a desolate place : the landlord spent most of his evenings drinking alone in the bar , and guests were few and far between on the hard , winter - bound road . If any traveler did stumble into the warmth of the rooms , caught out in the storm , you could be sure that there was more on his mind than a good night ' s sleep .

title: Weeping Wyvern
description: Weeping Wyvern The Weeping Wyvern was an inn in the city of Tantras in the Vast . Location . The Weeping Wyvern lay close by the eastern wall of Tantras , at the end of Stumble Street .
description_long: Weeping Wyvern The Weeping Wyvern was an inn in the city of Tantras in the Vast . Location . The Weeping Wyvern lay close by the eastern wall of Tantras , at the end of Stumble Street . Description . It was a large , good - quality establishment , with high prices but often crowded . History . The Weeping Wyvern was still fairly new in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR . During the Time of Troubles of that year , it avoided being commandeered by the Guard of Tantras for use as an army barracks .

title: Weet Greenspen
description: Weet Greenspen Weet Greenspen was an alchemist in the Moonsea . History . During of the Rage of Demons , the doppelganger Tak , posing as the Doctor Jubal of the wandering Doctor Jubal ' s Carnival of Curiosities , kidnapped Weet and forced her to brew alchemical items .
description_long: Weet Greenspen Weet Greenspen was an alchemist in the Moonsea . History . During of the Rage of Demons , the doppelganger Tak , posing as the Doctor Jubal of the wandering Doctor Jubal ' s Carnival of Curiosities , kidnapped Weet and forced her to brew alchemical items . Weet was imprisoned inside the mirror maze together with Berl Cuttler , Aelia , the true Doctor Jubal , and others .

title: Wei Do Peak
description: Wei Do Peak Wei Do Peak was a mountain in the eastern Vorkani Mountains in the realm of Koryo in Kara - Tur . Each year after he took the throne in the 1350s DR , a three - day - long ceremony was held on Wei Do Peak to honor King Wanang Sun and his new dynasty . Many monk s and shukenja attended the festival , and bestowed blessings on the king and his court .
description_long: Wei Do Peak Wei Do Peak was a mountain in the eastern Vorkani Mountains in the realm of Koryo in Kara - Tur . Each year after he took the throne in the 1350s DR , a three - day - long ceremony was held on Wei Do Peak to honor King Wanang Sun and his new dynasty . Many monk s and shukenja attended the festival , and bestowed blessings on the king and his court . It culminated with the king himself ritually beheading the most infamous criminal in the kingdom ' s prisons . This act symbolized his power to defeat evil in the kingdom . It was rumored that when the king wielded the Golden Sword of Ammatok to do this duty , a spirit of the Celestial Heavens would appear beside him and consecrate his rule under their guidance .

title: Weighed in the balance
description: Weighed in the balance Weighed in the balance is a necromancy spell unique to cleric s with the Balance domain . It harms or heals creatures within 30 feet . Effect .
description_long: Weighed in the balance Weighed in the balance is a necromancy spell unique to cleric s with the Balance domain . It harms or heals creatures within 30 feet . Effect . This spell harms or heals creatures within its area based on their alignment s and life status , as given in the table below . The effect does the most harm to those creatures most extreme in alignment and most out of balance with the natural world ( the baselines being true neutral and living creatures , respectively ) .

title: Weighty chest
description: Weighty chest Weighty chest was an alteration spell that made an object extremely difficult to move when touched by someone other than the caster . Effects . The caster had to touch the object to cast this spell .
description_long: Weighty chest Weighty chest was an alteration spell that made an object extremely difficult to move when touched by someone other than the caster . Effects . The caster had to touch the object to cast this spell . The object could be a chest , a book , a box , a present , a small chest of drawers , a bookshelf , or any non - living movable object that fit in a 5 ft ( 1 . 5 m ) cube . Whenever one or more creatures touched the object , the weight of the object increased in proportion to ( and at least double ) the combined weight of all those touching it . Unless a creature had exceptional strength , it would not be able to lift the enchanted object for very long or at all . This spell lasted at least one day and more advanced priests could make it last many more days . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , his spell required a small lead ball to cast .

title: Weir
description: Weir Weir trees , also known as weirwoods , were rare trees in Faerûn . Description . Weir trees resembled oak s and could grow huge in their later years .
description_long: Weir Weir trees , also known as weirwoods , were rare trees in Faerûn . Description . Weir trees resembled oak s and could grow huge in their later years . The most remarkable feature of the weir tree was its leaves : they were silvery brown on the top and velvety black on the bottom . Any weirwood item brought into a magically - lit area would continue to glow for some time after leaving that area . Usage . The wood was not naturally flammable , making it excellent for construction purposes . ( Living trees were more fire resistant than harvested wood , however . ) It was also often used for making musical instruments , especially lute s , harp s , birdpipe s , and longhorn s , because of its lovely sound . Alustriel Silverhand created no more than 12 staves out of weirwood that were known as " lesser staves of Silverymoon " . Weirwood could be used to craft a " thyrsus of the druid " . Locations . Weir trees were found mainly far into large , old forests . Most weir trees were protected by protectors of the forest , such as dryad s , treant s , ranger s , or druid s .

title: Weird
description: Weird Weird , originally known as Trebbe ' s weird , was an illusion spell that created a deadly phantasm to kill or injure multiple victims . Effects . This spell functioned in the same manner as " phantasmal killer " , except that it could affect more than one target .
description_long: Weird Weird , originally known as Trebbe ' s weird , was an illusion spell that created a deadly phantasm to kill or injure multiple victims . Effects . This spell functioned in the same manner as " phantasmal killer " , except that it could affect more than one target . The older version of this spell could affect all creatures within a 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) radius . After the Time of Troubles and before the Spellplague , the radius shrank to 15 ft ( 4 . 6 m ) . Against this version of the spell , subjects with strong constitutions could survive the shock to their system , but would still be harmed and stunned for several seconds . They would also be weakened physically for ten minutes . After the Second Sundering , the radius grew to 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) and the victims were continually assaulted for one minute by their worst nightmare beasts until they individually managed to disbelieve the illusion , the spell expired , or they died of psychic damage . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell . History . This spell was invented by the Netherese arcanist Trebbe in – 2240 DR ( 1619 NY , during Netheril ' s Silver Age ) .

title: Weirdstone
description: Weirdstone Weirdstones were powerful magic al trinkets that impeded many spells and abilities which allowed extradimensional movement and scry ing . Description . Though made of cut glass , a " weirdstone " appeared to be a faceted diamond about the size of a humanoid ' s clenched fist .
description_long: Weirdstone Weirdstones were powerful magic al trinkets that impeded many spells and abilities which allowed extradimensional movement and scry ing . Description . Though made of cut glass , a " weirdstone " appeared to be a faceted diamond about the size of a humanoid ' s clenched fist . When active , it pulsed with white light . Abilities . When placed on a solid , flat surface , the " weirdstone " would float three feet into the air and began glowing . While in such a state , it rendered all divination magic unable to detect anything within a six mile radius ( which included six miles above and beneath it ) . Extraplanar movement , movement via plants with druid ic magic and the natural abilities of some creatures such as xorn s , would not function within that same area . All such abilities were disabled , whether magical , supernatural or psionic in nature . Deactivating a " weirdstone " was as simple as activating it - one merely needed to snatch the item from out of the air and place it inside a container or onto a less regular surface , just as long as it wasn ' t flat enough to activate it again .

title: Weldrarn Orblin
description: Weldrarn Orblin Weldrarn Orblin was a magister who held the title for less than a year in 242 DR . Personality . Weldrarn was an arrogant and brutal wizard .
description_long: Weldrarn Orblin Weldrarn Orblin was a magister who held the title for less than a year in 242 DR . Personality . Weldrarn was an arrogant and brutal wizard . History . Weldrarn ' s magical skills were honed during a series of covert wars between rival clans in Calimshan . After assuming the title of Magister , he spent much of his time hiding in various castles , hording an arsenal of magic that would allow him to obliterate any challenger . He was rumored to have been working on a special chain of magic that would allow him to hurls dozens of spells at once with minimal effort . It was during this period of research when he was challenged by Tsanbrin Aulmeroevler , who was Weldrarn ' s third challenge to his title . Weldrarn perished because of his own folly when a tower collapsed on him during their duel .

title: Well of Dragons
description: Well of Dragons The Well of Dragons was a citadel operated by the Cult of the Dragon in the canyonlands near the Sunset Mountains . The site was a legendary graveyard of dragons and historically many dragons would travel to the Well of Dragons to die . Cultists freed the shadow dragon guardian of the site and built a citadel where they carried out their activities which mainly involved attempting to transform dragon s into dracoliches .
description_long: Well of Dragons The Well of Dragons was a citadel operated by the Cult of the Dragon in the canyonlands near the Sunset Mountains . The site was a legendary graveyard of dragons and historically many dragons would travel to the Well of Dragons to die . Cultists freed the shadow dragon guardian of the site and built a citadel where they carried out their activities which mainly involved attempting to transform dragon s into dracoliches . The citadel was well defended as it often came under attack from treasure hunters and dragons angered by the cult ' s beliefs . In the late 15th century DR the citadel was co - ruled by a death knight named Naergoth Bladelord and a lich known as Vargo the Faceless .

title: Well of Kashan
description: Well of Kashan The Well of Kashan was an enchanted oasis found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate , in 1367 DR . Geography . The Well of Kashan was found somewhere within the Genies ' Anvil of the High Desert near a stone called the Hand of Makti .
description_long: Well of Kashan The Well of Kashan was an enchanted oasis found in Zakhara , the Land of Fate , in 1367 DR . Geography . The Well of Kashan was found somewhere within the Genies ' Anvil of the High Desert near a stone called the Hand of Makti . Description . The Well was rumored to be extremely deep . Lush gardens and magical groves were said to exist at its bottom . History . Amir Bouladin al - Mutajalli stored all of the wealth of the jann of the House of Sihr at the bottom of the well . The special password needed to view the wonders at the bottom of the well was known only by him and his eldest daughter , Jamala .

title: Well of the Cloven Rock
description: Well of the Cloven Rock The Well of the Cloven Rock was a popular well and oasis in Anauroch . Geography . The oasis was located in the Hills of Scent in the Sword , about 60 miles ( 97 kilometers ) east of Elah ' zad .
description_long: Well of the Cloven Rock The Well of the Cloven Rock was a popular well and oasis in Anauroch . Geography . The oasis was located in the Hills of Scent in the Sword , about 60 miles ( 97 kilometers ) east of Elah ' zad . The oasis consisted of a large , crescent - shaped lake , surrounded by many varieties of trees , within a grass - filled , bowl - shaped valley in the hills . The lake was fed by a powerful spring that gushed form from a cleft in a large rock in the center of the meadow . At the end of the meadow , the lake drained into a tiny stream that circled the perimeter of the valley . A well was also here , from before the spring burst forth . Flora and Fauna . Lion s roamed the area and lived near the oasis when not hunting in the Hills of Scent . Inhabitants . The oasis and well were popular among the Bedine tribes . When they encamped here , they always drove away the lions and then posted pairs of guards armed with spear s , bow s , and sword s to keep the tribe safe .

title: Wellspring Endless
description: Wellspring Endless The Wellspring Endless was a legendary pool said to exist somewhere in the Forest of Mir . By 1370 DR , it had still not been discovered , if it had ever existed at all . Description .
description_long: Wellspring Endless The Wellspring Endless was a legendary pool said to exist somewhere in the Forest of Mir . By 1370 DR , it had still not been discovered , if it had ever existed at all . Description . The pool was said to by a crystal - blue color and was surrounded by a ring of white stones . It was fed by a subterranean spring . The legends said that if one were to drink from the pool , she or he would live forever . Others warned that the " eternal life " granted by the pool left one in a nightmare - filled state of unconsciousness .

title: Welsea Parenthe
description: Welsea Parenthe Welsea Parenthe was a vampire sorcerer and Zhentarim agent in Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Welsea normally stick to the shadows , but when forced by circumstances to go into the open , she tried to conceal her features .
description_long: Welsea Parenthe Welsea Parenthe was a vampire sorcerer and Zhentarim agent in Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Welsea normally stick to the shadows , but when forced by circumstances to go into the open , she tried to conceal her features . She spoke clearly , carefully , and quietly , never raising her voice . Welsea never discussed her undead condition . History . Welsea one of the Zhent delegates in the resistance against Vorgansharax . She helped the Lord Sage of Phlan to send adventurers to explore Yarash ' s pyramid .

title: Welwyn Tracegar
description: Welwyn Tracegar Welwyn Tracegar was a War Wizard of Cormyr . History . Around 1479 DR , Welwyn was among the many War Wizards sent to besiege the Stormserpent Towers near Suzail .
description_long: Welwyn Tracegar Welwyn Tracegar was a War Wizard of Cormyr . History . Around 1479 DR , Welwyn was among the many War Wizards sent to besiege the Stormserpent Towers near Suzail . He commented about the deaths of many nobles that had just happened in Suzail . During the later battle at the house of Larak Dardulkyn against the Elminster Aumar ' s party Glathra Barcantle nominated him battle master . For a time Welwyn managed to imprisoned Elminster ' s party .

title: Wemic
description: Wemic A wemic was a creature with the upper body of a humanoid and the lower body of a lion . Like centaur s , they were considered " taur ic " creatures . Wemics were found primarily in The Shaar , but also in many other lands of Faerûn .
description_long: Wemic A wemic was a creature with the upper body of a humanoid and the lower body of a lion . Like centaur s , they were considered " taur ic " creatures . Wemics were found primarily in The Shaar , but also in many other lands of Faerûn . Description . Wemics were larger and stronger than human s . A wemic could make great leaps with a running start . Their front claws were sharp , and they could fight with both claws and weapons at the same time . They could also rake with their back claws . They had keen eyesight and hearing . The human part of a wemic had feline characteristics around his or her eyes and ears , and perhaps in the nose and teeth as well . Males were generally represented as having long mane - like hair . Society . Wemics were excellent hunters and fighters . They did not make settled homes , but generally followed the herds they hunted for food . A nomadic folk , wemics were often represented as barbaric , illiterate , and uncivilized ; they were famous for being highly superstitious . Others would describe wemics as nature - oriented people with a rich tradition of oral history . They live close to the earth and were in tune with its magical forces .

title: Wenda Wildeye
description: Wenda Wildeye Wenda Wildeye was an infamous bandit and mage operating out of the Serpent Valley in the Utter East during the time of the Bloodforge Wars ( 648 – 657 DR ) . Wenda Wildeye used the Serpent Valley as a hideout and mustering area . While preparing for another raid , the commander of the Legendary Campaign came to put an end to the banditry .
description_long: Wenda Wildeye Wenda Wildeye was an infamous bandit and mage operating out of the Serpent Valley in the Utter East during the time of the Bloodforge Wars ( 648 – 657 DR ) . Wenda Wildeye used the Serpent Valley as a hideout and mustering area . While preparing for another raid , the commander of the Legendary Campaign came to put an end to the banditry .

title: Wendonai
description: Wendonai Wendonai was a balor lord who in - 11500 DR was tasked by Lolth with seducing the Sethomiir clan , rulers of the Ilythiiri , into her worship and granting them evil magics . He succeeded and was probably the greatest ( but by no means the only ) influence on the fall of the dark elves . After the Descent , Wendonai continued his work , acting as an adviser , tutor , and sometimes consort to the most powerful drow Matron Mother s .
description_long: Wendonai Wendonai was a balor lord who in - 11500 DR was tasked by Lolth with seducing the Sethomiir clan , rulers of the Ilythiiri , into her worship and granting them evil magics . He succeeded and was probably the greatest ( but by no means the only ) influence on the fall of the dark elves . After the Descent , Wendonai continued his work , acting as an adviser , tutor , and sometimes consort to the most powerful drow Matron Mother s . He tried to claim a little power for himself by leading a successful drow and duergar attack against the Elven Court in - 4400 DR , called the Dark Court Slaughter . Wendonai ' s efforts at personal growth over the next two millennia earned Lolth ' s ire as she had no intention to let the drow return to the surface . Lolth withdrew her favor from the demon in - 2549 DR and the Matrons followed suit . Wendonai then allied himself with Eltab , serving as his emissary to Faerûn for several centuries . In - 623 DR , however , he was summoned by a Nar demonbinder but was soon banished by an incredibly powerful cleric of Horus - Re for 2000 years .

title: Wengwater
description: Wengwater The Wengwater was a tributary of Lake Weng in Amn . Description . The river was fast and had dangerous rapids .
description_long: Wengwater The Wengwater was a tributary of Lake Weng in Amn . Description . The river was fast and had dangerous rapids . Each year , it flooded , which left small ponds north of the town of Amnwater . Geography . The Wengwater began in the Cloud Peaks and flowed past Amnwater until it poured into Lake Weng from the east . History . Every few years , someone tried to run the rapids of the Wengwater in a feat of daring , but as of 1370 DR , no one in 300 years had successfully navigated them .

title: Wenslan Amthur
description: Wenslan Amthur Wenslan Amthur was a priest of Deneir at the temple of Deneir in the city of Procampur in the Vast . History . By " circa " 1361 DR , Amthur was Prelate or Hierarch of the temple of Deneir in Procampur , where he had the title of High Scrivener .
description_long: Wenslan Amthur Wenslan Amthur was a priest of Deneir at the temple of Deneir in the city of Procampur in the Vast . History . By " circa " 1361 DR , Amthur was Prelate or Hierarch of the temple of Deneir in Procampur , where he had the title of High Scrivener . Amthur permitted a historian writing a history of the Tuigan Horde to examine the temple ' s complete copy of Vilhiard ' s " A Discovery of the World " . The High Scrivener praised the lama Koja of Khazari , who was a guest at his temple in the Year of the Helm , 1362 DR , for his wisdom and knowledge . The priest Foxe promised to have the High Scrivener distribute Koja ' s new work , " A History of the Tuigan " , to every other temple of Deneir .

title: Wenszrin
description: Wenszrin Wenszrin was a doppelganger and a baron of the city of Calaunt in the Vast in 1358 DR . Activities . Together with Uthorn , a fellow baron and doppelganger , Wenszrin commanded the city ' s standing army , The Teeth of Calaunt , with all warcaptains reporting to the two barons .
description_long: Wenszrin Wenszrin was a doppelganger and a baron of the city of Calaunt in the Vast in 1358 DR . Activities . Together with Uthorn , a fellow baron and doppelganger , Wenszrin commanded the city ' s standing army , The Teeth of Calaunt , with all warcaptains reporting to the two barons . The pair also commanded all mercenary forces the city hired to supplement its military . Wenszrin and Uthorn also served as spies and scouts for the Merchant Duke s of Calaunt . However , they were under the magical control of Duke Iritar the Dark . Possessions . Wenszrin was supplied with a variety of magical item s for protection . Description . Wenszrin normally adopted the appearance of a plain , veteran warrior .

title: Werebear
description: Werebear A werebear is a shapeshifter able to transform into a bear . Most werebears are good - natured and desire to help others in their communities . They see themselves as the guardians standing between the natural world and civilization .
description_long: Werebear A werebear is a shapeshifter able to transform into a bear . Most werebears are good - natured and desire to help others in their communities . They see themselves as the guardians standing between the natural world and civilization . Their animal instincts guide them to protect the splendors of nature , while their humanoid minds tell them to help travelers and provide aid to the weak . Description . Werebears are humanoids that can transform themselves into large brown bears . Their humanoid forms are often large and heavily - muscled . Werebears dress in simple garments that can be easily removed .
