Their children are born appearing humanoid until they turn eight , at which point they will gain the ability to transforms in large shaggy bears .

title: Wereboar
description: Wereboar A wereboar was a humanoid or giant lycanthrope that was bitten by another wereboar . Wereboars were often of neutral alignment but hunted anything for food . Any humanoid or giant that survived a wereboar ' s bite could be infected with the curse , thus becoming a wereboar themselves .
description_long: Wereboar A wereboar was a humanoid or giant lycanthrope that was bitten by another wereboar . Wereboars were often of neutral alignment but hunted anything for food . Any humanoid or giant that survived a wereboar ' s bite could be infected with the curse , thus becoming a wereboar themselves . Wereboars were aggressive and unfriendly creatures . They would often provoke fights for the sake of fighting . While mean - spirited , they were not necessarily evil in nature . Physical Appearance . A wereboar in humanoid form tends to be a stocky , muscular individual of average height . Wereboars have three forms , a boar , the normal form of whatever creature is cursed , and that of a hybrid host / boar mix .

title: Werecrocodile
description: Werecrocodile Werecrocodiles were lycanthrope s whose animal form was that of a crocodile . They preferred to live in swamps or flooded plains and had a taste for human flesh . In human form , werecrocodiles often used a khopesh sword ; in crocodile form they preferred to grab their opponent and hold it underwater .
description_long: Werecrocodile Werecrocodiles were lycanthrope s whose animal form was that of a crocodile . They preferred to live in swamps or flooded plains and had a taste for human flesh . In human form , werecrocodiles often used a khopesh sword ; in crocodile form they preferred to grab their opponent and hold it underwater . Werecrocodiles might also assume a hybrid form with the head of a crocodile and body of a muscular human . They were powerful hunters and were feared throughout many lands .

title: Werefox
description: Werefox Werefoxes a type of lycanthrope that are mostly female , thus they are often referred to as foxwomen . Description . In humanoid form , all foxwomen have lustrous silver hair sporting a widow ' s peak , appearing incredibly attractive .
description_long: Werefox Werefoxes a type of lycanthrope that are mostly female , thus they are often referred to as foxwomen . Description . In humanoid form , all foxwomen have lustrous silver hair sporting a widow ' s peak , appearing incredibly attractive . The rare male werefox has a similar appearance but their hair may vary from silver , black , or red . Ecology . Personality . Often dwelling in secluded woodlands , werefox are rarely seen in numbers as they prefer to act alone . Their only purpose is pampering themselves and making sure they have an heir or heiress to raise . In hybrid form , werefoxes use their claws and their poisonous bite and sometimes longsword s . They rarely use their animal form for battle , but then they may use their claws .

title: Weregund
description: Weregund Weregund was a trader in who owned the General Store in the town of Shadowdale . Biography . Weregund was a longstanding plant of Zhentil Keep in the town .
description_long: Weregund Weregund was a trader in who owned the General Store in the town of Shadowdale . Biography . Weregund was a longstanding plant of Zhentil Keep in the town . Although his stock was the more limited of the two stores in town , his was considered the town ' s trading post as his store larger and he was the one who regularly traded with passing caravans . During the Zhentarim occupation of Shadowdale in 1374 DR , Weregund ' s identity as a spy was only known to Scyllua Darkhope and Eregul the Freestave . Weregund set up an underground resistance movement called the Free Shadowdale Alliance that merely served to allow the trader to pass on any plans of action against the occupying force to the Zhentarim . Description . The large trader was known to walk with a limp . Personality . Weregund had a reputation for greed and cowardice but his neighbours also erroneously believed him to be loyal to Shadowdale , marking him as an adept liar . Relationships . The merchant had a wife Meershand , a son Dabragund , and a daughter Dletagund .

title: Werehyena
description: Werehyena Werehyenas were humans in Zakhara who could transform into a hyena - like form . Description . Most werehyenas were male and usually had long shaggy hair .
description_long: Werehyena Werehyenas were humans in Zakhara who could transform into a hyena - like form . Description . Most werehyenas were male and usually had long shaggy hair . The long hair concealed a second mouth located at the base of the skull . Werehyenas went to great lengths to keep this hidden . Their hyena form was usually 6 feet ( 1 . 8 m ) long and had golden fur on their back with black fur on their belly and feet . Combat . In human form , werehyenas used their special charm powers to avoid combat . In canine form , werehyenas attacked with a savage bite that could lock on to a victim . Magical or iron weapons were needed to harm a werehyena . These creatures were also immune to enchantment or charm spell s . Fire was a werehyena ' s greatest fear . Flaming torches would keep them at bay . Habitat / Society . Werehyenas traveled in packs of up to a dozen individuals . A dominant male made all of the decisions for the pack . Werehyenas mated for life , but only with members of their pack . While in human form , werehyenas often infiltrated villages and lured victims out to where the rest of the pack waited . Ecology . Werehyenas preyed on gullible humans whenever they could .

title: Werelion
description: Werelion Werelions were human s in Zakhara who could assume a lion form . Description . Werelions were usually thin and sinewy while in human form .
description_long: Werelion Werelions were human s in Zakhara who could assume a lion form . Description . Werelions were usually thin and sinewy while in human form . They had deep , melodious voices . Males typically had long curly hair of gold or brown . Females kept their hair cropped almost to the scalp . Both sexes were deeply tanned and well - muscled . Werelions did not have a half - human form . Combat . Werelions preferred ambush attacks whenever possible . They hunted in packs and communicated effectively through their roars . Werelions could strike with their front claws and use a special rake attack with their rear claws . Werelions could leap up to 60 ft ( 18 . 3 m ) when attacking . Habitat / Society . These creatures were social lycanthrope s . Prides usually had more female members than males . A female , or matriarch , always ruled a pride . Ecology . Occasionally , werelions served sabu lord s . They were known to strike deals with desert centaur s and settlements bordering plains . Unlike other large hunting cats , werelions often attacked humans . Werelions and weretiger s were bitter enemies .

title: Wererat
description: Wererat Wererats ( alternately known as ratmen ) are lycanthrope s common in urban areas . Wererats could transform into dire rat s . Physical Description .
description_long: Wererat Wererats ( alternately known as ratmen ) are lycanthrope s common in urban areas . Wererats could transform into dire rat s . Physical Description . A wererat in humanoid form tended to be a thin , wiry individual of shorter than average height . The eyes constantly darted around , and the nose and mouth may have twitched if he or she was excited . Males often have thin , ragged mustaches . The animal form of a wererat was that of a dire rat two feet long from nose to rump . In hybrid form , the wererat was shorter than in its human form and its head , torso and tail were those of a rat while its limbs were a little more humanoid in appearance . Culture . A wererat never lived alone if they could help it , though they did not tend to form strong interpersonal relationships beyond a pack mentality - love and marriage were almost alien concepts to them . They delighted in pitting their superior cunning against surface - dwellers , seeing the cities that tended to be above their lairs as hunting grounds where they could steal food and wealth by killing its inhabitants in an almost parasitical manner .

title: Weretiger
description: Weretiger Weretigers were usually female . They tended to hide from civilized society , assuming the role of witches or hermits in the wild . Many weretigers took the time to learn magical arts to enhance this façade .
description_long: Weretiger Weretigers were usually female . They tended to hide from civilized society , assuming the role of witches or hermits in the wild . Many weretigers took the time to learn magical arts to enhance this façade . This , unfortunately , had the effect of the lycanthrope being confused with a rakshasa . Appearance . Weretigers in humanoid form tended to be sleekly muscular , taller than average , and very agile . They didn ' t often wear clothes beyond jewelry due to the fact that even in " human " form they were covered in tiger - like fur . Appendix . title: Werewolf
description: Werewolf Werewolves are a type of shape - changing monster in Faerûn that are vulnerable to silver or enchanted weapons and can regenerate most wounds . Infected werewolves transform during the full moon involuntarily . Members of their race that are born with the curse can infect others and can control their shifting .
description_long: Werewolf Werewolves are a type of shape - changing monster in Faerûn that are vulnerable to silver or enchanted weapons and can regenerate most wounds . Infected werewolves transform during the full moon involuntarily . Members of their race that are born with the curse can infect others and can control their shifting . Selûne has a group of non - evil werewolves that worship her , though most lycanthrope s are drawn towards the worship of Malar . Werewolves are the most common type of lycanthropes in the world . They are found in all climates , both in the wild and hidden in civilization . Werewolf packs are organized similar to wolf packs , with a powerful alpha in command of the entire group . The moral and ethical outlook of the pack tends to follow that of the alpha .

title: Werond Torophar
description: Werond Torophar Werond Torophar was a teamster on the Sword Coast just before the Tyranny of Dragons . Personality . Werond was a quiet but romantic woman .
description_long: Werond Torophar Werond Torophar was a teamster on the Sword Coast just before the Tyranny of Dragons . Personality . Werond was a quiet but romantic woman . She mastered her animals like no other on the Trade Way , but at heart she was a starry - eyed romantic , capable of making strong men cry over her tales of unlucky past loves . History . Werond was one of the best teamsters in the Western Heartlands . At the start of the Tyranny of Dragons , in 1489 DR she acted as lead teamster for a great caravan that , unbeknownst to her , was full of agents of the Cult of the Dragon transporting treasures for the Hoard of the Dragon Queen .

title: Werz Saltbaron
description: Werz Saltbaron Werz Saltbaron was a duergar merchant in Gracklstugh during the Rage of Demons . Activities . Werz was a merchant with dealings with some corrupt officials like Gorglak .
description_long: Werz Saltbaron Werz Saltbaron was a duergar merchant in Gracklstugh during the Rage of Demons . Activities . Werz was a merchant with dealings with some corrupt officials like Gorglak . History . During the Rage of Demons , in Mantol - Derith , Werz met the deep gnome alchemist Kazook Pickshine and the two started a gem business behind their superiors ' backs . Later for unknown reasons , Werz was targeted by the notorious Empty - Scabbard Killers and asked for the help of an adventuring party that had escaped the drow of Velkynvelve .

title: Wesclodat
description: Wesclodat Wesclodat the Aged was a human Deneir an priest of unknown origins . Description . In his old age , Wesclodat retained only thin whisps of long , white hair , and a similar beard .
description_long: Wesclodat Wesclodat the Aged was a human Deneir an priest of unknown origins . Description . In his old age , Wesclodat retained only thin whisps of long , white hair , and a similar beard . His robe was dyed deep blue . Personality . Wesclodat kept a regular schedule , even as he grew old . Possessions . Among his possessions was a " robe of blending " . History . None of Wesclodat ' s peers knew his origins , but some elders claimed he had once followed a different god , swapping to Deneir as the result of a trade between the two deities .

title: Wessalen Arturia
description: Wessalen Arturia Wessalen Arturia was a human paladin of Lathander from Cimbar , Chessenta . He sailed the Pirate Isles in 1359 DR . Activities .
description_long: Wessalen Arturia Wessalen Arturia was a human paladin of Lathander from Cimbar , Chessenta . He sailed the Pirate Isles in 1359 DR . Activities . Wessalen was a Chessenta n noble and a follower of Lathander . His goal was to restore his home country to its former glory and reunite the fractious city - states into an empire , which he believed would lead the Inner Sea into a golden age of prosperity and unity . He discovered from records in his temple in Cimbar that a very powerful artifact essential to the spread of the ancient Chessentan Empire had been lost on the Pirate Isles before the empire ' s decline . He knew almost nothing about this artifact but believed that Lathander would guide him . He traveled all over the isles in search of ancient Chessentan ruins . However , he feared that someone else would want the artifact for personal profit and did not wish to inadvertently give away a vital clue to its nature or location , so he was tight - lipped about his quest . Although not seeking battle , his secretive habits led him into several conflicts with the inhabitants , and he in turn adopted more hostile , defensive attitudes . Personality .

title: Wessic
description: Wessic Wessic the Wizened was a member of the reformed Cult of the Dragon under Severin Silrajin . History . Wessic was an old cultist and , alongside Sorvic and Maelgot , was one of the bodyguards of Talis Kasterel in the Cult ' s occupied hunting lodge in the Greypeak Mountains .
description_long: Wessic Wessic the Wizened was a member of the reformed Cult of the Dragon under Severin Silrajin . History . Wessic was an old cultist and , alongside Sorvic and Maelgot , was one of the bodyguards of Talis Kasterel in the Cult ' s occupied hunting lodge in the Greypeak Mountains . He acted as backup for his two companions .

title: West Center
description: West Center The West Center was a ward of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Activities . Found in the Central District , this ward controlled all activity through the Suq Gate , Harbor Gate , and the Grand Bazaar .
description_long: West Center The West Center was a ward of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Activities . Found in the Central District , this ward controlled all activity through the Suq Gate , Harbor Gate , and the Grand Bazaar . Inhabitants . Many of Huzuz ' s tax collectors were based in the West Center . Hosan Khalid was in charge of the bureaucrats here .

title: West Cwm
description: West Cwm The West Cwm was a large high valley in the Shaeradim , the hills surrounding Evereska . In the south , there was a large deep lake of very cold water , and to the east lay the Vine Vale , through the Sunset Gate . It was the site of the Battle of the Cwm between the daemonfey army and the defending elves of Evereska and Evermeet .
description_long: West Cwm The West Cwm was a large high valley in the Shaeradim , the hills surrounding Evereska . In the south , there was a large deep lake of very cold water , and to the east lay the Vine Vale , through the Sunset Gate . It was the site of the Battle of the Cwm between the daemonfey army and the defending elves of Evereska and Evermeet .

title: West Faerûn
description: West Faerûn The western part of Faerûn includes the nations south of Waterdeep and north of the Shining Sea , that border along the Sea of Swords . It also includes the multitude of islands that lie to the west in the vast ocean called the Trackless Sea . The closely - linked nations of Amn , Tethyr , and Calimshan have been collectively termed the " Lands of Intrigue " .
description_long: West Faerûn The western part of Faerûn includes the nations south of Waterdeep and north of the Shining Sea , that border along the Sea of Swords . It also includes the multitude of islands that lie to the west in the vast ocean called the Trackless Sea . The closely - linked nations of Amn , Tethyr , and Calimshan have been collectively termed the " Lands of Intrigue " . Some inhabitants of this region refer to Northwest Faerûn as " the Savage North , " after the Savage Frontier at a time when it was less civilized . Regions . Amn . A land of merchants that lies to the north of Tethyr along the Sword Coast , this region is a fertile plain between mountain ranges to the north and south . The northern border is formed by the Cloud Peaks and the Snakewood . To the south is the evil humanoid - infested mountain range called the Small Teeth . The capital city of Athkatla is a port along the coast . Much of the trade in the country is carried by a series of rivers . Calimshan . This is a nation with an ancient flavor , being formed from an empire of genies . It lies along the north coast of the Shining Sea , to the south of Tethyr .

title: West Harbor
description: West Harbor West Harbor was a small village near the southern end of the Mere of Dead Men along the Sword Coast . Geography . West Harbor is located in Mere of Dead Men , south of Highcliff .
description_long: West Harbor West Harbor was a small village near the southern end of the Mere of Dead Men along the Sword Coast . Geography . West Harbor is located in Mere of Dead Men , south of Highcliff . Near the village is the portal of Illefarn ruins . The swamp also made West Harbor ' s farmland incredibly fertile and more than enough crops were grown to sustain the village . Inhabitants . Due to its swampy terrain and annual harvest festival where the inhabitants compete against each other to win prizes in tests of skill , the villagers of West Harbor ( referred to as " Harbormen " ) were renowned in the lands surrounding them for their natural toughness . This put them in high demand for positions as guards and military service . In addition , they tended their fields with care , since most worshiped Chauntea . However , they were a shy people . History . Unfortunately , West Harbor has been destroyed twice , both times in recent memory . Once , when the King of Shadows first attacked Neverwinter and again several decades later when it was revisited by Ammon Jerro .

title: West Wall
description: West Wall West Wall was a district of the drow city of Menzoberranzan . Geography . West Wall encompassed the area next to the entire western wall of the cavern where Menzoberranzan was located , from Tier Breche in the north to Narbondellyn in the south .
description_long: West Wall West Wall was a district of the drow city of Menzoberranzan . Geography . West Wall encompassed the area next to the entire western wall of the cavern where Menzoberranzan was located , from Tier Breche in the north to Narbondellyn in the south . Inhabitants . West Wall was home to many of the older noble families .

title: West Zakhara
description: West Zakhara West Zakhara was a giant peninsula that contained the arid plateau of the High Desert , populated by nomadic tribes , in the north , and the wealthy Pearl Cities , centers of trade , in the south . Geography . The only land connection to the rest of the Land of Fate lay towards the north , where the edge of the Mountains of the Lizard ' s Tongue met the area around Qudra .
description_long: West Zakhara West Zakhara was a giant peninsula that contained the arid plateau of the High Desert , populated by nomadic tribes , in the north , and the wealthy Pearl Cities , centers of trade , in the south . Geography . The only land connection to the rest of the Land of Fate lay towards the north , where the edge of the Mountains of the Lizard ' s Tongue met the area around Qudra . Otherwise , west Zakhara was surrounded by water : the Great Sea with the mysterious land of Akota to the west , the Crowded Sea with the archipelagos of Al - Sartan and Nada al - Hazan to the south and southeast . Towards interior Zakhara , the Golden Gulf and the Cities of the Pantheon beyond lay to the east , Suq Bay and the Cities of the Heart to the northeast . Al - Tariq and the Sea of Caravans were the waters to the north . Except at the Cities of the Pearl , the borders of west Zakhara were made even more pronounced by a series of elevations , Al - Suqut Mountains , the Mountains of the Lizard ' s Tongue , the Spine of the Dog , and a long ridges of hills along Suq Bay . High Desert .

title: Westbridge
description: Westbridge Westbridge was a village along the Long Road . It stood at the intersection of the Long Road and the trail to the Stone Bridge . As of 1368 DR , all the major industries in Westbridge , including the market , stockyard and grain warehouses , were owned by a halfling named Ghaliver Longstocking .
description_long: Westbridge Westbridge was a village along the Long Road . It stood at the intersection of the Long Road and the trail to the Stone Bridge . As of 1368 DR , all the major industries in Westbridge , including the market , stockyard and grain warehouses , were owned by a halfling named Ghaliver Longstocking . It was the home for the Harvest Inn .

title: Western Heartlands
description: Western Heartlands The Western Heartlands is a region located in West Faerûn . The Western Heartlands stretch west from Cormyr and the Dragon Coast to the east , and slowly blend into the coastal Sword Coast region at the Sea of Swords . The city of Baldur ' s Gate is the strongest city in the Western Heartlands and also Faerûn ' s most powerful , along with Evereska ; due to a massive influx of refugees created by the Spellplague , the city has swelled and grown as big as half of Elturgard .
description_long: Western Heartlands The Western Heartlands is a region located in West Faerûn . The Western Heartlands stretch west from Cormyr and the Dragon Coast to the east , and slowly blend into the coastal Sword Coast region at the Sea of Swords . The city of Baldur ' s Gate is the strongest city in the Western Heartlands and also Faerûn ' s most powerful , along with Evereska ; due to a massive influx of refugees created by the Spellplague , the city has swelled and grown as big as half of Elturgard . Before the Spellplague , there were not any nations in the Western Heartlands , despite Amn ' s attempts . As of 1479 DR , Elturgard and Najara have grown to be powerful nations in the Western Heartlands ; however , the city of Baldur ' s Gate could still best both of them in a hypothetical war . Settlements and other features . Baldur ' s Gate . Baldur ' s Gate is a port metropolis on the north bank of the River Chionthar , to the south of Waterdeep and to the north of Amn . Between Baldur ' s Gate and Amn stretches the important merchant road , the Coast Way . It is well known for the presence of the powerful Flaming Fist mercenary company that keep the city generally peaceful and safe .

title: Westgate
description: Westgate Westgate was a seedy and squalid metropolis — with a history in piracy , powerful crime syndicates , and nameless vampiric crime - lords . Westgate thrived on blackmarket trade and corruption , and was perhaps one of the most sordid cities in all of Faerûn . The legacy of scoundrels and spies was found in every alley , and danger lurked for the unprepared in every corner .
description_long: Westgate Westgate was a seedy and squalid metropolis — with a history in piracy , powerful crime syndicates , and nameless vampiric crime - lords . Westgate thrived on blackmarket trade and corruption , and was perhaps one of the most sordid cities in all of Faerûn . The legacy of scoundrels and spies was found in every alley , and danger lurked for the unprepared in every corner . It was an open city that welcomed all travellers and citizens alike as long as they abided by the local laws and , of course , had enough coin . It was probably the oldest , richest and most corrupt port on the Sea of Fallen Stars . It received the nickname , " Gateway to the West " , from its role as the Inner Sea ' s most prolific port city . A person from Westgate was known as a Westar or a Westhavian . History . This area of the Dragon Coast was first settled by human s from the Vilhon Reach roughly 3 , 000 years ago . The largest place was the human town of Westgate , ruled cruelly by the great topaz dragon Kisonraathiisar . In - 349 DR , Saldrinar destroyed Kisonraathiisar and became Westgate ' s first human king .

title: Westgate Ruby
description: Westgate Ruby Westgate Ruby was a wine exported from Westgate . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description .
description_long: Westgate Ruby Westgate Ruby was a wine exported from Westgate . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description . This bold crimson wine was slightly acidic . It was complimented best when served with a beef or a hearty stew . Prices . Westgate Ruby could be purchased in the following containers :

title: Westways
description: Westways The Westways were a series of tunnels and roads that led west from the drow city of Menzoberranzan to Blingdenstone and Mithral Hall , as well as to Mantol - Derith and Phanlinksal . Description . The Westways tunnels were heavily patrolled by drow forces near Menzoberranzan .
description_long: Westways The Westways were a series of tunnels and roads that led west from the drow city of Menzoberranzan to Blingdenstone and Mithral Hall , as well as to Mantol - Derith and Phanlinksal . Description . The Westways tunnels were heavily patrolled by drow forces near Menzoberranzan . Route . The Westways ran from Menzoberranzan some 50 miles west to the svirfneblin city of Blingdenstone . They then turned east to Mithral Hall and led to some entrances to the surface in Luruar . The route also branched out to Mantol - Derith and the illithid enclave of Phanlinksal . History . The Westways gates in Menzoberranzan had never successfully been breached by invading forces by the 1360s DR .

title: Westwood
description: Westwood Westwood was a forest on the Sword Coast North on the eastern edge of the Sword Mountains . Geography . The closest settlement to Westwood was Kheldell which sat on the north western edge of the wood at the bottom of the Sword Mountains .
description_long: Westwood Westwood was a forest on the Sword Coast North on the eastern edge of the Sword Mountains . Geography . The closest settlement to Westwood was Kheldell which sat on the north western edge of the wood at the bottom of the Sword Mountains . This forest covered part of the eastern slopes of the Sword Mountains south of Kheldell . Amphail lay to the south of Westwood . Westwood was part of a group of forests that were referred to as the Other Woods . The forests in the Other Woods were Lurkwood , Southkrypt garden , Southwood , Moonwood and Westwood . History . Some sages claimed that Westwood was once as vast as the High Forest and stretched as far north as Yartar and as far south as the Delimbiyr Route . In - 4420 DR the dwarven realm of Besilmer was founded . The western edges of Besilmer territory ended at Westwood . In - 1100 DR the remnants of the elven empire of Illefarn splinter into the independant realms of Ardeep , Iliyanbruen and Rilithar . Rilithar settles in Westwood and Kryptgarden Forest . Sages claimed that Westwood had been shrinking after the destruction of Netheril . Sometime between 936 DR and 941 DR , the Battle of Westwood took place .

title: Wetwoods
description: Wetwoods The Wetwoods was an area of wooded and grazing land south of the Wet River in the Vilhon Reach area . Geography . Two - thirds of the southern area of the Wetwoods was a misty bog with fungus - coated trees .
description_long: Wetwoods The Wetwoods was an area of wooded and grazing land south of the Wet River in the Vilhon Reach area . Geography . Two - thirds of the southern area of the Wetwoods was a misty bog with fungus - coated trees . History . Around 1372 DR , several animal herders were killed while tending to their herds and flocks , and although none of the animals were harmed , they were left mysteriously weakened . Despite the survival of some of the herders , there were no sightings of any malevolent beings in the area and people speculated the attacks were made by vampire s or stirge s . Lord Quwen of Orbrekh ordered an investigation .

title: Whale
description: Whale Whales were the largest mammals in the world . They were gentle sea - dwelling creatures that migrate from place to place in the oceans . While peaceful , whales are known to only attack ships and other sea creatures when provoked .
description_long: Whale Whales were the largest mammals in the world . They were gentle sea - dwelling creatures that migrate from place to place in the oceans . While peaceful , whales are known to only attack ships and other sea creatures when provoked . " Baleen whales " : were the larger of the type , including blue whale s , humpback whale s , and gray whale s . These whales feed by straining seawater through long strips of baleen that they had in place of teeth , from which they got their name . " Cachalot whales " : included such breeds as sperm whale s , beluga whale s , and narwhal . They were active hunters , feeding on fish , squid , and smaller marine mammals .

title: Whamite Isles
description: Whamite Isles The Whamite Isles consisted of a number of islands in the Sea of Fallen Stars . History . During the Twelfth Serôs War , Iakhovas reintroduced the kelpie species of sentient seaweed , long extinct in the Realms , back to the sea .
description_long: Whamite Isles The Whamite Isles consisted of a number of islands in the Sea of Fallen Stars . History . During the Twelfth Serôs War , Iakhovas reintroduced the kelpie species of sentient seaweed , long extinct in the Realms , back to the sea . The vast majority of the residents of the Isles were affected by the kelpies " charm " powers which caused many people to jump into the sea and drown . The corpses were quickly animated and turned into sea zombies which plagued several coastal cities for the next few years . As of 1370 DR , the major ports of Agenais and Garhunclen were both disused . That year though , the Emerald Enclave , who seemed to have discovered a way to circumvent the kelpies , seized control of the islands . Notes . The Whamite Isles were named after board game designer Tom Wham who designed a non - canonical strategy game set on the Isles .

title: Wheel of bones
description: Wheel of bones Wheel of bones was a divine magic spell available to specialty priest s and other followers of Eldath , the Green Goddess . It created a whirling weapon of bone fragments around one appendage of the caster that could be used as both a melee weapon and a ranged weapon . Effects .
description_long: Wheel of bones Wheel of bones was a divine magic spell available to specialty priest s and other followers of Eldath , the Green Goddess . It created a whirling weapon of bone fragments around one appendage of the caster that could be used as both a melee weapon and a ranged weapon . Effects . When cast , a halo of bone fragments formed around the chosen limb of the caster , spinning rapidly like a circular saw blade for five minutes ( longer for more experienced casters ) or until the caster willed the spell to end , whichever came first . The " wheel of bones " made a slashing melee weapon that the caster could wield at his or her normal skill level . In addition , the caster could fire a random number of bone shards ( maximum of three per use ) at a chosen target with a very high level of skill for a small amount of damage . The target of flung fragments did not have to be the same as the melee target , and the caster could choose either attack form , or use both at the same time . The ranged attack was similar to that of a short bow with no penalty or bonus for targets at point blank range .

title: Whelgar Taerncole
description: Whelgar Taerncole Whelgar Taerncole was a human man of the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . He was a former adventurer and proprietor of the Sleeping Cat restaurant . Whelgar was once an adventurer and a member of the Easy Blades Adventuring Band , a group often suspected of smuggling .
description_long: Whelgar Taerncole Whelgar Taerncole was a human man of the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . He was a former adventurer and proprietor of the Sleeping Cat restaurant . Whelgar was once an adventurer and a member of the Easy Blades Adventuring Band , a group often suspected of smuggling . He later retired . Before 1358 DR , he bought the Sleeping Cat tavern in Wheloon . Sick of the brawling , Whelgar got rid of both taproom and wine cellar , and developed the place as a restaurant instead . By around 1369 DR , the Sleeping Cat had steadily become a proper , quality restaurant under Whelgar ' s ownership .

title: Wheloon
description: Wheloon Wheloon , sometimes nicknamed the " Jade Towers " , was a town and later small city in the kingdom of Cormyr in interior Faerûn . It lay at the junction of the Wyvernflow River and the Way of the Manticore and at the end of the Hullack Trail in southeastern Cormyr . Language .
description_long: Wheloon Wheloon , sometimes nicknamed the " Jade Towers " , was a town and later small city in the kingdom of Cormyr in interior Faerûn . It lay at the junction of the Wyvernflow River and the Way of the Manticore and at the end of the Hullack Trail in southeastern Cormyr . Language . The name " Wheloon " was pronounced " way - LOON " . People and things from here were called " Whelunian " . History . Early history . Predating Wheloon and the ferry was the God ' s Grove , a shrine to Silvanus and duskwood grove to the east . Also built before Wheloon ' s founding was a so - called citadel built into a bluff north of the site . Later ruined , nothing more than the crumbling foundations inhabited by displacer serpent s would remain by the 1370s DR . Originally a small thorp that lived off the trade of river crossings on the Wyvern Ferry Route , Wheloon slowly developed as trade along the Way of the Manticore increased and more ships starting using the Wyvernflow . It grew into a town based around the ferry . The Harvest Hall temple of Chauntea was built around this time .

title: Wheloon Moothouse
description: Wheloon Moothouse The Wheloon Moothouse was a meeting hall located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . It stood on Wheloon Way , opposite Oldstone Hall . The moothouse served as Wheloon ' s courthouse and a hall for meetings .
description_long: Wheloon Moothouse The Wheloon Moothouse was a meeting hall located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . It stood on Wheloon Way , opposite Oldstone Hall . The moothouse served as Wheloon ' s courthouse and a hall for meetings . It also contained apartments for visiting court messengers and high - ranking Purple Dragon s . The building was constructed of timber and stone . It was built wide and with few internal walls or furniture to allow as many people as possible to gather inside .

title: Wheloon Tack & Leather
description: Wheloon Tack & Leather Wheloon Tack & Leather was a store located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr that sold leather goods . Its proprietor was Landon Bhentyl . The store sold leather products of all kinds .
description_long: Wheloon Tack & Leather Wheloon Tack & Leather was a store located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr that sold leather goods . Its proprietor was Landon Bhentyl . The store sold leather products of all kinds . This included clothing such as belts , gloves , and riding breeches , scabbards for weapon s , and armor s from a light leather armor to a full studded leather armor . It also sold harnesses , bridles , reins , and traces for wagons suitable for up to sixteen horse s or ox en . Landon Bhentyl always kept everything in stock so a customer was never left needy . As a result , the store had a strong leathery smell .

title: Wheloon Watch
description: Wheloon Watch The Wheloon Watch was a militia and law - enforcement organization that operated in Wheloon in Cormyr , in the 14th century DR . Organization . The Wheloon Watch was a militia force of volunteers , all merchants and tradesmen by day , with basic fighting ability .
description_long: Wheloon Watch The Wheloon Watch was a militia and law - enforcement organization that operated in Wheloon in Cormyr , in the 14th century DR . Organization . The Wheloon Watch was a militia force of volunteers , all merchants and tradesmen by day , with basic fighting ability . They were led by a captain . Activities . As well as being a militia force , the Wheloon Watch had the power to arrest those suspected of crimes such as murder . However , the Wheloon Watch did not investigate missing persons . Base of operations . They were based out of the Wheloon Watch House . Possessions . Members of the Watch were equipped with leather armor , mace s , short sword s , dagger s , and crossbow s . Relationships . The Wheloon Watch worked with the local Purple Dragons contingent , and shared the Wheloon Watch House with them . History . During the Time of Troubles in the Year of Shadows , 1358 DR , in Wheloon , Kelemvor was framed for the robbery and murder of a local merchant , with Cyric ' s agent testifying to Lord Sarp Redbeard that they had seen him leave the house with a bloody sword .

title: Wheloon Watch House
description: Wheloon Watch House The Wheloon Watch House was a watch house located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . It stood at the intersection of Wheloon Way and the Way of the Manticore . The watch house was a base for the Wheloon Watch and also served as a barracks for the local Purple Dragons .
description_long: Wheloon Watch House The Wheloon Watch House was a watch house located in the city of Wheloon in Cormyr . It stood at the intersection of Wheloon Way and the Way of the Manticore . The watch house was a base for the Wheloon Watch and also served as a barracks for the local Purple Dragons . Also a part of the building was the Wheloon Jail and an armory . Around thirty Dragons manned the watch house at a time , either hearing public complaints , guarding the jail , or sleeping . History . In the Year of Lightning Storms , 1374 DR , some prisoners of the Wheloon Jail , those who chose to repent and perform holy service in exchange for their sentences being commuted , were recruited to serve as temple guards for the new Temple of Mystra .

title: Whip
description: Whip A whip ( the common name for what we call a bullwhip ) is an exotic , one - handed melee reach weapon that only does non - lethal damage . Description . The whip is a long , flexible , braided leather cord which tapers gradually from the handle to the tip .
description_long: Whip A whip ( the common name for what we call a bullwhip ) is an exotic , one - handed melee reach weapon that only does non - lethal damage . Description . The whip is a long , flexible , braided leather cord which tapers gradually from the handle to the tip . The handle is either thick braided leather or leather - covered wood and is 8 to 12 in ( 20 . 3 to 30 . 5 cm ) long . When stretched to full length , the whip can be up to 20 ft ( 6 . 1 m ) long . An optional tassel of horsehair or twine on the end ( called a cracker ) will amplify the sound of the whip . An average whip costs 1 gp and weighs 2 lb ( 0 . 9 kg ) . Use . The whip can only damage creatures not wearing armor or without tough natural armor . It is a melee weapon with reach , giving it an effective range of 15 ft ( 4 . 6 m ) . Unlike other reach weapon s , it can be used to attack adjacent opponents as well . Whips also can be used to trip an opponent and they are particularly good at disarming . However , it takes special training and practice to use a whip effectively without hurting yourself , therefore it is considered an exotic weapon .

title: Whip sash
description: Whip sash Whip sashes were special weapons used by Holy slayer assassin s in Zakhara . Description . Outwardly , these weapons appeared as regular silk sashes .
description_long: Whip sash Whip sashes were special weapons used by Holy slayer assassin s in Zakhara . Description . Outwardly , these weapons appeared as regular silk sashes . Underneath the silk rested a leather sash that had metal wire with a steel tip . Uses . This weapon could be used as either a horsewhip or a . It was favored by the Moon - spinners . Price . Whip sashes cost six gold pieces .

title: Whiptail
description: Whiptail Whiptail was a lizardfolk member of the Muckmarsh tribe in Twilight Marsh near Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Whiptail was very resolute but believed heavily in superstitions .
description_long: Whiptail Whiptail was a lizardfolk member of the Muckmarsh tribe in Twilight Marsh near Phlan in 1489 DR . Personality . Whiptail was very resolute but believed heavily in superstitions . She spoke to her weapons , especially her chosen dagger . She would not explain to anyone why that weapon was so important to her . History . In 1489 DR , Whiptail acted as an escort for her chieftain Bogclaw and shaman Scalesneer to a meeting with adventurers . However , they were attacked by a group of will - o ' - wisp s and Whiptail was one of the few survivors . She was chosen to guide the adventurers to the lair of Throstulgrael .

title: Whirlchain
description: Whirlchain Whirlchain was a divine evocation spell that created a chain that battered one ' s foe . Effect . The spell conjured a chain around the target creature in a helix fashion , that then whipped and battered the victim before disappearing .
description_long: Whirlchain Whirlchain was a divine evocation spell that created a chain that battered one ' s foe . Effect . The spell conjured a chain around the target creature in a helix fashion , that then whipped and battered the victim before disappearing . Components . The spell required a metal chain of any kind and any length longer than the caster ' s own hand . History . The " whirlchain " spell appeared within the " Tome of Torment " , the holiest book of the church of Ilmater , which first appeared in the Realms in 848 DR .

title: Whirling blade
description: Whirling blade Whirling blade is a relatively powerful spell learned by some swordmage s early in their training . When a swordmage casts " whirling blade " he or she first throws a melee weapon of their choice at a target within twenty - five , using the power of the spell to keep the weapon aloft in the air , striking the creature with deadly force . If they miss the first target , a swordmage may spend their weapon twirling towards another creature within ten feet of the first .
description_long: Whirling blade Whirling blade is a relatively powerful spell learned by some swordmage s early in their training . When a swordmage casts " whirling blade " he or she first throws a melee weapon of their choice at a target within twenty - five , using the power of the spell to keep the weapon aloft in the air , striking the creature with deadly force . If they miss the first target , a swordmage may spend their weapon twirling towards another creature within ten feet of the first . This process can be repeated another two times and it is only upon striking true or missing a fourth target that the weapon ultimately returns to its wielder . The spell , due to its power , requires a vast amount of energy on the swordmage ' s part , meaning that it can only be cast once per day .

title: Whirling scimitar
description: Whirling scimitar The whirling scimitar was a Zakhara n magic al weapon that could bestow the ability to fly . Description . This item usually appeared as a scimitar , but versions in the form of a broadsword or two - handed sword also existed .
description_long: Whirling scimitar The whirling scimitar was a Zakhara n magic al weapon that could bestow the ability to fly . Description . This item usually appeared as a scimitar , but versions in the form of a broadsword or two - handed sword also existed . It was most common in the lands of Zakhara but could be found elsewhere , too . Powers . Used in a fight , the " whirling scimitar " showed a stronger magical attack potential against flying creatures than against others and a still stronger one against those from the Elemental Plane of Air . When whirled above the head of the wielder instead of attacking , it bestowed the ability of a " fly " spell . The ability to fly stopped immediately if the wielder lost hold of the weapon .

title: Whirlpool
description: Whirlpool Whirlpool was an arcane alteration spell that created a large swirling vortex in a body of water that could pull creatures and ships down into the depths . Effects . This spell took ten minutes to cast and could be directed at a point up to 420 ft ( 128 m ) away .
description_long: Whirlpool Whirlpool was an arcane alteration spell that created a large swirling vortex in a body of water that could pull creatures and ships down into the depths . Effects . This spell took ten minutes to cast and could be directed at a point up to 420 ft ( 128 m ) away . When completed , a funnel - shaped depression appeared in the midst of a swirling area of water with a radius of at least 350 ft ( 107 m ) rotating swiftly counterclockwise and lasting over two hours . More experienced casters could achieve greater range , size , and duration of the " whirlpool " . Creatures in the water were pummeled and tossed about and had to continually fight against being pulled to the center . If they failed to resist , they could easily drown — even water - breathing creatures could die from cumulative injury . Ships in the area of effect constantly spiraled toward the center in addition to whatever movement they were able to achieve with oars or sails , and their seaworthiness was sorely tested . Those that failed capsized and sank , possibly depositing some passengers and crew into the churning waters . Components .

title: Whirlwind
description: Whirlwind Whirlwind was an evocation spell that created a small but powerful tornado that could be directed along the ground or over a body of water . The goddesses Akadi and Aerdrie Faenya granted their own version of this spell . Effects .
description_long: Whirlwind Whirlwind was an evocation spell that created a small but powerful tornado that could be directed along the ground or over a body of water . The goddesses Akadi and Aerdrie Faenya granted their own version of this spell . Effects . The funnel - shaped cyclone picked up dirt , dust , and debris ( or whatever it was directed to pass over ) , and twirled it around at high velocity . Creatures caught by the cyclone were subjected to possible damage from this flying debris and human - sized creatures or smaller could be picked up bodily and held aloft , buffeted fiercely by the raging winds . The caster could cause the whirlwind to eject any creatures it held , but they could be flung from as high as 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) above the surface with unknown speed and trajectory to land in the vicinity . This spell required continuous concentration by the caster . If the whirlwind moved out of range or the caster became distracted , it moved in a random path for a few minutes before collapsing and dropping its contents . Components .

title: Whirlwind ( Akadi )
description: Whirlwind ( Akadi ) This whirlwind spell was an extremely powerful version of the " whirlwind " spell that was only given to priests of Akadi , the Queen of Air , and Aerdrie Faenya , the Winged Mother . It created a towering rotational vortex on land or sea that destroyed most everything in its path . Effects .
description_long: Whirlwind ( Akadi ) This whirlwind spell was an extremely powerful version of the " whirlwind " spell that was only given to priests of Akadi , the Queen of Air , and Aerdrie Faenya , the Winged Mother . It created a towering rotational vortex on land or sea that destroyed most everything in its path . Effects . This spell took ten minutes to cast , which was longer than the duration of the effect . Upon completion of this spell , a swirling cone - shaped cyclone was formed , 10 ft ( 3 m ) across the base , 30 ft ( 9 . 1 m ) across the top , and 270 ft ( 82 m ) tall . This spell would only function if there was enough room for a gigantic twister of these dimensions to form within 360 ft ( 110 m ) of the caster . The speed of the " whirlwind " was chosen at the time of casting and could be 90 ft ( 27 m ) or 180 ft ( 55 m ) per minute . The " whirlwind " could change direction by 60 degrees per minute . The caster had to concentrate for a full minute to change the speed or direction of the destructive vortex . If cast on land , the " whirlwind " had the form and destructive power of a tornado ; over water , it hit with hurricane force .

title: Whirlwind ( horse )
description: Whirlwind ( horse ) The Whirlwind was a legendary horse living in Zakhara in 1367 DR . Personality . The Whirlwind had a vicious temperament and actually appeared to enjoy fighting .
description_long: Whirlwind ( horse ) The Whirlwind was a legendary horse living in Zakhara in 1367 DR . Personality . The Whirlwind had a vicious temperament and actually appeared to enjoy fighting . Activities . Shod with special steel shoes , the Whirlwind performed devastating attacks with his rider during raids on caravans traveling between Huzuz and Halwa . Relationships . The Whirlwind was ridden by Fasim Kaldur , the leader of the Riders of Blood . Rumors and Legends . One rumor stated that Fasim was about to fall before a swarm of enemies , but his horse brutally attacked them in a whirlwind of bites and kicks , saving Fasim ' s life in the process .

title: Whisper
description: Whisper Whisper was a cruel and calculating mage with great ambition , but he angered the wrong group of adventurers . Working as an agent of the Zhentarim in northern Cormyr , he spied on trade routes and troop movements , organizing raids and ambushes . His ambition was to rise in the ranks of the Zhentarim and also head up his own secret society .
description_long: Whisper Whisper was a cruel and calculating mage with great ambition , but he angered the wrong group of adventurers . Working as an agent of the Zhentarim in northern Cormyr , he spied on trade routes and troop movements , organizing raids and ambushes . His ambition was to rise in the ranks of the Zhentarim and also head up his own secret society . To that end , he was gathering agents and organizing strongholds that were under his exclusive control . Whisper ' s base was known as Whisper ' s Crypt , a subterranean lair located beneath the Haunted Halls just north of Eveningstar . When one of his attacks happened to target a group of visiting adventurers led by Doust Sulwood , the attackers were defeated and Doust and his companions learned of Whisper and decided to hunt him down . The adventurers were able to break the enchantments and overcome the guardian creatures and ultimately kill Whisper in his underground home . In the treasure found in Whisper ' s crypt were two of the seven Lost Rings of Mhzentul . These were gifted to temples in the area by Doust and his companions . Whisper ' s personal wizard rune was a stylized , clutching human hand , black and claw - like .

title: Whisper ( Luskan )
description: Whisper ( Luskan ) Whisper was a vicious criminal in Luskan . Activities . Whisper was a criminal with a vile reputation .
description_long: Whisper ( Luskan ) Whisper was a vicious criminal in Luskan . Activities . Whisper was a criminal with a vile reputation . She had a network of fence contacts and was one of the few who could smuggle people inside and outside the city without the knowledge of the High Captains of Luskan . Whisper was always secretly followed by her minions when she traded with a client , in order to protect her . History . In 1356 DR , Whisper traded a map to Mithral Hall with Drizzt Do ' Urden and Bruenor Battlehammer . Later , Artemis Entreri asked her for information about the Companions of the Hall . Whisper tried to double - cross Entreri but the assassin subdued her and later killed Whisper in order to leave no witnesses .

title: Whispering Children
description: Whispering Children The Whispering Children were twenty - two powerful artifact s in the form of portraits . In reality , they were the transformed demi - power children of the god Oghma . The paintings were referred to as Whispering Children because they whispered secrets to those nearby .
description_long: Whispering Children The Whispering Children were twenty - two powerful artifact s in the form of portraits . In reality , they were the transformed demi - power children of the god Oghma . The paintings were referred to as Whispering Children because they whispered secrets to those nearby . History . Shortly after ascending to godhood , Oghma fathered many demi - power children . A few of his children decided to each specialize in an area of knowledge of their choosing . Twenty - two of the children were turned away from Oghma by Cyric , who transformed them into paintings . The goddess Mystra attempted to take the paintings from Cyric but he scattered the paintings across Faerûn and most were lost . The noble house Norjah of Airspur managed to collect seven of the children . The knowledge held by the Whispering Children was dangerous to the gods , especially to Oghma .

title: Whispering Serpent
description: Whispering Serpent The Whispering Serpent was the main advisor of the rulers of Sammaresh in Lapaliiya . Believed to be the ghost of a couatl , in truth he was a living couatl using " ethereal jaunt " . He advised Lady Ilnara Mremman around 1373 DR .
description_long: Whispering Serpent The Whispering Serpent was the main advisor of the rulers of Sammaresh in Lapaliiya . Believed to be the ghost of a couatl , in truth he was a living couatl using " ethereal jaunt " . He advised Lady Ilnara Mremman around 1373 DR . His main duty was to ready the forces of western Lapaliiya to defend against the yuan - ti . Sometimes he hired adventurers to thwart yuan - ti plots , by manifesting before them .

title: Whispering of the wind
description: Whispering of the wind The whispering of the wind was a special ritual used by sha ' ir s to enhance their gen ' s hearing ability . Preparation . All rituals that enhanced a gen ' s hearing required a set of earrings studded with valuable gems worth at least 500 dinar s .
description_long: Whispering of the wind The whispering of the wind was a special ritual used by sha ' ir s to enhance their gen ' s hearing ability . Preparation . All rituals that enhanced a gen ' s hearing required a set of earrings studded with valuable gems worth at least 500 dinar s . This ritual lasted for 16 hours . Once the ritual was complete the gen was able to hear any conversation that they could see taking place , including those were the participants used magic to mask their voices .

title: Whispering sand
description: Whispering sand Whispering sand was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell imbued a handful of sand with a message from the caster .
description_long: Whispering sand Whispering sand was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell imbued a handful of sand with a message from the caster . The caster determined the specific sand that was to hold a message . Examples of this were a cup of sand , a small patch of sand near a gate , etc . The caster would determine specific conditions that would trigger the sand message to whisper to the recipient . This condition needed to occur within 30 yards ( 27 . 4 m ) of the sand . A wizard would then record a message into the sand ; more powerful wizards could record longer messages . Anyone within 20 feet ( 6 m ) could hear the message . The sand could also be used to store any spell that only required a verbal component . The stored spell must be one known by the caster . The stored spell would trigger when the specific condition was met . Components . This spell required sand to cast .

title: Whistler
description: Whistler Whistlers were special halfling bard s found commonly in Luiren in the Shining South . Requirements . Only halfling bards could be whistlers .
description_long: Whistler Whistlers were special halfling bard s found commonly in Luiren in the Shining South . Requirements . Only halfling bards could be whistlers . Role . Whistlers served as special guardians for halfling settlements in Luiren . Nearly every village or hamlet had a least one whistler to help protect them from harm . They often worked together with cleric s of Yondalla . Skills . Through whistling their unique songs , whistlers were able to summon and control animals , control plants , and even control the weather .

title: Whistling Wizard
description: Whistling Wizard The Whistling Wizard was an inn in Voonlar that catered to adventurers and had a shady reputation around the Moonsea region . It was also famous for a cistern in its basement , called the Wizard Well , that would talk to people and give advice . Location .
description_long: Whistling Wizard The Whistling Wizard was an inn in Voonlar that catered to adventurers and had a shady reputation around the Moonsea region . It was also famous for a cistern in its basement , called the Wizard Well , that would talk to people and give advice . Location . The Whistling Wizard sat at the southern tip of Voonlar where the North Ride entered the forest and was somewhat isolated from the rest of the town . It was on the east side of the road and the southern face abutted the forest . Structure . The inn sat back from the North Ride a few horse - lengths across a perpetually muddy front yard . A lantern post at the edge of the road held a sign carved in the shape of a wizard ' s head , its lips puckered as if whistling . Across the front of the inn was a covered porch with a railing for hitching horses . Above the porch was a balcony attached to the owner ' s apartments . The railing of this balcony had been turned into a makeshift herb garden by adding troughs of dirt along its length . The two - story inn extended quite far eastward , forming a long rectangle . The upper - floor rooms each had a window or a balcony .

title: Whitchthorn
description: Whitchthorn Whitchthorn was a powerful archfey of Kryptgarden Forest in 1489 DR . Activities . Whitchthorn was the ruler of all the fey living in Kryptgarden .
description_long: Whitchthorn Whitchthorn was a powerful archfey of Kryptgarden Forest in 1489 DR . Activities . Whitchthorn was the ruler of all the fey living in Kryptgarden . When he was a prince , he lived with his spouse , the dryad Ishaldra , who balanced his evil inclination with her good nature . History . In 1489 DR , the arrival of Claugiyliamatar corrupted Ishaldra and her treant bodyguard . Thus Whitchthorn , who had become king , unleashed his evil against the desecrator of the forest , but Old Gnawbones was too powerful for him . Ultimately , an adventuring party hired to defeat Old Gnawbones gained an audience with the fey king . Whitchthorn agreed to give his help in order to defeat the green dragon , but only if one of the adventurers made an oath with him . Presumably , the adventurers agreed to the pact .

title: White Agate ' s Tower
description: White Agate ' s Tower The White Agate ' s Tower was located within the Court District of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . The mansion was situated around the base of the tower .
description_long: White Agate ' s Tower The White Agate ' s Tower was located within the Court District of Huzuz in 1367 DR . Description . The mansion was situated around the base of the tower . The presence of wealth was evident on every visible surface of the mansion . Beautiful spires and shrubberies surrounded the two story structure . All prospective students were met and interviewed in the mansion ' s parlor . The basement contained two large pools — one of fresh water and one of sea water . Many aspiring sea mages used these pools during their conjurations of water elemental s and even marid s . The rest of the basement contained the treasure of the White Agate . A wide variety of guardians protected the wealth stored here . The keys to the treasure rooms were kept behind a plain wall that was opened by a single command word that only the White Agate and his five most trusted students knew . The tower portion of this complex rose 90 ft . ( 27m ) into the air and sat at the opposite end of a small courtyard where students often ate their meals . The tower housed the personal quarters of the White Agate , a library , the dormitory for his prized pupils , as well as his school for mages .

title: White Lady
description: White Lady The White Lady was a amnesiac elf lady in Waterdeep in 1479 DR . History . One day in 1479 a elderly lady in white dress arrived in Yawning Portal tavern .
description_long: White Lady The White Lady was a amnesiac elf lady in Waterdeep in 1479 DR . History . One day in 1479 a elderly lady in white dress arrived in Yawning Portal tavern . She drunk and ate and after started whispering a strange message : " The eye is open . It casts its glance far . Some follow the eye ' s glance , coming here . Some fall in and spiral down like a whirlpool . Nothing lies at the bottom . Even the darkness is empty . The eye cannot see . The eye is open " . For month the white lady repeated this routine , sometimes only repeating the message in a different language . One day some priests of Oghma , believing her a prophet , trying to examine her but she lose her mind , becoming aggressive . Durnan banned her from the Yawning Portal but she went back the next night continuing her routine and Durnan decided to comply , saying to all to no disturb her . One day a suffered adventurer returned from Undermountain babbling . The white lady approached him and and soon she too became afflicted from the same disease of the adventurer . However her daily mantra stopped the spreading of the infection . Possibly she was infected by the Abyssal Plague .

title: White Maw
description: White Maw White Maw was a massive intelligent gray ooze in the Doomvault dungeon in 1486 DR . History . White Maw was the result of one of the experiments of the transmuter Sarkalla to create a sentient ooze beside the Ooze Master .
description_long: White Maw White Maw was a massive intelligent gray ooze in the Doomvault dungeon in 1486 DR . History . White Maw was the result of one of the experiments of the transmuter Sarkalla to create a sentient ooze beside the Ooze Master . In 1486 DR , it was destroyed by the heroes of Daggerford . Personailty . White Maw was completely crazy . It held all the multiple identities of the creatures sacrificed to give it sentience . Powers . It could communicate telepathically and was quite intelligent but also deeply insane . It was linked to the Ooze Master .

title: White Worm
description: White Worm The Tribe of the White Worm , or simply White Worm , were a barbarian tribe dwelling in northern Vaasa , beside the Great Glacier , and in the Earthspur Mountains around the Glacier of the White Worm , in north Faerûn . They saw the white worm — an albino remorhaz — as their totem beast and were notoriously unwelcoming of strangers . Infamously , they fought for Zhengyi , the Witch - King , but did turn away from his evil .
description_long: White Worm The Tribe of the White Worm , or simply White Worm , were a barbarian tribe dwelling in northern Vaasa , beside the Great Glacier , and in the Earthspur Mountains around the Glacier of the White Worm , in north Faerûn . They saw the white worm — an albino remorhaz — as their totem beast and were notoriously unwelcoming of strangers . Infamously , they fought for Zhengyi , the Witch - King , but did turn away from his evil . Description . The folk of White Worm were tall and strongly built . Their hair was fair , typically blond . Culture . Viewing all strangers as threats , White Worm were utterly unwelcoming of outsiders , and offered only harm to those who came upon them . If they came upon a traveler , whether in trouble or not , they would give no aid , but instead take them captive , or more likely kill them on the spot . White Worm folk felt a near mystical connection and symbiosis with " Nature " . This was thought to be a product of their hard lives in the harsh wilds , instilling in them a deep respect and understanding of the power of Nature .

title: White copper ring of fire
description: White copper ring of fire The white copper ring of fire was a unique magical ring that was forged by the djinn to aid them against the efreet . Description . This ring was made from white copper .
description_long: White copper ring of fire The white copper ring of fire was a unique magical ring that was forged by the djinn to aid them against the efreet . Description . This ring was made from white copper . Powers . If worn by any spellcaster , this ring augmented any flame spell cast so that it caused intense white flames to strike any evil creatures or those who drew magic from the Negative Energy plane . The ring accomplished this by drawing its power from the Positive Energy plane and the Elemental Plane of Fire . Additionally , fire - based spells cast by the wearer fully harmed any creature that was normally immune to such attacks .

title: White dragon
description: White dragon White dragons ( also known as ice dragons or glacial wyrms ) were the weakest and most feral of the classic chromatic dragon s . Description . White dragons were physically the smallest of the chromatic dragons , even smaller than black dragon s .
description_long: White dragon White dragons ( also known as ice dragons or glacial wyrms ) were the weakest and most feral of the classic chromatic dragon s . Description . White dragons were physically the smallest of the chromatic dragons , even smaller than black dragon s . They appeared in shades from white to grey and ice - blue , and in arctic environments , this appearance served as good camouflage . White dragons were physically distinguished by several features : their heads and necks seemed to blend seamlessly into one another , and their wings appeared somewhat frayed along the edges . They had a flap of skin , called a dewlap , lined with spines beneath their chins . Their heads were very streamlined , and they had high crests atop their skulls . They had a crisp , vaguely chemical odor . White dragon toes were spaced more widely than those of other dragons , with barbed claws to aid movement on ice . Their very thin eyelids prevented snowblindness when observing arctic landscapes . Combat . White dragons were not strong combatants as dragons went , but they were not to be underestimated . Their icy breath could freeze an unprepared foe solid in an instant .

title: Whitey
description: Whitey Whitey was a promising young assassin of the Night Masks in 1370 DR . History . Whitey was born in the Shore area of Westgate in the Year of the Morningstar , 1350 DR .
description_long: Whitey Whitey was a promising young assassin of the Night Masks in 1370 DR . History . Whitey was born in the Shore area of Westgate in the Year of the Morningstar , 1350 DR . His father was unknown and his mother was a festhall worker who died giving birth to him . He eked out a living as a street urchin until Tyaa Tymmyr saw him kill a bigger boy in a knife fight and decided to train Whitey as an assassin . The privations of his previous life made Whitey appear to be a pale , emaciated , twelve - year - old boy , a characteristic he made good use of in his work . After more than a dozen successful assassinations , Dahlia Vhammos herself took an interest in him .

title: Whyllwyst
description: Whyllwyst Whyllwyst was a gray and the familiar of Araevin Teshurr . It died over eight years ago , based on the current year being 1374 DR . Discrepancy .
description_long: Whyllwyst Whyllwyst was a gray and the familiar of Araevin Teshurr . It died over eight years ago , based on the current year being 1374 DR . Discrepancy . Although pages 12 - 13 of " Forsaken House " state " it had been more than ten years since his familiar had died " , Araevin states on page 79 of the same book , " Whyllwyst died eight years ago . " This might be accounted for if Araevin had not correctly recalled the length of time since Whyllwyst ' s death , either accidentally or on purpose .

title: Wibisono
description: Wibisono Wibisono was a pirate leader in Panjardu . History . Wibisono was born in Nahdatul on the isle of Bawa in the merchant caste , but soon he went ro Djagong , where he joined the yakuza .
description_long: Wibisono Wibisono was a pirate leader in Panjardu . History . Wibisono was born in Nahdatul on the isle of Bawa in the merchant caste , but soon he went ro Djagong , where he joined the yakuza . After some time , however , he grew bored of the yakuza life and went into wilderness , where he lived for eight years with the savage Kabundusil tribe . During this time , he defeated the hero Harijo Ten Rasid Nahdatul . Later , he switched careers again and became a pirate leader in Panjardu . In 1357 DR , he was secretly searching for a new base for his pirate activities , probably knowing of an imminent attack on Panjardu . Personality . Despite his love of thrills , Wibisono was a prudent and cautious man . He never fought to the death .

title: Widowmaker
description: Widowmaker Widowmaker was the moniker of a powerful great scimitar wielded by a tasked slayer genie called the Head Taker . " Widowmaker " was one of two dangerous swords wielded by the Head Taker , with the other being " Firefiend " . Powers .
description_long: Widowmaker Widowmaker was the moniker of a powerful great scimitar wielded by a tasked slayer genie called the Head Taker . " Widowmaker " was one of two dangerous swords wielded by the Head Taker , with the other being " Firefiend " . Powers . " Widowmaker " was a vorpal weapon , making it much easier for its wielder to decapitate or dismember their opponents .

title: Wiggan Nettlebee
description: Wiggan Nettlebee Wiggan Nettlebee was the patriarch of the halfling Nettlebee in the Dessarin Valley clan during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Wiggan disliked outsiders , believing all of them to be evildoers who would steal from him if they could .
description_long: Wiggan Nettlebee Wiggan Nettlebee was the patriarch of the halfling Nettlebee in the Dessarin Valley clan during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . Wiggan disliked outsiders , believing all of them to be evildoers who would steal from him if they could . He did not fully understand the true plan of the Black Earth , but considered them only a good ally for securing his finances and sustaining his position . A greedy miser , Wiggan become visibly upset at the thought of parting with even a few spare coins from his hoard . Activities . Wiggan managed a ranch in the Dessarin Valley with his clan . Secretly , he joined the Cult of the Black Earth . History . Wiggan had led his clan for a long time . Thanks to his cunning , they ' d amassed a fortune . To gain more money , he approached the Cult of the Black Earth , but soon become intrigued by earth powers and joined the cult . Thanks to the cultists , the Nettlebees became even more rich . In 1491 DR , after some adventurers defeated the earth cultists at the Sacred Stone Monastery , the cult ' s leaders ordered Wiggan and his family to set up a trap to kill the adventurers .

title: Wigglefingers
description: Wigglefingers Wigglefingers was a mage and captain of Morada Topolino , the assassin / thieves ' guild run by Pericolo Topolino in Delthuntle . Description . Wigglefingers wore a mustache .
description_long: Wigglefingers Wigglefingers was a mage and captain of Morada Topolino , the assassin / thieves ' guild run by Pericolo Topolino in Delthuntle . Description . Wigglefingers wore a mustache . One of his chief responsibilities in the guild was casting spells to determine the location of oysters that would suitable for the cultivation of pink pearl s . He also cast spells of water breathing and furnished Spider Parrafin with potions of water breathing . Relationships . Wigglefingers was Pericolo Topolino ' s closest friend and advisor , as well as a captain of Morada Topolino . They grew up together on Delthuntle ' s streets .

title: Wight
description: Wight A wight was an undead creature given a semblance of life through sheer violence and hatred . They could drain the life energy out of victims by touch , turning them into new wights upon death . Wights appeared as a weird and twisted reflections of the forms they had in life .
description_long: Wight A wight was an undead creature given a semblance of life through sheer violence and hatred . They could drain the life energy out of victims by touch , turning them into new wights upon death . Wights appeared as a weird and twisted reflections of the forms they had in life .

title: Wigluf
description: Wigluf Wigluf was a stone giant who helped Blagothkus in managing the flying Skyreach Castle . Personality . Wigluf was very concerned about Blagothkus ' plan to ally with dragon s and the Cult of the Dragon .
description_long: Wigluf Wigluf was a stone giant who helped Blagothkus in managing the flying Skyreach Castle . Personality . Wigluf was very concerned about Blagothkus ' plan to ally with dragon s and the Cult of the Dragon . He was scared that the consequences for giant kind would be terrible , but he supported Blagothkus out of loyalty . History . Wigluf and his companion Hulda were guests at Skyreach Castle . Wigluf tried to use a magic cauldron to interrogate the giant pantheon about Blagothkus ' s plan .

title: Wild Yak Meadows
description: Wild Yak Meadows The Wild Yak Meadows formed a large portion of the Katakoro Plateau in the Hordelands . Geopgraphy . The Wild Yak Meadows were surrounded by Nor Tso on the east , the Hungste River to the south , the Muren Tso to the north , and the mountains of Katakoro Shan to the west .
description_long: Wild Yak Meadows The Wild Yak Meadows formed a large portion of the Katakoro Plateau in the Hordelands . Geopgraphy . The Wild Yak Meadows were surrounded by Nor Tso on the east , the Hungste River to the south , the Muren Tso to the north , and the mountains of Katakoro Shan to the west . Description . This open section of the tundra stretched for several hundred miles in every direction .

title: Wild dog
description: Wild dog Wild dogs roam throughout Faerûn . They do not usually approach humanoids unless they are starving or they have been provoked . Species .
description_long: Wild dog Wild dogs roam throughout Faerûn . They do not usually approach humanoids unless they are starving or they have been provoked . Species . Cormanthor . The Cormanthor wild dog is native to the forest of Cormanthor and behaves unlike other wild dogs . It is extremely aggressive and vengeful and will track its prey for as long as is necessary to make its kill . It is not adverse to attacking medium - sized humanoids . Although omnivorous , the Cormanthor wild dog prefers to eat mammal flesh .

title: Wild dwarf
description: Wild dwarf Wild dwarves , also know as jungle dwarves and dur Authalar ( " the People " ) , were primitive dwarves who inhabited the Jungles of Chult and the Mhair and Black Jungle s . Description . This dwarven subrace was little - known except by those familiar with the jungles of South Faerûn .
description_long: Wild dwarf Wild dwarves , also know as jungle dwarves and dur Authalar ( " the People " ) , were primitive dwarves who inhabited the Jungles of Chult and the Mhair and Black Jungle s . Description . This dwarven subrace was little - known except by those familiar with the jungles of South Faerûn . The jungle dwarves were smaller than most other dwarves but sturdy and well - muscled . Over millennia in the hot jungles , they had developed a strong resistance to heat and disease . They wore very little , if any , clothing , and greased their tattoo - covered dark skin to keep away insects and make themselves slippery . Both males and females could grow beards , and their beards and woven hair provided satisfactory covering for their otherwise naked bodies . They often plastered themselves , skin and hair , with dried mud , which served as a surprisingly effective armor . For adornment , they carved earrings , bracelets and necklaces out of bone . Personality . As a rule , wild dwarves were not trusting of strangers , and would avoid detection whenever possible .

title: Wild elf
description: Wild elf Wild elves or green elves , also known as Sy - tel - quessir , are a feral , stealthy subrace of the elven species that have become more and more reclusive over the years . As of 1374 DR , they are an extremely insular race who remain close to nature and are rarely seen by other races . They have a heavier build and darker skin than other elf subraces despite having a similar average height .
description_long: Wild elf Wild elves or green elves , also known as Sy - tel - quessir , are a feral , stealthy subrace of the elven species that have become more and more reclusive over the years . As of 1374 DR , they are an extremely insular race who remain close to nature and are rarely seen by other races . They have a heavier build and darker skin than other elf subraces despite having a similar average height . Ecology . Physical characteristics . Wild elves have darker skin than other elven subraces , in a range of light brown to dark brown . An average male is 5 ' 8 " ( 173 cm ) in height and weighs 150 lbs ( 68 kg ) , while an average female is 5 ' 3 " ( 160 cm ) and 130 lbs ( 60 kg ) . Their hair can be anything from black to light brown , and it grays and turns to white with old age . They prefer to wear as little clothing as possible and choose instead to adorn themselves with other decorations like tattoos , feathers or body paint . They can make and wear complicated and intricate beadwork . Males are usually larger than females , sometimes by as much as five inches or twenty pounds , but wild elves differ little in size from other elves .

title: Wild halfling
description: Wild halfling Wild halflings were halfling s native to Far Payit and other jungles in Maztica . Society . They were extremely primitive and wore no clothing but painted their bodies with red and black paint .
description_long: Wild halfling Wild halflings were halfling s native to Far Payit and other jungles in Maztica . Society . They were extremely primitive and wore no clothing but painted their bodies with red and black paint . Wild halflings ' primary weapon was the bow and they use poisoned arrow s .

title: Wild mage
