description: Wild mage Wild mages are powerful sorcerer s or specialist wizard s who have chosen to master the unpredictable art of casting wild magic , a form of arcane magic noted for its erratic behavior and random effects . Devastatingly powerful , wild mages believe the attempts of others to codify and define magic is a useless pursuit that can end only in failure . Instead , wild mages seek out what they consider magic in its purest form , accepting the risks that come along with wild magic in exchange for the chance to realize even more power in the random chance of a single spell .
description_long: Wild mage Wild mages are powerful sorcerer s or specialist wizard s who have chosen to master the unpredictable art of casting wild magic , a form of arcane magic noted for its erratic behavior and random effects . Devastatingly powerful , wild mages believe the attempts of others to codify and define magic is a useless pursuit that can end only in failure . Instead , wild mages seek out what they consider magic in its purest form , accepting the risks that come along with wild magic in exchange for the chance to realize even more power in the random chance of a single spell . Like other chaos sorcerer s , wild mages draw their power from the entropic power of the elemental plane s , which they may gain through unusually potent exposure to the forces that run there , such as through birth on one such plane or survived infection by a slaad i tadpole . Culture . While all arcane spellcaster s accept the fact that magic is a powerful and often unpredictable force , most believe that through the proper training and diligence it is something that one can learn to control .

title: Wild magic
description: Wild magic Wild magic zones were areas where the Weave was damaged or distorted . In such areas , a spell could backfire upon its caster , target the wrong location , be dramatically increased in power , or indeed , anything could occur . These areas were thought to have been caused by the titanic battles of the god s during the Time of Troubles .
description_long: Wild magic Wild magic zones were areas where the Weave was damaged or distorted . In such areas , a spell could backfire upon its caster , target the wrong location , be dramatically increased in power , or indeed , anything could occur . These areas were thought to have been caused by the titanic battles of the god s during the Time of Troubles . Wild - magic zones were the first areas where raw magic burst forth in the Spellplague . Wild mages and the school of wild magic . Thorough study of the wild magic zones after the Time of Troubles led to the young spellcasting tradition of wild mage s , who learned to tap directly into the raw magic of the Weave , independent of location . To access this power , they relinquished some of the control exercised by conventional mages and accepted the fluctuating and sometimes chaotic results of their spells . The spells of their school of wild magic were open only to these specialists . As a way of powering spells different from the traditional schools of magic , wild magic was considered a school of thaumaturgy . It was not opposed to any other schools . Wild surges .

title: Wildcat stalker
description: Wildcat stalker Wildcat stalkers are beastmaster ranger s who have a special bond with feline s such as panther s or wildcat s . Less social than other animals , felines are nonetheless valuable as beast companions for their stealth and swiftness and wildcat stalkers seek to evoke these qualities within themselves by taking on a feline as their friend and ally . Wildcat stalkers learn to mimic the behavior of felines , darting in silently only to retreat as swiftly as they come .
description_long: Wildcat stalker Wildcat stalkers are beastmaster ranger s who have a special bond with feline s such as panther s or wildcat s . Less social than other animals , felines are nonetheless valuable as beast companions for their stealth and swiftness and wildcat stalkers seek to evoke these qualities within themselves by taking on a feline as their friend and ally . Wildcat stalkers learn to mimic the behavior of felines , darting in silently only to retreat as swiftly as they come . Advanced senses , swift strikes , surprise , and cunning are the key weapons of a wildcat stalker , as they are for their feline companion . This similarity of methodology is what drives and binds the two together into a deadly pair , each becoming a strong warrior unto their own but an even stronger unit together . More close partners than one mind , wildcat stalkers and their companions are nonetheless bound closely , moving together silently and inseparably . Abilities . Wildcat stalkers seek to emulate the nature of their beast companions , using stealth and guile to overcome weak and powerful foes alike .

title: Wilddwarf Brigade
description: Wilddwarf Brigade The Wilddwarf Brigade ( also known as the Wilddwarves ) was a dwarven battlerager squad in Citadel Adbar . History . In 1484 DR , the Wilddwarves were led by a dwarf simply known as Crunch .
description_long: Wilddwarf Brigade The Wilddwarf Brigade ( also known as the Wilddwarves ) was a dwarven battlerager squad in Citadel Adbar . History . In 1484 DR , the Wilddwarves were led by a dwarf simply known as Crunch . In that year , Crunch and other Wilddwarves were present , with many of them killed , during an orcish sneak attack in which King Bromm was killed by Arauthator and Hartusk . Tactics . The Wilddwarves drank liquor before battle . One of their main tactics involved the use of " dwarf tossers " : pairs of dwarves holding a plank on which another Wilddwarf stood ; the pairs subsequently tossed their target dwarf into battle .

title: Wilderness domain
description: Wilderness domain The forests and plains , deserts and mountains and all the places untouched by the hand of civilization have a connection with the deities of the wilderness domain . Corellon , the protector , is one of these deities , as seen by a lot of the forests in the reaches of the feywild has had there lush beauty shaped by him . And the beauty of the archetypal forest homes that the eladrin reside in are one of the many lush examples of his contributions to nature .
description_long: Wilderness domain The forests and plains , deserts and mountains and all the places untouched by the hand of civilization have a connection with the deities of the wilderness domain . Corellon , the protector , is one of these deities , as seen by a lot of the forests in the reaches of the feywild has had there lush beauty shaped by him . And the beauty of the archetypal forest homes that the eladrin reside in are one of the many lush examples of his contributions to nature . Mielikki both Sheela Peryroyl champion the cause of harmony with nature . They think that people can get the benifits from nature without over taxing it or destroying or exploiting it . The father of forest Silvanus easily brings life to his wild forests whom is protected by his druids . He is know to be more militant in the protection his woods than other deities , but the vengefulness that he is known for is over exaggerated . Power of wilderness domain . Any divine caster that worships a deity who claims the wilderness domain may choose to channel the deities powers within the domain , and when the caster choses the domain she will become more skilled in her nature knowledge .

title: Wildfire
description: Wildfire Wildfire was a peculiar phenomenon observed once or twice a year in the city of Raven ' s Bluff and was defined as the ability to use magic when placed in dangerous situations , albeit haphazardly and in a chaotic fashion . It manifested itself in a small portion of the residents , and people who exhibited signs of wildfire were always native residents of Raven ' s Bluff who had no formal training in the arcane arts . The Warlord Myrkyssa Jelan discovered the reason for this : a wild mythal , built by the Dark Elves .
description_long: Wildfire Wildfire was a peculiar phenomenon observed once or twice a year in the city of Raven ' s Bluff and was defined as the ability to use magic when placed in dangerous situations , albeit haphazardly and in a chaotic fashion . It manifested itself in a small portion of the residents , and people who exhibited signs of wildfire were always native residents of Raven ' s Bluff who had no formal training in the arcane arts . The Warlord Myrkyssa Jelan discovered the reason for this : a wild mythal , built by the Dark Elves . The mythal ' s magic seeped into the air , earth , and water surrounding Raven ' s Bluff , and was the source of wildfire .

title: Wildhound Court
description: Wildhound Court Wildhound Court was a courtyard in the Mountainside neighborhood of Waterdeep . It ' s name was derived from the strange effect it had on stray dogs who seem to be attracted to the courtyard by an old curse . Dogs who entered the courtyard often turned savage and formed a pack even if they were normally docile .
description_long: Wildhound Court Wildhound Court was a courtyard in the Mountainside neighborhood of Waterdeep . It ' s name was derived from the strange effect it had on stray dogs who seem to be attracted to the courtyard by an old curse . Dogs who entered the courtyard often turned savage and formed a pack even if they were normally docile .

title: Wildwoods
description: Wildwoods Wildwoods was a mansion located in the King ' s Forest near Waymoot in Cormyr . Inhabitants . The original owner of the mansion was a wizard named Orthaerus Manycloaks .
description_long: Wildwoods Wildwoods was a mansion located in the King ' s Forest near Waymoot in Cormyr . Inhabitants . The original owner of the mansion was a wizard named Orthaerus Manycloaks . Orthaerus was slain during a spell - duel by the traveling wizard Endarthar , who then assumed ownership of the estate . Rumors and Legends . After his death , the ghost of Orthaerus still resided within the mansion , jumping on any opportunity to make Endarthar ' s life miserable .

title: Wilfred
description: Wilfred Private Wilfred was a male human living in Neverwinter in 1484 DR , serving as soldier in the army of Lord Dagult Neverember . Under orders from Sergeant Knox , he fought against an undead horde commanded by Valindra Shadowmantle . He was the first to meet a new adventurer arriving in the city .
description_long: Wilfred Private Wilfred was a male human living in Neverwinter in 1484 DR , serving as soldier in the army of Lord Dagult Neverember . Under orders from Sergeant Knox , he fought against an undead horde commanded by Valindra Shadowmantle . He was the first to meet a new adventurer arriving in the city . He led the adventurer to Lt . Josef Linkletter ' s camp and later fought beside the adventurer against the undead , but was finally killed by Valindra herself . Appendix . Behind the scenes . Wilfred is the first character the player meets at the entrance to the city .

title: Will - o ' - wisp
description: Will - o ' - wisp Will - o ' - wisps , also called will - o ' - the - wisps , are malicious fey creatures often seen floating over lakes or within swamps . They enjoy leading lone travelers off the beaten path at night . As the traveler follows the ghost ly light into a dangerous swamp , the will - o ' - wisp then extinguishes its light , leaving the traveler lost within a dark swamp where it is easy pray for the wisp or any other malicious creatures .
description_long: Will - o ' - wisp Will - o ' - wisps , also called will - o ' - the - wisps , are malicious fey creatures often seen floating over lakes or within swamps . They enjoy leading lone travelers off the beaten path at night . As the traveler follows the ghost ly light into a dangerous swamp , the will - o ' - wisp then extinguishes its light , leaving the traveler lost within a dark swamp where it is easy pray for the wisp or any other malicious creatures . The wisp then feeds on the fear and despair of the lost traveler .

title: Will Turnstone
description: Will Turnstone Will Turnstone was a halfling scout and a companion of Dorn Graybrook during the Rage of Dragons of 1373 DR . History . Will was a halfing scout .
description_long: Will Turnstone Will Turnstone was a halfling scout and a companion of Dorn Graybrook during the Rage of Dragons of 1373 DR . History . Will was a halfing scout . At one point , he joined the mercenary band of Dorn Graybrook , which specialized in dragon slaying . In 1373 DR , like all his companions , he became involved in Sammaster ' s plot . He survived until the end of the mission and decided to follow his companion Raryn Snowstealer back to the Great Glacier .

title: William
description: William William was a villager of Highcliff on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . William was a villager , who got tired of his life , since he had take care of his child with Juni every day ( which made him look much older ) .
description_long: William William was a villager of Highcliff on the Sword Coast North in the 1370s DR . History . William was a villager , who got tired of his life , since he had take care of his child with Juni every day ( which made him look much older ) . The Kalach - Cha could get the task from Juni to find him . The Kalach - Cha could persuade him to go back to his house or to let him go . Afterwards , the Kalach - Cha would need to return to Juni and tell her what William did or lie to her .

title: William ( halfling )
description: William ( halfling ) William was the mayor of the halfling town of Waukeshire in Bloodstone Barony in 1357 DR . Activities . William liked to make long , formal speeches .
description_long: William ( halfling ) William was the mayor of the halfling town of Waukeshire in Bloodstone Barony in 1357 DR . Activities . William liked to make long , formal speeches . History . In 1357 DR , William and his people met Gareth Dragonsbane ' s party . Later he joined the council that ruled the Barony . In 1359 DR , William and his people had joined the Alliance of Belt Watchers with local dwarves and centaur s .

title: William Horgath
description: William Horgath Duke William Horgath , most commonly know as William the Lazy , was the eight duke of Arcata in Damara in 1357 DR and 1359 DR . History . In 1357 William the Lazy , in league with the Grandfather of Assassins , gathered an army to conquer the Barony of Bloodstone .
description_long: William Horgath Duke William Horgath , most commonly know as William the Lazy , was the eight duke of Arcata in Damara in 1357 DR and 1359 DR . History . In 1357 William the Lazy , in league with the Grandfather of Assassins , gathered an army to conquer the Barony of Bloodstone . However his troops were defeated by the Bloodstone army led by Gareth Dragonsbane . He surrendered to Gareth that imposed to him no penalties . At 1359 DR William was deeply unpopular in his own lands , so much so that in the mining village of Sudrav , it was not uncommon for effigies of him to be burned .

title: William O ' Connor
description: William O ' Connor William O ' Connor is an award - winning fantasy illustrator who has contributed to many role - playing games . He is the author and illustrator of the Dracopedia trilogy . Education .
description_long: William O ' Connor William O ' Connor is an award - winning fantasy illustrator who has contributed to many role - playing games . He is the author and illustrator of the Dracopedia trilogy . Education . O ' Connor was educated at the Huntington School of Fine Arts and attended college at , the , and . Career . In addition to work in other gaming systems , O ' Connor has contributed artwork to Dungeons & Dragons sourcebooks since 1995 .

title: Willing Smile
description: Willing Smile The Willing Smile was a brothel in Suzail with a reputation as a seedy establishment that employed workers too young or too old for mainstream clients . In reality , it was a clean and quiet , if somewhat rundown house of pleasure . Inhabitants .
description_long: Willing Smile The Willing Smile was a brothel in Suzail with a reputation as a seedy establishment that employed workers too young or too old for mainstream clients . In reality , it was a clean and quiet , if somewhat rundown house of pleasure . Inhabitants . The proprietress , Mother Maraedra , was an old friend of Elminster .

title: Willow
description: Willow The willow was a type of tree found in Faerûn . Locations . Willow trees with droopy branches grew on hillsides in the Rimwood area of the forest of Cormanthor .
description_long: Willow The willow was a type of tree found in Faerûn . Locations . Willow trees with droopy branches grew on hillsides in the Rimwood area of the forest of Cormanthor . They also grew within the Vast Swamp . Varieties . The weeping willow was a variety of willow with long drooping branches . They were also found in the Vast Swamp , such as around the Skull Staff . The sturdy gray willow was found in the Farsea Marshes . Its bark was used by the Marsh Drovers to make an effective bug repellent .

title: Wilton Mortaire
description: Wilton Mortaire Wilton Mortaire was a sergeant in the Zhent army that occupied Daggerdale in 1369 DR but was also an honorable man . History . Wilton Mortaire was a member of the Zhentarim and became a sergeant in the Zhent army that occupied Daggerdale in 1369 DR .
description_long: Wilton Mortaire Wilton Mortaire was a sergeant in the Zhent army that occupied Daggerdale in 1369 DR but was also an honorable man . History . Wilton Mortaire was a member of the Zhentarim and became a sergeant in the Zhent army that occupied Daggerdale in 1369 DR . When resistance fighters started the last battle against the invaders , Mortaire and some of his men retreated into a warehouse . Adventurers with the resistance had the option of attacking and slaying Mortaire and his fellows or convince him to go out and talk .

title: Wind ( province )
description: Wind ( province ) The province of wind in the Zakhara n view of magic was a group of spells related to the element of air , felt most clearly in the free - roaming winds in the Land of Fate . The four elemental provinces played a very similar role for Zakharan magic - users as the eight ( or nine ) schools of magic did for Faerûn ian ones . Elemental mage s in Zakhara specialized exclusively in one province , like wind , while sorcerers took spells from two provinces , shunning the other two .
description_long: Wind ( province ) The province of wind in the Zakhara n view of magic was a group of spells related to the element of air , felt most clearly in the free - roaming winds in the Land of Fate . The four elemental provinces played a very similar role for Zakharan magic - users as the eight ( or nine ) schools of magic did for Faerûn ian ones . Elemental mage s in Zakhara specialized exclusively in one province , like wind , while sorcerers took spells from two provinces , shunning the other two . Unlike elementalist s , magic - users from the Land of Fate recognized no opposition between wind and sand . Paths of power . Zakharan practicioners of path magic recognized four paths of power within the province of wind :

title: Wind blade
description: Wind blade Wind blade was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a wind - made invisible sword that the caster could instantly extend and retract from his hand .
description_long: Wind blade Wind blade was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created a wind - made invisible sword that the caster could instantly extend and retract from his hand . The wind blade was not actually held in the caster ' s hand , so he could hold something else while using the weapon . The blade sounded like roaring wind when swung and bludgeoned targets with force . Components . This spell did not require physical components to cast .

title: Wind blast
description: Wind blast Wind blast was a divine magic spell given to priests of Aerdrie Faenya . It created a powerful gust of wind that struck all in the area of effect with blunt force . Effects .
description_long: Wind blast Wind blast was a divine magic spell given to priests of Aerdrie Faenya . It created a powerful gust of wind that struck all in the area of effect with blunt force . Effects . When cast , this spell created a single burst of wind in a cone shape emanating from the caster ' s outstretched hand . The minimum cone was 25 ft ( 7 . 6 m ) long and 5 ft ( 1 . 5 m ) wide at the base . Higher level casters could extend this out to a maximum of 50 ft ( 15 m ) with a diameter of 10 ft ( 3 m ) . Human - sized creatures and larger caught in the cone were struck as if by a blunt weapon . Smaller creatures were also struck and had to resist being thrown backward up to 25 ft ( 7 . 6 m ) . If they failed to resist , and collided with a solid , immovable object , they could suffer additional damage and be stunned for a few minutes . Components . In addition to verbal and somatic components , this spell required a small paper fan ( which was consumed in the casting ) and the priest ' s holy symbol .

title: Wind burial
description: Wind burial A wind burial was a common type of burial used by the Tuigan . The bodies of commoners were placed on simple wooden frames . Offerings were placed around the body , and it was left exposed to the elements until the remains and structure crumbled into dust .
description_long: Wind burial A wind burial was a common type of burial used by the Tuigan . The bodies of commoners were placed on simple wooden frames . Offerings were placed around the body , and it was left exposed to the elements until the remains and structure crumbled into dust .

title: Wind carpet
description: Wind carpet Wind carpet was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell allowed the caster , or someone they touched , to command a flying carpet created from a glowing magical force .
description_long: Wind carpet Wind carpet was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell allowed the caster , or someone they touched , to command a flying carpet created from a glowing magical force . Casters who commanded more magical might could create larger carpets compared to weaker wizard s . Their carpets could also carry far more weight . The carpet flew through the air quickly and deftly but was susceptible to normal and magical damage . A " dispel magic " spell would instantly destroy it . The carpet flew smoothly , allowing delicate functions such as spellcasting to be performed by the primary controller during travel . The controller remained firmly planted to the carpet even if they were flying upside down . However , any inanimate objects , or other occupants that were not held or tied down could fall off . Only someone touched by the caster could command the carpet . Components . This spell required a scrap of woven cloth to cast .

title: Wind compass
description: Wind compass Wind compass was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects .
description_long: Wind compass Wind compass was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . This spell was only usable by wizard s . Effects . This spell created a small moaning wind in the caster ' s ear that only he or she could hear . The caster chose a direction and whenever their ear faced that direction they would hear a steady tone . Moving the ear from the selected direction raised or lowered the pitch of the tone . This spell lasted for several hours based on the caster ' s power . Components . This spell required a bit of earth mixed with spittle to cast .

title: Wind of Fate
description: Wind of Fate The Wind of Fate was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara who followed the teachings of Haku , the Zakharan god of freedom and personal independence . The symbol of the Wind of Fate was a blowgun . Activities .
description_long: Wind of Fate The Wind of Fate was a holy slayer organization in Zakhara who followed the teachings of Haku , the Zakharan god of freedom and personal independence . The symbol of the Wind of Fate was a blowgun . Activities . Experts in desert lore and survival , members of the Wind of Fate infiltrated every major desert tribe within the two great deserts of the Land of Fate . Organization . The Wind of Fate was the only holy slayer organization where all of the members were male . Base of Operations . Holy slayers from the Wind of Fate were active within the High Desert and the Haunted Lands . Their citadel was hidden within the Genies ' Anvil .

title: Wind of Quick Death
description: Wind of Quick Death The Wind of Quick Death was a pirate who sailed the Golden Gulf in 1367 DR . Activities . The Wind of Quick Death attacked merchant ships traveling along the Southeastern Sea Route until he was successfully defeated by the Admirality of Huzuz .
description_long: Wind of Quick Death The Wind of Quick Death was a pirate who sailed the Golden Gulf in 1367 DR . Activities . The Wind of Quick Death attacked merchant ships traveling along the Southeastern Sea Route until he was successfully defeated by the Admirality of Huzuz . History . Aided by a pair of djinn , ships from Huzuz attacked and killed the Wind of Quick Death upon the open waters . His head was returned to Huzuz and the Grand Caliph rewarded the captains involved with a magical cutlass .

title: Wind servant
description: Wind servant Wind servant was a conjuration spell that allowed the caster to summon and control a weak air elemental to manipulate air currents and winds . There was a divine and an arcane version of this spell that differed mainly in duration and scope . Effects .
description_long: Wind servant Wind servant was a conjuration spell that allowed the caster to summon and control a weak air elemental to manipulate air currents and winds . There was a divine and an arcane version of this spell that differed mainly in duration and scope . Effects . The divine version of this spell lasted only a few minutes , but the caster was able to coerce the " wind servant " to exert fine control over the air in a small area , enough to extinguish small fires ; create stinging whirlwinds of dust , sand , or snow ; hinder attacks by arrows and light missiles ; and carry or push objects within the spell ' s weight limit . Ordinary objects up to about a pound ( 0 . 45 kg ) per caster level could be carried at a normal human walking pace . If the object had a large surface area compared to its weight , like a scroll , a cloak , or a haystack , this weight limit was doubled . If the object was designed to use the wind , like a ship ' s sail or a winged flying creature , the weight limit was increased tenfold .

title: Wind shadow
description: Wind shadow Wind shadow was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell caused the target to assume a nearly weightless , translucent form that was capable of gliding on a breeze .
description_long: Wind shadow Wind shadow was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell caused the target to assume a nearly weightless , translucent form that was capable of gliding on a breeze . Strong gales slowed any target attempting to move while under the influence of this spell . The target could not speak out loud until the spell ended . Components . This spell required a piece of silk or gossamer to cast .

title: Wind walker
description: Wind walker Wind walkers , or maswat - rih , were rare creatures from the Elemental Plane of Air where they served the djinn . They could be found in Zakhara high in the mountains or in caves located deep underground . A distinct whistling or roaring sound preceded the approach of a group of wind walkers .
description_long: Wind walker Wind walkers , or maswat - rih , were rare creatures from the Elemental Plane of Air where they served the djinn . They could be found in Zakhara high in the mountains or in caves located deep underground . A distinct whistling or roaring sound preceded the approach of a group of wind walkers . Description . These creatures appeared like a mass of constantly writhing serpents . They were barely visible unless viewed while within a sandstorm . Combat . Wind walkers could use telepathy to hear any thought within 100 yards ( 91 m ) . A group of wind walkers working together could use this ability up to 300 yards ( 274 m ) . The primary attack of a wind walker was a blast of forceful air . Any gas based attack used against them could be dispersed quickly , causing minimal damage . All sounds of battle with a wind walker were muffled by the sound of roaring wind . Thus , orders from superior officers were nearly useless when facing wind walkers . As partially ethereal creatures , wind walkers could only be attacked by other ethereal creatures such as djinn , invisible stalker s , or ghost s . Magical weapons were needed to physically strike a wind walker .

title: Wind wall
description: Wind wall Wind wall is an evocation spell that deflects arrows , smaller creatures , and gases . Effect . An invisible vertical curtain of wind appears .
description_long: Wind wall Wind wall is an evocation spell that deflects arrows , smaller creatures , and gases . Effect . An invisible vertical curtain of wind appears . It is 2 feet thick and of considerable strength . It is a roaring blast sufficient to blow away any bird smaller than an eagle or tear papers and similar materials from unsuspecting hands . ( A Reflex save allows a creature to maintain its grasp on an object . ) Tiny and Small flying creatures cannot pass through the barrier . Loose materials and cloth garments fly upward when caught in a " wind wall " . Arrows and bolts are deflected upward and miss , while any other normal ranged weapon passing through the wall suffers a 30 % miss chance . ( A giant - thrown boulder , a siege projectile , and other massive ranged weapons are not affected . ) Gases , most gaseous breath weapons , and creatures in gaseous form cannot pass through the wall ( although it is no barrier to incorporeal creatures ) . While the wall must be vertical , you can shape it in any continuous path along the ground that you like . It is possible to create cylindrical or square wind walls to enclose specific points .

title: Windharrow
description: Windharrow Windharrow was a high - ranking member of the Cult of the Howling Hatred at the Temple of Howling Hatred in Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . He was at heart an opportunist .
description_long: Windharrow Windharrow was a high - ranking member of the Cult of the Howling Hatred at the Temple of Howling Hatred in Tyar - Besil during the Elemental Evil crisis . Personality . He was at heart an opportunist . Windharrow was loyal to Aerisi Kalinoth as long as he feared her power . However , confronted with danger to his life or a richer offer , he would betray the air cult without a backward glance . Possessions . In battle , Windharrow wielded a rapier and wore studded leather . History . Born as Harald Grayspear , he was a rake and a bandit until he met Aerisi Kalinoth when she was still with her family . Harald charmed and flattered his way into her favor . When Aerisi joined the Cult of the Howling Hatred , Harald , now renamed by his lady as Windharrow , loyally followed . Aerisi instructed him to gather a band of flutists from the ranks of new converts to the air cult , the Windwyrds . In 1491 DR , Windharrow was with his flutist minions at the Temple of Howling Hatred in Tyar - Besil until he was confronted by some adventurers .

title: Winding Water
description: Winding Water The Winding Water was a river located along the Sword Coast , roughly 250 miles north of Baldur ' s Gate and the River Chionthar . It flowed from several tributaries , some as far away as the Marsh of Chelimber , and eventually flowed into the Sea of Swords south of the Troll Hills . Notable locations along the river were Boareskyr Bridge , Trollclaw Ford , and Serpent ' s Cowl .
description_long: Winding Water The Winding Water was a river located along the Sword Coast , roughly 250 miles north of Baldur ' s Gate and the River Chionthar . It flowed from several tributaries , some as far away as the Marsh of Chelimber , and eventually flowed into the Sea of Swords south of the Troll Hills . Notable locations along the river were Boareskyr Bridge , Trollclaw Ford , and Serpent ' s Cowl . The river also formed the northern boundary of the Fields of the Dead .

title: Winding Way
description: Winding Way The Winding Way was a tavern located in the center of Soubar in the Western Heartlands . History . The tavern was also the home of Mag , a mysterious woman who owned the bar around 1367 DR .
description_long: Winding Way The Winding Way was a tavern located in the center of Soubar in the Western Heartlands . History . The tavern was also the home of Mag , a mysterious woman who owned the bar around 1367 DR . Geography . The Winding Way was located by the ruins of the old temple or abbey of Bane , that was the heart of the village .

title: Windle
description: Windle Windle was a member of the Harpers in 1489 DR . Personality . Windle was a sly but dutiful individual .
description_long: Windle Windle was a member of the Harpers in 1489 DR . Personality . Windle was a sly but dutiful individual . History . Windle was a Harper rogue based in Neverwinter ' s graveyard . In 1489 DR , she was the Harper delegated to help a hired adventuring party to defeat the great dragon Claugiyliamatar of Kryptgarden Forest . The Harpers ' main objectives were to investigate some Red Wizards of Thay inside the new faction of the Cult of the Dragon and to gain the alliance of fey lords of the forest .

title: Windon Lumbus
description: Windon Lumbus Windon Lumbus was a halfling boy in the Moonsea . Activities . Windon lived with his family at the Lumbus farm , near the village of The Stop .
description_long: Windon Lumbus Windon Lumbus was a halfling boy in the Moonsea . Activities . Windon lived with his family at the Lumbus farm , near the village of The Stop . History . During the Rage of Demons , a group of goblin s wearing strange robes attacked the Lumbus farm , killing all the Lumbuses while they slept . Windon however managed to escape and hid himself in the barn among the surviving goats . Personality . Windon trusted halflings and human s but was shy with other races . He knew much about goblins , as they fascinated his young mind .

title: Windriders
description: Windriders The Windriders were an all - but - retired mercenary company based in Chondath . History . They fought during the war against the arcanaloth Yrkhetep and were decisive in defeating the yugoloth ' s army in Hades .
description_long: Windriders The Windriders were an all - but - retired mercenary company based in Chondath . History . They fought during the war against the arcanaloth Yrkhetep and were decisive in defeating the yugoloth ' s army in Hades . Membership . The Windriders were griffon - mounted cavalry . Contracts . By 1358 DR , the Windriders worked only for the glory .

title: Windrise Ports
description: Windrise Ports The Windrise Ports were a loose confederation of independent , free port cities on the southeastern shores of the Dragon Sea . Those ports served as bastions of trade and civilization in Returned Abeir . Geography .
description_long: Windrise Ports The Windrise Ports were a loose confederation of independent , free port cities on the southeastern shores of the Dragon Sea . Those ports served as bastions of trade and civilization in Returned Abeir . Geography . The Windrise Ports were located on the eastern shore of the Dragon Sea . Government . Each port was an independent and self - ruling state , rival to each other but able to cooperate when was needed . Background . Tarmalune was the most important city in the Windrise Ports , although it was not very welcoming to outsiders if those individuals were slaves or didn ' t had enough money to live in a city were money was so important as it was in Tarmalune . Whereas the other Windrise Ports , although each an independent city , different to each other and with its own feel and character , were all united by three common goals — the pursuit of wealth , their tolerance of outsiders , which the leaders believed was good for commerce ; and their disdain for Tarmalune ’ s prominence .

title: Windsong Tower
description: Windsong Tower Windsong Tower was the physical location of a school of magic in the elven city of Myth Drannor . After Myth Drannor ' s fall , the central tower was all but razed but other portions of the school survived . As of 1376 DR , many ruins of the school still existed .
description_long: Windsong Tower Windsong Tower was the physical location of a school of magic in the elven city of Myth Drannor . After Myth Drannor ' s fall , the central tower was all but razed but other portions of the school survived . As of 1376 DR , many ruins of the school still existed . Structure . The tower consisted of a central tower , with structures in the boughs of a massive oak , structures in the boughs of a Shadowsong Tree , and extra - dimensional spaces . Entry to the school was mainly by portal using a special ring , a Windsong Towerkin ring , that served as a special portal key . By 1376 , the physical tower was all but destroyed and the structures in the trees were deteriorating , but the extra - dimensional spaces were generally in good condition .

title: Windsoul genasi
description: Windsoul genasi Windsoul genasi , also known as air genasi , are one of the five main " manifestations " or subraces of the genasi race . The name " windsoul genasi " usually refers to genasi for whom the manifestation is their primary one , though like all of the genasi manifestations it is possible for genasi of another subrace to learn how to manifest it . Ecology .
description_long: Windsoul genasi Windsoul genasi , also known as air genasi , are one of the five main " manifestations " or subraces of the genasi race . The name " windsoul genasi " usually refers to genasi for whom the manifestation is their primary one , though like all of the genasi manifestations it is possible for genasi of another subrace to learn how to manifest it . Ecology . Physical characteristics . Most genasi are descended from djinn , air genie s , though other origins exist , and the touch of the elemental power of wind and air shapes the genasi physique . Like all genasi , the exact appearance of a windsoul genasi varies from individual to individual but all windsoul genasi have " szuldar " , typically light blue in color . Many also have blue or gray ice crystal spikes crowning their head as well as silvery - hued skin . Compared with other genasi , those of the windsoul manifestation are often slightly quicker , but also somewhat physically weaker . However , just as the wind may vary in strength and temperature , so do windsoul genasi vary in appearance and a few have other distinguishing features .

title: Windtomb
description: Windtomb Windtomb was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created an impenetrable tomb of wind that surrounded the target .
description_long: Windtomb Windtomb was a spell unique to Zakhara , the Land of Fate . Effects . This spell created an impenetrable tomb of wind that surrounded the target . This spell could be used on virtually anything ranging in size from a small animal to a fortress . Living creatures that were entombed entered a state of suspended animation similar to a " temporal stasis " spell . The caster could determine if the windtomb was silent or if it howled or moaned . The cast also decided if the windtomb was invisible or consisted of colored air . Invisible windtombs imparted the invisibility to the target of the spell . Colored air blurred the contents of the windtomb . The caster also determined whether or not divination spells would ascertain the nature of the entombed target . Living creatures trying to break into or out of the wind tomb were thrown about and suffered damage accordingly . Creatures shifted into another plane could escape damage , though they still could not penetrate the windtomb . All magical attempts to enter or exit the windtomb failed . Windtombs were permanent unless dispelled by the caster or by using a full " wish " , making them the ultimate prisons or vaults .

title: Windvane
description: Windvane Windvane was a spear forged by the drow wizard Vizeran DeVir , and wielded by Aerisi Kalinoth during her time as the leader of the Cult of the Howling Hatred . History . Vizeran DeVir , a drow worshiper of the Elder Elemental Eye , forged the spear " Windvane " using part of the essence of Yan - C - Bin , Prince of Evil Air , in a temple known as the Fane of the Eye .
description_long: Windvane Windvane was a spear forged by the drow wizard Vizeran DeVir , and wielded by Aerisi Kalinoth during her time as the leader of the Cult of the Howling Hatred . History . Vizeran DeVir , a drow worshiper of the Elder Elemental Eye , forged the spear " Windvane " using part of the essence of Yan - C - Bin , Prince of Evil Air , in a temple known as the Fane of the Eye . He left the spear to await its prophesied bearer . Sometime in 1491 DR , Aerisi Kalinoth found the spear and used it to open an elemental node to the Elemental Plane of Air to summon Yan - C - Bin . The weapon was destroyed by adventures who used it to seal the node .

title: Windwalker ( artifact )
description: Windwalker ( artifact ) The Windwalker was a magical artifact of the ancient Rus , who brought it to the eastern parts of Faerun , where their descendants , the Rashemi , continued to use it . Description . The artifact itself was an amulet resembling a small , golden dagger , 3 inches long , encased in a rune - carved sheath hung from a chain ( also of gold ) .
description_long: Windwalker ( artifact ) The Windwalker was a magical artifact of the ancient Rus , who brought it to the eastern parts of Faerun , where their descendants , the Rashemi , continued to use it . Description . The artifact itself was an amulet resembling a small , golden dagger , 3 inches long , encased in a rune - carved sheath hung from a chain ( also of gold ) . The runes were in the ancient language of the Rus , and the metal was described as worn and darkened with age . If someone unsheathed the dagger , the hilt twisted off to reveal a tiny chisel , and also that the base of the sheath was hollow . History . In distant days , the folk of Rus swept over much of the continent of Faerûn , raiding and pillaging the costal lands . Some bands of Rus took the rivers and traveled inland , making their way across the Anauroch ( this was before it became a desert ) to the lands now known as Rashemen . Their descendants , who retained some cultural echoes , remained in the country and can still be found there . The Windwalker amulet was created by the Rus to help them cast their ancient form of magic , known as rune lore , and they brought it with them to their new homes .

title: Windwalker ( novel )
description: Windwalker ( novel ) Windwalker is the third and final book in the Starlight and Shadows trilogy by Elaine Cunningham . Summary . The novel opens with the Battle of Immil Dale ( 1360 DR ) , in which the Tuigan Horde has engaged the berserkers of Rashemen in a dead - magic zone .
description_long: Windwalker ( novel ) Windwalker is the third and final book in the Starlight and Shadows trilogy by Elaine Cunningham . Summary . The novel opens with the Battle of Immil Dale ( 1360 DR ) , in which the Tuigan Horde has engaged the berserkers of Rashemen in a dead - magic zone . The Tuigan send forth zombies to attack the Rashemi and would have nearly succeeded had not young Fyodor charged forth against orders to win the day . Because Fyodor is unable to control his berserker rages , he is given a blunt sword in anticipation of his death , but his grandmother , the elder witch Zofia , commands him to travel west to find the Windwalker to save both himself and the land of Rashemen , whose magic is failing . Back in the present day ( 1361 DR ) , Liriel Baenre and Fyodor are enroute to Rashemen in order to return the Windwalker . They disembark from a ship in Waterdeep and travel to the Promenade of the Dark Maiden near Skullport , where Qilue Veladorn attempts to speed their way via a portal . However , Liriel inadvertently leads Lolth ' s power into the temple , despite ( or perhaps because of ) having turned away from the Spider Queen .

title: Wine
description: Wine Wine was an alcoholic beverage popular throughout the Realms . Most wines were poured into wooden casks for transport . The casks were then tapped by innkeepers or other consumers .
description_long: Wine Wine was an alcoholic beverage popular throughout the Realms . Most wines were poured into wooden casks for transport . The casks were then tapped by innkeepers or other consumers . Some monasteries experimented with bottling alcoholic beverages such as wines and some merchants were known to bottle wine from casks .

title: Winefiddle
description: Winefiddle Winefiddle was once a member of the group known as the King ' s Men . Physical Description . He is a rotund man with thinning brown hair and puffy red cheeks .
description_long: Winefiddle Winefiddle was once a member of the group known as the King ' s Men . Physical Description . He is a rotund man with thinning brown hair and puffy red cheeks . There is a scar on his belly where he was once stabbed with a goblin ' s spear . His holy symbol , a plain silver disk , can be found around his neck .

title: Winemaker genie
description: Winemaker genie Winemaker genies were unique tasked genie s dedicated to making the best possible wines in Zakhara . They were believed to have originally been created from marid and therefore considered by some to be the greatest of all tasked genies . Some hakima s and seers believed that winemaker genies were exiled noble marid s who were punished for transgressions within the marid court .
description_long: Winemaker genie Winemaker genies were unique tasked genie s dedicated to making the best possible wines in Zakhara . They were believed to have originally been created from marid and therefore considered by some to be the greatest of all tasked genies . Some hakima s and seers believed that winemaker genies were exiled noble marid s who were punished for transgressions within the marid court . Description . Focused on their vineyards , winemaker genies were quiet creatures . These genies possessed the head of a cat , body of a dog , and a long elephant - like trunk that they used to crush grapes . They stood erect at about four to five feet ( 1 . 2 – 1 . 5 m ) tall . These creatures did not wear clothes but used grape leaves to cover themselves . Combat . These genies were poor fighters . If angered enough , they could use their trunk to grab and squeeze enemies . Spraying wine from their trunks was another useful attack as it could temporarily blind opponents .

title: Wing - ta
description: Wing - ta The Wing - ta was a monastic order based in the town of Goisho in Koryo . For many years , the Wing - ta monks tended a shrine outside Goisho , the centerpiece of which was the Hu ' i Wing , a massive magical brazier that revealed the future and was one of the most valued relics of Koryo . However , some ten generations before 1357 DR , Kozakura n forces stole the Hu ' i Wing and carried it off to Karak , and they built it into their fortress there .
description_long: Wing - ta The Wing - ta was a monastic order based in the town of Goisho in Koryo . For many years , the Wing - ta monks tended a shrine outside Goisho , the centerpiece of which was the Hu ' i Wing , a massive magical brazier that revealed the future and was one of the most valued relics of Koryo . However , some ten generations before 1357 DR , Kozakura n forces stole the Hu ' i Wing and carried it off to Karak , and they built it into their fortress there .

title: Winged Bulls
description: Winged Bulls The Winged Bulls were a faction within the Everlasting in 1367 DR . Base of Operations . The Winged Bulls were based in the fortress of Sarahin located deep within the Haunted Lands .
description_long: Winged Bulls The Winged Bulls were a faction within the Everlasting in 1367 DR . Base of Operations . The Winged Bulls were based in the fortress of Sarahin located deep within the Haunted Lands . Activities . Generally speaking , the Winged Bulls were the most unpolished members of the Everlasting . Most of the time the tasks they were assigned were designed simply to keep them from hindering the other members of the Everlasting in their work . They were eager and fanatical , but lacked the necessary skills to rise within the ranks . Members . The Winged Bulls were led by Nusrah bin Kerim . Rumors . The true leader of the Winged Bulls , Aida al - Irrahman , was busy in Qudra spreading propaganda .

title: Winged serpent
description: Winged serpent Winged serpents , also called “ spark snakes , ” were reptiles that lived in the jungles and forests of Zakhara . Description . These snakes appeared with a variety of colors including sky blue , emerald , and raspberry red .
description_long: Winged serpent Winged serpents , also called “ spark snakes , ” were reptiles that lived in the jungles and forests of Zakhara . Description . These snakes appeared with a variety of colors including sky blue , emerald , and raspberry red . A pair of gossamer wings moved so quickly that they were invisible unless stationary . Combat . Winged serpents were graceful and quick . Surprising one was very difficult . A bite from a winged serpent injected corrosive venom that burned the victim for several minutes . A winged serpent ’ s most dangerous attack was a special lightning - based breath weapon . If threatened , these snakes could discharge a shower of sparks that could cause clothing to burst into flame . These creatures were immune to electricity . Fire was especially damaging to their delicate wings . A winged serpent that lost their wings could not use their electrical breath weapon until they grew back . Habitat / Society . Winged serpents had an extremely high metabolism and needed to eat constantly to survive . Tropical fruit was their food of choice .

title: Wingham
description: Wingham Wingham , often callen Weird Wingham is an old half - orc of the region of Damara . Appearance . Wingham is old , his stature bent by age , bald and limping , but with a sparkle in his bright eyes locking the stares of any young woman .
description_long: Wingham Wingham , often callen Weird Wingham is an old half - orc of the region of Damara . Appearance . Wingham is old , his stature bent by age , bald and limping , but with a sparkle in his bright eyes locking the stares of any young woman . He often speaks with a lyrical barker ' s voice , mastered in his decades with his traveling troupe . Background . Wingham is the uncle of the wizard Arrayan , a relationship of deep affection for one another . Weird Wingham ' s Wacky Weapon Wielders . He is the head of a traveling merchant band called " Wingham ' s Rascals " , better known as " Weird Wingham ' s Wacky Weapon Wielders " who travel the Bloodstone Lands with their twenty colored waggons . Bards and jugglers accompany the merchants to entertain with song and dance and artstics . The troupe trades exotic goods , weapons and clothes from faraway lands and wondrous tales of distant heroes and mighty villains .

title: Wingle Spewgold
description: Wingle Spewgold Wingle Spewgold was a male gnome illusionist and thief and a spy of Glinda Scatterstar in the Rogue ' s Guild of Hillsfar in 1367 DR . Description . He used his illusions to pass as an ordinary human thief .
description_long: Wingle Spewgold Wingle Spewgold was a male gnome illusionist and thief and a spy of Glinda Scatterstar in the Rogue ' s Guild of Hillsfar in 1367 DR . Description . He used his illusions to pass as an ordinary human thief . Personality . Wingle was a very daring individual . He confided in no one about his secret identity but hoped that in time of need he could confide in paladins , good clerics , and rangers .

title: Wingstarl
description: Wingstarl The Wingstarl family was a human family of merchants in Zhentil Keep who plied their trades around the Moonsea area . The family made its fortunes by building fine temples in the Dalelands and the Moonsea in the 13th century DR . The wizard Sememmon was originally Malathar Wingstarl , a member of this family .
description_long: Wingstarl The Wingstarl family was a human family of merchants in Zhentil Keep who plied their trades around the Moonsea area . The family made its fortunes by building fine temples in the Dalelands and the Moonsea in the 13th century DR . The wizard Sememmon was originally Malathar Wingstarl , a member of this family .

title: Winking Eyes of Rhauron
description: Winking Eyes of Rhauron The Winking Eyes of Rhauron were numerous magically enchanted gemstones which , when touched bare - handed , would melt into the handler ' s hand and compel the person to attempt to assassinate a target . Description . All the gems were approximately the size of a large man ' s thumb and could be sapphire s , emerald s , diamond s , or rubies .
description_long: Winking Eyes of Rhauron The Winking Eyes of Rhauron were numerous magically enchanted gemstones which , when touched bare - handed , would melt into the handler ' s hand and compel the person to attempt to assassinate a target . Description . All the gems were approximately the size of a large man ' s thumb and could be sapphire s , emerald s , diamond s , or rubies . Effect . When held bare - handed , a spell on the gem activated , causing a visible flash . If not immediately dropped or flung blindly , the gem appeared to melt into the body of the handler . The spell on the gem caused a vision showing the face of a given quarry , giving increasing detail concerning the target ' s location every few days . Upon meeting the quarry , the spell attempted to seize full control and force an assassination attempt ( or retreat if it was unlikely to be successful ) . History . The name of the stones was apparently a bard ' s attempt to get even with an innkeeper known as Rhauron who had cheated him out of money . The true name of the enchanter was unknown . In reality , the gems were enchanted by a person in Returned Abeir who sought to assassinate persons who had fled to Faerûn .

title: Winko Battleblade
description: Winko Battleblade Winko Battleblade was a dwarf of Mithril Hall in the late 15th century DR . History . During the late stages of the War of the Silver Marches in 1485 DR , Winko and his young cousin Rollo were among the dwarves that marched from Mithril Hall to battle against the orc s and drow .
description_long: Winko Battleblade Winko Battleblade was a dwarf of Mithril Hall in the late 15th century DR . History . During the late stages of the War of the Silver Marches in 1485 DR , Winko and his young cousin Rollo were among the dwarves that marched from Mithril Hall to battle against the orc s and drow .

title: Winlof
description: Winlof Winlof was one of the many Doomguide s who were part of the contingent in Neverdeath Graveyard in Neverwinter in 1484 DR . History . She and some of her fellows became lost in the graveyard after an assault by undead .
description_long: Winlof Winlof was one of the many Doomguide s who were part of the contingent in Neverdeath Graveyard in Neverwinter in 1484 DR . History . She and some of her fellows became lost in the graveyard after an assault by undead . Winlof was the first to be rescued by an adventurer recruited to find them .

title: Winski Perorate
description: Winski Perorate Winski Perorate was Sarevok ' s mentor . Relations . He taught Sarevok " in the darkest of rituals " and helped orchestrate his intended rise to power as the new Lord of Murder .
description_long: Winski Perorate Winski Perorate was Sarevok ' s mentor . Relations . He taught Sarevok " in the darkest of rituals " and helped orchestrate his intended rise to power as the new Lord of Murder . He was not even certain himself of Sarevok ' s interpretation of the prophecy of the Bhaalspawn , that causing enough slaughter would cause him to ascend , and he was convinced even success would mean his own death . Nevertheless , he wanted to help him ascend in order to be remembered for his role in history . History . When Gorion ' s Ward foiled Sarevok ' s plans by exposing him in front of the surviving Grand Duke s of Baldur ' s Gate , Winski teleported in and took Sarevok away by magic , hoping to save his life in spite of the suddenly low odds of Sarevok ever ascending . The two fled to a maze under the base of the local thieves ' guild , but at the entrance of the Undercity Sarevok cut Winski down in retaliation for saving him rather than helping him to fight the Grand Dukes , their guards , and Gorion ' s Ward head on .

title: Winter ' s Cradle Tavern
description: Winter ' s Cradle Tavern The Winter ' s Cradle Tavern was a tavern in Easthaven within the Ten - Towns of Icewind Dale . Structure . Located in the northern part of Easthaven , the wooden building looked ramshackle on the outside .
description_long: Winter ' s Cradle Tavern The Winter ' s Cradle Tavern was a tavern in Easthaven within the Ten - Towns of Icewind Dale . Structure . Located in the northern part of Easthaven , the wooden building looked ramshackle on the outside . Interior . The tavern was a comfortable place with a fireplace burning to keep the cold northern chill from the bones of any adventurer . Inhabitants . The tavern was owned by Grisella who sold winter wine , , frost giant yellow snow melt s , Grisella ' s Dale , Luskan , Cormyrian , and knee cracker . The tavern was often patronized by the dwarf Hildeth Highhammer and the soldier Hrothgar . History . In Mirtul , 1281 DR , the cellar of the Winter ' s Cradle had an infestation of beetle s .

title: Winter Edge
description: Winter Edge Winter Edge was a hamlet in the Silver Marches of Northwest Faerûn . Geography . West of the Moonwood , the hamlet was east of River Surbrin and near Mithral Hall located in the Frost Hills .
description_long: Winter Edge Winter Edge was a hamlet in the Silver Marches of Northwest Faerûn . Geography . West of the Moonwood , the hamlet was east of River Surbrin and near Mithral Hall located in the Frost Hills . History . Winter Edge has been gaining importance since Obould Manny Arrows besieged Mithral Hall and then Mithral Hall by aid of Citadel Felbarr succeeded to open east gate . Mithral Hall provide to trade other Silver Marches cities via Winter Edge . High Lady of Silverymoon Alustriel Silverhand promised to Bruenor Battlehammer , king of Mithral Hall , help and trade via Winter Edge . Inhabitants . People of Winter Edge earn a living with trade and farming . Only humans live there but many times elves from north , specially Moonwood , or Silvermoon visit Winter Edge .

title: Winter Wine
description: Winter Wine Winter Wine was a wine crafted in the North . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description .
description_long: Winter Wine Winter Wine was a wine crafted in the North . It was also sold through Aurora ' s Whole Realms Catalogue . Description . This purplish wine was made after allowing the grapes to freeze on the vine . Winter Wine was was typically served in small portions with dessert since it was strong and sweet . It also had a slight spicy tone . Prices . Winter Wine could be purchased in the following containers :

title: Winter Zulth
description: Winter Zulth Winter Zulth was a half - elf living in Waterdeep and the regional agent of the Moonstars for non - Faerûn ian locations in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . History . Winter was raised in Waterdeep and worked at the Horizon ' s Sails as a map - maker .
description_long: Winter Zulth Winter Zulth was a half - elf living in Waterdeep and the regional agent of the Moonstars for non - Faerûn ian locations in the Year of the Tankard , 1370 DR . History . Winter was raised in Waterdeep and worked at the Horizon ' s Sails as a map - maker . He used his position for the Moonstars ' cause by collating maps and logbooks from exotic places like Zakhara , Maztica , and Kara - Tur and producing unique maps that were extremely valuable to explorers and navigators . He could also provide a ship for the Moonstar ' s needs upon request .

title: Winter wolf
description: Winter wolf A winter wolf was more akin to a worg than an actual wolf , being of wicked intelligence and cunning . Description . It grew to about 8 ft ( 2 .
description_long: Winter wolf A winter wolf was more akin to a worg than an actual wolf , being of wicked intelligence and cunning . Description . It grew to about 8 ft ( 2 . 4 m ) in length , 4 . 5 ft ( 1 . 4 m ) at the shoulder , and weighed around 450 lb ( 204 kg ) . They usually had blue eyes . Combat . Using their fur as camouflage , winter wolves would lay in wait for prey . When an ambush was triggered , winter wolves would encircle their prey and take turns to attack , or attempt to pin it . They could breathe gusts of cold as well as bite their victims . They could also trip their enemies . They were immune to cold and cold magic , but were vulnerable to fire . Society . Winter wolves lived in packs of around three to five , sometimes found as allies and guardians of frost giant s , white dragon s , and other evil arctic beings . They spoke their own language , Winter Wolf , as well as Giant and Common .

title: Wintercloak River
description: Wintercloak River The Wintercloak River connected the Deepwash with the Nagawater . Description . The river was swift but still navigable , even going upstream if the wind was right and the rowers were strong enough .
description_long: Wintercloak River The Wintercloak River connected the Deepwash with the Nagawater . Description . The river was swift but still navigable , even going upstream if the wind was right and the rowers were strong enough . It passed through several of gorges as it passed through the Cloven Mountains and through the Winterwood .

title: Winterhaven
description: Winterhaven The town of Winterhaven was located on the East Way , between the nations of Sembia and Cormyr . It was situated on the road between Arabel and Highmoon . Due to its location in the middle of the Thunder Peaks , it was not uncommon for the inhabitants to be attacked by monstrous races such as kobolds and goblins .
description_long: Winterhaven The town of Winterhaven was located on the East Way , between the nations of Sembia and Cormyr . It was situated on the road between Arabel and Highmoon . Due to its location in the middle of the Thunder Peaks , it was not uncommon for the inhabitants to be attacked by monstrous races such as kobolds and goblins . An ancient dragon burial site laid southwest of the town , and the ruined Shadowfell Keep laid northeast . History . Long before the birth of Cormyr in 26 DR , the shadow dragon Shadraxil lurked in the Thunder Peaks . When Cormyr began to create a series of fortresses along its frontier in 236 DR , Shadraxil took this as an affront to his lands and began attacking the outposts . In response to Shadraxil ' s depredations , Cormyr sent a small force of armed men and War Wizard s led by the paladin Jerold Keegan . Keegan created a magical trap within one of the keeps and trapped Shadraxil in the Plane of Shadow . Sir Jerold Keegan became the lord of that outpost , which was then called Keegan ' s Keep . The town of Winterhaven was founded nearby due to the keep ' s protection .

title: Winterkeep
description: Winterkeep Winterkeep was a ruin located on the southern tip of the Yal Tengri . East of Winterkeep were the Glittering Spires . Description .
description_long: Winterkeep Winterkeep was a ruin located on the southern tip of the Yal Tengri . East of Winterkeep were the Glittering Spires . Description . On the surface , only rubble remained , but the extensive subterranean passageways and chambers remained mostly intact . The royal family and their servants retreated beneath the surface during winter storms ; as a result these halls were comfortably furnished . To the Vil Adanrath , Winterkeep was known as " " Iket Sotha " " . History . Winterkeep was built as a nobleman ' s estate , in the days of Raumathar . It later became a retreat for the royal family . After the fall of the empire , Winterkeep gradually fell to ruins . In 1374 DR , the gelugon Ultael enslaved several ice troll warbands and started to attempt to make a fiefdom for himself . He sent several warbands out to raid along the Golden Way .

title: Wintersun
description: Wintersun Wintersun was a noble house of Cormyr . Their holdings were mostly in Cormyr ' s back country and they were considered backwater hicks by most other noble families . After the Abraxus affair in 1369 DR the family began buying properties in Suzail in an effort to seem more cosmopolitan and by the late 15th century DR was the largest landlord in the city .
description_long: Wintersun Wintersun was a noble house of Cormyr . Their holdings were mostly in Cormyr ' s back country and they were considered backwater hicks by most other noble families . After the Abraxus affair in 1369 DR the family began buying properties in Suzail in an effort to seem more cosmopolitan and by the late 15th century DR was the largest landlord in the city . The Wintersuns were allied with House Dracohorn and House Illance .

title: Winterwood
description: Winterwood Winterwood was a vast woodland filled with pine s and oak s and was the darkest forest in the region . The thick foliage from these tall tress blocked out the sunlight and a cool , light , white mist was commonly seen floating along the ground . The white mist was so dense it looks like newly fallen snow , especially on the edges of the forest when the morning light struck the it ; hence its name : Winterwood .
description_long: Winterwood Winterwood was a vast woodland filled with pine s and oak s and was the darkest forest in the region . The thick foliage from these tall tress blocked out the sunlight and a cool , light , white mist was commonly seen floating along the ground . The white mist was so dense it looks like newly fallen snow , especially on the edges of the forest when the morning light struck the it ; hence its name : Winterwood . Inhabitants . The secluded nature of Winterwood allowed a tribe of mold men to establish a territory in the northern reaches of the forest ; they claimed their territory includes everything south of the Wintercloak river . This claim caused the tribe to remain at odds with the orcs of the White Hand . This band consisted of an amassed group of around 250 members who formed the village of Shen , which sat about four miles from the river in the very heart of the Winterwood . The ongoing dispute between these two factions made the Winterwood a dangerous locale to visit . South of the Wintercloak River was much more hospitable and an old male green dragon by the name of Foilsunder with druid powers , was said to lair about 20 miles or so to the south . Notes .

title: Winthrop
description: Winthrop Winthrop was the innkeep of the Candlekeep Inn in the 1350s DR . He was known for his good - humored nature and frequent jests . Appearance .
description_long: Winthrop Winthrop was the innkeep of the Candlekeep Inn in the 1350s DR . He was known for his good - humored nature and frequent jests . Appearance . By 1368 DR , Winthrop appeared as a portly man , and was considered old by Candlekeep ' s youth . Personality . Winthrop had a jocular manner , often proclaiming his inn to be " as clean as an elven arse . " His prices were considered fair , and he did his best to keep them as low as possible . Relationships . Winthrop was friends with the Bhaalspawn known as Gorion ' s Ward , and would perform practical jokes at the Ward ' s expense . Imoen , another orphaned Bhaalspawn residing in Candlekeep , helped Winthrop run his inn by performing various chores , much to her annoyance . She referred to the innkeep as " Old Puffguts " , which in turn annoyed him . Despite their bickering , Imoen enjoyed Winthrop ' s company , and he taught her various roguish skills . Winthrop felt Gorion , the foster father of both Imoen and the Ward , was too stiff for his liking . Activities . In addition to running the inn , Winthrop sold various merchandise , including both weapons and armor . He kept a book with pictures of naked women in his room .

title: Wired cane
description: Wired cane A wired cane was a tool used by some rogue s when pickpocketing . Uses . Wired canes were attached to a rogue ' s hand by a thin wire .
description_long: Wired cane A wired cane was a tool used by some rogue s when pickpocketing . Uses . Wired canes were attached to a rogue ' s hand by a thin wire . By pretending to be crippled , the rogue could approach a target without raising suspicion , allowing them to pilfer coins from the target ' s purse . Some wired canes were hollowed out and had a hinged handle , allowing coins and small gems to be stored within the barrel of the cane . Prices . The cost of a wired cane depended on the material from which it was made , but most could be acquired for 3 – 10 gold .

title: Wiri Fleagol
description: Wiri Fleagol Wiri Fleagol was a slave of the fire giant s in Ironslag sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Wiri was captured by fire giants and taken to Ironslag where she worked as a miner together with many other gnome s and dwarves , overseen by salamander guards .
description_long: Wiri Fleagol Wiri Fleagol was a slave of the fire giant s in Ironslag sometime after the War of the Silver Marches . History . In the late 1480s or early 1490s DR , Wiri was captured by fire giants and taken to Ironslag where she worked as a miner together with many other gnome s and dwarves , overseen by salamander guards .

title: Wish
description: Wish Wish was arguably the most powerful spell that a sorcerer or wizard could hope to learn . It allowed its caster to accomplish multiple , various effects ranging from duplicating other spell effects to altering reality to suit the caster ' s wish , hence its name . History .
description_long: Wish Wish was arguably the most powerful spell that a sorcerer or wizard could hope to learn . It allowed its caster to accomplish multiple , various effects ranging from duplicating other spell effects to altering reality to suit the caster ' s wish , hence its name . History . The " wish " spell was not crafted until a hundred years after the Fall of Netheril .

title: Wispling
description: Wispling Wisplings were planetouched , native outsider s descended from the breeding of halfling s and demons . Description . Wisplings descended from demons and halflings ; however , they lacked the " traditional " fiendish traits , instead having light brown skin and bright red hair .
description_long: Wispling Wisplings were planetouched , native outsider s descended from the breeding of halfling s and demons . Description . Wisplings descended from demons and halflings ; however , they lacked the " traditional " fiendish traits , instead having light brown skin and bright red hair . Despite their great abilities for stealth , wisplings chose to commonly wear bright colors in order to stand out in a crowd . Like most planetouched , they had darkvision , which was limited to 60 ft ( 18 . 3 m ) . Abilities . Wisplings had the innate ability to appear as any humanoid creature once per day .

title: Witches of Rashemen
description: Witches of Rashemen The Witches of Rashemen , also known as Wychlaran , meaning " wise old women " in the ancient language of Halardrim , were the spiritual leaders of Rashemen , communing with the spirits and guiding the souls of the Rashemi people . History . The Witches of Rashemen were formed in - 160 DR to preserve the lore and magic of Raumathar at the beginning of their final conflict with Narfell .
description_long: Witches of Rashemen The Witches of Rashemen , also known as Wychlaran , meaning " wise old women " in the ancient language of Halardrim , were the spiritual leaders of Rashemen , communing with the spirits and guiding the souls of the Rashemi people . History . The Witches of Rashemen were formed in - 160 DR to preserve the lore and magic of Raumathar at the beginning of their final conflict with Narfell . Membership . The formal term for a member of this group was " hathran " ( " learned sister " ) , while the most powerful and respected were called " othlor " ( " true one " ) . In Rashemen , a member of the Wychlaran could do no wrong . Her word was law and to disobey it was punishable by death . Regions . The Witches of Rashemen were based in Urlingwood , an area forbidden to any non - Wychlaran . Any trespassers found in the wood were killed on sight . The witch es met here to brew jhuild , as well as to bind and control hostile spirits and spy on Thay an forces . Relationships . While most Witches of Rashemen sought to protect the land and ensure peace , some merely desired power . These were known as the Durthan .

title: Witchfire
description: Witchfire Witchfire was a mildly complex invocation wielded by several warlock s . When " witchfire " was cast , it summoned from the Feywild a hot , white flame into a target of the warlock ' s choosing within fifty feet ( fifteen meters ) . If set inside a living creature , the flame caused the creature immense pain , sending streams of enchanted fire through the creature ' s orifices with such pain as to distract them from all other things , making them less effective combatants .
description_long: Witchfire Witchfire was a mildly complex invocation wielded by several warlock s . When " witchfire " was cast , it summoned from the Feywild a hot , white flame into a target of the warlock ' s choosing within fifty feet ( fifteen meters ) . If set inside a living creature , the flame caused the creature immense pain , sending streams of enchanted fire through the creature ' s orifices with such pain as to distract them from all other things , making them less effective combatants . The potency of " witchfire " was largely determined by the strength of personality possessed by the warlock casting it , though warlocks of the fey pact also found a strong intellect to be of enormous importance . The spell was not easily cast , and once it had been used , it could not be recast by the warlock without a brief respite for the body and mind .

title: Withdraw
description: Withdraw Withdraw was an alteration spell that allowed the caster to slow time as he or she experienced it in order to contemplate a problem or cast a personal spell . Effects . This spell bent time around the caster so that a few minutes ( based on the caster ' s level ) passed for the caster while only one minute passed for everyone else .
description_long: Withdraw Withdraw was an alteration spell that allowed the caster to slow time as he or she experienced it in order to contemplate a problem or cast a personal spell . Effects . This spell bent time around the caster so that a few minutes ( based on the caster ' s level ) passed for the caster while only one minute passed for everyone else . During the time spent withdrawn from the time stream , the caster could use this extra time to ponder his or her next move , solve a problem , cast a divination spell , or cast a heal or cure on himself or herself . The caster could not move from the spot where " withdraw " was cast , nor interact with others , nor perform any actions other than those listed above — attempting to do so canceled the spell . A successful attack on the caster also broke the spell . Components . Only verbal and somatic components were required to cast this spell .

title: Withegroo Seian ' Doo
description: Withegroo Seian ' Doo Withegroo Seian ' Doo is a wizard who lives in Shallows where he has his own tower . He founded , and leads the hamlet . Appearance .
description_long: Withegroo Seian ' Doo Withegroo Seian ' Doo is a wizard who lives in Shallows where he has his own tower . He founded , and leads the hamlet . Appearance . Withegroo looks old and has a white beard . He has a wrinkly face , large ears and a hawk - like nose . His white hair is unkempt . He stands over 6 feet ( 1 . 83m ) tall . He wears red robes with gold stars ( similar to the pennant hanging from his tower ) and a pointy hat . Background . Withegroo made a name and a fortune for himself by adventuring in caves and fighting creatures . He used the money to build himself a tower , and it gradually turned into a settlement as more and more people came to live in safe proximity . In 1370 DR , during the orc and frost giant attack on Shallows , Withegroo was hit by a hurled boulder while on top of his tower , and seriously injured . Ultimately , Withegroo falls , as witnessed by Catti - brie and Wulfgar when the orcs pressed ahead into the mostly destroyed settlement . His final act was that of a fireball , incinerating some of the orcs , this was the last spell he ever cast and the use of his powers felled him .

title: Witherite
description: Witherite Witherite was a yellow to white semi - precious gemstone . Description . Witherite was found in large , fibrous deposits containing zones of translucent gem - quality material .
description_long: Witherite Witherite was a yellow to white semi - precious gemstone . Description . Witherite was found in large , fibrous deposits containing zones of translucent gem - quality material . If large enough , they yielded faceted pale yellow to whitish gems . Rarely , witherite occurred in clusters of translucent yellowish crystals which also yielded faceted gemstones . A typical specimen had a base value of 50gp . Powers . Witherite gave some protection or even immunity to the withering effects of necromantic reversed healing spells and certain psionic attacks . The stone had to be mounted in a special electrum setting that allowed direct skin contact with the witherite . This was known to work for at least human s and demihuman s .

title: Wittel
description: Wittel Wittel was a teamster in Hillsfar in the Moonsea . Activities . Wittel was a teamster who worked transferring goods from the farms around Hillsfar to the city .
description_long: Wittel Wittel was a teamster in Hillsfar in the Moonsea . Activities . Wittel was a teamster who worked transferring goods from the farms around Hillsfar to the city . History . During the Rage of Demons , his wife Dottee announced that she was pregnant and they decided to go for a trip in the Cormanthor forest . There , a family of jackalwere s ambushed them : Wittel was left unconscious and Dottee taken .

title: Wizard
description: Wizard Wizards are a form of spellcaster who learn the art of arcane magic through research and learning . What wizards lack in combat prowess and armor they make up with a broad range of magical spell s and abilities learned through years of practice and training .
